item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: الم alif-lam-meem Alif, Lām, Meem.1 مِن قَبْلُ Aforetime Meaning: before the Qur'an was revealed: هُدًى لِّلنَّاسِ As a guidance to mankind in their time. وَأَنزَلَ الْفُرْقَانَ And He sent down the criterion which is the distinction between misguidance, falsehood and deviation on one hand, and guidance, truth and piety on the other hand. This is because of the indications, signs, plain evidences and clear proofs that it contains, and because of its explanations, clarifications, etc. Allah's statement: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ Truly, those who disbelieve in the Ayat of Allah means they denied, refused and unjustly rejected them: لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ For them there is a severe torment on the Day of Resurrection: وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ And Allah is All-Mighty Meaning: His grandeur is invincible and His sovereignty is infinite: ذُو انتِقَامٍ All-Able of Retribution. from those who reject His…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: الم alif-lam-meem Alif Laam, Mim Alif, Laam, Meem, (Huraf al-Muqatta'at1).

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ al-lahu lā ilāha illā huwa l-ḥayu l-qayūmu Allah—there is no god except Him— is the Living One, the All-sustainer.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ al-lahu lā ilāha illā huwa l-ḥayu l-qayūmu Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining.1 See 3:1

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ al-lahu lā ilāha illā huwa l-ḥayu l-qayūmu God! there is no God but He, the Ever (Self-Living 2:255.) Living the Se1f-Subsistent (Sustainer of all things-or By Whom all things are sustained 2:255.) (The Sustainer of all things) See Note on the opening words of Verse 2:255. 'Ibn Ishaq says that over 80 verses from the beginning of this Surah, were revealed about the Christians of 'Najran' whose embassy to the Prophet is described in the note to verse 54. The whole of the section 2 refers to the stress laid on the two attributes of God, the Ever-living (Hai) and the Self-Subsisting by whom all things subsist (Qayyum) which deals a death-blow to the doctrine of the divinity of Jesus Christ, because his birth and his death, do not entitle him to claim…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ بِالْحَقِّ مُصَدِّقًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَأَنْزَلَ التَّوْرَاةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ nazzala ʿalayka l-kitāba bil-ḥaqi muṣaddiqan limā bayna yadayhi wa-anzala l-tawrāta wal-injīla He has sent down to you the Book with the truth confirming what was [revealed] before it, and He had sent down the Torah and the Evangel

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ بِالْحَقِّ مُصَدِّقًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَأَنْزَلَ التَّوْرَاةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ nazzala ʿalayka l-kitāba bil-ḥaqi muṣaddiqan limā bayna yadayhi wa-anzala l-tawrāta wal-injīla He has sent down upon you, (O Muḥammad), the Book in truth, confirming what was before it. And He revealed the Torah and the Gospel. See 3:1

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ بِالْحَقِّ مُصَدِّقًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَأَنْزَلَ التَّوْرَاةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ nazzala ʿalayka l-kitāba bil-ḥaqi muṣaddiqan limā bayna yadayhi wa-anzala l-tawrāta wal-injīla He hath sent down unto thee the Book (The Qur'an.) with Truth confirming what was before it; And He sent down the Torah (The Scripture given to Moses.) and the Evangel (The Scripture given to Jesus.) 'Taurat', 'Injeel', and the 'Books' used here and elsewhere in Qur'an refer to what was revealed to the respective prophets. Hence the present gospels of the Christian church cannot be termed as the 'Injeel' revealed to Jesus, to which Jesus himself refers while he commands his disciples, saying, "Go and preach the Gospel", and while he exhorts his people to believe in the Gospel1. The book called the Bible contains only some extracts from the utterances of Jesus and his experiences in…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مِنْ قَبْلُ هُدًى لِلنَّاسِ وَأَنْزَلَ الْفُرْقَانَ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا بِءَايَاتِ اللَّهِ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ ذُو انْتِقَامٍ min qablu hudan lilnnāsi wa-anzala l-fur'qāna inna alladhīna kafarū biāyāti l-lahi lahum ʿadhābun shadīdun wal-lahu ʿazīzun dhū intiqāmin before as guidance for mankind, and He has sent down the Criterion.1 Indeed those who defy the signs of Allah, there is a severe punishment for them; and Allah is all-mighty, avenger.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مِنْ قَبْلُ هُدًى لِلنَّاسِ وَأَنْزَلَ الْفُرْقَانَ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا بِءَايَاتِ اللَّهِ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ ذُو انْتِقَامٍ min qablu hudan lilnnāsi wa-anzala l-fur'qāna inna alladhīna kafarū biāyāti l-lahi lahum ʿadhābun shadīdun wal-lahu ʿazīzun dhū intiqāmin Before, as guidance for the people. And He revealed the Criterion (i.e., the Qur’ān). Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of Allah will have a severe punishment, and Allah is Exalted in Might, the Owner of Retribution.1 See 3:1

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مِنْ قَبْلُ هُدًى لِلنَّاسِ وَأَنْزَلَ الْفُرْقَانَ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا بِءَايَاتِ اللَّهِ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ ذُو انْتِقَامٍ min qablu hudan lilnnāsi wa-anzala l-fur'qāna inna alladhīna kafarū biāyāti l-lahi lahum ʿadhābun shadīdun wal-lahu ʿazīzun dhū intiqāmin Aforetime, a guidance for people and sent down the Distinction (Ar. Furqan i.e. Qur'an - The Distinctive Standard.) (Furqan), Verily for those who disbelieve in the signs of God, for them is a severe punishment; God is Mighty, Lord of Retribution See 3:3

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَخْفَى عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ inna l-laha lā yakhfā ʿalayhi shayon fī l-arḍi walā fī l-samāi Nothing is indeed hidden from Allah in the earth or in the sky.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَخْفَى عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ inna l-laha lā yakhfā ʿalayhi shayon fī l-arḍi walā fī l-samāi Indeed, from Allah nothing is hidden in the earth nor in the heaven. Truly, nothing is hidden from Allah, in the earth or in the heaven (3:5). He it is Who shapes you in the wombs as He wills. None has the right to be worshipped but He, the Almighty, the All-Wise (3:6). Allah states that He has perfect knowledge in the heavens and earth and that nothing in them is hidden from His watch. هُوَ الَّذِي يُصَوِّرُكُمْ فِي الْأَرْحَامِ كَيْفَ يَشَاءُ He it is Who shapes you in the wombs as He wills. Meaning: He creates you in the wombs as He wills, whether male or female, handsome or otherwise, happy or miserable. لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَخْفَى عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ inna l-laha lā yakhfā ʿalayhi shayon fī l-arḍi walā fī l-samāi Verily, God, nothing hidden is there from Him, in the Earth and in the Heavens The knowledge of everything in the world, be that manifest or hidden, belongs to none but God. Verse Mark. 13/32 clearly denotes that Jesus was nothing more than a man, a mortal and not God as conceived by the Christian Church. Jesus in this verse clearly says that he does not know what God alone knows: - "But of that day and that hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels which are in heaven, neither the son, but Father" Mark 13/32.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: هُوَ الَّذِي يُصَوِّرُكُمْ فِي الْأَرْحَامِ كَيْفَ يَشَاءُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ huwa alladhī yuṣawwirukum fī l-arḥāmi kayfa yashāu lā ilāha illā huwa l-ʿazīzu l-ḥakīmu It is He who forms you in the wombs however He wishes. There is no god except Him, the All-mighty, the All-wise.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: هُوَ الَّذِي يُصَوِّرُكُمْ فِي الْأَرْحَامِ كَيْفَ يَشَاءُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ huwa alladhī yuṣawwirukum fī l-arḥāmi kayfa yashāu lā ilāha illā huwa l-ʿazīzu l-ḥakīmu It is He who forms you in the wombs however He wills. There is no deity except Him, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. See 3:5

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: هُوَ الَّذِي يُصَوِّرُكُمْ فِي الْأَرْحَامِ كَيْفَ يَشَاءُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ huwa alladhī yuṣawwirukum fī l-arḥāmi kayfa yashāu lā ilāha illā huwa l-ʿazīzu l-ḥakīmu He it is Who fashioneth you in the wombs (of your mothers) as He liketh; There is no God but HE, the All-Mighty, the All-Wise 'Kaifa Yasha' i.e. As He likes or as it pleases Him. This indicates the Omnipotence and the absolute power and the absolute freedom of the divine will. God acts in whatever way or manner it pleases Him. He may create an issue in the ordinary or the usual course of the union of male and female matters, or He, if it be His will, create an issue out of a female element alone, as in Parthenogenesis which is common in insects and the bees, etc. The ignorance of this…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: هُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ عَلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ مِنْهُ آيَاتٌ مُحْكَمَاتٌ هُنَّ أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ وَأُخَرُ مُتَشَابِهَاتٌ فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ زَيْغٌ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَابَهَ مِنْهُ ابْتِغَاءَ الْفِتْنَةِ وَابْتِغَاءَ تَأْوِيلِهِ وَمَا يَعْلَمُ تَأْوِيلَهُ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَالرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ يَقُولُونَ اٰمَنَّا بِهِ كُلٌّ مِنْ عِنْدِ رَبِّنَا وَمَا يَذَّكَّرُ إِلَّا أُولُوْۤا الْأَلْبَابِ huwa alladhī anzala ʿalayka l-kitāba min'hu āyātun muḥ'kamātun hunna ummu l-kitābi wa-ukharu mutashābihātun fa-ammā alladhīna fī qulūbihim zayghun fayattabiʿūna mā tashābaha min'hu ib'tighāa l-fit'nati wa-ib'tighāa tawīlihi wamā yaʿlamu tawīlahu illā l-lahu wal-rāsikhūna fī l-ʿil'mi yaqūlūna āmannā bihi kullun min ʿindi rabbinā wamā yadhakkaru illā ulū l-albābi It is He who has sent down to you the Book. Parts of it are definitive verses, which are the mother of the Book, while others are metaphorical.1 As for those in whose hearts is deviance, they pursue what is metaphorical in it, courting temptation and courting its…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: هُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ عَلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ مِنْهُ آيَاتٌ مُحْكَمَاتٌ هُنَّ أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ وَأُخَرُ مُتَشَابِهَاتٌ فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ زَيْغٌ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَابَهَ مِنْهُ ابْتِغَاءَ الْفِتْنَةِ وَابْتِغَاءَ تَأْوِيلِهِ وَمَا يَعْلَمُ تَأْوِيلَهُ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَالرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ يَقُولُونَ اٰمَنَّا بِهِ كُلٌّ مِنْ عِنْدِ رَبِّنَا وَمَا يَذَّكَّرُ إِلَّا أُولُوْۤا الْأَلْبَابِ huwa alladhī anzala ʿalayka l-kitāba min'hu āyātun muḥ'kamātun hunna ummu l-kitābi wa-ukharu mutashābihātun fa-ammā alladhīna fī qulūbihim zayghun fayattabiʿūna mā tashābaha min'hu ib'tighāa l-fit'nati wa-ib'tighāa tawīlihi wamā yaʿlamu tawīlahu illā l-lahu wal-rāsikhūna fī l-ʿil'mi yaqūlūna āmannā bihi kullun min ʿindi rabbinā wamā yadhakkaru illā ulū l-albābi It is He who has sent down to you, (O Muḥammad), the Book; in it are verses (that are) precise - they are the foundation of the Book - and others unspecific.1 As for those in whose hearts is deviation (from truth), they will follow that of it…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran

'the Book (Qur'an.) of it there are (some) verses (Refer to: 13:39, 4:162, 29:49, 3:11, 38:11) decisive (Clear.) these are the Basis (Mother or Essence.) of the Book, and others are ambiguous (Figurative.) ; But…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: رَبَّنَا لَا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا وَهَبْ لَنَا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ رَحْمَةً إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْوَهَّابُ rabbanā lā tuzigh qulūbanā baʿda idh hadaytanā wahab lanā min ladunka raḥmatan innaka anta l-wahābu [They say,] 'Our Lord! Do not make our hearts swerve after You have guided us, and bestow Your mercy on us. Indeed You are the All-munificent.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: رَبَّنَا لَا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا وَهَبْ لَنَا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ رَحْمَةً إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْوَهَّابُ rabbanā lā tuzigh qulūbanā baʿda idh hadaytanā wahab lanā min ladunka raḥmatan innaka anta l-wahābu (Who say), "Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower.1 See 3:7

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: رَبَّنَا لَا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا وَهَبْ لَنَا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ رَحْمَةً إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْوَهَّابُ rabbanā lā tuzigh qulūbanā baʿda idh hadaytanā wahab lanā min ladunka raḥmatan innaka anta l-wahābu (They pray) "Our Lord! Suffer not our hearts to perverse after Thou hast guided (aright) and grant us from unto Thee mercy, for verily Thou, and Thou (Alone) art the (Ar. 'Wahab') Ever- Bestower" This is the prayer of those 'Raasikhoona fil ilm.' This is a precautionary prayer against the possible perversion (of the mind and heart, even after receiving the guidance. (A.P.)

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: رَبَّنَا إِنَّكَ جَامِعُ النَّاسِ لِيَوْمٍ لَا رَيْبَ فِیْهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُخْلِفُ الْمِيعَادَ rabbanā innaka jāmiʿu l-nāsi liyawmin lā rayba fīhi inna l-laha lā yukh'lifu l-mīʿāda Our Lord! You will indeed gather mankind on a day in which there is no doubt. Indeed Allah does not break His promise.'

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: رَبَّنَا إِنَّكَ جَامِعُ النَّاسِ لِيَوْمٍ لَا رَيْبَ فِیْهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُخْلِفُ الْمِيعَادَ rabbanā innaka jāmiʿu l-nāsi liyawmin lā rayba fīhi inna l-laha lā yukh'lifu l-mīʿāda Our Lord, surely You will gather the people for a Day about which there is no doubt. Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise." See 3:7

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: رَبَّنَا إِنَّكَ جَامِعُ النَّاسِ لِيَوْمٍ لَا رَيْبَ فِیْهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُخْلِفُ الْمِيعَادَ rabbanā innaka jāmiʿu l-nāsi liyawmin lā rayba fīhi inna l-laha lā yukh'lifu l-mīʿāda Our (This is the continuation of the prayer of the believers Refer to Verse . 8.) Lord! Verily Thou art the Gatherer of mankind unto the Day (of Judgment) about which there is no doubt; (Be Merciful to us then); Verily God faileth not His promise The prayer in this verse and in the preceding one, refers to the ideal or the life-object of those 'Raasikhoona fil ilm.' They pray for their welfare in the life hereafter and on the Day of Judgment This prayer itself speaks loudly that the object of the lives of those 'Raasikhoona fil ilm' is nothing connected with their welfare in this life which, they know it for certain,…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا لَنْ تُغْنِيَ عَنْهُمْ أَمْوَالُهُمْ وَلَا أَوْلَادُهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا وَاُولٰٓىِٕكَ هُمْ وَقُودُ النَّارِ inna alladhīna kafarū lan tugh'niya ʿanhum amwāluhum walā awlāduhum mina l-lahi shayan wa-ulāika hum waqūdu l-nāri As for the faithless, neither their wealth nor their children shall avail them anything against Allah; it is they who will be fuel for the Fire;

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا لَنْ تُغْنِيَ عَنْهُمْ أَمْوَالُهُمْ وَلَا أَوْلَادُهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا وَاُولٰٓىِٕكَ هُمْ وَقُودُ النَّارِ inna alladhīna kafarū lan tugh'niya ʿanhum amwāluhum walā awlāduhum mina l-lahi shayan wa-ulāika hum waqūdu l-nāri Indeed, those who disbelieve - never will their wealth or their children avail them against Allah at all. And it is they who are fuel for the Fire. Verily, those who disbelieve, neither their properties nor their offspring will avail them whatsoever against Allah; and it is they who will be fuel of the Fire (3:10). Like the behavior of the people of Fir'awn and those before them; they belied Our Ayat. So Allah punished them for their sins. And Allah is severe in punishment (3:11). On the Day of Resurrection, No Wealth or Offspring Shall Avail Allah states that the disbelievers shall be fuel for the Fire:…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا لَنْ تُغْنِيَ عَنْهُمْ أَمْوَالُهُمْ وَلَا أَوْلَادُهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا وَاُولٰٓىِٕكَ هُمْ وَقُودُ النَّارِ inna alladhīna kafarū lan tugh'niya ʿanhum amwāluhum walā awlāduhum mina l-lahi shayan wa-ulāika hum waqūdu l-nāri Verily, those who disbelieve, never shall their wealth (This is a clear warning to the puffed ones with wealth against their irreligiousness.) nor their progeny avail them aught against (the Wrath of) God; They and They are the fuel of the (Hell) fire This verse along with the two others immediately succeeding, is a clear prophecy of the vanquishment of the enemies of the Holy Prophet. Though the 'Quraish' had suffered a crushing defeat at 'Badr' they could yet muster heavy forces from their allies around them and gather tremendous strength against the poor and practically unarmed Muslim group at Madina. The number of the Muslims was very…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ كَذَّبُوْۤا بِاٰیٰتِنَاۤ فَأَخَذَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ وَاللَّهُ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ kadabi āli fir'ʿawna wa-alladhīna min qablihim kadhabū biāyātinā fa-akhadhahumu l-lahu bidhunūbihim wal-lahu shadīdu l-ʿiqābi as in the case of Pharaoh's clan and those who were before them, who denied Our signs. So Allah seized them for their sins, and Allah is severe in retribution.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ كَذَّبُوْۤا بِاٰیٰتِنَاۤ فَأَخَذَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ وَاللَّهُ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ kadabi āli fir'ʿawna wa-alladhīna min qablihim kadhabū biāyātinā fa-akhadhahumu l-lahu bidhunūbihim wal-lahu shadīdu l-ʿiqābi (Theirs is) like the custom of the people of Pharaoh and those before them. They denied Our signs, so Allah seized them for their sins. And Allah is severe in penalty. See 3:10

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ كَذَّبُوْۤا بِاٰیٰتِنَاۤ فَأَخَذَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ وَاللَّهُ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ kadabi āli fir'ʿawna wa-alladhīna min qablihim kadhabū biāyātinā fa-akhadhahumu l-lahu bidhunūbihim wal-lahu shadīdu l-ʿiqābi Like (A warning to those who depend on their wealth and forget God.) unto the wont of the people of Pharaoh and those before them; they belied our signs; so God caught them for their sins; and Verily God is (very) severe in requiting (evil) 'Daab' is generally interpreted as 'manner' or 'wont' but here it more appropriately signifies 'striving hard' or 'labouring' or 'endeavouring.' The Quraishites were feverishly busy day and night, in preparing themselves for a decisive onslaught. To be sure of their attack this time, at least being fully successful in taking their desired revenge upon the Holy Prophet and the poor Muslims, they were busy enlisting the Jewish…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا سَتُغْلَبُونَ وَتُحْشَرُونَ إِلَى جَهَنَّمَ وَبِئْسَ الْمِهَادُ qul lilladhīna kafarū satugh'labūna watuḥ'sharūna ilā jahannama wabi'sa l-mihādu Say to the faithless, 'You shall be overcome and mustered toward hell, and it is an evil resting place.'

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا سَتُغْلَبُونَ وَتُحْشَرُونَ إِلَى جَهَنَّمَ وَبِئْسَ الْمِهَادُ qul lilladhīna kafarū satugh'labūna watuḥ'sharūna ilā jahannama wabi'sa l-mihādu Say to those who disbelieve, "You will be overcome and gathered together to Hell, and wretched is the resting place." Say to those who disbelieve: You will be defeated and gathered together to Hell, and worst indeed is that place of rest (3:12). There has already been a sign for you in the two armies that met. One was fighting in the cause of Allah, and as for the other, in disbelief. They saw them with their own eyes twice their number. And Allah supports with His aid whom He wills. Verily, in this is a lesson for those who understand (3:13). Threatening the Jews With Defeat and Encouraging Them to Learn a Lesson From the Battle of Badr Allah commanded the…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا سَتُغْلَبُونَ وَتُحْشَرُونَ إِلَى جَهَنَّمَ وَبِئْسَ الْمِهَادُ qul lilladhīna kafarū satugh'labūna watuḥ'sharūna ilā jahannama wabi'sa l-mihādu Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) to those who disbelieve "ye shall be vanquished and gathered together unto Hell; (what) a wretched resting place (it shall be)" The Jews of 'Bani Qaniqaa' who lived in the suburbs of Madina got greatly alarmed by the crushing and the decisive victory the Muslims won at Badr and became active to do everything possible to prevent the growing power of the Muslims. They inflamed the fire already burning in the hearts of Quraish to a speedy revenge. Kaab Ibn Ashraf went to Mecca with a delegation to instigate the Quraish against the Muslims, stimulating the feelings of their tribal honour and their grief for their chiefs killed in the battle of Badr. From Mecca went Abu-Sufiyan…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ ءَايَةٌ فِي فِئَتَيْنِ الْتَقَتَا فِئَةٌ تُقَاتِلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَأُخْرٰی كَافِرَةٌ يَرَوْنَهُمْ مِثْلَيْهِمْ رَأْيَ الْعَيْنِ وَاللَّهُ يُؤَيِّدُ بِنَصْرِهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ إِنَّ فِي ذٰلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً لِأُولِي الْأَبْصَارِ qad kāna lakum āyatun fī fi-atayni l-taqatā fi-atun tuqātilu fī sabīli l-lahi wa-ukh'rā kāfiratun yarawnahum mith'layhim raya l-ʿayni wal-lahu yu-ayyidu binaṣrihi man yashāu inna fī dhālika laʿib'ratan li-ulī l-abṣāri There was certainly a sign for you in the two hosts that met: one host fighting in the way of Allah and the other faithless, who saw them visibly twice as many.1 Allah strengthens with His help whomever He wishes. There is indeed a moral in that for those who have insight.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ ءَايَةٌ فِي فِئَتَيْنِ الْتَقَتَا فِئَةٌ تُقَاتِلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَأُخْرٰی كَافِرَةٌ يَرَوْنَهُمْ مِثْلَيْهِمْ رَأْيَ الْعَيْنِ وَاللَّهُ يُؤَيِّدُ بِنَصْرِهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ إِنَّ فِي ذٰلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً لِأُولِي الْأَبْصَارِ qad kāna lakum āyatun fī fi-atayni l-taqatā fi-atun tuqātilu fī sabīli l-lahi wa-ukh'rā kāfiratun yarawnahum mith'layhim raya l-ʿayni wal-lahu yu-ayyidu binaṣrihi man yashāu inna fī dhālika laʿib'ratan li-ulī l-abṣāri Already there has been for you a sign in the two armies which met (in combat at Badr) - one fighting in the cause of Allah and another of disbelievers. They saw them (to be) twice their (own) number by (their) eyesight.1 But Allah supports with His victory whom He wills. Indeed in that is a lesson for those of vision. See 3:12

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:13 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ ءَايَةٌ فِي فِئَتَيْنِ الْتَقَتَا فِئَةٌ تُقَاتِلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَأُخْرٰی كَافِرَةٌ يَرَوْنَهُمْ مِثْلَيْهِمْ رَأْيَ الْعَيْنِ وَاللَّهُ يُؤَيِّدُ بِنَصْرِهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ إِنَّ فِي ذٰلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً لِأُولِي الْأَبْصَارِ qad kāna lakum āyatun fī fi-atayni l-taqatā fi-atun tuqātilu fī sabīli l-lahi wa-ukh'rā kāfiratun yarawnahum mith'layhim raya l-ʿayni wal-lahu yu-ayyidu binaṣrihi man yashāu inna fī dhālika laʿib'ratan li-ulī l-abṣāri Indeed, there was a sign for you in the two hosts (which) met together in the (The Battle of Badr.) encounter; one host fighting in the path of God and the other disbelieving, (they') (The believers saw the dis-believers as only double in number.) saw them twice their number with their (own) sight (Refer to Verses. 8:44, 8:66.) of the eye; Verily God aideth with His (As Moses was aided by Aaron the Holy Prophet was aided with Ali who displayed the…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:14 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: زُيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ حُبُّ الشَّهَوَاتِ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ وَالْبَنِينَ وَالْقَنَاطِيرِ الْمُقَنْطَرَةِ مِنَ الذَّهَبِ وَالْفِضَّةِ وَالْخَيْلِ الْمُسَوَّمَةِ وَالْأَنْعَامِ وَالْحَرْثِ ذٰلِكَ مَتَاعُ الْحَيَوةِ الدُّنْيَا وَاللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ حُسْنُ الْمَءَابِ zuyyina lilnnāsi ḥubbu l-shahawāti mina l-nisāi wal-banīna wal-qanāṭīri l-muqanṭarati mina l-dhahabi wal-fiḍati wal-khayli l-musawamati wal-anʿāmi wal-ḥarthi dhālika matāʿu l-ḥayati l-dun'yā wal-lahu ʿindahu ḥus'nu l-maābi To mankind has been made to seem decorous the love of [worldly] desires, including women and children, accumulated piles of gold and silver, horses of mark, livestock, and farms. Those are the wares of the life of this world; but Allah—with Him is a good destination.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:14 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: زُيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ حُبُّ الشَّهَوَاتِ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ وَالْبَنِينَ وَالْقَنَاطِيرِ الْمُقَنْطَرَةِ مِنَ الذَّهَبِ وَالْفِضَّةِ وَالْخَيْلِ الْمُسَوَّمَةِ وَالْأَنْعَامِ وَالْحَرْثِ ذٰلِكَ مَتَاعُ الْحَيَوةِ الدُّنْيَا وَاللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ حُسْنُ الْمَءَابِ zuyyina lilnnāsi ḥubbu l-shahawāti mina l-nisāi wal-banīna wal-qanāṭīri l-muqanṭarati mina l-dhahabi wal-fiḍati wal-khayli l-musawamati wal-anʿāmi wal-ḥarthi dhālika matāʿu l-ḥayati l-dun'yā wal-lahu ʿindahu ḥus'nu l-maābi Beautified for people is the love of that which they desire - of women and sons, heaped-up sums of gold and silver, fine branded horses, and cattle and tilled land. That is the enjoyment of worldly life, but Allah has with Him the best return (i.e., Paradise). Beautified for men is the love of things they covet; women, children, Qanatir Al-Muqantarah of gold and silver, branded beautiful horses (Musawwamah), cattle and fertile land. This is the pleasure of the present world's life; but Allah has the excellent return with Him (3:14). Say:…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:14 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: زُيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ حُبُّ الشَّهَوَاتِ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ وَالْبَنِينَ وَالْقَنَاطِيرِ الْمُقَنْطَرَةِ مِنَ الذَّهَبِ وَالْفِضَّةِ وَالْخَيْلِ الْمُسَوَّمَةِ وَالْأَنْعَامِ وَالْحَرْثِ ذٰلِكَ مَتَاعُ الْحَيَوةِ الدُّنْيَا وَاللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ حُسْنُ الْمَءَابِ zuyyina lilnnāsi ḥubbu l-shahawāti mina l-nisāi wal-banīna wal-qanāṭīri l-muqanṭarati mina l-dhahabi wal-fiḍati wal-khayli l-musawamati wal-anʿāmi wal-ḥarthi dhālika matāʿu l-ḥayati l-dun'yā wal-lahu ʿindahu ḥus'nu l-maābi (It has been) made to seem attractively fair unto men, the love of the lusts for women and sons and the hoarded treasures of gold and silver and well-bred horses (Beautiful and Luxurious Conveyances like the costly cars of the modern days.) and cattle and tilth (The Zamindaries and the landed properties.) ; this is the provision of the life of this world, while God! Verily with Him is the best destination The words used in this verse are to be carefully noted, and the verse as a whole to be studied…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ أَؤُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِخَيْرٍ مِنْ ذَلِكُمْ لِلَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا وَأَزْوَاجٌ مُطَهَّرَةٌ وَرِضْوَانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِالْعِبَادِ qul a-unabbi-ukum bikhayrin min dhālikum lilladhīna ittaqaw ʿinda rabbihim jannātun tajrī min taḥtihā l-anhāru khālidīna fīhā wa-azwājun muṭahharatun wariḍ'wānun mina l-lahi wal-lahu baṣīrun bil-ʿibādi Say, 'Shall I inform you of something better than that? For those who are Godwary there will be gardens near their Lord, with streams running in them, to remain in them [forever], and chaste mates, and Allah's pleasure.' And Allah sees best the servants.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ أَؤُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِخَيْرٍ مِنْ ذَلِكُمْ لِلَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا وَأَزْوَاجٌ مُطَهَّرَةٌ وَرِضْوَانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِالْعِبَادِ qul a-unabbi-ukum bikhayrin min dhālikum lilladhīna ittaqaw ʿinda rabbihim jannātun tajrī min taḥtihā l-anhāru khālidīna fīhā wa-azwājun muṭahharatun wariḍ'wānun mina l-lahi wal-lahu baṣīrun bil-ʿibādi Say, "Shall I inform you of (something) better than that? For those who fear Allah will be gardens in the presence of their Lord beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally, and purified spouses and approval from Allah. And Allah is Seeing (i.e., aware) of (His) servants. See 3:14

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ أَؤُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِخَيْرٍ مِنْ ذَلِكُمْ لِلَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا وَأَزْوَاجٌ مُطَهَّرَةٌ وَرِضْوَانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِالْعِبَادِ qul a-unabbi-ukum bikhayrin min dhālikum lilladhīna ittaqaw ʿinda rabbihim jannātun tajrī min taḥtihā l-anhāru khālidīna fīhā wa-azwājun muṭahharatun wariḍ'wānun mina l-lahi wal-lahu baṣīrun bil-ʿibādi Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Shall I tell you of what is better than these?; for those who take shelter (The pious.) in God are gardens with their Lord, beneath which flow rivers, to abide in them and mates pure, and God's pleasure; and verily God is well aware of the servants" The life after death is only a continuation of the present life, heading towards the state of realisation and spiritual perfection which, is in store for every human soul but only for those sincerely desirous and have duly endeavoured for…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا إِنَّنَا اٰمَنَّا فَاغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ alladhīna yaqūlūna rabbanā innanā āmannā fa-igh'fir lanā dhunūbanā waqinā ʿadhāba l-nāri Those who say, 'Our Lord! Indeed we have faith. So forgive us our sins, and save us from the punishment of the Fire.'

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا إِنَّنَا اٰمَنَّا فَاغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ alladhīna yaqūlūna rabbanā innanā āmannā fa-igh'fir lanā dhunūbanā waqinā ʿadhāba l-nāri Those who say, 'Our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.' " Those who say: Our Lord! We have indeed believed, so forgive us our sins and save us from the punishment of the Fire (3:16). (They are) the patient, the true believers, and obedient with sincere devotion in worship to Allah. Those who spend (in good) and those who pray and beg Allah's pardon in the last hours of the night (3:17). The Supplication and Description of Al-Muttaqin Allah describes the Muttaqin, His pious servants, whom He promised tremendous rewards: الَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا إِنَّنَا آمَنَّا Those who say: "Our Lord! We have indeed believed" in…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا إِنَّنَا اٰمَنَّا فَاغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ alladhīna yaqūlūna rabbanā innanā āmannā fa-igh'fir lanā dhunūbanā waqinā ʿadhāba l-nāri Those who pray saying "O' Our Lord! Indeed, we believe, so forgive us our sins and save us from the torment of the (Hell) fire" The prayer is nothing but a preparation for the life hereafter. No radical change is possible in the spirituality of the individual, unless one endeavours hard for it and feels remorse for his failure in maintaining the original attachment to those who have earned God's pleasure and thus become one of the beloved or the blessed ones of God.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلصَّابِرِينَ وَالصَّادِقِينَ وَالْقَانِتِينَ وَالْمُنْفِقِينَ وَالْمُسْتَغْفِرِينَ بِالْأَسْحَارِ al-ṣābirīna wal-ṣādiqīna wal-qānitīna wal-munfiqīna wal-mus'taghfirīna bil-asḥāri Patient and truthful, obedient and charitable, and pleading [Allah's] forgiveness at dawns.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلصَّابِرِينَ وَالصَّادِقِينَ وَالْقَانِتِينَ وَالْمُنْفِقِينَ وَالْمُسْتَغْفِرِينَ بِالْأَسْحَارِ al-ṣābirīna wal-ṣādiqīna wal-qānitīna wal-munfiqīna wal-mus'taghfirīna bil-asḥāri The patient, the true, the obedient, those who spend (in the way of Allah), and those who seek forgiveness before dawn. See 3:16

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:17 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلصَّابِرِينَ وَالصَّادِقِينَ وَالْقَانِتِينَ وَالْمُنْفِقِينَ وَالْمُسْتَغْفِرِينَ بِالْأَسْحَارِ al-ṣābirīna wal-ṣādiqīna wal-qānitīna wal-munfiqīna wal-mus'taghfirīna bil-asḥāri The patient, and the truthful, and the devout (ones), and those who spend (in the way of God) and those who seek forgiveness e're (Before.) dawn This verse gives the qualities that entitle one to the grace of God, and gives the clue to the special potency and effectiveness of prayer in the early hours of the dawn.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:18 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: شَهِدَ اللَّهُ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ وَأُولُوْۤا الْعِلْمِ قَائِمًا بِالْقِسْطِ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ shahida l-lahu annahu lā ilāha illā huwa wal-malāikatu wa-ulū l-ʿil'mi qāiman bil-qis'ṭi lā ilāha illā huwa l-ʿazīzu l-ḥakīmu Allah bears witness that there is no god except Him —and [so do] the angels and those who possess knowledge— maintainer of justice, there is no god but Him, the Almighty, the All-wise.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:18 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: شَهِدَ اللَّهُ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ وَأُولُوْۤا الْعِلْمِ قَائِمًا بِالْقِسْطِ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ shahida l-lahu annahu lā ilāha illā huwa wal-malāikatu wa-ulū l-ʿil'mi qāiman bil-qis'ṭi lā ilāha illā huwa l-ʿazīzu l-ḥakīmu Allah witnesses that there is no deity except Him, and (so do) the angels and those of knowledge - (that He is) maintaining (creation) in justice. There is no deity except Him, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. Allah bears witness that none has the right to be worshipped but He, and the angels, and those having knowledge (also bear witness to this); (He always) maintains His creation in justice. None has the right to be worshipped but He, the Almighty, the All-Wise (3:18). Truly, the religion with Allah is Islam. Those who were given the Scripture (Jews and Christians) did not differ except…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:18 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: شَهِدَ اللَّهُ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ وَأُولُوْۤا الْعِلْمِ قَائِمًا بِالْقِسْطِ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ shahida l-lahu annahu lā ilāha illā huwa wal-malāikatu wa-ulū l-ʿil'mi qāiman bil-qis'ṭi lā ilāha illā huwa l-ʿazīzu l-ḥakīmu God (Refer to: 57:25, 3:6, 4:162 5:8 15:27 29:49. Refer to Verses 2:112; 3:84; 42:14.) (Himself) witnesseth that there is no god but HE, and (so do) the angels and those possessed of knowledge, (See note to Verse 6 for 'Rasikhoona fil ilm'.) standing firm for justice (Not inclined to any extreme.) ; (there is) no god but He, the Mighty, the Wise God Himself witnessing to His Own Unity, is quite logical and meaningful, for unless God Himself, out of His Infinite Mercy, declares to us about His Own Existence, how can any of His creation by itself ever know about the truth…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:19 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الدِّينَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الْإِسْلَامُ وَمَا اخْتَلَفَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوْۤا الْكِتَابَ إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَهُمُ الْعِلْمُ بَغْيًا بَيْنَهُمْ وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِءَايَاتِ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ inna l-dīna ʿinda l-lahi l-is'lāmu wamā ikh'talafa alladhīna ūtū l-kitāba illā min baʿdi mā jāahumu l-ʿil'mu baghyan baynahum waman yakfur biāyāti l-lahi fa-inna l-laha sarīʿu l-ḥisābi Indeed, with Allah religion is Islām,1 and those who were given the Book did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves. And whoever defies Allah's signs [should know that] Allah is swift at reckoning.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:19 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الدِّينَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الْإِسْلَامُ وَمَا اخْتَلَفَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوْۤا الْكِتَابَ إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَهُمُ الْعِلْمُ بَغْيًا بَيْنَهُمْ وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِءَايَاتِ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ inna l-dīna ʿinda l-lahi l-is'lāmu wamā ikh'talafa alladhīna ūtū l-kitāba illā min baʿdi mā jāahumu l-ʿil'mu baghyan baynahum waman yakfur biāyāti l-lahi fa-inna l-laha sarīʿu l-ḥisābi Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islām. And those who were given the Scripture did not differ except after knowledge had come to them - out of jealous animosity between themselves. And whoever disbelieves in the verses of Allah, then indeed, Allah is swift in (taking) account. See 3:18

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:19 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الدِّينَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الْإِسْلَامُ وَمَا اخْتَلَفَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوْۤا الْكِتَابَ إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَهُمُ الْعِلْمُ بَغْيًا بَيْنَهُمْ وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِءَايَاتِ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ inna l-dīna ʿinda l-lahi l-is'lāmu wamā ikh'talafa alladhīna ūtū l-kitāba illā min baʿdi mā jāahumu l-ʿil'mu baghyan baynahum waman yakfur biāyāti l-lahi fa-inna l-laha sarīʿu l-ḥisābi Verily the religion with God is ISLAM (Total Submission to God's will.) (Submission to God's will), and those whom the Book had been given (Reference is to those who after believing in the Book of God and then differed from it - applicable to those who differed after embracing Islam. Refer to Verses 85 and 86.) did not differ but after the knowledge (of the Truth) had come unto them, out of envy among themselves; and whosoever disbelieveth in the signs (Including the apostles and the Holy Imams.)…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:20 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِنْ حَاجُّوكَ فَقُلْ أَسْلَمْتُ وَجْهِيَ لِلَّهِ وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَنِ وَقُلْ لِلَّذِينَ أُوتُوْۤا الْكِتَابَ وَالْأُمِّيِّينَ ءَأَسْلَمْتُمْ فَإِنْ أَسْلَمُوْۤا فَقَدِ اهْتَدَوْا وَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ الْبَلَاغُ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِالْعِبَادِ fa-in ḥājjūka faqul aslamtu wajhiya lillahi wamani ittabaʿani waqul lilladhīna ūtū l-kitāba wal-umiyīna a-aslamtum fa-in aslamū faqadi ih'tadaw wa-in tawallaw fa-innamā ʿalayka l-balāghu wal-lahu baṣīrun bil-ʿibādi So if they argue with you, say, 'I have submitted my will to Allah, and [so has] he who follows me.' And say to those who were given the Book and the uninstructed ones,1 'Do you submit?' If they submit, they will certainly be guided; but if they turn away, then your duty is only to communicate; and Allah sees best the servants.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:20 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِنْ حَاجُّوكَ فَقُلْ أَسْلَمْتُ وَجْهِيَ لِلَّهِ وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَنِ وَقُلْ لِلَّذِينَ أُوتُوْۤا الْكِتَابَ وَالْأُمِّيِّينَ ءَأَسْلَمْتُمْ فَإِنْ أَسْلَمُوْۤا فَقَدِ اهْتَدَوْا وَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ الْبَلَاغُ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِالْعِبَادِ fa-in ḥājjūka faqul aslamtu wajhiya lillahi wamani ittabaʿani waqul lilladhīna ūtū l-kitāba wal-umiyīna a-aslamtum fa-in aslamū faqadi ih'tadaw wa-in tawallaw fa-innamā ʿalayka l-balāghu wal-lahu baṣīrun bil-ʿibādi So if they argue with you, say, "I have submitted myself to Allah (in Islām), and (so have) those who follow me." And say to those who were given the Scripture and (to) the unlearned,1 "Have you submitted yourselves?" And if they submit (in Islām), they are rightly guided; but if they turn away - then upon you is only the (duty of) notification. And Allah is Seeing of (His) servants. See 3:18

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:20 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِنْ حَاجُّوكَ فَقُلْ أَسْلَمْتُ وَجْهِيَ لِلَّهِ وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَنِ وَقُلْ لِلَّذِينَ أُوتُوْۤا الْكِتَابَ وَالْأُمِّيِّينَ ءَأَسْلَمْتُمْ فَإِنْ أَسْلَمُوْۤا فَقَدِ اهْتَدَوْا وَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ الْبَلَاغُ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِالْعِبَادِ fa-in ḥājjūka faqul aslamtu wajhiya lillahi wamani ittabaʿani waqul lilladhīna ūtū l-kitāba wal-umiyīna a-aslamtum fa-in aslamū faqadi ih'tadaw wa-in tawallaw fa-innamā ʿalayka l-balāghu wal-lahu baṣīrun bil-ʿibādi But if they dispute with thee (O' Our apostle Muhammad!) then say, "I have submitted myself (wholly) to God and (so) doeth everyone who followeth me and say (Ask.) to those who have been given the Book and the unlettered (ones') (Applicable to all those who follow not any heavenly scripture.) "have ye (too) submitted;"? If they submit (themselves to God) then indeed they are rightly guided, and if they turn away, then upon thee is only the delivery (of the message) (Islam.) ', and verily, God is…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:21 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْفُرُونَ بِءَايَاتِ اللَّهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ النَّبِيِّينَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ وَيَقْتُلُونَ الَّذِينَ يَأْمُرُونَ بِالْقِسْطِ مِنَ النَّاسِ فَبَشِّرْهُمْ بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ inna alladhīna yakfurūna biāyāti l-lahi wayaqtulūna l-nabiyīna bighayri ḥaqqin wayaqtulūna alladhīna yamurūna bil-qis'ṭi mina l-nāsi fabashir'hum biʿadhābin alīmin Those who defy Allah's signs and kill the prophets unjustly,1 and kill those who call for justice from among the people, inform them of a painful punishment.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:21 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْفُرُونَ بِءَايَاتِ اللَّهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ النَّبِيِّينَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ وَيَقْتُلُونَ الَّذِينَ يَأْمُرُونَ بِالْقِسْطِ مِنَ النَّاسِ فَبَشِّرْهُمْ بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ inna alladhīna yakfurūna biāyāti l-lahi wayaqtulūna l-nabiyīna bighayri ḥaqqin wayaqtulūna alladhīna yamurūna bil-qis'ṭi mina l-nāsi fabashir'hum biʿadhābin alīmin Those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right and kill those who order justice from among the people - give them tidings of a painful punishment. Verily, those who disbelieve in the Ayat of Allah and kill the Prophets without right, and kill those men who order just dealings, then announce to them a painful torment (3:21). They are those whose works will be lost in this world and in the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers (3:22). Chastising the Jews for Their Disbelief and for Killing the Prophets and Righteous People This Ayah chastises the People…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:21 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْفُرُونَ بِءَايَاتِ اللَّهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ النَّبِيِّينَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ وَيَقْتُلُونَ الَّذِينَ يَأْمُرُونَ بِالْقِسْطِ مِنَ النَّاسِ فَبَشِّرْهُمْ بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ inna alladhīna yakfurūna biāyāti l-lahi wayaqtulūna l-nabiyīna bighayri ḥaqqin wayaqtulūna alladhīna yamurūna bil-qis'ṭi mina l-nāsi fabashir'hum biʿadhābin alīmin Verily (Refer to Verses. 2:61 and 3:111.) to those who deny the signs of God, and unjustly slay the apostles, and slay (Applicable to the assassins and their persecutors of the Holy Imams of the Ahl Al-Bayt the successors to the Last Apostle of God The Holy Prophet.) those among men who enjoin justice, give tidings to them of a painful chastisement Reference to the Jews who were notorious for slaying apostles of God and the righteous ones1 which they themselves admit2. The reference here seems to point out the Jewish plans to kill the Holy Prophet. "And say, If we had been in…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:22 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اُولٰٓئِكَ الَّذِينَ حَبِطَتْ أَعْمَالُهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْءَاخِرَةِ وَمَا لَهُمْ مِنْ نَاصِرِينَ ulāika alladhīna ḥabiṭat aʿmāluhum fī l-dun'yā wal-ākhirati wamā lahum min nāṣirīna They are the ones whose works have failed in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:22 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اُولٰٓئِكَ الَّذِينَ حَبِطَتْ أَعْمَالُهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْءَاخِرَةِ وَمَا لَهُمْ مِنْ نَاصِرِينَ ulāika alladhīna ḥabiṭat aʿmāluhum fī l-dun'yā wal-ākhirati wamā lahum min nāṣirīna They are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and for them there will be no helpers. See 3:21

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:22 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اُولٰٓئِكَ الَّذِينَ حَبِطَتْ أَعْمَالُهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْءَاخِرَةِ وَمَا لَهُمْ مِنْ نَاصِرِينَ ulāika alladhīna ḥabiṭat aʿmāluhum fī l-dun'yā wal-ākhirati wamā lahum min nāṣirīna These are they whose works come to naught in this world and in the next; and for them there shall not be any helper It is a prophetic declaration consisting also of admonition, meaning all their plans in this world will be frustrated and all their good deeds, if there be any, will be of no avail in the life after death and on the Day of Requital. Good deeds of righteousness of anyone, be he a believer or an unbeliever, will never go without the due recompense, both in the present life and in the hereafter. The reward may be possible in case of unbelief or disbelief owing to ignorance or indolence. But those who deliberately hated…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:23 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوْۤا نَصِيبًا مِنَ الْكِتَابِ يُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى كِتَابِ اللَّهِ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهُمْ ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّى فَرِيقٌ مِنْهُمْ وَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ alam tara ilā alladhīna ūtū naṣīban mina l-kitābi yud'ʿawna ilā kitābi l-lahi liyaḥkuma baynahum thumma yatawallā farīqun min'hum wahum muʿ'riḍūna Have you not regarded those who were given a share of the Book, who are summoned to the Book of Allah in order that it may judge between them, whereat a part of them refuse to comply and they are disregardful?

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:23 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوْۤا نَصِيبًا مِنَ الْكِتَابِ يُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى كِتَابِ اللَّهِ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهُمْ ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّى فَرِيقٌ مِنْهُمْ وَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ alam tara ilā alladhīna ūtū naṣīban mina l-kitābi yud'ʿawna ilā kitābi l-lahi liyaḥkuma baynahum thumma yatawallā farīqun min'hum wahum muʿ'riḍūna Do you not consider, (O Muḥammad), those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They are invited to the Scripture of Allah that it should arbitrate between them;1 then a party of them turns away, and they are refusing. Have you not seen those who have been given a portion of the Scripture? They are being invited to the Book of Allah to settle their dispute, then a party of them turned away, and they are averse (3:23). This is because they say: "The Fire shall not touch us but for a number of days." And that which they…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:23 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوْۤا نَصِيبًا مِنَ الْكِتَابِ يُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى كِتَابِ اللَّهِ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهُمْ ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّى فَرِيقٌ مِنْهُمْ وَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ alam tara ilā alladhīna ūtū naṣīban mina l-kitābi yud'ʿawna ilā kitābi l-lahi liyaḥkuma baynahum thumma yatawallā farīqun min'hum wahum muʿ'riḍūna Hast thou not (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) (Considered.) seen those (the Jews) who have been given a portion (Rut. John 16/5-14.) of the Book, when they are summoned unto the Book of God that it may judge between them, then a faction of them turn back while they are those who withdraw (Withdraw i.e. arrogantly persist on infidelity.) A portion of the Book, God's revelation of His will regarding disciplining the human soul to qualify it for higher levels of spirituality, through all the ages, is "The Book" The Law of Moses and the Evangel of Jesus were only portions…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:24 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ذٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُوْا لَنْ تَمَسَّنَا النَّارُ إِلَّا أَيَّامًا مَعْدُودَاتٍ وَغَرَّهُمْ فِي دِينِهِمْ مَا كَانُوْۤا يَفْتَرُونَ dhālika bi-annahum qālū lan tamassanā l-nāru illā ayyāman maʿdūdātin wagharrahum fī dīnihim mā kānū yaftarūna That is because they say, 'The Fire shall not touch us except for a number of days,' and they have been misled in their religion by what they used to fabricate.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:24 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ذٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُوْا لَنْ تَمَسَّنَا النَّارُ إِلَّا أَيَّامًا مَعْدُودَاتٍ وَغَرَّهُمْ فِي دِينِهِمْ مَا كَانُوْۤا يَفْتَرُونَ dhālika bi-annahum qālū lan tamassanā l-nāru illā ayyāman maʿdūdātin wagharrahum fī dīnihim mā kānū yaftarūna That is because they say, "Never will the Fire touch us except for (a few) numbered days," and (because) they were deluded in their religion by what they were inventing. See 3:23

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:24 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ذٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُوْا لَنْ تَمَسَّنَا النَّارُ إِلَّا أَيَّامًا مَعْدُودَاتٍ وَغَرَّهُمْ فِي دِينِهِمْ مَا كَانُوْۤا يَفْتَرُونَ dhālika bi-annahum qālū lan tamassanā l-nāru illā ayyāman maʿdūdātin wagharrahum fī dīnihim mā kānū yaftarūna This, because they say "The (Hell) fire shall by no means touch us but for (some) numbered (Counted.) days, and deceiveth them in the matter of their religion what they have forged (Applicable to the modern days irreligious arrogants and their conjectures.)" In continuation of the same line of argument, the verse condemns the people of the Book who seek judicial favour other than what is established by the scripture. The mental background for this rebellious tendency of the people of the Book, is the fanciful belief that the ultimate salvation rests in the mere declaration of the faith, for misdeeds and wrong actions, if there be any punishment, it…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:25 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَكَيْفَ إِذَا جَمَعْنَاهُمْ لِيَوْمٍ لَا رَيْبَ فِیْهِ وَوُفِّيَتْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَا كَسَبَتْ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ fakayfa idhā jamaʿnāhum liyawmin lā rayba fīhi wawuffiyat kullu nafsin mā kasabat wahum lā yuẓ'lamūna But how will it be [with them] when We gather them on a day in which there is no doubt, and every soul shall be recompensed fully for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged?

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:25 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَكَيْفَ إِذَا جَمَعْنَاهُمْ لِيَوْمٍ لَا رَيْبَ فِیْهِ وَوُفِّيَتْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَا كَسَبَتْ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ fakayfa idhā jamaʿnāhum liyawmin lā rayba fīhi wawuffiyat kullu nafsin mā kasabat wahum lā yuẓ'lamūna So how will it be when We assemble them for a Day about which there is no doubt? And each soul will be compensated (in full for) what it earned, and they will not be wronged. See 3:23

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:25 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَكَيْفَ إِذَا جَمَعْنَاهُمْ لِيَوْمٍ لَا رَيْبَ فِیْهِ وَوُفِّيَتْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَا كَسَبَتْ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ fakayfa idhā jamaʿnāhum liyawmin lā rayba fīhi wawuffiyat kullu nafsin mā kasabat wahum lā yuẓ'lamūna How then (will it be with them) when We shall gather them together for the Day (of Judgment) about which there is no doubt; and every soul shall be paid in full (Fully repaid according to the merit and the demerit of one's own faith and deeds.) that which it hath earned, and they shall not be wronged? Everyone, be he a believer or disbeliever, shall be recompensed for whatever one has wrought in the present life1. This proves that a believer shall not be convicted to hell for all times for the reward for his true faith in God, he can never have in the hell or before it.…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:26 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ مَالِكَ الْمُلْكِ تُؤْتِي الْمُلْكَ مَنْ تَشَاءُ وَتَنْزِعُ الْمُلْكَ مِمَّنْ تَشَاءُ وَتُعِزُّ مَنْ تَشَاءُ وَتُذِلُّ مَنْ تَشَاءُ بِيَدِكَ الْخَيْرُ إِنَّكَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ quli l-lahuma mālika l-mul'ki tu'tī l-mul'ka man tashāu watanziʿu l-mul'ka mimman tashāu watuʿizzu man tashāu watudhillu man tashāu biyadika l-khayru innaka ʿalā kulli shayin qadīrun Say, 'O Allah, Master of all sovereignty! You give sovereignty to whomever You wish, and strip of sovereignty whomever You wish; You make mighty whomever You wish, and You abase whomever You wish; all good is in Your hand. Indeed You have power over all things.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:26 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ مَالِكَ الْمُلْكِ تُؤْتِي الْمُلْكَ مَنْ تَشَاءُ وَتَنْزِعُ الْمُلْكَ مِمَّنْ تَشَاءُ وَتُعِزُّ مَنْ تَشَاءُ وَتُذِلُّ مَنْ تَشَاءُ بِيَدِكَ الْخَيْرُ إِنَّكَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ quli l-lahuma mālika l-mul'ki tu'tī l-mul'ka man tashāu watanziʿu l-mul'ka mimman tashāu watuʿizzu man tashāu watudhillu man tashāu biyadika l-khayru innaka ʿalā kulli shayin qadīrun Say, "O Allah, Owner of Sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty away from whom You will. You honor whom You will and You humble whom You will. In Your hand1 is (all) good. Indeed, You are over all things competent. Say: O Allah! Possessor of the power, You give power to whom You will, and You take power from whom You will, and You endue with honor whom You will, and You humiliate whom You will. In Your Hand is the good. Verily, You…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:26 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ مَالِكَ الْمُلْكِ تُؤْتِي الْمُلْكَ مَنْ تَشَاءُ وَتَنْزِعُ الْمُلْكَ مِمَّنْ تَشَاءُ وَتُعِزُّ مَنْ تَشَاءُ وَتُذِلُّ مَنْ تَشَاءُ بِيَدِكَ الْخَيْرُ إِنَّكَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ quli l-lahuma mālika l-mul'ki tu'tī l-mul'ka man tashāu watanziʿu l-mul'ka mimman tashāu watuʿizzu man tashāu watudhillu man tashāu biyadika l-khayru innaka ʿalā kulli shayin qadīrun Say (O' Apostle Muhammad!) "O' God! Master of the Kingdom, Thou givest the kingdom (Refer to: 2:269, 2:258, 3:73.) unto whomsoever Thou likest and takest away the kingdom from whomsoever Thou likest! Thou exaltest whomsoever Thou likest and abasest whomsoever Thou likest; in Thine hands is all good; verily Thou art over all things Mighty" As already pointed out from the beginning of this sura, the Quranic aim is to make man in his thinking, alive to the fact that God is the sole and the ultimate authority in both…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:27 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: تُولِجُ اللَّيْلَ فِي النَّهَارِ وَتُولِجُ النَّهَارَ فِي اللَّيْلِ وَتُخْرِجُ الْحَيَّ مِنَ الْمَيِّتِ وَتُخْرِجُ الْمَيِّتَ مِنَ الْحَيِّ وَتَرْزُقُ مَنْ تَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ tūliju al-layla fī l-nahāri watūliju l-nahāra fī al-layli watukh'riju l-ḥaya mina l-mayiti watukh'riju l-mayita mina l-ḥayi watarzuqu man tashāu bighayri ḥisābin You make the night pass into the day and You make the day pass into the night. You bring forth the living from the dead and You bring forth the dead from the living, and You provide for whomever You wish without any reckoning.'

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:27 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: تُولِجُ اللَّيْلَ فِي النَّهَارِ وَتُولِجُ النَّهَارَ فِي اللَّيْلِ وَتُخْرِجُ الْحَيَّ مِنَ الْمَيِّتِ وَتُخْرِجُ الْمَيِّتَ مِنَ الْحَيِّ وَتَرْزُقُ مَنْ تَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ tūliju al-layla fī l-nahāri watūliju l-nahāra fī al-layli watukh'riju l-ḥaya mina l-mayiti watukh'riju l-mayita mina l-ḥayi watarzuqu man tashāu bighayri ḥisābin You cause the night to enter the day, and You cause the day to enter the night; and You bring the living out of the dead, and You bring the dead out of the living. And You give provision to whom You will without account (i.e., limit or measure)." See 3:26

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:27 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: تُولِجُ اللَّيْلَ فِي النَّهَارِ وَتُولِجُ النَّهَارَ فِي اللَّيْلِ وَتُخْرِجُ الْحَيَّ مِنَ الْمَيِّتِ وَتُخْرِجُ الْمَيِّتَ مِنَ الْحَيِّ وَتَرْزُقُ مَنْ تَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ tūliju al-layla fī l-nahāri watūliju l-nahāra fī al-layli watukh'riju l-ḥaya mina l-mayiti watukh'riju l-mayita mina l-ḥayi watarzuqu man tashāu bighayri ḥisābin Thou causest the night to pass into the day, and Thou causest the day to pass into the night, Thou bringest forth the living out of the dead, and Thou bringest forth the dead out of the living, and Thou givest sustenance to whomsoever Thou likest, without measure These verses aim at preparing the hearts of the Muslims, the sincere believers in God's Omnipotence and His most supreme authority, by inculcating in them the conviction that God and God alone can do and undo things, conceivable and inconceivable by any human mind, and thus create complete resignation to…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:28 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا يَتَّخِذِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذٰلِكَ فَلَيْسَ مِنَ اللَّهِ فِي شَيْءٍ إِلَّا أَنْ تَتَّقُوْۤا مِنْهُمْ تُقَاةً وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ وَإِلَى اللَّهِ الْمَصِيرُ lā yattakhidhi l-mu'minūna l-kāfirīna awliyāa min dūni l-mu'minīna waman yafʿal dhālika falaysa mina l-lahi fī shayin illā an tattaqū min'hum tuqātan wayuḥadhirukumu l-lahu nafsahu wa-ilā l-lahi l-maṣīru The faithful should not take the faithless for allies instead of the faithful, and whoever does that Allah will have nothing to do with him, except when you are wary of them out of caution. Allah warns you to beware of [disobeying] Him, and toward Allah is the return.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:28 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا يَتَّخِذِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذٰلِكَ فَلَيْسَ مِنَ اللَّهِ فِي شَيْءٍ إِلَّا أَنْ تَتَّقُوْۤا مِنْهُمْ تُقَاةً وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ وَإِلَى اللَّهِ الْمَصِيرُ lā yattakhidhi l-mu'minūna l-kāfirīna awliyāa min dūni l-mu'minīna waman yafʿal dhālika falaysa mina l-lahi fī shayin illā an tattaqū min'hum tuqātan wayuḥadhirukumu l-lahu nafsahu wa-ilā l-lahi l-maṣīru Let not believers take disbelievers as allies (i.e., supporters or protectors) rather than believers. And whoever (of you) does that has nothing (i.e., no association) with Allah, except when taking precaution against them in prudence.1 And Allah warns you of Himself, and to Allah is the (final) destination. Let not the believers take the disbelievers as friends instead of the believers, and whoever does that, will never be helped by Allah in any way, unless you indeed fear a danger from them. And Allah warns you…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:28 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا يَتَّخِذِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذٰلِكَ فَلَيْسَ مِنَ اللَّهِ فِي شَيْءٍ إِلَّا أَنْ تَتَّقُوْۤا مِنْهُمْ تُقَاةً وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ وَإِلَى اللَّهِ الْمَصِيرُ lā yattakhidhi l-mu'minūna l-kāfirīna awliyāa min dūni l-mu'minīna waman yafʿal dhālika falaysa mina l-lahi fī shayin illā an tattaqū min'hum tuqātan wayuḥadhirukumu l-lahu nafsahu wa-ilā l-lahi l-maṣīru Let (Refer to: 16:106.) not the believers take the disbelievers as their friends (Verse 29, referring to Prophet Muhammad (S).) rather than the believers, whoso shall do then nothing (A guidance and grace.) of God is his, except (when) ye (have to) guard yourselves against (them) for fear from them (The principal underlaying taqiyyah.) ; but cautioneth (Hence hiding the faith at heart under the sanction of Verse 29 is not objectionable for God knoweth what is at heart and what is expressed.) you of Himself;…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:29 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ إِنْ تُخْفُوْۤا مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمْ أَوْ تُبْدُوهُ يَعْلَمْهُ اللَّهُ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ qul in tukh'fū mā fī ṣudūrikum aw tub'dūhu yaʿlamhu l-lahu wayaʿlamu mā fī l-samāwāti wamā fī l-arḍi wal-lahu ʿalā kulli shayin qadīrun Say, 'Whether you hide what is in your hearts, or disclose it, Allah knows it, and He knows whatever there is in the heavens and whatever there is in the earth; and Allah has power over all things.'

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:29 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ إِنْ تُخْفُوْۤا مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمْ أَوْ تُبْدُوهُ يَعْلَمْهُ اللَّهُ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ qul in tukh'fū mā fī ṣudūrikum aw tub'dūhu yaʿlamhu l-lahu wayaʿlamu mā fī l-samāwāti wamā fī l-arḍi wal-lahu ʿalā kulli shayin qadīrun Say, "Whether you conceal what is in your breasts or reveal it, Allah knows it. And He knows that which is in the heavens and that which is on the earth. And Allah is over all things competent. Say: Whether you hide what is in your breasts or reveal it, Allah knows it, and He knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth. And Allah is able to do all things (3:29). On the Day when every person will be confronted with the good he has done, and all the evil he…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:29 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ إِنْ تُخْفُوْۤا مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمْ أَوْ تُبْدُوهُ يَعْلَمْهُ اللَّهُ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ qul in tukh'fū mā fī ṣudūrikum aw tub'dūhu yaʿlamhu l-lahu wayaʿlamu mā fī l-samāwāti wamā fī l-arḍi wal-lahu ʿalā kulli shayin qadīrun Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) whether ye conceal what is in your hearts or manifest it, God knoweth it; and knoweth He all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth; and verily God hath power over all things It is for everyone to beware that nothing is hidden from the All-Knowing Lord. All the actions and droughts of everyone, hidden as well the manifest, are equally known to God. No thought or action can ever be concealed from the knowledge of God.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:30 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ تَجِدُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَا عَمِلَتْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ مُحْضَرًا وَمَا عَمِلَتْ مِنْ سُوءٍ تَوَدُّ لَوْ أَنَّ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَهُ أَمَدًا بَعِيدًا وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ وَاللَّهُ رَءُوفٌ بِالْعِبَادِ yawma tajidu kullu nafsin mā ʿamilat min khayrin muḥ'ḍaran wamā ʿamilat min sūin tawaddu law anna baynahā wabaynahu amadan baʿīdan wayuḥadhirukumu l-lahu nafsahu wal-lahu raūfun bil-ʿibādi The day when every soul will find present whatever good it has done; and as to whatever evil it has done it will wish there were a far distance between it and itself. Allah warns you to beware of [disobeying] Him, and Allah is most kind to [His] servants.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:30 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ تَجِدُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَا عَمِلَتْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ مُحْضَرًا وَمَا عَمِلَتْ مِنْ سُوءٍ تَوَدُّ لَوْ أَنَّ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَهُ أَمَدًا بَعِيدًا وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ وَاللَّهُ رَءُوفٌ بِالْعِبَادِ yawma tajidu kullu nafsin mā ʿamilat min khayrin muḥ'ḍaran wamā ʿamilat min sūin tawaddu law anna baynahā wabaynahu amadan baʿīdan wayuḥadhirukumu l-lahu nafsahu wal-lahu raūfun bil-ʿibādi The Day every soul will find what it has done of good present (before it) and what it has done of evil, it will wish that between itself and that (evil) was a great distance. And Allah warns you of Himself, and Allah is Kind to (His) servants." See 3:29

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:30 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ تَجِدُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَا عَمِلَتْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ مُحْضَرًا وَمَا عَمِلَتْ مِنْ سُوءٍ تَوَدُّ لَوْ أَنَّ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَهُ أَمَدًا بَعِيدًا وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ وَاللَّهُ رَءُوفٌ بِالْعِبَادِ yawma tajidu kullu nafsin mā ʿamilat min khayrin muḥ'ḍaran wamā ʿamilat min sūin tawaddu law anna baynahā wabaynahu amadan baʿīdan wayuḥadhirukumu l-lahu nafsahu wal-lahu raūfun bil-ʿibādi (Remember) (Or "On".) the (Refer to 2:281.) Day (of Judgment) when every soul shall find present whatever it hath wrought of good; and whatever it hath wrought of evil; it will wish that wide were the interval (Distance.) between it (Evil.) , and himself; But God cautioneth (Refer to: Verse 28.) you of Himself; and God is affectionate to His (faithful) servants Man's wish would be that by repentance he had cast away his sins long, long ago and they should have gone into oblivion. Cautioning man against…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:31 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تُحِبُّونَ اللَّهَ فَاتَّبِعُونِي يُحْبِبْكُمُ اللَّهُ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ qul in kuntum tuḥibbūna l-laha fa-ittabiʿūnī yuḥ'bib'kumu l-lahu wayaghfir lakum dhunūbakum wal-lahu ghafūrun raḥīmun Say, 'If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins, and Allah is all-forgiving, all-merciful.'

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:31 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تُحِبُّونَ اللَّهَ فَاتَّبِعُونِي يُحْبِبْكُمُ اللَّهُ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ qul in kuntum tuḥibbūna l-laha fa-ittabiʿūnī yuḥ'bib'kumu l-lahu wayaghfir lakum dhunūbakum wal-lahu ghafūrun raḥīmun Say, (O Muḥammad), "If you should love Allah, then follow me, (so) Allah will love you and forgive you your sins. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." Say (O Muhammad SAW to mankind): If you (really) love Allah, then follow me (i.e. Muhammad), Allah will love you and forgive you your sins. And Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful (3:31). Say: "Obey Allah and the Messenger." But if they turn away, then Allah does not like the disbelievers (3:32). Allah's Love is Attained by Following the Messenger SAW This honorable Ayah judges against those who claim to love Allah, yet do not follow the way of Muhammad SAW. Such people are not true…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:31 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تُحِبُّونَ اللَّهَ فَاتَّبِعُونِي يُحْبِبْكُمُ اللَّهُ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ qul in kuntum tuḥibbūna l-laha fa-ittabiʿūnī yuḥ'bib'kumu l-lahu wayaghfir lakum dhunūbakum wal-lahu ghafūrun raḥīmun Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "If ye do love God, then follow (Following the Holy Prophet is loving God and earning God's love and His pardon for the Sins, Following the Holy Prophet in his love of those whom he loved, is loving God and enmity with them is the enmity of God.) me (The Holy Prophet.) , God will love you and forgive you your sins; Verily, God is Forgiving, Merciful" Love of God has to be proved by the faithful following of the Holy Prophet. Only when we follow the Holy Prophet, God will love us and forgive our sins. No amount of any claim to love of God in…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:32 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ أَطِيعُوْۤا اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الْكَافِرِينَ qul aṭīʿū l-laha wal-rasūla fa-in tawallaw fa-inna l-laha lā yuḥibbu l-kāfirīna Say, 'Obey Allah and the Apostle.' But if they turn away, indeed Allah does not like the faithless.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:32 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ أَطِيعُوْۤا اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الْكَافِرِينَ qul aṭīʿū l-laha wal-rasūla fa-in tawallaw fa-inna l-laha lā yuḥibbu l-kāfirīna Say, "Obey Allah and the Messenger. But if you turn away - then indeed, Allah does not like the disbelievers." See 3:31

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:32 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ أَطِيعُوْۤا اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الْكَافِرِينَ qul aṭīʿū l-laha wal-rasūla fa-in tawallaw fa-inna l-laha lā yuḥibbu l-kāfirīna Say (O' Qur Apostle Muhammad!) Obey God and the Apostle; but if they turn back, then verily God loveth not the disbelievers The address is to the Muslims. Disobedience or even reluctance to obey the Holy Prophet is referred to as infidelity, i.e., 'Kufr.'

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:33 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفَى اٰدَمَ وَنُوحًا وَءَالَ اِبْرَاهِیْمَ وَءَالَ عِمْرَانَ عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ inna l-laha iṣ'ṭafā ādama wanūḥan waāla ib'rāhīma waāla ʿim'rāna ʿalā l-ʿālamīna Indeed Allah chose Adam and Noah, and the progeny of Abraham and the progeny of Imran above all the nations;

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:33 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفَى اٰدَمَ وَنُوحًا وَءَالَ اِبْرَاهِیْمَ وَءَالَ عِمْرَانَ عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ inna l-laha iṣ'ṭafā ādama wanūḥan waāla ib'rāhīma waāla ʿim'rāna ʿalā l-ʿālamīna Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Nuh and the family of Ibrahim and the family of ʿImrān over the worlds. Allah chose Adam, Nuh, the family of Ibrahim and the family of 'Imran above the nations (3:33). Offspring, one of the other, and Allah is All-Hearer, All-Knower (3:34). The Chosen Ones Among the People of the Earth Allah states that He has chosen these households over the people of the earth. For instance, Allah chose Adam, created him with His Hand and blew life into him. Allah commanded the angels to prostrate before Adam, taught him the names of everything and allowed him to dwell in Paradise, but then sent him down from it out of His wisdom. Allah…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:33 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفَى اٰدَمَ وَنُوحًا وَءَالَ اِبْرَاهِیْمَ وَءَالَ عِمْرَانَ عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ inna l-laha iṣ'ṭafā ādama wanūḥan waāla ib'rāhīma waāla ʿim'rāna ʿalā l-ʿālamīna Verily, God did choose Adam and Noah and the descendants of Abraham and the descendants of Imran (Father of Moses.) above all the worlds In this verse Adam and Noah are mentioned alone, whereas Abraham and Imran are referred to in connection with their posterity. Perhaps the 'Aal' or the posterity of Adam and Noah, was not brought into the special reference because in the immediate issues of both Adam and Noah (i.e., the son of Adam, Cabel, and the notorious son of Noah) were among the worst sinners. Though there were in their posterity many apostles of God, but an indefinite or an unqualified mention of the common term 'Aal' meaning the issues or sons or the…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:34 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ذُرِّيَّةً بَعْضُهَا مِنْ بَعْضٍ وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِیْمٌ dhurriyyatan baʿḍuhā min baʿḍin wal-lahu samīʿun ʿalīmun some of them are descendants of the others, and Allah is all-hearing, all-knowing.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:34 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ذُرِّيَّةً بَعْضُهَا مِنْ بَعْضٍ وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِیْمٌ dhurriyyatan baʿḍuhā min baʿḍin wal-lahu samīʿun ʿalīmun Descendants, some of them from others. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing. See 3:33

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:34 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ذُرِّيَّةً بَعْضُهَا مِنْ بَعْضٍ وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِیْمٌ dhurriyyatan baʿḍuhā min baʿḍin wal-lahu samīʿun ʿalīmun Offspring, one from the other; and verily God is All-Hearing; All Knowing The fact pointed out here is that the choice of God has fallen not only upon the holy persons referred to in this verse but also upon their posterity. But the wording of the verse suggests the continuation of the divine choice of God, without any break or cessation, and such an aspect of the declaration is absent in the case of Adam and Noah whose names are mentioned as the recipients of the divine choice, for one of the sons of Adam, and the son of Noah, were the cursed ones. Adam's son Cabel having been an assassin of his own brother Abel, and Noah's son being an open unbeliever in God, thus…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:35 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ قَالَتِ امْرَأَتُ عِمْرَانَ رَبِّ اِنِّیْ نَذَرْتُ لَكَ مَا فِي بَطْنِي مُحَرَّرًا فَتَقَبَّلْ مِنِّي إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ idh qālati im'ra-atu ʿim'rāna rabbi innī nadhartu laka mā fī baṭnī muḥarraran fataqabbal minnī innaka anta l-samīʿu l-ʿalīmu When the wife of Imran said, 'My Lord, I dedicate to You what is in my belly, in consecration. Accept it from me; indeed You are the All-hearing, the All-knowing.'

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:35 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ قَالَتِ امْرَأَتُ عِمْرَانَ رَبِّ اِنِّیْ نَذَرْتُ لَكَ مَا فِي بَطْنِي مُحَرَّرًا فَتَقَبَّلْ مِنِّي إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ idh qālati im'ra-atu ʿim'rāna rabbi innī nadhartu laka mā fī baṭnī muḥarraran fataqabbal minnī innaka anta l-samīʿu l-ʿalīmu (Mention, O Muḥammad), when the wife of ʿImrān said, "My Lord, indeed I have pledged to You what is in my womb, consecrated (for Your service), so accept this from me. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing." (Remember) when the wife of 'Imran said: O my Lord! I have vowed to You what is in my womb to be dedicated for Your services, so accept this from me. Verily, You are the All-Hearer, the All-Knowing (3:35). Then when she gave birth to her, she said: "O my Lord! I have given birth to a female child, ـ and Allah knew better what she…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:35 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ قَالَتِ امْرَأَتُ عِمْرَانَ رَبِّ اِنِّیْ نَذَرْتُ لَكَ مَا فِي بَطْنِي مُحَرَّرًا فَتَقَبَّلْ مِنِّي إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ idh qālati im'ra-atu ʿim'rāna rabbi innī nadhartu laka mā fī baṭnī muḥarraran fataqabbal minnī innaka anta l-samīʿu l-ʿalīmu When said (Hanna) the wife of Imran (Father of Virgin Mary- not the father of Moses.) "My Lord! I have vowed unto Thee what is in my womb to be (dedicated) for Thee (exclusively for Thy service) freed (from all worldly responsibilities) therefore accept (it) from me; Verily Thou art the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing" Devotees to the temple in the Jewish creed, remained as recluses, cut off from worldly life and practised celibacy. Imran the father of Mary (the mother of Jesus) seems evidently to be of priestly descent. This factor is borne out from the vow which his wife makes about her issue…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:36 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا وَضَعَتْهَا قَالَتْ رَبِّ اِنِّیْ وَضَعْتُهَا أُنْثَى وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا وَضَعَتْ وَلَيْسَ الذَّكَرُ كَالْأُنْثَى وَإِنِّي سَمَّيْتُهَا مَرْيَمَ وَإِنِّي أُعِيذُهَا بِكَ وَذُرِّيَّتَهَا مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ falammā waḍaʿathā qālat rabbi innī waḍaʿtuhā unthā wal-lahu aʿlamu bimā waḍaʿat walaysa l-dhakaru kal-unthā wa-innī sammaytuhā maryama wa-innī uʿīdhuhā bika wadhurriyyatahā mina l-shayṭāni l-rajīmi And when she bore her,1 she said, 'My Lord, I have borne a female [child]' —and Allah knew better what she had borne— 'and the female is not like the male. I have named her Mary, and I commend her and her offspring to Your care against [the evil of] the outcast Satan.'

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:36 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا وَضَعَتْهَا قَالَتْ رَبِّ اِنِّیْ وَضَعْتُهَا أُنْثَى وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا وَضَعَتْ وَلَيْسَ الذَّكَرُ كَالْأُنْثَى وَإِنِّي سَمَّيْتُهَا مَرْيَمَ وَإِنِّي أُعِيذُهَا بِكَ وَذُرِّيَّتَهَا مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ falammā waḍaʿathā qālat rabbi innī waḍaʿtuhā unthā wal-lahu aʿlamu bimā waḍaʿat walaysa l-dhakaru kal-unthā wa-innī sammaytuhā maryama wa-innī uʿīdhuhā bika wadhurriyyatahā mina l-shayṭāni l-rajīmi But when she delivered her, she said, "My Lord, I have delivered a female." And Allah was most knowing of what she delivered, and the male is not like the female. "And I have named her Maryam, and I seek refuge for her in You and (for) her descendants from Satan, the expelled (from the mercy of Allah)." See 3:35

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:36 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا وَضَعَتْهَا قَالَتْ رَبِّ اِنِّیْ وَضَعْتُهَا أُنْثَى وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا وَضَعَتْ وَلَيْسَ الذَّكَرُ كَالْأُنْثَى وَإِنِّي سَمَّيْتُهَا مَرْيَمَ وَإِنِّي أُعِيذُهَا بِكَ وَذُرِّيَّتَهَا مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ falammā waḍaʿathā qālat rabbi innī waḍaʿtuhā unthā wal-lahu aʿlamu bimā waḍaʿat walaysa l-dhakaru kal-unthā wa-innī sammaytuhā maryama wa-innī uʿīdhuhā bika wadhurriyyatahā mina l-shayṭāni l-rajīmi And when she delivered her, she said "My Lord! I have delivered a female (Virgin Mary.) (child); and God knew best what she delivered; and the male is not like the female; and I have named it Mary (Virgin Mary, mother of Jesus.) and commend her to Thy protection and also her offspring from Satan the castaway (The accursed one of God.) (accursed)" It was a custom in the days of Mary that people used to dedicate one of their sons to the service of the temple at Jerusalem. Imran's wife, Lady…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:37 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَتَقَبَّلَهَا رَبُّهَا بِقَبُولٍ حَسَنٍ وَأَنْبَتَهَا نَبَاتًا حَسَنًا وَكَفَّلَهَا زَكَرِيَّا كُلَّمَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا زَكَرِيَّا الْمِحْرَابَ وَجَدَ عِنْدَهَا رِزْقًا قَالَ يَامَرْيَمُ أَنَّى لَكِ هَذَا قَالَتْ هُوَ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ fataqabbalahā rabbuhā biqabūlin ḥasanin wa-anbatahā nabātan ḥasanan wakaffalahā zakariyyā kullamā dakhala ʿalayhā zakariyyā l-miḥ'rāba wajada ʿindahā riz'qan qāla yāmaryamu annā laki hādhā qālat huwa min ʿindi l-lahi inna l-laha yarzuqu man yashāu bighayri ḥisābin Thereupon her Lord accepted her with a gracious acceptance, and made her grow up in a worthy fashion, and He charged Zechariah with her care. Whenever Zechariah visited her in the sanctuary, he would find provisions with her. He said, 'O Mary, from where does this come for you?' She said, 'It comes from Allah. Allah provides whomever He wishes without any reckoning.'

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:37 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَتَقَبَّلَهَا رَبُّهَا بِقَبُولٍ حَسَنٍ وَأَنْبَتَهَا نَبَاتًا حَسَنًا وَكَفَّلَهَا زَكَرِيَّا كُلَّمَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا زَكَرِيَّا الْمِحْرَابَ وَجَدَ عِنْدَهَا رِزْقًا قَالَ يَامَرْيَمُ أَنَّى لَكِ هَذَا قَالَتْ هُوَ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ fataqabbalahā rabbuhā biqabūlin ḥasanin wa-anbatahā nabātan ḥasanan wakaffalahā zakariyyā kullamā dakhala ʿalayhā zakariyyā l-miḥ'rāba wajada ʿindahā riz'qan qāla yāmaryamu annā laki hādhā qālat huwa min ʿindi l-lahi inna l-laha yarzuqu man yashāu bighayri ḥisābin So her Lord accepted her with good acceptance and caused her to grow in a good manner and put her in the care of Zakariyya. Every time Zakariyya entered upon her in the prayer chamber, he found with her provision. He said, "O Maryam, from where is this (coming) to you?" She said, "It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account." So her Lord (Allah) accepted her…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:37 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَتَقَبَّلَهَا رَبُّهَا بِقَبُولٍ حَسَنٍ وَأَنْبَتَهَا نَبَاتًا حَسَنًا وَكَفَّلَهَا زَكَرِيَّا كُلَّمَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا زَكَرِيَّا الْمِحْرَابَ وَجَدَ عِنْدَهَا رِزْقًا قَالَ يَامَرْيَمُ أَنَّى لَكِ هَذَا قَالَتْ هُوَ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ fataqabbalahā rabbuhā biqabūlin ḥasanin wa-anbatahā nabātan ḥasanan wakaffalahā zakariyyā kullamā dakhala ʿalayhā zakariyyā l-miḥ'rāba wajada ʿindahā riz'qan qāla yāmaryamu annā laki hādhā qālat huwa min ʿindi l-lahi inna l-laha yarzuqu man yashāu bighayri ḥisābin ''So accepted her Lord with a gracious acceptance and made her grow up a graceful growing and trusted her into the charge of Zachariah; Whenever Zachariah entered (to see) her in the Sanctuary, (he) found her with a sustenance; He said "O' Mary! whence (cometh) this to thee?"
