item.description: فَاسْتَجَابَ لَهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ أَنِّي لَا أُضِيعُ عَمَلَ عَامِلٍ مِنْكُمْ مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثَى بَعْضُكُمْ مِنْ بَعْضٍ فَالَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوْۤا وَأُخْرِجُوا مِنْ دِيَارِهِمْ وَأُوذُوْۤا فِي سَبِيلِي وَقَاتَلُوا وَقُتِلُوْۤا لَأُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ وَلَأُدْخِلَنَّهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ ثَوَابًا مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ حُسْنُ الثَّوَابِ fa-is'tajāba lahum rabbuhum annī lā uḍīʿu ʿamala ʿāmilin minkum min dhakarin aw unthā baʿḍukum min baʿḍin fa-alladhīna hājarū wa-ukh'rijū min diyārihim waūdhū fī sabīlī waqātalū waqutilū la-ukaffiranna ʿanhum sayyiātihim wala-ud'khilannahum jannātin tajrī min taḥtihā l-anhāru thawāban min ʿindi l-lahi wal-lahu ʿindahu ḥus'nu l-thawābi And their Lord responded to them, "Never will I allow to be lost the work of (any) worker among you, whether male or female; you are of one another. So those who emigrated or were evicted from their homes or were harmed in My cause or fought or were killed - I will surely…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:195 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَاسْتَجَابَ لَهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ أَنِّي لَا أُضِيعُ عَمَلَ عَامِلٍ مِنْكُمْ مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثَى بَعْضُكُمْ مِنْ بَعْضٍ فَالَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوْۤا وَأُخْرِجُوا مِنْ دِيَارِهِمْ وَأُوذُوْۤا فِي سَبِيلِي وَقَاتَلُوا وَقُتِلُوْۤا لَأُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ وَلَأُدْخِلَنَّهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ ثَوَابًا مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ حُسْنُ الثَّوَابِ fa-is'tajāba lahum rabbuhum annī lā uḍīʿu ʿamala ʿāmilin minkum min dhakarin aw unthā baʿḍukum min baʿḍin fa-alladhīna hājarū wa-ukh'rijū min diyārihim waūdhū fī sabīlī waqātalū waqutilū la-ukaffiranna ʿanhum sayyiātihim wala-ud'khilannahum jannātin tajrī min taḥtihā l-anhāru thawāban min ʿindi l-lahi wal-lahu ʿindahu ḥus'nu l-thawābi So their Lord did respond to them (saying) "I will not suffer the work of any of you that worketh to be lost, be he male or female (Men and Women equally rewardable and punishable for the good and the evil they do in this life.) , the one of you being from the…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:196 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا يَغُرَّنَّكَ تَقَلُّبُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا فِي الْبِلَادِ lā yaghurrannaka taqallubu alladhīna kafarū fī l-bilādi Never be misled by the bustle of the faithless in the towns.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:196 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا يَغُرَّنَّكَ تَقَلُّبُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا فِي الْبِلَادِ lā yaghurrannaka taqallubu alladhīna kafarū fī l-bilādi Be not deceived by the (uninhibited) movement of the disbelievers throughout the land. Let not the free disposal (and affluence) of the disbelievers throughout the land deceive you (3:196). A brief enjoyment; then their ultimate abode is Hell; and worst indeed is that place for rest (3:197). But, for those who have Taqwa of their Lord, are Gardens under which rivers flow (in Paradise); therein are they to dwell, an entertainment from Allah; and that which is with Allah is the best for Al-Abrar (the most righteous) (3:198). Warning Against Being Deceived by This Life; the Rewards of the Righteous Believers Allah said, do not look at the disbelievers, who are enjoying various delights and joys. Soon, they will loose all this and be tied to…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:196 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا يَغُرَّنَّكَ تَقَلُّبُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا فِي الْبِلَادِ lā yaghurrannaka taqallubu alladhīna kafarū fī l-bilādi Let not deceive (Enamour.) thee (Address to the Muslims i.e. those who follow thee.) the (prosperous) going about (In glamour and pride.) of those who disbelieve in the cities (The prosperous one in the cities. A warning sounded to the people through the Holy Prophet against getting misled by the prosperity of the disbelievers.) . See 3:195

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:197 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَتَاعٌ قَلِيلٌ ثُمَّ مَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَبِئْسَ الْمِهَادُ matāʿun qalīlun thumma mawāhum jahannamu wabi'sa l-mihādu It is a trivial enjoyment; then their refuge is hell, and it is an evil resting place.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:197 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَتَاعٌ قَلِيلٌ ثُمَّ مَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَبِئْسَ الْمِهَادُ matāʿun qalīlun thumma mawāhum jahannamu wabi'sa l-mihādu (It is but) a small enjoyment; then their (final) refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place. See 3:196

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:197 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَتَاعٌ قَلِيلٌ ثُمَّ مَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَبِئْسَ الْمِهَادُ matāʿun qalīlun thumma mawāhum jahannamu wabi'sa l-mihādu A brief enjoyment (it is)! Thereafter their abode is Hell and how bad the resting place (it is)! See 3:195

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:198 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَكِنِ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا رَبَّهُمْ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا نُزُلًا مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ وَمَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ لِلْأَبْرَارِ lākini alladhīna ittaqaw rabbahum lahum jannātun tajrī min taḥtihā l-anhāru khālidīna fīhā nuzulan min ʿindi l-lahi wamā ʿinda l-lahi khayrun lil'abrāri But those who are wary of their Lord —for them shall be gardens with streams running in them, to remain in them [forever], a hospitality from Allah; and what is with Allah is better for the pious.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:198 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَكِنِ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا رَبَّهُمْ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا نُزُلًا مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ وَمَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ لِلْأَبْرَارِ lākini alladhīna ittaqaw rabbahum lahum jannātun tajrī min taḥtihā l-anhāru khālidīna fīhā nuzulan min ʿindi l-lahi wamā ʿinda l-lahi khayrun lil'abrāri But those who feared their Lord will have gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding eternally therein, as accommodation from Allah. And that which is with Allah is best for the righteous. See 3:196

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:198 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَكِنِ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا رَبَّهُمْ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا نُزُلًا مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ وَمَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ لِلْأَبْرَارِ lākini alladhīna ittaqaw rabbahum lahum jannātun tajrī min taḥtihā l-anhāru khālidīna fīhā nuzulan min ʿindi l-lahi wamā ʿinda l-lahi khayrun lil'abrāri But as to those who fear (the wrath of) their Lord, for them are the gardens beneath which flow the rivers, therein shall they abide for ever. Such is their reception (Entertainment.) with God; and whatever is with God is the best for the righteous ones. See 3:195

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:199 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ لَمَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ خَاشِعِينَ لِلَّهِ لَا يَشْتَرُونَ بِءَايَاتِ اللَّهِ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا اُولٰٓئِكَ لَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ wa-inna min ahli l-kitābi laman yu'minu bil-lahi wamā unzila ilaykum wamā unzila ilayhim khāshiʿīna lillahi lā yashtarūna biāyāti l-lahi thamanan qalīlan ulāika lahum ajruhum ʿinda rabbihim inna l-laha sarīʿu l-ḥisābi Indeed among the People of the Book there are surely some who have faith in Allah, and in what has been sent down to you, and in what has been sent down to them. Humble toward Allah, they do not sell the signs of Allah for a paltry gain. They shall have their reward near their Lord; indeed Allah is swift at reckoning.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:199 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ لَمَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ خَاشِعِينَ لِلَّهِ لَا يَشْتَرُونَ بِءَايَاتِ اللَّهِ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا اُولٰٓئِكَ لَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ wa-inna min ahli l-kitābi laman yu'minu bil-lahi wamā unzila ilaykum wamā unzila ilayhim khāshiʿīna lillahi lā yashtarūna biāyāti l-lahi thamanan qalīlan ulāika lahum ajruhum ʿinda rabbihim inna l-laha sarīʿu l-ḥisābi And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah and what was revealed to you and what was revealed to them, (being) humbly submissive to Allah. They do not exchange the verses of Allah for a small price. Those will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is swift in account. And there are, certainly, among the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians), those who believe in Allah and in that which has…

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:199 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ لَمَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ خَاشِعِينَ لِلَّهِ لَا يَشْتَرُونَ بِءَايَاتِ اللَّهِ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا اُولٰٓئِكَ لَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ wa-inna min ahli l-kitābi laman yu'minu bil-lahi wamā unzila ilaykum wamā unzila ilayhim khāshiʿīna lillahi lā yashtarūna biāyāti l-lahi thamanan qalīlan ulāika lahum ajruhum ʿinda rabbihim inna l-laha sarīʿu l-ḥisābi And Verily among the people of the Book are those who believe in God, and in what (The Holy Qur'an.) hath been sent down unto you and in what hath been sent down unto them, humbling (Ar. 'Khusho'.) themselves before God, They sell not the signs of God for a mean price; These! for them is their recompense with their Lord; aye! God is quick in reckoning. See 3:195

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:200 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا اصْبِرُوْۤا وَصَابِرُوا وَرَابِطُوا وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ yāayyuhā alladhīna āmanū iṣ'birū waṣābirū warābiṭū wa-ittaqū l-laha laʿallakum tuf'liḥūna O you who have faith! Be patient, stand firm, and close [your] ranks, and be wary of Allah so that you may be felicitous.

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:200 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا اصْبِرُوْۤا وَصَابِرُوا وَرَابِطُوا وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ yāayyuhā alladhīna āmanū iṣ'birū waṣābirū warābiṭū wa-ittaqū l-laha laʿallakum tuf'liḥūna O you who have believed, persevere1 and endure2 and remain stationed3 and fear Allah that you may be successful. See 3:199

item.title: Aal-i-Imraan:200 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا اصْبِرُوْۤا وَصَابِرُوا وَرَابِطُوا وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ yāayyuhā alladhīna āmanū iṣ'birū waṣābirū warābiṭū wa-ittaqū l-laha laʿallakum tuf'liḥūna O' ye who believe! be patient and vie (Excel each other in patience.) with, in endurance and be ever-garrisoned (To be ever ready to defend against any surprise attack from the enemy (the disbelievers). Ar. 'Rabita'- To participate in garrisoning the Muslim frontiers against the possible attack from the disbelievers-A duty of 'Jehad' commended - This could be done by turns- The minimum period of stay for each Muslim is three days and the maximum forty days. This indicates the state of risk and the danger in which the early Muslims were.) ; and fear (the wrath of) God, that ye may be successful. The concluding Verse of this chapter gives out the keynotes to the success of the journey…

item.title: Abasa:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّى ʿabasa watawallā He frowned and turned away

item.title: Abasa:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّى ʿabasa watawallā He (i.e., the Prophet SAW ) frowned and turned away. كِرَامٍ بَرَرَةٍ Honorable and obedient. Meaning: they are noble, handsome, and honorable in their creation. Their character and their deeds are righteous, pure and perfect. Here it should be noted that it is necessary for one who carries the Qur'an (i.e., the angel) to be following righteousness and guidance. Imam Ahmad recorded from Aisha that the Messenger of Allah SAW said: الَّذِي يَقْرَأُ الْقُرْآنَ وَهُوَ مَاهِرٌ بِهِ، مَعَ السَّفَرَةِ الْكِرَامِ الْبَرَرَةِ، وَالَّذِي يَقْرَؤُهُ وَهُوَ عَلَيْهِ شَاقٌّ، لَهُ أَجْرَانِ He who recites the Qur'an proficiently, will be with the noble, righteous, ambassador angels, and the one who recites it with difficulty will receive two rewards. This Hadith was reported by the group.

item.title: Abasa:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّى ʿabasa watawallā He frowned and he turned away The occasion for the revelation of this chapter was a historic incident which took place. Once the Holy Prophet was with some chieftains of the Quraish when Abdullah Ibn-Maktoom who was blind and was one of the intimate companions of the Holy Prophet came to the Holy Prophet. The Holy Prophet received him with honour and pleasure and gave him the place closest to him. Since Abdullah was poor and blind, the chieftains of the Quraish looked down upon him, and did not like the honour done and the place given to him by the Holy Prophet in their own presence and one of them frowned at Abdullah and sat turning his back to him. This displeased God, and Gabriel brought this Surah and revealed it to the Holy Prophet…

item.title: Abasa:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنْ جَاءَهُ الْأَعْمَى an jāahu l-aʿmā when the blind man approached him.

item.title: Abasa:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنْ جَاءَهُ الْأَعْمَى an jāahu l-aʿmā Because there came to him the blind man,1 (interrupting). See 80:1

item.title: Abasa:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنْ جَاءَهُ الْأَعْمَى an jāahu l-aʿmā Because came unto him the blind man The blind man is the reference to Abdullah Ibn Maktoom. Note the address is to the second person, i.e., to the Holy Prophet, but it is meant for the companion.

item.title: Abasa:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّهُ يَزَّكَّى wamā yud'rīka laʿallahu yazzakkā And how do you know, maybe he would purify himself,

item.title: Abasa:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّهُ يَزَّكَّى wamā yud'rīka laʿallahu yazzakkā But what would make you perceive, (O Muḥammad), that perhaps he might be purified.1 See 80:1

item.title: Abasa:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّهُ يَزَّكَّى wamā yud'rīka laʿallahu yazzakkā And what maketh thee to know that he would cleanse himself The questioning in this verse clearly indicates that the doubt about Abdullah being benefited by the talk with the Holy Prophet or not, could have been in the mind of one who had not yet embraced the faith, and which could never have occurred to an Apostle of God who has been sent to preach the faith to one and all, irrespective of any worldly position of the people. The questioning clearly indicates that the addressee was someone other than the Holy Prophet. The factor which this verse wants to preach, i.e., no spiritual value should be assigned to material wealth and the prospects of guidance being effective or not, should not be measured by any one's economic position in life…

item.title: Abasa:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوْ يَذَّكَّرُ فَتَنْفَعَهُ الذِّكْرٰی aw yadhakkaru fatanfaʿahu l-dhik'rā or take admonition, and the admonition would benefit him!

item.title: Abasa:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوْ يَذَّكَّرُ فَتَنْفَعَهُ الذِّكْرٰی aw yadhakkaru fatanfaʿahu l-dhik'rā Or be reminded and the remembrance would benefit him? See 80:1

item.title: Abasa:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوْ يَذَّكَّرُ فَتَنْفَعَهُ الذِّكْرٰی aw yadhakkaru fatanfaʿahu l-dhik'rā Or he warned, and profiteth him the warning? What is wanted to acquire knowledge is the will to learn. This essential urge in any poor man, may help him to grow more in spiritual excellence than the arrogant self-exalting wealthy one puffed up of his riches and position.

item.title: Abasa:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَمَّا مَنِ اسْتَغْنَى ammā mani is'taghnā But as for someone who is self-complacent,

item.title: Abasa:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَمَّا مَنِ اسْتَغْنَى ammā mani is'taghnā As for he who thinks himself without need.1 See 80:1

item.title: Abasa:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَمَّا مَنِ اسْتَغْنَى ammā mani is'taghnā As for him who thinketh himself independent (on account of his wealth) It is the poor who by nature or necessity, turn to God and become godly to earn His grace and mercy which they need very badly. The arrogant wealthy ones in their self-sufficiency always rebel against the laws of God and transgress the prescribed limits and if they ever join the ranks of faithful, it would be only when it profits them and gives them an advantageous position in their life and society or for the promotion of their worldly interest. Faith needs humility and naturally goes with meekness and the humble.

item.title: Abasa:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَنْتَ لَهُ تَصَدَّى fa-anta lahu taṣaddā you attend to him,

item.title: Abasa:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَنْتَ لَهُ تَصَدَّى fa-anta lahu taṣaddā To him you give attention. See 80:1

item.title: Abasa:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَنْتَ لَهُ تَصَدَّى fa-anta lahu taṣaddā Unto him dost thou attend The divine will is opposed to any attention paid to such arrogant one who looked down at Abdullah Ibn-Maktoom for his poverty and being blind and helpless.

item.title: Abasa:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا عَلَيْكَ أَلَّا يَزَّكَّى wamā ʿalayka allā yazzakkā though you are not liable if he does not purify himself.

item.title: Abasa:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا عَلَيْكَ أَلَّا يَزَّكَّى wamā ʿalayka allā yazzakkā And not upon you (is any blame) if he will not be purified.1 See 80:1

item.title: Abasa:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا عَلَيْكَ أَلَّا يَزَّكَّى wamā ʿalayka allā yazzakkā It shall be no blame on thee if cleansed not himself It was not the concern of anyone if the poor man did not benefit himself by the preachings of the Holy Prophet.

item.title: Abasa:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا مَنْ جَاءَكَ يَسْعَى wa-ammā man jāaka yasʿā But he who comes hurrying to you,

item.title: Abasa:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا مَنْ جَاءَكَ يَسْعَى wa-ammā man jāaka yasʿā But as for he who came to you striving (for knowledge). See 80:1

item.title: Abasa:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا مَنْ جَاءَكَ يَسْعَى wa-ammā man jāaka yasʿā But as to him (Abdullah ibn Makhtoom.) who cometh unto thee striving in earnest The reference is to Abdullah Ibn-Maktoom.

item.title: Abasa:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهُوَ يَخْشٰی wahuwa yakhshā while he fears [Allah],

item.title: Abasa:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهُوَ يَخْشٰی wahuwa yakhshā While he fears (Allah). See 80:1

item.title: Abasa:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهُوَ يَخْشٰی wahuwa yakhshā And feareth he (at heart) Attention should be paid first to the one who comes striving with earnestness, be he poor and lowly in his position, it is nothing to do with his receiving the knowledge, he comes for.

item.title: Abasa:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَنْتَ عَنْهُ تَلَهَّى fa-anta ʿanhu talahhā you are neglectful of him.

item.title: Abasa:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَنْتَ عَنْهُ تَلَهَّى fa-anta ʿanhu talahhā From him you are distracted. See 80:1

item.title: Abasa:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَنْتَ عَنْهُ تَلَهَّى fa-anta ʿanhu talahhā From him wilt thou be indifferent See 80:9

item.title: Abasa:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا إِنَّهَا تَذْكِرَةٌ kallā innahā tadhkiratun No indeed! These [verses of the Qur'ān] are a reminder

item.title: Abasa:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا إِنَّهَا تَذْكِرَةٌ kallā innahā tadhkiratun No! Indeed, they (i.e., these verses) are a reminder. See 80:1

item.title: Abasa:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا إِنَّهَا تَذْكِرَةٌ kallā innahā tadhkiratun Nay! but it (the Qur'an) is a reminder The Reminder (The Holy Qur'an) from God or the faith it preaches, is universal in its application - none should be excluded on the merit of any worldly calculation of wealth or poverty, the individual being high or low. The craving for spiritual growth, if with the necessary earnestness, must be given preference if it be needed.

item.title: Abasa:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَمَنْ شَاءَ ذَكَرَهُ faman shāa dhakarahu —so let anyone who wishes remember it—

item.title: Abasa:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَمَنْ شَاءَ ذَكَرَهُ faman shāa dhakarahu So whoever wills may remember it.1 See 80:1

item.title: Abasa:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَمَنْ شَاءَ ذَكَرَهُ faman shāa dhakarahu So, let whosoever pleaseth, mind it The choice to accept the Holy Qur'an as the Word of God and to abide by it, is left to every individual man and woman.

item.title: Abasa:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي صُحُفٍ مُكَرَّمَةٍ fī ṣuḥufin mukarramatin in honoured scriptures,

item.title: Abasa:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي صُحُفٍ مُكَرَّمَةٍ fī ṣuḥufin mukarramatin (It is recorded) in honored sheets. See 80:1

item.title: Abasa:13 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي صُحُفٍ مُكَرَّمَةٍ fī ṣuḥufin mukarramatin (It is written) in the Books (Sohof.) greatly honoured. (Refer to: 56:77, 56:78.) The truth about the Unity of God had been in all the previously revealed scriptures which are undoubtedly the honoured scripts.

item.title: Abasa:14 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَرْفُوعَةٍ مُطَهَّرَةٍ marfūʿatin muṭahharatin exalted and purified,

item.title: Abasa:14 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَرْفُوعَةٍ مُطَهَّرَةٍ marfūʿatin muṭahharatin Exalted and purified. See 80:1

item.title: Abasa:14 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَرْفُوعَةٍ مُطَهَّرَةٍ marfūʿatin muṭahharatin Exalted high, purified See 80:13

item.title: Abasa:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: بِأَيْدِي سَفَرَةٍ bi-aydī safaratin in the hands of envoys,1

item.title: Abasa:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: بِأَيْدِي سَفَرَةٍ bi-aydī safaratin (Carried) by the hands of messenger-angels. See 80:1

item.title: Abasa:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: بِأَيْدِي سَفَرَةٍ bi-aydī safaratin In the hands (Scribes.) of the deputy (The divine representative entities - either angels, or the prophets or the Imams.) angels i.e., The Holy Books have been either in the hands of the angels who conveyed them to the apostles of God or in the hands of those who have been purified by God Himself1. i.e., the purified ones are only the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt, i.e., the Holy Prophet, his godly daughter Lady Fatimah and the Twelve Holy Imams viz., Ali, his two sons, Hasan and Husayn, and nine Holy Imams in the seed of Husayn. The angels or those pious ones who preserved the Word of God in its original purity, recorded in writing. The divine representative entities are either angels, prophets or the Imams. (A.P.)

item.title: Abasa:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: كِرَامٍ بَرَرَةٍ kirāmin bararatin noble and pious.

item.title: Abasa:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: كِرَامٍ بَرَرَةٍ kirāmin bararatin Noble and dutiful. See 80:1

item.title: Abasa:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: كِرَامٍ بَرَرَةٍ kirāmin bararatin Noble, virtuous The quality of the scribes. There can never be any other than those whom God Himself purified1, i.e., the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt.

item.title: Abasa:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُتِلَ الْإِنْسَانُ مَا أَكْفَرَهُ qutila l-insānu mā akfarahu Perish man! How ungrateful is he!

item.title: Abasa:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُتِلَ الْإِنْسَانُ مَا أَكْفَرَهُ qutila l-insānu mā akfarahu Destroyed (i.e., cursed) is man;1 how disbelieving is he. Qutila mankind! How ungrateful he is (80:17). From what thing did He create him (80:18). From a Nutfah He created him and then set him in due proportion (80:19). Then He made the path easy for him (80:20). Then He causes him to die and puts him in his grave (80:21). Then when it is His will, He will resurrect him (80:22). Nay, but he has not done what He commanded him (80:23). Then let man look at his food (80:24). We pour forth water in abundance (80:25). And We split the earth in clefts (80:26). And We cause therein Habb to grow (80:27). And grapes and Qadb (80:28). And olives and date palms (80:29). And Ghulb Hada'iq (80:30). And fruits (Fakihah) and…

item.title: Abasa:17 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُتِلَ الْإِنْسَانُ مَا أَكْفَرَهُ qutila l-insānu mā akfarahu Cursed be man! How ungrateful is he? The trend of the address, which is to those who disbelieve the Holy Qur'an, clearly indicates that the matter of this Surah is an admonition to the disbelievers or those half-hearted converts who still, even after embracing the faith, lacked conviction, as one of them proved and himself declared to be the doubter about bonafide of the Holy Prophet's position as the apostle of God on the day of Hudaibiyya.

item.title: Abasa:18 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مِنْ أَيِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ min ayyi shayin khalaqahu From what has He created him?

item.title: Abasa:18 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مِنْ أَيِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ min ayyi shayin khalaqahu From what thing (i.e., substance) did He create him? See 80:17

item.title: Abasa:18 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مِنْ أَيِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ min ayyi shayin khalaqahu Of" what (What an insignificant thing.) thing did He (God.) create him? Man is reminded of his humblest origin as a life germ and the ultimate and as the dust, to be raised again at the will of the Lord. About the origin of man1 - About man's rising again2.

item.title: Abasa:19 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ min nuṭ'fatin khalaqahu faqaddarahu He has created him from a drop of [seminal] fluid, and then proportioned him.

item.title: Abasa:19 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ min nuṭ'fatin khalaqahu faqaddarahu From a sperm-drop He created him and destined for him.1 See 80:17

item.title: Abasa:19 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ min nuṭ'fatin khalaqahu faqaddarahu Of a Seminal - a drop (Refer to: 76:2, 86:6.) ; He created him, then fixed its measure See 80:18

item.title: Abasa:20 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ السَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ thumma l-sabīla yassarahu Then He made the way easy for him;

item.title: Abasa:20 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ السَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ thumma l-sabīla yassarahu Then He eased the way for him.1 See 80:17

item.title: Abasa:20 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ السَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ thumma l-sabīla yassarahu (And) then the way (for him) He made it easy (Refer to: 76:3.) See 80:18

item.title: Abasa:21 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ أَمَاتَهُ فَأَقْبَرَهُ thumma amātahu fa-aqbarahu then He made him die and buried him;

item.title: Abasa:21 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ أَمَاتَهُ فَأَقْبَرَهُ thumma amātahu fa-aqbarahu Then He causes his death and provides a grave for him.1 See 80:17

item.title: Abasa:21 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ أَمَاتَهُ فَأَقْبَرَهُ thumma amātahu fa-aqbarahu Then He causeth him to die, and got him buried See 80:18

item.title: Abasa:22 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ إِذَا شَاءَ أَنْشَرَهُ thumma idhā shāa ansharahu and then, when He wished, resurrected him.

item.title: Abasa:22 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ إِذَا شَاءَ أَنْشَرَهُ thumma idhā shāa ansharahu Then when He wills, He will resurrect him. See 80:17

item.title: Abasa:22 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ إِذَا شَاءَ أَنْشَرَهُ thumma idhā shāa ansharahu Then, when He willeth, He will again raise (Refer to: 22:55.) him (to life) See 80:18

item.title: Abasa:23 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا لَمَّا يَقْضِ مَا أَمَرَهُ kallā lammā yaqḍi mā amarahu No indeed! He has not yet carried out what He had commanded him.

item.title: Abasa:23 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا لَمَّا يَقْضِ مَا أَمَرَهُ kallā lammā yaqḍi mā amarahu No! He (i.e., man) has not yet accomplished what He commanded him. See 80:17

item.title: Abasa:23 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا لَمَّا يَقْضِ مَا أَمَرَهُ kallā lammā yaqḍi mā amarahu Nay! he hath fulfilled not what He (God.) bade him Refers to man's deviating from the right path of the faith and the prescribed conduct of life.

item.title: Abasa:24 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلْيَنْظُرِ الْإِنْسَانُ إِلَى طَعَامِهِ falyanẓuri l-insānu ilā ṭaʿāmihi So let man observe1 his food:

item.title: Abasa:24 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلْيَنْظُرِ الْإِنْسَانُ إِلَى طَعَامِهِ falyanẓuri l-insānu ilā ṭaʿāmihi Then let mankind look at his food. See 80:17

item.title: Abasa:24 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلْيَنْظُرِ الْإِنْسَانُ إِلَى طَعَامِهِ falyanẓuri l-insānu ilā ṭaʿāmihi Then, let man look at his food Man is reminded of the bounties of God, showered on him, upon which rests his life and the life of all the creatures serving Him. About the provision made for man, of the cattle1. The Sixth Holy Imam Ja'far Ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq says concerning verse 24: ''Man should also look at the knowledge which he obtains and not to see from what source he gets it" The Creator who was so careful about providing man with physical sustenance undoubtedly will be much more careful about providing proper nourishment for his mental and spiritual development. (A.P.)

item.title: Abasa:25 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا الْمَاءَ صَبًّا annā ṣababnā l-māa ṣabban We poured down water plenteously,

item.title: Abasa:25 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا الْمَاءَ صَبًّا annā ṣababnā l-māa ṣabban How We poured down water in torrents. See 80:17

item.title: Abasa:25 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا الْمَاءَ صَبًّا annā ṣababnā l-māa ṣabban That it was We Who poured down water in an abundant pouring See 80:24

item.title: Abasa:26 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ شَقَقْنَا الْأَرْضَ شَقًّا thumma shaqaqnā l-arḍa shaqqan then We split the earth into fissures

item.title: Abasa:26 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ شَقَقْنَا الْأَرْضَ شَقًّا thumma shaqaqnā l-arḍa shaqqan Then We broke open the earth, splitting (it with sprouts). See 80:17

item.title: Abasa:26 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ شَقَقْنَا الْأَرْضَ شَقًّا thumma shaqaqnā l-arḍa shaqqan Then We cleft the earth, with a (necessary) cleaving See 80:24

item.title: Abasa:27 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَنْبَتْنَا فِيهَا حَبًّا fa-anbatnā fīhā ḥabban and made the grain grow in it,

item.title: Abasa:27 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَنْبَتْنَا فِيهَا حَبًّا fa-anbatnā fīhā ḥabban And caused to grow within it grain. See 80:17

item.title: Abasa:27 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَنْبَتْنَا فِيهَا حَبًّا fa-anbatnā fīhā ḥabban And caused We to grow' therein the grain See 80:24

item.title: Abasa:28 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَعِنَبًا وَقَضْبًا waʿinaban waqaḍban and vines and vegetables,

item.title: Abasa:28 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَعِنَبًا وَقَضْبًا waʿinaban waqaḍban And grapes and herbage. See 80:17

item.title: Abasa:28 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَعِنَبًا وَقَضْبًا waʿinaban waqaḍban And grapes and the vegetables See 80:24

item.title: Abasa:29 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَزَيْتُونًا وَنَخْلًا wazaytūnan wanakhlan olives and date palms,

item.title: Abasa:29 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَزَيْتُونًا وَنَخْلًا wazaytūnan wanakhlan And olive and palm trees. See 80:17

item.title: Abasa:29 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَزَيْتُونًا وَنَخْلًا wazaytūnan wanakhlan The Olive and the Palm See 80:24

item.title: Abasa:30 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَحَدَائِقَ غُلْبًا waḥadāiqa ghul'ban and densely-planted gardens,

item.title: Abasa:30 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَحَدَائِقَ غُلْبًا waḥadāiqa ghul'ban And gardens of dense shrubbery. See 80:17

item.title: Abasa:30 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَحَدَائِقَ غُلْبًا waḥadāiqa ghul'ban And gardens enclosed, thick with trees See 80:24

item.title: Abasa:31 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَفَاكِهَةً وَأَبًّا wafākihatan wa-abban fruits and pastures,

item.title: Abasa:31 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَفَاكِهَةً وَأَبًّا wafākihatan wa-abban And fruit and grass. See 80:17

item.title: Abasa:31 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَفَاكِهَةً وَأَبًّا wafākihatan wa-abban And fruits and the herbage See 80:24

item.title: Abasa:32 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَتَاعًا لَكُمْ وَلِأَنْعَامِكُمْ matāʿan lakum wali-anʿāmikum as a sustenance for you and your livestock.

item.title: Abasa:32 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَتَاعًا لَكُمْ وَلِأَنْعَامِكُمْ matāʿan lakum wali-anʿāmikum (As) enjoyment (i.e., provision) for you and your grazing livestock. See 80:17

item.title: Abasa:32 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَتَاعًا لَكُمْ وَلِأَنْعَامِكُمْ matāʿan lakum wali-anʿāmikum A provision (Refer to: 79:33.) for you and your cattle See 80:24

item.title: Abasa:33 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِذَا جَاءَتِ الصَّاخَّةُ fa-idhā jāati l-ṣākhatu So when the deafening Cry comes

item.title: Abasa:33 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِذَا جَاءَتِ الصَّاخَّةُ fa-idhā jāati l-ṣākhatu But when there comes the Deafening Blast.1 Then when there comes As-Sakhkha (33)That Day shall a man flee from his brother (34)And from his mother and his father (35)And from his wife and his children (36)Every man that Day will have enough to make him careless of others (37)Some faces that Day will be bright (38)Laughing, rejoicing at good news (39)And other faces that Day will be dust-stained (40)Darkness will cover them (41)Such will be the disbelieving, the wicked evil doers (42) The Day of Judgement and the Fleeing of the People from Their Relatives during it Ibn 'Abbas said, "As-Sakhkhah is one of the names of the Day of Judgement that Allah has magnified and warned His servants of." Ibn Jarir said, "Perhaps it is a name for the blowing into Trumpet." Al-Baghawi…

item.title: Abasa:33 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِذَا جَاءَتِ الصَّاخَّةُ fa-idhā jāati l-ṣākhatu But when cometh the deafening Trumpet Blast This verse repeats the warning to man against the great Day of Judgment, which is sure to come, relating how violent will be the dawn of the day and in what agony and tumult will be mankind that everyone will be for himself forgetting the closest ties of even the nearest relations, his own parents, spouses and issues. No friend will even enquire about a friend1.

item.title: Abasa:34 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ الْمَرْءُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ yawma yafirru l-maru min akhīhi —the day when a man will evade his brother,

item.title: Abasa:34 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ الْمَرْءُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ yawma yafirru l-maru min akhīhi On the Day a man will flee from his brother. See 80:33

item.title: Abasa:34 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ الْمَرْءُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ yawma yafirru l-maru min akhīhi That day man will fly from his (own) brother See 80:33

item.title: Abasa:35 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأُمِّهِ وَأَبِيهِ wa-ummihi wa-abīhi his mother and his father,

item.title: Abasa:35 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأُمِّهِ وَأَبِيهِ wa-ummihi wa-abīhi And his mother and his father. See 80:33

item.title: Abasa:35 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأُمِّهِ وَأَبِيهِ wa-ummihi wa-abīhi And (from) his mother and (from) his father See 80:33

item.title: Abasa:36 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَصَاحِبَتِهِ وَبَنِيهِ waṣāḥibatihi wabanīhi his spouse and his sons—

item.title: Abasa:36 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَصَاحِبَتِهِ وَبَنِيهِ waṣāḥibatihi wabanīhi And his wife and his children. See 80:33

item.title: Abasa:36 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَصَاحِبَتِهِ وَبَنِيهِ waṣāḥibatihi wabanīhi And (from) his wife and (his) children See 80:33

item.title: Abasa:37 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ شَأْنٌ يُغْنِيهِ likulli im'ri-in min'hum yawma-idhin shanun yugh'nīhi that day each of them will have a task to keep him preoccupied.

item.title: Abasa:37 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ شَأْنٌ يُغْنِيهِ likulli im'ri-in min'hum yawma-idhin shanun yugh'nīhi For every man, that Day, will be a matter adequate for him.1 See 80:33

item.title: Abasa:37 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ شَأْنٌ يُغْنِيهِ likulli im'ri-in min'hum yawma-idhin shanun yugh'nīhi For every man (Every one of them.) of them on that day will have a concern enough to make him heedless (of others) See 80:33

item.title: Abasa:38 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ مُسْفِرَةٌ wujūhun yawma-idhin mus'firatun That day some faces will be bright,

item.title: Abasa:38 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ مُسْفِرَةٌ wujūhun yawma-idhin mus'firatun (Some) faces, that Day, will be bright. See 80:33

item.title: Abasa:38 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ مُسْفِرَةٌ wujūhun yawma-idhin mus'firatun (there shall be) faces on that day radiant This will be the state of the happiness and the joy of the faithful and the righteous ones.

item.title: Abasa:39 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ضَاحِكَةٌ مُسْتَبْشِرَةٌ ḍāḥikatun mus'tabshiratun laughing and joyous.

item.title: Abasa:39 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ضَاحِكَةٌ مُسْتَبْشِرَةٌ ḍāḥikatun mus'tabshiratun Laughing, rejoicing at good news. See 80:33

item.title: Abasa:39 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ضَاحِكَةٌ مُسْتَبْشِرَةٌ ḍāḥikatun mus'tabshiratun Laughing, joyous See 80:38

item.title: Abasa:40 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَلَيْهَا غَبَرَةٌ wawujūhun yawma-idhin ʿalayhā ghabaratun And some faces on that day will be covered with dust,

item.title: Abasa:40 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَلَيْهَا غَبَرَةٌ wawujūhun yawma-idhin ʿalayhā ghabaratun And (other) faces, that Day, will have upon them dust. See 80:33

item.title: Abasa:40 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَلَيْهَا غَبَرَةٌ wawujūhun yawma-idhin ʿalayhā ghabaratun And (there shall be) faces on that day on them shall be dust This refers to the fate of the disbelievers and the wicked ones.

item.title: Abasa:41 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: تَرْهَقُهَا قَتَرَةٌ tarhaquhā qataratun overcast with gloom.

item.title: Abasa:41 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: تَرْهَقُهَا قَتَرَةٌ tarhaquhā qataratun Blackness will cover them. See 80:33

item.title: Abasa:41 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: تَرْهَقُهَا قَتَرَةٌ tarhaquhā qataratun Darkness shall cover them See 80:40

item.title: Abasa:42 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اُولٰٓئِكَ هُمُ الْكَفَرَةُ الْفَجَرَةُ ulāika humu l-kafaratu l-fajaratu It is they who are the faithless, the vicious.1

item.title: Abasa:42 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اُولٰٓئِكَ هُمُ الْكَفَرَةُ الْفَجَرَةُ ulāika humu l-kafaratu l-fajaratu Those are the disbelievers, the wicked ones. See 80:33

item.title: Abasa:42 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اُولٰٓئِكَ هُمُ الْكَفَرَةُ الْفَجَرَةُ ulāika humu l-kafaratu l-fajaratu These are they who are the disbelievers, the wicked See 80:40

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالضُّحَى wal-ḍuḥā By the morning brightness,

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالضُّحَى wal-ḍuḥā By the morning brightness. وَأَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْ And procalim the grace of your Lord. Meaning: 'just as you were poor and needy, and Allah made you wealthy, then tell about Allah's favor upon you.' Abu Dawud recorded from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet SAW said: لَا يَشْكُرُ اللهَ مَنْ لَا يَشْكُرُ النَّاسَ Whoever is not thankful to the people, then he is not thankful to Allah. At-Tirmidhi also recorded this Hadith and he said, "Sahih". Abu Dawud recorded from Jabir that the Prophet SAW said: مَنْ أُبْلِيَ بَلَاءً فَذَكَرَهُ فَقَدْ شَكَرَهُ، وَمَنْ كَتَمَهُ فَقَدْ كَفَرَهُ Whoever overcomes some test (i.e., calamity) and mentions it (to others), then he is indeed thankful. And whoever conceals it, then indeed he was ungrateful. Abu Dawud was alone in recording this Hadith. This is the end of the Tafsir of Surat…

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالضُّحَى wal-ḍuḥā (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) By the Noonday (Radiation) (Brightness) (Refer to: 94:5, 94:6.) 'Doha', i.e., the glory of the earliest moments of the dawn that heralds the arrival of the light of the sun, which gradually increases in its brightness and heat1. It is practically the resurrection of the light of the day and its activities when after dark, stillness or quietness of the night, the life on earth is once again quickened. The darkness of the night does not mean that God has forsaken the light for all times and similarly the stillness or the quietness of the night does not mean that the daily life and its activities have once for all been forsaken. The darkness, and its quietness, has to go and in its place light and activity has again to be returned. The darkness…

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا سَجَى wa-al-layli idhā sajā by the night when it is calm!

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا سَجَى wa-al-layli idhā sajā And (by) the night when it covers with darkness.1 See 93:1

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا سَجَى wa-al-layli idhā sajā By the Night when it darkeneth (Refer to: 94:5, 94:6.) ! Things or qualities are understood better by the contrast with their opposites. The darkness, the silence, the stillness of the night is mentioned to compare and contrast with the light, the life and the activity of the day. An insight into the marvels of the phenomenon active on the wonderful forces of nature, will help man to realise the real significance of bringing such daily occurrences to witness the greatness and the Glory of the Almighty Author of the Universe.

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا وَدَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وَمَا قَلَى mā waddaʿaka rabbuka wamā qalā Your Lord has neither forsaken you nor is He displeased with you,

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا وَدَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وَمَا قَلَى mā waddaʿaka rabbuka wamā qalā Your Lord has not taken leave of you, (O Muḥammad), nor has He detested (you). See 93:1

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا وَدَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وَمَا قَلَى mā waddaʿaka rabbuka wamā qalā Hath forsaken not thee thy Lord, nor hath He been displeased (with thee)! In the early stages of the ministry, there was some suspense or a short interval between a revelation and another. The pagans of Mecca taunted that God had forsaken the Holy Prophet and started a slander to the effect. But neither this nor even the worst of the torturous persecution had in the least affected the feelings of the Holy Prophet, though an apostle of God like Jesus is reported by the Christians themselves to have cried in the agony, ''My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?"1 the Crier was not in fact Jesus, the Spirit of God, but the one crucified in his stead. The brief pause is said to be only of a…

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَلْءَاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لَكَ مِنَ الْأُولَى walalākhiratu khayrun laka mina l-ūlā and the Hereafter shall be better for you than the world.

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَلْءَاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لَكَ مِنَ الْأُولَى walalākhiratu khayrun laka mina l-ūlā And the Hereafter is better for you than the first (life). See 93:1

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَلْءَاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لَكَ مِنَ الْأُولَى walalākhiratu khayrun laka mina l-ūlā And verily the end is better for thee than the beginning (of life) (For in spite of the ups and downs, he is in constant progress towards infinite perfection. See 20:114.) ! This refers to the great promise of the Lord to the Holy Prophet that greatness in this world and also in the hereafter, will be his. Because in spite of the ups and downs, he is in constant progress towards infinite perfection1. (A.P.).

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَى walasawfa yuʿ'ṭīka rabbuka fatarḍā Soon your Lord will give you [that with which] you will be pleased.

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَى walasawfa yuʿ'ṭīka rabbuka fatarḍā And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied. See 93:1

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَى walasawfa yuʿ'ṭīka rabbuka fatarḍā And soon will give thee thy Lord that thou shalt be well pleased! The grant to the utmost satisfaction or the pleasure of the Holy Prophet, could never be restricted to anything of this material world, which is low, mean and strictly temporary. It is the right of intercession for the sinners. It is said that the Holy Prophet said that he will not be pleased even if a single believer in God, is left unredeemed of his sins and admitted to the bliss in the heaven. The granting mentioned, is indefinite, anything indefinitely mentioned means everything possible under the term. The grant or the gift is always according to the position or the greatness or the excellence of the giver. The one who grants here is the All-Merciful, All-Mighty and All-Divine…

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيمًا فءَاوَى alam yajid'ka yatīman faāwā Did He not find you an orphan, and shelter you?

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيمًا فءَاوَى alam yajid'ka yatīman faāwā Did He not find you an orphan and give (you) refuge? See 93:1

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيمًا فءَاوَى alam yajid'ka yatīman faāwā What! Found He not thee an orphan, and sheltered (thee) (Refer to: 4:113, 53:2.) ? Commentators say that this is a reference to the providential protection which was divinely arranged for the Holy Prophet through guardian after guardian when he was orphaned. Only a few days after the Holy Prophet's birth his father Abdullah passed away and he was taken into the care of his grandfather Abdul Muttalib and when he was only of two years, his mother Amina Bint Wahab also left this world. And when he was of eight years his grandfather Abdul Muttalib departed handing over the charge of his grandson the Hob, Prophet, to his son Abu Talib (Ali's father). And it was the protection of Abu Talib (Ali's father) that was a providential plan to give the…

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَوَجَدَكَ ضَالًّا فَهَدَى wawajadaka ḍāllan fahadā Did He not find you astray, and guide you?

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَوَجَدَكَ ضَالًّا فَهَدَى wawajadaka ḍāllan fahadā And He found you lost and guided (you). See 93:1

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَوَجَدَكَ ضَالًّا فَهَدَى wawajadaka ḍāllan fahadā And (He) found thee in loss (and immediately) guided thee Mere common sense would suggest to any learned one to take the meaning of every word in its proper context or study any event with its background. The meaning of the word 'Zall' is taken as ignorant, whereas it means also lost and in view of the common story connected with the interpretation of this verse, it means only lost. What the common story says is that when Halima the nurse to the Holy Prophet, started on her journey to Mecca to restore the young Muhammad to his grandfather, she left him at a place at the outskirts of the town and went into the desert to answer the call of nature. When she returned, she did not find the holy child in the…

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَوَجَدَكَ عَائِلًا فَأَغْنَى wawajadaka ʿāilan fa-aghnā Did He not find you needy, and enrich you?

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَوَجَدَكَ عَائِلًا فَأَغْنَى wawajadaka ʿāilan fa-aghnā And He found you poor and made (you) self-sufficient. See 93:1

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَوَجَدَكَ عَائِلًا فَأَغْنَى wawajadaka ʿāilan fa-aghnā And (He) found thee in need, and (immediately) made thee independent Commentators interpret this verse as a reference to the pecuniary provisions which the Holy Prophet received from the wealth of his wife Khadija and what he got through the leftover of the enemies, he dedicated for the defensive battles. But it would be too low and even a very mean estimate of the provision which God says that He has made for the Holy Prophet. God's provision would be in accordance with God's Greatness and glory. The Eighth Holy Imam Ali Ibn Musa ar-Riza says that the word 'Yateem' here means lonely. The Holy Prophet was lonely, alone without any friends or sympathisers and God directed the hearts of men and got the people around him as his devotees.

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا الْيَتِيمَ فَلَا تَقْهَرْ fa-ammā l-yatīma falā taqhar So, as for the orphan, do not oppress him;

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا الْيَتِيمَ فَلَا تَقْهَرْ fa-ammā l-yatīma falā taqhar So as for the orphan, do not oppress (him). See 93:1

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا الْيَتِيمَ فَلَا تَقْهَرْ fa-ammā l-yatīma falā taqhar So, unto an orphan, oppress (People addressed through the Prophet.) not! The address is to the Holy Prophet, but it is an ordinance for the believers in particular and mankind as a whole. The Holy Prophet said that ''he who pleases an orphan, I shall be pleased with him on the day of Judgment" Again the Holy Prophet said ''He who maintains an orphan in honour, he and I will be together in heaven". While saying this he raised his palm and showed his two fingers and said ''as these two fingers are together".

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا السَّائِلَ فَلَا تَنْهَرْ wa-ammā l-sāila falā tanhar and as for the beggar, do not chide him;

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا السَّائِلَ فَلَا تَنْهَرْ wa-ammā l-sāila falā tanhar And as for the petitioner,1 do not repel (him). See 93:1

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا السَّائِلَ فَلَا تَنْهَرْ wa-ammā l-sāila falā tanhar And as to the beggar, chide him not! 'Sayil', i.e., a seeker need not always be a Begger asking for any pecuniary charity. It may as well refer to the seeker of knowledge. Taking the meaning as a Begger, we are warned against rebuking them or treating them with the least hardship or scorn. The Holy Prophet said that ''If any seeker comes to thee even mounted on a horse even then, return him not disappointed. Even then he has a right over thee to help him as much as thou canst do it" Though begging is condemned in Islam, yet as the Holy Prophet has suggested in one of his sayings - If a person gives up his self-respect and stretches out his hand in begging, he should not be further…

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْ wa-ammā biniʿ'mati rabbika faḥaddith and as for your Lord's blessing, proclaim it!

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْ wa-ammā biniʿ'mati rabbika faḥaddith But as for the favor of your Lord, report (it). See 93:1

item.title: Ad-Dhuhaa:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْ wa-ammā biniʿ'mati rabbika faḥaddith And as to the bounties of thy Lord, thou announce (Or remember or Let mankind know that it is God who bestows bounties and grace and none else.) (them unto others) Man is enjoined to be always grateful and thankful to God's grace and bounties and be mindful of his grace and mercy. He who does not thank for a little will not thank for much also. Man must always be celebrating the grace and the bounties he receives from the Lord, before the others. To make it known to the people by contribution - not boastfully. (A.P.).

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: حم hha-meem Ḥā, Mīm.

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: حم hha-meem Ḥā, Meem.1 لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ ۖ رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ آبَائِكُمُ الْأَوَّلِينَ La ilaha illa Huwa. He gives life and causes death – your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers. This is like the Ayah: قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إِلَيْكُمْ جَمِيعًا الَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۖ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ ۖ Say: "O mankind! Verily, I am sent to you all as the Messenger of Allah – to Whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. La ilaha illa Huwa. He gives life and causes death... (7:158)

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: حم hha-meem Ha. Mim. (H. M.) Ha, Meem (H. M.) refer to verse 2:1

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْكِتَابِ الْمُبِينِ wal-kitābi l-mubīni By the Manifest Book!

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْكِتَابِ الْمُبِينِ wal-kitābi l-mubīni By the clear Book. See 44:1

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْكِتَابِ الْمُبِينِ wal-kitābi l-mubīni By the Manifesting Book (Qur'an), (Which makes the Truth manifest.) By the Book, the Holy Qur'an, which makes the truth with all the laws for the discipline of the human life on earth, plain enough for mankind to understand them and abide by them.

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ فِي لَيْلَةٍ مُبَارَكَةٍ إِنَّا كُنَّا مُنْذِرِينَ innā anzalnāhu fī laylatin mubārakatin innā kunnā mundhirīna Indeed We sent it down on a blessed night, and indeed We have been warning [mankind].

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ فِي لَيْلَةٍ مُبَارَكَةٍ إِنَّا كُنَّا مُنْذِرِينَ innā anzalnāhu fī laylatin mubārakatin innā kunnā mundhirīna Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night.1 Indeed, We were to warn (mankind). See 44:1

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ فِي لَيْلَةٍ مُبَارَكَةٍ إِنَّا كُنَّا مُنْذِرِينَ innā anzalnāhu fī laylatin mubārakatin innā kunnā mundhirīna Verily We sent it down on a Blessed Night - verily We have ever been warning – In verse 2:185, it is said that the Holy Qur'an was sent down in the month of Ramazan - verse 97:1, it is said that it was sent down in the 'Laylat ul-Qadr,' i.e., the Night of Great Value and Worth - which is literally translated as the Night of Power. This verse read along with these two verses would mean that the Holy Qur'an was revealed in the Night of 'Qadr' in the month of Ramazan and the Night of Qadr has been kept a secret but it is held in the highest sanctity, for it is accepted in the Islamic World as a whole, that…

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيهَا يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ fīhā yuf'raqu kullu amrin ḥakīmin Every definitive matter is resolved in it,1

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيهَا يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ fīhā yuf'raqu kullu amrin ḥakīmin Therein (i.e., on that night) is made distinct1 every precise matter. See 44:1

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيهَا يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ fīhā yuf'raqu kullu amrin ḥakīmin Therein (The Night.) are made distinct (Determined.) all wise affairs, In the night of 'Qadr' whatever every one has to receive that year, is decreed. This is why the believers are ordained by the Holy Prophet to spend the whole of the night in prayers, seeking the grace of God, His pardon for the sins and the grant of the bounties one desires to have. It is said in this night is decreed the question of sustenance, life and death of each individual. It is a night when the All-Merciful Lord invites everyone to seek His pardon and mercy1.

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَمْرًا مِنْ عِنْدِنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا مُرْسِلِينَ amran min ʿindinā innā kunnā mur'silīna as an ordinance1 from Us. Indeed We have been sending [apostles],

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَمْرًا مِنْ عِنْدِنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا مُرْسِلِينَ amran min ʿindinā innā kunnā mur'silīna (Every) matter (proceeding) from Us. Indeed, We were to send (a messenger). See 44:1

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَمْرًا مِنْ عِنْدِنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا مُرْسِلِينَ amran min ʿindinā innā kunnā mur'silīna (Becoming) a command from unto Us; Verily, We are the senders (of mercy and peace). Everything men had to have and every event which has to take place is desired by God and the command is issued from Him. And it is God alone Who commissions His chosen men with the apostleship and sends them into the world. This makes the point very clear that neither a spiritual guide is made in this world nor is it a matter of promotion for anyone to earn, by his efforts in the life in this world but a grace of God endowed by God Himself with the native excellence of body and soul essential for the purpose, and then the individual is sent into the world. The same is the…

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: رَحْمَةً مِنْ رَبِّكَ إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ raḥmatan min rabbika innahu huwa l-samīʿu l-ʿalīmu as a mercy from your Lord —indeed He is the All-hearing, the All-knowing—

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: رَحْمَةً مِنْ رَبِّكَ إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ raḥmatan min rabbika innahu huwa l-samīʿu l-ʿalīmu As mercy from your Lord. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing. See 44:1

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: رَحْمَةً مِنْ رَبِّكَ إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ raḥmatan min rabbika innahu huwa l-samīʿu l-ʿalīmu A mercy from thy Lord; Verily, He is the All-Hearing (This process is one of the manifestations of God's universal mercy. (A.P.).) , the All-Knowing, (hints to the utility of supplication.) Whatever is granted or sent down by God, is His mercy and grace. Some commentators say that the mercy referred to here, is a reference to the Holy Prophet about whom God says - "We have not sent thee (O' Our Apostle Muhammad) but a Mercy unto the worlds."1

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: رَبِّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُوقِنِينَ rabbi l-samāwāti wal-arḍi wamā baynahumā in kuntum mūqinīna the Lord of the heavens and the earth, and whatever is between them, should you have conviction.

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: رَبِّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُوقِنِينَ rabbi l-samāwāti wal-arḍi wamā baynahumā in kuntum mūqinīna Lord of the heavens and the earth and that between them, if you would be certain. See 44:1

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: رَبِّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُوقِنِينَ rabbi l-samāwāti wal-arḍi wamā baynahumā in kuntum mūqinīna The Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them two, if ye be sure in faith. See 44:6

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ ءَابَائِكُمُ الْأَوَّلِينَ lā ilāha illā huwa yuḥ'yī wayumītu rabbukum warabbu ābāikumu l-awalīna There is no god except Him: He gives life and brings death, your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers.

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ ءَابَائِكُمُ الْأَوَّلِينَ lā ilāha illā huwa yuḥ'yī wayumītu rabbukum warabbu ābāikumu l-awalīna There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death. (He is) your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers. See 44:1

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ ءَابَائِكُمُ الْأَوَّلِينَ lā ilāha illā huwa yuḥ'yī wayumītu rabbukum warabbu ābāikumu l-awalīna There is no god but He; He giveth life and causeth death; your Lord and the Lord of your fathers of yore. See 44:6

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ هُمْ فِي شَكٍّ يَلْعَبُونَ bal hum fī shakkin yalʿabūna Rather they play around in doubt.

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ هُمْ فِي شَكٍّ يَلْعَبُونَ bal hum fī shakkin yalʿabūna But they are in doubt, amusing themselves. Nay! They play about in doubt (44:9). Then wait you for the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke (44:10). Covering mankind, this is a painful torment (44:11). (They will say): "Our Lord! Remove the torment from us, really we shall become believers! (44:12). How can there be for them an admonition, when a Messenger explaining things clearly has already come to them (44:13). Then they had turned away from him and said: "(He is) one taught, a madman! (44:14). Verily, We shall remove the torment for a while. Verily, you will revert (44:15). On the Day when We shall strike you with the great Batshah. Verily, We will exact retribution (44:16). Alarming the Idolators with News of the Day…

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ هُمْ فِي شَكٍّ يَلْعَبُونَ bal hum fī shakkin yalʿabūna Yet they are sporting in doubt. See 44:6

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَارْتَقِبْ يَوْمَ تَأْتِي السَّمَاءُ بِدُخَانٍ مُبِينٍ fa-ir'taqib yawma tatī l-samāu bidukhānin mubīnin So watch out for the day when the sky brings on a manifest smoke,

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَارْتَقِبْ يَوْمَ تَأْتِي السَّمَاءُ بِدُخَانٍ مُبِينٍ fa-ir'taqib yawma tatī l-samāu bidukhānin mubīnin Then watch for the Day when the sky will bring a visible smoke. See 44:9

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَارْتَقِبْ يَوْمَ تَأْتِي السَّمَاءُ بِدُخَانٍ مُبِينٍ fa-ir'taqib yawma tatī l-samāu bidukhānin mubīnin So await thou the day when the heaven shall give out a smoke clearly visible, When the Quraysh became too hard-hearted and inflicted heartless, torturous and mortifying persecution upon those who embrace the Truth, God, made the tyrants taste some years of drought as in the time of Joseph, (i.e., seven years). A distressful famine overtook the people when they ate the corpses of dead dogs and the bones of the dead bodies. They ate even the skin of the dead animals soaked in their blood. The famine had reduced the people to bones and affected their eyesight and consequently when they looked up, they saw a smoke between their eyes and the sky. At last, when the people came to the Holy Prophet and implored him to…

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَغْشٰی النَّاسَ هَذَا عَذَابٌ اَلِیْمٌ yaghshā l-nāsa hādhā ʿadhābun alīmun enveloping the people. [They will cry out:] 'This is a painful punishment.

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَغْشٰی النَّاسَ هَذَا عَذَابٌ اَلِیْمٌ yaghshā l-nāsa hādhā ʿadhābun alīmun Covering the people; this is a painful torment. See 44:9

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَغْشٰی النَّاسَ هَذَا عَذَابٌ اَلِیْمٌ yaghshā l-nāsa hādhā ʿadhābun alīmun Enveloping the people; This will be painful chastisement. When the people would come to the Holy Prophet and implore him to pray and get them the relief, and he would pray and get it from the Lord. It does not refer to the final resurrection day but to one of the earlier calamities which will overtake mankind for their failure to abide by the Last Apostle. The difference is that since the mission of the other apostles were limited to particular peoples and ages, the calamities also were limited to the people concerned. But since the mission of the Last Apostle is universal the calamity also will naturally be enveloping the humanity as a whole, to which the ancient prophets had hinted. The details are given by the Holy Ahl…

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: رَبَّنَا اكْشِفْ عَنَّا الْعَذَابَ إِنَّا مُؤْمِنُونَ rabbanā ik'shif ʿannā l-ʿadhāba innā mu'minūna Our Lord! Remove from us this punishment. Indeed we have believed!'

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: رَبَّنَا اكْشِفْ عَنَّا الْعَذَابَ إِنَّا مُؤْمِنُونَ rabbanā ik'shif ʿannā l-ʿadhāba innā mu'minūna (They will say), "Our Lord, remove from us the torment; indeed, we are believers." See 44:9

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: رَبَّنَا اكْشِفْ عَنَّا الْعَذَابَ إِنَّا مُؤْمِنُونَ rabbanā ik'shif ʿannā l-ʿadhāba innā mu'minūna (They will say): "O' our Lord! Remove from us the torment; Verily we are believers!" See 44:11

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنَّى لَهُمُ الذِّكْرَى وَقَدْ جَاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ مُبِينٌ annā lahumu l-dhik'rā waqad jāahum rasūlun mubīnun What will the admonition avail them, when a manifest apostle had already come to them,

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنَّى لَهُمُ الذِّكْرَى وَقَدْ جَاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ مُبِينٌ annā lahumu l-dhik'rā waqad jāahum rasūlun mubīnun How will there be for them a reminder (at that time)? And there had come to them a clear Messenger. See 44:9

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:13 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنَّى لَهُمُ الذِّكْرَى وَقَدْ جَاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ مُبِينٌ annā lahumu l-dhik'rā waqad jāahum rasūlun mubīnun How shall they be admonished when there came unto them an apostle making (the truth) mani fest, See 44:11

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:14 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ تَوَلَّوْا عَنْهُ وَقَالُوْۤا مُعَلَّمٌ مَجْنُونٌ thumma tawallaw ʿanhu waqālū muʿallamun majnūnun but they turned away from him, and said, 'A tutored madman?'

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:14 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ تَوَلَّوْا عَنْهُ وَقَالُوْۤا مُعَلَّمٌ مَجْنُونٌ thumma tawallaw ʿanhu waqālū muʿallamun majnūnun Then they turned away from him and said, "(He was) taught (and is) a madman." See 44:9

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:14 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ تَوَلَّوْا عَنْهُ وَقَالُوْۤا مُعَلَّمٌ مَجْنُونٌ thumma tawallaw ʿanhu waqālū muʿallamun majnūnun (And yet) turned they their backs unto him and said: "(He is) tutored (by others), a mad man." See 44:11

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا كَاشِفُوْۤا الْعَذَابِ قَلِيلًا إِنَّكُمْ عَائِدُونَ innā kāshifū l-ʿadhābi qalīlan innakum ʿāidūna Indeed We will withdraw the punishment a little; but you will indeed revert [to your earlier ways].

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا كَاشِفُوْۤا الْعَذَابِ قَلِيلًا إِنَّكُمْ عَائِدُونَ innā kāshifū l-ʿadhābi qalīlan innakum ʿāidūna Indeed, We will remove the torment for a little. Indeed, you (disbelievers) will return (to disbelief). See 44:9

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا كَاشِفُوْۤا الْعَذَابِ قَلِيلًا إِنَّكُمْ عَائِدُونَ innā kāshifū l-ʿadhābi qalīlan innakum ʿāidūna Verily, We will remove the torment a little (but) verily, ye will return (unto evil). See 44:11

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ الْبَطْشَةَ الْكُبْرٰی إِنَّا مُنْتَقِمُونَ yawma nabṭishu l-baṭshata l-kub'rā innā muntaqimūna The day We shall strike with the most terrible striking, We will indeed take vengeance [on them].

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ الْبَطْشَةَ الْكُبْرٰی إِنَّا مُنْتَقِمُونَ yawma nabṭishu l-baṭshata l-kub'rā innā muntaqimūna The Day We will strike with the greatest assault, indeed, We will take retribution. See 44:9

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ الْبَطْشَةَ الْكُبْرٰی إِنَّا مُنْتَقِمُونَ yawma nabṭishu l-baṭshata l-kub'rā innā muntaqimūna That day We shall seize (them) with a great seizure; Verily, We shall retribute (them). See 44:11

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَجَاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ كَرِيمٌ walaqad fatannā qablahum qawma fir'ʿawna wajāahum rasūlun karīmun Certainly We tried the people of Pharaoh before them, when a noble apostle came to them,

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَجَاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ كَرِيمٌ walaqad fatannā qablahum qawma fir'ʿawna wajāahum rasūlun karīmun And We had already tried before them the people of Pharaoh, and there came to them a noble messenger (i.e., Musa). And indeed We tried before them Fir'awn's people, when there came to them a noble Messenger (44:17). Saying: Deliver to me the servants of Allah. Verily, I am to you a Messenger worthy of all trust (44:18). "And exalt not yourselves against Allah. Truly, I have come to you with a manifest authority (44:19). "And truly, I seek refuge with my Lord and your Lord, lest you should stone me (44:20). "But if you believe me not, then keep away from me and leave me alone (44:21). So he (Musa) called upon his Lord (saying): "These are indeed the people who are criminals…

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:17 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَجَاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ كَرِيمٌ walaqad fatannā qablahum qawma fir'ʿawna wajāahum rasūlun karīmun And indeed We tried before them the people of Pharaoh, and there came unto them a noble Apostle, The reference from this verse to verse 44:28 is to the encounter of Moses with Pharaoh, and the fate which Pharaoh with his hosts, met. It could be naturally inferred that the heavens and the earth weep or mourn for those who lay their lives in the way of God and not for the dead who taste death as the punishment for their own disbelief and wickedness. History relates of instances when signs extraordinary manifesting in the heavens and fresh blood having been found under each stone that was removed from the earth on the occasion of the martyrdom of Ali and Husayn. According to Sahib…

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:18 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنْ أَدُّوْۤا إِلَيَّ عِبَادَ اللَّهِ اِنِّیْ لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ an addū ilayya ʿibāda l-lahi innī lakum rasūlun amīnun [saying,] 'Give over the servants of Allah1 to me; indeed I am a trusted apostle [sent] to you.

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:18 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنْ أَدُّوْۤا إِلَيَّ عِبَادَ اللَّهِ اِنِّیْ لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ an addū ilayya ʿibāda l-lahi innī lakum rasūlun amīnun (Saying), "Render to me the servants of Allah.1 Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger." See 44:17

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:18 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنْ أَدُّوْۤا إِلَيَّ عِبَادَ اللَّهِ اِنِّیْ لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ an addū ilayya ʿibāda l-lahi innī lakum rasūlun amīnun Saying: "Deliver unto me the servants of God; Verily, I am unto you a trusted apostle," See 44:17

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:19 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنْ لَا تَعْلُوْۤا عَلَى اللَّهِ اِنِّیْ ءَاتِيكُمْ بِسُلْطَانٍ مُبِينٍ wa-an lā taʿlū ʿalā l-lahi innī ātīkum bisul'ṭānin mubīnin Do not defy Allah. Indeed I bring you a manifest authority.

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:19 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنْ لَا تَعْلُوْۤا عَلَى اللَّهِ اِنِّیْ ءَاتِيكُمْ بِسُلْطَانٍ مُبِينٍ wa-an lā taʿlū ʿalā l-lahi innī ātīkum bisul'ṭānin mubīnin And (saying), "Be not haughty with Allah. Indeed, I have come to you with clear evidence. See 44:17

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:19 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنْ لَا تَعْلُوْۤا عَلَى اللَّهِ اِنِّیْ ءَاتِيكُمْ بِسُلْطَانٍ مُبِينٍ wa-an lā taʿlū ʿalā l-lahi innī ātīkum bisul'ṭānin mubīnin And that exalt ye not yourselves against God; Verily, I come unto you with an authority manifest. See 44:17

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:20 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنِّي عُذْتُ بِرَبِّي وَرَبِّكُمْ أَنْ تَرْجُمُونِ wa-innī ʿudh'tu birabbī warabbikum an tarjumūni I seek the protection of my Lord and your Lord, lest you should stone me.

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:20 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنِّي عُذْتُ بِرَبِّي وَرَبِّكُمْ أَنْ تَرْجُمُونِ wa-innī ʿudh'tu birabbī warabbikum an tarjumūni And indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord, lest you stone me.1 See 44:17

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:20 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنِّي عُذْتُ بِرَبِّي وَرَبِّكُمْ أَنْ تَرْجُمُونِ wa-innī ʿudh'tu birabbī warabbikum an tarjumūni And verily, I take refuge with my Lord and your Lord lest ye stone me (to death); See 44:17

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:21 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنْ لَمْ تُؤْمِنُوْۤا لِي فَاعْتَزِلُونِ wa-in lam tu'minū lī fa-iʿ'tazilūni And if you do not believe me, keep out of my way.'

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:21 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنْ لَمْ تُؤْمِنُوْۤا لِي فَاعْتَزِلُونِ wa-in lam tu'minū lī fa-iʿ'tazilūni But if you do not believe me, then leave me alone." See 44:17

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:21 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنْ لَمْ تُؤْمِنُوْۤا لِي فَاعْتَزِلُونِ wa-in lam tu'minū lī fa-iʿ'tazilūni And if ye believe not in me, then leave me alone. See 44:17

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:22 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَدَعَا رَبَّهُ أَنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ قَوْمٌ مُجْرِمُونَ fadaʿā rabbahu anna hāulāi qawmun muj'rimūna Then he invoked his Lord, [saying,] 'These are indeed a guilty lot.'

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:22 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَدَعَا رَبَّهُ أَنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ قَوْمٌ مُجْرِمُونَ fadaʿā rabbahu anna hāulāi qawmun muj'rimūna And (finally) he called to his Lord that these were a criminal people. See 44:17

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:22 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَدَعَا رَبَّهُ أَنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ قَوْمٌ مُجْرِمُونَ fadaʿā rabbahu anna hāulāi qawmun muj'rimūna (But they began tormenting him); Then cried he unto his Lord that "these are a people guilty ones" See 44:17

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:23 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَسْرِ بِعِبَادِي لَيْلًا إِنَّكُمْ مُتَّبَعُونَ fa-asri biʿibādī laylan innakum muttabaʿūna [Allah told him,] 'Set out with My servants by night; for you will indeed be pursued.

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:23 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَسْرِ بِعِبَادِي لَيْلًا إِنَّكُمْ مُتَّبَعُونَ fa-asri biʿibādī laylan innakum muttabaʿūna (Allah said), "Then set out with My servants by night. Indeed, you are to be pursued. See 44:17

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:23 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَسْرِ بِعِبَادِي لَيْلًا إِنَّكُمْ مُتَّبَعُونَ fa-asri biʿibādī laylan innakum muttabaʿūna (He was commanded saying): "Then march forth with My servants by night; verily ye will be pursued," See 44:17

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:24 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاتْرُكِ الْبَحْرَ رَهْوًا إِنَّهُمْ جُنْدٌ مُغْرَقُونَ wa-ut'ruki l-baḥra rahwan innahum jundun mugh'raqūna And leave the sea calmly; they will indeed be a drowned host.'

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:24 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاتْرُكِ الْبَحْرَ رَهْوًا إِنَّهُمْ جُنْدٌ مُغْرَقُونَ wa-ut'ruki l-baḥra rahwan innahum jundun mugh'raqūna And leave the sea in stillness.1 Indeed, they are an army to be drowned." See 44:17

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:24 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاتْرُكِ الْبَحْرَ رَهْوًا إِنَّهُمْ جُنْدٌ مُغْرَقُونَ wa-ut'ruki l-baḥra rahwan innahum jundun mugh'raqūna And leave thou the sea calm; Verily, they are a host that shall be drowned. See 44:17

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:25 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: كَمْ تَرَكُوْۤا مِنْ جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ kam tarakū min jannātin waʿuyūnin How many gardens and springs did they leave behind!

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:25 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: كَمْ تَرَكُوْۤا مِنْ جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ kam tarakū min jannātin waʿuyūnin How much they left behind of gardens and springs. See 44:17

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:25 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: كَمْ تَرَكُوْۤا مِنْ جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ kam tarakū min jannātin waʿuyūnin How many have they (The people of Pharaoh.) left, of the gardens and fountains! See 44:17

item.title: Ad-Dukhaan:26 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
