item.title: Al-A'laa:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلَا تَنْسٰی sanuq'ri-uka falā tansā And We make thee to read so that thou shouldst not forget The Holy Qur'an was revealed in stages1 to facilitate people learning the truth gradually leaving the margin of time for the people to remember each commandment so that the knowledge of it may have a gradual growth. This indicates that the Holy Prophet was divinely endowed with the wonderful memory to remember the very text of the Word of God even though it was revealed to him only once. There is another aspect of the meaning 'Tansa', i.e., forget or forsake. It may mean, that the Holy Prophet was divinely protected against any forgetfulness. The Holy Prophet was made to read - by God and the divine agencies. Hence, he never forgets. The tradition which indicates that the Holy Prophet while conducting…

item.title: Al-A'laa:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ إِنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ الْجَهْرَ وَمَا يَخْفَى illā mā shāa l-lahu innahu yaʿlamu l-jahra wamā yakhfā except what Allah may wish. Indeed He knows the overt and what is hidden.

item.title: Al-A'laa:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ إِنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ الْجَهْرَ وَمَا يَخْفَى illā mā shāa l-lahu innahu yaʿlamu l-jahra wamā yakhfā Except what Allah should will. Indeed, He knows what is declared and what is hidden. See 87:1

item.title: Al-A'laa:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ إِنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ الْجَهْرَ وَمَا يَخْفَى illā mā shāa l-lahu innahu yaʿlamu l-jahra wamā yakhfā Save what willeth God (Refer to: 11:108.) ; Verily He knoweth the declared and what is hidden See 87:6

item.title: Al-A'laa:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَنُيَسِّرُكَ لِلْيُسْرَى wanuyassiruka lil'yus'rā We shall smooth your way to [preach] the easiest [canon].

item.title: Al-A'laa:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَنُيَسِّرُكَ لِلْيُسْرَى wanuyassiruka lil'yus'rā And We will ease you toward ease.1 See 87:1

item.title: Al-A'laa:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَنُيَسِّرُكَ لِلْيُسْرَى wanuyassiruka lil'yus'rā We shall ease (thy way) unto an ease (for thee) The declaration is prophetic about the easy march of Islam from success to success, in its spread.

item.title: Al-A'laa:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَذَكِّرْ إِنْ نَفَعَتِ الذِّكْرٰی fadhakkir in nafaʿati l-dhik'rā So admonish, for admonition is indeed beneficial:

item.title: Al-A'laa:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَذَكِّرْ إِنْ نَفَعَتِ الذِّكْرٰی fadhakkir in nafaʿati l-dhik'rā So remind, if the reminder should benefit.1 See 87:1

item.title: Al-A'laa:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَذَكِّرْ إِنْ نَفَعَتِ الذِّكْرٰی fadhakkir in nafaʿati l-dhik'rā And thou go on reminding, for it profiteth (mankind) reminding it (Refer to: 88:21.) Commentators consider 'In' here as to mean certainty and not conditional, but it may also mean 'when' or 'if' denoting condition but in the sense that reminding should be when there is some use, either for or against. It would mean that reminding should correspond with the capacity of the audience either to accept or to reject it. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-A'laa:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: سَيَذَّكَّرُ مَنْ يَخْشٰی sayadhakkaru man yakhshā he who fears will take admonition,

item.title: Al-A'laa:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: سَيَذَّكَّرُ مَنْ يَخْشٰی sayadhakkaru man yakhshā He who fears (Allah) will be reminded. See 87:1

item.title: Al-A'laa:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: سَيَذَّكَّرُ مَنْ يَخْشٰی sayadhakkaru man yakhshā He that feareth (God) will mind the warning See 87:9

item.title: Al-A'laa:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا الْأَشْقَى wayatajannabuhā l-ashqā and the most wretched will shun it

item.title: Al-A'laa:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا الْأَشْقَى wayatajannabuhā l-ashqā But the wretched one will avoid it. See 87:1

item.title: Al-A'laa:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا الْأَشْقَى wayatajannabuhā l-ashqā And will avoid it, the most reprobate one See 87:9

item.title: Al-A'laa:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي يَصْلَى النَّارَ الْكُبْرٰی alladhī yaṣlā l-nāra l-kub'rā —he who will enter the Great Fire,

item.title: Al-A'laa:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي يَصْلَى النَّارَ الْكُبْرٰی alladhī yaṣlā l-nāra l-kub'rā (He) who will (enter and) burn in the greatest Fire. See 87:1

item.title: Al-A'laa:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي يَصْلَى النَّارَ الْكُبْرٰی alladhī yaṣlā l-nāra l-kub'rā Who shall be committed to great fire See 87:9

item.title: Al-A'laa:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَى thumma lā yamūtu fīhā walā yaḥyā then neither live in it, nor die.

item.title: Al-A'laa:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَى thumma lā yamūtu fīhā walā yaḥyā Neither dying therein nor living. See 87:1

item.title: Al-A'laa:13 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَى thumma lā yamūtu fīhā walā yaḥyā Then he shall die not therein, nor shall he live (in it) (Refer to: 20:74.) This is the state in which the wicked in Hell will be committed to. There will be no death in Hell for death means the extinction of life, i.e., the state of absence from a state, the sinner will be there in Hell suffering the consequences of his own deeds and motives1.

item.title: Al-A'laa:14 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكَّى qad aflaḥa man tazakkā Felicitous is he who purifies himself,

item.title: Al-A'laa:14 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكَّى qad aflaḥa man tazakkā He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself. Indeed whosoever purifies himself shall achieve success (87:14). And remembers the Name of his Lord, and performs Salah (87:15). Rather you prefer the life of this world (87:16). Although the Hereafter is better and more lasting (87:17). Verily, this is in the former Scripture (87:18). The Scriptures of Ibrahim and Musa (87:19). A Statement Concerning the People of Success Allah says: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ Indeed whosoever purifies himself shall achieve success. Meaning: he purifies himself from despised characteristics and he follows what Allah has revealed to the Messenger SAW. وَذَكَرَ اسْمَ رَبِّهِ فَصَلَّىٰ And remembers the Name of his Lord, and performs Salah. Meaning: he establishes the prayer in its appointed time, seeking the pleasure of Allah, obedience to His command, and implementation of…

item.title: Al-A'laa:14 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكَّى qad aflaḥa man tazakkā Indeed he (alone) succeedeth who purifieth himself (At least by giving alms.) 'Aflaha', i.e., successful achievement of the cherished goal, attainment of the Eternal Bliss or Salvation. The purification of the self means to be pure and clean against any disobedience or rebellion against any of God's commands, to keep the soul always in submission to the Divine Will and never allowing it to get astray from the path of righteousness and piety.

item.title: Al-A'laa:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَذَكَرَ اسْمَ رَبِّهِ فَصَلَّى wadhakara is'ma rabbihi faṣallā celebrates the Name of his Lord, and prays.

item.title: Al-A'laa:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَذَكَرَ اسْمَ رَبِّهِ فَصَلَّى wadhakara is'ma rabbihi faṣallā And mentions the name of his Lord and prays. See 87:14

item.title: Al-A'laa:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَذَكَرَ اسْمَ رَبِّهِ فَصَلَّى wadhakara is'ma rabbihi faṣallā And remembereth the Name of his Lord and (regularly) prayeth See 87:14

item.title: Al-A'laa:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا bal tu'thirūna l-ḥayata l-dun'yā Rather you prefer the life of this world,

item.title: Al-A'laa:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا bal tu'thirūna l-ḥayata l-dun'yā But you prefer the worldly life. See 87:14

item.title: Al-A'laa:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا bal tu'thirūna l-ḥayata l-dun'yā Nay! prefer ye the life of this world Man is often beguiled by the powerful attraction front the enjoyment of the pleasures of this world which are the common tools of Satan to lead man astray.

item.title: Al-A'laa:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْءَاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَى wal-ākhiratu khayrun wa-abqā while the Hereafter is better and more lasting.

item.title: Al-A'laa:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْءَاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَى wal-ākhiratu khayrun wa-abqā While the Hereafter is better and more enduring. See 87:14

item.title: Al-A'laa:17 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْءَاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَى wal-ākhiratu khayrun wa-abqā Although the hereafter is better and more lasting See 87:16

item.title: Al-A'laa:18 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ هَذَا لَفِیْ الصُّحُفِ الْأُولَى inna hādhā lafī l-ṣuḥufi l-ūlā This is indeed in the former scriptures,

item.title: Al-A'laa:18 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ هَذَا لَفِیْ الصُّحُفِ الْأُولَى inna hādhā lafī l-ṣuḥufi l-ūlā Indeed, this is in the former scriptures. See 87:14

item.title: Al-A'laa:18 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ هَذَا لَفِیْ الصُّحُفِ الْأُولَى inna hādhā lafī l-ṣuḥufi l-ūlā Verily, this is in the scriptures earlier Every scripture that was revealed prior to the Holy Qur'an to the earlier apostles, contained only the truth about God, be that in any language for the apostles were sent in the languages of the respective people. See 14:4 and naturally the scriptures given to the apostles must have been in the language spoken and understood by the respective people. The contents from verse 14 downwards, i.e., it is the gist of what all the prophets came or and man's attitude towards their teachings. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-A'laa:19 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: صُحُفِ اِبْرَاهِیْمَ وَمُوسٰی ṣuḥufi ib'rāhīma wamūsā the scriptures of Abraham and Moses.

item.title: Al-A'laa:19 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: صُحُفِ اِبْرَاهِیْمَ وَمُوسٰی ṣuḥufi ib'rāhīma wamūsā The scriptures of Ibrahim and Musa. See 87:14

item.title: Al-A'laa:19 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: صُحُفِ اِبْرَاهِیْمَ وَمُوسٰی ṣuḥufi ib'rāhīma wamūsā The Scriptures of Abraham and Moses The book given to Abraham has not been definitely named. According to the Old Testament also, Abraham is recognised as one of the Apostles of God1. Mr. G. H. flux has brought out a translation of Greek text, in the name of the Testament of Abraham, published by the CPCK, London in 1927. The Greek version might be a translation from the Hebrew language. The Book of Moses referred to here, its original is called Taurat or the Pentateuch.

item.title: Al-Alaq:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اِقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ iq'ra bi-is'mi rabbika alladhī khalaqa Read in the Name of your Lord who created;

item.title: Al-Alaq:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اِقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ iq'ra bi-is'mi rabbika alladhī khalaqa Recite in the name of your Lord who created. اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ Read in the Name of your Lord who has created. until he reached the Ayah: مَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ That which he knew not. So he returned with them (those Ayat) and with his heart trembling until he came (home) to Khadijah, and he said: زَمِّلُونِي زَمِّلُونِي Wrap me up, wrap me up! So they wrapped him up until his fear went away. After that he told Khadijah everything that had happened (and said): قَدْ خَشِيتُ عَلَى نَفْسِي I fear that something may happen to me. Khadijah replied, "Never! By Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. You keep good relations with your relatives, you speak the truth, you help the poor and the destitute, you serve your…

item.title: Al-Alaq:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اِقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ iq'ra bi-is'mi rabbika alladhī khalaqa Read thou! (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) In the name of thy Lord Who created (Everything in the Universe) The popular report of the commentators is that this Surah or the first five verses of it were the first revelations received by the Holy Prophet through the Messenger Angel Gabriel in the cave of Hira. Formerly the Holy Prophet used to receive the communion through dreams and the voices while he was alone in lonely places and did not see the speaker. In the fortieth year of his life on the 27th night of the month Rajab when the Holy Prophet was busy in his meditation and prayers in the cave on the Mount Hira, in deep silence and the calm atmosphere, all of a sudden, he heard a voice calling…

item.title: Al-Alaq:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: خَلَقَ الْاِنْسَانَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ khalaqa l-insāna min ʿalaqin created man from a clinging mass.

item.title: Al-Alaq:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: خَلَقَ الْاِنْسَانَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ khalaqa l-insāna min ʿalaqin Created man from a clinging substance. See 96:1

item.title: Al-Alaq:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: خَلَقَ الْاِنْسَانَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ khalaqa l-insāna min ʿalaqin He created man from a clot (Refer to: 23:14.) ! Man is reminded of the lowly origin of the animal in him, in contrast to the great heights of intellectual, moral and spiritual excellence, open to him to reach, with sincere will and the faithful endeavour, essential for the rise1.

item.title: Al-Alaq:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اِقْرَأْ وَرَبُّكَ الْأَكْرَمُ iq'ra warabbuka l-akramu Read, and your Lord is the most generous,

item.title: Al-Alaq:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اِقْرَأْ وَرَبُّكَ الْأَكْرَمُ iq'ra warabbuka l-akramu Recite, and your Lord is the most Generous. See 96:1

item.title: Al-Alaq:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اِقْرَأْ وَرَبُّكَ الْأَكْرَمُ iq'ra warabbuka l-akramu Recite (Thou O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) And thy Lord is the Most Honourable! This is the grant of the commission to the ministry with the command to proclaim only the Truth to mankind and to start openly, the invitation to the people to the right way to salvation.

item.title: Al-Alaq:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي عَلَّمَ بِالْقَلَمِ alladhī ʿallama bil-qalami who taught by the pen,

item.title: Al-Alaq:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي عَلَّمَ بِالْقَلَمِ alladhī ʿallama bil-qalami Who taught by the pen. See 96:1

item.title: Al-Alaq:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي عَلَّمَ بِالْقَلَمِ alladhī ʿallama bil-qalami (He) Who taught (to write) with the Pen (Refer to: 68:1.) 'Qalam', i.e., pen is a mystic symbol1. In this outer world also pen, is the source of learning and knowledge. Reading needs some inscribed matter and pen is the first need to inscribe. Inscription needs no ink for pen could create the inscription on any matter without any liquid. Permanent inscription is that which is graven deep on any matter without the risk of the figures, made of some liquid, fading away or getting wiped out. The commandments given to Moses, were on Tablets of stone with the matter engraved on them.

item.title: Al-Alaq:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: عَلَّمَ الْاِنْسَانَ مَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ ʿallama l-insāna mā lam yaʿlam taught man what he did not know.

item.title: Al-Alaq:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: عَلَّمَ الْاِنْسَانَ مَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ ʿallama l-insāna mā lam yaʿlam Taught man that which he knew not. See 96:1

item.title: Al-Alaq:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: عَلَّمَ الْاِنْسَانَ مَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ ʿallama l-insāna mā lam yaʿlam (He) taught man what he knew not! Reference to the humblest origin of man and the gradual growth of consciousness and knowledge in him with the development of the wonderful faculties endowed in him1.

item.title: Al-Alaq:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا إِنَّ الْاِنْسَانَ لَيَطْغَى kallā inna l-insāna layaṭghā Indeed man becomes rebellious

item.title: Al-Alaq:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا إِنَّ الْاِنْسَانَ لَيَطْغَى kallā inna l-insāna layaṭghā No! (But) indeed, man transgresses. The Threat against Man's Transgression for the Sake of Wealth Allah informs that man is very pleased, most evil, scornful and transgressive when he considers himself self-sufficient and having an abundance of wealth. Then Allah threatens, warns and admonishes him in His saying: إِنَّ إِلَى رَبِّكَ الرُّجْعَى Surely, unto your Lord is the return. Meaning: 'unto Allah is the final destination and return, and He will hold you accountable for your wealth, as to where you obtained it from and how did you spend it.' Scolding of Abu Jahl and the Threat of Seizing Him Then Allah says: أَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِى يَنْهَى - عَبْداً إِذَا صَلَّى Have you seen him who prevents. A servant when he prays This was revealed about Abu Jahl, may Allah curse him. He…

item.title: Al-Alaq:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا إِنَّ الْاِنْسَانَ لَيَطْغَى kallā inna l-insāna layaṭghā Nay! Verily man is wont to rebel! Having received the grace and the bounties from his Creator Lord, man gets rebellious - forgets his origin and his inherent helplessness, and thinks that he is self-sufficient and can-do things without any help and without the fear of any one to check or control him or his being) accountable to the Lord. Though this is a general statement, but its immediate application was meant for Abu Jahl one of the leaders of the enemies of the Holy Prophet and Islam. It is said that once Abu Jahl told some men ''You see Muhammad praying, placing his forehead on the ground and you do not stop him. I swear that if I see him again doing it, I will stand on his neck until he…

item.title: Al-Alaq:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنْ رَاٰهُ اسْتَغْنَى an raāhu is'taghnā when he considers himself without need.

item.title: Al-Alaq:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنْ رَاٰهُ اسْتَغْنَى an raāhu is'taghnā Because he sees himself self-sufficient. See 96:6

item.title: Al-Alaq:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنْ رَاٰهُ اسْتَغْنَى an raāhu is'taghnā As he deemeth himself needless (Free from need, independent of God, This is a warning.) ! See 96:6

item.title: Al-Alaq:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ إِلَى رَبِّكَ الرُّجْعَى inna ilā rabbika l-ruj'ʿā Indeed to your Lord is the return.

item.title: Al-Alaq:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ إِلَى رَبِّكَ الرُّجْعَى inna ilā rabbika l-ruj'ʿā Indeed, to your Lord is the return. See 96:6

item.title: Al-Alaq:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ إِلَى رَبِّكَ الرُّجْعَى inna ilā rabbika l-ruj'ʿā Verily unto thy Lord (alone) is the return! Man should remember that ultimate, for the return of everything in the Universe is to the Lord.

item.title: Al-Alaq:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَرَءَيْتَ الَّذِي يَنْهَى ara-ayta alladhī yanhā Tell me, he who forbids

item.title: Al-Alaq:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَرَءَيْتَ الَّذِي يَنْهَى ara-ayta alladhī yanhā Have you seen the one who forbids. See 96:6

item.title: Al-Alaq:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَرَءَيْتَ الَّذِي يَنْهَى ara-ayta alladhī yanhā Hast, thou seen the man who forbiddeth? Reference to Abul Jehl's conduct See note on verse 6 and 7 above - 'The one who prayed' is the reference to the Holy Prophet. Abu Jahl the inveterate enemy of the Holy Prophet and Islam, in the early days of the Holy Prophet's ministry, used not only to tease the Holy Prophet but also to obstruct the others joining the faith or listening to the Islamic preachings and persecuted those who did not yield to his obstruction.

item.title: Al-Alaq:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: عَبْدًا إِذَا صَلَّى ʿabdan idhā ṣallā a servant when he prays,

item.title: Al-Alaq:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: عَبْدًا إِذَا صَلَّى ʿabdan idhā ṣallā A servant when he prays? See 96:6

item.title: Al-Alaq:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: عَبْدًا إِذَا صَلَّى ʿabdan idhā ṣallā A servant when he (The Holy Prophet.) prayeth? See 96:9

item.title: Al-Alaq:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَرَءَيْتَ إِنْ كَانَ عَلَى الْهُدَى ara-ayta in kāna ʿalā l-hudā tell me, should he be on [true] guidance,

item.title: Al-Alaq:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَرَءَيْتَ إِنْ كَانَ عَلَى الْهُدَى ara-ayta in kāna ʿalā l-hudā Have you seen if he is upon guidance. See 96:6

item.title: Al-Alaq:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَرَءَيْتَ إِنْ كَانَ عَلَى الْهُدَى ara-ayta in kāna ʿalā l-hudā Hast, thou seen if he were rightly guided (Reference to Abu Jahl's conduct.) ? He (Abu Jahl) would not have done it if he had been guided aright. One should always guard himself against getting misled by wicked minds, by a careful study- and scrutiny of the bonafide of their claims.

item.title: Al-Alaq:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوْ أَمَرَ بِالتَّقْوَى aw amara bil-taqwā or bid [others] to Godwariness,

item.title: Al-Alaq:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوْ أَمَرَ بِالتَّقْوَى aw amara bil-taqwā Or enjoins righteousness? See 96:6

item.title: Al-Alaq:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوْ أَمَرَ بِالتَّقْوَى aw amara bil-taqwā Or enjoined piety? See 96:11

item.title: Al-Alaq:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَرَءَيْتَ إِنْ كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى ara-ayta in kadhaba watawallā tell me, should he call him a liar and turn away

item.title: Al-Alaq:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَرَءَيْتَ إِنْ كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى ara-ayta in kadhaba watawallā Have you seen if he denies and turns away. See 96:6

item.title: Al-Alaq:13 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَرَءَيْتَ إِنْ كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى ara-ayta in kadhaba watawallā 'Hast, thou seen if he belieth the Truth and turneth (his) back? With the consideration enjoined in the two verses above, here it is said, that man must always be on his guard against the crooked minds who mislead others. The great Muslim Mystic Roomi says: Ai basa Iblees Aadam rooyi hast Pas bahardasti nashayad daad dast i.e. ''Often times Satan appears in human form. Thus, one should not give his hand (surrender) into the hand of every one that appears to be human"

item.title: Al-Alaq:14 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَرٰی alam yaʿlam bi-anna l-laha yarā —does he not know that Allah sees?

item.title: Al-Alaq:14 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَرٰی alam yaʿlam bi-anna l-laha yarā Does he not know that Allah sees? See 96:6

item.title: Al-Alaq:14 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَرٰی alam yaʿlam bi-anna l-laha yarā Knowest he not that God seeth? Does not man know that God is ever vigilant and sees and knows his deeds and his motives? Man should always be conscious and mindful of God's presence and his being seen by his Lord.

item.title: Al-Alaq:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا لَئِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهِ لَنَسْفَعًا بِالنَّاصِيَةِ kallā la-in lam yantahi lanasfaʿan bil-nāṣiyati No indeed! If he does not stop, We shall seize him by the forelock,

item.title: Al-Alaq:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا لَئِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهِ لَنَسْفَعًا بِالنَّاصِيَةِ kallā la-in lam yantahi lanasfaʿan bil-nāṣiyati No! If he does not desist, We will surely drag him by the forelock1. See 96:6

item.title: Al-Alaq:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا لَئِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهِ لَنَسْفَعًا بِالنَّاصِيَةِ kallā la-in lam yantahi lanasfaʿan bil-nāṣiyati Nay! (let him beware!) if he desisteth not, We shall surely drag him by the forelock! This prophecy was fulfilled even in this life at Badr where Abu Jahl was smitten on his forehead. But the warning here is about the punishment, Abu Jahl will receive in the life hereafter and on the Day of the Final Judgment. The other instance which is said about Abu Jahl's earning this punishment for him was – that once Abu Jahl met the Holy Prophet and warned him for offering the prayers in the Islamic way and threatened him saying that he had the great number of leading personalities of the people on his side. This verse was revealed saying that if Abu Jahl does not desist from his disbelief and…

item.title: Al-Alaq:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: نَاصِيَةٍ كَاذِبَةٍ خَاطِئَةٍ nāṣiyatin kādhibatin khāṭi-atin a lying, sinful forelock!

item.title: Al-Alaq:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: نَاصِيَةٍ كَاذِبَةٍ خَاطِئَةٍ nāṣiyatin kādhibatin khāṭi-atin A lying, sinning forelock. See 96:6

item.title: Al-Alaq:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: نَاصِيَةٍ كَاذِبَةٍ خَاطِئَةٍ nāṣiyatin kādhibatin khāṭi-atin A forelock, lying, sinful! This is the description of the qualities of the man Abu Jahl. The parts of his body are taken for his personality.

item.title: Al-Alaq:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلْيَدْعُ نَادِيَهُ falyadʿu nādiyahu Then let him call out his gang!

item.title: Al-Alaq:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلْيَدْعُ نَادِيَهُ falyadʿu nādiyahu Then let him call his associates. See 96:6

item.title: Al-Alaq:17 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلْيَدْعُ نَادِيَهُ falyadʿu nādiyahu Then let him summon his fellows in council When Abu Jahl will be receiving the return for his disbelief and wickedness, i.e., when on the Day of Judgment, he will be committed to the hell-fire, let him then call his council of assembly to his aid, i.e., his council will be of no avail to him then.

item.title: Al-Alaq:18 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: سَنَدْعُ الزَّبَانِيَةَ sanadʿu l-zabāniyata We [too] shall call the keepers of hell.

item.title: Al-Alaq:18 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: سَنَدْعُ الزَّبَانِيَةَ sanadʿu l-zabāniyata We will call the angels of Hell.1 See 96:6

item.title: Al-Alaq:18 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: سَنَدْعُ الزَّبَانِيَةَ sanadʿu l-zabāniyata We too will summon the Angels of the Hell (to punish) Abu Jahl will not be able to call any one to his help nor will any one of his councils be able to be of any avail to him. On the other hand, angels will be called to execute the punishment to him. Though the reference is to Abu Jahl and the address is to the Holy Prophet, in fact the Holy Prophet was not the one to have been even in the least affected or influenced by Abu Jahl's threats in having his own way. It is a command to mankind never to adhere or care for such threats or any evil influences in the execution of the prescribed duties, particularly in the matter of paying obeisance to the Lord but to go on…

item.title: Al-Alaq:19 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا لَا تُطِعْهُ وَاسْجُدْ وَاقْتَرِبْ kallā lā tuṭiʿ'hu wa-us'jud wa-iq'tarib No indeed! Do not obey him, but prostrate and draw near [to Allah]!

item.title: Al-Alaq:19 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا لَا تُطِعْهُ وَاسْجُدْ وَاقْتَرِبْ kallā lā tuṭiʿ'hu wa-us'jud wa-iq'tarib No! Do not obey him. But prostrate and draw near (to Allah). See 96:6

item.title: Al-Alaq:19 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا لَا تُطِعْهُ وَاسْجُدْ وَاقْتَرِبْ kallā lā tuṭiʿ'hu wa-us'jud wa-iq'tarib Nay! Heed him not! Prostrate thou in obeisance (unto thy Lord) and draw thyself near (unto Him)! According to Shafayi, none of the verses of Qur'an recommending Sajdah is compulsory and according to Abu-Haneefa all the places, where the Sajdah is mentioned is Wajib - and according to the School of Ahl Al-Bayt 'Sajdah' is 'Wajib' only in four places: (1) Alif, Lam, Sajdah, (2) Ha Meem. Sajdah, (3) 'An-Najm' and (4) Iqra and in the other places, it is optional. (A.P.).

item.title: Al-An'aam:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَجَعَلَ الظُّلُمَاتِ وَالنُّورَ ثُمَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا بِرَبِّهِمْ يَعْدِلُونَ al-ḥamdu lillahi alladhī khalaqa l-samāwāti wal-arḍa wajaʿala l-ẓulumāti wal-nūra thumma alladhīna kafarū birabbihim yaʿdilūna All praise belongs to Allah who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light. Yet the faithless equate [others] with their Lord.

item.title: Al-An'aam:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَجَعَلَ الظُّلُمَاتِ وَالنُّورَ ثُمَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا بِرَبِّهِمْ يَعْدِلُونَ al-ḥamdu lillahi alladhī khalaqa l-samāwāti wal-arḍa wajaʿala l-ẓulumāti wal-nūra thumma alladhīna kafarū birabbihim yaʿdilūna (All) praise is (due) to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darkness and the light. Then those who disbelieve equate (others) with their Lord. وَهُوَ اللَّهُ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَفِي الْأَرْضِ يَعْلَمُ سِرَّكُمْ وَجَهْرَكُمْ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا تَكْسِبُونَ And He is Allah in the heavens and the earth, He knows what you conceal and what you reveal, and He knows what you earn. Meaning, it is He Who is called Allah, throughout the heavens and the earth, that is, it is He who is worshipped, singled out, whose divinity is believed in by the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth. They call Him Allah, and they supplicate to…

item.title: Al-An'aam:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَجَعَلَ الظُّلُمَاتِ وَالنُّورَ ثُمَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا بِرَبِّهِمْ يَعْدِلُونَ al-ḥamdu lillahi alladhī khalaqa l-samāwāti wal-arḍa wajaʿala l-ẓulumāti wal-nūra thumma alladhīna kafarū birabbihim yaʿdilūna All praise is God's, Who created the heavens and the earth and caused the darkness and the light; yet those who disbelieve set up equals with their Lord. God being presented here as the Maker of both the darkness and the light, is only in contrast to the dualistic faith of the Magians which give co-eternal existence to darkness as well as to light. Islam as a pure and a strict monotheistic religion establishes the truth that the ultimate genetic cause of everything in the universe, be that in the heavens or in the earth or in between them is God and none else. By its pure monotheism Islam wants to make…

item.title: Al-An'aam:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ طِينٍ ثُمَّ قَضَى أَجَلًا وَأَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى عِنْدَهُ ثُمَّ أَنْتُمْ تَمْتَرُونَ huwa alladhī khalaqakum min ṭīnin thumma qaḍā ajalan wa-ajalun musamman ʿindahu thumma antum tamtarūna It is He who created you from clay, then ordained the term [of your life] —the specified term is with Him— and yet you are in doubt.

item.title: Al-An'aam:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ طِينٍ ثُمَّ قَضَى أَجَلًا وَأَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى عِنْدَهُ ثُمَّ أَنْتُمْ تَمْتَرُونَ huwa alladhī khalaqakum min ṭīnin thumma qaḍā ajalan wa-ajalun musamman ʿindahu thumma antum tamtarūna It is He who created you from clay and then decreed a term1 and a specified time (known) to Him;2 then (still) you are in dispute. See 6:1

item.title: Al-An'aam:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ طِينٍ ثُمَّ قَضَى أَجَلًا وَأَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى عِنْدَهُ ثُمَّ أَنْتُمْ تَمْتَرُونَ huwa alladhī khalaqakum min ṭīnin thumma qaḍā ajalan wa-ajalun musamman ʿindahu thumma antum tamtarūna He it is Who Created you of clay, then decreed the term (In Arabic Ajl. Refer to Verse 82:7.) (of your life); and the term determined (Lit. fixed time for resurrection or judgment.) is with Him and yet (In spite of all the changes obvious to you.) ye doubt (About the fixity of the term.) (thereof). 'Created you', 'You' stands for Adam the Progenitor of the human species or every human being, or the address can be to any creature on earth. The origin of every earthly thing is from clay. The first term is the life until death and the second one, is the resurrection. However, all men are created from…

item.title: Al-An'aam:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهُوَ اللَّهُ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَفِي الْأَرْضِ يَعْلَمُ سِرَّكُمْ وَجَهْرَكُمْ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا تَكْسِبُونَ wahuwa l-lahu fī l-samāwāti wafī l-arḍi yaʿlamu sirrakum wajahrakum wayaʿlamu mā taksibūna He is Allah in the heavens and on the earth: He knows your secret and your overt [matters], and He knows what you earn.

item.title: Al-An'aam:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهُوَ اللَّهُ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَفِي الْأَرْضِ يَعْلَمُ سِرَّكُمْ وَجَهْرَكُمْ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا تَكْسِبُونَ wahuwa l-lahu fī l-samāwāti wafī l-arḍi yaʿlamu sirrakum wajahrakum wayaʿlamu mā taksibūna And He is Allah, (the only deity) in the heavens and the earth. He knows your secret and what you make public, and He knows that which you earn. See 6:1

item.title: Al-An'aam:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهُوَ اللَّهُ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَفِي الْأَرْضِ يَعْلَمُ سِرَّكُمْ وَجَهْرَكُمْ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا تَكْسِبُونَ wahuwa l-lahu fī l-samāwāti wafī l-arḍi yaʿlamu sirrakum wajahrakum wayaʿlamu mā taksibūna And (While.) He is God in the heavens and in the earth! He knoweth your secrets and your disclosures! and He knoweth what ye earn (for yourselves by your deeds). This is a repeated assertion of the Unity of God, the Only Creator, Lord, Cherisher of the Universe. He is the Knower of everything, be it hidden or manifest. Hidden and manifest are the two terms that are related only to man; for, to God nothing can be hidden for He is the maker of everything. Everything is in His view, and nothing is out of His knowledge. His knowledge envelops everything1. This is a warning as well, meaning, let not anyone think that what one…

item.title: Al-An'aam:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا تَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ اٰیَةٍ مِنْ اٰیٰتِ رَبِّهِمْ إِلَّا كَانُوْۤا عَنْهَا مُعْرِضِينَ wamā tatīhim min āyatin min āyāti rabbihim illā kānū ʿanhā muʿ'riḍīna There did not come to them any sign from among the signs of their Lord, but that they used to disregard it.

item.title: Al-An'aam:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا تَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ اٰیَةٍ مِنْ اٰیٰتِ رَبِّهِمْ إِلَّا كَانُوْۤا عَنْهَا مُعْرِضِينَ wamā tatīhim min āyatin min āyāti rabbihim illā kānū ʿanhā muʿ'riḍīna And no sign comes to them from the signs of their Lord except that they turn away therefrom. And never an Ayah comes to them from the Ayat of their Lord, but that they have been turning away from it (6:4). Indeed, they rejected the truth when it came to them, but there will come to them the news of that which they used to mock at (6:5). Have they not seen how many a generation before them We have destroyed whom We had established on the earth such as We have not established you? And We poured out on them rain from the sky in abundance, and made the rivers flow under them. Yet We destroyed them…

item.title: Al-An'aam:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا تَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ اٰیَةٍ مِنْ اٰیٰتِ رَبِّهِمْ إِلَّا كَانُوْۤا عَنْهَا مُعْرِضِينَ wamā tatīhim min āyatin min āyāti rabbihim illā kānū ʿanhā muʿ'riḍīna There came not unto them any sign from the signs of their Lord but they turned away from it. 'Aayaat' means signs, revelations, communications - Every Prophet or Apostle and every divinely commissioned successor of the Holy Prophet (i.e., the Imams) all were the 'Aayaat', i.e., the signs through whom God and godliness was manifested into this world.

item.title: Al-An'aam:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوْۤا بِالْحَقِّ لَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ فَسَوْفَ يَأْتِيهِمْ أَنبَؤُا مَا كَانُوْۤا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ faqad kadhabū bil-ḥaqi lammā jāahum fasawfa yatīhim anbāu mā kānū bihi yastahziūna They certainly denied the truth when it came to them, but soon there will come to them the news of what they have been deriding.

item.title: Al-An'aam:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوْۤا بِالْحَقِّ لَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ فَسَوْفَ يَأْتِيهِمْ أَنبَؤُا مَا كَانُوْۤا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ faqad kadhabū bil-ḥaqi lammā jāahum fasawfa yatīhim anbāu mā kānū bihi yastahziūna For they had denied the truth when it came to them, but there is going to reach them the news of what they used to ridicule.1 See 6:4

item.title: Al-An'aam:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوْۤا بِالْحَقِّ لَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ فَسَوْفَ يَأْتِيهِمْ أَنبَؤُا مَا كَانُوْۤا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ faqad kadhabū bil-ḥaqi lammā jāahum fasawfa yatīhim anbāu mā kānū bihi yastahziūna They have indeed belied the truth when it came to them; therefore, very soon the tidings (News- Tidings, i.e. about the Truth.) will come (be known) to them of what they mocked at. See 6:4

item.title: Al-An'aam:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَمْ يَرَوْا كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِنْ قَرْنٍ مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَا لَمْ نُمَكِّنْ لَكُمْ وَأَرْسَلْنَا السَّمَاءَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِدْرَارًا وَجَعَلْنَا الْأَنْهَارَ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهِمْ فَأَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ وَأَنْشَأْنَا مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ قَرْنًا ءَاخَرِينَ alam yaraw kam ahlaknā min qablihim min qarnin makkannāhum fī l-arḍi mā lam numakkin lakum wa-arsalnā l-samāa ʿalayhim mid'rāran wajaʿalnā l-anhāra tajrī min taḥtihim fa-ahlaknāhum bidhunūbihim wa-anshanā min baʿdihim qarnan ākharīna Have they not regarded how many a generation We have destroyed before them whom We had granted power in the land in respects that We did not grant you, and We sent abundant rains for them from the sky and made streams run for them. Then We destroyed them for their sins, and brought forth another generation after them.

item.title: Al-An'aam:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَمْ يَرَوْا كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِنْ قَرْنٍ مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَا لَمْ نُمَكِّنْ لَكُمْ وَأَرْسَلْنَا السَّمَاءَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِدْرَارًا وَجَعَلْنَا الْأَنْهَارَ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهِمْ فَأَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ وَأَنْشَأْنَا مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ قَرْنًا ءَاخَرِينَ alam yaraw kam ahlaknā min qablihim min qarnin makkannāhum fī l-arḍi mā lam numakkin lakum wa-arsalnā l-samāa ʿalayhim mid'rāran wajaʿalnā l-anhāra tajrī min taḥtihim fa-ahlaknāhum bidhunūbihim wa-anshanā min baʿdihim qarnan ākharīna Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them which We had established upon the earth as We have not established you? And We sent (rain from) the sky upon them in showers and made rivers flow beneath them; then We destroyed them for their sins and brought forth after them a generation of others. See 6:4

item.title: Al-An'aam:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَمْ يَرَوْا كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِنْ قَرْنٍ مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَا لَمْ نُمَكِّنْ لَكُمْ وَأَرْسَلْنَا السَّمَاءَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِدْرَارًا وَجَعَلْنَا الْأَنْهَارَ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهِمْ فَأَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ وَأَنْشَأْنَا مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ قَرْنًا ءَاخَرِينَ alam yaraw kam ahlaknā min qablihim min qarnin makkannāhum fī l-arḍi mā lam numakkin lakum wa-arsalnā l-samāa ʿalayhim mid'rāran wajaʿalnā l-anhāra tajrī min taḥtihim fa-ahlaknāhum bidhunūbihim wa-anshanā min baʿdihim qarnan ākharīna See they not how many a generation before them We have destroyed, whom We had established in the earth (to the extent to) which We had not yet established you (till now), and We sent the clouds to rain abundantly upon them, and We made the rivers flow beneath (their dwellings) and yea We destroyed them for their sins and raised (The modern time excavations and the findings of the ancient cities buried - prove the truth in…

item.title: Al-An'aam:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَوْ نَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ كِتَابًا فِي قِرْطَاسٍ فَلَمَسُوهُ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ لَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا إِنْ هَذَا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ walaw nazzalnā ʿalayka kitāban fī qir'ṭāsin falamasūhu bi-aydīhim laqāla alladhīna kafarū in hādhā illā siḥ'run mubīnun Had We sent down to you a Book on paper so they could touch it with their [own] hands, [still] the faithless would have said, 'This is nothing but plain magic.'

item.title: Al-An'aam:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَوْ نَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ كِتَابًا فِي قِرْطَاسٍ فَلَمَسُوهُ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ لَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا إِنْ هَذَا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ walaw nazzalnā ʿalayka kitāban fī qir'ṭāsin falamasūhu bi-aydīhim laqāla alladhīna kafarū in hādhā illā siḥ'run mubīnun And even if We had sent down to you, (O Muḥammad), a written scripture on a page and they touched it with their hands, the disbelievers would say, "This is not but obvious magic." And even if We had sent down unto you a Message written on paper so that they could touch it with their hands, the disbelievers would have said: "This is nothing but obvious magic! (6:7). And they say: "Why has not an angel been sent down to him" Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been judged at once, and no respite would be granted to them (6:8). And had We…

item.title: Al-An'aam:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَوْ نَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ كِتَابًا فِي قِرْطَاسٍ فَلَمَسُوهُ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ لَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا إِنْ هَذَا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ walaw nazzalnā ʿalayka kitāban fī qir'ṭāsin falamasūhu bi-aydīhim laqāla alladhīna kafarū in hādhā illā siḥ'run mubīnun And had We sent down unto thee a book written on a paper, and they had touched it with their hands, surely those who disbelieved had said, "This is naught but obvious sorcery (A similar demand was made to Moses. Refer to Verse 4:153.) ." See 6:4

item.title: Al-An'aam:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالُوْۤا لَوْلَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ مَلَكٌ وَلَوْ أَنْزَلْنَا مَلَكًا لَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ ثُمَّ لَا يُنْظَرُونَ waqālū lawlā unzila ʿalayhi malakun walaw anzalnā malakan laquḍiya l-amru thumma lā yunẓarūna And they say, 'Why has not an angel been sent down to him?' Were We to send down an angel, the matter would surely be decided, and then they would not be granted any respite.

item.title: Al-An'aam:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالُوْۤا لَوْلَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ مَلَكٌ وَلَوْ أَنْزَلْنَا مَلَكًا لَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ ثُمَّ لَا يُنْظَرُونَ waqālū lawlā unzila ʿalayhi malakun walaw anzalnā malakan laquḍiya l-amru thumma lā yunẓarūna And they say, "Why was there not sent down to him an angel?"1 But if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided;2 then they would not be reprieved. See 6:7

item.title: Al-An'aam:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالُوْۤا لَوْلَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ مَلَكٌ وَلَوْ أَنْزَلْنَا مَلَكًا لَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ ثُمَّ لَا يُنْظَرُونَ waqālū lawlā unzila ʿalayhi malakun walaw anzalnā malakan laquḍiya l-amru thumma lā yunẓarūna And they say "Why has not an angel been sent down unto him (The Holy Prophet Muhammad.) ?" And had We sent down an angel the matter would certainly have been decided (About their activity or efforts. Refer to Verse 2:210.) (once for all) and then they would not have been respited. 'The matter would have been certainly decided' means that punishment would certainly have followed any rejection thereafter1.

item.title: Al-An'aam:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَوْ جَعَلْنَاهُ مَلَكًا لَجَعَلْنَاهُ رَجُلًا وَلَلَبَسْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ مَا يَلْبِسُونَ walaw jaʿalnāhu malakan lajaʿalnāhu rajulan walalabasnā ʿalayhim mā yalbisūna And had We made him1 an angel, We would have surely made him a man, and We would have surely confounded them in regard to [the truth] that they confound.

item.title: Al-An'aam:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَوْ جَعَلْنَاهُ مَلَكًا لَجَعَلْنَاهُ رَجُلًا وَلَلَبَسْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ مَا يَلْبِسُونَ walaw jaʿalnāhu malakan lajaʿalnāhu rajulan walalabasnā ʿalayhim mā yalbisūna And if We had made him (i.e., the messenger) an angel, We would have made him (appear as) a man, and We would have covered them with that in which they cover themselves (i.e., confusion and doubt). See 6:7

item.title: Al-An'aam:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَوْ جَعَلْنَاهُ مَلَكًا لَجَعَلْنَاهُ رَجُلًا وَلَلَبَسْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ مَا يَلْبِسُونَ walaw jaʿalnāhu malakan lajaʿalnāhu rajulan walalabasnā ʿalayhim mā yalbisūna And had We made him an Angel, We would have certainly made him a man (Even it an angel had been sent he would have necessarily come in human form for the angelic state is far from Social Contact with men of the low mentality and it would not have removed the state of their confusion.) , and We would certainly have made confused to them what they (now) make confused. Even if an angel had been deputed to act as an Apostle to men, he would also have been in human form for the physical eye of man, can see things material and in some form or other - and even then, the circumstances for men would have been the same.…

item.title: Al-An'aam:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدِ اسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ فَحَاقَ بِالَّذِينَ سَخِرُوْۤا مِنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوْۤا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ walaqadi us'tuh'zi-a birusulin min qablika faḥāqa bi-alladhīna sakhirū min'hum mā kānū bihi yastahziūna Apostles were certainly derided before you. Then those who ridiculed them were besieged by what they used to deride.

item.title: Al-An'aam:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدِ اسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ فَحَاقَ بِالَّذِينَ سَخِرُوْۤا مِنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوْۤا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ walaqadi us'tuh'zi-a birusulin min qablika faḥāqa bi-alladhīna sakhirū min'hum mā kānū bihi yastahziūna And already were messengers ridiculed before you, but those who mocked them were enveloped by that which they used to ridicule. See 6:7

item.title: Al-An'aam:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدِ اسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ فَحَاقَ بِالَّذِينَ سَخِرُوْۤا مِنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوْۤا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ walaqadi us'tuh'zi-a birusulin min qablika faḥāqa bi-alladhīna sakhirū min'hum mā kānū bihi yastahziūna And certainly, were mocked (many) apostles before thee but that which they mocked at encompassed the scoffers among them (Refer to Verses 21:41; 36:30.) . It is a reference to the people of Noah, Lot, Aad and Thamud who ridiculed the apostles, and acted rebelliously and were destroyed. It indirectly infers that the ultimate success will be of the Holy Prophet and the Jews and the Christians who ridiculed him and his message, will be subjugated under his control.

item.title: Al-An'aam:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ سِيرُوْۤا فِي الْأَرْضِ ثُمَّ انْظُرُوْۤا كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ qul sīrū fī l-arḍi thumma unẓurū kayfa kāna ʿāqibatu l-mukadhibīna Say, 'Travel over the land, and then observe how was the fate of the deniers.'

item.title: Al-An'aam:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ سِيرُوْۤا فِي الْأَرْضِ ثُمَّ انْظُرُوْۤا كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ qul sīrū fī l-arḍi thumma unẓurū kayfa kāna ʿāqibatu l-mukadhibīna Say, "Travel through the land; then observe how was the end of the deniers." See 6:7

item.title: Al-An'aam:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ سِيرُوْۤا فِي الْأَرْضِ ثُمَّ انْظُرُوْۤا كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ qul sīrū fī l-arḍi thumma unẓurū kayfa kāna ʿāqibatu l-mukadhibīna Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Travel (Encouraging the study of the terrestrial conditions - and the fate of the wicked ones - and draw lessons from it.) ye in the earth; then see ye what hath been the end of the beliers (of our apostles')." See 6:10

item.title: Al-An'aam:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ لِمَنْ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ قُلْ لِلَّهِ كَتَبَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ الرَّحْمَةَ لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ لَا رَيْبَ فِیْهِ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوْۤا أَنْفُسَهُمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ qul liman mā fī l-samāwāti wal-arḍi qul lillahi kataba ʿalā nafsihi l-raḥmata layajmaʿannakum ilā yawmi l-qiyāmati lā rayba fīhi alladhīna khasirū anfusahum fahum lā yu'minūna Say, 'To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth?' Say, 'To Allah. He has made mercy incumbent upon Himself. He will surely gather you on the Day of Resurrection, in which there is no doubt. Those who have ruined their souls1 will not have faith.'

item.title: Al-An'aam:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ لِمَنْ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ قُلْ لِلَّهِ كَتَبَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ الرَّحْمَةَ لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ لَا رَيْبَ فِیْهِ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوْۤا أَنْفُسَهُمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ qul liman mā fī l-samāwāti wal-arḍi qul lillahi kataba ʿalā nafsihi l-raḥmata layajmaʿannakum ilā yawmi l-qiyāmati lā rayba fīhi alladhīna khasirū anfusahum fahum lā yu'minūna Say, "To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth?" Say, "To Allah." He has decreed upon Himself mercy. He will surely assemble you for the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. Those who will lose themselves (that Day) do not believe. Say: To whom belongs all that is in the heavens and the earth?" Say: "To Allah." He has prescribed mercy for Himself. Indeed He will gather you together on the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. Those who destroy themselves will…

item.title: Al-An'aam:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ لِمَنْ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ قُلْ لِلَّهِ كَتَبَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ الرَّحْمَةَ لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ لَا رَيْبَ فِیْهِ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوْۤا أَنْفُسَهُمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ qul liman mā fī l-samāwāti wal-arḍi qul lillahi kataba ʿalā nafsihi l-raḥmata layajmaʿannakum ilā yawmi l-qiyāmati lā rayba fīhi alladhīna khasirū anfusahum fahum lā yu'minūna Say! "To whom belongeth what is in the heavens and the earth?" Say thou "To God; He hath prescribed (With the explanation of the universe being God's and there being a collective stage when all will be viewed together. It is inevitable that His treatment to all will be based only on His grace. (A.P.).) mercy on Himself; Most certainly He will gather you on the Resurrection Day, there is no doubt about it; (As for) those who have lost (ruined) their selves, they will not believe." This Verse refers…

item.title: Al-An'aam:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَهُ مَا سَكَنَ فِي اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ walahu mā sakana fī al-layli wal-nahāri wahuwa l-samīʿu l-ʿalīmu To Him belongs whatever abides in the night and the day, and He is the All-hearing, the All-knowing.

item.title: Al-An'aam:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَهُ مَا سَكَنَ فِي اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ walahu mā sakana fī al-layli wal-nahāri wahuwa l-samīʿu l-ʿalīmu And to Him belongs that which reposes by night and by day, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing. See 6:12

item.title: Al-An'aam:13 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَهُ مَا سَكَنَ فِي اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ walahu mā sakana fī al-layli wal-nahāri wahuwa l-samīʿu l-ʿalīmu And to Him belongeth whatever dwelleth in the night and the day; And He is the All-Hearing and the All-Knowing. See 6:12

item.title: Al-An'aam:14 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أَتَّخِذُ وَلِيًّا فَاطِرِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ يُطْعِمُ وَلَا يُطْعَمُ قُلْ اِنِّیْ أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ qul aghayra l-lahi attakhidhu waliyyan fāṭiri l-samāwāti wal-arḍi wahuwa yuṭ'ʿimu walā yuṭ'ʿamu qul innī umir'tu an akūna awwala man aslama walā takūnanna mina l-mush'rikīna Say, 'Shall I take for guardian [anyone] other than Allah, the originator of the heavens and the earth, who feeds and is not fed?' Say, 'I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit [to Allah],' and never be one of the polytheists.

item.title: Al-An'aam:14 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أَتَّخِذُ وَلِيًّا فَاطِرِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ يُطْعِمُ وَلَا يُطْعَمُ قُلْ اِنِّیْ أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ qul aghayra l-lahi attakhidhu waliyyan fāṭiri l-samāwāti wal-arḍi wahuwa yuṭ'ʿimu walā yuṭ'ʿamu qul innī umir'tu an akūna awwala man aslama walā takūnanna mina l-mush'rikīna Say, "Is it other than Allah I should take as a protector, Creator of the heavens and earth, while it is He who feeds and is not fed?" Say, (O Muḥammad), "Indeed, I have been commanded to be the first (among you) who submit (to Allah) and (was commanded), 'Do not ever be of the polytheists.'" See 6:12

item.title: Al-An'aam:14 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أَتَّخِذُ وَلِيًّا فَاطِرِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ يُطْعِمُ وَلَا يُطْعَمُ قُلْ اِنِّیْ أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ qul aghayra l-lahi attakhidhu waliyyan fāṭiri l-samāwāti wal-arḍi wahuwa yuṭ'ʿimu walā yuṭ'ʿamu qul innī umir'tu an akūna awwala man aslama walā takūnanna mina l-mush'rikīna Say, "Shall I take a guardian besides God, the Originator of the heavens and the earth? while He feedeth (Sustains.) (others) and is not (Himself) fed (Not Sustained.) Say! "I (The Holy Prophet Muhammad.) am commanded to be the first who submitteth himself (to God) (Refer to Verse 39:12.) " and be not thou (The Prophet addressed for the people.) of the polytheists (Those who associate others with God in authority.) ." Some critics say that this passage and the other similar ones which present the Holy Prophet as the first Muslim1…

item.title: Al-An'aam:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ اِنِّیْ أَخَافُ إِنْ عَصَيْتُ رَبِّي عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ qul innī akhāfu in ʿaṣaytu rabbī ʿadhāba yawmin ʿaẓīmin Say, 'Indeed, should I disobey my Lord, I fear the punishment of a tremendous day.'

item.title: Al-An'aam:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ اِنِّیْ أَخَافُ إِنْ عَصَيْتُ رَبِّي عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ qul innī akhāfu in ʿaṣaytu rabbī ʿadhāba yawmin ʿaẓīmin Say, "Indeed I fear, if I should disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day." See 6:12

item.title: Al-An'aam:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ اِنِّیْ أَخَافُ إِنْ عَصَيْتُ رَبِّي عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ qul innī akhāfu in ʿaṣaytu rabbī ʿadhāba yawmin ʿaẓīmin Say! (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Verily I fear should I disobey my Lord, the chastisement of a great Day." See 6:14

item.title: Al-An'aam:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَنْ يُصْرَفْ عَنْهُ يَوْمَئِذٍ فَقَدْ رَحِمَهُ وَذٰلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْمُبِينُ man yuṣ'raf ʿanhu yawma-idhin faqad raḥimahu wadhālika l-fawzu l-mubīnu Whoever is spared of it on that day, He has certainly been merciful to him, and that is the manifest success.

item.title: Al-An'aam:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَنْ يُصْرَفْ عَنْهُ يَوْمَئِذٍ فَقَدْ رَحِمَهُ وَذٰلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْمُبِينُ man yuṣ'raf ʿanhu yawma-idhin faqad raḥimahu wadhālika l-fawzu l-mubīnu He from whom it is averted that Day - (Allah) has granted him mercy. And that is the clear attainment. See 6:12

item.title: Al-An'aam:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَنْ يُصْرَفْ عَنْهُ يَوْمَئِذٍ فَقَدْ رَحِمَهُ وَذٰلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْمُبِينُ man yuṣ'raf ʿanhu yawma-idhin faqad raḥimahu wadhālika l-fawzu l-mubīnu From whomsoever it (the Chastisement) is averted on that day, indeed He (God.) had mercy ('Rahimiyat' not 'Rahmaniyat'.) on him; and this will be the manifest triumph (Salvation.) ". See 6:14

item.title: Al-An'aam:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنْ يَمْسَسْكَ اللَّهُ بِضُرٍّ فَلَا كَاشِفَ لَهُ إِلَّا هُوَ وَإِنْ يَمْسَسْكَ بِخَيْرٍ فَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ wa-in yamsaska l-lahu biḍurrin falā kāshifa lahu illā huwa wa-in yamsaska bikhayrin fahuwa ʿalā kulli shayin qadīrun Should Allah visit you with some distress there is no one to remove it except Him; and should He bring you some good, then He has power over all things.

item.title: Al-An'aam:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنْ يَمْسَسْكَ اللَّهُ بِضُرٍّ فَلَا كَاشِفَ لَهُ إِلَّا هُوَ وَإِنْ يَمْسَسْكَ بِخَيْرٍ فَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ wa-in yamsaska l-lahu biḍurrin falā kāshifa lahu illā huwa wa-in yamsaska bikhayrin fahuwa ʿalā kulli shayin qadīrun And if Allah should touch you with adversity, there is no remover of it except Him. And if He touches you with good - then He is over all things competent. And if Allah touches you with harm, none can remove it but He, and if He touches you with good, then He is able to do all things (6:17). And He is the Irresistible, above His servants, and He is the All-Wise, Well-Acquainted with all things (6:18). Say: What thing is the most great in witness?" Say: "Allah is Witness between you and I; this Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may therewith…

item.title: Al-An'aam:17 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنْ يَمْسَسْكَ اللَّهُ بِضُرٍّ فَلَا كَاشِفَ لَهُ إِلَّا هُوَ وَإِنْ يَمْسَسْكَ بِخَيْرٍ فَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ wa-in yamsaska l-lahu biḍurrin falā kāshifa lahu illā huwa wa-in yamsaska bikhayrin fahuwa ʿalā kulli shayin qadīrun And if God toucheth thee with affliction, none can remove it but He; and if He toucheth thee with Good, then He hath power over all things. Meaning the soul, the Only and the Supreme Master doing good or harming anyone, whose decision is ever irrevocable, is God and none else. Hence man needs to love or to fear only God and no other authority and to depend only on Hint and on none else.

item.title: Al-An'aam:18 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهُوَ الْقَاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِ وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ wahuwa l-qāhiru fawqa ʿibādihi wahuwa l-ḥakīmu l-khabīru And He is the All-dominant over His servants, and He is the All-wise, the All-aware.

item.title: Al-An'aam:18 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهُوَ الْقَاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِ وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ wahuwa l-qāhiru fawqa ʿibādihi wahuwa l-ḥakīmu l-khabīru And He is the subjugator over His servants. And He is the Wise,1 the Aware.2 See 6:17

item.title: Al-An'aam:18 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهُوَ الْقَاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِ وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ wahuwa l-qāhiru fawqa ʿibādihi wahuwa l-ḥakīmu l-khabīru He is the Supreme (Lord) above (In authority with wisdom and awareness.) His servants (Creatures.) ; and He is the All-Wise and the All-Aware. See 6:17

item.title: Al-An'aam:19 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ أَيُّ شَيْءٍ أَكْبَرُ شَهَادَةً قُلِ اللَّهُ شَهِيدٌ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ وَأُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ هَذَا الْقُرْاٰنُ لِأُنْذِرَكُمْ بِهِ وَمَنْ بَلَغَ أَئِنَّكُمْ لَتَشْهَدُونَ أَنَّ مَعَ اللَّهِ آلِهَةً أُخْرٰی قُلْ لَا أَشْهَدُ قُلْ إِنَّمَا هُوَ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ وَإِنَّنِي بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تُشْرِكُونَ qul ayyu shayin akbaru shahādatan quli l-lahu shahīdun baynī wabaynakum waūḥiya ilayya hādhā l-qur'ānu li-undhirakum bihi waman balagha a-innakum latashhadūna anna maʿa l-lahi ālihatan ukh'rā qul lā ashhadu qul innamā huwa ilāhun wāḥidun wa-innanī barīon mimmā tush'rikūna Say, 'What thing is greatest as witness?' Say, 'Allah! [He is] witness between me and you, and this Qur'ān has been revealed to me that I may warn thereby you and whomever it may reach.' 'Do you indeed bear witness that there are other gods besides Allah?' Say, 'I do not bear witness [to any such thing].' Say, 'Indeed He is the One God, and I…

item.title: Al-An'aam:19 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ أَيُّ شَيْءٍ أَكْبَرُ شَهَادَةً قُلِ اللَّهُ شَهِيدٌ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ وَأُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ هَذَا الْقُرْاٰنُ لِأُنْذِرَكُمْ بِهِ وَمَنْ بَلَغَ أَئِنَّكُمْ لَتَشْهَدُونَ أَنَّ مَعَ اللَّهِ آلِهَةً أُخْرٰی قُلْ لَا أَشْهَدُ قُلْ إِنَّمَا هُوَ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ وَإِنَّنِي بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تُشْرِكُونَ qul ayyu shayin akbaru shahādatan quli l-lahu shahīdun baynī wabaynakum waūḥiya ilayya hādhā l-qur'ānu li-undhirakum bihi waman balagha a-innakum latashhadūna anna maʿa l-lahi ālihatan ukh'rā qul lā ashhadu qul innamā huwa ilāhun wāḥidun wa-innanī barīon mimmā tush'rikūna Say, "What thing is greatest in testimony?" Say, "Allah is witness between me and you. And this Qur’ān was revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whomever it reaches.1 Do you (truly) testify that with Allah there are other deities?" Say, "I will not testify (with you)." Say, "Indeed, He is but one God, and indeed, I am free of what you associate…

item.title: Al-An'aam:19 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ أَيُّ شَيْءٍ أَكْبَرُ شَهَادَةً قُلِ اللَّهُ شَهِيدٌ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ وَأُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ هَذَا الْقُرْاٰنُ لِأُنْذِرَكُمْ بِهِ وَمَنْ بَلَغَ أَئِنَّكُمْ لَتَشْهَدُونَ أَنَّ مَعَ اللَّهِ آلِهَةً أُخْرٰی قُلْ لَا أَشْهَدُ قُلْ إِنَّمَا هُوَ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ وَإِنَّنِي بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تُشْرِكُونَ qul ayyu shayin akbaru shahādatan quli l-lahu shahīdun baynī wabaynakum waūḥiya ilayya hādhā l-qur'ānu li-undhirakum bihi waman balagha a-innakum latashhadūna anna maʿa l-lahi ālihatan ukh'rā qul lā ashhadu qul innamā huwa ilāhun wāḥidun wa-innanī barīon mimmā tush'rikūna Say! (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "What thing is the weightiest in testimony?" Say thou: "God is witness between me and you; and hath been revealed unto me this Qur'an (As the divine evidence.) that I may warn you with it, and whomsoever it reacheth (Indicates the. universality of 'the mission of the Holy Prophet compared to that of those before him.) ; Do ye really bear…

item.title: Al-An'aam:20 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِينَ ءَاتَيْنَاهُمُ الْكِتَابَ يَعْرِفُونَهُ كَمَا يَعْرِفُونَ أَبْنَاءَهُمُ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوْۤا أَنْفُسَهُمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ alladhīna ātaynāhumu l-kitāba yaʿrifūnahu kamā yaʿrifūna abnāahumu alladhīna khasirū anfusahum fahum lā yu'minūna Those whom We have given the Book recognize him just as they recognize their sons.1 Those who have ruined their souls will not have faith.

item.title: Al-An'aam:20 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِينَ ءَاتَيْنَاهُمُ الْكِتَابَ يَعْرِفُونَهُ كَمَا يَعْرِفُونَ أَبْنَاءَهُمُ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوْۤا أَنْفُسَهُمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ alladhīna ātaynāhumu l-kitāba yaʿrifūnahu kamā yaʿrifūna abnāahumu alladhīna khasirū anfusahum fahum lā yu'minūna Those to whom We have given the Scripture recognize it1 as they recognize their (own) sons. Those who will lose themselves (in the Hereafter) do not believe. See 6:17

item.title: Al-An'aam:20 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِينَ ءَاتَيْنَاهُمُ الْكِتَابَ يَعْرِفُونَهُ كَمَا يَعْرِفُونَ أَبْنَاءَهُمُ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوْۤا أَنْفُسَهُمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ alladhīna ātaynāhumu l-kitāba yaʿrifūnahu kamā yaʿrifūna abnāahumu alladhīna khasirū anfusahum fahum lā yu'minūna Those whom We have given the Book recognise him (Muhammad), as they recognise their (own) sons; (yet) those who have lost (Ruined.) their selves, they will not believe. As none can fail to recognize his own son, the prophecies about and the identification of the Holy Prophet was so doubtlessly clear in the ancient scriptures, particularly in the scriptures of the Jews and the Christians and no prophet answering the given description had ever appeared anywhere in the world. The Jews and the Christians had no reasons at all, or there was not the least difficulty for them to recognize the genuine apostolic personality of the Holy Prophet.

item.title: Al-An'aam:21 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرٰی عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا أَوْ كَذَّبَ بِءَايَاتِهِ إِنَّهُ لَا يُفْلِحُ الظَّالِمُونَ waman aẓlamu mimmani if'tarā ʿalā l-lahi kadhiban aw kadhaba biāyātihi innahu lā yuf'liḥu l-ẓālimūna Who is a greater wrongdoer than him who fabricates a lie against Allah, or denies His signs? Indeed the wrongdoers will not be felicitous.

item.title: Al-An'aam:21 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرٰی عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا أَوْ كَذَّبَ بِءَايَاتِهِ إِنَّهُ لَا يُفْلِحُ الظَّالِمُونَ waman aẓlamu mimmani if'tarā ʿalā l-lahi kadhiban aw kadhaba biāyātihi innahu lā yuf'liḥu l-ẓālimūna And who is more unjust than one who invents about Allah a lie or denies His verses? Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed. See 6:17

item.title: Al-An'aam:21 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرٰی عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا أَوْ كَذَّبَ بِءَايَاتِهِ إِنَّهُ لَا يُفْلِحُ الظَّالِمُونَ waman aẓlamu mimmani if'tarā ʿalā l-lahi kadhiban aw kadhaba biāyātihi innahu lā yuf'liḥu l-ẓālimūna And who is more unjust than he who forgeth a lie against God or (he who) giveth the lie to His signs; verily the unjust will not succeed (Refer to Verses 6:94; 6:144; 6:158; 39:32.) . Forging lies against God means saying or believing in things falsely relating them to God, viz. God having a son or sons and daughters or God having delegated His authority to anyone else to act on His behalf - and the similar other heathenic belief. The tone of the set of Verses 6:21 - 6:25 is that of a conversation between two persons before whom the whole scene of the ultimate days was present, as going…

item.title: Al-An'aam:22 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَوْمَ نَحْشُرُهُمْ جَمِيعًا ثُمَّ نَقُولُ لِلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوْۤا أَيْنَ شُرَكَاؤُكُمُ الَّذِينَ كُنْتُمْ تَزْعُمُونَ wayawma naḥshuruhum jamīʿan thumma naqūlu lilladhīna ashrakū ayna shurakāukumu alladhīna kuntum tazʿumūna On the day when We gather them all together, We shall say to those who ascribed partners [to Allah] 'Where are your partners that you used to claim?'

item.title: Al-An'aam:22 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَوْمَ نَحْشُرُهُمْ جَمِيعًا ثُمَّ نَقُولُ لِلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوْۤا أَيْنَ شُرَكَاؤُكُمُ الَّذِينَ كُنْتُمْ تَزْعُمُونَ wayawma naḥshuruhum jamīʿan thumma naqūlu lilladhīna ashrakū ayna shurakāukumu alladhīna kuntum tazʿumūna And (mention, O Muḥammad), the Day We will gather them all together; then We will say to those who associated others with Allah, "Where are your 'partners' that you used to claim (with Him)?" And on the Day when We shall gather them all together, We shall say to those who joined partners in worship (with Us): Where are your partners (false deities) whom you used to assert (as partners in worship with Allah)? (6:22). There will then be (left) no Fitnah for them but to say: "By Allah, our Lord, we were not those who joined others (in worship with Allah) (6:23). Look! How they lie against themselves! But the (lie) which they invented will…

item.title: Al-An'aam:22 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَوْمَ نَحْشُرُهُمْ جَمِيعًا ثُمَّ نَقُولُ لِلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوْۤا أَيْنَ شُرَكَاؤُكُمُ الَّذِينَ كُنْتُمْ تَزْعُمُونَ wayawma naḥshuruhum jamīʿan thumma naqūlu lilladhīna ashrakū ayna shurakāukumu alladhīna kuntum tazʿumūna And on the day (of Judgment) We shall gather them all together, then We shall say to those who associated others (With God.) "Where are your associate-gods whom ye used to conject?" See 6:21

item.title: Al-An'aam:23 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ فِتْنَتُهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ قَالُوْا وَاللَّهِ رَبِّنَا مَا كُنَّا مُشْرِكِينَ thumma lam takun fit'natuhum illā an qālū wal-lahi rabbinā mā kunnā mush'rikīna Then their only excuse will be to say, 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.'

item.title: Al-An'aam:23 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ فِتْنَتُهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ قَالُوْا وَاللَّهِ رَبِّنَا مَا كُنَّا مُشْرِكِينَ thumma lam takun fit'natuhum illā an qālū wal-lahi rabbinā mā kunnā mush'rikīna Then there will be no (excuse upon) examination except they will say, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not those who associated." See 6:22

item.title: Al-An'aam:23 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ فِتْنَتُهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ قَالُوْا وَاللَّهِ رَبِّنَا مَا كُنَّا مُشْرِكِينَ thumma lam takun fit'natuhum illā an qālū wal-lahi rabbinā mā kunnā mush'rikīna Then their excuse (In Arabic 'Fitna', the mischief of their disbelief will not be there.) would be nothing but that they would say: "By God, Our Lord! we were not polytheists." 'Fitna', i.e., the lie they uttered or their disbelief would not remain any longer, but they would say 'By our Lord, ire are not polytheists.'

item.title: Al-An'aam:24 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اُنْظُرْ كَيْفَ كَذَبُوْۤا عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ وَضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوْۤا يَفْتَرُونَ unẓur kayfa kadhabū ʿalā anfusihim waḍalla ʿanhum mā kānū yaftarūna Look, how they forswear themselves, and what they used to fabricate has forsaken them!

item.title: Al-An'aam:24 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اُنْظُرْ كَيْفَ كَذَبُوْۤا عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ وَضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوْۤا يَفْتَرُونَ unẓur kayfa kadhabū ʿalā anfusihim waḍalla ʿanhum mā kānū yaftarūna See how they will lie about themselves. And lost from them will be what they used to invent. See 6:22

item.title: Al-An'aam:24 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اُنْظُرْ كَيْفَ كَذَبُوْۤا عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ وَضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوْۤا يَفْتَرُونَ unẓur kayfa kadhabū ʿalā anfusihim waḍalla ʿanhum mā kānū yaftarūna Behold (In Arabic 'Unzur' Lit. See - This indicates that the whole scene of the day was visualised before the Holy Prophet or he could himself visualise it. Otherwise to Command with something impossible to be implemented will be meaningless.) ! how they lie against their own selves, and that which they forged has passed away from them. See 6:23

item.title: Al-An'aam:25 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُ إِلَيْكَ وَجَعَلْنَا عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ أَكِنَّةً أَنْ يَفْقَهُوهُ وَفِي اٰذَانِهِمْ وَقْرًا وَإِنْ يَرَوْا كُلَّ اٰیَةٍ لَا يُؤْمِنُوْۤا بِهَا حَتّٰی إِذَا جَاءُوكَ يُجَادِلُونَكَ يَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا إِنْ هَذَا إِلَّا أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ wamin'hum man yastamiʿu ilayka wajaʿalnā ʿalā qulūbihim akinnatan an yafqahūhu wafī ādhānihim waqran wa-in yaraw kulla āyatin lā yu'minū bihā ḥattā idhā jāūka yujādilūnaka yaqūlu alladhīna kafarū in hādhā illā asāṭīru l-awalīna There are some of them who prick up their ears at you, but We have cast veils on their hearts lest they should understand it, and a deafness into their ears; and though they should see every sign, they will not believe in it. When they come to you, to dispute with you, the faithless say, 'These are nothing but myths of the ancients.'

item.title: Al-An'aam:25 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُ إِلَيْكَ وَجَعَلْنَا عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ أَكِنَّةً أَنْ يَفْقَهُوهُ وَفِي اٰذَانِهِمْ وَقْرًا وَإِنْ يَرَوْا كُلَّ اٰیَةٍ لَا يُؤْمِنُوْۤا بِهَا حَتّٰی إِذَا جَاءُوكَ يُجَادِلُونَكَ يَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا إِنْ هَذَا إِلَّا أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ wamin'hum man yastamiʿu ilayka wajaʿalnā ʿalā qulūbihim akinnatan an yafqahūhu wafī ādhānihim waqran wa-in yaraw kulla āyatin lā yu'minū bihā ḥattā idhā jāūka yujādilūnaka yaqūlu alladhīna kafarū in hādhā illā asāṭīru l-awalīna And among them are those who listen to you,1 but We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness. And if they should see every sign, they will not believe in it. Even when they come to you arguing with you, those who disbelieve say, "This is not but legends of the former peoples." See 6:22

item.title: Al-An'aam:25 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُ إِلَيْكَ وَجَعَلْنَا عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ أَكِنَّةً أَنْ يَفْقَهُوهُ وَفِي اٰذَانِهِمْ وَقْرًا وَإِنْ يَرَوْا كُلَّ اٰیَةٍ لَا يُؤْمِنُوْۤا بِهَا حَتّٰی إِذَا جَاءُوكَ يُجَادِلُونَكَ يَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا إِنْ هَذَا إِلَّا أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ wamin'hum man yastamiʿu ilayka wajaʿalnā ʿalā qulūbihim akinnatan an yafqahūhu wafī ādhānihim waqran wa-in yaraw kulla āyatin lā yu'minū bihā ḥattā idhā jāūka yujādilūnaka yaqūlu alladhīna kafarū in hādhā illā asāṭīru l-awalīna And of them are those who hearken unto thee, and We have cast veils over their hearts lest they understand it, and a heaviness into their ears; and together (even) if they see every (All the signs i.e. all miracles together.) sign they will not believe in it; to the extent that when they come (Refer to Verse 47:16.) to thee they only dispute with thee, those who disbelieve say: "This is naught but the legends…

item.title: Al-An'aam:26 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهُمْ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ وَيَنْءَوْنَ عَنْهُ وَإِنْ يُهْلِكُونَ إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ wahum yanhawna ʿanhu wayanawna ʿanhu wa-in yuh'likūna illā anfusahum wamā yashʿurūna They dissuade [others] from [following] him, and [themselves] avoid him; yet they destroy no one except themselves, but they are not aware.

item.title: Al-An'aam:26 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهُمْ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ وَيَنْءَوْنَ عَنْهُ وَإِنْ يُهْلِكُونَ إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ wahum yanhawna ʿanhu wayanawna ʿanhu wa-in yuh'likūna illā anfusahum wamā yashʿurūna And they prevent (others) from him and are (themselves) remote from him. And they do not destroy except themselves, but they perceive (it) not. See 6:22

item.title: Al-An'aam:26 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهُمْ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ وَيَنْءَوْنَ عَنْهُ وَإِنْ يُهْلِكُونَ إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ wahum yanhawna ʿanhu wayanawna ʿanhu wa-in yuh'likūna illā anfusahum wamā yashʿurūna They prohibit (others) from it, and (themselves) keep far away from it; they only destroy their own selves, and (yet) they perceive (it) not. See 6:25

item.title: Al-An'aam:27 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَوْ تَرٰی إِذْ وُقِفُوْۤا عَلَى النَّارِ فَقَالُوْۤا يَالَيْتَنَا نُرَدُّ وَلَا نُكَذِّبَ بِءَايَاتِ رَبِّنَا وَنَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ walaw tarā idh wuqifū ʿalā l-nāri faqālū yālaytanā nuraddu walā nukadhiba biāyāti rabbinā wanakūna mina l-mu'minīna Were you to see when they are brought to a halt by the Fire, whereupon they will say, 'If only we were sent back [into the world]! Then we will not deny the signs of our Lord, and we will be among the faithful!'

item.title: Al-An'aam:27 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَوْ تَرٰی إِذْ وُقِفُوْۤا عَلَى النَّارِ فَقَالُوْۤا يَالَيْتَنَا نُرَدُّ وَلَا نُكَذِّبَ بِءَايَاتِ رَبِّنَا وَنَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ walaw tarā idh wuqifū ʿalā l-nāri faqālū yālaytanā nuraddu walā nukadhiba biāyāti rabbinā wanakūna mina l-mu'minīna If you could but see when they are made to stand before the Fire and will say, "Oh, would that we could be returned (to life on earth) and not deny the signs of our Lord and be among the believers." If you could but see when they will be held over the (Hell) Fire! They will say: Would that we were but sent back (to the world)! Then we would not deny the Ayat of our Lord, and we would be of the believers! (6:27). Nay, what they had been concealing before has become manifest to them. But if they were returned (to the world), they would…

item.title: Al-An'aam:27 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَوْ تَرٰی إِذْ وُقِفُوْۤا عَلَى النَّارِ فَقَالُوْۤا يَالَيْتَنَا نُرَدُّ وَلَا نُكَذِّبَ بِءَايَاتِ رَبِّنَا وَنَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ walaw tarā idh wuqifū ʿalā l-nāri faqālū yālaytanā nuraddu walā nukadhiba biāyāti rabbinā wanakūna mina l-mu'minīna And couldst thou see when they are made confronting (Stop at.) the (Hell) fire, then they shall say, "Would that we were sent back and we would not belie the signs of our Lord, and we would be of the believers.''" See 6:25

item.title: Al-An'aam:28 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ بَدَا لَهُمْ مَا كَانُوْۤا يُخْفُونَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَلَوْ رُدُّوْۤا لَعَادُوْۤا لِمَا نُهُوْۤا عَنْهُ وَإِنَّهُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ bal badā lahum mā kānū yukh'fūna min qablu walaw ruddū laʿādū limā nuhū ʿanhu wa-innahum lakādhibūna Rather, now has become evident to them what they used to hide before. But were they to be sent back they would revert to what they were forbidden, and they are indeed liars.

item.title: Al-An'aam:28 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ بَدَا لَهُمْ مَا كَانُوْۤا يُخْفُونَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَلَوْ رُدُّوْۤا لَعَادُوْۤا لِمَا نُهُوْۤا عَنْهُ وَإِنَّهُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ bal badā lahum mā kānū yukh'fūna min qablu walaw ruddū laʿādū limā nuhū ʿanhu wa-innahum lakādhibūna But what they concealed before has (now) appeared to them. And even if they were returned, they would return to that which they were forbidden; and indeed, they are liars. See 6:27

item.title: Al-An'aam:28 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ بَدَا لَهُمْ مَا كَانُوْۤا يُخْفُونَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَلَوْ رُدُّوْۤا لَعَادُوْۤا لِمَا نُهُوْۤا عَنْهُ وَإِنَّهُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ bal badā lahum mā kānū yukh'fūna min qablu walaw ruddū laʿādū limā nuhū ʿanhu wa-innahum lakādhibūna Nay, it has been manifested to them what they did conceal before; and if they were sent back they would certainly return to what they were forbidden and most certainly they are liars (Refers to the possibility of any improvement or expiation through transmigration because of the inherent nature, every soul will always reveal itself in whatever form it may assume.) . See 6:25

item.title: Al-An'aam:29 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالُوْۤا إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا حَيَاتُنَا الدُّنْيَا وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَبْعُوثِينَ waqālū in hiya illā ḥayātunā l-dun'yā wamā naḥnu bimabʿūthīna They say, 'There is nothing but our life of this world, and we shall not be resurrected.'

item.title: Al-An'aam:29 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالُوْۤا إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا حَيَاتُنَا الدُّنْيَا وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَبْعُوثِينَ waqālū in hiya illā ḥayātunā l-dun'yā wamā naḥnu bimabʿūthīna And they say, "There is none but our worldly life, and we will not be resurrected." See 6:27

item.title: Al-An'aam:29 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالُوْۤا إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا حَيَاتُنَا الدُّنْيَا وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَبْعُوثِينَ waqālū in hiya illā ḥayātunā l-dun'yā wamā naḥnu bimabʿūthīna And they say: "there is nothing (beyond') this our life in this world, and we are not to be raised again (This doctrine applies to those who totally deny the life hereafter or believe that they will only be sent back to another earthly form.) ." See 6:25

item.title: Al-An'aam:30 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
