item.description: وَمِنَ الْاِبِلِ اثْنَيْنِ وَمِنَ الْبَقَرِ اثْنَيْنِ قُلْ ءَالذَّكَرَيْنِ حَرَّمَ أَمِ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ أَمَّا اشْتَمَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ أَرْحَامُ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ أَمْ كُنْتُمْ شُهَدَاءَ إِذْ وَصَّاكُمُ اللَّهُ بِهَذَا فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرٰی عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا لِيُضِلَّ النَّاسَ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ wamina l-ibili ith'nayni wamina l-baqari ith'nayni qul āldhakarayni ḥarrama ami l-unthayayni ammā ish'tamalat ʿalayhi arḥāmu l-unthayayni am kuntum shuhadāa idh waṣṣākumu l-lahu bihādhā faman aẓlamu mimmani if'tarā ʿalā l-lahi kadhiban liyuḍilla l-nāsa bighayri ʿil'min inna l-laha lā yahdī l-qawma l-ẓālimīna And two of camels and two of oxen. Say, 'Is it the two males that He has forbidden or the two females, or what is contained in the wombs of the two females? Were you witnesses when Allah enjoined this upon you?' So who is a greater wrongdoer than him who fabricates a lie against Allah to mislead the people…

item.title: Al-An'aam:144 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمِنَ الْاِبِلِ اثْنَيْنِ وَمِنَ الْبَقَرِ اثْنَيْنِ قُلْ ءَالذَّكَرَيْنِ حَرَّمَ أَمِ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ أَمَّا اشْتَمَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ أَرْحَامُ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ أَمْ كُنْتُمْ شُهَدَاءَ إِذْ وَصَّاكُمُ اللَّهُ بِهَذَا فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرٰی عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا لِيُضِلَّ النَّاسَ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ wamina l-ibili ith'nayni wamina l-baqari ith'nayni qul āldhakarayni ḥarrama ami l-unthayayni ammā ish'tamalat ʿalayhi arḥāmu l-unthayayni am kuntum shuhadāa idh waṣṣākumu l-lahu bihādhā faman aẓlamu mimmani if'tarā ʿalā l-lahi kadhiban liyuḍilla l-nāsa bighayri ʿil'min inna l-laha lā yahdī l-qawma l-ẓālimīna And of the camels, two and of the cattle, two. Say, "Is it the two males He has forbidden or the two females or that which the wombs of the two females contain? Or were you witnesses when Allah charged you with this? Then who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah to mislead the people…

item.title: Al-An'aam:144 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمِنَ الْاِبِلِ اثْنَيْنِ وَمِنَ الْبَقَرِ اثْنَيْنِ قُلْ ءَالذَّكَرَيْنِ حَرَّمَ أَمِ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ أَمَّا اشْتَمَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ أَرْحَامُ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ أَمْ كُنْتُمْ شُهَدَاءَ إِذْ وَصَّاكُمُ اللَّهُ بِهَذَا فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرٰی عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا لِيُضِلَّ النَّاسَ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ wamina l-ibili ith'nayni wamina l-baqari ith'nayni qul āldhakarayni ḥarrama ami l-unthayayni ammā ish'tamalat ʿalayhi arḥāmu l-unthayayni am kuntum shuhadāa idh waṣṣākumu l-lahu bihādhā faman aẓlamu mimmani if'tarā ʿalā l-lahi kadhiban liyuḍilla l-nāsa bighayri ʿil'min inna l-laha lā yahdī l-qawma l-ẓālimīna And of the two camels and of the two oxen; say, the two males hath He forbidden or the two females or that which contain the (wombs) of the two females? or were ye witnesses when God did enjoin this;" Who, then is more unjust than he who forgeth (Applicable also to all kinds of conjectures about the divine affairs…

item.title: Al-An'aam:145 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ لَا أَجِدُ فِي مَا أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ مُحَرَّمًا عَلَى طَاعِمٍ يَطْعَمُهُ إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ مَيْتَةً أَوْ دَمًا مَسْفُوحًا أَوْ لَحْمَ خِنْزِيرٍ فَإِنَّهُ رِجْسٌ أَوْ فِسْقًا أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ غَيْرَ بَاغٍ وَلَا عَادٍ فَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ qul lā ajidu fī mā ūḥiya ilayya muḥarraman ʿalā ṭāʿimin yaṭʿamuhu illā an yakūna maytatan aw daman masfūḥan aw laḥma khinzīrin fa-innahu rij'sun aw fis'qan uhilla lighayri l-lahi bihi famani uḍ'ṭurra ghayra bāghin walā ʿādin fa-inna rabbaka ghafūrun raḥīmun Say, 'I do not find in what has been revealed to me that anyone be forbidden to eat anything except carrion or spilt blood, or the flesh of swine —for that is indeed unclean— or an impiety offered to other than Allah.' But should someone be compelled, without being rebellious or aggressive, indeed your Lord is all-forgiving, all-merciful.

item.title: Al-An'aam:145 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ لَا أَجِدُ فِي مَا أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ مُحَرَّمًا عَلَى طَاعِمٍ يَطْعَمُهُ إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ مَيْتَةً أَوْ دَمًا مَسْفُوحًا أَوْ لَحْمَ خِنْزِيرٍ فَإِنَّهُ رِجْسٌ أَوْ فِسْقًا أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ غَيْرَ بَاغٍ وَلَا عَادٍ فَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ qul lā ajidu fī mā ūḥiya ilayya muḥarraman ʿalā ṭāʿimin yaṭʿamuhu illā an yakūna maytatan aw daman masfūḥan aw laḥma khinzīrin fa-innahu rij'sun aw fis'qan uhilla lighayri l-lahi bihi famani uḍ'ṭurra ghayra bāghin walā ʿādin fa-inna rabbaka ghafūrun raḥīmun Say, "I do not find within that which was revealed to me (anything) forbidden to one who would eat it unless it be a dead animal or blood spilled out or the flesh of swine - for indeed, it is impure - or it be (that slaughtered in) disobedience, dedicated to other than Allah.1 But whoever is forced (by necessity), neither desiring…

item.title: Al-An'aam:145 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ لَا أَجِدُ فِي مَا أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ مُحَرَّمًا عَلَى طَاعِمٍ يَطْعَمُهُ إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ مَيْتَةً أَوْ دَمًا مَسْفُوحًا أَوْ لَحْمَ خِنْزِيرٍ فَإِنَّهُ رِجْسٌ أَوْ فِسْقًا أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ غَيْرَ بَاغٍ وَلَا عَادٍ فَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ qul lā ajidu fī mā ūḥiya ilayya muḥarraman ʿalā ṭāʿimin yaṭʿamuhu illā an yakūna maytatan aw daman masfūḥan aw laḥma khinzīrin fa-innahu rij'sun aw fis'qan uhilla lighayri l-lahi bihi famani uḍ'ṭurra ghayra bāghin walā ʿādin fa-inna rabbaka ghafūrun raḥīmun Say: "I find not in what hath been revealed unto me anything forbidden to an eater to eat except it be died of itself, or blood poured forth or flesh of swine for verily that is unclean or a transgression,(a) slain invoking the name of other than Allah (God), but (even so) if one is forced (Forced not by friends or the…

item.title: Al-An'aam:146 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ هَادُوْۤا حَرَّمْنَا كُلَّ ذِي ظُفُرٍ وَمِنَ الْبَقَرِ وَالْغَنَمِ حَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ شُحُومَهُمَا إِلَّا مَا حَمَلَتْ ظُهُورُهُمَا أَوِ الْحَوَايَا أَوْ مَا اخْتَلَطَ بِعَظْمٍ ذٰلِكَ جَزَيْنَاهُمْ بِبَغْيِهِمْ وَإِنَّا لَصَادِقُونَ waʿalā alladhīna hādū ḥarramnā kulla dhī ẓufurin wamina l-baqari wal-ghanami ḥarramnā ʿalayhim shuḥūmahumā illā mā ḥamalat ẓuhūruhumā awi l-ḥawāyā aw mā ikh'talaṭa biʿaẓmin dhālika jazaynāhum bibaghyihim wa-innā laṣādiqūna To the Jews We forbade every animal having an undivided hoof, and of oxen and sheep We forbade them their fat, except what is borne by their backs or the entrails or what is attached to the bones. We requited them with that for their rebelliousness, and We indeed speak the truth.

item.title: Al-An'aam:146 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ هَادُوْۤا حَرَّمْنَا كُلَّ ذِي ظُفُرٍ وَمِنَ الْبَقَرِ وَالْغَنَمِ حَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ شُحُومَهُمَا إِلَّا مَا حَمَلَتْ ظُهُورُهُمَا أَوِ الْحَوَايَا أَوْ مَا اخْتَلَطَ بِعَظْمٍ ذٰلِكَ جَزَيْنَاهُمْ بِبَغْيِهِمْ وَإِنَّا لَصَادِقُونَ waʿalā alladhīna hādū ḥarramnā kulla dhī ẓufurin wamina l-baqari wal-ghanami ḥarramnā ʿalayhim shuḥūmahumā illā mā ḥamalat ẓuhūruhumā awi l-ḥawāyā aw mā ikh'talaṭa biʿaẓmin dhālika jazaynāhum bibaghyihim wa-innā laṣādiqūna And to those who are Jews We prohibited every animal of uncloven hoof; and of the cattle and the sheep We prohibited to them their fat, except what adheres to their backs or the entrails or what is joined with bone. (By) that We repaid them for their transgression. And indeed, We are truthful. And unto those who are Jews, We forbade every (animal) with undivided hoof, and We forbade them the fat of the ox and the sheep except what adheres to their…

item.title: Al-An'aam:146 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ هَادُوْۤا حَرَّمْنَا كُلَّ ذِي ظُفُرٍ وَمِنَ الْبَقَرِ وَالْغَنَمِ حَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ شُحُومَهُمَا إِلَّا مَا حَمَلَتْ ظُهُورُهُمَا أَوِ الْحَوَايَا أَوْ مَا اخْتَلَطَ بِعَظْمٍ ذٰلِكَ جَزَيْنَاهُمْ بِبَغْيِهِمْ وَإِنَّا لَصَادِقُونَ waʿalā alladhīna hādū ḥarramnā kulla dhī ẓufurin wamina l-baqari wal-ghanami ḥarramnā ʿalayhim shuḥūmahumā illā mā ḥamalat ẓuhūruhumā awi l-ḥawāyā aw mā ikh'talaṭa biʿaẓmin dhālika jazaynāhum bibaghyihim wa-innā laṣādiqūna And unto those who were Jews forbade We every animal having undivided hoof, and of oxen and sheep forbade We unto them the fat of both, save what is upon their backs or the entrails or what is mixed with bones; this We recompensed (Temporary prohibition for a local reason.) them for their rebellion, and verily We are truthful. 'Zufr' means talons and claws. 'Zi-zufr' means every beast or bird which has not divided toes as has the camel, ostrich, goose and duck.

item.title: Al-An'aam:147 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِنْ كَذَّبُوكَ فَقُلْ رَبُّكُمْ ذُو رَحْمَةٍ وَاسِعَةٍ وَلَا يُرَدُّ بَأْسُهُ عَنِ الْقَوْمِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ fa-in kadhabūka faqul rabbukum dhū raḥmatin wāsiʿatin walā yuraddu basuhu ʿani l-qawmi l-muj'rimīna But if they deny you, say, 'Your Lord is dispenser of an all-embracing mercy, but His punishment will not be averted from the guilty lot.'

item.title: Al-An'aam:147 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِنْ كَذَّبُوكَ فَقُلْ رَبُّكُمْ ذُو رَحْمَةٍ وَاسِعَةٍ وَلَا يُرَدُّ بَأْسُهُ عَنِ الْقَوْمِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ fa-in kadhabūka faqul rabbukum dhū raḥmatin wāsiʿatin walā yuraddu basuhu ʿani l-qawmi l-muj'rimīna So if they deny you, (O Muḥammad), say, "Your Lord is the possessor of vast mercy; but His punishment cannot be repelled from the people who are criminals." If they deny you say: Your Lord is the Owner of vast mercy, and never will His wrath be turned back from the people who are criminals (6:147). Allah says, if your opponents among the idolators, Jews and their likes reject you, O Muhammad: فَقُل رَّبُّكُمْ ذُو رَحْمَةٍ وَاسِعَةٍ Say: "Your Lord is the Owner of vast mercy..." encouraging them to seek Allah's vast mercy and follow His Messenger SAW: وَلَا يُرَدُّ بَأْسُهُ عَنِ الْقَوْمِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ and never will His wrath be turned back from the…

item.title: Al-An'aam:147 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِنْ كَذَّبُوكَ فَقُلْ رَبُّكُمْ ذُو رَحْمَةٍ وَاسِعَةٍ وَلَا يُرَدُّ بَأْسُهُ عَنِ الْقَوْمِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ fa-in kadhabūka faqul rabbukum dhū raḥmatin wāsiʿatin walā yuraddu basuhu ʿani l-qawmi l-muj'rimīna If they belie thee (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) then say (though) "thy Lord is full of Mercy all-embracing but His wrath shall not be returned from the people who are guilty (Refer to Verse 3:92.) ." 'Zu-Rahmat', i.e., Lord of Mercy-the people who even rejected the true faith, offered to them by the Holy Prophet were destroyed. Sometimes their punishment had only been postponed with a respite. The concluding words clearly sav that such rebels against God will not always escape the return for their infidelity.

item.title: Al-An'aam:148 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: سَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوْۤا لَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ مَا أَشْرَكْنَا وَلَا ءَابَاؤُنَا وَلَا حَرَّمْنَا مِنْ شَيْءٍ كَذٰلِكَ كَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ حَتّٰی ذَاقُوْۤا بَأْسَنَا قُلْ هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ مِنْ عِلْمٍ فَتُخْرِجُوهُ لَنَا إِنْ تَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَإِنْ أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا تَخْرُصُونَ sayaqūlu alladhīna ashrakū law shāa l-lahu mā ashraknā walā ābāunā walā ḥarramnā min shayin kadhālika kadhaba alladhīna min qablihim ḥattā dhāqū basanā qul hal ʿindakum min ʿil'min fatukh'rijūhu lanā in tattabiʿūna illā l-ẓana wa-in antum illā takhruṣūna The polytheists will say, 'Had Allah wished we would not have ascribed any partner [to Him], nor our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything.' Those who were before them had denied1 likewise until they tasted Our punishment. Say, 'Do you have any [revealed] knowledge that you can produce before us? You follow nothing but conjectures, and you do nothing but surmise.'

item.title: Al-An'aam:148 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: سَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوْۤا لَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ مَا أَشْرَكْنَا وَلَا ءَابَاؤُنَا وَلَا حَرَّمْنَا مِنْ شَيْءٍ كَذٰلِكَ كَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ حَتّٰی ذَاقُوْۤا بَأْسَنَا قُلْ هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ مِنْ عِلْمٍ فَتُخْرِجُوهُ لَنَا إِنْ تَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَإِنْ أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا تَخْرُصُونَ sayaqūlu alladhīna ashrakū law shāa l-lahu mā ashraknā walā ābāunā walā ḥarramnā min shayin kadhālika kadhaba alladhīna min qablihim ḥattā dhāqū basanā qul hal ʿindakum min ʿil'min fatukh'rijūhu lanā in tattabiʿūna illā l-ẓana wa-in antum illā takhruṣūna Those who associated (others) with Allah will say, "If Allah had willed, we would not have associated (anything) and neither would our fathers, nor would we have prohibited anything." Likewise did those before deny until they tasted Our punishment. Say, "Do you have any knowledge that you can produce for us? You follow not except assumption, and you are not but misjudging." Those who committed Shirk…

item.title: Al-An'aam:148 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: سَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوْۤا لَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ مَا أَشْرَكْنَا وَلَا ءَابَاؤُنَا وَلَا حَرَّمْنَا مِنْ شَيْءٍ كَذٰلِكَ كَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ حَتّٰی ذَاقُوْۤا بَأْسَنَا قُلْ هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ مِنْ عِلْمٍ فَتُخْرِجُوهُ لَنَا إِنْ تَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَإِنْ أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا تَخْرُصُونَ sayaqūlu alladhīna ashrakū law shāa l-lahu mā ashraknā walā ābāunā walā ḥarramnā min shayin kadhālika kadhaba alladhīna min qablihim ḥattā dhāqū basanā qul hal ʿindakum min ʿil'min fatukh'rijūhu lanā in tattabiʿūna illā l-ẓana wa-in antum illā takhruṣūna Those who are polytheists will say: "Had (The fallacy in the argument of the polytheists is that they have omitted the fact that there is no compulsion on the part of God with regard to the human action in this life. The divine will in this regard is always legislative and not creative. Refer to note in the margin of Verse 6:138.) God wished we would…

item.title: Al-An'aam:149 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ فَلِلَّهِ الْحُجَّةُ الْبَالِغَةُ فَلَوْ شَاءَ لَهَدَاكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ qul falillahi l-ḥujatu l-bālighatu falaw shāa lahadākum ajmaʿīna Say, 'To Allah belongs the conclusive argument. Had He wished, He would have surely guided you all.'

item.title: Al-An'aam:149 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ فَلِلَّهِ الْحُجَّةُ الْبَالِغَةُ فَلَوْ شَاءَ لَهَدَاكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ qul falillahi l-ḥujatu l-bālighatu falaw shāa lahadākum ajmaʿīna Say, "With Allah is the far-reaching (i.e., conclusive) argument. If He had willed, He would have guided you all." See 6:148

item.title: Al-An'aam:149 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ فَلِلَّهِ الْحُجَّةُ الْبَالِغَةُ فَلَوْ شَاءَ لَهَدَاكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ qul falillahi l-ḥujatu l-bālighatu falaw shāa lahadākum ajmaʿīna Say thou: "Then, God's (alone) is the argument decisive; Had God wished He would surely have guided you all aright." The polytheist used to say that if God had willed, they would all have been guided. God had not willed so. They even attributed their going astray to God's will. This is said against the argument of the polytheists that God never misleads men, but on the other hand He sends apostle after apostle to guide man on the right path of truth. Man has been created with a free will to use his discretion to thankfully accept the guidance from God or to ungratefully reject it1.

item.title: Al-An'aam:150 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ هَلُمَّ شُهَدَاءَكُمُ الَّذِينَ يَشْهَدُونَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ حَرَّمَ هَذَا فَإِنْ شَهِدُوْۤا فَلَا تَشْهَدْ مَعَهُمْ وَلَا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْوَاءَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوْۤا بِاٰیٰتِنَاۤ وَالَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْاٰخِرَةِ وَهُمْ بِرَبِّهِمْ يَعْدِلُونَ qul halumma shuhadāakumu alladhīna yashhadūna anna l-laha ḥarrama hādhā fa-in shahidū falā tashhad maʿahum walā tattabiʿ ahwāa alladhīna kadhabū biāyātinā wa-alladhīna lā yu'minūna bil-ākhirati wahum birabbihim yaʿdilūna Say, 'Bring your witnesses who may testify that Allah has forbidden this.' So if they testify, do not testify with them, and do not follow the desires of those who deny Our signs, and those who do not believe in the Hereafter and equate [others] with their Lord.

item.title: Al-An'aam:150 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ هَلُمَّ شُهَدَاءَكُمُ الَّذِينَ يَشْهَدُونَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ حَرَّمَ هَذَا فَإِنْ شَهِدُوْۤا فَلَا تَشْهَدْ مَعَهُمْ وَلَا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْوَاءَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوْۤا بِاٰیٰتِنَاۤ وَالَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْاٰخِرَةِ وَهُمْ بِرَبِّهِمْ يَعْدِلُونَ qul halumma shuhadāakumu alladhīna yashhadūna anna l-laha ḥarrama hādhā fa-in shahidū falā tashhad maʿahum walā tattabiʿ ahwāa alladhīna kadhabū biāyātinā wa-alladhīna lā yu'minūna bil-ākhirati wahum birabbihim yaʿdilūna Say, (O Muḥammad), "Bring forward your witnesses who will testify that Allah has prohibited this." And if they testify, do not testify with them. And do not follow the desires of those who deny Our verses and those who do not believe in the Hereafter, while they equate (others) with their Lord. See 6:148

item.title: Al-An'aam:150 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ هَلُمَّ شُهَدَاءَكُمُ الَّذِينَ يَشْهَدُونَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ حَرَّمَ هَذَا فَإِنْ شَهِدُوْۤا فَلَا تَشْهَدْ مَعَهُمْ وَلَا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْوَاءَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوْۤا بِاٰیٰتِنَاۤ وَالَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْاٰخِرَةِ وَهُمْ بِرَبِّهِمْ يَعْدِلُونَ qul halumma shuhadāakumu alladhīna yashhadūna anna l-laha ḥarrama hādhā fa-in shahidū falā tashhad maʿahum walā tattabiʿ ahwāa alladhīna kadhabū biāyātinā wa-alladhīna lā yu'minūna bil-ākhirati wahum birabbihim yaʿdilūna Say thou: "Bring ye your witnesses who bear witness that God hath forbidden this," then (even) if they bear witness, bear thou not witness with them; and follow not thou the inclinations of those who belie Our signs; and those who believe not in the hereafter, and while they with their Lord equalize (In authority.) (others). See 6:149

item.title: Al-An'aam:151 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ تَعَالَوْا أَتْلُ مَا حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ أَلَّا تُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئًا وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا وَلَا تَقْتُلُوْۤا أَوْلَادَكُمْ مِنْ إِمْلَاقٍ نَحْنُ نَرْزُقُكُمْ وَإِيَّاهُمْ وَلَا تَقْرَبُوْۤا الْفَوَاحِشَ مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا وَمَا بَطَنَ وَلَا تَقْتُلُوْۤا النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ ذَلِكُمْ وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ qul taʿālaw atlu mā ḥarrama rabbukum ʿalaykum allā tush'rikū bihi shayan wabil-wālidayni iḥ'sānan walā taqtulū awlādakum min im'lāqin naḥnu narzuqukum wa-iyyāhum walā taqrabū l-fawāḥisha mā ẓahara min'hā wamā baṭana walā taqtulū l-nafsa allatī ḥarrama l-lahu illā bil-ḥaqi dhālikum waṣṣākum bihi laʿallakum taʿqilūna Say, 'Come, I will recount what your Lord has forbidden you from. That you shall not ascribe any partners to Him, and you shall be good to the parents, you shall not kill your children due to penury —We will provide for you and for them— you shall not approach indecencies, the outward among them and…

item.title: Al-An'aam:151 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ تَعَالَوْا أَتْلُ مَا حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ أَلَّا تُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئًا وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا وَلَا تَقْتُلُوْۤا أَوْلَادَكُمْ مِنْ إِمْلَاقٍ نَحْنُ نَرْزُقُكُمْ وَإِيَّاهُمْ وَلَا تَقْرَبُوْۤا الْفَوَاحِشَ مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا وَمَا بَطَنَ وَلَا تَقْتُلُوْۤا النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ ذَلِكُمْ وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ qul taʿālaw atlu mā ḥarrama rabbukum ʿalaykum allā tush'rikū bihi shayan wabil-wālidayni iḥ'sānan walā taqtulū awlādakum min im'lāqin naḥnu narzuqukum wa-iyyāhum walā taqrabū l-fawāḥisha mā ẓahara min'hā wamā baṭana walā taqtulū l-nafsa allatī ḥarrama l-lahu illā bil-ḥaqi dhālikum waṣṣākum bihi laʿallakum taʿqilūna Say, "Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you. (He commands) that you not associate anything with Him, and to parents, good treatment, and do not kill your children out of poverty; We will provide for you and them. And do not approach immoralities - what is apparent of them and what is…

item.title: Al-An'aam:151 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ تَعَالَوْا أَتْلُ مَا حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ أَلَّا تُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئًا وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا وَلَا تَقْتُلُوْۤا أَوْلَادَكُمْ مِنْ إِمْلَاقٍ نَحْنُ نَرْزُقُكُمْ وَإِيَّاهُمْ وَلَا تَقْرَبُوْۤا الْفَوَاحِشَ مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا وَمَا بَطَنَ وَلَا تَقْتُلُوْۤا النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ ذَلِكُمْ وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ qul taʿālaw atlu mā ḥarrama rabbukum ʿalaykum allā tush'rikū bihi shayan wabil-wālidayni iḥ'sānan walā taqtulū awlādakum min im'lāqin naḥnu narzuqukum wa-iyyāhum walā taqrabū l-fawāḥisha mā ẓahara min'hā wamā baṭana walā taqtulū l-nafsa allatī ḥarrama l-lahu illā bil-ḥaqi dhālikum waṣṣākum bihi laʿallakum taʿqilūna Say: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad) "Come ye! I will recite (unto) you what your Lord hath forbidden to you that ye associate not with Him anything and to ( your) parents be good, and slay (Applicable to the unwarranted and 'Family Planning'.) ye not your children for (fear of) poverty; We provide for you and for…

item.title: Al-An'aam:152 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا تَقْرَبُوْۤا مَالَ الْيَتِيمِ إِلَّا بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ حَتّٰی يَبْلُغَ أَشُدَّهُ وَأَوْفُوْۤا الْكَيْلَ وَالْمِيزَانَ بِالْقِسْطِ لَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا وَإِذَا قُلْتُمْ فَاعْدِلُوا وَلَوْ كَانَ ذَا قُرْبٰی وَبِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ أَوْفُوْۤا ذَلِكُمْ وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ walā taqrabū māla l-yatīmi illā bi-allatī hiya aḥsanu ḥattā yablugha ashuddahu wa-awfū l-kayla wal-mīzāna bil-qis'ṭi lā nukallifu nafsan illā wus'ʿahā wa-idhā qul'tum fa-iʿ'dilū walaw kāna dhā qur'bā wabiʿahdi l-lahi awfū dhālikum waṣṣākum bihi laʿallakum tadhakkarūna Do not approach the orphan's property, except in the best [possible] manner, until he comes of age. And observe fully the measure and the balance1 with justice.' We task no soul except according to its capacity. 'And when you speak, be fair, even if it were a relative; and fulfill Allah's covenant. This is what He enjoins upon you so that you may take admonition.'

item.title: Al-An'aam:152 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا تَقْرَبُوْۤا مَالَ الْيَتِيمِ إِلَّا بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ حَتّٰی يَبْلُغَ أَشُدَّهُ وَأَوْفُوْۤا الْكَيْلَ وَالْمِيزَانَ بِالْقِسْطِ لَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا وَإِذَا قُلْتُمْ فَاعْدِلُوا وَلَوْ كَانَ ذَا قُرْبٰی وَبِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ أَوْفُوْۤا ذَلِكُمْ وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ walā taqrabū māla l-yatīmi illā bi-allatī hiya aḥsanu ḥattā yablugha ashuddahu wa-awfū l-kayla wal-mīzāna bil-qis'ṭi lā nukallifu nafsan illā wus'ʿahā wa-idhā qul'tum fa-iʿ'dilū walaw kāna dhā qur'bā wabiʿahdi l-lahi awfū dhālikum waṣṣākum bihi laʿallakum tadhakkarūna And do not approach the orphan's property except in a way that is best (i.e., intending improvement) until he reaches maturity. And give full measure and weight in justice. We do not charge any soul except (with that within) its capacity. And when you speak (i.e., testify), be just, even if (it concerns) a near relative. And the covenant of Allah fulfill. This has He instructed you that you may…

item.title: Al-An'aam:152 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا تَقْرَبُوْۤا مَالَ الْيَتِيمِ إِلَّا بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ حَتّٰی يَبْلُغَ أَشُدَّهُ وَأَوْفُوْۤا الْكَيْلَ وَالْمِيزَانَ بِالْقِسْطِ لَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا وَإِذَا قُلْتُمْ فَاعْدِلُوا وَلَوْ كَانَ ذَا قُرْبٰی وَبِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ أَوْفُوْۤا ذَلِكُمْ وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ walā taqrabū māla l-yatīmi illā bi-allatī hiya aḥsanu ḥattā yablugha ashuddahu wa-awfū l-kayla wal-mīzāna bil-qis'ṭi lā nukallifu nafsan illā wus'ʿahā wa-idhā qul'tum fa-iʿ'dilū walaw kāna dhā qur'bā wabiʿahdi l-lahi awfū dhālikum waṣṣākum bihi laʿallakum tadhakkarūna And approach ye not the property of an orphan save that be in the best manner till he attaineth his maturity; Give ye full measure and full weight in (perfect) justice; We task not a soul but according to his ability, and when ye speak be just; though it be against a kinsman; and fulfil ye God's covenant (This serves as a reminder as well as a warning to the…

item.title: Al-An'aam:153 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّ هَذَا صِرَاطِي مُسْتَقِيمًا فَاتَّبِعُوهُ وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا السُّبُلَ فَتَفَرَّقَ بِكُمْ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ ذَلِكُمْ وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ wa-anna hādhā ṣirāṭī mus'taqīman fa-ittabiʿūhu walā tattabiʿū l-subula fatafarraqa bikum ʿan sabīlihi dhālikum waṣṣākum bihi laʿallakum tattaqūna 'This indeed is my straight path, so follow it, and do not follow [other] ways, for they will separate you from His way. This is what He enjoins upon you so that you may be Godwary.'

item.title: Al-An'aam:153 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّ هَذَا صِرَاطِي مُسْتَقِيمًا فَاتَّبِعُوهُ وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا السُّبُلَ فَتَفَرَّقَ بِكُمْ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ ذَلِكُمْ وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ wa-anna hādhā ṣirāṭī mus'taqīman fa-ittabiʿūhu walā tattabiʿū l-subula fatafarraqa bikum ʿan sabīlihi dhālikum waṣṣākum bihi laʿallakum tattaqūna And, (moreover), this is My path, which is straight, so follow it; and do not follow (other) ways, for you will be separated from His way. This has He instructed you that you may become righteous. And verily, this is My straight path, so follow it, and follow not (other) paths, for they will separate you away from His path. This He has ordained for you that you may have Taqwa (6:153). The Command to Follow Allah's Straight Path and to Avoid All Other Path and to Avoid All Other Paths Ali bin Abi Talhah reported that Ibn 'Abbas commented on Allah's statements: وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا السُّبُلَ…

item.title: Al-An'aam:153 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّ هَذَا صِرَاطِي مُسْتَقِيمًا فَاتَّبِعُوهُ وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا السُّبُلَ فَتَفَرَّقَ بِكُمْ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ ذَلِكُمْ وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ wa-anna hādhā ṣirāṭī mus'taqīman fa-ittabiʿūhu walā tattabiʿū l-subula fatafarraqa bikum ʿan sabīlihi dhālikum waṣṣākum bihi laʿallakum tattaqūna And (know ye) Verily this My path, is the straight (right) one, so ye follow it, and follow ye not (other) ways for they will scatter you away from His path; this doth He enjoin you with, so that ye may guard (yourselves against evil) (Refer to Verse 6:160.) . The Right or the Straight path referred to in this Verse is what the Holy Prophet showed to mankind at the conclusion of his apostolic mission, saying: I leave behind me Two weighty things, the Book of God, i.e., the Holy Qur'an, and my 'Ahl Al-Bayt' (i.e., the divinely chosen ones of my family, i.e., the…

item.title: Al-An'aam:154 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ اٰتَیْنَا مُوسٰی الْكِتَابَ تَمَامًا عَلَى الَّذِي أَحْسَنَ وَتَفْصِيلًا لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةً لَعَلَّهُمْ بِلِقَاءِ رَبِّهِمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ thumma ātaynā mūsā l-kitāba tamāman ʿalā alladhī aḥsana watafṣīlan likulli shayin wahudan waraḥmatan laʿallahum biliqāi rabbihim yu'minūna Then We gave Moses the Book, completing [Our blessing] on him who is virtuous, and as an elaboration1 of all things, and as a guidance and mercy, so that they may believe in the encounter with their Lord.

item.title: Al-An'aam:154 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ اٰتَیْنَا مُوسٰی الْكِتَابَ تَمَامًا عَلَى الَّذِي أَحْسَنَ وَتَفْصِيلًا لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةً لَعَلَّهُمْ بِلِقَاءِ رَبِّهِمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ thumma ātaynā mūsā l-kitāba tamāman ʿalā alladhī aḥsana watafṣīlan likulli shayin wahudan waraḥmatan laʿallahum biliqāi rabbihim yu'minūna Then1 We gave Musa the Scripture, making complete (Our favor) upon the one who did good (i.e., Musa) and as a detailed explanation of all things and as guidance and mercy that perhaps in the meeting with their Lord they would believe. Then, We gave Musa the Book (the Tawrah), complete for that which is best, and explaining all things in detail and a guidance and a mercy that they might believe in the meeting with their Lord (6:154). And this is a blessed Book (the Qur'an) which We have sent down, so follow it and have Taqwa, so that you may receive mercy (6:155). Praising…

item.title: Al-An'aam:154 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ اٰتَیْنَا مُوسٰی الْكِتَابَ تَمَامًا عَلَى الَّذِي أَحْسَنَ وَتَفْصِيلًا لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةً لَعَلَّهُمْ بِلِقَاءِ رَبِّهِمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ thumma ātaynā mūsā l-kitāba tamāman ʿalā alladhī aḥsana watafṣīlan likulli shayin wahudan waraḥmatan laʿallahum biliqāi rabbihim yu'minūna Besides, We gave Moses the Book completing (our favours) on those who would do good and explaining all things in details, and a guidance and a mercy, so that in the meeting (The day of resurrection and for the Final Judgement. Refer to Verse 35:42.) of their Lord they may believe. By 'all things' meaning everything needed for the guidance of the Israelites of Moses' time, which includes the prophecy relating to the advent of the Holy Prophet Muhammad. Deut. 18/18-19.1.

item.title: Al-An'aam:155 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهَذَا كِتَابٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ مُبَارَكٌ فَاتَّبِعُوهُ وَاتَّقُوا لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ wahādhā kitābun anzalnāhu mubārakun fa-ittabiʿūhu wa-ittaqū laʿallakum tur'ḥamūna And this Book that We have sent down is a blessed one; so follow it, and be Godwary so that you may receive [His] mercy.

item.title: Al-An'aam:155 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهَذَا كِتَابٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ مُبَارَكٌ فَاتَّبِعُوهُ وَاتَّقُوا لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ wahādhā kitābun anzalnāhu mubārakun fa-ittabiʿūhu wa-ittaqū laʿallakum tur'ḥamūna And this (Qur’ān) is a Book We have revealed (which is) blessed, so follow it and fear Allah that you may receive mercy. See 6:154

item.title: Al-An'aam:155 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهَذَا كِتَابٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ مُبَارَكٌ فَاتَّبِعُوهُ وَاتَّقُوا لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ wahādhā kitābun anzalnāhu mubārakun fa-ittabiʿūhu wa-ittaqū laʿallakum tur'ḥamūna And this (Qur'an) is a Book, We have sent it down, blessed, so follow it, and guard (your-selves against evil) so that ye may be done mercy (Receive God's mercy.) . It should be noted that all the previous revelations being only for the time, and not a complete code for all times, were not called a complete Book and it is the Holy Qur'an which is presented as a complete Book. Besides, there is the quality of the book mentioned as 'Mubarak', i.e., a blessing-a blessing is continued grace of God which infers that this is the Book which shall for ever remain a blessing for mankind in general and its adherents in particular.

item.title: Al-An'aam:156 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنْ تَقُولُوْۤا إِنَّمَا أُنْزِلَ الْكِتَابُ عَلَى طَائِفَتَيْنِ مِنْ قَبْلِنَا وَإِنْ كُنَّا عَنْ دِرَاسَتِهِمْ لَغَافِلِينَ an taqūlū innamā unzila l-kitābu ʿalā ṭāifatayni min qablinā wa-in kunnā ʿan dirāsatihim laghāfilīna Lest you should say, 'The Book was sent down only to two communities before us,1 and we were indeed unaware of their studies,'

item.title: Al-An'aam:156 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنْ تَقُولُوْۤا إِنَّمَا أُنْزِلَ الْكِتَابُ عَلَى طَائِفَتَيْنِ مِنْ قَبْلِنَا وَإِنْ كُنَّا عَنْ دِرَاسَتِهِمْ لَغَافِلِينَ an taqūlū innamā unzila l-kitābu ʿalā ṭāifatayni min qablinā wa-in kunnā ʿan dirāsatihim laghāfilīna (We revealed it) lest you say, "The Scripture was only sent down to two groups before us, but we were of their study unaware." Lest you should say: The Book was sent down only to two sects before us, and for our part, we were in fact unaware of what they studied (6:156). Or lest you should say: "If only the Book had been sent down to us, we would surely have been better guided than they." So now has come unto you a clear proof from your Lord, and a guidance and a mercy. Who then does more wrong than one who rejects the Ayat of Allah and Sadafa away therefrom?…

item.title: Al-An'aam:156 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنْ تَقُولُوْۤا إِنَّمَا أُنْزِلَ الْكِتَابُ عَلَى طَائِفَتَيْنِ مِنْ قَبْلِنَا وَإِنْ كُنَّا عَنْ دِرَاسَتِهِمْ لَغَافِلِينَ an taqūlū innamā unzila l-kitābu ʿalā ṭāifatayni min qablinā wa-in kunnā ʿan dirāsatihim laghāfilīna Lest ye (Polytheists) should say "that the Book (from God) was sent down unto two parties (This indicates that the previous Scriptures were sectional, not universal, which fact is confirmed by several passages of the Qur'an pointing out that Moses and Jesus were sent but only to the Children of Israel-This is clearly and openly acknowledged by the Bible of the Christian church and the national character of the belief in godhead as presented in the Old and the New Testaments Math-15/22-26 10/5 - John- 16/5-14 Etc.) (the Christians and the Jews) before us, and verily we were of what they read, unaware." See 6:155

item.title: Al-An'aam:157 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوْ تَقُولُوْۤا لَوْ أَنَّا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْنَا الْكِتَابُ لَكُنَّا أَهْدَى مِنْهُمْ فَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ بَيِّنَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةٌ فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنْ كَذَّبَ بِءَايَاتِ اللَّهِ وَصَدَفَ عَنْهَا سَنَجْزِي الَّذِينَ يَصْدِفُونَ عَنْ ءَايَاتِنَا سُوءَ الْعَذَابِ بِمَا كَانُوْۤا يَصْدِفُونَ aw taqūlū law annā unzila ʿalaynā l-kitābu lakunnā ahdā min'hum faqad jāakum bayyinatun min rabbikum wahudan waraḥmatun faman aẓlamu mimman kadhaba biāyāti l-lahi waṣadafa ʿanhā sanajzī alladhīna yaṣdifūna ʿan āyātinā sūa l-ʿadhābi bimā kānū yaṣdifūna or [lest] you should say, 'If the Book had been sent down to us, surely we would have been better-guided than them.' There has already come to you a manifest proof from your Lord and a guidance and mercy. So who is a greater wrongdoer than him who denies the signs of Allah, and turns away from them? Soon We shall requite those who turn away from Our signs with…

item.title: Al-An'aam:157 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوْ تَقُولُوْۤا لَوْ أَنَّا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْنَا الْكِتَابُ لَكُنَّا أَهْدَى مِنْهُمْ فَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ بَيِّنَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةٌ فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنْ كَذَّبَ بِءَايَاتِ اللَّهِ وَصَدَفَ عَنْهَا سَنَجْزِي الَّذِينَ يَصْدِفُونَ عَنْ ءَايَاتِنَا سُوءَ الْعَذَابِ بِمَا كَانُوْۤا يَصْدِفُونَ aw taqūlū law annā unzila ʿalaynā l-kitābu lakunnā ahdā min'hum faqad jāakum bayyinatun min rabbikum wahudan waraḥmatun faman aẓlamu mimman kadhaba biāyāti l-lahi waṣadafa ʿanhā sanajzī alladhīna yaṣdifūna ʿan āyātinā sūa l-ʿadhābi bimā kānū yaṣdifūna Or lest you say, "If only the Scripture had been revealed to us, we would have been better guided than they." So there has (now) come to you a clear evidence from your Lord and a guidance and mercy. Then who is more unjust than one who denies the verses of Allah and turns away from them? We will recompense those who turn away from Our verses with the worst…

item.title: Al-An'aam:157 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوْ تَقُولُوْۤا لَوْ أَنَّا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْنَا الْكِتَابُ لَكُنَّا أَهْدَى مِنْهُمْ فَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ بَيِّنَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةٌ فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنْ كَذَّبَ بِءَايَاتِ اللَّهِ وَصَدَفَ عَنْهَا سَنَجْزِي الَّذِينَ يَصْدِفُونَ عَنْ ءَايَاتِنَا سُوءَ الْعَذَابِ بِمَا كَانُوْۤا يَصْدِفُونَ aw taqūlū law annā unzila ʿalaynā l-kitābu lakunnā ahdā min'hum faqad jāakum bayyinatun min rabbikum wahudan waraḥmatun faman aẓlamu mimman kadhaba biāyāti l-lahi waṣadafa ʿanhā sanajzī alladhīna yaṣdifūna ʿan āyātinā sūa l-ʿadhābi bimā kānū yaṣdifūna Or (lest) ye should say: "Had only been sent unto us a book we should have been better guided than they;" so indeed hath (now) come unto you a manifest proof from your Lord, and guidance and mercy; who then is more unjust than he who belieth the signs of God and turneth away from them? Soon shall We recompense those who turn away from Our signs with an evil…

item.title: Al-An'aam:158 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ أَوْ يَأْتِيَ رَبُّكَ أَوْ يَأْتِيَ بَعْضُ اٰیٰتِ رَبِّكَ يَوْمَ يَأْتِي بَعْضُ اٰیٰتِ رَبِّكَ لَا يَنْفَعُ نَفْسًا إِيمَانُهَا لَمْ تَكُنْ اٰمَنَتْ مِنْ قَبْلُ أَوْ كَسَبَتْ فِي إِيمَانِهَا خَيْرًا قُلِ انْتَظِرُوا إِنَّا مُنْتَظِرُونَ hal yanẓurūna illā an tatiyahumu l-malāikatu aw yatiya rabbuka aw yatiya baʿḍu āyāti rabbika yawma yatī baʿḍu āyāti rabbika lā yanfaʿu nafsan īmānuhā lam takun āmanat min qablu aw kasabat fī īmānihā khayran quli intaẓirū innā muntaẓirūna Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them, or your Lord should come, or some of your Lord's signs should come? The day when some of your Lord's signs do come, faith shall not benefit any soul that had not believed beforehand and had not earned some goodness in its faith. Say, 'Wait! We too are waiting!'

item.title: Al-An'aam:158 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ أَوْ يَأْتِيَ رَبُّكَ أَوْ يَأْتِيَ بَعْضُ اٰیٰتِ رَبِّكَ يَوْمَ يَأْتِي بَعْضُ اٰیٰتِ رَبِّكَ لَا يَنْفَعُ نَفْسًا إِيمَانُهَا لَمْ تَكُنْ اٰمَنَتْ مِنْ قَبْلُ أَوْ كَسَبَتْ فِي إِيمَانِهَا خَيْرًا قُلِ انْتَظِرُوا إِنَّا مُنْتَظِرُونَ hal yanẓurūna illā an tatiyahumu l-malāikatu aw yatiya rabbuka aw yatiya baʿḍu āyāti rabbika yawma yatī baʿḍu āyāti rabbika lā yanfaʿu nafsan īmānuhā lam takun āmanat min qablu aw kasabat fī īmānihā khayran quli intaẓirū innā muntaẓirūna Do they (then) wait for anything except that the angels should come to them or your Lord should come or that there come some of the signs1 of your Lord? The Day that some of the signs of your Lord will come no soul will benefit from its faith as long as it had not believed before or had earned through its faith some good. Say,…

item.title: Al-An'aam:158 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ أَوْ يَأْتِيَ رَبُّكَ أَوْ يَأْتِيَ بَعْضُ اٰیٰتِ رَبِّكَ يَوْمَ يَأْتِي بَعْضُ اٰیٰتِ رَبِّكَ لَا يَنْفَعُ نَفْسًا إِيمَانُهَا لَمْ تَكُنْ اٰمَنَتْ مِنْ قَبْلُ أَوْ كَسَبَتْ فِي إِيمَانِهَا خَيْرًا قُلِ انْتَظِرُوا إِنَّا مُنْتَظِرُونَ hal yanẓurūna illā an tatiyahumu l-malāikatu aw yatiya rabbuka aw yatiya baʿḍu āyāti rabbika yawma yatī baʿḍu āyāti rabbika lā yanfaʿu nafsan īmānuhā lam takun āmanat min qablu aw kasabat fī īmānihā khayran quli intaẓirū innā muntaẓirūna They wait not but (to see) that (Refer to the adamance of the disbelievers.) come unto them the angels, or cometh thy Lord (Himself), or that come (unto them) some signs of thy Lord; on the day when come (i.e. the good deeds of the one who believed but acted only after the sign.) some of the signs of thy Lord, its faith shall profit not…

item.title: Al-An'aam:159 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ فَرَّقُوْۤا دِينَهُمْ وَكَانُوْۤا شِيَعًا لَسْتَ مِنْهُمْ فِي شَيْءٍ إِنَّمَا أَمْرُهُمْ إِلَى اللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِمَا كَانُوْۤا يَفْعَلُونَ inna alladhīna farraqū dīnahum wakānū shiyaʿan lasta min'hum fī shayin innamā amruhum ilā l-lahi thumma yunabbi-uhum bimā kānū yafʿalūna Indeed those who split up their religion and became sects, you will not have anything to do with them. Their matter rests only with Allah; then He will inform them concerning what they used to do.

item.title: Al-An'aam:159 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ فَرَّقُوْۤا دِينَهُمْ وَكَانُوْۤا شِيَعًا لَسْتَ مِنْهُمْ فِي شَيْءٍ إِنَّمَا أَمْرُهُمْ إِلَى اللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِمَا كَانُوْۤا يَفْعَلُونَ inna alladhīna farraqū dīnahum wakānū shiyaʿan lasta min'hum fī shayin innamā amruhum ilā l-lahi thumma yunabbi-uhum bimā kānū yafʿalūna Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects - you, (O Muḥammad), are not (associated) with them in anything. Their affair is only (left) to Allah; then He will inform them about what they used to do. Verily, those who divide their religion and break up into sects, you have no concern with them in the least. Their affair is only with Allah, Who then will tell them what they used to do (6:159). Criticizing Division in the Religion Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak and As-Suddi said that this Ayah was revealed about the Jews and Christians. Al-'Awfi said that Ibn 'Abbas…

item.title: Al-An'aam:159 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ فَرَّقُوْۤا دِينَهُمْ وَكَانُوْۤا شِيَعًا لَسْتَ مِنْهُمْ فِي شَيْءٍ إِنَّمَا أَمْرُهُمْ إِلَى اللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِمَا كَانُوْۤا يَفْعَلُونَ inna alladhīna farraqū dīnahum wakānū shiyaʿan lasta min'hum fī shayin innamā amruhum ilā l-lahi thumma yunabbi-uhum bimā kānū yafʿalūna Verily those who divided their religion and became parties, thou hast no concern with anything of them; their affair is with God only, then will He inform them of what they did (Refer to Verse 6:154.) . This refers to sectarianism in all religions, i.e., accepting a part and rejecting the other or, misinterpreting the Word of God by one's own imagination and not following the meaning rendered by the authentic sources commissioned by God. The best and the only authority about God, godliness and the correct interpretation of the Word of God after the Holy Prophet are the Holy Imams. Referring…

item.title: Al-An'aam:160 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَنْ جَاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا وَمَنْ جَاءَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ فَلَا يُجْزَى إِلَّا مِثْلَهَا وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ man jāa bil-ḥasanati falahu ʿashru amthālihā waman jāa bil-sayi-ati falā yuj'zā illā mith'lahā wahum lā yuẓ'lamūna Whoever brings virtue shall receive ten times its like; but whoever brings vice shall not be requited except with its like, and they will not be wronged.1

item.title: Al-An'aam:160 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَنْ جَاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا وَمَنْ جَاءَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ فَلَا يُجْزَى إِلَّا مِثْلَهَا وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ man jāa bil-ḥasanati falahu ʿashru amthālihā waman jāa bil-sayi-ati falā yuj'zā illā mith'lahā wahum lā yuẓ'lamūna Whoever comes (on the Day of Judgement) with a good deed will have ten times the like thereof (to his credit), and whoever comes with an evil deed will not be recompensed except the like thereof; and they will not be wronged.1 Whoever brings a good deed shall have ten times the like thereof to his credit, and whoever brings an evil deed shall have only the recompense of the like thereof, and they will not be wronged (6:160). The Good Deed is Multiplied Tenfold, While the Sin is Recompensed with the Same This Ayah explains the general Ayah; مَن جَاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ خَيْرٌ مِّنْهَا Whoever comes with…

item.title: Al-An'aam:160 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَنْ جَاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا وَمَنْ جَاءَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ فَلَا يُجْزَى إِلَّا مِثْلَهَا وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ man jāa bil-ḥasanati falahu ʿashru amthālihā waman jāa bil-sayi-ati falā yuj'zā illā mith'lahā wahum lā yuẓ'lamūna Whosoever cometh with a good (deed) for him shall be ten (According to God's grace.) like it; and whosoever cometh with an evil (deed) he shall be recompensed not but with the like (According to God's Justice.) of it, and they shall not be dealt with unjustly. This Verse announces only the maximum amount of punishment for evil and the minimum reward for virtue otherwise the Holy Prophet had announced a greater encouragement to those who desire to build up goodness for themselves saying that every evil will be recompensed with the like of it, whereas a virtue of or a goodness will get from the All-Merciful Lord,…

item.title: Al-An'aam:161 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ إِنَّنِي هَدَانِي رَبِّي إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ دِينًا قِيَمًا مِلَّةَ اِبْرَاهِیْمَ حَنِيفًا وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ qul innanī hadānī rabbī ilā ṣirāṭin mus'taqīmin dīnan qiyaman millata ib'rāhīma ḥanīfan wamā kāna mina l-mush'rikīna Say, 'Indeed my Lord has guided me to a straight path, the upright religion, the creed of Abraham, a ḥanīf, and he was not one of the polytheists.'

item.title: Al-An'aam:161 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ إِنَّنِي هَدَانِي رَبِّي إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ دِينًا قِيَمًا مِلَّةَ اِبْرَاهِیْمَ حَنِيفًا وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ qul innanī hadānī rabbī ilā ṣirāṭin mus'taqīmin dīnan qiyaman millata ib'rāhīma ḥanīfan wamā kāna mina l-mush'rikīna Say, "Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path - a correct religion - the way of Ibrahim, inclining toward truth. And he was not among those who associated others with Allah." Say: Truly, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a right religion, the religion of Ibrahim, Hanifan (monotheism) and he was not of the Mushrikin (6:161). Say: "Verily, my Salah, my sacrifice, my living, and my dying are for Allah, the Lord of all that exists (6:162). "He has no partner. And of this I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims (6:163). Islam is the Straight Path…

item.title: Al-An'aam:161 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ إِنَّنِي هَدَانِي رَبِّي إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ دِينًا قِيَمًا مِلَّةَ اِبْرَاهِیْمَ حَنِيفًا وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ qul innanī hadānī rabbī ilā ṣirāṭin mus'taqīmin dīnan qiyaman millata ib'rāhīma ḥanīfan wamā kāna mina l-mush'rikīna Say: (O' Our Apostle Muhammad) "Verily my Lord hath guided me unto the straight (right) path (Islam-i.e. Absolute submission to the divine will.) ; the established (Which never changes – unimpeachable.) religion, the faith of Abraham, the upright one; and he (Abraham.) was not of the polytheists." See 6:160

item.title: Al-An'aam:162 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ إِنَّ صَلَاتِي وَنُسُكِي وَمَحْيَايَ وَمَمَاتِي لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ qul inna ṣalātī wanusukī wamaḥyāya wamamātī lillahi rabbi l-ʿālamīna Say, 'Indeed my prayer and my worship, my life and my death are for the sake of Allah, the Lord of all the worlds.

item.title: Al-An'aam:162 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ إِنَّ صَلَاتِي وَنُسُكِي وَمَحْيَايَ وَمَمَاتِي لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ qul inna ṣalātī wanusukī wamaḥyāya wamamātī lillahi rabbi l-ʿālamīna Say, "Indeed, my prayer, my rites of sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds. See 6:161

item.title: Al-An'aam:162 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ إِنَّ صَلَاتِي وَنُسُكِي وَمَحْيَايَ وَمَمَاتِي لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ qul inna ṣalātī wanusukī wamaḥyāya wamamātī lillahi rabbi l-ʿālamīna Say: "Verily my prayer and my sacrifice, my life and my death, (are all, only) for God, the Lord of the worlds (This is what the term Islam inspires and demands of every Muslim. That every act of his in this life secular or religious- to be exclusively for God. Refer to Verse 2:156.) ." The highest goal of human life is the Law of God which alone must be the mainspring or the generative factor of every word and deed of a man or a woman in this life. Be that the love of one's self, of one's family and children, love of one's friends and relatives, the law of one's country and countrymen, the lover of wealth or any other…

item.title: Al-An'aam:163 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَبِذٰلِكَ أُمِرْتُ وَأَنَا أَوَّلُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ lā sharīka lahu wabidhālika umir'tu wa-anā awwalu l-mus'limīna He has no partner, and this [creed] I have been commanded [to follow], and I am the first of those who submit [to Allah].'

item.title: Al-An'aam:163 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَبِذٰلِكَ أُمِرْتُ وَأَنَا أَوَّلُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ lā sharīka lahu wabidhālika umir'tu wa-anā awwalu l-mus'limīna No partner has He. And this I have been commanded, and I am the first (among you) of the Muslims."1 See 6:161

item.title: Al-An'aam:163 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَبِذٰلِكَ أُمِرْتُ وَأَنَا أَوَّلُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ lā sharīka lahu wabidhālika umir'tu wa-anā awwalu l-mus'limīna No associate (In the devotion of The Holy Prophet to Him.) (is there) for Him; and this I am commanded, I am the first of the Muslims (i.e., those who submit to God) (Refer to Verse 6:14.) . This Verse clearly says that the first, i.e., the ideal or the perfect model of a true Muslim, was the Holy Prophet himself.

item.title: Al-An'aam:164 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أَبْغِي رَبًّا وَهُوَ رَبُّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَلَا تَكْسِبُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ إِلَّا عَلَيْهَا وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرٰی ثُمَّ إِلَى رَبِّكُمْ مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ فِیْهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ qul aghayra l-lahi abghī rabban wahuwa rabbu kulli shayin walā taksibu kullu nafsin illā ʿalayhā walā taziru wāziratun wiz'ra ukh'rā thumma ilā rabbikum marjiʿukum fayunabbi-ukum bimā kuntum fīhi takhtalifūna Say, 'Shall I seek a Lord other than Allah, while He is the Lord of all things?' No soul does evil except against itself, and no bearer shall bear another's burden; then to your Lord will be your return, whereat He will inform you concerning that about which you used to differ.

item.title: Al-An'aam:164 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أَبْغِي رَبًّا وَهُوَ رَبُّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَلَا تَكْسِبُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ إِلَّا عَلَيْهَا وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرٰی ثُمَّ إِلَى رَبِّكُمْ مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ فِیْهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ qul aghayra l-lahi abghī rabban wahuwa rabbu kulli shayin walā taksibu kullu nafsin illā ʿalayhā walā taziru wāziratun wiz'ra ukh'rā thumma ilā rabbikum marjiʿukum fayunabbi-ukum bimā kuntum fīhi takhtalifūna Say, "Is it other than Allah I should desire as a lord while He is the Lord of all things? And every soul earns not (blame) except against itself, and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you concerning that over which you used to differ." Say: Shall I seek a lord other than Allah, while He is the Lord of all things? No person earns any (sin)…

item.title: Al-An'aam:164 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أَبْغِي رَبًّا وَهُوَ رَبُّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَلَا تَكْسِبُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ إِلَّا عَلَيْهَا وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرٰی ثُمَّ إِلَى رَبِّكُمْ مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ فِیْهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ qul aghayra l-lahi abghī rabban wahuwa rabbu kulli shayin walā taksibu kullu nafsin illā ʿalayhā walā taziru wāziratun wiz'ra ukh'rā thumma ilā rabbikum marjiʿukum fayunabbi-ukum bimā kuntum fīhi takhtalifūna Say: "Shall I seek other than God a Lord? While He is the Lord of all things; and no soul earneth (any evil deed) but against itself; and no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another; then unto your Lord is your return, so He will inform you of what ye used to differ (about) (Refer to Verses 2:48; 2:123; 2:254; 17:15; 35:18; 39:7; 53:38; 53:39.)" Islam does not allow any belief in any unconditional redemption of any one, merely…

item.title: Al-An'aam:165 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَكُمْ خَلَائِفَ الْأَرْضِ وَرَفَعَ بَعْضَكُمْ فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجَاتٍ لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ فِي مَا ءَاتَاكُمْ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ سَرِيعُ الْعِقَابِ وَإِنَّهُ لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ wahuwa alladhī jaʿalakum khalāifa l-arḍi warafaʿa baʿḍakum fawqa baʿḍin darajātin liyabluwakum fī mā ātākum inna rabbaka sarīʿu l-ʿiqābi wa-innahu laghafūrun raḥīmun It is He who has made you successors on the earth, and raised some of you in rank above others so that He may test you in respect to what He has given you. Indeed your Lord is swift in retribution, and indeed He is all-forgiving, all-merciful.

item.title: Al-An'aam:165 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَكُمْ خَلَائِفَ الْأَرْضِ وَرَفَعَ بَعْضَكُمْ فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجَاتٍ لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ فِي مَا ءَاتَاكُمْ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ سَرِيعُ الْعِقَابِ وَإِنَّهُ لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ wahuwa alladhī jaʿalakum khalāifa l-arḍi warafaʿa baʿḍakum fawqa baʿḍin darajātin liyabluwakum fī mā ātākum inna rabbaka sarīʿu l-ʿiqābi wa-innahu laghafūrun raḥīmun And it is He who has made you successors upon the earth and has raised some of you above others in degrees (of rank) that He may try you through what He has given you. Indeed, your Lord is swift in penalty; but indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful. And it is He Who has made you generations coming after generations, replacing each other on the earth. And He has raised you in ranks, some above others that He may try you in that which He has bestowed on you. Surely, your Lord is Swift in retribution, and…

item.title: Al-An'aam:165 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَكُمْ خَلَائِفَ الْأَرْضِ وَرَفَعَ بَعْضَكُمْ فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجَاتٍ لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ فِي مَا ءَاتَاكُمْ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ سَرِيعُ الْعِقَابِ وَإِنَّهُ لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ wahuwa alladhī jaʿalakum khalāifa l-arḍi warafaʿa baʿḍakum fawqa baʿḍin darajātin liyabluwakum fī mā ātākum inna rabbaka sarīʿu l-ʿiqābi wa-innahu laghafūrun raḥīmun And He (God.) it is who hath made you (His) Vicegerent in the earth and raised some of you above others in grades, that He may try you in what He gave you; Verily thy Lord is quick in the requital (of evil) and (yet) verily He is the Oft-Forgiving, the Merciful. The word 'Khalif' meaning the deputies of God, i.e., man or woman, has been created to manifest the divine attributes in his or her life. If one remains conscious of this great assignment and tries to be true to the trust, it will be quite sufficient…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اِقْتَرَبَ لِلنَّاسِ حِسَابُهُمْ وَهُمْ فِي غَفْلَةٍ مُعْرِضُونَ iq'taraba lilnnāsi ḥisābuhum wahum fī ghaflatin muʿ'riḍūna Mankind's reckoning has drawn near to them, yet they are disregardful in [their] obliviousness.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اِقْتَرَبَ لِلنَّاسِ حِسَابُهُمْ وَهُمْ فِي غَفْلَةٍ مُعْرِضُونَ iq'taraba lilnnāsi ḥisābuhum wahum fī ghaflatin muʿ'riḍūna (The time of) their account has approached for the people, while they are in heedlessness turning away. مَا آمَنَتْ قَبْلَهُم مِّن قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَاهَا ۖ أَفَهُمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ Not one of the towns of those which We destroyed, believed before them; will they then believe? None of the peoples to whom Messengers were sent were given a sign at the hands of their Prophet and believed. On the contrary, they disbelieved and We destroyed them as a result. Would these people believe in a sign if they saw it? Not at all! In fact: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ حَقَّتْ عَلَيْهِمْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ - وَلَوْ جَاءَتْهُمْ كُلُّ آيَةٍ حَتَّىٰ يَرَوُا الْعَذَابَ الْأَلِيمَ Truly, those, against whom the Word of your Lord has been justified, will not believe. Even if…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اِقْتَرَبَ لِلنَّاسِ حِسَابُهُمْ وَهُمْ فِي غَفْلَةٍ مُعْرِضُونَ iq'taraba lilnnāsi ḥisābuhum wahum fī ghaflatin muʿ'riḍūna Hath drawn nigh (Nigh because Muhammad the last Apostle or Warner to mankind has come and the Final Word (Qur'an) delivered. This is what the people did with the previous apostles also.) unto the people (the day of) their reckoning, and they in heedlessness are turning aside. Since Muhammad, the Last Apostle of God promised to mankind has already come, the Holy Qur'an, the Final Word of God has been revealed and Islam, the religion prescribed by God has been preached, the Day of Judgment is naturally nearer at hand than before. Everyone is sure to meet death sooner or later and none knows when he would reach the end of his life-journey at which he will have to account for his faith and deeds and…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ ذِكْرٍ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ مُحْدَثٍ إِلَّا اسْتَمَعُوهُ وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ mā yatīhim min dhik'rin min rabbihim muḥ'dathin illā is'tamaʿūhu wahum yalʿabūna There does not come to them any new reminder from their Lord but they listen to it as they play around,

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ ذِكْرٍ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ مُحْدَثٍ إِلَّا اسْتَمَعُوهُ وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ mā yatīhim min dhik'rin min rabbihim muḥ'dathin illā is'tamaʿūhu wahum yalʿabūna No mention (i.e., revelation) comes to them anew from their Lord except that they listen to it while they are at play. See 21:1

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ ذِكْرٍ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ مُحْدَثٍ إِلَّا اسْتَمَعُوهُ وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ mā yatīhim min dhik'rin min rabbihim muḥ'dathin illā is'tamaʿūhu wahum yalʿabūna (There) Cometh not unto them a reminder from their Lord, anew, save they hear it and they get busy in sport. Even with the repeated reminder from the Lord, instead of getting awakened to be guided aright, the people only listen to the admonition only to ridicule and laugh at them. They waste their life and wealth in wasteful fooleries forgetting totally the life Hereafter.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَاهِيَةً قُلُوبُهُمْ وَأَسَرُّوا النَّجْوَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوْۤا هَلْ هَذَا إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُكُمْ أَفَتَأْتُونَ السِّحْرَ وَأَنْتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ lāhiyatan qulūbuhum wa-asarrū l-najwā alladhīna ẓalamū hal hādhā illā basharun mith'lukum afatatūna l-siḥ'ra wa-antum tub'ṣirūna their hearts set on diversions. The wrongdoers secretly whisper together, [saying], 'Is not this [man] just a human being like yourselves? Will you give in to magic with open eyes?'

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَاهِيَةً قُلُوبُهُمْ وَأَسَرُّوا النَّجْوَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوْۤا هَلْ هَذَا إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُكُمْ أَفَتَأْتُونَ السِّحْرَ وَأَنْتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ lāhiyatan qulūbuhum wa-asarrū l-najwā alladhīna ẓalamū hal hādhā illā basharun mith'lukum afatatūna l-siḥ'ra wa-antum tub'ṣirūna With their hearts distracted. And those who do wrong conceal their private conversation, (saying), "Is this (Prophet) except a human being like you? So would you approach magic while you are aware (of it)?" See 21:1

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَاهِيَةً قُلُوبُهُمْ وَأَسَرُّوا النَّجْوَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوْۤا هَلْ هَذَا إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُكُمْ أَفَتَأْتُونَ السِّحْرَ وَأَنْتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ lāhiyatan qulūbuhum wa-asarrū l-najwā alladhīna ẓalamū hal hādhā illā basharun mith'lukum afatatūna l-siḥ'ra wa-antum tub'ṣirūna Pre-occupied at their hearts with trifles; and discoursed in secret (Refer to verse 20:62.) ; those who did wrong (saying) "Is this (man) (The Holy Prophet.) other (Not more than an ordinary man.) than a human being like unto yourselves; What! will ye then yield unto sorcery while ye see (it)?" The reference is to the attitude of the disbelievers towards the recital of the Holy Qur'an. They listened with a trifling heart and when struck with the miraculous impression of the Word of God they secretly counselled to each other saying that the Holy Prophet was merely a man like them and what he recited was only a sorcery,…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ رَبِّي يَعْلَمُ الْقَوْلَ فِي السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ qāla rabbī yaʿlamu l-qawla fī l-samāi wal-arḍi wahuwa l-samīʿu l-ʿalīmu He said, 'My Lord knows every word [spoken] in the sky and the earth, and He is the All-hearing, the All-knowing.'

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ رَبِّي يَعْلَمُ الْقَوْلَ فِي السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ qāla rabbī yaʿlamu l-qawla fī l-samāi wal-arḍi wahuwa l-samīʿu l-ʿalīmu He (the Prophet SAW) said, "My Lord knows whatever is said throughout the heaven and earth, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing." See 21:1

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ رَبِّي يَعْلَمُ الْقَوْلَ فِي السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ qāla rabbī yaʿlamu l-qawla fī l-samāi wal-arḍi wahuwa l-samīʿu l-ʿalīmu He (The Holy Prophet who brought the Reminder anew.) said: "My Lord (well) knoweth (every) word (spoken) in the heaven and the earth; and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing." See 21:3

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ قَالُوْا أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلَامٍ بَلِ افْتَرَاهُ بَلْ هُوَ شَاعِرٌ فَلْيَأْتِنَا بِاٰیَةٍ كَمَا أُرْسِلَ الْأَوَّلُونَ bal qālū aḍghāthu aḥlāmin bali if'tarāhu bal huwa shāʿirun falyatinā biāyatin kamā ur'sila l-awalūna Rather they said, '[They are] confused nightmares!' 'Rather he has fabricated it!' 'Rather he is a poet!' 'Let him bring us a sign, like those sent to the ancients.'

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ قَالُوْا أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلَامٍ بَلِ افْتَرَاهُ بَلْ هُوَ شَاعِرٌ فَلْيَأْتِنَا بِاٰیَةٍ كَمَا أُرْسِلَ الْأَوَّلُونَ bal qālū aḍghāthu aḥlāmin bali if'tarāhu bal huwa shāʿirun falyatinā biāyatin kamā ur'sila l-awalūna But they say, "(The revelation is but) a mixture of false dreams; rather, he has invented it; rather, he is a poet. So let him bring us a sign just as the previous (messengers) were sent (with miracles)." See 21:1

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ قَالُوْا أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلَامٍ بَلِ افْتَرَاهُ بَلْ هُوَ شَاعِرٌ فَلْيَأْتِنَا بِاٰیَةٍ كَمَا أُرْسِلَ الْأَوَّلُونَ bal qālū aḍghāthu aḥlāmin bali if'tarāhu bal huwa shāʿirun falyatinā biāyatin kamā ur'sila l-awalūna Nay! say they: (these are) medleys of dreams (Refer to verse 12:44.) ! Nay! he hath forged it; Nay! he is a poet; let him then bring unto us a sign like unto the ones that were sent unto the former ones (of the apostles). They were struck with the miraculous effect the Holy Qur'an created and notwithstanding the natural and the irresistible impression the Word of God created on them, which they helplessly called it sorcery, or the wonders of a dream or the marvel of poetry. They demanded a miracle although the Holy Qur'an is by itself a challenging miracle. This was the actual position of the pagans who used…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا اٰمَنَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَاهَا أَفَهُمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ mā āmanat qablahum min qaryatin ahlaknāhā afahum yu'minūna No town that We destroyed before them believed.1 Will these then have faith [if they are sent signs]?

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا اٰمَنَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَاهَا أَفَهُمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ mā āmanat qablahum min qaryatin ahlaknāhā afahum yu'minūna Not a (single) city which We destroyed believed before them,1 so will they believe? See 21:1

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا اٰمَنَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَاهَا أَفَهُمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ mā āmanat qablahum min qaryatin ahlaknāhā afahum yu'minūna Believed not before them (the people of) any of the towns which We did destroy: what! will these (now) believe? What happened to the miracles already shown heretofore by the previous apostles of God? Were they not sufficient? Should God and His apostles be ever ready to go on showing miracles as and when they are demanded by men stubborn, in their disbelief with a determination never to believe at all? Persistence in disbelief and wickedness in spite of the miracles had always been punished. Hence the mercy of the Lord demands belief through the use of reasoning. If miracles accompany the admonishing, surely the next step as the natural consequence would be destruction. And if the people resist even the clearest arguments, they…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا قَبْلَكَ إِلَّا رِجَالًا نُوحِي إِلَيْهِمْ فَسْءَلُوْۤا أَهْلَ الذِّكْرِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ wamā arsalnā qablaka illā rijālan nūḥī ilayhim fasalū ahla l-dhik'ri in kuntum lā taʿlamūna We did not send [any apostles] before you except as men, to whom We revealed. Ask the People of the Reminder1 if you do not know.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا قَبْلَكَ إِلَّا رِجَالًا نُوحِي إِلَيْهِمْ فَسْءَلُوْۤا أَهْلَ الذِّكْرِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ wamā arsalnā qablaka illā rijālan nūḥī ilayhim fasalū ahla l-dhik'ri in kuntum lā taʿlamūna And We sent not before you, (O Muḥammad), except men to whom We revealed (the message), so ask the people of the message (i.e., former scriptures) if you do not know. And We sent not before you but men to whom We revealed. So ask the people of the Reminder if you do not know (21:7). And We did not place them in bodies that did not eat food, nor were they immortals (21:8). Then We fulfilled to them the promise. So We saved them and those whom We willed, but We destroyed Al-Musrifin (21:9). The Messengers are No More than Human Beings Here Allah refutes those who denied that human Messengers…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا قَبْلَكَ إِلَّا رِجَالًا نُوحِي إِلَيْهِمْ فَسْءَلُوْۤا أَهْلَ الذِّكْرِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ wamā arsalnā qablaka illā rijālan nūḥī ilayhim fasalū ahla l-dhik'ri in kuntum lā taʿlamūna And We sent not before thee, but men unto whom We did reveal, so ask ye the people of the (The Ahl al-Bayt with whom the Reminder (the Qur'an) was left see 'Hadith al-Thaqlayn'. See note to verse 21:7.) Reminder (Refer to note on verse 16:43.) if ye know not. 'Dhikr' - literally meaning a 'Reminder.' It is one of the names of the Holy Qur'an. 'Ahl al-Dhikr' means here the people of the Holy Qur'an, i.e., the Holy Prophet and the Holy Ahl al-Bayt whom God Himself purified1 and sent into the world for the guidance of humanity. It has repeatedly been pointed out as to who the 'Ahl al-Dhikr' are,…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا جَعَلْنَاهُمْ جَسَدًا لَا يَأْكُلُونَ الطَّعَامَ وَمَا كَانُوْۤا خَالِدِينَ wamā jaʿalnāhum jasadan lā yakulūna l-ṭaʿāma wamā kānū khālidīna We did not make them bodies that did not eat food, and they were not immortal.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا جَعَلْنَاهُمْ جَسَدًا لَا يَأْكُلُونَ الطَّعَامَ وَمَا كَانُوْۤا خَالِدِينَ wamā jaʿalnāhum jasadan lā yakulūna l-ṭaʿāma wamā kānū khālidīna And We did not make them (i.e., the prophets) forms not eating food,1 nor were they immortal (on earth). See 21:7

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا جَعَلْنَاهُمْ جَسَدًا لَا يَأْكُلُونَ الطَّعَامَ وَمَا كَانُوْۤا خَالِدِينَ wamā jaʿalnāhum jasadan lā yakulūna l-ṭaʿāma wamā kānū khālidīna We made them not (such) bodies not eating the food, and they were not to abide (in this world) for ever. Meaning that all the other apostles of God were also men with a mortal body which is sustained only by some material food. Jesus, though born without a male parent had also a mortal body, and God who raised him in his body, to heaven is not a helpless and a resourceless being like any one of us; He is the Almighty Lord who created Jesus as the Sign or the Token of His independent Will, Authority and Omnipotence and He can sustain Jesus similarly with, in some way unknown to we mortals or even providing him with the needs of…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ صَدَقْنَاهُمُ الْوَعْدَ فَأَنْجَيْنَاهُمْ وَمَنْ نَشَاءُ وَأَهْلَكْنَا الْمُسْرِفِينَ thumma ṣadaqnāhumu l-waʿda fa-anjaynāhum waman nashāu wa-ahlaknā l-mus'rifīna Then We fulfilled Our promise to them, and We delivered them and whomever We wished, and We destroyed the profligates.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ صَدَقْنَاهُمُ الْوَعْدَ فَأَنْجَيْنَاهُمْ وَمَنْ نَشَاءُ وَأَهْلَكْنَا الْمُسْرِفِينَ thumma ṣadaqnāhumu l-waʿda fa-anjaynāhum waman nashāu wa-ahlaknā l-mus'rifīna Then1 We fulfilled for them the promise, and We saved them and whom We willed and destroyed the transgressors. See 21:7

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ صَدَقْنَاهُمُ الْوَعْدَ فَأَنْجَيْنَاهُمْ وَمَنْ نَشَاءُ وَأَهْلَكْنَا الْمُسْرِفِينَ thumma ṣadaqnāhumu l-waʿda fa-anjaynāhum waman nashāu wa-ahlaknā l-mus'rifīna Then fulfilled We unto them Our promise (of punishment), then We delivered them, and those whom We willed, and We destroyed the extravagant (Those who exceeded the limits.) ones. The reference is to the promise of the triumph of the apostles over their enemies - the destruction of all those who disbelieved in the Word of God and defied His apostles.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَقَدْ أَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكُمْ كِتَابًا فِیْهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ laqad anzalnā ilaykum kitāban fīhi dhik'rukum afalā taʿqilūna Certainly We have sent down to you a Book in which there is an admonition for you. Do you not apply reason?

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَقَدْ أَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكُمْ كِتَابًا فِیْهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ laqad anzalnā ilaykum kitāban fīhi dhik'rukum afalā taʿqilūna We have certainly sent down to you a Book (i.e., the Qur’ān) in which is your mention.1 Then will you not reason? Indeed, We have sent down for you a Book in which there is Dhikrukum. Will you not then understand (21:10). How many a town given to wrongdoing, have We destroyed, and raised up after them another people (21:11). Then, when they sensed Our torment, behold, they (tried to) flee from it (21:12). Flee not, but return to that wherein you lived a luxurious life, and to your homes, in order that you may be questioned (21:13). They cried: Woe to us! Certainly we have been wrongdoers (21:14). And that cry of theirs ceased not, till We made them as a field that…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَقَدْ أَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكُمْ كِتَابًا فِیْهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ laqad anzalnā ilaykum kitāban fīhi dhik'rukum afalā taʿqilūna Indeed have We sent down unto you a Book (the Qur'an) wherein is your remembrance; (Also, admonition.) What! Do ye not then understand? See 21:9

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَكَمْ قَصَمْنَا مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ كَانَتْ ظَالِمَةً وَأَنْشَأْنَا بَعْدَهَا قَوْمًا ءَاخَرِينَ wakam qaṣamnā min qaryatin kānat ẓālimatan wa-anshanā baʿdahā qawman ākharīna How many a town We have smashed that had been wrongdoing, and We brought forth another people after it.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَكَمْ قَصَمْنَا مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ كَانَتْ ظَالِمَةً وَأَنْشَأْنَا بَعْدَهَا قَوْمًا ءَاخَرِينَ wakam qaṣamnā min qaryatin kānat ẓālimatan wa-anshanā baʿdahā qawman ākharīna And how many a city which was unjust1 have We shattered and produced after it another people. See 21:10

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَكَمْ قَصَمْنَا مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ كَانَتْ ظَالِمَةً وَأَنْشَأْنَا بَعْدَهَا قَوْمًا ءَاخَرِينَ wakam qaṣamnā min qaryatin kānat ẓālimatan wa-anshanā baʿdahā qawman ākharīna How many a town (the people of) which were iniquitous, We did (Break.) destroy, and raised We up after it another (Nation – folk.) people? See 21:9

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا أَحَسُّوْۤا بَأْسَنَا إِذَا هُمْ مِنْهَا يَرْكُضُونَ falammā aḥassū basanā idhā hum min'hā yarkuḍūna So when they sighted Our punishment, behold, they ran away from it.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا أَحَسُّوْۤا بَأْسَنَا إِذَا هُمْ مِنْهَا يَرْكُضُونَ falammā aḥassū basanā idhā hum min'hā yarkuḍūna And when they (i.e., its inhabitants) perceived Our punishment, at once they fled from it. See 21:10

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا أَحَسُّوْۤا بَأْسَنَا إِذَا هُمْ مِنْهَا يَرْكُضُونَ falammā aḥassū basanā idhā hum min'hā yarkuḍūna So when they felt (the coming of) Our torment, lo! they began (trying) to fly from it. People do not avail of the respite given to them and when the Wrath of God comes, they try to flee from it; but where would they go?

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا تَرْكُضُوْۤا وَارْجِعُوا إِلَى مَا أُتْرِفْتُمْ فِیْهِ وَمَسَاكِنِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُسْءَلُونَ lā tarkuḍū wa-ir'jiʿū ilā mā ut'rif'tum fīhi wamasākinikum laʿallakum tus'alūna 'Do not run away! Return to the opulence you were given to enjoy and to your dwellings so that you may be questioned!'

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا تَرْكُضُوْۤا وَارْجِعُوا إِلَى مَا أُتْرِفْتُمْ فِیْهِ وَمَسَاكِنِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُسْءَلُونَ lā tarkuḍū wa-ir'jiʿū ilā mā ut'rif'tum fīhi wamasākinikum laʿallakum tus'alūna (Some angels said), "Do not flee but return to where you were given luxury and to your homes - perhaps you will be questioned."1 See 21:10

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:13 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا تَرْكُضُوْۤا وَارْجِعُوا إِلَى مَا أُتْرِفْتُمْ فِیْهِ وَمَسَاكِنِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُسْءَلُونَ lā tarkuḍū wa-ir'jiʿū ilā mā ut'rif'tum fīhi wamasākinikum laʿallakum tus'alūna (Said We (God.) ): "Flee not ye but return unto that wherein ye revelled, (Lived easy – extravagantly.) and unto your dwellings, happly ye will be questioned." It is an ironical statement asking them why they do not return to the life of the luxuries on earth, which they were engrossed in and thought the life on earth to be permanent, and they did not believe in the Day of Reckoning.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:14 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا يَاوَيْلَنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ qālū yāwaylanā innā kunnā ẓālimīna They said, 'Woe to us! We have indeed been wrongdoers!'

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:14 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا يَاوَيْلَنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ qālū yāwaylanā innā kunnā ẓālimīna They said, "O woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers." See 21:10

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:14 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا يَاوَيْلَنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ qālū yāwaylanā innā kunnā ẓālimīna Said they: "Oh! Woe unto us! Verily, we were unjust!" This would be the repentant lamentations of the disbelievers.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَمَا زَالَتْ تِلْكَ دَعْوَاهُمْ حَتّٰی جَعَلْنَاهُمْ حَصِيدًا خَامِدِينَ famā zālat til'ka daʿwāhum ḥattā jaʿalnāhum ḥaṣīdan khāmidīna That remained their cry until We turned them into a mown field, stilled [like burnt ashes].

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَمَا زَالَتْ تِلْكَ دَعْوَاهُمْ حَتّٰی جَعَلْنَاهُمْ حَصِيدًا خَامِدِينَ famā zālat til'ka daʿwāhum ḥattā jaʿalnāhum ḥaṣīdan khāmidīna And that declaration of theirs did not cease until We made them (as) a harvest (mowed down), extinguished (like a fire). See 21:10

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَمَا زَالَتْ تِلْكَ دَعْوَاهُمْ حَتّٰی جَعَلْنَاهُمْ حَصِيدًا خَامِدِينَ famā zālat til'ka daʿwāhum ḥattā jaʿalnāhum ḥaṣīdan khāmidīna And ceased not this their cry till We made them like reaped (Cut off.) corn, extinct. The two similes refer to the fate with which the disbelievers are warned, as to what their end would be.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا خَلَقْنَا السَّمَاءَ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا لَاعِبِينَ wamā khalaqnā l-samāa wal-arḍa wamā baynahumā lāʿibīna We did not create the sky and the earth and whatever is between them for play.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا خَلَقْنَا السَّمَاءَ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا لَاعِبِينَ wamā khalaqnā l-samāa wal-arḍa wamā baynahumā lāʿibīna And We did not create the heaven and earth and that between them in play. We created not the heavens and the earth and all that is between them for play (21:16). Had We intended to take a pastime, We could surely have taken it from Us, if We were going to do (that) (21:17). Nay, We fling the truth against the falsehood, so it destroys it, and behold, it disappears. And woe to you for that which you ascribe (21:18). To Him belongs whosoever is in the heavens and on earth. And those who are near Him are not too proud to worship Him, nor are they weary (21:19). They glorify His praises night and day, they never slacken (21:20). Creation was Made with Justice…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا خَلَقْنَا السَّمَاءَ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا لَاعِبِينَ wamā khalaqnā l-samāa wal-arḍa wamā baynahumā lāʿibīna And We created not the heavens and the earth and what is between them for (Refer to verse 44:38.) sport. Nothing in the universe has been created without any object behind its existence. People are warned not to take life lightly. To consider every factor of life seriously.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَوْ أَرَدْنَا أَنْ نَتَّخِذَ لَهْوًا لَاتَّخَذْنَاهُ مِنْ لَدُنَّا إِنْ كُنَّا فَاعِلِينَ law aradnā an nattakhidha lahwan la-ittakhadhnāhu min ladunnā in kunnā fāʿilīna Had We desired to take up some diversion We would have surely taken it up with Ourselves, were We to do [so].

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَوْ أَرَدْنَا أَنْ نَتَّخِذَ لَهْوًا لَاتَّخَذْنَاهُ مِنْ لَدُنَّا إِنْ كُنَّا فَاعِلِينَ law aradnā an nattakhidha lahwan la-ittakhadhnāhu min ladunnā in kunnā fāʿilīna Had We intended to take a diversion,1 We could have taken it from (what is) with Us - if (indeed) We were to do so. See 21:16

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:17 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَوْ أَرَدْنَا أَنْ نَتَّخِذَ لَهْوًا لَاتَّخَذْنَاهُ مِنْ لَدُنَّا إِنْ كُنَّا فَاعِلِينَ law aradnā an nattakhidha lahwan la-ittakhadhnāhu min ladunnā in kunnā fāʿilīna Had We intended that We should take amusement, We could certainly have taken it from (the things) with Us, if We had been doing (it) We had willed to do it. If at all God had desired anything like a mere sport, the things of real excellence with Him, would have sufficed the purpose and not the lowly creation of the earthly beings. Asserts that the creation of the heavens and the earth is not purposeless, and the purpose is something serious - and not playful and not for mere amusement. The analogical tendency in man makes him always to conceive about God after his own image. As man's action is sometimes motivated by fun or amusement, he…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:18 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ نَقْذِفُ بِالْحَقِّ عَلَى الْبَاطِلِ فَيَدْمَغُهُ فَإِذَا هُوَ زَاهِقٌ وَلَكُمُ الْوَيْلُ مِمَّا تَصِفُونَ bal naqdhifu bil-ḥaqi ʿalā l-bāṭili fayadmaghuhu fa-idhā huwa zāhiqun walakumu l-waylu mimmā taṣifūna Rather We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes its head, and behold, falsehood vanishes! And woe to you for what you allege [about Allah].

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:18 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
