item.description: بَلْ نَقْذِفُ بِالْحَقِّ عَلَى الْبَاطِلِ فَيَدْمَغُهُ فَإِذَا هُوَ زَاهِقٌ وَلَكُمُ الْوَيْلُ مِمَّا تَصِفُونَ bal naqdhifu bil-ḥaqi ʿalā l-bāṭili fayadmaghuhu fa-idhā huwa zāhiqun walakumu l-waylu mimmā taṣifūna Rather, We dash the truth upon falsehood, and it destroys it,1 and thereupon it departs. And for you is destruction from that which you describe.2 See 21:16

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:18 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ نَقْذِفُ بِالْحَقِّ عَلَى الْبَاطِلِ فَيَدْمَغُهُ فَإِذَا هُوَ زَاهِقٌ وَلَكُمُ الْوَيْلُ مِمَّا تَصِفُونَ bal naqdhifu bil-ḥaqi ʿalā l-bāṭili fayadmaghuhu fa-idhā huwa zāhiqun walakumu l-waylu mimmā taṣifūna Nay! We hurl truth upon falsehood, that it crusheth its head, and lo! it vanisheth; and woe unto you for what ye describe (of God). 'Describe' refers to the false belief of God having partners1 and God having begotten a son2 or His having daughters3 or any other polytheistic belief about God.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:19 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَهُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَنْ عِنْدَهُ لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِهِ وَلَا يَسْتَحْسِرُونَ walahu man fī l-samāwāti wal-arḍi waman ʿindahu lā yastakbirūna ʿan ʿibādatihi walā yastaḥsirūna To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and those who are near Him do not disdain to worship Him, nor do they become weary.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:19 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَهُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَنْ عِنْدَهُ لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِهِ وَلَا يَسْتَحْسِرُونَ walahu man fī l-samāwāti wal-arḍi waman ʿindahu lā yastakbirūna ʿan ʿibādatihi walā yastaḥsirūna To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth. And those near Him (i.e., the angels) are not prevented by arrogance from His worship, nor do they tire. See 21:16

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:19 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَهُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَنْ عِنْدَهُ لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِهِ وَلَا يَسْتَحْسِرُونَ walahu man fī l-samāwāti wal-arḍi waman ʿindahu lā yastakbirūna ʿan ʿibādatihi walā yastaḥsirūna And His is whosoever is in the heavens and the earth; and those who are (Present with God.) with Him are not proud to worship Him, nor do they get weary. The heavenly beings which are also the created ones of God unceasingly adore the Majesty of the Glory of the Lord.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:20 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يُسَبِّحُونَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ لَا يَفْتُرُونَ yusabbiḥūna al-layla wal-nahāra lā yafturūna They glorify [Him] night and day, and they do not flag.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:20 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يُسَبِّحُونَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ لَا يَفْتُرُونَ yusabbiḥūna al-layla wal-nahāra lā yafturūna They exalt (Him) night and day (and) do not slacken. See 21:16

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:20 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يُسَبِّحُونَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ لَا يَفْتُرُونَ yusabbiḥūna al-layla wal-nahāra lā yafturūna They glorify (Him) by night and day, they (even) intermit (Relax not.) not. See 21:19

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:21 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَمِ اتَّخَذُوا آلِهَةً مِنَ الْأَرْضِ هُمْ يُنْشِرُونَ ami ittakhadhū ālihatan mina l-arḍi hum yunshirūna Have they taken gods from the earth who raise [the dead]?

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:21 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَمِ اتَّخَذُوا آلِهَةً مِنَ الْأَرْضِ هُمْ يُنْشِرُونَ ami ittakhadhū ālihatan mina l-arḍi hum yunshirūna Or have they (i.e., men) taken for themselves gods from the earth who resurrect (the dead)? Or have they taken (for worship) gods from the earth who raise the dead (21:21). Had there been therein (in the heavens and the earth) gods besides Allah, then verily, both would have been ruined. Glorified be Allah, the Lord of the Throne, (High is He) above all that (evil) they associate with Him (21:22). He cannot be questioned as to what He does, while they will be questioned (21:23). Refutation of False Gods Allah denounces those who take other gods instead of Him: أَمِ اتَّخَذُوا آلِهَةً مِّنَ الْأَرْضِ هُمْ يُنشِرُونَ Or have they taken gods from the earth who raise the dead? Meaning: can they bring the dead back…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:21 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَمِ اتَّخَذُوا آلِهَةً مِنَ الْأَرْضِ هُمْ يُنْشِرُونَ ami ittakhadhū ālihatan mina l-arḍi hum yunshirūna Or have they taken gods from the earth who can raise (the dead)? It is made clear that the false gods or the imaginary deities can never give life to anything which God has destined to die. This does not mean that any of the apostles of God also who show miracles manifesting the Omnipotence of God, cannot raise the dead which they can do by God's will. Thus, the raising of the dead caused by Jesus as a miracle can never be brought under this statement.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:22 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَا آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتَا فَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَرْشِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ law kāna fīhimā ālihatun illā l-lahu lafasadatā fasub'ḥāna l-lahi rabbi l-ʿarshi ʿammā yaṣifūna Had there been gods in them1 other than Allah, they would surely have fallen apart. Clear is Allah, the Lord of the Throne, of what they allege [concerning Him].

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:22 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَا آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتَا فَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَرْشِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ law kāna fīhimā ālihatun illā l-lahu lafasadatā fasub'ḥāna l-lahi rabbi l-ʿarshi ʿammā yaṣifūna Had there been within them (i.e., the heavens and earth) gods besides Allah, they both would have been ruined. So exalted is Allah, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe. See 21:21

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:22 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَا آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتَا فَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَرْشِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ law kāna fīhimā ālihatun illā l-lahu lafasadatā fasub'ḥāna l-lahi rabbi l-ʿarshi ʿammā yaṣifūna Had there been in (the heavens and the earth) (other) gods except God, they both had been in disorder; So glorified is God, the Lord of the 'Arsh' (The Throne of Supreme Authority.) (High above) from what they attribute (unto Him). This is the simplest and the greatest and the self-proved argument about the Unity of God. The unity and the perfect harmony with which the universe is going on since its birth, itself is the proof positive that there is only One single authority which is governing the working of the universe with the laws regulated in perfect harmony with each other. If there be two or more beings holding equal authorities over…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:23 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا يُسْءَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْءَلُونَ lā yus'alu ʿammā yafʿalu wahum yus'alūna He is not questioned concerning what He does, but they are questioned.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:23 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا يُسْءَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْءَلُونَ lā yus'alu ʿammā yafʿalu wahum yus'alūna He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned. See 21:21

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:23 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا يُسْءَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْءَلُونَ lā yus'alu ʿammā yafʿalu wahum yus'alūna He is not questioned about what He doeth, but they shall be questioned. There can be no argument against any Act of God. God is never questionable, whereas it is man who would be questioned.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:24 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَمِ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ آلِهَةً قُلْ هَاتُوْۤا بُرْهَانَكُمْ هَذَا ذِكْرُ مَنْ مَعِيَ وَذِكْرُ مَنْ قَبْلِي بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ الْحَقَّ فَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ ami ittakhadhū min dūnihi ālihatan qul hātū bur'hānakum hādhā dhik'ru man maʿiya wadhik'ru man qablī bal aktharuhum lā yaʿlamūna l-ḥaqa fahum muʿ'riḍūna Have they taken gods besides Him? Say, 'Produce your evidence! This is a precept of those who are with me, and a precept of those [who went] before me.' Rather most of them do not know the truth, and so they are disregardful.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:24 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَمِ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ آلِهَةً قُلْ هَاتُوْۤا بُرْهَانَكُمْ هَذَا ذِكْرُ مَنْ مَعِيَ وَذِكْرُ مَنْ قَبْلِي بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ الْحَقَّ فَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ ami ittakhadhū min dūnihi ālihatan qul hātū bur'hānakum hādhā dhik'ru man maʿiya wadhik'ru man qablī bal aktharuhum lā yaʿlamūna l-ḥaqa fahum muʿ'riḍūna Or have they taken gods besides Him? Say, (O Muḥammad), "Produce your proof. This (Qur’ān) is the message for those with me and the message of those before me."1 But most of them do not know the truth, so they are turning away. Or have they taken for worship gods besides Him Say: Bring your proof. This is the Reminder for those with me and the Reminder for those before me." But most of them know not the Truth, so they are averse (21:24). And We did not send any Messenger before you but We revealed…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:24 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَمِ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ آلِهَةً قُلْ هَاتُوْۤا بُرْهَانَكُمْ هَذَا ذِكْرُ مَنْ مَعِيَ وَذِكْرُ مَنْ قَبْلِي بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ الْحَقَّ فَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ ami ittakhadhū min dūnihi ālihatan qul hātū bur'hānakum hādhā dhik'ru man maʿiya wadhik'ru man qablī bal aktharuhum lā yaʿlamūna l-ḥaqa fahum muʿ'riḍūna Have they taken beside Him other gods? Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Bring ye your proof: (that they are gods). This (Qur'an) is the Reminder unto those with me, and the Reminder unto those before (Indicates the unity of God and the universal aspect of Islam.) me; Nay! most of them know not the truth, so they turn aside." This is the declaration that the Unity of God advocated by the Holy Qur'an is the truth which is found in the scriptures given to every other apostle of God who visited the earth, preceding the…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:25 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا نُوحِي إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاعْبُدُونِ wamā arsalnā min qablika min rasūlin illā nūḥī ilayhi annahu lā ilāha illā anā fa-uʿ'budūni We did not send any apostle before you but We revealed to him that 'There is no god except Me; so worship Me.'

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:25 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا نُوحِي إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاعْبُدُونِ wamā arsalnā min qablika min rasūlin illā nūḥī ilayhi annahu lā ilāha illā anā fa-uʿ'budūni And We sent not before you any messenger except We revealed to him that, "There is no deity except Me, so worship Me." See 21:24

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:25 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا نُوحِي إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاعْبُدُونِ wamā arsalnā min qablika min rasūlin illā nūḥī ilayhi annahu lā ilāha illā anā fa-uʿ'budūni And sent We not before thee (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) any apostle but revealed We unto him that "Verily there is no god but I; so worship ye Me (alone)" See 21:24

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:26 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالُوْۤا اتَّخَذَ الرَّحْمَنُ وَلَدًا سُبْحَانَهُ بَلْ عِبَادٌ مُكْرَمُونَ waqālū ittakhadha l-raḥmānu waladan sub'ḥānahu bal ʿibādun muk'ramūna They say, 'The All-beneficent has taken offsprings.' Immaculate is He! Rather they are [His] honoured servants.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:26 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالُوْۤا اتَّخَذَ الرَّحْمَنُ وَلَدًا سُبْحَانَهُ بَلْ عِبَادٌ مُكْرَمُونَ waqālū ittakhadha l-raḥmānu waladan sub'ḥānahu bal ʿibādun muk'ramūna And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Exalted is He! Rather, they1 are (but) honored servants. And they say: "The Most Gracious has begotten children." Glory to Him! They are but honored servants (21:26). They speak not until He has spoken, and they act on His command (21:27). He knows what is before them, and what is behind them, and they cannot intercede except for him with whom He is pleased. And they stand in awe for fear of Him (21:28). And if any of them should say: "Verily, I am a god besides Him," such We should recompense with Hell. Thus We recompense the wrongdoers (21:29). The Refutation of Those Who Claim that the Angels are the Daughters of Allah;…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:26 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالُوْۤا اتَّخَذَ الرَّحْمَنُ وَلَدًا سُبْحَانَهُ بَلْ عِبَادٌ مُكْرَمُونَ waqālū ittakhadha l-raḥmānu waladan sub'ḥānahu bal ʿibādun muk'ramūna And say they: "The Beneficent (God) hath taken unto Him a (Taken to - or adopted - has begun - beget – issuing.) son; Glory be to Him! Nay! They (The prophets and the angels whom they worshipped as gods or the sons or the daughters of God.) are (His) honoured servants." This verse refutes the false belief not only of the Christian trinity but also of the angels being worshipped as the daughters of God. The trinitarian belief is an innovation of the people of the church founded in the name of Christ. There is nothing there in the Bible to support any such phenomenon which is only the product of the over enthusiasm of the converts to the creed of the church…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:27 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا يَسْبِقُونَهُ بِالْقَوْلِ وَهُمْ بِأَمْرِهِ يَعْمَلُونَ lā yasbiqūnahu bil-qawli wahum bi-amrihi yaʿmalūna They do not venture to speak ahead of Him, and they act by His command.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:27 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا يَسْبِقُونَهُ بِالْقَوْلِ وَهُمْ بِأَمْرِهِ يَعْمَلُونَ lā yasbiqūnahu bil-qawli wahum bi-amrihi yaʿmalūna They cannot precede Him in word, and they act by His command. See 21:26

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:27 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا يَسْبِقُونَهُ بِالْقَوْلِ وَهُمْ بِأَمْرِهِ يَعْمَلُونَ lā yasbiqūnahu bil-qawli wahum bi-amrihi yaʿmalūna They speak not ere He speaketh, and they on His bidding (only) act. This verse clearly states that the apostles of God neither spoke nor acted at any time, of their own accord. It was only the Divine Will which they translated into their words and deeds. Hence they never sinned. Since always acting under the Divine Will they were naturally infallible. Jesus is reported to have said: "For I have not spoken of myself but the Father which sent me; he gave me a commandment, what I should say, and what I should speak. "And I know that his commandment is life everlasting; whatsoever I speak therefore, even as the Father said unto me, so I speak." John 12/49-50. This is one of the unique characteristics of…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:28 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَلَا يَشْفَعُونَ إِلَّا لِمَنِ ارْتَضَى وَهُمْ مِنْ خَشْيَتِهِ مُشْفِقُونَ yaʿlamu mā bayna aydīhim wamā khalfahum walā yashfaʿūna illā limani ir'taḍā wahum min khashyatihi mush'fiqūna He knows that which is before them and that which is behind them, and they do not intercede except for someone He approves of, and they are apprehensive for the fear of Him.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:28 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَلَا يَشْفَعُونَ إِلَّا لِمَنِ ارْتَضَى وَهُمْ مِنْ خَشْيَتِهِ مُشْفِقُونَ yaʿlamu mā bayna aydīhim wamā khalfahum walā yashfaʿūna illā limani ir'taḍā wahum min khashyatihi mush'fiqūna He knows what is (presently) before them and what will be after them,1 and they cannot intercede except on behalf of one whom He approves. And they, from fear of Him, are apprehensive. See 21:26

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:28 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَلَا يَشْفَعُونَ إِلَّا لِمَنِ ارْتَضَى وَهُمْ مِنْ خَشْيَتِهِ مُشْفِقُونَ yaʿlamu mā bayna aydīhim wamā khalfahum walā yashfaʿūna illā limani ir'taḍā wahum min khashyatihi mush'fiqūna Knoweth He what is before them and what is behind them, and they can not intercede but for him whom He approveth, and they, of His fear, tremble. The fear mentioned here is not dread but the regard for the Majesty of the Glory of the Lord. And as for the question of the right of redemption or intercession allowed to the chosen ones of God.1

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:29 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَنْ يَقُلْ مِنْهُمْ اِنِّیْ إِلَهٌ مِنْ دُونِهِ فَذٰلِكَ نَجْزِيهِ جَهَنَّمَ كَذٰلِكَ نَجْزِي الظَّالِمِينَ waman yaqul min'hum innī ilāhun min dūnihi fadhālika najzīhi jahannama kadhālika najzī l-ẓālimīna Should any of them say, 'I am a god besides Him,' We will requite him with hell. Thus do We requite the wrongdoers.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:29 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَنْ يَقُلْ مِنْهُمْ اِنِّیْ إِلَهٌ مِنْ دُونِهِ فَذٰلِكَ نَجْزِيهِ جَهَنَّمَ كَذٰلِكَ نَجْزِي الظَّالِمِينَ waman yaqul min'hum innī ilāhun min dūnihi fadhālika najzīhi jahannama kadhālika najzī l-ẓālimīna And whoever of them should say, "Indeed, I am a god besides Him" - that one We would recompense with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers. See 21:26

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:29 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَنْ يَقُلْ مِنْهُمْ اِنِّیْ إِلَهٌ مِنْ دُونِهِ فَذٰلِكَ نَجْزِيهِ جَهَنَّمَ كَذٰلِكَ نَجْزِي الظَّالِمِينَ waman yaqul min'hum innī ilāhun min dūnihi fadhālika najzīhi jahannama kadhālika najzī l-ẓālimīna And whosoever of them sayeth; Verily I am god besides Him, such a one will We recompense with hell; Thus do We recompense the iniquitous. This refers to the priests and the kings who claimed godhead for themselves besides God - i.e., claimed Divinity. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:30 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوَلَمْ يَرَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا أَنَّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًا فَفَتَقْنَاهُمَا وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ أَفَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ awalam yara alladhīna kafarū anna l-samāwāti wal-arḍa kānatā ratqan fafataqnāhumā wajaʿalnā mina l-māi kulla shayin ḥayyin afalā yu'minūna Have the faithless not regarded that the heavens and the earth were interwoven and We unravelled them, and We made every living thing out of water? Will they not then have faith?

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:30 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوَلَمْ يَرَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا أَنَّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًا فَفَتَقْنَاهُمَا وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ أَفَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ awalam yara alladhīna kafarū anna l-samāwāti wal-arḍa kānatā ratqan fafataqnāhumā wajaʿalnā mina l-māi kulla shayin ḥayyin afalā yu'minūna Have those who disbelieved not considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, and then We separated them and made from water every living thing? Then will they not believe? Have not those who disbelieve known that the heavens and the earth were joined together as one united piece, then We parted them? And We have made from water every living thing. Will they not then believe (21:30). And We have placed on the earth firm mountains, lest it should shake with them, and We placed therein broad highways for them to pass through, that they may be guided (21:31). And…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:30 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوَلَمْ يَرَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا أَنَّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًا فَفَتَقْنَاهُمَا وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ أَفَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ awalam yara alladhīna kafarū anna l-samāwāti wal-arḍa kānatā ratqan fafataqnāhumā wajaʿalnā mina l-māi kulla shayin ḥayyin afalā yu'minūna Or see not those who disbelieve that the heavens and the earth were one piece, (One solid mass.) and that We clave them asunder; and made We of water everything alive; Will they not then believe? A man asked the Fifth Holy Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir the explanation of 'Closed up' in this verse. The holy Imam asked the man, "Do thou thinkest that the heavens and the earth were combined or joined together and they were separated." The man answered, 'Yes, my Lord!' The holy Imam said: "Seek thou the pardon of God, for it means that the heavens were neither showering…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:31 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا فِي الْأَرْضِ رَوَاسِيَ أَنْ تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا فِجَاجًا سُبُلًا لَعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ wajaʿalnā fī l-arḍi rawāsiya an tamīda bihim wajaʿalnā fīhā fijājan subulan laʿallahum yahtadūna We set firm mountains in the earth lest it should shake with them, and We made broad ways in them so that they may be guided [to their destinations].

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:31 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا فِي الْأَرْضِ رَوَاسِيَ أَنْ تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا فِجَاجًا سُبُلًا لَعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ wajaʿalnā fī l-arḍi rawāsiya an tamīda bihim wajaʿalnā fīhā fijājan subulan laʿallahum yahtadūna And We placed within the earth firmly set mountains, lest it should shift with them, and We made therein (mountain) passes (as) roads that they might be guided. See 21:30

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:31 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا فِي الْأَرْضِ رَوَاسِيَ أَنْ تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا فِجَاجًا سُبُلًا لَعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ wajaʿalnā fī l-arḍi rawāsiya an tamīda bihim wajaʿalnā fīhā fijājan subulan laʿallahum yahtadūna And We have made in the earth, (lofty) mountains (standing firm) lest it should shake with them, and We have made therein broad highways that they may be guided aright. The position of mountains on earth is a factor of guidance. Those who have travelled through the barren plains of Sahara without any mountains in them, know the task of finding out the correct direction for the routes to the different places. If taking the figurative use of the word mountain, as some commentators have taken, it will mean that God by His infinite mercy has sent His apostles and His chosen guides for the guidance of man towards the correct route he has…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:32 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا السَّمَاءَ سَقْفًا مَحْفُوظًا وَهُمْ عَنْ ءَايَاتِهَا مُعْرِضُونَ wajaʿalnā l-samāa saqfan maḥfūẓan wahum ʿan āyātihā muʿ'riḍūna We made the sky a preserved roof and yet they are disregardful of its signs.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:32 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا السَّمَاءَ سَقْفًا مَحْفُوظًا وَهُمْ عَنْ ءَايَاتِهَا مُعْرِضُونَ wajaʿalnā l-samāa saqfan maḥfūẓan wahum ʿan āyātihā muʿ'riḍūna And We made the sky a protected ceiling, but they, from its signs,1 are turning away. See 21:30

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:32 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا السَّمَاءَ سَقْفًا مَحْفُوظًا وَهُمْ عَنْ ءَايَاتِهَا مُعْرِضُونَ wajaʿalnā l-samāa saqfan maḥfūẓan wahum ʿan āyātihā muʿ'riḍūna And We have made the heavens a canopy, (Roof or vault.) well guarded; and yet they, from its signs turn aside. None can ever even imagine passing through the heavens. Though man is trying to travel through space, even if he succeeds, the journey will be only with its own limitation. None can ever know the exact extent of the space and the existence of the millions and millions of the solar systems, one after the other being continuously discovered more and ever more by every stronger telescope that man could make. It clearly indicates the impossibility of any travel by any one all through the whole of space. Besides the professors of witchcraft falsely claim of their journeys into the heavens. This verse…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:33 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ كُلٌّ فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ wahuwa alladhī khalaqa al-layla wal-nahāra wal-shamsa wal-qamara kullun fī falakin yasbaḥūna It is He who created the night and the day, the sun and the moon, each swimming in an orbit.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:33 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ كُلٌّ فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ wahuwa alladhī khalaqa al-layla wal-nahāra wal-shamsa wal-qamara kullun fī falakin yasbaḥūna And it is He who created the night and the day and the sun and the moon; all (heavenly bodies) in an orbit are swimming. See 21:30

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:33 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ كُلٌّ فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ wahuwa alladhī khalaqa al-layla wal-nahāra wal-shamsa wal-qamara kullun fī falakin yasbaḥūna And He it is Who created the night and the day and the sun and the moon; all in their (respective) orbits move (in a swim). Until yesterday, the world of science believed the sun to be stationary and all the other planets revolving around it. As early as about fourteen hundred years, the Holy Qur'an informed man that the Sun also is on its march towards a fixed destination.1

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:34 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا جَعَلْنَا لِبَشَرٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ الْخُلْدَ أَفَإِينْ مِتَّ فَهُمُ الْخَالِدُونَ wamā jaʿalnā libasharin min qablika l-khul'da afa-in mitta fahumu l-khālidūna We did not give immortality to any human before you. If you are fated to die, will they live on forever?

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:34 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا جَعَلْنَا لِبَشَرٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ الْخُلْدَ أَفَإِينْ مِتَّ فَهُمُ الْخَالِدُونَ wamā jaʿalnā libasharin min qablika l-khul'da afa-in mitta fahumu l-khālidūna And We did not grant to any man before you eternity (on earth); so if you die - would they be eternal? And We granted not to any human being immortality before you; then if you die, would they live forever (21:34). Everyone is going to taste death, and We shall test you with evil and with good by way of trial. And to Us you will be returned (21:35). No One has been Granted Immortality in this World وَمَا جَعَلْنَا لِبَشَرٍ مِّن قَبْلِكَ And We granted not to any human being immortality before you; means, O Muhammad. الْخُلْدَ immortality means, in this world. On the contrary: كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍ - وَيَبْقَىٰ وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ Whatsoever is…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:34 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا جَعَلْنَا لِبَشَرٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ الْخُلْدَ أَفَإِينْ مِتَّ فَهُمُ الْخَالِدُونَ wamā jaʿalnā libasharin min qablika l-khul'da afa-in mitta fahumu l-khālidūna We granted not unto any man before thee life eternal, What! then if thou diest, will they live for ever? No man on earth has ever been granted to live for ever, altogether exempted from tasting death. Certain chosen ones of God are granted extraordinary long life, but even they have one day to taste death.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:35 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ وَنَبْلُوكُمْ بِالشَّرِّ وَالْخَيْرِ فِتْنَةً وَإِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ kullu nafsin dhāiqatu l-mawti wanablūkum bil-shari wal-khayri fit'natan wa-ilaynā tur'jaʿūna Every soul shall taste death, and We will test you with good and ill by way of test, and to Us you will be brought back.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:35 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ وَنَبْلُوكُمْ بِالشَّرِّ وَالْخَيْرِ فِتْنَةً وَإِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ kullu nafsin dhāiqatu l-mawti wanablūkum bil-shari wal-khayri fit'natan wa-ilaynā tur'jaʿūna Every soul will taste death. And We test you with evil and with good as trial; and to Us you will be returned. See 21:34

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:35 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ وَنَبْلُوكُمْ بِالشَّرِّ وَالْخَيْرِ فِتْنَةً وَإِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ kullu nafsin dhāiqatu l-mawti wanablūkum bil-shari wal-khayri fit'natan wa-ilaynā tur'jaʿūna Every soul shall taste of death; We try you with evil and (with) good (by way of) a test (Refer to note on verses 8:185, 29:57 & 67:2.) ; and unto Us shall ye (all) be returned. In the preceding verse, reference is made to 'Bashar,' i.e., man, but here 'Nafs,' i.e., soul, is used for self. It obviously means that death or extinction of life is destined even for the non-human souls like the spirits like the angels. It is said that before the day of Final Judgment the whole universe along with the angels and the spirits will be ordered by God to go out of existence and then again everything will be brought to exist for the…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:36 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا رَءَاكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا إِنْ يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُوًا أَهَذَا الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ آلِهَتَكُمْ وَهُمْ بِذِكْرِ الرَّحْمَنِ هُمْ كَافِرُونَ wa-idhā raāka alladhīna kafarū in yattakhidhūnaka illā huzuwan ahādhā alladhī yadhkuru ālihatakum wahum bidhik'ri l-raḥmāni hum kāfirūna Whenever the faithless see you they only take you in derision: 'Is this the one who speaks ill of your gods?' And they defy the remembrance of the All-beneficent.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:36 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا رَءَاكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا إِنْ يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُوًا أَهَذَا الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ آلِهَتَكُمْ وَهُمْ بِذِكْرِ الرَّحْمَنِ هُمْ كَافِرُونَ wa-idhā raāka alladhīna kafarū in yattakhidhūnaka illā huzuwan ahādhā alladhī yadhkuru ālihatakum wahum bidhik'ri l-raḥmāni hum kāfirūna And when those who disbelieve see you, (O Muḥammad), they take you not except in ridicule, (saying), "Is this the one who mentions (i.e., insults) your gods?" And they are, at the mention of the Most Merciful, disbelievers. And when those who disbelieved see you, they take you not except for mockery (saying): "Is this the one who talks about your gods?" While they disbelieve at the mention of the Most Gracious (21:36). Man is created of haste. I will show you My Ayat. So ask Me not to hasten (them) (21:37). How the Idolators Mocked the Prophet SAW Allah tells His Prophet SAW: وَإِذَا رَآكَ…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:36 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا رَءَاكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا إِنْ يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُوًا أَهَذَا الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ آلِهَتَكُمْ وَهُمْ بِذِكْرِ الرَّحْمَنِ هُمْ كَافِرُونَ wa-idhā raāka alladhīna kafarū in yattakhidhūnaka illā huzuwan ahādhā alladhī yadhkuru ālihatakum wahum bidhik'ri l-raḥmāni hum kāfirūna When behold thee those who disbelieve, they take thee not but for a ridicule; (saying) "Is this he who speaketh of your gods?" and (while) they, at the mention of the Beneficent (God), are themselves disbelievers. The sceptic minds of the disbelievers used to take the warning against their infidelity and evils, as a joke and ridiculed the Holy Prophet. They did not even like the name of God to be taken even by the others.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:37 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: خُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ سَأُورِيكُمْ ءَايَاتِي فَلَا تَسْتَعْجِلُونِ khuliqa l-insānu min ʿajalin sa-urīkum āyātī falā tastaʿjilūni Man is a creature of haste. Soon I will show you My signs. So do not ask Me to hasten.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:37 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: خُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ سَأُورِيكُمْ ءَايَاتِي فَلَا تَسْتَعْجِلُونِ khuliqa l-insānu min ʿajalin sa-urīkum āyātī falā tastaʿjilūni Man was created of haste (i.e., impatience). I will show you My signs (i.e., vengeance), so do not impatiently urge Me. See 21:36

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:37 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: خُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ سَأُورِيكُمْ ءَايَاتِي فَلَا تَسْتَعْجِلُونِ khuliqa l-insānu min ʿajalin sa-urīkum āyātī falā tastaʿjilūni Man is made of haste; I shall show you My signs, so ask Me not to hasten (on) A man named Harith bin Nasr, by way of taunting, used to frequently ask the Holy Prophet as to when the threatened wrath of God would come. This verse is in reply to it.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:38 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَقُولُونَ مَتٰی هَذَا الْوَعْدُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ wayaqūlūna matā hādhā l-waʿdu in kuntum ṣādiqīna And they say, 'When will this promise be fulfilled, should you be truthful?'

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:38 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَقُولُونَ مَتٰی هَذَا الْوَعْدُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ wayaqūlūna matā hādhā l-waʿdu in kuntum ṣādiqīna And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?" And they say: When will this promise (come to pass), if you are truthful (21:38). If only those who disbelieved knew (the time) when they will not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces, nor from their backs, and they will not be helped (21:39). Nay, it will come upon them all of a sudden and will perplex them, and they will have no power to avert it nor will they get respite (21:40). The Idolators Seek to Hasten on the Punishment Allah also tells us how the idolators seek to hasten punishment upon themselves, out of denial, rejection, disbelief, stubbornness and a belief that it will never happen. He says:…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:38 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَقُولُونَ مَتٰی هَذَا الْوَعْدُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ wayaqūlūna matā hādhā l-waʿdu in kuntum ṣādiqīna And say they: "When will this threat come to pass, if ye be truthful?" See 21:37

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:39 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَوْ يَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا حِينَ لَا يَكُفُّونَ عَنْ وُجُوهِهِمُ النَّارَ وَلَا عَنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ law yaʿlamu alladhīna kafarū ḥīna lā yakuffūna ʿan wujūhihimu l-nāra walā ʿan ẓuhūrihim walā hum yunṣarūna If only the faithless knew of the time when they will not be able to keep the Fire off their faces and their backs, nor will they be helped!1

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:39 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَوْ يَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا حِينَ لَا يَكُفُّونَ عَنْ وُجُوهِهِمُ النَّارَ وَلَا عَنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ law yaʿlamu alladhīna kafarū ḥīna lā yakuffūna ʿan wujūhihimu l-nāra walā ʿan ẓuhūrihim walā hum yunṣarūna If those who disbelieved but knew the time when they will not avert the Fire from their faces or from their backs and they will not be aided...1 See 21:38

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:39 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَوْ يَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا حِينَ لَا يَكُفُّونَ عَنْ وُجُوهِهِمُ النَّارَ وَلَا عَنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ law yaʿlamu alladhīna kafarū ḥīna lā yakuffūna ʿan wujūhihimu l-nāra walā ʿan ẓuhūrihim walā hum yunṣarūna If only know those who disbelieve, (of the time) when they shall not be able to keep off from their faces and the backs the (Hell) fire nor shall they be helped. See 21:37

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:40 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ تَأْتِيهِمْ بَغْتَةً فَتَبْهَتُهُمْ فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ رَدَّهَا وَلَا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ bal tatīhim baghtatan fatabhatuhum falā yastaṭīʿūna raddahā walā hum yunẓarūna Rather it will overtake them suddenly, dumbfounding them. So neither will they be able to avert it, nor will they be granted any respite.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:40 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ تَأْتِيهِمْ بَغْتَةً فَتَبْهَتُهُمْ فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ رَدَّهَا وَلَا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ bal tatīhim baghtatan fatabhatuhum falā yastaṭīʿūna raddahā walā hum yunẓarūna Rather, it will come to them unexpectedly and bewilder them, and they will not be able to repel it, nor will they be reprieved. See 21:38

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:40 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ تَأْتِيهِمْ بَغْتَةً فَتَبْهَتُهُمْ فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ رَدَّهَا وَلَا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ bal tatīhim baghtatan fatabhatuhum falā yastaṭīʿūna raddahā walā hum yunẓarūna Nay! but it shall come on them suddenly, and make them confounded, so they shall neither be able to repel it, nor will they (then) be respited. See 21:37

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:41 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدِ اسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ فَحَاقَ بِالَّذِينَ سَخِرُوْۤا مِنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوْۤا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ walaqadi us'tuh'zi-a birusulin min qablika faḥāqa bi-alladhīna sakhirū min'hum mā kānū bihi yastahziūna Apostles were certainly derided before you; but those who ridiculed them were besieged by what they had been deriding.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:41 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدِ اسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ فَحَاقَ بِالَّذِينَ سَخِرُوْۤا مِنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوْۤا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ walaqadi us'tuh'zi-a birusulin min qablika faḥāqa bi-alladhīna sakhirū min'hum mā kānū bihi yastahziūna And already were messengers ridiculed before you, but those who mocked them were enveloped by what they used to ridicule. Indeed (many) Messengers were mocked before you, but the scoffers were surrounded by what they used to mock (21:41). Say: "Who can guard and protect you in the night or in the day from the Most Gracious?" Nay, but they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord (21:42). Or have they gods who can guard them from Us? They have no power to help themselves, nor can they be protected from Us (21:43). The Lessons to be Learned from Those Who Mocked the Messengers in the Past Allah says consoling His Messenger SAW…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:41 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدِ اسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ فَحَاقَ بِالَّذِينَ سَخِرُوْۤا مِنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوْۤا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ walaqadi us'tuh'zi-a birusulin min qablika faḥāqa bi-alladhīna sakhirū min'hum mā kānū bihi yastahziūna And indeed were (also) ridiculed (some) of the apostles before thee, but surrounded those who ridiculed that (very torment) which they had been ridiculing. All those of the disbelievers who were punished in the previous generations did similarly ridicule but they were made to realise what their ridicule actually meant.1

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:42 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ مَنْ يَكْلَؤُكُمْ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ بَلْ هُمْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِمْ مُعْرِضُونَ qul man yakla-ukum bi-al-layli wal-nahāri mina l-raḥmāni bal hum ʿan dhik'ri rabbihim muʿ'riḍūna Say, 'Who can guard you, day and night, from [the punishment of] the All-beneficent?' Rather they are disregardful of their Lord's remembrance.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:42 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ مَنْ يَكْلَؤُكُمْ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ بَلْ هُمْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِمْ مُعْرِضُونَ qul man yakla-ukum bi-al-layli wal-nahāri mina l-raḥmāni bal hum ʿan dhik'ri rabbihim muʿ'riḍūna Say, "Who can protect you at night or by day from the Most Merciful?" But they are, from the remembrance of their Lord, turning away. See 21:41

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:42 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ مَنْ يَكْلَؤُكُمْ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ بَلْ هُمْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِمْ مُعْرِضُونَ qul man yakla-ukum bi-al-layli wal-nahāri mina l-raḥmāni bal hum ʿan dhik'ri rabbihim muʿ'riḍūna Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!): Who can protect you by night and by day from the Beneficent (God)? Nay! they from the remembrance of their Lord turn aside. There is none who could save the disbelievers against the wrath of God. None of the gods whom they worshipped, would be of any avail to them. It is the mercy of the Lord that is delaying their punishment to give them the respite.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:43 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَمْ لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ تَمْنَعُهُمْ مِنْ دُونِنَا لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَ أَنْفُسِهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ مِنَّا يُصْحَبُونَ am lahum ālihatun tamnaʿuhum min dūninā lā yastaṭīʿūna naṣra anfusihim walā hum minnā yuṣ'ḥabūna Do they have gods besides Us to defend them? Neither can they help themselves, nor can they provide them with an escort against Us.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:43 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَمْ لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ تَمْنَعُهُمْ مِنْ دُونِنَا لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَ أَنْفُسِهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ مِنَّا يُصْحَبُونَ am lahum ālihatun tamnaʿuhum min dūninā lā yastaṭīʿūna naṣra anfusihim walā hum minnā yuṣ'ḥabūna Or do they have gods to defend them other than Us? They are unable (even) to help themselves, nor can they be protected from Us. See 21:41

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:43 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَمْ لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ تَمْنَعُهُمْ مِنْ دُونِنَا لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَ أَنْفُسِهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ مِنَّا يُصْحَبُونَ am lahum ālihatun tamnaʿuhum min dūninā lā yastaṭīʿūna naṣra anfusihim walā hum minnā yuṣ'ḥabūna Or have they gods who can protect them from Us; They have no power to help their own selves, and nor shall they from Us (From our punishment.) be protected. See 21:42

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:44 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ مَتَّعْنَا هَؤُلَاءِ وَءَابَاءَهُمْ حَتّٰی طَالَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْعُمُرُ أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَنَّا نَأْتِي الْأَرْضَ نَنْقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا أَفَهُمُ الْغَالِبُونَ bal mattaʿnā hāulāi waābāahum ḥattā ṭāla ʿalayhimu l-ʿumuru afalā yarawna annā natī l-arḍa nanquṣuhā min aṭrāfihā afahumu l-ghālibūna Rather We have provided for them and their fathers until they lived on for long years. Do they not see how We visit the land diminishing it at its edges?1 Are they the ones who will prevail?

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:44 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ مَتَّعْنَا هَؤُلَاءِ وَءَابَاءَهُمْ حَتّٰی طَالَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْعُمُرُ أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَنَّا نَأْتِي الْأَرْضَ نَنْقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا أَفَهُمُ الْغَالِبُونَ bal mattaʿnā hāulāi waābāahum ḥattā ṭāla ʿalayhimu l-ʿumuru afalā yarawna annā natī l-arḍa nanquṣuhā min aṭrāfihā afahumu l-ghālibūna But, (on the contrary), We have provided good things for these (disbelievers) and their fathers until life was prolonged for them. Then do they not see that We set upon the land, reducing it from its borders?1 Is it they who will overcome? Nay, We gave the luxuries of this life to these men and their fathers until the period grew long for them. See they not that We gradually reduce the land from its outlying borders Is it then they who will overcome (21:44). Say: I warn you only by the revelation. "But the deaf will not hear the call, (even) when they…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:44 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ مَتَّعْنَا هَؤُلَاءِ وَءَابَاءَهُمْ حَتّٰی طَالَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْعُمُرُ أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَنَّا نَأْتِي الْأَرْضَ نَنْقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا أَفَهُمُ الْغَالِبُونَ bal mattaʿnā hāulāi waābāahum ḥattā ṭāla ʿalayhimu l-ʿumuru afalā yarawna annā natī l-arḍa nanquṣuhā min aṭrāfihā afahumu l-ghālibūna Nay! Provided We (enjoyment) unto these and their fathers until lasted their life; What! See they not that We come unto the land, shortening (Refer to verse 13:41.) its borders; Shall they then be the prevailing ones? In spite of the terrible resistance from the heathen world around Mecca, Islam flourished and gradually the lands in the hands of those openly opposed to Islam, were snatched away from the hands of the disbelievers and the land around was subjected to the Muslim rule. The disbelievers could not prevail over Islam which began its course amidst heartless persecution, brutal tyrannies, and unprovoked monstrous aggressions and…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:45 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ إِنَّمَا أُنْذِرُكُمْ بِالْوَحْيِ وَلَا يَسْمَعُ الصُّمُّ الدُّعَاءَ إِذَا مَا يُنْذَرُونَ qul innamā undhirukum bil-waḥyi walā yasmaʿu l-ṣumu l-duʿāa idhā mā yundharūna Say, 'I indeed warn you by the means of revelation.' But the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:45 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ إِنَّمَا أُنْذِرُكُمْ بِالْوَحْيِ وَلَا يَسْمَعُ الصُّمُّ الدُّعَاءَ إِذَا مَا يُنْذَرُونَ qul innamā undhirukum bil-waḥyi walā yasmaʿu l-ṣumu l-duʿāa idhā mā yundharūna Say, "I only warn you by revelation." But the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned. See 21:44

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:45 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ إِنَّمَا أُنْذِرُكُمْ بِالْوَحْيِ وَلَا يَسْمَعُ الصُّمُّ الدُّعَاءَ إِذَا مَا يُنْذَرُونَ qul innamā undhirukum bil-waḥyi walā yasmaʿu l-ṣumu l-duʿāa idhā mā yundharūna Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!): "Verily I do but warn you by the revelation (from God):" But the deaf will hear not whenever they are warned. See 21:44

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:46 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَئِنْ مَسَّتْهُمْ نَفْحَةٌ مِنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّكَ لَيَقُولُنَّ يَاوَيْلَنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ wala-in massathum nafḥatun min ʿadhābi rabbika layaqūlunna yāwaylanā innā kunnā ẓālimīna Should a whiff of your Lord's punishment touch them, they will surely say, 'Woe to us! We have indeed been wrongdoers!'

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:46 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَئِنْ مَسَّتْهُمْ نَفْحَةٌ مِنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّكَ لَيَقُولُنَّ يَاوَيْلَنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ wala-in massathum nafḥatun min ʿadhābi rabbika layaqūlunna yāwaylanā innā kunnā ẓālimīna And if (as much as) a whiff of the punishment of your Lord should touch them, they would surely say, "O woe to us! Indeed, we have been wrongdoers." See 21:44

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:46 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَئِنْ مَسَّتْهُمْ نَفْحَةٌ مِنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّكَ لَيَقُولُنَّ يَاوَيْلَنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ wala-in massathum nafḥatun min ʿadhābi rabbika layaqūlunna yāwaylanā innā kunnā ẓālimīna And yet if toucheth them a blast (Lit. Breath.) of thy Lord's punishment, certainly will they say, "Woe unto us! Verily we had been unjust!" See 21:44

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:47 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَنَضَعُ الْمَوَازِينَ الْقِسْطَ لِيَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ فَلَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْئًا وَإِنْ كَانَ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ أَتَيْنَا بِهَا وَكَفَى بِنَا حَاسِبِينَ wanaḍaʿu l-mawāzīna l-qis'ṭa liyawmi l-qiyāmati falā tuẓ'lamu nafsun shayan wa-in kāna mith'qāla ḥabbatin min khardalin ataynā bihā wakafā binā ḥāsibīna We shall set up the scales of justice on the Day of Resurrection, and no soul will be wronged in the least. Even if it be the weight of a mustard seed We shall produce it and We suffice as reckoners.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:47 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَنَضَعُ الْمَوَازِينَ الْقِسْطَ لِيَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ فَلَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْئًا وَإِنْ كَانَ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ أَتَيْنَا بِهَا وَكَفَى بِنَا حَاسِبِينَ wanaḍaʿu l-mawāzīna l-qis'ṭa liyawmi l-qiyāmati falā tuẓ'lamu nafsun shayan wa-in kāna mith'qāla ḥabbatin min khardalin ataynā bihā wakafā binā ḥāsibīna And We place the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be treated unjustly at all. And if there is (even) the weight of a mustard seed,1 We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as accountant. See 21:44

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:47 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَنَضَعُ الْمَوَازِينَ الْقِسْطَ لِيَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ فَلَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْئًا وَإِنْ كَانَ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ أَتَيْنَا بِهَا وَكَفَى بِنَا حَاسِبِينَ wanaḍaʿu l-mawāzīna l-qis'ṭa liyawmi l-qiyāmati falā tuẓ'lamu nafsun shayan wa-in kāna mith'qāla ḥabbatin min khardalin ataynā bihā wakafā binā ḥāsibīna And We shall set up the balances of justice on the Day of Judgment, so no soul shall be dealt with unjustly in the least; (Refer to verses 7:8, 57:25 & 55:7.) and even if there be the weight of a grain of mustard seed, (even that) will We bring it (into account); And sufficient are We (as) reckoners. The First Holy Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib answering a question said that: "The thoughts and the deeds have no body to be weighed in any physical balance which could weigh only things material. Nothing is hidden or unknown to God.…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:48 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ اٰتَیْنَا مُوسٰی وَهَارُونَ الْفُرْقَانَ وَضِيَاءً وَذِكْرًا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ walaqad ātaynā mūsā wahārūna l-fur'qāna waḍiyāan wadhik'ran lil'muttaqīna Certainly We gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion, a light and reminder for the Godwary.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:48 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ اٰتَیْنَا مُوسٰی وَهَارُونَ الْفُرْقَانَ وَضِيَاءً وَذِكْرًا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ walaqad ātaynā mūsā wahārūna l-fur'qāna waḍiyāan wadhik'ran lil'muttaqīna And We had already given Musa and Harun the criterion and a light and a reminder1 for the righteous. And indeed We granted to Musa and Harun the criterion, and a shining light and a Reminder for those who have Taqwa (21:48). Those who fear their Lord in the unseen, and they are afraid of the Hour (21:49). And this is a blessed Reminder which We have sent down; will you then deny it (21:50). The Revelation of the Tawrah and the Qur'an We have already noted that Allah often mentions Musa and Muhammad together – may the peace and blessings of Allah be upon them both – and He often mentions their Books together as well. He says: وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ وَهَارُونَ الْفُرْقَانَ…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:48 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ اٰتَیْنَا مُوسٰی وَهَارُونَ الْفُرْقَانَ وَضِيَاءً وَذِكْرًا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ walaqad ātaynā mūsā wahārūna l-fur'qāna waḍiyāan wadhik'ran lil'muttaqīna And indeed We did grant unto Moses and Aaron the (Book of) Criterion (Distinguishing measure - The same was given to the Holy Prophet and Ali ibn Abi Talib, the First Holy Imam.) (between the right and wrong), and Light and a Reminder (Refer to verses 2:2, 2:177, 3:137 & 45:20.) for the pious ones. 'Furqan', i.e., the Criterion of judgment or the Means to distinguish falsehood from the truth or to sift or separate truth from falsehood, i.e., the heavenly scripture and the knowledge contained in the scriptures. The god-fearing are those who are always mindful of God and guard against evil with the correct belief in Him and the hereafter, the reckoning and the Final Requital. Whatever was proved for Moses was…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:49 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَيْبِ وَهُمْ مِنَ السَّاعَةِ مُشْفِقُونَ alladhīna yakhshawna rabbahum bil-ghaybi wahum mina l-sāʿati mush'fiqūna Those who fear their Lord in secret, and who are apprehensive of the Hour.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:49 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَيْبِ وَهُمْ مِنَ السَّاعَةِ مُشْفِقُونَ alladhīna yakhshawna rabbahum bil-ghaybi wahum mina l-sāʿati mush'fiqūna Who fear their Lord unseen,1 while they are of the Hour apprehensive. See 21:48

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:49 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَيْبِ وَهُمْ مِنَ السَّاعَةِ مُشْفِقُونَ alladhīna yakhshawna rabbahum bil-ghaybi wahum mina l-sāʿati mush'fiqūna Those who fear their Lord unseen, and of the Hour (of doom) they are frightened. This is the continuation of the description of the qualities of the god-fearing ones, though they do not see God and yet they fear His wrath and His reckoning.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:50 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهَذَا ذِكْرٌ مُبَارَكٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ أَفَأَنْتُمْ لَهُ مُنْكِرُونَ wahādhā dhik'run mubārakun anzalnāhu afa-antum lahu munkirūna This is a blessed reminder which We have sent down. Will you then deny it?

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:50 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهَذَا ذِكْرٌ مُبَارَكٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ أَفَأَنْتُمْ لَهُ مُنْكِرُونَ wahādhā dhik'run mubārakun anzalnāhu afa-antum lahu munkirūna And this (Qur’ān) is a blessed message which We have sent down. Then are you with it unacquainted?1 See 21:48

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:50 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهَذَا ذِكْرٌ مُبَارَكٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ أَفَأَنْتُمْ لَهُ مُنْكِرُونَ wahādhā dhik'run mubārakun anzalnāhu afa-antum lahu munkirūna And this (Qur'an) is a Reminder (Qur'an.) full of blessings which We have sent it down (Unto Our Apostle Muhammad) Do ye then deny it? See 21:49

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:51 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ اٰتَیْنَا اِبْرَاهِیْمَ رُشْدَهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَكُنَّا بِهِ عَالِمِينَ walaqad ātaynā ib'rāhīma rush'dahu min qablu wakunnā bihi ʿālimīna Certainly We had given Abraham his rectitude before, and We knew him

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:51 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ اٰتَیْنَا اِبْرَاهِیْمَ رُشْدَهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَكُنَّا بِهِ عَالِمِينَ walaqad ātaynā ib'rāhīma rush'dahu min qablu wakunnā bihi ʿālimīna And We had certainly given Ibrahim his sound judgement before,1 and We were of him well-Knowing. And indeed We bestowed aforetime on Ibrahim his guidance, and We were Well-Acquainted with him (21:51). When he said to his father and his people: What are these images to which you are devoted? (21:52). They said: "We found our fathers worshipping them (21:53). He said: "Indeed you and your fathers have been in manifest error (21:54). They said: "Have you brought us the Truth, or are you one of those who play about?? (21:55). He said: "Nay, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, Who created them and to that I am one of the witnesses (21:56). The Story of Ibrahim…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:51 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ اٰتَیْنَا اِبْرَاهِیْمَ رُشْدَهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَكُنَّا بِهِ عَالِمِينَ walaqad ātaynā ib'rāhīma rush'dahu min qablu wakunnā bihi ʿālimīna And indeed gave We unto Abraham his rectitude (Refer to verse 6:75. The power of discerning between the right and the wrong.) before, and We did know him well. Abraham is the one who has been the most repeatedly mentioned in the Holy Qur'an and on each occasion with reference to a different aspect of his personal excellence.1 Abraham was given 'Rushd', i.e., guidance, i.e., apostleship before Moses and Aaron. These verses assert that Abraham got his discerning power before he started preaching to Aazar in verse 6:75 - Abraham's preaching to Aazar is before his argument with the people about the divinity of the stars.2 This clearly proves that Abraham never accepted the divinity of the stars. It was just for…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:52 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ مَا هَذِهِ التَّمَاثِيلُ الَّتِي أَنْتُمْ لَهَا عَاكِفُونَ idh qāla li-abīhi waqawmihi mā hādhihi l-tamāthīlu allatī antum lahā ʿākifūna when he said to his father and his people, 'What are these images to which you keep on clinging?'

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:52 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ مَا هَذِهِ التَّمَاثِيلُ الَّتِي أَنْتُمْ لَهَا عَاكِفُونَ idh qāla li-abīhi waqawmihi mā hādhihi l-tamāthīlu allatī antum lahā ʿākifūna When he said to his father and his people, "What are these statues to which you are devoted?" See 21:51

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:52 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ مَا هَذِهِ التَّمَاثِيلُ الَّتِي أَنْتُمْ لَهَا عَاكِفُونَ idh qāla li-abīhi waqawmihi mā hādhihi l-tamāthīlu allatī antum lahā ʿākifūna (Recollect thou O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) when (Abraham) said unto his father (Godfather - paternal uncle.) and his people: "What are these images unto which ye (as devotees) cleave" See verses 6:75 - 6:83. 'Aazar' was the paternal uncle of Abraham who had brought up Abraham. Hence Aazar is addressed as the father. Abraham asked Aazar and his people, about the idols which they worshipped.1

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:53 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا وَجَدْنَا ءَابَاءَنَا لَهَا عَابِدِينَ qālū wajadnā ābāanā lahā ʿābidīna They said, 'We found our fathers worshipping them.'

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:53 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا وَجَدْنَا ءَابَاءَنَا لَهَا عَابِدِينَ qālū wajadnā ābāanā lahā ʿābidīna They said, "We found our fathers worshippers of them." See 21:51

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:53 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا وَجَدْنَا ءَابَاءَنَا لَهَا عَابِدِينَ qālū wajadnā ābāanā lahā ʿābidīna Said they: "Found we our fathers, (Parents as well as ancestors.) worshippers unto them" They (the people) replied saying that they only followed their ancestors - to which Abraham though young and in the clutches of the idolaters opposed the very Sire, who was to him a father for he had brought him up and boldly condemned idolatry, declaring that the people and their fathers both had gone astray. This part of the life-history of Abraham informs some important guiding factors for mankind, i.e., how the duty to God should be the first concern of man when it is in conflict with the duty even to his parents, how boldly truth should be advocated and upheld against falsehood and be overcome and the fight against evil be carried to the…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:54 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ لَقَدْ كُنْتُمْ أَنْتُمْ وَءَابَاؤُكُمْ فِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ qāla laqad kuntum antum waābāukum fī ḍalālin mubīnin He said, 'Certainly you and your fathers have been in manifest error.'

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:54 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ لَقَدْ كُنْتُمْ أَنْتُمْ وَءَابَاؤُكُمْ فِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ qāla laqad kuntum antum waābāukum fī ḍalālin mubīnin He said, "You were certainly, you and your fathers, in manifest error." See 21:51

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:54 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ لَقَدْ كُنْتُمْ أَنْتُمْ وَءَابَاؤُكُمْ فِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ qāla laqad kuntum antum waābāukum fī ḍalālin mubīnin Said (Abraham.) he: "Indeed ye and your fathers had been in error (Clear.) manifest." See 21:53

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:55 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا أَجِئْتَنَا بِالْحَقِّ أَمْ أَنْتَ مِنَ اللَّاعِبِينَ qālū aji'tanā bil-ḥaqi am anta mina l-lāʿibīna They said, 'Are you telling the truth,1 or are you [just] kidding?'

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:55 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا أَجِئْتَنَا بِالْحَقِّ أَمْ أَنْتَ مِنَ اللَّاعِبِينَ qālū aji'tanā bil-ḥaqi am anta mina l-lāʿibīna They said, "Have you come to us with truth, or are you of those who jest?" See 21:51

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:55 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا أَجِئْتَنَا بِالْحَقِّ أَمْ أَنْتَ مِنَ اللَّاعِبِينَ qālū aji'tanā bil-ḥaqi am anta mina l-lāʿibīna Said they: "Hast thou brought unto us the truth, or art thou of the jesters?" See 21:53

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:56 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ بَلْ رَبُّكُمْ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ الَّذِي فَطَرَهُنَّ وَأَنَا عَلَى ذَلِكُمْ مِنَ الشَّاهِدِينَ qāla bal rabbukum rabbu l-samāwāti wal-arḍi alladhī faṭarahunna wa-anā ʿalā dhālikum mina l-shāhidīna He said, 'Rather your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who originated them, and I am a witness to this.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:56 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ بَلْ رَبُّكُمْ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ الَّذِي فَطَرَهُنَّ وَأَنَا عَلَى ذَلِكُمْ مِنَ الشَّاهِدِينَ qāla bal rabbukum rabbu l-samāwāti wal-arḍi alladhī faṭarahunna wa-anā ʿalā dhālikum mina l-shāhidīna He said, "(No), rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth who created them, and I, to that, am of those who testify. See 21:51

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:56 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ بَلْ رَبُّكُمْ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ الَّذِي فَطَرَهُنَّ وَأَنَا عَلَى ذَلِكُمْ مِنَ الشَّاهِدِينَ qāla bal rabbukum rabbu l-samāwāti wal-arḍi alladhī faṭarahunna wa-anā ʿalā dhālikum mina l-shāhidīna Said he: "Nay! Your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, Who hath created them; and I am unto this, (This Truth.) one of the witnesses." See 21:53

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:57 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَتَاللَّهِ لَأَكِيدَنَّ أَصْنَامَكُمْ بَعْدَ أَنْ تُوَلُّوْۤا مُدْبِرِينَ watal-lahi la-akīdanna aṣnāmakum baʿda an tuwallū mud'birīna By Allah, I will devise a stratagem against your idols after you have gone away.'

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:57 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَتَاللَّهِ لَأَكِيدَنَّ أَصْنَامَكُمْ بَعْدَ أَنْ تُوَلُّوْۤا مُدْبِرِينَ watal-lahi la-akīdanna aṣnāmakum baʿda an tuwallū mud'birīna And (I swear) by Allah, I will surely plan against your idols after you have turned and gone away." "And by Allah, I shall plot a plan for your idols after you have gone away and turned your backs (21:57). So he broke them to pieces, except the biggest of them, that they might turn to it (21:58). They said: "Who has done this to our gods He must indeed be one of the wrongdoers (21:59). They said: "We heard a young man talking against them, who is called Ibrahim (21:60). They said: "Then bring him before the eyes of the people, that they may testify (21:61). They said: "Are you the one who has done this to our gods, O Ibrahim? (21:62). He said: "Nay,…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:57 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَتَاللَّهِ لَأَكِيدَنَّ أَصْنَامَكُمْ بَعْدَ أَنْ تُوَلُّوْۤا مُدْبِرِينَ watal-lahi la-akīdanna aṣnāmakum baʿda an tuwallū mud'birīna And by God, I will scheme (This is what Abraham determines to do.) against your idols after ye go away, turning back Abraham determines to make the idolaters realize the fallacy of their creed by breaking the idols when they had gone from the place. The next day was the festival of the idolaters. They all went out to rejoice and Abraham with the excuse of sickness remained behind. The people had arranged all their idols adorned.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:58 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَجَعَلَهُمْ جُذَاذًا إِلَّا كَبِيرًا لَهُمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ يَرْجِعُونَ fajaʿalahum judhādhan illā kabīran lahum laʿallahum ilayhi yarjiʿūna So he broke them into pieces, —all except the biggest of them— so that they might come back to it.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:58 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَجَعَلَهُمْ جُذَاذًا إِلَّا كَبِيرًا لَهُمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ يَرْجِعُونَ fajaʿalahum judhādhan illā kabīran lahum laʿallahum ilayhi yarjiʿūna So he made them into fragments, except a large one among them, that they might return to it (and question). See 21:57

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:58 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَجَعَلَهُمْ جُذَاذًا إِلَّا كَبِيرًا لَهُمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ يَرْجِعُونَ fajaʿalahum judhādhan illā kabīran lahum laʿallahum ilayhi yarjiʿūna So he broke them (The idols.) into pieces, except the chief of them, that happly they may unto him return. It is said that Abraham's breaking of the idols is mentioned in the Jewish Rabbinical literature Gen. R. 38, and Tauna Debe Eliyahu 2:35 (Jewish Edition). Abraham broke all the idols save the biggest or chief one of them to convince the people of their gods being nothing but a senseless stock of stones, i.e., a helpless material.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:59 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا مَنْ فَعَلَ هَذَا بِآلِهَتِنَا إِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ qālū man faʿala hādhā biālihatinā innahu lamina l-ẓālimīna They said, 'Whoever has done this to Our gods?! He is indeed a wrongdoer!'

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:59 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا مَنْ فَعَلَ هَذَا بِآلِهَتِنَا إِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ qālū man faʿala hādhā biālihatinā innahu lamina l-ẓālimīna They said, "Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he is of the wrongdoers." See 21:57

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:59 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا مَنْ فَعَلَ هَذَا بِآلِهَتِنَا إِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ qālū man faʿala hādhā biālihatinā innahu lamina l-ẓālimīna Said they: "Who hath done this to our gods? Verily he is of the unjust ones" See 21:58

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:60 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا سَمِعْنَا فَتًى يَذْكُرُهُمْ يُقَالُ لَهُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ qālū samiʿ'nā fatan yadhkuruhum yuqālu lahu ib'rāhīmu They said, 'We heard a young man speaking ill of them. He is called "Abraham." '

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:60 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا سَمِعْنَا فَتًى يَذْكُرُهُمْ يُقَالُ لَهُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ qālū samiʿ'nā fatan yadhkuruhum yuqālu lahu ib'rāhīmu They said, "We heard a young man mention them who is called Ibrahim." See 21:57

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:60 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا سَمِعْنَا فَتًى يَذْكُرُهُمْ يُقَالُ لَهُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ qālū samiʿ'nā fatan yadhkuruhum yuqālu lahu ib'rāhīmu (Some others) said: "We heard a youth speak of them, he is called Abraham" See 21:58

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:61 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا فَأْتُوْۤا بِهِ عَلَى أَعْيُنِ النَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْهَدُونَ qālū fatū bihi ʿalā aʿyuni l-nāsi laʿallahum yashhadūna They said, 'Bring him before the people's eyes so that they may bear witness [against him].'

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:61 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا فَأْتُوْۤا بِهِ عَلَى أَعْيُنِ النَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْهَدُونَ qālū fatū bihi ʿalā aʿyuni l-nāsi laʿallahum yashhadūna They said, "Then bring him before the eyes of the people that they may testify."1 See 21:57

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:61 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا فَأْتُوْۤا بِهِ عَلَى أَعْيُنِ النَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْهَدُونَ qālū fatū bihi ʿalā aʿyuni l-nāsi laʿallahum yashhadūna They said: "Then bring him before the eyes of the people, that they may bear witness." See 21:58

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:62 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا ءَأَنْتَ فَعَلْتَ هَذَا بِآلِهَتِنَا يَاإِبْرَاهِيمُ qālū a-anta faʿalta hādhā biālihatinā yāib'rāhīmu They said, 'Was it you who did this to our gods, O Abraham?'

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:62 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا ءَأَنْتَ فَعَلْتَ هَذَا بِآلِهَتِنَا يَاإِبْرَاهِيمُ qālū a-anta faʿalta hādhā biālihatinā yāib'rāhīmu They said, "Have you done this to our gods, O Ibrahim?" See 21:57

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:62 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا ءَأَنْتَ فَعَلْتَ هَذَا بِآلِهَتِنَا يَاإِبْرَاهِيمُ qālū a-anta faʿalta hādhā biālihatinā yāib'rāhīmu Said (Asked.) they: "Hast thou done this to our gods, O' Abraham?" See 21:58

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:63 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ بَلْ فَعَلَهُ كَبِيرُهُمْ هَذَا فَسْءَلُوهُمْ إِنْ كَانُوْۤا يَنْطِقُونَ qāla bal faʿalahu kabīruhum hādhā fasalūhum in kānū yanṭiqūna He said, 'Rather it was this biggest of them who did it! Ask them, if they can speak.'

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:63 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ بَلْ فَعَلَهُ كَبِيرُهُمْ هَذَا فَسْءَلُوهُمْ إِنْ كَانُوْۤا يَنْطِقُونَ qāla bal faʿalahu kabīruhum hādhā fasalūhum in kānū yanṭiqūna He said, "Rather, this - the largest of them - did it, so ask them, if they should (be able to) speak." See 21:57

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:63 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ بَلْ فَعَلَهُ كَبِيرُهُمْ هَذَا فَسْءَلُوهُمْ إِنْ كَانُوْۤا يَنْطِقُونَ qāla bal faʿalahu kabīruhum hādhā fasalūhum in kānū yanṭiqūna (Abraham) said: "Nay! Hath done it he, the chief of them is this (idol) so ye ask them, if they can speak" When Abraham was asked if it was he who broke the idols - Abraham replied, 'Why do ye not ask the chief (of the idols) who is standing there safe. Perhaps he has done it, i.e., if your idol-gods can speak, ask them as to who broke them. When they were unable to ask their idol-gods, nothing but the confession of their own folly, was the alternative left to them. Note that Abraham did not utter any lie denying what he had done. He only wanted the people to first ask their own idols as to who had done it.…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:64 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَرَجَعُوْۤا إِلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ فَقَالُوْۤا إِنَّكُمْ أَنْتُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ farajaʿū ilā anfusihim faqālū innakum antumu l-ẓālimūna Thereat they came to themselves and said [to one another], 'Indeed it is you who are the wrongdoers!'

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:64 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَرَجَعُوْۤا إِلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ فَقَالُوْۤا إِنَّكُمْ أَنْتُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ farajaʿū ilā anfusihim faqālū innakum antumu l-ẓālimūna So they returned to (blaming) themselves and said (to each other), "Indeed, you are the wrongdoers." So they turned to themselves and said: "Verily, you are the wrongdoers (21:64). Then they turned to themselves: "Indeed you know well that these speak not! (21:65). He said: "Do you then worship besides Allah, things that can neither profit you nor harm you? (21:66). "Fie upon you, and upon that which you worship besides Allah! Have you then no sense? (21:67). The People's Admission of their Gods' Incapability, and Ibrahim's Preaching Allah tells us that when Ibrahim said what he said, his people: فَرَجَعُوا إِلَىٰ أَنفُسِهِمْ turned to themselves Meaning: they blamed themselves for not taking precautions and protecting their gods. They said: إِنَّكُمْ أَنتُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ Verily, you are…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:64 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَرَجَعُوْۤا إِلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ فَقَالُوْۤا إِنَّكُمْ أَنْتُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ farajaʿū ilā anfusihim faqālū innakum antumu l-ẓālimūna Then they turned unto them selves and said, "Verily, ye are yourselves the unjust ones," The idolaters being ashamed of the well-proved fallacy of their creed and getting convinced of the truth preached by Abraham condemned themselves. Similarly, after the great event of Karbala, Yazid and the Yazidians stood self-condemned and condemned forever also by the human world for all times.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:65 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ نُكِسُوْۤا عَلَى رُءُوسِهِمْ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا هَؤُلَاءِ يَنْطِقُونَ thumma nukisū ʿalā ruūsihim laqad ʿalim'ta mā hāulāi yanṭiqūna Then they hung their heads. [They said], 'You certainly know that they cannot speak.'

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:65 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ نُكِسُوْۤا عَلَى رُءُوسِهِمْ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا هَؤُلَاءِ يَنْطِقُونَ thumma nukisū ʿalā ruūsihim laqad ʿalim'ta mā hāulāi yanṭiqūna Then they reversed themselves,1 (saying), "You have already known that these do not speak!" See 21:64

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:65 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ نُكِسُوْۤا عَلَى رُءُوسِهِمْ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا هَؤُلَاءِ يَنْطِقُونَ thumma nukisū ʿalā ruūsihim laqad ʿalim'ta mā hāulāi yanṭiqūna Then they were confounded (Figuratively their heads turned upside down - in shame.) in their heads, (and they helplessly said): "Thou knowest fully well that these (idols) speak not!" See 21:64

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:66 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ أَفَتَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنْفَعُكُمْ شَيْئًا وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمْ qāla afataʿbudūna min dūni l-lahi mā lā yanfaʿukum shayan walā yaḍurrukum He said, 'Do you then worship, besides Allah, that which cannot cause you any benefit or harm?

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:66 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ أَفَتَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنْفَعُكُمْ شَيْئًا وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمْ qāla afataʿbudūna min dūni l-lahi mā lā yanfaʿukum shayan walā yaḍurrukum He said, "Then do you worship instead of Allah that which does not benefit you at all or harm you? See 21:64

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:66 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ أَفَتَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنْفَعُكُمْ شَيْئًا وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمْ qāla afataʿbudūna min dūni l-lahi mā lā yanfaʿukum shayan walā yaḍurrukum Said: (Abraham) "What! worship ye then besides God what profiteth you not, nor do any harm unto you?" This is what Abraham told addressing the ashamed idolaters. Compare this to Husayn's sermon at Karbala. 'O' people! I say unto you! guard ye against evil! Fear the wrath of the Lord!'.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:67 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أُفٍّ لَكُمْ وَلِمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ uffin lakum walimā taʿbudūna min dūni l-lahi afalā taʿqilūna Fie on you and what you worship besides Allah! Do you not apply reason?'

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:67 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أُفٍّ لَكُمْ وَلِمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ uffin lakum walimā taʿbudūna min dūni l-lahi afalā taʿqilūna Uff1 to you and to what you worship instead of Allah. Then will you not use reason?" See 21:64

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:67 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أُفٍّ لَكُمْ وَلِمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ uffin lakum walimā taʿbudūna min dūni l-lahi afalā taʿqilūna Fie on you and on what ye worship besides God. What! Do ye not understand? See 21:66

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:68 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا حَرِّقُوهُ وَانْصُرُوا آلِهَتَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ فَاعِلِينَ qālū ḥarriqūhu wa-unṣurū ālihatakum in kuntum fāʿilīna They said, 'Burn him, and help your gods, if you are to do anything!'

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:68 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا حَرِّقُوهُ وَانْصُرُوا آلِهَتَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ فَاعِلِينَ qālū ḥarriqūhu wa-unṣurū ālihatakum in kuntum fāʿilīna They said, "Burn him and support your gods - if you are to act." They said: "Burn him and help your gods, if you will be doing (21:68). We said: "O fire! Be you cool and safety for Ibrahim! (21:69). And they wanted to harm him, but We made them the worst losers (21:70). How Ibrahim was Thrown into the Fire and How Allah Controlled it When their arguments were refuted and their incapability became clear, when truth was made manifest and falsehood was defeated, they resorted to using their power and strength, and said: حَرِّقُوهُ وَانصُرُوا آلِهَتَكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ فَاعِلِينَ "Burn him and help your gods, if you will be doing." So they gathered together a huge amount of wood. As-Suddi said, "I if a…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:68 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا حَرِّقُوهُ وَانْصُرُوا آلِهَتَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ فَاعِلِينَ qālū ḥarriqūhu wa-unṣurū ālihatakum in kuntum fāʿilīna Said they: "Burn him (Abraham.) and help your gods, if ye can do (anything at all);" Having been totally defeated by the arguments of Abraham, and recovering from the shame against their inability to talk to the idols and ask them as to who it was that had broken them to pieces, the people shouted in their anger to one another to burn Abraham in defence of their gods who had already been destroyed by Abraham. This is what the enemies of the Holy Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt did when they could not face the truth from these holy ones. They killed the holy ones one after another and persecuted their devotees and also killed them. It is said that a huge furnace was specially…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:69 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْنَا يَانَارُ كُونِي بَرْدًا وَسَلَامًا عَلَى اِبْرَاهِیْمَ qul'nā yānāru kūnī bardan wasalāman ʿalā ib'rāhīma We said, 'O fire! Be cool and safe for Abraham!'

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:69 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْنَا يَانَارُ كُونِي بَرْدًا وَسَلَامًا عَلَى اِبْرَاهِیْمَ qul'nā yānāru kūnī bardan wasalāman ʿalā ib'rāhīma We (i.e., Allah) said, "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim." See 21:68

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:69 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْنَا يَانَارُ كُونِي بَرْدًا وَسَلَامًا عَلَى اِبْرَاهِیْمَ qul'nā yānāru kūnī bardan wasalāman ʿalā ib'rāhīma Said (When Abraham was put into the fire.) We; (God.) "O' fire! Be thou cold, and a safety unto Abraham," When Abraham was being actually thrown into the fire through the sling, God willed the fire to get cooled to the degree of becoming a comfort to Abraham. And if the command from God had not been qualified by "Salaman", i.e., Comfort or Safety - the fire would have frozen Abraham to death had not been as it would have otherwise burnt him to ashes.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:70 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَرَادُوا بِهِ كَيْدًا فَجَعَلْنَاهُمُ الْأَخْسَرِينَ wa-arādū bihi kaydan fajaʿalnāhumu l-akhsarīna They sought to outmaneuver him, but We made them the biggest losers.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:70 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَرَادُوا بِهِ كَيْدًا فَجَعَلْنَاهُمُ الْأَخْسَرِينَ wa-arādū bihi kaydan fajaʿalnāhumu l-akhsarīna And they intended for him a plan (i.e., harm), but We made them the greatest losers. See 21:68

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:70 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَرَادُوا بِهِ كَيْدًا فَجَعَلْنَاهُمُ الْأَخْسَرِينَ wa-arādū bihi kaydan fajaʿalnāhumu l-akhsarīna And they intended a device against him, but We made them the greatest losers, Thus those who desired to be cruel to Abraham, their plans were frustrated and they were the losers and the sufferers too far, a host of mosquitoes was sent down and they ate away the flesh and drank the blood and the people suffered a very painful death and a mosquito entered the nostrils of Nimrod and passed on to his brain and the heathen despot met a miserable end.1 Compare this to the miserable end the devilish despot of Damascus met after enacting the gruesome massacre of Husayn and his holy band at Karbala.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:71 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ وَلُوطًا إِلَى الْأَرْضِ الَّتِي بَارَكْنَا فِيهَا لِلْعَالَمِينَ wanajjaynāhu walūṭan ilā l-arḍi allatī bāraknā fīhā lil'ʿālamīna We delivered him and Lot toward the land which We have blessed for all nations.1

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:71 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ وَلُوطًا إِلَى الْأَرْضِ الَّتِي بَارَكْنَا فِيهَا لِلْعَالَمِينَ wanajjaynāhu walūṭan ilā l-arḍi allatī bāraknā fīhā lil'ʿālamīna And We delivered him and Lut to the land which We had blessed for the worlds (i.e., peoples). And We rescued him and Lut to the land which We have blessed for the nations (21:71). And We bestowed upon him Ishaq, and Ya'qub Nafilatan. Each one We made righteous (21:72). And We made them leaders, guiding by Our command, and We revealed to them the doing of good deeds, performing Salah, and the giving of Zakah, and of Us (Alone) they were the worshippers (21:73). And (remember) Lut, We gave him wisdom and knowledge, and We saved him from the town who practised Al-Khaba'ith. Verily, they were a people given to evil, and were rebellious (21:74). And We admitted him to Our mercy; truly,…

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:71 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ وَلُوطًا إِلَى الْأَرْضِ الَّتِي بَارَكْنَا فِيهَا لِلْعَالَمِينَ wanajjaynāhu walūṭan ilā l-arḍi allatī bāraknā fīhā lil'ʿālamīna And We delivered him and (also) Lot, (and took them safely) to the land which We have blessed for all worlds. See 21:70

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:72 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ إِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ نَافِلَةً وَكُلًّا جَعَلْنَا صَالِحِينَ wawahabnā lahu is'ḥāqa wayaʿqūba nāfilatan wakullan jaʿalnā ṣāliḥīna And We gave him Isaac, and Jacob as well for a grandson,1 and each of them We made righteous.

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:72 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ إِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ نَافِلَةً وَكُلًّا جَعَلْنَا صَالِحِينَ wawahabnā lahu is'ḥāqa wayaʿqūba nāfilatan wakullan jaʿalnā ṣāliḥīna And We gave him Ishaq and Ya'qub in addition, and all (of them) We made righteous. See 21:71

item.title: Al-Anbiyaa:72 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
