Say: "Verily I only follow what is revealed unto me from my Lord; these are clear proofs (An eye opener.) from your Lord, and a guidance, and a mercy for a people who believe." See 7:196

item.title: Al-A'raaf:204 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا قُرِئَ الْقُرْاٰنُ فَاسْتَمِعُوا لَهُ وَأَنْصِتُوا لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ wa-idhā quri-a l-qur'ānu fa-is'tamiʿū lahu wa-anṣitū laʿallakum tur'ḥamūna When the Qur'ān is recited, listen to it and be silent, maybe you will receive [Allah's] mercy.

item.title: Al-A'raaf:204 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا قُرِئَ الْقُرْاٰنُ فَاسْتَمِعُوا لَهُ وَأَنْصِتُوا لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ wa-idhā quri-a l-qur'ānu fa-is'tamiʿū lahu wa-anṣitū laʿallakum tur'ḥamūna So when the Qur’ān is recited, then listen to it and pay attention that you may receive mercy. So, when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it, and be silent that you may receive mercy (7:204). The Order to Listen to the Qur'an After Allah mentioned that this Qur'an is a clear evidence, guidance and mercy for mankind, He commanded that one listen to the Qur'an when it is recited, in respect and honor of the Qur'an. This is to the contrary of the practice of the pagans of Quraysh, who said: لَا تَسْمَعُوا لِهَٰذَا الْقُرْآنِ وَالْغَوْا فِيهِ "Listen not to this Qur'an, and make noise in the midst of its (recitation)" (41:26) Ibn Jarir reported that Ibn Mas'ud said; We would give Salams…

item.title: Al-A'raaf:204 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا قُرِئَ الْقُرْاٰنُ فَاسْتَمِعُوا لَهُ وَأَنْصِتُوا لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ wa-idhā quri-a l-qur'ānu fa-is'tamiʿū lahu wa-anṣitū laʿallakum tur'ḥamūna And when the Qur'an is recited; then ye listen to it and be attentive, that mercy be done unto you. Listening to the recital of Qur'an is no doubt highly commendable but it becomes imperative only when the recital is by the Imam of the Jam'at in congregational prayer or in the 'Khutba' (Sermon) of the Friday Prayer. This is almost unanimous among the various Schools Refer to 'Fiqh' (A.P.)

item.title: Al-A'raaf:205 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاذْكُرْ رَبَّكَ فِي نَفْسِكَ تَضَرُّعًا وَخِيفَةً وَدُونَ الْجَهْرِ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ بِالْغُدُوِّ وَالْءَاصَالِ وَلَا تَكُنْ مِنَ الْغَافِلِينَ wa-udh'kur rabbaka fī nafsika taḍarruʿan wakhīfatan wadūna l-jahri mina l-qawli bil-ghuduwi wal-āṣāli walā takun mina l-ghāfilīna And remember your Lord within your heart beseechingly and reverentially, without being loud, morning and evening, and do not be among the heedless.

item.title: Al-A'raaf:205 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاذْكُرْ رَبَّكَ فِي نَفْسِكَ تَضَرُّعًا وَخِيفَةً وَدُونَ الْجَهْرِ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ بِالْغُدُوِّ وَالْءَاصَالِ وَلَا تَكُنْ مِنَ الْغَافِلِينَ wa-udh'kur rabbaka fī nafsika taḍarruʿan wakhīfatan wadūna l-jahri mina l-qawli bil-ghuduwi wal-āṣāli walā takun mina l-ghāfilīna And remember your Lord within yourself in humility and in fear without being apparent in speech - in the mornings and the evenings. And do not be among the heedless. And remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and with fear and without loudness in words in the mornings and in the afternoons, and be not of those who are neglectful (7:205). Surely, those who are with your Lord (angels) are never too proud to perform acts of worship to Him, but they glorify His praise and prostrate themselves before Him (7:206). Remembering Allah in the Mornings and Afternoons Allah ordains that He be remembered more often in the…

item.title: Al-A'raaf:205 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاذْكُرْ رَبَّكَ فِي نَفْسِكَ تَضَرُّعًا وَخِيفَةً وَدُونَ الْجَهْرِ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ بِالْغُدُوِّ وَالْءَاصَالِ وَلَا تَكُنْ مِنَ الْغَافِلِينَ wa-udh'kur rabbaka fī nafsika taḍarruʿan wakhīfatan wadūna l-jahri mina l-qawli bil-ghuduwi wal-āṣāli walā takun mina l-ghāfilīna And remember thy Lord within thy self in humility and awe, and not (Less aloud.) aloud a voice, in the morning and the evening; and be thou not of the negligent (The Prophet addressed for the people.) ones. It is related that this order to recite the Holy Qur'an silently is an instruction as to what the 'Ma'mum', i.e., the guided one in prayer in the congregational prayers (Salat al-jama' at) has to do, i.e., to recite the passage along with the Imam but not aloud.

item.title: Al-A'raaf:206 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِهِ وَيُسَبِّحُونَهُ وَلَهُ يَسْجُدُونَ inna alladhīna ʿinda rabbika lā yastakbirūna ʿan ʿibādatihi wayusabbiḥūnahu walahu yasjudūna Indeed those who are [stationed] near your Lord do not disdain to worship Him. They glorify Him and prostrate to Him.

item.title: Al-A'raaf:206 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِهِ وَيُسَبِّحُونَهُ وَلَهُ يَسْجُدُونَ inna alladhīna ʿinda rabbika lā yastakbirūna ʿan ʿibādatihi wayusabbiḥūnahu walahu yasjudūna Indeed, those who are near your Lord (i.e., the angels) are not prevented by arrogance from His worship, and they exalt Him, and to Him they prostrate. See 7:205

item.title: Al-A'raaf:206 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِهِ وَيُسَبِّحُونَهُ وَلَهُ يَسْجُدُونَ inna alladhīna ʿinda rabbika lā yastakbirūna ʿan ʿibādatihi wayusabbiḥūnahu walahu yasjudūna Verily those who are with (In direct Communion 'Sajdah', prostration. According to the Ahl Al-Bayt – 'Sajdah' i.e., prostration at the recital of certain Verses is 'Wajib' Compulsory - in four Chapters of the Qur'an: Surah As-Sajdah (32:15) Surah Fussilat (41:37) Surah An-Najm (53:62) Surah Al-Alaq (96:19) In rest of the chapters 'Sunnat' Optional. Refer to verses 13:15, 22:77, 32:15.) thy Lord, pride not to worship Him; they glorify Him and (in worship) unto Him they prostrate. The recital of this is as a Sunnat traditional, to be followed by a 'Sajdah' (i.e., a prostration). According to the 'Shi'a Ithna-'Ashari' school which is Islam-Original, i.e., according to the Holy Prophet and the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt 'Sajdah' the prostration…

item.title: Al-Asr:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْعَصْرِ wal-ʿaṣri By Time!

item.title: Al-Asr:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْعَصْرِ wal-ʿaṣri By time.1 وَالْعَصْرِ - إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ - إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ 1. By Al-'Asr. 2. Verily, man is in loss. 3. Except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and recommend one another to the truth, and recommend one another to patience. Al-'Asr is the time in which the movements of the Children of Adam occur, whether good or evil. Malik narrated from Zayd bin Aslam that he said, "It is the evening." However, the first view is the popular opinion. Thus, Allah swears by this, that man is in Khusr, which means in loss and destruction. إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ Except those who believe and do righteous good deeds So Allah makes an exception, among the species of man being in loss, for those who believe in their hearts…

item.title: Al-Asr:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْعَصْرِ wal-ʿaṣri By the Time (Lit. Squeezing.) ! 'Asr', i.e., Age, which is the continuity of time. The word 'Asr' meaning age or time is used in a mystic use. Commentators say it is a reference to the Age of the Holy Prophet, i.e., a period when the Lord's Promised Last Reformer and Final Law-giver was sent into the world and stayed preaching the truth and taught men the correct ways and means by which man can rise from the ignoble and the loathsome depth of the material world into the glorious heights of spiritual bliss. Some commentators take the word 'Asr' to mean the ceremonial afternoon prayer and the Sixth Holy Imam Ja'far Ibn Muhammad As-Sadiq says it is a reference to the age when the Last one of the promised Guide or Imam, in the seed of the…

item.title: Al-Asr:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الْاِنْسَانَ لَفِیْ خُسْرٍ inna l-insāna lafī khus'rin Indeed man is in loss,

item.title: Al-Asr:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الْاِنْسَانَ لَفِیْ خُسْرٍ inna l-insāna lafī khus'rin Indeed, mankind is in loss. See 103:1

item.title: Al-Asr:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الْاِنْسَانَ لَفِیْ خُسْرٍ inna l-insāna lafī khus'rin Verily, man is in loss! It is needless to go into the details that man amidst innumerable temptations, is always caught in the lust for the satisfaction of his carnal desires, thus under the risk of being easily beguiled by the innumerable and the most powerful and irresistible attractions. And if man, is not on his guard against all the formidable forces of Satan who is ever active to lead man astray, man suffers the loss, the loss of the pleasure of his Lord which is the loss of his own salvation, the loss real. It is said that this is, as well a reference to the taunt of Abu Jahl and Walid Ibn Moghaira who said that the Holy Prophet and his followers are the losers, for they have abandoned the…

item.title: Al-Asr:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِلَّا الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا وَعَمِلُوْۤا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ illā alladhīna āmanū waʿamilū l-ṣāliḥāti watawāṣaw bil-ḥaqi watawāṣaw bil-ṣabri except those who have faith and do righteous deeds, and enjoin one another to [follow] the truth, and enjoin one another to patience.

item.title: Al-Asr:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِلَّا الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا وَعَمِلُوْۤا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ illā alladhīna āmanū waʿamilū l-ṣāliḥāti watawāṣaw bil-ḥaqi watawāṣaw bil-ṣabri Except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience. See 103:1

item.title: Al-Asr:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِلَّا الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا وَعَمِلُوْۤا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ illā alladhīna āmanū waʿamilū l-ṣāliḥāti watawāṣaw bil-ḥaqi watawāṣaw bil-ṣabri Save those who believe, and do good deeds, and exhort each other to truth and exhort each other to endurance (Refer to: 90:17.) 'Those who believe' may include every believer to the extent or the degree of the strength of his conviction or faith and those who will be meant here with the fullest application of the term, will be only those who satisfy to the fullest extent the owning of the several great qualities of a believer mentioned by God1. The believers are those from whom God has purchased their wealth and their lives in exchange for His pleasure with them 9:111. Those who hold the Holy Prophet in preference to their own souls 33:6. The perfection or the purity in…

item.title: Al-Balad:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا أُقْسِمُ بِهَذَا الْبَلَدِ lā uq'simu bihādhā l-baladi I swear by this town,

item.title: Al-Balad:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا أُقْسِمُ بِهَذَا الْبَلَدِ lā uq'simu bihādhā l-baladi I swear by this city (i.e., Makkah). عَلَيْهِمْ نَارٌ مُّؤْصَدَةٌ Upon them Fire will Mu'sadah. Meaning: it will be sealed over them and there will be no way for them to avoid it, nor will they have any way out. Abu Hurayrah, Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id bin Jubayr, Mujahid, Muhammad bin Ka'b Al-Qurazi, 'Atiyah Al-'Awfi, Al-Hasan, Qatadah and As-Suddi, all said: مُّؤْصَدَةٌ Mu'sadah. "This means shut." Ibn 'Abbas said, "Its doors will be closed." Ad-Dahhak said: مُّؤْصَدَةٌ Mu'sadah. "It will be sealed over them and it will have no door." Qatadah said: مُّؤْصَدَةٌ Mu'sadah. "It will be shut and there will be no light in it, no crevice (escape), and no way out of it forever." This is the end of the Tafsir of Surat Al-Balad, and all praise and blessings are…

item.title: Al-Balad:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا أُقْسِمُ بِهَذَا الْبَلَدِ lā uq'simu bihādhā l-baladi Nay! Swear I by this City (Mecca)! City, i.e., Mecca - The people were already aware of the sanctity of the place which was chosen by the great prophet Abraham where at the command of the Lord he left his wife Hagar and his son Ishmael. For the connection of Ishmael's name with Arabia is historic fact through Kedar, son of Bhima. This is vouched by the Old Testament: Gen. 25/13, 18 ps. 120/5, Isa. 42/11, 60/7. Abraham and Ishmael had built the Holy Ka'ba which they raised, dedicating it exclusively for the remembrance of the Lord1 and Abraham in his prayers to the Lord wanted a Prophet to be raised in his seed and to raise some holy one2 who would uphold the sanctity of the House and maintain it in…

item.title: Al-Balad:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنْتَ حِلٌّ بِهَذَا الْبَلَدِ wa-anta ḥillun bihādhā l-baladi as you reside in this town;

item.title: Al-Balad:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنْتَ حِلٌّ بِهَذَا الْبَلَدِ wa-anta ḥillun bihādhā l-baladi And you, (O Muḥammad), are free of restriction in this city. See 90:1

item.title: Al-Balad:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنْتَ حِلٌّ بِهَذَا الْبَلَدِ wa-anta ḥillun bihādhā l-baladi While thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) hath been settler (Unfettered - (A.P.).) in this City! It is given as an exclusive privilege to the Holy Prophet to act freely in the city irrespective of the conventional observance of the sanctity of the place, i.e., to use force, arrest the disbelievers, punish them, deal with them as he deems necessary in the execution of his duties as the Apostle of God, which freedom none else had or would ever have, till the end of the world. This refers to the freedom that God gave the Holy Prophet when he had to enter Mecca by force to free the Holy Place from the control of the pagans who had desecrated the Holy House by turning it into the centre of idol worship and all…

item.title: Al-Balad:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَوَالِدٍ وَمَا وَلَدَ wawālidin wamā walada by the father and him whom he begot:

item.title: Al-Balad:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَوَالِدٍ وَمَا وَلَدَ wawālidin wamā walada And (by) the father1 and that which was born (of him). See 90:1

item.title: Al-Balad:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَوَالِدٍ وَمَا وَلَدَ wawālidin wamā walada And the Begetter (Refers to Adam as a chosen one and what he begot of chosen ones of God. (A.P.). Refer to: 3:32; 3:33.) (Adam) and whom he begat (mankind) The Begetter, i.e., the First begetter of man, i.e., Adam, and the begotten, the human race as a whole or Abraham the Begetter of Ishmael who assisted Abraham in building the Holy Ka'ba, the House of God, and in whose seed is the Holy Prophet. Refers to Adam as a Chosen one and what he begot, of the chosen ones of God. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Balad:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْاِنْسَانَ فِي كَبَدٍ laqad khalaqnā l-insāna fī kabadin certainly We created man in travail.

item.title: Al-Balad:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْاِنْسَانَ فِي كَبَدٍ laqad khalaqnā l-insāna fī kabadin We have certainly created man into hardship. See 90:1

item.title: Al-Balad:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْاِنْسَانَ فِي كَبَدٍ laqad khalaqnā l-insāna fī kabadin Indeed We have created man (to dwell) amidst hardship It is a well-known fact that man has been mysteriously created with distress and difficulties, pangs and pains connected with his birth and is placed in the world to face distress, difficulties and miseries to live in toil and labour and also in mental worries of which not a single human soul, could be free since the birth of the first man on earth till the end of the world, and with the burden of the responsibility of his accountability in the ultimate1. ''For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief, yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity" Eccles. 2/23.

item.title: Al-Balad:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَيَحْسَبُ أَنْ لَنْ يَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ أَحَدٌ ayaḥsabu an lan yaqdira ʿalayhi aḥadun Does he suppose that no one will ever have power over him?

item.title: Al-Balad:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَيَحْسَبُ أَنْ لَنْ يَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ أَحَدٌ ayaḥsabu an lan yaqdira ʿalayhi aḥadun Does he think that never will anyone overcome him? See 90:1

item.title: Al-Balad:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَيَحْسَبُ أَنْ لَنْ يَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ أَحَدٌ ayaḥsabu an lan yaqdira ʿalayhi aḥadun What! Thinketh he (Man.) that over him none, ever hath (any) power? Let no man even for a while imagine that there is none over him to control or to take an account of his motives and deeds - verse 89:14 clearly warns man to beware saying ''Thy Lord is watchful"

item.title: Al-Balad:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَقُولُ أَهْلَكْتُ مَالًا لُبَدًا yaqūlu ahlaktu mālan lubadan He says, 'I have squandered immense wealth.'

item.title: Al-Balad:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَقُولُ أَهْلَكْتُ مَالًا لُبَدًا yaqūlu ahlaktu mālan lubadan He says, "I have spent wealth in abundance." See 90:1

item.title: Al-Balad:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَقُولُ أَهْلَكْتُ مَالًا لُبَدًا yaqūlu ahlaktu mālan lubadan Saith he (Man.) : ''I have wasted, wealth enormous! This is what the disbelievers said when they saw Islam progressing in spite of all their wealth which they exhausted to obstruct its march1. They at last felt their spending away the wealth to stop the Holy Prophet from preaching the Truth, (i.e., Islam from spreading) was all a waste, being of no avail at all. And what some hypocrites felt and said that at their embracing Islam they had been made to spend in dispensing the prescribed poor-rate and the other charities which they deemed as a waste of their wealth. It is clearly indicated here that wealth is given to man as a trial to test his disposition with it.

item.title: Al-Balad:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَيَحْسَبُ أَنْ لَمْ يَرَهُ أَحَدٌ ayaḥsabu an lam yarahu aḥadun Does he suppose that no one sees him?

item.title: Al-Balad:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَيَحْسَبُ أَنْ لَمْ يَرَهُ أَحَدٌ ayaḥsabu an lam yarahu aḥadun Does he think that no one has seen him? See 90:1

item.title: Al-Balad:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَيَحْسَبُ أَنْ لَمْ يَرَهُ أَحَدٌ ayaḥsabu an lam yarahu aḥadun What! Thinketh he that no one seeth him (Refer to: 8:36.) ? The way of righteousness has been shown and explained by Islam and the way of evil has been pointed out and warned against, informing man of the evil consequences if it - Both the ways have been shown and man has been given eyes and mouths - With the eyes man can see the facts and differentiate between the right and the wrong and the mouth is given to speak, i.e., to enquire about the truth and also to speak it out, tongue to taste the right food and the wrong one, before he devours anything and everything. The eye and the mouth are the two highways shown to man A proper pondering over this will disclose the…

item.title: Al-Balad:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَمْ نَجْعَلْ لَهُ عَيْنَيْنِ alam najʿal lahu ʿaynayni Have We not made for him two eyes,

item.title: Al-Balad:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَمْ نَجْعَلْ لَهُ عَيْنَيْنِ alam najʿal lahu ʿaynayni Have We not made for him two eyes? See 90:1

item.title: Al-Balad:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَمْ نَجْعَلْ لَهُ عَيْنَيْنِ alam najʿal lahu ʿaynayni What! Made We not for him, (his) two eyes? See 90:7

item.title: Al-Balad:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلِسَانًا وَشَفَتَيْنِ walisānan washafatayni a tongue, and two lips,

item.title: Al-Balad:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلِسَانًا وَشَفَتَيْنِ walisānan washafatayni And a tongue and two lips? See 90:1

item.title: Al-Balad:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلِسَانًا وَشَفَتَيْنِ walisānan washafatayni And a tongue and two lips See 90:7

item.title: Al-Balad:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهَدَيْنَاهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ wahadaynāhu l-najdayni and shown him the two paths [of good and evil]?

item.title: Al-Balad:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهَدَيْنَاهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ wahadaynāhu l-najdayni And have shown him the two ways?1 See 90:1

item.title: Al-Balad:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهَدَيْنَاهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ wahadaynāhu l-najdayni And we showed him the two high-ways (Refer to: 76:3, 91:8.) (of good and evil) Refer to 76:3 and 91:8 and this verse clearly assert that man has been gifted with the power of discrimination and discretion between right and wrong, i.e., one should depend on this native endowment to some extent, independent of the guidance from without, through the apostles - or rather it can be said that without the inborn guidance, i.e., the power of reason, there would be no use of the external guidance. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Balad:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَا اقْتَحَمَ الْعَقَبَةَ falā iq'taḥama l-ʿaqabata Yet he has not embarked upon the uphill task.

item.title: Al-Balad:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَا اقْتَحَمَ الْعَقَبَةَ falā iq'taḥama l-ʿaqabata But he has not broken through the difficult pass.1 See 90:1

item.title: Al-Balad:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَا اقْتَحَمَ الْعَقَبَةَ falā iq'taḥama l-ʿaqabata But he strove not unto (crossing over) the Ascent steep (To ascend the steep.) The path of righteousness is well-known to be an uphill task for it needs to conquer one's self, fighting one's own passion of the carnal desires which go on forging luxuries which are forbidden, and thus lead a restrained life in this world. See Math. 7/14, and man is least inclined to adopt it. This has been referred to also by the Holy Prophet Jesus: ''Because straight is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it" Math 7/14.

item.title: Al-Balad:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْعَقَبَةُ wamā adrāka mā l-ʿaqabatu And what will show you what is the uphill task?

item.title: Al-Balad:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْعَقَبَةُ wamā adrāka mā l-ʿaqabatu And what can make you know what is (breaking through) the difficult pass? See 90:1

item.title: Al-Balad:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْعَقَبَةُ wamā adrāka mā l-ʿaqabatu What would make thee know what is the Ascent steep? See 90:11

item.title: Al-Balad:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ fakku raqabatin [It is] the freeing of a slave,

item.title: Al-Balad:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ fakku raqabatin It is the freeing of a slave. See 90:1

item.title: Al-Balad:13 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ fakku raqabatin (It is) the freeing a slave or a captive Note the setting free of the slave has been so highly commended. Islam controlled slavery in such a graceful and practical way that it made the maintaining of a slave, a great responsibility for the Master and at the same it enjoined so much care and kindness to the slaves that when they were duly maintained, the slaves themselves, in many cases when they were freed did not like to have the freedom and to leave their masters. For the facilities to be given to the slaves to earn their freedom - See 'Fiqh.'

item.title: Al-Balad:14 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ aw iṭ'ʿāmun fī yawmin dhī masghabatin or feeding [the needy] on a day of starvation,

item.title: Al-Balad:14 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ aw iṭ'ʿāmun fī yawmin dhī masghabatin Or feeding on a day of severe hunger. See 90:1

item.title: Al-Balad:14 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ aw iṭ'ʿāmun fī yawmin dhī masghabatin Or feeding in the day of hunger Note the care of the orphans, the needy, the destitute prescribed in all the acts of charity, as the test of the degree of the sincerity of the one in the faith.

item.title: Al-Balad:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَتِيمًا ذَا مَقْرَبَةٍ yatīman dhā maqrabatin or an orphan among relatives,

item.title: Al-Balad:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَتِيمًا ذَا مَقْرَبَةٍ yatīman dhā maqrabatin An orphan of near relationship. See 90:1

item.title: Al-Balad:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَتِيمًا ذَا مَقْرَبَةٍ yatīman dhā maqrabatin To an Orphan (Refer to: 4:2, 4:127, 2:220.) , being near of kin See 90:14

item.title: Al-Balad:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوْ مِسْكِينًا ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ aw mis'kīnan dhā matrabatin or a needy man in desolation,

item.title: Al-Balad:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوْ مِسْكِينًا ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ aw mis'kīnan dhā matrabatin Or a needy person in misery. See 90:1

item.title: Al-Balad:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوْ مِسْكِينًا ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ aw mis'kīnan dhā matrabatin Or to the poor one lying in the dust See 90:14

item.title: Al-Balad:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ كَانَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْمَرْحَمَةِ thumma kāna mina alladhīna āmanū watawāṣaw bil-ṣabri watawāṣaw bil-marḥamati while being one of those who have faith and who enjoin one another to patience, and enjoin one another to compassion.

item.title: Al-Balad:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ كَانَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْمَرْحَمَةِ thumma kāna mina alladhīna āmanū watawāṣaw bil-ṣabri watawāṣaw bil-marḥamati And then being among those who believed and advised one another to patience and advised one another to compassion. See 90:1

item.title: Al-Balad:17 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ كَانَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْمَرْحَمَةِ thumma kāna mina alladhīna āmanū watawāṣaw bil-ṣabri watawāṣaw bil-marḥamati Besides this, to be of those who believe, and enjoin (Recommend (A.P.).) steadfastness on each other, and enjoin mercy on each other (Refer to: 103:3.) Here, patience and compassion is stressed upon whereas in 103:3 endurance and adherence to the Truth. Taking both together, indicated that man's perfection in theory and practice is intended. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Balad:18 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اُولٰٓئِكَ أَصْحَابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ ulāika aṣḥābu l-maymanati They are the People of the Right Hand.

item.title: Al-Balad:18 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اُولٰٓئِكَ أَصْحَابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ ulāika aṣḥābu l-maymanati Those are the companions of the right.1 See 90:1

item.title: Al-Balad:18 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اُولٰٓئِكَ أَصْحَابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ ulāika aṣḥābu l-maymanati These are the people of the Right Hand (Refer to: 56:8.) Those who achieve their cherished goal of salvation1.

item.title: Al-Balad:19 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا بِاٰیٰتِنَاۤ هُمْ أَصْحَابُ الْمَشْءَمَةِ wa-alladhīna kafarū biāyātinā hum aṣḥābu l-mashamati But those who defy Our signs, they are the People of the Left Hand.

item.title: Al-Balad:19 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا بِاٰیٰتِنَاۤ هُمْ أَصْحَابُ الْمَشْءَمَةِ wa-alladhīna kafarū biāyātinā hum aṣḥābu l-mashamati But they who disbelieved in Our signs - those are the companions of the left.1 See 90:1

item.title: Al-Balad:19 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا بِاٰیٰتِنَاۤ هُمْ أَصْحَابُ الْمَشْءَمَةِ wa-alladhīna kafarū biāyātinā hum aṣḥābu l-mashamati And those who disbelieve in Our signs, they are the people of the Left Hand (Refer to: 56:9.) Those who would lose the game of life and thus be committed to the hell-fire which will encompass them from all sides1.

item.title: Al-Balad:20 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: عَلَيْهِمْ نَارٌ مُؤْصَدَةٌ ʿalayhim nārun mu'ṣadatun [Imposed] upon them will be a closed Fire.

item.title: Al-Balad:20 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: عَلَيْهِمْ نَارٌ مُؤْصَدَةٌ ʿalayhim nārun mu'ṣadatun Over them will be fire closed in.1 See 90:1

item.title: Al-Balad:20 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: عَلَيْهِمْ نَارٌ مُؤْصَدَةٌ ʿalayhim nārun mu'ṣadatun On them shall be the fire closed over See 90:19

item.title: Al-Baqara:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: الم alif-lam-meem Alif, Lām, Mīm.

item.title: Al-Baqara:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: الم alif-lam-meem Alif, Lām, Meem.1 الم Alif Lam Mim (2: 1) and four letters, such as: المر 'Alif Lam Mim Ra (13:1) And: المص Alif Lam Mim Sad (7:1) Sometimes, five letters were mentioned, such as: كهيعص Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad (19:1) And; حـم - عسق Ha Mim. 'Ayn Sin Qaf (42:1-2) This is because the words that are used in speech are usually comprised of one, two, three, four, or five letters. Every Surah that begins with these letters demonstrates the Qur'an's miracle and magnificence, and this fact is known by those well-versed in such matters. The count of these Surahs is twenty-nine. For instance, Allah said: الم - ذَٰلِكَ الْكِتَابُ لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ Alif Lam Mim This is the Book (the Qur'an), wherein there is no doubt (2:1-2): الم - اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ…

item.title: Al-Baqara:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: الم alif-lam-meem Alif, Lam, Mim Bismi-Llah. - Bismi-Llah, Al-Rahman, Al-Rahim Bismi-Llah, Al-Rahmani, Al-Rahim is a part of the Surah al-Fatiha and all the other Surahs save the 9th. It has been used obviously for the following important purposes: To condition the mind of the reader with the sanctity of the purpose i.e. the Divine Guidance for which the Holy Word of God is recited. By the meaning of the words 'I begin in the Holy name of God, the Beneficent, the Merciful', means to invoke the Beneficence and the Mercy of the Lord to bestow upon the reciter, the guidance he needs. By using Bismi-Llah before the very commencement of any good work, also means that the individual does it, not for any selfish motives of his own, but he does it on behalf of, and as commanded by the…

item.title: Al-Baqara:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ذٰلِكَ الْكِتَابُ لَا رَيْبَ فِیْهِ هُدًى لِلْمُتَّقِينَ dhālika l-kitābu lā rayba fīhi hudan lil'muttaqīna This is the Book,1 there is no doubt in it, a guidance to the Godwary,2

item.title: Al-Baqara:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ذٰلِكَ الْكِتَابُ لَا رَيْبَ فِیْهِ هُدًى لِلْمُتَّقِينَ dhālika l-kitābu lā rayba fīhi hudan lil'muttaqīna This is the Book about which there is no doubt, a guidance for those conscious of Allah1. That is Book in which there is no Rayb, guidance for the Muttaqin (2:2). There is No Doubt in the Qur'an The Book, is the Qur'an, and Rayb means doubt. As-Suddi said that Abu Malik and Abu Salih narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, and Murrah Al-Hamadani narrated from Ibn Mas'ud and several other Companions of the Messenger of Allah SAW that: لَا رَيْبَ ۛ فِيهِ ۛ In which there is no Rayb Means about which there is no doubt. Abu Ad-Darda', Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id bin Jubayr, Abu Malik, Nafi' 'Ata', Abu Al-'Aliyah, Ar-Rabi' bin Anas, Muqatil bin Hayyan, As-Suddi, Qatadah and Ismail bin Abi Khalid said similarly. In addition,…

item.title: Al-Baqara:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ذٰلِكَ الْكِتَابُ لَا رَيْبَ فِیْهِ هُدًى لِلْمُتَّقِينَ dhālika l-kitābu lā rayba fīhi hudan lil'muttaqīna This is the Book, there is no doubt in it, (being the Word of God) (it is) a guidance for the pious (ones) 'Dhalika al-Kitab' - 'Dhalika' synonymous to 'that' is a demonstrative pronoun referring to the remote object but sometimes the same is used for the object close at hand in reverence and respect indicating the lofty status of the object referred to. This Holy Book as the most comprehensive and complete Word of God, in the sphere of revelation, is the most sublime and the most revered one. For this reason, here and in many subsequent places to refer to this Holy Book, this demonstrative i.e. Dhalika is used and when a reference is made to its verses the pronoun 'Tilka' the feminine gender…

item.title: Al-Baqara:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْغَيْبِ وَيُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ alladhīna yu'minūna bil-ghaybi wayuqīmūna l-ṣalata wamimmā razaqnāhum yunfiqūna who believe in the Unseen, and maintain the prayer, and spend1 out of what We have provided for them;

item.title: Al-Baqara:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْغَيْبِ وَيُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ alladhīna yu'minūna bil-ghaybi wayuqīmūna l-ṣalata wamimmā razaqnāhum yunfiqūna Who believe in the unseen, establish prayer,1 and spend out of what We2 have provided for them. Those Who have faith in the Ghayb (2:3). The Meaning of Iman Abu Ja'far Ar-Razi said that Al-'Ala' bin Al-Musayyib bin Rafi' narrated from Abu Ishaq that Abu Al-Ahwas said that 'Abdullah said, "Iman is to trust.". Ali bin Abi Talhah reported that Ibn 'Abbas said: يُؤْمِنُونَ who have faith means they trust. Also, Ma'mar said that Az-Zuhri said, "Iman is the deeds." In addition, Abu Ja'far Ar-Razi said that Ar-Rabi' bin Anas said that, 'They have faith', means, they fear (Allah). Ibn Jarir (At-Tabari) commented, "The prefered view is that they be described as having faith in the Unseen by the tongue, deed and creed. In…

item.title: Al-Baqara:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْغَيْبِ وَيُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ alladhīna yu'minūna bil-ghaybi wayuqīmūna l-ṣalata wamimmā razaqnāhum yunfiqūna Who believe in the unseen, and establish the prayers and of what We have provided them with, they give (in the way of their Lord) 'Muttaqeen' The description of the 'Muttaqeen' or the pious ones mentioned in 2:2 - 2:5. Vs. 2-5 give very important guidance as to the correct identification of those who are in fact the pious ones meant by God. A similar description of the pious ones is given in verse 3. It must also be remembered by those who seek to be led aright on the right path, that when a definition or description of any quality is used, the perfect degree of that attribute will be the object of the address. For instance, when 'Muttaqeen' or 'Muttaqoon' or 'Mu'minin'…

item.title: Al-Baqara:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ وَبِالْآخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ wa-alladhīna yu'minūna bimā unzila ilayka wamā unzila min qablika wabil-ākhirati hum yūqinūna and who believe in what has been sent down to you1 and what was sent down before you, and are certain of the Hereafter.

item.title: Al-Baqara:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ وَبِالْآخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ wa-alladhīna yu'minūna bimā unzila ilayka wamā unzila min qablika wabil-ākhirati hum yūqinūna And who believe in what has been revealed to you, (O Muḥammad), and what was revealed before you, and of the Hereafter they are certain (in faith). And who have faith in what is revealed to you and in what was revealed before you, and in the Hereafter they are certain (2:4). Ibn 'Abbas said that: وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ مِن قَبْلِكَ And who have faith in what is revealed to you and in what was revealed before you. means, "They believe in what Allah sent you with, and in what the previous Messengers were sent with, they do not distinguish between (believing) them, nor do they reject what they brought from their…

item.title: Al-Baqara:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ وَبِالْآخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ wa-alladhīna yu'minūna bimā unzila ilayka wamā unzila min qablika wabil-ākhirati hum yūqinūna And who believe in that which hath been sent down unto thee (O' Our Apostle Muhammad) and that which hath been sent down (unto the other apostles) before thee, and of the hereafter, they are sure The Universality of Islam being the Religion for the mankind as a whole, is testified by this part of the verse, which means that the pious ones are those who believe, not only in the truthfulness of the Qur'an which has been sent down to the Holy Prophet but also in the Holy Books sent down to all the apostles of God preceding him. Islam alone and no other religion in the world enjoins as an article of faith, the…

item.title: Al-Baqara:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اُولٰٓئِكَ عَلَى هُدًى مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ وَاُولٰٓىِٕكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ ulāika ʿalā hudan min rabbihim wa-ulāika humu l-muf'liḥūna Those follow their Lord's guidance, and it is they who are the felicitous.

item.title: Al-Baqara:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اُولٰٓئِكَ عَلَى هُدًى مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ وَاُولٰٓىِٕكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ ulāika ʿalā hudan min rabbihim wa-ulāika humu l-muf'liḥūna Those are upon (right) guidance from their Lord, and it is those who are the successful. They are on guidance from their Lord, and they are the successful (2:5). Guidance and Success are Awarded to the Believers Allah said: وَأُوْلَٰـئِكَ They are refers to those who believe in the Unseen, establish the prayer, spend from what Allah has granted them, believe in what Allah has revealed to the Messenger and the Messengers before him, believe in the Hereafter with certainty, and prepare the necessary requirements for the Hereafter by performing good deeds and avoiding the prohibitions. Allah then said: عَلَىٰ هُدًى On guidance Meaning: they are (following) a light, guidance, and have insight from Allah: وَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ And they are the successful Meaning:…

item.title: Al-Baqara:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اُولٰٓئِكَ عَلَى هُدًى مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ وَاُولٰٓىِٕكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ ulāika ʿalā hudan min rabbihim wa-ulāika humu l-muf'liḥūna These are the ones on the guidance from their Lord, and these are the ones who shall be the successful ones 'Wabil-Aakhirati - hum - youquinoon'. 'Aakhirat', i.e., Hereafter, literally meaning the End. This word has been used in the Holy Qur'an mostly in the sense of the Hereafter, (i.e., the life after death), but in some places it has been used in a wider sense viz., the world or the realm of being beyond the visible world (30:7) i.e., "they know of the lower life its apparent phase and of its other phase they are negligent" The use of the word 'Zahir', i.e., Apparent and 'Ghafil', i.e., negligent, testify the fact that the 'Aakhirat' referred to is something opposite to 'Zahir', i.e., apparent,…

item.title: Al-Baqara:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ inna alladhīna kafarū sawāon ʿalayhim a-andhartahum am lam tundhir'hum lā yu'minūna As for the faithless, it is the same to them whether you warn them or do not warn them, they will not have faith.

item.title: Al-Baqara:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ inna alladhīna kafarū sawāon ʿalayhim a-andhartahum am lam tundhir'hum lā yu'minūna Indeed, those who disbelieve1 - it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe. Verily, those who disbelieve, it is the same to them whether you warn them or do not warn them, they will not believe (2:6). Allah said: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا Verily, those who disbelieve Meaning: covered the truth and hid it. Since Allah has written that they would do so, it does not matter if you (O Muhammad SAW) warn them or not, they would still have disbelieved in what you were sent with. Similarly, Allah said: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ حَقَّتْ عَلَيْهِمْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ - وَلَوْ جَاءَتْهُمْ كُلُّ آيَةٍ حَتَّىٰ يَرَوُا الْعَذَابَ…

item.title: Al-Baqara:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ inna alladhīna kafarū sawāon ʿalayhim a-andhartahum am lam tundhir'hum lā yu'minūna Verily (as for) those who disbelieve, alike is it for them, thou warneth them or warneth them not; (for) they will not believe 'Kufr' is to cover. It has been used in the Holy Qur'an to mean to cover the Truth or to cover the fault. Covering the Truth means turning the mind from it and to cover the fault means to redeem or to redress1 or to wipe it out. It is mostly used in the sense opposed to 'Imam.' It is obvious that those who lack faith as stated before will not be able to avail themselves of the guidance whether they are warned or not. But this passage should not be interpreted to mean to…

item.title: Al-Baqara:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: خَتَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ وَعَلَى سَمْعِهِمْ وَعَلَى أَبْصَارِهِمْ غِشَاوَةٌ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ khatama l-lahu ʿalā qulūbihim waʿalā samʿihim waʿalā abṣārihim ghishāwatun walahum ʿadhābun ʿaẓīmun Allah has set a seal on their hearts and their hearing, and there is a blindfold on their sight,1 and there is a great punishment for them.

item.title: Al-Baqara:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: خَتَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ وَعَلَى سَمْعِهِمْ وَعَلَى أَبْصَارِهِمْ غِشَاوَةٌ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ khatama l-lahu ʿalā qulūbihim waʿalā samʿihim waʿalā abṣārihim ghishāwatun walahum ʿadhābun ʿaẓīmun Allah has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their vision is a veil.1 And for them is a great punishment. Allah has set a seal on their hearts and on their hearing, and on their eyes there is a covering. Theirs will be a great torment (2:7). Meaning of Khatama As-Suddi said that: خَتَمَ اللَّهُ Khatama Allah means, "Allah has sealed." Qatadah said that this Ayah means, "Shaytan controlled them when they obeyed him. Therefore, Allah sealed their hearts, hearing and sight, and they could neither see the guidance nor hear, comprehend or understand." Ibn Jurayj said that Mujahid said: خَتَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ Allah has set a seal on…

item.title: Al-Baqara:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: خَتَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ وَعَلَى سَمْعِهِمْ وَعَلَى أَبْصَارِهِمْ غِشَاوَةٌ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ khatama l-lahu ʿalā qulūbihim waʿalā samʿihim waʿalā abṣārihim ghishāwatun walahum ʿadhābun ʿaẓīmun God hath sealed up their hearts and their hearing; and upon their sight is a covering; and for them is a great chastisement Sealing the hearts of the reprobates is done as a natural consequence of their being abandoned to sin. Their senses get automatically blunt for lack of the proper or the correct use. If the edge of a sharp knife is rubbed on a stone or any such hard material the edge automatically loses it sharpness and gets blunt and useless for any use as a knife. As a natural penalty of themselves having lost in persistent sinning, their senses have been made blunt. This consequence is referred to in Verse 7:179, and against…

item.title: Al-Baqara:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَقُولُ اٰمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَبِالْيَوْمِ الْاٰخِرِ وَمَا هُمْ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ wamina l-nāsi man yaqūlu āmannā bil-lahi wabil-yawmi l-ākhiri wamā hum bimu'minīna And among the people are those who say, 'We have faith in Allah and the Last Day,' but they have no faith.

item.title: Al-Baqara:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَقُولُ اٰمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَبِالْيَوْمِ الْاٰخِرِ وَمَا هُمْ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ wamina l-nāsi man yaqūlu āmannā bil-lahi wabil-yawmi l-ākhiri wamā hum bimu'minīna And of the people are some who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but they are not believers. And of mankind, there are some who say: "We believe in Allah and the Last Day" while in fact they do not believe (2:8). They try to deceive Allah and those who believe, while they only deceive themselves, and perceive (it) not (2:9). Meaning of Nifaq Nifaq means to show conformity - or agreement - and to conceal evil. Nifaq has several types: Nifaq in the creed that causes its people to reside in Hell for eternity, and Nifaq in deed, which is one of the major sins, as we will explain soon, Allah willing. Ibn Jurayj…

item.title: Al-Baqara:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَقُولُ اٰمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَبِالْيَوْمِ الْاٰخِرِ وَمَا هُمْ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ wamina l-nāsi man yaqūlu āmannā bil-lahi wabil-yawmi l-ākhiri wamā hum bimu'minīna And of the people (are some) who say, "we believe in God and in the Last Day (of Judgment)", (while in fact) they are not believers (at all) This verse and the next twelve verses refer to the conduct of the hypocrites. By the faith in God and in the Later Day i.e., the Day of Judgment means Islam. The Munafiq i.e., the hypocrites are those disbelievers who just to serve their own purpose of justifying their social position or the safety and security of themselves and their personal interest, had made just a show of their joining the ranks of the Muslims, against the fast - increasing power and strength of the adherents of Islam. The Leader…

item.title: Al-Baqara:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يُخَادِعُونَ اللَّهَ وَالَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا وَمَا يَخْدَعُونَ إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ yukhādiʿūna l-laha wa-alladhīna āmanū wamā yakhdaʿūna illā anfusahum wamā yashʿurūna They seek to deceive Allah and those who have faith, yet they deceive no one but themselves, but they are not aware.

item.title: Al-Baqara:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يُخَادِعُونَ اللَّهَ وَالَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا وَمَا يَخْدَعُونَ إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ yukhādiʿūna l-laha wa-alladhīna āmanū wamā yakhdaʿūna illā anfusahum wamā yashʿurūna They (think to) deceive Allah and those who believe, but they deceive not except themselves and perceive (it) not. See 2:8

item.title: Al-Baqara:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يُخَادِعُونَ اللَّهَ وَالَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا وَمَا يَخْدَعُونَ إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ yukhādiʿūna l-laha wa-alladhīna āmanū wamā yakhdaʿūna illā anfusahum wamā yashʿurūna They (intend to) 'deceive God and those who believe, while they deceive not but themselves, but they perceive (it) not This verse clearly shows their individual position. When it is proved to delude himself thinking that the real state of his mind is hidden from God and many a time bases his belief upon his own imaginations and false conceptions. When for any worldly considerations to gain reputation in the world and the goodwill of the people, he does something of seeming virtue, he gains honour for him and expects God also to reward him so much. This is nothing but the individual's deceiving the All-Knowing God Who fully knows the latent intentions concealed in the depths of the hearts…

item.title: Al-Baqara:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ فَزَادَهُمُ اللَّهُ مَرَضًا وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ اَلِیْمٌ بِمَا كَانُوْۤا يَكْذِبُونَ fī qulūbihim maraḍun fazādahumu l-lahu maraḍan walahum ʿadhābun alīmun bimā kānū yakdhibūna There is a sickness in their hearts; then Allah increased their sickness, and there is a painful punishment for them because of the lies they used to tell.

item.title: Al-Baqara:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ فَزَادَهُمُ اللَّهُ مَرَضًا وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ اَلِیْمٌ بِمَا كَانُوْۤا يَكْذِبُونَ fī qulūbihim maraḍun fazādahumu l-lahu maraḍan walahum ʿadhābun alīmun bimā kānū yakdhibūna In their hearts is disease, so Allah has increased their disease;1 and for them is a painful punishment because they (habitually) used to lie. In their hearts is a disease and Allah has increased their disease. A painful torment is theirs because they used to tell lies (2:10). The Meaning of 'Disease' in this Ayah As-Suddi narrated from Abu Malik and (also) from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, and (also) Murrah Al-Hamdani from Ibn Mas'ud and other Companions that this Ayah: فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌ In their hearts is a disease means, 'doubt', and: فَزَادَهُمُ اللَّهُ مَرَضًا And Allah has increased their disease also means 'doubt'. Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Abu Al-'Aliyah, Ar-Rabi' bin Anas and Qatadah…

item.title: Al-Baqara:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ فَزَادَهُمُ اللَّهُ مَرَضًا وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ اَلِیْمٌ بِمَا كَانُوْۤا يَكْذِبُونَ fī qulūbihim maraḍun fazādahumu l-lahu maraḍan walahum ʿadhābun alīmun bimā kānū yakdhibūna In their heart is a disease, and God increaseth their disease, for them is a painful chastisement, because of the lie they were saying The disease referred to, is the envy and jealousy which burnt those who had not sincerely believed and had envied the Holy Prophet's ever increasing supreme power and authority. The more and evermore increased the glory of the Holy Prophet, the more did increase also the envy and the jealousy of the hypocrites. The disbelief, the envy and the jealousy of the hypocrites is termed as disease, and since it was God's Will that caused the increase of the Holy Prophet's supreme power and authority over the peoples, the increase in the…

item.title: Al-Baqara:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ لَا تُفْسِدُوْۤا فِي الْأَرْضِ قَالُوْا إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُصْلِحُونَ wa-idhā qīla lahum lā tuf'sidū fī l-arḍi qālū innamā naḥnu muṣ'liḥūna When they are told, 'Do not cause corruption on the earth,' they say, 'We are only reformers!'

item.title: Al-Baqara:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ لَا تُفْسِدُوْۤا فِي الْأَرْضِ قَالُوْا إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُصْلِحُونَ wa-idhā qīla lahum lā tuf'sidū fī l-arḍi qālū innamā naḥnu muṣ'liḥūna And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth," they say, "We are but reformers." And when it is said to them: Do not make mischief on the earth," they say: "We are only peacemakers (2:11). Verily, they are the ones who make mischief, but they perceive not (2:12). Meaning of Mischief In his Tafsir, As-Suddi said that Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud commented: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ لَا تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ قَالُوا إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُصْلِحُونَ And when it is said to them: "Do not make mischief on the earth," they say: "We are only peacemakers." They are the hypocrites. As for: لَا تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ "Do not make mischief on the earth" That…

item.title: Al-Baqara:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ لَا تُفْسِدُوْۤا فِي الْأَرْضِ قَالُوْا إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُصْلِحُونَ wa-idhā qīla lahum lā tuf'sidū fī l-arḍi qālū innamā naḥnu muṣ'liḥūna And when it is said unto them, "make ye not mischief in the earth" say they, 'Verily, we are only the well – doers' The notorious hypocrite of Madina, Abd Allah Ibn Ubayy and those like him continued their intimacy with the infidels. When the suspicion, against their faithfulness to Islam and the Muslims arose, they said they only endeavoured to bring the infidels to friendly terms with the Muslims, and hence they were the peacemakers, but the truth was that the fire of envy and jealousy did not allow them to rest. They had resorted to duplicity and underhand dealings to upset the growing supremacy of the Holy Prophet and the increasing dominance of Islam which was…

item.title: Al-Baqara:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْمُفْسِدُونَ وَلَكِنْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ alā innahum humu l-muf'sidūna walākin lā yashʿurūna Look! They are themselves the agents of corruption, but they are not aware.

item.title: Al-Baqara:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْمُفْسِدُونَ وَلَكِنْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ alā innahum humu l-muf'sidūna walākin lā yashʿurūna Unquestionably, it is they who are the corrupters, but they perceive (it) not. See 2:11

item.title: Al-Baqara:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْمُفْسِدُونَ وَلَكِنْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ alā innahum humu l-muf'sidūna walākin lā yashʿurūna Beware! Verily, they are the mischief - mongers but they perceive (it) not See 2:11

item.title: Al-Baqara:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ اٰمِنُوْۤا كَمَا اٰمَنَ النَّاسُ قَالُوْا أَنُؤْمِنُ كَمَا اٰمَنَ السُّفَهَاءُ أَلَا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ السُّفَهَاءُ وَلَكِنْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ wa-idhā qīla lahum āminū kamā āmana l-nāsu qālū anu'minu kamā āmana l-sufahāu alā innahum humu l-sufahāu walākin lā yaʿlamūna And when they are told, 'Believe like the people who have believed,' they say, 'Shall we believe like the fools who have believed?' Look! They are themselves the fools, but they do not know.

item.title: Al-Baqara:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ اٰمِنُوْۤا كَمَا اٰمَنَ النَّاسُ قَالُوْا أَنُؤْمِنُ كَمَا اٰمَنَ السُّفَهَاءُ أَلَا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ السُّفَهَاءُ وَلَكِنْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ wa-idhā qīla lahum āminū kamā āmana l-nāsu qālū anu'minu kamā āmana l-sufahāu alā innahum humu l-sufahāu walākin lā yaʿlamūna And when it is said to them, "Believe as the people have believed," they say, "Should we believe as the foolish have believed?" Unquestionably, it is they who are the foolish, but they know (it) not. And when it is said to them: Believe as the people believe, They say: "Shall we believe as the fools have believed?" Verily, they are the fools, but they do not know (2:13). Allah said that if the hypocrites are told: آمِنُوا كَمَا آمَنَ النَّاسُ "Believe as the people believe," Which is meaning, 'Believe just as the believers believe in Allah, His angels, His Books, His…

item.title: Al-Baqara:13 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ اٰمِنُوْۤا كَمَا اٰمَنَ النَّاسُ قَالُوْا أَنُؤْمِنُ كَمَا اٰمَنَ السُّفَهَاءُ أَلَا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ السُّفَهَاءُ وَلَكِنْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ wa-idhā qīla lahum āminū kamā āmana l-nāsu qālū anu'minu kamā āmana l-sufahāu alā innahum humu l-sufahāu walākin lā yaʿlamūna When it is said unto them, "Believe ye as the (other) people did believe, they say, "shall we believe as the fools did believe?" Beware! Verily, they are the fools, but they know not" To believe in a new phenomenon, independent of any personal profit or loss, and against one's personal pride or prejudice, is not an ordinary problem. Ordinary men who constitute the general masses of the human beings inhabiting the earth, follow only those principles which agree to their personal inclinations and which harmonize with their individual selfish interest in this world. A faith, demanding a complete conquest of the…

item.title: Al-Baqara:14 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا لَقُوْۤا الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا قَالُوْا اٰمَنَّا وَإِذَا خَلَوْا إِلَى شَيَاطِينِهِمْ قَالُوْا إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُسْتَهْزِءُونَ wa-idhā laqū alladhīna āmanū qālū āmannā wa-idhā khalaw ilā shayāṭīnihim qālū innā maʿakum innamā naḥnu mus'tahziūna When they meet the faithful, they say, 'We believe,' but when they are alone with their devils, they say, 'We are with you; we were only deriding [them].'

item.title: Al-Baqara:14 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا لَقُوْۤا الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا قَالُوْا اٰمَنَّا وَإِذَا خَلَوْا إِلَى شَيَاطِينِهِمْ قَالُوْا إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُسْتَهْزِءُونَ wa-idhā laqū alladhīna āmanū qālū āmannā wa-idhā khalaw ilā shayāṭīnihim qālū innā maʿakum innamā naḥnu mus'tahziūna And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone with their evil ones, they say, "Indeed, we are with you; we were only mockers." And when they meet those who believe, they say: We believe," but when they are alone with their Shayatin (devils), they say: "Truly, we are with you; verily, we were but mocking (2:14). Allah mocks at them and leaves them increasing in their deviation to wander blindly (2:15). The Hypocrites' Cunning and Deceit Allah said that when the hypocrites meet the believers, they proclaim their faith and pretend to be believers, loyalists and friends. They do this…

item.title: Al-Baqara:14 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا لَقُوْۤا الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا قَالُوْا اٰمَنَّا وَإِذَا خَلَوْا إِلَى شَيَاطِينِهِمْ قَالُوْا إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُسْتَهْزِءُونَ wa-idhā laqū alladhīna āmanū qālū āmannā wa-idhā khalaw ilā shayāṭīnihim qālū innā maʿakum innamā naḥnu mus'tahziūna And when they meet with those who believe, they say, "we believe" but when they go apart to their devils, they say, "surely we are with you, verily, we did but mock" 'Istehza' or mockery which is repeated in the retort, in the sense that they will reap in the end only that which they sow here, for the law of nature is 'Ma lil insan ilia ma Sa'a'. For man there is nothing but what he strove for. God's mockery lies in instead of punishing the disbelievers immediately, granting them respite until the Day of Judgment and allowing them to enjoy life and their false pride with…

item.title: Al-Baqara:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَللَّهُ يَسْتَهْزِئُ بِهِمْ وَيَمُدُّهُمْ فِي طُغْيَانِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ al-lahu yastahzi-u bihim wayamudduhum fī ṭugh'yānihim yaʿmahūna It is Allah who derides them,1 and leaves them bewildered in their rebellion.

item.title: Al-Baqara:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَللَّهُ يَسْتَهْزِئُ بِهِمْ وَيَمُدُّهُمْ فِي طُغْيَانِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ al-lahu yastahzi-u bihim wayamudduhum fī ṭugh'yānihim yaʿmahūna (But) Allah mocks them and prolongs them in their transgression (while) they wander blindly. See 2:14

item.title: Al-Baqara:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَللَّهُ يَسْتَهْزِئُ بِهِمْ وَيَمُدُّهُمْ فِي طُغْيَانِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ al-lahu yastahzi-u bihim wayamudduhum fī ṭugh'yānihim yaʿmahūna God mocketh at them and He only alloweth them to continue bewildered in their rebellion See 2:14

item.title: Al-Baqara:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اُولٰٓئِكَ الَّذِينَ اشْتَرَوُا الضَّلَالَةَ بِالْهُدَى فَمَا رَبِحَتْ تِجَارَتُهُمْ وَمَا كَانُوْۤا مُهْتَدِينَ ulāika alladhīna ish'tarawū l-ḍalālata bil-hudā famā rabiḥat tijāratuhum wamā kānū muh'tadīna They are the ones who bought error for guidance, so their trade did not profit them, nor were they guided.

item.title: Al-Baqara:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اُولٰٓئِكَ الَّذِينَ اشْتَرَوُا الضَّلَالَةَ بِالْهُدَى فَمَا رَبِحَتْ تِجَارَتُهُمْ وَمَا كَانُوْۤا مُهْتَدِينَ ulāika alladhīna ish'tarawū l-ḍalālata bil-hudā famā rabiḥat tijāratuhum wamā kānū muh'tadīna Those are the ones who have purchased error (in exchange) for guidance, so their transaction has brought no profit, nor were they guided. These are they who have purchased error with guidance, so their commerce was profitless. And they were not guided (2:16). In his Tafsir, As-Suddi reported that Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud commented on; أُولَٰئِكَ الَّذِينَ اشْتَرَوُا الضَّلَالَةَ بِالْهُدَىٰ These are they who have purchased error with guidance saying it means, "They pursued misguidance and abandoned guidance. " Mujahid said, "They believed and then disbelieved," while Qatadah said, "They preferred deviation to guidance." Qatadah's statement is similar in meaning to Allah's statement about Thamud: وَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ فَاسْتَحَبُّوا الْعَمَىٰ عَلَى الْهُدَىٰ And as for Thamud, We…

item.title: Al-Baqara:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اُولٰٓئِكَ الَّذِينَ اشْتَرَوُا الضَّلَالَةَ بِالْهُدَى فَمَا رَبِحَتْ تِجَارَتُهُمْ وَمَا كَانُوْۤا مُهْتَدِينَ ulāika alladhīna ish'tarawū l-ḍalālata bil-hudā famā rabiḥat tijāratuhum wamā kānū muh'tadīna These are they who purchase error for guidance, hence their transaction profitteth them not, neither are they guided aright The adopting of error is compared to purchasing, and their foregoing the right guidance from God, as the price paid and in their dealing.

item.title: Al-Baqara:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَثَلُهُمْ كَمَثَلِ الَّذِي اسْتَوْقَدَ نَارًا فَلَمَّا أَضَاءَتْ مَا حَوْلَهُ ذَهَبَ اللَّهُ بِنُورِهِمْ وَتَرَكَهُمْ فِي ظُلُمَاتٍ لَا يُبْصِرُونَ mathaluhum kamathali alladhī is'tawqada nāran falammā aḍāat mā ḥawlahu dhahaba l-lahu binūrihim watarakahum fī ẓulumātin lā yub'ṣirūna Their parable is that of one who lighted a torch, and when it had lit up all around him, Allah took away their light, and left them sightless in a manifold darkness.1

item.title: Al-Baqara:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَثَلُهُمْ كَمَثَلِ الَّذِي اسْتَوْقَدَ نَارًا فَلَمَّا أَضَاءَتْ مَا حَوْلَهُ ذَهَبَ اللَّهُ بِنُورِهِمْ وَتَرَكَهُمْ فِي ظُلُمَاتٍ لَا يُبْصِرُونَ mathaluhum kamathali alladhī is'tawqada nāran falammā aḍāat mā ḥawlahu dhahaba l-lahu binūrihim watarakahum fī ẓulumātin lā yub'ṣirūna Their example is that of one who kindled a fire, but when it illuminated what was around him, Allah took away their light and left them in darkness (so) they could not see. Their likeness is as the likeness of one who kindled a fire; then, when it illuminated all around him, Allah removed their light and left them in darkness. (So) they could not see (2:17). They are deaf, dumb, and blind, so they return not (to the right path) (2:18). The Example of the Hypocrites Allah likened the hypocrites when they bought deviation with guidance, thus acquiring utter blindness, to the example of a…

item.title: Al-Baqara:17 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَثَلُهُمْ كَمَثَلِ الَّذِي اسْتَوْقَدَ نَارًا فَلَمَّا أَضَاءَتْ مَا حَوْلَهُ ذَهَبَ اللَّهُ بِنُورِهِمْ وَتَرَكَهُمْ فِي ظُلُمَاتٍ لَا يُبْصِرُونَ mathaluhum kamathali alladhī is'tawqada nāran falammā aḍāat mā ḥawlahu dhahaba l-lahu binūrihim watarakahum fī ẓulumātin lā yub'ṣirūna The likeness of them is like unto one who kindleth a fire, and when it lighteth all around him, God taketh away the light and leaveth them in darkness, they see not The simile in this verse refers to people first believing in the truth which is compared to kindling the fire, and the illuminating of the surrounding is compared to the social and the other privileges which profited such believers consequent upon their embracing the truth. The spark of faith which had just been kindled could have been developed into a full fire but the adverse attitude of the people made them lose their inner…

item.title: Al-Baqara:18 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ عُمْيٌ فَهُمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ ṣummun buk'mun ʿum'yun fahum lā yarjiʿūna Deaf, dumb, and blind, they will not come back.

item.title: Al-Baqara:18 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ عُمْيٌ فَهُمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ ṣummun buk'mun ʿum'yun fahum lā yarjiʿūna Deaf, dumb and blind - so they will not return (to the right path). See 2:17

item.title: Al-Baqara:18 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ عُمْيٌ فَهُمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ ṣummun buk'mun ʿum'yun fahum lā yarjiʿūna (They are) deaf, dumb and blind; hence they will return not (from their darkness) See 2:17

item.title: Al-Baqara:19 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوْ كَصَيِّبٍ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ فِیْهِ ظُلُمَاتٌ وَرَعْدٌ وَبَرْقٌ يَجْعَلُونَ أَصَابِعَهُمْ فِي اٰذَانِهِمْ مِنَ الصَّوَاعِقِ حَذَرَ الْمَوْتِ وَاللَّهُ مُحِيطٌ بِالْكَافِرِينَ aw kaṣayyibin mina l-samāi fīhi ẓulumātun waraʿdun wabarqun yajʿalūna aṣābiʿahum fī ādhānihim mina l-ṣawāʿiqi ḥadhara l-mawti wal-lahu muḥīṭun bil-kāfirīna Or that of a rainstorm from the sky, wherein is darkness, thunder, and lightning: they put their fingers in their ears due to the thunderclaps, apprehensive of death; and Allah besieges the faithless.1

item.title: Al-Baqara:19 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوْ كَصَيِّبٍ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ فِیْهِ ظُلُمَاتٌ وَرَعْدٌ وَبَرْقٌ يَجْعَلُونَ أَصَابِعَهُمْ فِي اٰذَانِهِمْ مِنَ الصَّوَاعِقِ حَذَرَ الْمَوْتِ وَاللَّهُ مُحِيطٌ بِالْكَافِرِينَ aw kaṣayyibin mina l-samāi fīhi ẓulumātun waraʿdun wabarqun yajʿalūna aṣābiʿahum fī ādhānihim mina l-ṣawāʿiqi ḥadhara l-mawti wal-lahu muḥīṭun bil-kāfirīna Or (it is) like a rainstorm from the sky within which is darkness, thunder and lightning. They put their fingers in their ears against the thunderclaps in dread of death. But Allah is encompassing1 of the disbelievers. Or like a rainstorm in the sky, bringing darkness, thunder, and lightning. They thrust their fingers in their ears to keep out the stunning thunderclap for fear of death. But Allah ever encompasses the disbelievers (2:19). The lightning almost snatches away their sight, whenever it flashes for them, they walk therein, and when darkness covers them, they stand still. And if Allah willed, He could…

item.title: Al-Baqara:19 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوْ كَصَيِّبٍ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ فِیْهِ ظُلُمَاتٌ وَرَعْدٌ وَبَرْقٌ يَجْعَلُونَ أَصَابِعَهُمْ فِي اٰذَانِهِمْ مِنَ الصَّوَاعِقِ حَذَرَ الْمَوْتِ وَاللَّهُ مُحِيطٌ بِالْكَافِرِينَ aw kaṣayyibin mina l-samāi fīhi ẓulumātun waraʿdun wabarqun yajʿalūna aṣābiʿahum fī ādhānihim mina l-ṣawāʿiqi ḥadhara l-mawti wal-lahu muḥīṭun bil-kāfirīna Or like a rainstorm from heaven fraught with darkness, thunder and lightning, they put their fingers in their ears against the thunderclaps for fear of death; and verily, God encompasseth the disbelievers Rain is the life - giving source for the dead dry earth. Islam has been compared to the life - giving rain. Those who embraced Islam were definitely profited as they were taken out of the darkness of their belief in the false and imaginary deities. The lightning mentioned in this verse, stands for the occasional triumph Islam had over the forces of the infidels. On every such occasion when…

item.title: Al-Baqara:20 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَكَادُ الْبَرْقُ يَخْطَفُ أَبْصَارَهُمْ كُلَّمَا أَضَاءَ لَهُمْ مَشَوْا فِیْهِ وَإِذَا أَظْلَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ قَامُوْۤا وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَذَهَبَ بِسَمْعِهِمْ وَأَبْصَارِهِمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ yakādu l-barqu yakhṭafu abṣārahum kullamā aḍāa lahum mashaw fīhi wa-idhā aẓlama ʿalayhim qāmū walaw shāa l-lahu ladhahaba bisamʿihim wa-abṣārihim inna l-laha ʿalā kulli shayin qadīrun The lightning almost snatches away their sight: whenever it shines for them, they walk in it, and when the darkness falls upon them, they stand. Had Allah willed, He would have taken away their hearing and their sight. Indeed Allah has power over all things.

item.title: Al-Baqara:20 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَكَادُ الْبَرْقُ يَخْطَفُ أَبْصَارَهُمْ كُلَّمَا أَضَاءَ لَهُمْ مَشَوْا فِیْهِ وَإِذَا أَظْلَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ قَامُوْۤا وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَذَهَبَ بِسَمْعِهِمْ وَأَبْصَارِهِمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ yakādu l-barqu yakhṭafu abṣārahum kullamā aḍāa lahum mashaw fīhi wa-idhā aẓlama ʿalayhim qāmū walaw shāa l-lahu ladhahaba bisamʿihim wa-abṣārihim inna l-laha ʿalā kulli shayin qadīrun The lightning almost snatches away their sight. Every time it lights (the way) for them, they walk therein; but when darkness comes over them, they stand (still). And if Allah had willed, He could have taken away their hearing and their sight. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent. See 2:19

item.title: Al-Baqara:20 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَكَادُ الْبَرْقُ يَخْطَفُ أَبْصَارَهُمْ كُلَّمَا أَضَاءَ لَهُمْ مَشَوْا فِیْهِ وَإِذَا أَظْلَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ قَامُوْۤا وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَذَهَبَ بِسَمْعِهِمْ وَأَبْصَارِهِمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ yakādu l-barqu yakhṭafu abṣārahum kullamā aḍāa lahum mashaw fīhi wa-idhā aẓlama ʿalayhim qāmū walaw shāa l-lahu ladhahaba bisamʿihim wa-abṣārihim inna l-laha ʿalā kulli shayin qadīrun The lightning well - nigh snatcheth away (a)their sight (from them)', as often as it gleameth for them, they walk therein and when it getteth dark for them, they halt; if God willed, He could take away their hearing and their sight. Verily, God hath power over all things See 2:19

item.title: Al-Baqara:21 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاأَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اعْبُدُوْۤا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ yāayyuhā l-nāsu uʿ'budū rabbakumu alladhī khalaqakum wa-alladhīna min qablikum laʿallakum tattaqūna O mankind! Worship your Lord, who created you and those who were before you, so that you may be Godwary.

item.title: Al-Baqara:21 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاأَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اعْبُدُوْۤا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ yāayyuhā l-nāsu uʿ'budū rabbakumu alladhī khalaqakum wa-alladhīna min qablikum laʿallakum tattaqūna O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you, that you may become righteous. O mankind! Worship your Lord (Allah), Who created you and those who were before you so that you may acquire Taqwa (2:21). Who has made the earth a resting place for you, and the sky as a canopy, and sent down water (rain) from the sky and brought forth therewith fruits as a provision for you. Then do not set up rivals unto Allah (in worship) while you know (that He alone has the right to be worshipped) (2:22). Tawhid Al-Uluhiyyah Allah next mentioned His Oneness in divinity and stated that He has favored His servants by bringing them to life…

item.title: Al-Baqara:21 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاأَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اعْبُدُوْۤا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ yāayyuhā l-nāsu uʿ'budū rabbakumu alladhī khalaqakum wa-alladhīna min qablikum laʿallakum tattaqūna O mankind! Worship ye (only) your Lord, Who created you and those before you, happily ye may guard (yourselves against evil) The Word 'La' alla' meaning happly - denotes that the truth preached by Islam is not forced upon any individual. This word stands as clear evidence to the degree to which Islam wants a human individual to exercise his or her personal or individual liberty or freedom in the choice of the faith. Otherwise, there can never be any merit in any virtue extracted of anyone by force. The word 'Rabb' or the 'Cherisher Lord' to Whom service is demanded of man, is in the spirit or the meaning of thankfulness for the invaluable gifts, favours and…

item.title: Al-Baqara:22 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ فِرَاشًا وَالسَّمَاءَ بِنَاءً وَأَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَخْرَجَ بِهِ مِنَ الثَّمَرَاتِ رِزْقًا لَكُمْ فَلَا تَجْعَلُوْۤا لِلَّهِ أَنْدَادًا وَأَنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ alladhī jaʿala lakumu l-arḍa firāshan wal-samāa bināan wa-anzala mina l-samāi māan fa-akhraja bihi mina l-thamarāti riz'qan lakum falā tajʿalū lillahi andādan wa-antum taʿlamūna He who made the earth a place of repose for you, and the sky a canopy, and He sends down water from the sky, and with it He brings forth crops for your sustenance. So do not set up equals to Allah, while you know.

item.title: Al-Baqara:22 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ فِرَاشًا وَالسَّمَاءَ بِنَاءً وَأَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَخْرَجَ بِهِ مِنَ الثَّمَرَاتِ رِزْقًا لَكُمْ فَلَا تَجْعَلُوْۤا لِلَّهِ أَنْدَادًا وَأَنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ alladhī jaʿala lakumu l-arḍa firāshan wal-samāa bināan wa-anzala mina l-samāi māan fa-akhraja bihi mina l-thamarāti riz'qan lakum falā tajʿalū lillahi andādan wa-antum taʿlamūna (He) who made for you the earth a bed (spread out) and the sky a ceiling and sent down from the sky, rain and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you. So do not attribute to Allah equals while you know (that there is nothing similar to Him). See 2:21

item.title: Al-Baqara:22 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ فِرَاشًا وَالسَّمَاءَ بِنَاءً وَأَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَخْرَجَ بِهِ مِنَ الثَّمَرَاتِ رِزْقًا لَكُمْ فَلَا تَجْعَلُوْۤا لِلَّهِ أَنْدَادًا وَأَنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ alladhī jaʿala lakumu l-arḍa firāshan wal-samāa bināan wa-anzala mina l-samāi māan fa-akhraja bihi mina l-thamarāti riz'qan lakum falā tajʿalū lillahi andādan wa-antum taʿlamūna Who made the earth a bed (resting place) for you and the sky a structure and causeth water to descend from heaven and thereby produceth fruits for your sustenance; set ye not Therefore, equals to God while ye already know See 2:21

item.title: Al-Baqara:23 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ فِي رَيْبٍ مِمَّا نَزَّلْنَا عَلَى عَبْدِنَا فَأْتُوْۤا بِسُورَةٍ مِنْ مِثْلِهِ وَادْعُوْۤا شُهَدَاءَكُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ wa-in kuntum fī raybin mimmā nazzalnā ʿalā ʿabdinā fatū bisūratin min mith'lihi wa-id'ʿū shuhadāakum min dūni l-lahi in kuntum ṣādiqīna And if you are in doubt concerning what We have sent down to Our servant, then bring a sūrah like it, and invoke your helpers besides Allah, should you be truthful.

item.title: Al-Baqara:23 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ فِي رَيْبٍ مِمَّا نَزَّلْنَا عَلَى عَبْدِنَا فَأْتُوْۤا بِسُورَةٍ مِنْ مِثْلِهِ وَادْعُوْۤا شُهَدَاءَكُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ wa-in kuntum fī raybin mimmā nazzalnā ʿalā ʿabdinā fatū bisūratin min mith'lihi wa-id'ʿū shuhadāakum min dūni l-lahi in kuntum ṣādiqīna And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down (i.e., the Qur’ān) upon Our Servant (i.e., Prophet Muḥammad SAW), then produce a sūrah the like thereof and call upon your witnesses (i.e., supporters) other than Allah, if you should be truthful. And if you (Arab pagans, Jews, and Christians) are in doubt concerning that which We have sent down (i.e. the Qur'an) to Our servant (Muhammad SAW), then produce a Surah (chapter) of the like thereof and call your witnesses (supporters and helpers) besides Allah, if you are truthful (2:23). But if you do it not, and…

item.title: Al-Baqara:23 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ فِي رَيْبٍ مِمَّا نَزَّلْنَا عَلَى عَبْدِنَا فَأْتُوْۤا بِسُورَةٍ مِنْ مِثْلِهِ وَادْعُوْۤا شُهَدَاءَكُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ wa-in kuntum fī raybin mimmā nazzalnā ʿalā ʿabdinā fatū bisūratin min mith'lihi wa-id'ʿū shuhadāakum min dūni l-lahi in kuntum ṣādiqīna If ye be in doubt about what We have sent down unto Our Servant (Muhammad) produce ye then a surah (chapter) like unto it, and call ye your witnesses other than God, if ye be truthful In this verse as in 17:88 an open challenge is thrown against everyone who claims as the master of the Arabic language, to bring ten Surahs or even one of its kind. This heavenly challenge remains current as long as the Holy Qur'an exists. It is a clear challenge and a doubtless proof to say that if What God has given to a man…

item.title: Al-Baqara:24 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلُوْۤا وَلَنْ تَفْعَلُوْۤا فَاتَّقُوْۤا النَّارَ الَّتِي وَقُودُهَا النَّاسُ وَالْحِجَارَةُ أُعِدَّتْ لِلْكَافِرِينَ fa-in lam tafʿalū walan tafʿalū fa-ittaqū l-nāra allatī waqūduhā l-nāsu wal-ḥijāratu uʿiddat lil'kāfirīna And if you do not—and you will not— then beware the Fire whose fuel will be humans and stones, prepared for the faithless.

item.title: Al-Baqara:24 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلُوْۤا وَلَنْ تَفْعَلُوْۤا فَاتَّقُوْۤا النَّارَ الَّتِي وَقُودُهَا النَّاسُ وَالْحِجَارَةُ أُعِدَّتْ لِلْكَافِرِينَ fa-in lam tafʿalū walan tafʿalū fa-ittaqū l-nāra allatī waqūduhā l-nāsu wal-ḥijāratu uʿiddat lil'kāfirīna But if you do not - and you will never be able to - then fear the Fire, whose fuel is people and stones, prepared for the disbelievers. See 2:23

item.title: Al-Baqara:24 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلُوْۤا وَلَنْ تَفْعَلُوْۤا فَاتَّقُوْۤا النَّارَ الَّتِي وَقُودُهَا النَّاسُ وَالْحِجَارَةُ أُعِدَّتْ لِلْكَافِرِينَ fa-in lam tafʿalū walan tafʿalū fa-ittaqū l-nāra allatī waqūduhā l-nāsu wal-ḥijāratu uʿiddat lil'kāfirīna But if ye do (it) not, and never shall ye do (it) then guard ye (yourselves) against the (Hell) fire whose fuel shall be the people and stones, prepared for the disbelievers The words 'Walan Taf'alu' further establishes the truth about the veritable position of the Holy Qur'an as a miracle, for the verdict is given in these words 'Walan Taf'alu' meaning, 'And ye shall never be able to do it.' It is nothing short of a prophecy as well as? warning against the delusion imagining the possibility of any successful imitation of the Holy Word of God, for ever. Thus, the challenge stands for ever and was not confined to the Arabian orators…

item.title: Al-Baqara:25 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَبَشِّرِ الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا وَعَمِلُوْۤا الصَّالِحَاتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ كُلَّمَا رُزِقُوْۤا مِنْهَا مِنْ ثَمَرَةٍ رِزْقًا قَالُوْا هَذَا الَّذِي رُزِقْنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ وَأُتُوْۤا بِهِ مُتَشَابِهًا وَلَهُمْ فِيهَا أَزْوَاجٌ مُطَهَّرَةٌ وَهُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ wabashiri alladhīna āmanū waʿamilū l-ṣāliḥāti anna lahum jannātin tajrī min taḥtihā l-anhāru kullamā ruziqū min'hā min thamaratin riz'qan qālū hādhā alladhī ruziq'nā min qablu wa-utū bihi mutashābihan walahum fīhā azwājun muṭahharatun wahum fīhā khālidūna And give good news to those who have faith and do righteous deeds, that for them shall be gardens with streams running in them: whenever they are provided with their fruit for nourishment, they will say, 'This is what we were provided before,' and they were given something resembling it. In it there will be chaste mates for them, and they will remain in it [forever].

item.title: Al-Baqara:25 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَبَشِّرِ الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا وَعَمِلُوْۤا الصَّالِحَاتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ كُلَّمَا رُزِقُوْۤا مِنْهَا مِنْ ثَمَرَةٍ رِزْقًا قَالُوْا هَذَا الَّذِي رُزِقْنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ وَأُتُوْۤا بِهِ مُتَشَابِهًا وَلَهُمْ فِيهَا أَزْوَاجٌ مُطَهَّرَةٌ وَهُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ wabashiri alladhīna āmanū waʿamilū l-ṣāliḥāti anna lahum jannātin tajrī min taḥtihā l-anhāru kullamā ruziqū min'hā min thamaratin riz'qan qālū hādhā alladhī ruziq'nā min qablu wa-utū bihi mutashābihan walahum fīhā azwājun muṭahharatun wahum fīhā khālidūna And give good tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds that they will have gardens (in Paradise) beneath which rivers flow. Whenever they are provided with a provision of fruit therefrom, they will say, "This is what we were provided with before." And it is given to them in likeness. And they will have therein purified spouses, and they will abide therein eternally. And give glad tidings to those who…
