item.title: Al-Baqara:283 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ عَلَى سَفَرٍ وَلَمْ تَجِدُوْۤا كَاتِبًا فَرِهَانٌ مَقْبُوضَةٌ فَإِنْ أَمِنَ بَعْضُكُمْ بَعْضًا فَلْيُؤَدِّ الَّذِي اؤْتُمِنَ أَمَانَتَهُ وَلْيَتَّقِ اللَّهَ رَبَّهُ وَلَا تَكْتُمُوْۤا الشَّهَادَةَ وَمَنْ يَكْتُمْهَا فَإِنَّهُ ءَاثِمٌ قَلْبُهُ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ عَلِیْمٌ wa-in kuntum ʿalā safarin walam tajidū kātiban farihānun maqbūḍatun fa-in amina baʿḍukum baʿḍan falyu-addi alladhī u'tumina amānatahu walyattaqi l-laha rabbahu walā taktumū l-shahādata waman yaktum'hā fa-innahu āthimun qalbuhu wal-lahu bimā taʿmalūna ʿalīmun If you are on a journey and cannot find a writer, then a retained pledge [shall suffice]. And if one of you entrusts to another, let him who is trusted deliver his trust, and let him be wary of Allah, his Lord. And do not conceal testimony; anyone who conceals it, his heart will indeed be sinful. And Allah knows best what you do.

item.title: Al-Baqara:283 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ عَلَى سَفَرٍ وَلَمْ تَجِدُوْۤا كَاتِبًا فَرِهَانٌ مَقْبُوضَةٌ فَإِنْ أَمِنَ بَعْضُكُمْ بَعْضًا فَلْيُؤَدِّ الَّذِي اؤْتُمِنَ أَمَانَتَهُ وَلْيَتَّقِ اللَّهَ رَبَّهُ وَلَا تَكْتُمُوْۤا الشَّهَادَةَ وَمَنْ يَكْتُمْهَا فَإِنَّهُ ءَاثِمٌ قَلْبُهُ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ عَلِیْمٌ wa-in kuntum ʿalā safarin walam tajidū kātiban farihānun maqbūḍatun fa-in amina baʿḍukum baʿḍan falyu-addi alladhī u'tumina amānatahu walyattaqi l-laha rabbahu walā taktumū l-shahādata waman yaktum'hā fa-innahu āthimun qalbuhu wal-lahu bimā taʿmalūna ʿalīmun And if you are on a journey and cannot find a scribe, then a security deposit (should be) taken. And if one of you entrusts another, then let him who is entrusted discharge his trust (faithfully) and let him fear Allah, his Lord. And do not conceal testimony, for whoever conceals it - his heart is indeed sinful, and Allah is Knowing of what you do. And if you are on a journey and cannot find…

item.title: Al-Baqara:283 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ عَلَى سَفَرٍ وَلَمْ تَجِدُوْۤا كَاتِبًا فَرِهَانٌ مَقْبُوضَةٌ فَإِنْ أَمِنَ بَعْضُكُمْ بَعْضًا فَلْيُؤَدِّ الَّذِي اؤْتُمِنَ أَمَانَتَهُ وَلْيَتَّقِ اللَّهَ رَبَّهُ وَلَا تَكْتُمُوْۤا الشَّهَادَةَ وَمَنْ يَكْتُمْهَا فَإِنَّهُ ءَاثِمٌ قَلْبُهُ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ عَلِیْمٌ wa-in kuntum ʿalā safarin walam tajidū kātiban farihānun maqbūḍatun fa-in amina baʿḍukum baʿḍan falyu-addi alladhī u'tumina amānatahu walyattaqi l-laha rabbahu walā taktumū l-shahādata waman yaktum'hā fa-innahu āthimun qalbuhu wal-lahu bimā taʿmalūna ʿalīmun And if ye be on a journey and ye find not a scribe then take a pledge (Security.) with possession; but if one of you trusteth the other, let the one trusted fulfil (Return the entrusted charge fully- Discharge of the trust one of the greatest demands of Islam.) his trust, and take shelter in God his Lord; and conceal not evidence; And whosoever concealeth it, then surely his heart is sinful; And Verily God knoweth…

item.title: Al-Baqara:284 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَإِنْ تُبْدُوْۤا مَا فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ يُحَاسِبْكُمْ بِهِ اللَّهُ فَيَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ lillahi mā fī l-samāwāti wamā fī l-arḍi wa-in tub'dū mā fī anfusikum aw tukh'fūhu yuḥāsib'kum bihi l-lahu fayaghfiru liman yashāu wayuʿadhibu man yashāu wal-lahu ʿalā kulli shayin qadīrun To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth; and whether you disclose what is in your hearts or hide it, Allah will bring you to account for it. Then He will forgive whomever He wishes and punish whomever He wishes, and Allah has power over all things.

item.title: Al-Baqara:284 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَإِنْ تُبْدُوْۤا مَا فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ يُحَاسِبْكُمْ بِهِ اللَّهُ فَيَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ lillahi mā fī l-samāwāti wamā fī l-arḍi wa-in tub'dū mā fī anfusikum aw tukh'fūhu yuḥāsib'kum bihi l-lahu fayaghfiru liman yashāu wayuʿadhibu man yashāu wal-lahu ʿalā kulli shayin qadīrun To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. Whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will bring you to account for it. Then He will forgive whom He wills and punish whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent. To Allah belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is on the earth, and whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account…

item.title: Al-Baqara:284 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَإِنْ تُبْدُوْۤا مَا فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ يُحَاسِبْكُمْ بِهِ اللَّهُ فَيَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ lillahi mā fī l-samāwāti wamā fī l-arḍi wa-in tub'dū mā fī anfusikum aw tukh'fūhu yuḥāsib'kum bihi l-lahu fayaghfiru liman yashāu wayuʿadhibu man yashāu wal-lahu ʿalā kulli shayin qadīrun God's is whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth; and whether ye manifest what is in your selves or conceal it, God will call you to account for it; and then will He forgive whomsoever He willeth and will punish whomsoever He willeth and Verily God is powerful over all things The heavens and the earth mentioned in this verse may be taken in the higher sense of the realms of spirit and matter i.e. God's are the realms concrete…

item.title: Al-Baqara:285 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَٰمَنَ الرَّسُولُ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ كُلٌّ اٰمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْ رُسُلِهِ وَقَالُوْۤا سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا غُفْرَانَكَ رَبَّنَا وَإِلَيْكَ الْمَصِيرُ āmana l-rasūlu bimā unzila ilayhi min rabbihi wal-mu'minūna kullun āmana bil-lahi wamalāikatihi wakutubihi warusulihi lā nufarriqu bayna aḥadin min rusulihi waqālū samiʿ'nā wa-aṭaʿnā ghuf'rānaka rabbanā wa-ilayka l-maṣīru The Apostle has faith in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and all the faithful. Each [of them] has faith in Allah, His angels, His scriptures and His apostles. [They declare,] 'We make no distinction between any of His apostles.' And they say, 'We hear and obey. Our Lord, forgive us, and toward You is the return.'

item.title: Al-Baqara:285 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَٰمَنَ الرَّسُولُ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ كُلٌّ اٰمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْ رُسُلِهِ وَقَالُوْۤا سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا غُفْرَانَكَ رَبَّنَا وَإِلَيْكَ الْمَصِيرُ āmana l-rasūlu bimā unzila ilayhi min rabbihi wal-mu'minūna kullun āmana bil-lahi wamalāikatihi wakutubihi warusulihi lā nufarriqu bayna aḥadin min rusulihi waqālū samiʿ'nā wa-aṭaʿnā ghuf'rānaka rabbanā wa-ilayka l-maṣīru The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and (so have) the believers. All of them have believed in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers, (saying), "We make no distinction between any of His messengers." And they say, "We hear and we obey. (We seek) Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the (final) destination." The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and (so do) the believers. Each one…

item.title: Al-Baqara:285 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَٰمَنَ الرَّسُولُ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ كُلٌّ اٰمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْ رُسُلِهِ وَقَالُوْۤا سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا غُفْرَانَكَ رَبَّنَا وَإِلَيْكَ الْمَصِيرُ āmana l-rasūlu bimā unzila ilayhi min rabbihi wal-mu'minūna kullun āmana bil-lahi wamalāikatihi wakutubihi warusulihi lā nufarriqu bayna aḥadin min rusulihi waqālū samiʿ'nā wa-aṭaʿnā ghuf'rānaka rabbanā wa-ilayka l-maṣīru The (Note the universality of the religion Islam - Faith in all the apostles of God and the holy Scriptures preached only by Islam and no other creed in the world. Refer to Verse . 3:84.) Prophet believeth in what hath come down unto him from his Lord, and (so do) the believers; all believe in God, and in His Angels and in His Books and in His apostles; (they say) "We make no difference (In their being equally truthful - Not partial to anyone of…

item.title: Al-Baqara:286 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا اكْتَسَبَتْ رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَا إِنْ نَسِينَا أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنَا إِصْرًا كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِنَا رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ وَاعْفُ عَنَّا وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا وَارْحَمْنَا أَنْتَ مَوْلَانَا فَانْصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ lā yukallifu l-lahu nafsan illā wus'ʿahā lahā mā kasabat waʿalayhā mā ik'tasabat rabbanā lā tuākhidh'nā in nasīnā aw akhṭanā rabbanā walā taḥmil ʿalaynā iṣ'ran kamā ḥamaltahu ʿalā alladhīna min qablinā rabbanā walā tuḥammil'nā mā lā ṭāqata lanā bihi wa-uʿ'fu ʿannā wa-igh'fir lanā wa-ir'ḥamnā anta mawlānā fa-unṣur'nā ʿalā l-qawmi l-kāfirīna Allah does not task any soul beyond its capacity. Whatever [good] it earns is to its benefit, and whatever [evil] it incurs is to its harm. 'Our Lord! Take us not to task if we forget or make mistakes! Our Lord! Place…

item.title: Al-Baqara:286 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا اكْتَسَبَتْ رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَا إِنْ نَسِينَا أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنَا إِصْرًا كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِنَا رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ وَاعْفُ عَنَّا وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا وَارْحَمْنَا أَنْتَ مَوْلَانَا فَانْصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ lā yukallifu l-lahu nafsan illā wus'ʿahā lahā mā kasabat waʿalayhā mā ik'tasabat rabbanā lā tuākhidh'nā in nasīnā aw akhṭanā rabbanā walā taḥmil ʿalaynā iṣ'ran kamā ḥamaltahu ʿalā alladhīna min qablinā rabbanā walā tuḥammil'nā mā lā ṭāqata lanā bihi wa-uʿ'fu ʿannā wa-igh'fir lanā wa-ir'ḥamnā anta mawlānā fa-unṣur'nā ʿalā l-qawmi l-kāfirīna Allah does not charge a soul except (with that within) its capacity. It will have (the consequence of) what (good) it has gained, and it will bear (the consequence of) what (evil) it has earned. "Our Lord, do not impose blame upon…

item.title: Al-Baqara:286 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا اكْتَسَبَتْ رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَا إِنْ نَسِينَا أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنَا إِصْرًا كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِنَا رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ وَاعْفُ عَنَّا وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا وَارْحَمْنَا أَنْتَ مَوْلَانَا فَانْصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ lā yukallifu l-lahu nafsan illā wus'ʿahā lahā mā kasabat waʿalayhā mā ik'tasabat rabbanā lā tuākhidh'nā in nasīnā aw akhṭanā rabbanā walā taḥmil ʿalaynā iṣ'ran kamā ḥamaltahu ʿalā alladhīna min qablinā rabbanā walā tuḥammil'nā mā lā ṭāqata lanā bihi wa-uʿ'fu ʿannā wa-igh'fir lanā wa-ir'ḥamnā anta mawlānā fa-unṣur'nā ʿalā l-qawmi l-kāfirīna Imposeth not God, any soul but to its (individual) (Capacity Everyone charged to the individual capacity.) ability; for it shall be (the good) what he hath acquired and against it (shall be) (the evil) he hath wrought; O' Our Lord ! hold…

item.title: Al-Bayyina:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَمْ يَكُنِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ مُنْفَكِّينَ حَتّٰی تَأْتِيَهُمُ الْبَيِّنَةُ lam yakuni alladhīna kafarū min ahli l-kitābi wal-mush'rikīna munfakkīna ḥattā tatiyahumu l-bayinatu The faithless from among the People of the Book and the polytheists were not set apart until the proof had come to them:

item.title: Al-Bayyina:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَمْ يَكُنِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ مُنْفَكِّينَ حَتّٰی تَأْتِيَهُمُ الْبَيِّنَةُ lam yakuni alladhīna kafarū min ahli l-kitābi wal-mush'rikīna munfakkīna ḥattā tatiyahumu l-bayinatu Those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists were not to be parted (from misbelief)1 until there came to them clear evidence. وَمَا أُمِرُوا إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ And they were commanded not, but that they should worship Allah, making religion purely for Him alone, This is similar to Allah's statement: وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا نُوحِي إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاعْبُدُونِ And We did not send any Messenger before you but We revealed to him: La ilaha illa Ana. (21:25) Thus, Allah says: حُنَفَاءَ Hunafa' Meaning: avoiding Shirk and being truly devout to Tawhid. This is like Allah's statement: وَلَقَدْ بَعَثْنَا فِي كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ رَّسُولًا…

item.title: Al-Bayyina:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَمْ يَكُنِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ مُنْفَكِّينَ حَتّٰی تَأْتِيَهُمُ الْبَيِّنَةُ lam yakuni alladhīna kafarū min ahli l-kitābi wal-mush'rikīna munfakkīna ḥattā tatiyahumu l-bayinatu Those who disbelieved from among the people of the Book and the polytheists could not have separated themselves (from the falsehood) until came unto them the Clear Evidence 'Munfakkeen', i.e., separated, i.e., separated from falsehood. It is a fact that the people of the Book, i.e., the Jews and the Christians of Arabia were relieved of their false dogma; the Jews about the false belief in Moses being the son of God and their rituals and the Christians of the inconceivable Trinity, i.e., of God being the one in three and three in one, by clear evidence the Holy Prophet presented through the Holy Qur'an. The Jews and the Christians who are addressed here as the…

item.title: Al-Bayyina:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: رَسُولٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ يَتْلُوْۤا صُحُفًا مُطَهَّرَةً rasūlun mina l-lahi yatlū ṣuḥufan muṭahharatan an apostle from Allah reciting impeccable scriptures,

item.title: Al-Bayyina:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: رَسُولٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ يَتْلُوْۤا صُحُفًا مُطَهَّرَةً rasūlun mina l-lahi yatlū ṣuḥufan muṭahharatan A Messenger from Allah, reciting purified1 scriptures. See 98:1

item.title: Al-Bayyina:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: رَسُولٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ يَتْلُوْۤا صُحُفًا مُطَهَّرَةً rasūlun mina l-lahi yatlū ṣuḥufan muṭahharatan (In the) Apostle from God reciting (unto them) the Purified Scripture ('Suhof' plural of Sahf, i.e. page - Lit. Pages - See note.) The Holy Prophet was none else but the Apostle from God and what he recited, the Holy Qur'an, was not any collection of ancient tales or anything of the creation of his own mind but it was the Truth, the original Word of God in its purity without any corruption having polluted it1. 'Sahof' plural of 'Safh' literally mean pages - but Qur'an used this term for the collection of the divine revelation2 and the term 'Mushaf' was used for the complete collection of the Holy Qur'an. (A.P.).

item.title: Al-Bayyina:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيهَا كُتُبٌ قَيِّمَةٌ fīhā kutubun qayyimatun wherein are upright writings.

item.title: Al-Bayyina:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيهَا كُتُبٌ قَيِّمَةٌ fīhā kutubun qayyimatun Within which are correct writings (i.e., rulings and laws). See 98:1

item.title: Al-Bayyina:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيهَا كُتُبٌ قَيِّمَةٌ fīhā kutubun qayyimatun Wherein are the decrees (correct and) strong What is contained in the Holy Qur'an is exactly the Word of God relating to His ordinance, meant for the human race. It (the Holy Qur'an) contains all the good or the truth mentioned in the previous scriptures with the necessary regulations to serve the purpose of its being the final code for a universal religion for the human race as a whole for all times. 'Qaiyyim' - Straight - Strong - Confirmed - Standardised - Definite and Permanent1. When the truth was revealed through the Holy Qur'an the disbelievers got themselves divided in two groups, one accepting Islam and the other rejecting it.

item.title: Al-Bayyina:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا تَفَرَّقَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوْۤا الْكِتَابَ إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَتْهُمُ الْبَيِّنَةُ wamā tafarraqa alladhīna ūtū l-kitāba illā min baʿdi mā jāathumu l-bayinatu And those who were given the Book did not divide, except after the proof had come to them.

item.title: Al-Bayyina:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا تَفَرَّقَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوْۤا الْكِتَابَ إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَتْهُمُ الْبَيِّنَةُ wamā tafarraqa alladhīna ūtū l-kitāba illā min baʿdi mā jāathumu l-bayinatu Nor did those who were given the Scripture become divided1 until after there had come to them clear evidence. See 98:1

item.title: Al-Bayyina:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا تَفَرَّقَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوْۤا الْكِتَابَ إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَتْهُمُ الْبَيِّنَةُ wamā tafarraqa alladhīna ūtū l-kitāba illā min baʿdi mā jāathumu l-bayinatu Nor were divided those who were given the Book but after had come unto them the Clear Evidence (Refer to: 3:19, 4:163 - 4:165.) See 98:3

item.title: Al-Bayyina:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أُمِرُوْۤا إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ حُنَفَاءَ وَيُقِيمُوْۤا الصَّلاةَ وَيُؤْتُوْۤا الزَّكَاةَ وَذٰلِكَ دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ wamā umirū illā liyaʿbudū l-laha mukh'liṣīna lahu l-dīna ḥunafāa wayuqīmū l-ṣalata wayu'tū l-zakata wadhālika dīnu l-qayimati Yet they were not commanded except to worship Allah, dedicating their faith to Him as men of pure faith, and to maintain the prayer and pay the zakāt. That is the upright religion.

item.title: Al-Bayyina:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أُمِرُوْۤا إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ حُنَفَاءَ وَيُقِيمُوْۤا الصَّلاةَ وَيُؤْتُوْۤا الزَّكَاةَ وَذٰلِكَ دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ wamā umirū illā liyaʿbudū l-laha mukh'liṣīna lahu l-dīna ḥunafāa wayuqīmū l-ṣalata wayu'tū l-zakata wadhālika dīnu l-qayimati And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, (being) sincere to Him in religion, inclining to truth, and to establish prayer and to give zakāh. And that is the correct religion. See 98:1

item.title: Al-Bayyina:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أُمِرُوْۤا إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ حُنَفَاءَ وَيُقِيمُوْۤا الصَّلاةَ وَيُؤْتُوْۤا الزَّكَاةَ وَذٰلِكَ دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ wamā umirū illā liyaʿbudū l-laha mukh'liṣīna lahu l-dīna ḥunafāa wayuqīmū l-ṣalata wayu'tū l-zakata wadhālika dīnu l-qayimati Yet Was not enjoined on them but that they should worship God (alone) in perfect sincerity, in religion (only) unto Him, and that they give away the poor-rate, and that (Submission to God and service to mankind is the Standing Religion Refer to: 25:30 - 25:33.) , is the religion (correct and) strong In the scriptures given to Moses and Jesus the Jews and the Christians were ordained only to worship the Only God exclusively to have their faith only in Him and none else - as 'Hanifs', i.e., as those devoted exclusively, to none but the One God1. 'Deen al-Qaiyyim' the Right Religion. The passage may mean…

item.title: Al-Bayyina:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا اُولٰٓئِكَ هُمْ شَرُّ الْبَرِيَّةِ inna alladhīna kafarū min ahli l-kitābi wal-mush'rikīna fī nāri jahannama khālidīna fīhā ulāika hum sharru l-bariyati Indeed the faithless from among the People of the Book and the polytheists will be in the fire of hell, to remain in it [forever]. It is they who are the worst of creatures.

item.title: Al-Bayyina:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا اُولٰٓئِكَ هُمْ شَرُّ الْبَرِيَّةِ inna alladhīna kafarū min ahli l-kitābi wal-mush'rikīna fī nāri jahannama khālidīna fīhā ulāika hum sharru l-bariyati Indeed, they who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein. Those are the worst of creatures. Verily, those who disbelieve from among the People of the Scripture and idolators, will abide in the fire of Hell. They are the worst of creatures (98:6). Verily, those who believe and do righteous good deeds, they are the best of creatures (98:7). Their reward with their Lord is Eternal Gardens, underneath which rivers flow. They will abide therein forever, Allah will be pleased with them, and they well-pleased with Him. That is for him who fears his Lord…

item.title: Al-Bayyina:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا اُولٰٓئِكَ هُمْ شَرُّ الْبَرِيَّةِ inna alladhīna kafarū min ahli l-kitābi wal-mush'rikīna fī nāri jahannama khālidīna fīhā ulāika hum sharru l-bariyati Verily, those who disbelieve from among the people of the Book and the polytheists shall be in the fire of hell, to abide therein. And it is they who are the worst of creatures Those who disbelieve in their Creator Lord their true Benefactor and refuse to worship Him and believe in false deities and worship them and are devoted to falsehood rejecting the truth, are certainly the worst of the creatures.

item.title: Al-Bayyina:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا وَعَمِلُوْۤا الصَّالِحَاتِ اُولٰٓئِكَ هُمْ خَيْرُ الْبَرِيَّةِ inna alladhīna āmanū waʿamilū l-ṣāliḥāti ulāika hum khayru l-bariyati Indeed those who have faith and do righteous deeds —it is they who are the best of creatures.

item.title: Al-Bayyina:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا وَعَمِلُوْۤا الصَّالِحَاتِ اُولٰٓئِكَ هُمْ خَيْرُ الْبَرِيَّةِ inna alladhīna āmanū waʿamilū l-ṣāliḥāti ulāika hum khayru l-bariyati Indeed, they who have believed and done righteous deeds - those are the best of creatures. See 98:6

item.title: Al-Bayyina:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا وَعَمِلُوْۤا الصَّالِحَاتِ اُولٰٓئِكَ هُمْ خَيْرُ الْبَرِيَّةِ inna alladhīna āmanū waʿamilū l-ṣāliḥāti ulāika hum khayru l-bariyati Verily, those who believe and do good deeds, it is they who are the best of creatures Ibn Abbas says by the term 'Khairal Bariyya' is meant Ali Ibn Abu Talib and the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt. Hafiz Abu-Nayeem Isphahani in his book Holyat al-Aulia reports on the authority of Ibn-Abbas that the Holy Prophet said ''O' Ali, Thou and thy Shias (devotees') will be in the heaven" (MS.) It is narrated by Haskani in his work 'Thawahidut Tanzeel' - from Yazeed Ibn Sharaheel al- Ansari - Ali Askarani - from Ali - that the Holy Prophet told him at the time of his departure when, his head was lying on my breast quoting this verse and said: ''Khair al-Bariyya' ''are thy Shias…

item.title: Al-Bayyina:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: جَزَاؤُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوْۤا عَنْهُ ذٰلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِيَ رَبَّهُ jazāuhum ʿinda rabbihim jannātu ʿadnin tajrī min taḥtihā l-anhāru khālidīna fīhā abadan raḍiya l-lahu ʿanhum waraḍū ʿanhu dhālika liman khashiya rabbahu Their reward, near their Lord, is the Gardens of Eden, with streams running in them, to remain in them forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. That is for those who fear their Lord.

item.title: Al-Bayyina:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: جَزَاؤُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوْۤا عَنْهُ ذٰلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِيَ رَبَّهُ jazāuhum ʿinda rabbihim jannātu ʿadnin tajrī min taḥtihā l-anhāru khālidīna fīhā abadan raḍiya l-lahu ʿanhum waraḍū ʿanhu dhālika liman khashiya rabbahu Their reward with their Lord will be gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever, Allah being pleased with them and they with Him. That is for whoever has feared his Lord. See 98:6

item.title: Al-Bayyina:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: جَزَاؤُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوْۤا عَنْهُ ذٰلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِيَ رَبَّهُ jazāuhum ʿinda rabbihim jannātu ʿadnin tajrī min taḥtihā l-anhāru khālidīna fīhā abadan raḍiya l-lahu ʿanhum waraḍū ʿanhu dhālika liman khashiya rabbahu Their recompense (Not restricted to any class of the believers of any particular age. (A.P.).) unto their Lord shall be gardens everlasting, 'neath which flow rivers, to abide therein for ever. Well pleased is God with them and they are well-pleased with Him; That is for him who feareth his Lord The great quality mentioned to be of those who would be pleased with God and God being pleased with them, could be found only in those who would have led the life of perfect faith in God and complete submission to His will and there could be…

item.title: Al-Burooj:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالسَّمَاءِ ذَاتِ الْبُرُوجِ wal-samāi dhāti l-burūji By the sky with its houses,

item.title: Al-Burooj:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالسَّمَاءِ ذَاتِ الْبُرُوجِ wal-samāi dhāti l-burūji By the sky containing great stars. إِنَّ الَّذِينَ فَتَنُوا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ Verily, those who put into trial the believing men and believing women, Meaning: they burned (them). This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, and Ibn Abza. ثُمَّ لَمْ يَتُوبُوا and then do not turn in repentance, Meaning: 'they do not cease from what they are doing, and do not regret what they had done before.' فَلَهُمْ عَذَابُ جَهَنَّمَ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابُ الْحَرِيقِ then they will have the torment of Hell, and they will have the punishment of the burning Fire. This is because the recompense is based upon the type of deed performed. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said, "Look at this generosity and kindness. These people killed Allah's Awliya' and He still invites them to make repentance and seek forgiveness."

item.title: Al-Burooj:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالسَّمَاءِ ذَاتِ الْبُرُوجِ wal-samāi dhāti l-burūji By the heaven full of Constellations (Zodiac. Refer to: 15:16.) ! 'Buruj' the twelve celestial stations through which the celestial bodies, the planets annually pass through - 'Buruj' are also interpreted as the Big Stars1. The twelve stations of the system of the constellations indicated by the following Zodiac signs are: - Hand - (Ram) - Aries. Thaur - (Bull) - Taurus. Jauz - (Twins) - Gemini. Sarihan - (Crab) – Cancer Asad - (Lion) – Leo Sumbula - (Virgin) – Virgo Meezan - (Balance) – Libra Aqrab - (Scorpion) – Scorpio Qaus - (Archer) – Sagittarius Jadi - (Goat) – Capricornus Dalv - (Water-bearer) – Aquarius Hooth - (Fishes) - Pisces. 'Buruj' is since been used for Zodiac signs or Constellations. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Burooj:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْيَوْمِ الْمَوْعُودِ wal-yawmi l-mawʿūdi by the Promised Day,

item.title: Al-Burooj:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْيَوْمِ الْمَوْعُودِ wal-yawmi l-mawʿūdi And (by) the promised Day. See 85:1

item.title: Al-Burooj:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْيَوْمِ الْمَوْعُودِ wal-yawmi l-mawʿūdi By the Day (Of judgment.) promised! The Day of the Final Judgment which every man is warned of - to be mindful of the inevitable requital in the ultimate even if respite is given for the whole of this life.

item.title: Al-Burooj:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَشَاهِدٍ وَمَشْهُودٍ washāhidin wamashhūdin by the Witness1 and the Witnessed:2

item.title: Al-Burooj:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَشَاهِدٍ وَمَشْهُودٍ washāhidin wamashhūdin And (by) the witness and what is witnessed. See 85:1

item.title: Al-Burooj:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَشَاهِدٍ وَمَشْهُودٍ washāhidin wamashhūdin By the witness and the witnessed! The terms are very comprehensive - Taking the meanings in terms of the legal proceedings of the administrating of justice of the Day of Judgment, the following are the position interpretations. For 'Shahid' the witness - the following can be meant: - God Himself - See 3:81, 10:61. The Apostles of God - See 31:81. The Recording Angels - See 50:21. The Limbs or the sinners - See 24:24. The Records of deeds - See 7:14. The Sinner himself - See 7:14. The subject witnessed may be: The deed or the crime. The sinner against whom the witness gives the evidence. The verse means that no sinner can ever possibly escape the consequence of the sins commit-ted by him. He must avail of the respite and immediately repent and amend…

item.title: Al-Burooj:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُتِلَ أَصْحَابُ الْأُخْدُودِ qutila aṣḥābu l-ukh'dūdi perish the Men of the Ditch!

item.title: Al-Burooj:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُتِلَ أَصْحَابُ الْأُخْدُودِ qutila aṣḥābu l-ukh'dūdi Destroyed (i.e., cursed) were the companions of the trench.1 See 85:1

item.title: Al-Burooj:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُتِلَ أَصْحَابُ الْأُخْدُودِ qutila aṣḥābu l-ukh'dūdi That (Self) destroyed were the fellows of the ditch The wording of this verse seems to refer to the conduct of some particular people. A commentator takes it to be of an illustration of general application. It is no doubt a fact that in ancient history of the world, particularly the Medieval Europe, people who did not conform to the religion of the people in power, were mercilessly sacrificed at the stake. There is the reference to Nimrod's treatment to Abraham1. There is the history of catholic Christendom enacting the Edict of Milan which victimised numberless Jewish men, women old and young and even innocent children. There is the case of Zu-Nawas the last Himyarite king of Yamen, a Jew by religion, mercilessly persecuting the Christians of Najran burning them at the stake. This…

item.title: Al-Burooj:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلنَّارِ ذَاتِ الْوَقُودِ al-nāri dhāti l-waqūdi The fire, abounding in fuel,

item.title: Al-Burooj:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلنَّارِ ذَاتِ الْوَقُودِ al-nāri dhāti l-waqūdi (Containing) the fire full of fuel. See 85:1

item.title: Al-Burooj:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلنَّارِ ذَاتِ الْوَقُودِ al-nāri dhāti l-waqūdi Of the fire with fuel See 85:4

item.title: Al-Burooj:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ هُمْ عَلَيْهَا قُعُودٌ idh hum ʿalayhā quʿūdun above which they sat

item.title: Al-Burooj:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ هُمْ عَلَيْهَا قُعُودٌ idh hum ʿalayhā quʿūdun When they were sitting near it. See 85:1

item.title: Al-Burooj:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ هُمْ عَلَيْهَا قُعُودٌ idh hum ʿalayhā quʿūdun When facing it sat they See 85:4

item.title: Al-Burooj:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهُمْ عَلَى مَا يَفْعَلُونَ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ شُهُودٌ wahum ʿalā mā yafʿalūna bil-mu'minīna shuhūdun as they were themselves witnesses to what they did to the faithful.

item.title: Al-Burooj:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهُمْ عَلَى مَا يَفْعَلُونَ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ شُهُودٌ wahum ʿalā mā yafʿalūna bil-mu'minīna shuhūdun And they, to what they were doing against the believers, were witnesses.1 See 85:1

item.title: Al-Burooj:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهُمْ عَلَى مَا يَفْعَلُونَ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ شُهُودٌ wahum ʿalā mā yafʿalūna bil-mu'minīna shuhūdun While they witnessed what they did unto the believers See 85:4

item.title: Al-Burooj:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا نَقَمُوْۤا مِنْهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوْۤا بِاللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ wamā naqamū min'hum illā an yu'minū bil-lahi l-ʿazīzi l-ḥamīdi They were vindictive towards them only because they had faith in Allah, the All-mighty, the All-laudable,

item.title: Al-Burooj:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا نَقَمُوْۤا مِنْهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوْۤا بِاللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ wamā naqamū min'hum illā an yu'minū bil-lahi l-ʿazīzi l-ḥamīdi And they resented them not except because they believed in Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy. See 85:1

item.title: Al-Burooj:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا نَقَمُوْۤا مِنْهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوْۤا بِاللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ wamā naqamū min'hum illā an yu'minū bil-lahi l-ʿazīzi l-ḥamīdi They (The disbelievers.) tormented (them) for naught but that they (The believers.) believe in God, the Ever-Prevalent, the Most Praised See 85:4

item.title: Al-Burooj:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ alladhī lahu mul'ku l-samāwāti wal-arḍi wal-lahu ʿalā kulli shayin shahīdun to whom belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is witness to all things.

item.title: Al-Burooj:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ alladhī lahu mul'ku l-samāwāti wal-arḍi wal-lahu ʿalā kulli shayin shahīdun To whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And Allah, over all things, is Witness.1 See 85:1

item.title: Al-Burooj:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ alladhī lahu mul'ku l-samāwāti wal-arḍi wal-lahu ʿalā kulli shayin shahīdun He, unto Whom belongeth the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth; and God is, over all things, a Witness See 85:4

item.title: Al-Burooj:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ فَتَنُوْۤا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَتُوبُوْۤا فَلَهُمْ عَذَابُ جَهَنَّمَ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابُ الْحَرِيقِ inna alladhīna fatanū l-mu'minīna wal-mu'mināti thumma lam yatūbū falahum ʿadhābu jahannama walahum ʿadhābu l-ḥarīqi Indeed those who persecute the faithful men and women, and then do not repent, for them there is the punishment of hell, and for them there is the punishment of burning.

item.title: Al-Burooj:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ فَتَنُوْۤا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَتُوبُوْۤا فَلَهُمْ عَذَابُ جَهَنَّمَ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابُ الْحَرِيقِ inna alladhīna fatanū l-mu'minīna wal-mu'mināti thumma lam yatūbū falahum ʿadhābu jahannama walahum ʿadhābu l-ḥarīqi Indeed, those who have tortured1 the believing men and believing women and then have not repented will have the punishment of Hell, and they will have the punishment of the Burning Fire. See 85:1

item.title: Al-Burooj:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ فَتَنُوْۤا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَتُوبُوْۤا فَلَهُمْ عَذَابُ جَهَنَّمَ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابُ الْحَرِيقِ inna alladhīna fatanū l-mu'minīna wal-mu'mināti thumma lam yatūbū falahum ʿadhābu jahannama walahum ʿadhābu l-ḥarīqi Verily, those who persecute the believer men and the believer women, and yet they repent not, for them shall be the chastisement of the hell and for them is a burning torture See 85:4

item.title: Al-Burooj:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا وَعَمِلُوْۤا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ ذٰلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْكَبِيرُ inna alladhīna āmanū waʿamilū l-ṣāliḥāti lahum jannātun tajrī min taḥtihā l-anhāru dhālika l-fawzu l-kabīru Indeed those who have faith and do righteous deeds, —for them will be gardens with streams running in them. That is the supreme success.

item.title: Al-Burooj:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا وَعَمِلُوْۤا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ ذٰلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْكَبِيرُ inna alladhīna āmanū waʿamilū l-ṣāliḥāti lahum jannātun tajrī min taḥtihā l-anhāru dhālika l-fawzu l-kabīru Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds will have gardens beneath which rivers flow. That is the great attainment. Verily, those who believe and do righteous good deeds, for them will be Gardens under which rivers flow. That is the supreme success (85:11). Verily, the punishment of your Lord is severe and painful (85:12). Verily, He it is Who begins and repeats (85:13). And He is Oft-Forgiving, Al-Wadud (85:14). Owner of the Throne, Al-Majid (the Glorious) (85:15). Doer of what He intends (85:16). Has the story reached you of the hosts (85:17). Of Fir'awn and Thamud (85:18). Nay! The disbelievers (persisted) in denying (85:19). And Allah encompasses them from behind…

item.title: Al-Burooj:21 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ هُوَ قُرْءَانٌ مَجِيدٌ bal huwa qur'ānun majīdun Nay! It is Qur'an the Glorious (Refer to: 56:77 - 56:79.) This verse condemning the disbelievers who belie the divine origin of Qur'an. It asserts that it is the glorious Qur'an, the original of it is in the Well-Guarded Tablet which has 56:78 as 'Kitab al-Maknoon', i.e., the Hidden Book which in 13:39 have been termed as the 'Ummul Kitab', i.e., the Mother Book and that is which is not within the reach of anyone save those who are purified by God 33:33 vide 56:79 and this is what is termed as 'Illiyoon' - in 83:19 - 83:22. (A.P.)

item.description: فِي لَوْحٍ مَحْفُوظٍ fī lawḥin maḥfūẓin (Inscribed) in a Preserved Slate. See 85:11

item.title: Al-Burooj:22 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي لَوْحٍ مَحْفُوظٍ fī lawḥin maḥfūẓin (Inscribed) in the 'Lauh al- Mahfuz' (the Guarded Tablet) Tablets1 mentioned are not of any material of this world. The tablets are only a figurative expression to mean that the Holy Qur'an is the Final Word from the Lord which is fully guarded and preserved in the heavens. Even the Qur'an on earth is a Book protected, God Himself having taken the responsibility of guarding or protecting it from being made extinct or getting corrupted in its form or meaning by any wicked hands. Before departing from this world, the Holy Prophet declared that: ''I leave behind me Two important things, The Book of God, i.e., the Holy Qur'an and my Ahl Al-Bayt. If ye be attached to these Two, ye will never get astray, for these Two will never be separated from each…

item.description: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ bis'mi l-lahi l-raḥmāni l-raḥīmi In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful.

item.title: Al-Faatiha:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ bis'mi l-lahi l-raḥmāni l-raḥīmi In the name of Allah,1 the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.2 بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَـنِ الرَّحِيمِ In the Name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful whether in the beginning or the end of the recitation. Similar is recorded in the Sunan books from 'Abdullah bin Mughaffal (RA). These are the opinions held by the respected Imams, and their statements are similar in that they agree that the prayer of those who recite Al-Fatihah aloud or in secret is correct. All the favor is from Allah. The Virtue of Al-Fatihah Imam Ahmad recorded in his Musnad, that a person who was riding behind the Prophet SAW said, The Prophet's animal tripped, so I said, 'Cursed Shaytan.' The Prophet said: لَا تَقُلْ: تَعِسَ الشَّيْطَانُ، فَإِنَّكَ إِذَا قُلْتَ: تَعِسَ الشَّيْطَانُ، تَعَاظَمَ وَقَالَ: بِقُوَّتِي صَرَعْتُهُ،…

item.title: Al-Faatiha:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ bis'mi l-lahi l-raḥmāni l-raḥīmi In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful Bismi-Llah' The words of 'Bismi-Llah' i.e. in the name of God, have wide and comprehending implications. The words may mean not only 'in the name of' but also: For the sake of To the service of These and the many other implications will go only to invoke the Mercy of God for the supplicant who so sincerely resorts to Him to be blessed. It is our common experience that when a mother beats her child, while punishing him to correct his conduct, the child even while being beaten, rushes towards the bosom of his mother. Why? Is it not because the young human soul is sure, and in his own heart is convinced of his mother's love and her being full of mercy…

item.description: اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ al-ḥamdu lillahi rabbi l-ʿālamīna All praise belongs to Allah,1 Lord of all the worlds,

item.title: Al-Faatiha:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ al-ḥamdu lillahi rabbi l-ʿālamīna (All) praise is (due) to Allah, Lord1 of the worlds. The Meaning of Al-Hamd Abu Ja'far bin Jarir said, "The meaning of الْحَمْدُ للَّهِ (Al-Hamdu Lillah) (all praise and thanks be to Allah) is: all thanks are due purely to Allah, alone, not any of the objects that are being worshipped instead of Him, nor any of His creation. These thanks are due to Allah's innumerable favors and bounties, that only He knows the amount of. Allah's bounties include creating the tools that help the creation worship Him, the physical bodies with which they are able to implement His commands, the sustenance that He provides them in this life, and the comfortable life He has granted them, without anything or anyone compelling Him to do so. Allah also warned His creation and…

item.title: Al-Faatiha:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ al-ḥamdu lillahi rabbi l-ʿālamīna (all) praise is (only) God's, the of the worlds Allah The word Allah is the pointing towards of something which is already in the mind or the realisation of everyone beyond any concept or definition, and not limited or arrested by the concept of any. Thus, it is universal and hence it is All-Merciful since it is universally connected with the whole as well as with the part. Therefore, the controversy among the commentators as to whether the word Allah is a proper noun or a common noun with the article 'al', can be reconciled in this way that 'ilah.' as common noun assumes definite sense with the definite article, which refers to something universally known and realised by every conscious being and that known being not confined to any form or…

item.title: Al-Faatiha:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ al-raḥmāni l-raḥīmi the All-beneficent, the All-merciful,

item.title: Al-Faatiha:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ al-raḥmāni l-raḥīmi The Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Allah said next: الرَّحْمَـنِ الرَّحِيمِ Ar-Rahman (the Most Gracious), Ar-Rahim (the Most Merciful) We explained these Names in the Basmalah. Al-Qurtubi said, Allah has described Himself by 'Ar-Rahman, Ar-Rahim' after saying 'the Lord of the Alamin', so His statement here includes a warning, and then an encouragement. Similarly, Allah said: نَبِّىءْ عِبَادِى أَنِّى أَنَا الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ - وَأَنَّ عَذَابِى هُوَ ٱلْعَذَابُ ٱلْأَلِيمُ Declare (O Muhammad SAW) unto My servants, that truly, I am the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful. And that My torment is indeed the most painful torment. (15:49-50) Allah said: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ سَرِيعُ الْعِقَابِ وَإِنَّهُ لَغَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ Surely, your Lord is swift in retribution, and certainly He is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful. (6:165) Hence, Rabb contains a warning while Ar-Rahman Ar-Rahim encourages. Further, Muslim recorded in his Sahih that the…

item.title: Al-Faatiha:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ al-raḥmāni l-raḥīmi The Beneficent, The Merciful Ar-Rahman, Ar-Rahim 'Rahman' and 'Rahim': The words, 'Rahman' and 'Rahim' both point out to the one and the same essence of the Divine Attribute, 'Rahmat' meaning Mercy. The two words though relate only to one and the same prime attribute of God, give the two different aspects of the Divine Mercy. Mercy unreserved shown to one and all of His creatures, be they obedient or disobedient to their Lord, is known as 'Rahmaniat' and Mercy done specially to those faithful to their Lord, as a reward or in appreciation of the goodness of the souls, is called 'Rahimiat.' (A.P.) 'Rahmat' i.e. Grace, which is the root of both the words 'Rahman' and 'Rahim' is the most comprehensive attribute implied in the name of Allah as here stated before. This attribute stands as…

item.title: Al-Faatiha:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ māliki yawmi l-dīni Master1 of the Day of Retribution.

item.title: Al-Faatiha:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ māliki yawmi l-dīni Sovereign of the Day of Recompense.1 Indicating Sovereignty on the Day of Judgment Allah mentioned His sovereignty of the Day of Resurrection, but this does not negate His sovereignty over all other things. For Allah mentioned that He is the Lord of existence, including this earthly life and the Hereafter. Allah only mentioned the Day of Recompense here because on that Day, no one except Him will be able to claim ownership of anything whatsoever. On that Day, no one will be allowed to speak without His permission. Similarly, Allah said: يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الرُّوحُ وَالْمَلَـئِكَةُ صَفّاً لاَّ يَتَكَلَّمُونَ إِلاَّ مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ الرَّحْمَـنُ وَقَالَ صَوَاباً The Day that Ar-Ruh (Jibril or another angel) and the angels will stand forth in rows, they will not speak except him whom the Most Gracious (Allah) allows, and…

item.title: Al-Faatiha:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ māliki yawmi l-dīni Master of the Day of Judgement Maliki Yawm Ad-Din Maliki Yawm ad-Din: Maliki can mean Master or the Lord or the King of the 'Yawm Ad-Din' the Day of Faith. The Day is the Day of the Final Judgment, but it is termed in the Qur'anic language as the Day of Faith. Firstly, the word 'Malik' meaning the Master or the Lord or the King, is used. He who sits at any judgment is commonly known and also called a judge and the Arabic word for it is 'Qazi' but the word 'Qazi' is not used, but the word used is 'Malik'. The subtle point to understand here is that a 'Qazi' is not the Lawmaker or the Lawgiver but only an executor of the law, made and enforced by some other authority, and…

item.title: Al-Faatiha:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ iyyāka naʿbudu wa-iyyāka nastaʿīnu You [alone] do we worship, and to You [alone] do we turn for help.

item.title: Al-Faatiha:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ iyyāka naʿbudu wa-iyyāka nastaʿīnu It is You we worship and You we ask for help. The Linguistic and Religious Meaning of 'Ibadah Linguistically, 'Ibadah means subdued. For instance, a road is described as Mu'abbadah, meaning, 'paved'. In religious terminology, 'Ibadah implies the utmost love, humility and fear. The Merit of Stating the Object of the Action before the Doer of the Act, and the Merit of these Negations "You...", means, we worship You alone and none else, and rely on You alone and none else. This is the perfect form of obedience and the entire religion is implied by these two ideas. Some of the Salaf said, Al-Fatihah is the secret of the Qur'an, while these words are the secret of Al-Fatihah: إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ 5 You we worship, and You we ask for help…

item.title: Al-Faatiha:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ iyyāka naʿbudu wa-iyyāka nastaʿīnu Thee (alone) worship we and of Thee (only) we seek help Iyyaka Iyyaka i.e. None else but Thee All creatures be they of the highest or the lowest order, commissioned by God with any authority or not, are alike in being subservient to His Will, in obedience and worship to Him and in seeking His help in their activities. None is left to be out of His servitude as His partner. God's relation to all, is the relation of the Absolute Creator and the Supreme Law - giver, and their relation to Him is the relation of the created being and the Law - abiders. Hence there is no room left for the deification of any finite being and there is no room for 'Ta'addud' i.e. the numeration of the Infinite. Thus,…

item.description: اِهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ ih'dinā l-ṣirāṭa l-mus'taqīma Guide us on the straight path,

item.title: Al-Faatiha:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اِهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ ih'dinā l-ṣirāṭa l-mus'taqīma Guide us to the straight path. The Meaning of Guidance Mentioned in the Surah The guidance mentioned in the Surah implies being directed and guided to success. Allah said: اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ Guide us to the straight path meaning guide, direct, lead and grant us the correct guidance. Also: وَهَدَيْنَـهُ النَّجْدَينِ And shown him the two ways (good and evil) (90:10) Means, 'We explained to him the paths of good and evil.' Also, Allah said: اجْتَبَـهُ وَهَدَاهُ إِلَى صِرَطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ He (Allah) chose him (as an intimate friend) and guided him to a straight path (16:121) And: فَاهْدُوهُمْ إِلَى صِرَطِ الْجَحِيمِ And lead them on to the way of flaming Fire (Hell) (37:23) Similarly, Allah said: وَإِنَّكَ لَتَهْدِى إِلَى صِرَطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ And verily, you (O Muhammad ) are indeed guiding (mankind) to the straight…

item.title: Al-Faatiha:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اِهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ ih'dinā l-ṣirāṭa l-mus'taqīma Guide us (O' Lord) on the right path Ihdina As-Sirat Al-Mustaqeem The phrase literally means 'Guide us to the right path' or 'show us the right way'. The word 'Ihdina' i.e. guide, or show is of the widest application. Even a true believer in the truth, however learned and wise he may be, has to necessarily pray for this blessing from the All-Merciful, the All-Knowing and the All-Wise Lord. Guidance which man needs, is not restricted to the knowledge or the practice of any doctrine. Man has to be ever seeking the knowledge of the higher truths leading to the higher spiritual elevations open to his personal progress. The straight or the Right Path, used in this verse does not confine itself to mean only doctrines of the religion. The path mentioned in this…

item.title: Al-Faatiha:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: صِرَاطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ ṣirāṭa alladhīna anʿamta ʿalayhim ghayri l-maghḍūbi ʿalayhim walā l-ḍālīna the path of those whom You have blessed1 —such as2 have not incurred Your wrath,3 nor are astray.4

item.title: Al-Faatiha:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: صِرَاطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ ṣirāṭa alladhīna anʿamta ʿalayhim ghayri l-maghḍūbi ʿalayhim walā l-ḍālīna The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, not of those who have earned (Your) anger or of those who are astray. We mentioned the Hadith in which the servant proclaims: اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ Guide us to the straight way and Allah says, "This is for My servant, and My servant shall acquire what he asks for." Allah's statement. صِرَاطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ The way of those upon whom You have bestowed Your grace defines the path. 'Those upon whom Allah has bestowed His grace' are those mentioned in Surat An-Nisa' (chapter 4), when Allah said: وَمَن يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ فَأُوْلَـئِكَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِم مِّنَ النَّبِيِّينَ وَالصِّدِّيقِينَ وَالشُّهَدَآءِ وَالصَّـلِحِينَ وَحَسُنَ أُولَـئِكَ رَفِيقاً - ذلِكَ الْفَضْلُ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَكَفَى…

item.title: Al-Faatiha:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: صِرَاطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ ṣirāṭa alladhīna anʿamta ʿalayhim ghayri l-maghḍūbi ʿalayhim walā l-ḍālīna The path of those upon whom Thou hast bestowed Thy bounties, not (the path) of those inflicted with Thy wrath, nor (of those) gone astray Sirat Alladhina An'amta Alayhim Sirat alladhina means the path of those and An'amta alayhim means on whom thou ('O' Our Lord!) has bestowed thy bounties. This verse explains and determines the right guidance which man needs and for which he must pray. Otherwise, by merely saying guide me aright on the Straight or the Right Path is indefinite, for every path which the fancy of anyone chooses, will naturally deem it to be straight and God does not send angels to everyone to guide him. When God Himself, through His last revealed Book, the Qur'an, teaches man…

item.title: Al-Fajr:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْفَجْرِ wal-fajri By the Dawn,1

item.title: Al-Fajr:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْفَجْرِ wal-fajri By the dawn. إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِالْمِرْصَادِ Verily, your Lord is Ever Watchful. Ibn 'Abbas said, "He hears and He sees." This means that He watches over His creation in that which they do, and He will reward them in this life and in the Hereafter based upon what each of them strove for. He will bring all of the creation before Him and He will judge them with justice. He will requit each of them with that which he deserves, for He is far removed from injustice and tyranny.

item.title: Al-Fajr:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْفَجْرِ wal-fajri By the Daybreak There are many interpretations of this mystic swearing in the Holy Qur'an and one of them is that the day break referred to here in this verse and the Ten Nights are the First Ten Days and the lunar month of Zul Hajjah, the Twelfth month of the lunar year, preceding the pilgrimage. The Holy Prophet said that fasting, feeding the poor, and the similar other deeds of righteousness during those days earn a special grace and reward from God. Some commentators say the reference could also be to the First Ten nights of the month of Muharram in which is the great eventful day of 'Ashoora'. Once it was reported to the Holy Prophet that a young man fasts during the first ten days of Zul Hajjah. The Holy Prophet sent for the young…

item.title: Al-Fajr:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَيَالٍ عَشْرٍ walayālin ʿashrin by the ten nights,

item.title: Al-Fajr:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَيَالٍ عَشْرٍ walayālin ʿashrin And (by) ten nights.1 See 89:1

item.title: Al-Fajr:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَيَالٍ عَشْرٍ walayālin ʿashrin And (by) the Ten Nights See 89:1

item.title: Al-Fajr:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالشَّفْعِ وَالْوَتْرِ wal-shafʿi wal-watri by the Even and the Odd,

item.title: Al-Fajr:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالشَّفْعِ وَالْوَتْرِ wal-shafʿi wal-watri And (by) the even (number) and the odd. See 89:1

item.title: Al-Fajr:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالشَّفْعِ وَالْوَتْرِ wal-shafʿi wal-watri And (by) the even and the odd This is another mystic expression. It may mean all things, for in them are the even and odd ones, or it may mean the opposites in sexes and energies and the other qualities in men, material and the natural phenomena active in the universe.

item.title: Al-Fajr:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَسْرِ wa-al-layli idhā yasri by the night when it departs!

item.title: Al-Fajr:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَسْرِ wa-al-layli idhā yasri And (by) the night when it passes. See 89:1

item.title: Al-Fajr:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَسْرِ wa-al-layli idhā yasri And (by) the Night as it passeth away The state invites attention to the great change in the effect of the daily functioning of the heavenly bodies, brought on earth regularly in a system ordained by the Almighty Creator lord of the Universe.

item.title: Al-Fajr:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: هَلْ فِي ذٰلِكَ قَسَمٌ لِذِي حِجْرٍ hal fī dhālika qasamun lidhī ḥij'rin Is there an oath in that for one possessing intellect?

item.title: Al-Fajr:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: هَلْ فِي ذٰلِكَ قَسَمٌ لِذِي حِجْرٍ hal fī dhālika qasamun lidhī ḥij'rin Is there (not) in (all) that an oath (sufficient) for one of perception?1 See 89:1

item.title: Al-Fajr:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: هَلْ فِي ذٰلِكَ قَسَمٌ لِذِي حِجْرٍ hal fī dhālika qasamun lidhī ḥij'rin Verily there is in this an oath for those who possess understanding This verse clearly indicates that the above expressions are purely mystic for the deeper consideration of those endowed with higher intellect, to know the secrets treasured in them and hold them for the proper use by them in their endeavour for spiritual progress. 'Hal' here stands for assertion, similar to Surah 76. 'Higr' controlling power - relating to that aspect of intellect which prevents man from wishful and fanciful thinking. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Fajr:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعَادٍ alam tara kayfa faʿala rabbuka biʿādin Have you not regarded how your Lord dealt with [the people of] 'Ād,

item.title: Al-Fajr:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعَادٍ alam tara kayfa faʿala rabbuka biʿādin Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with ʿAad. See 89:1

item.title: Al-Fajr:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعَادٍ alam tara kayfa faʿala rabbuka biʿādin Hast not thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) seen how did deal thy Lord with the (people) 'Ad' (Refer to: 7:65, 53:50, 38:12, 46:21.) ? This is a reference to what befell the people 'Ad of the city Iram, who were the people of the Arab antiquity the 'Ad and Thamood, they were powerful but rebelled against God's laws and were persistent in their arrogance and godlessness. The people were of tall stature and were proud of their strength and power1.

item.title: Al-Fajr:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِرَمَ ذَاتِ الْعِمَادِ irama dhāti l-ʿimādi [and] Iram, [the city] of the pillars,

item.title: Al-Fajr:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِرَمَ ذَاتِ الْعِمَادِ irama dhāti l-ʿimādi (With) Iram1 - who had lofty pillars.2 See 89:1

item.title: Al-Fajr:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِرَمَ ذَاتِ الْعِمَادِ irama dhāti l-ʿimādi (Of) Iram with tall statures (Or many columned.) See 89:6

item.title: Al-Fajr:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّتِي لَمْ يُخْلَقْ مِثْلُهَا فِي الْبِلَادِ allatī lam yukh'laq mith'luhā fī l-bilādi the like of which was not created among cities,

item.title: Al-Fajr:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّتِي لَمْ يُخْلَقْ مِثْلُهَا فِي الْبِلَادِ allatī lam yukh'laq mith'luhā fī l-bilādi The likes of whom had never been created in the land? See 89:1

item.title: Al-Fajr:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّتِي لَمْ يُخْلَقْ مِثْلُهَا فِي الْبِلَادِ allatī lam yukh'laq mith'luhā fī l-bilādi The like of which were not created in any of the (other) cities (of the world) The story of 'Ad is said to be that - 'Ad, son of Awz, son of Iram, son of Sam, son of Noah the people were called after 'Ad. 'Ad had two sons, Shaddad and Shadeed - Shadeed died and Shaddad became the ruler in the earth with several governors under him and claimed himself to be God, and his people had to worship him. God sent an Apostle to admonish Shaddad, but he did not amend his faith and conduct. The Apostle said that if he gets obedient to God he would be admitted to Paradise. Shaddad asked the apostle what was meant by Paradise. The Apostle gave a description of…

item.title: Al-Fajr:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَثَمُودَ الَّذِينَ جَابُوْۤا الصَّخْرَ بِالْوَادِ wathamūda alladhīna jābū l-ṣakhra bil-wādi and [the people of] Thamūd, who hollowed out the rocks in the valley,

item.title: Al-Fajr:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَثَمُودَ الَّذِينَ جَابُوْۤا الصَّخْرَ بِالْوَادِ wathamūda alladhīna jābū l-ṣakhra bil-wādi And (with) Thamūd, who carved out the rocks in the valley? See 89:1

item.title: Al-Fajr:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَثَمُودَ الَّذِينَ جَابُوْۤا الصَّخْرَ بِالْوَادِ wathamūda alladhīna jābū l-ṣakhra bil-wādi And the (Tribe) Thamood (Refer to: 7:73, 11:61, 51:43, 44.) who hewed out the rocks in the valley The Thamood, used to carve buildings out of the huge rocks in the mountains1. The apostle sent to them was Saleh. Reference to Pharaoh and the fall he met2.

item.title: Al-Fajr:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَفِرْعَوْنَ ذِي الْأَوْتَادِ wafir'ʿawna dhī l-awtādi and Pharaoh, the impaler,1

item.title: Al-Fajr:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَفِرْعَوْنَ ذِي الْأَوْتَادِ wafir'ʿawna dhī l-awtādi And (with) Pharaoh, owner of the stakes?1 See 89:1

item.title: Al-Fajr:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَفِرْعَوْنَ ذِي الْأَوْتَادِ wafir'ʿawna dhī l-awtādi And Pharaoh the owner (Ar. an idiom for arrogance, obstinacy and might may also refer to Tyrants binding his victims to the posts and punishing them.) of the stakes Pharaoh used to kill everyone who believed in the True God and disbelieved in his godhead, by nailing them to the ground or a post. Hence, he is called the Nailer. Among the victims were Ezkiel's wife with her six children and Asia the Pharaoh's wife, all were martyred - Ezkiel who is popularly known as the 'Momin al-Aale Fir'awn' i.e., the Believer among the people of Pharaoh, escaped into the mountains.

item.title: Al-Fajr:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِينَ طَغَوْا فِي الْبِلَادِ alladhīna ṭaghaw fī l-bilādi —those who rebelled [against Allah] in their cities

item.title: Al-Fajr:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِينَ طَغَوْا فِي الْبِلَادِ alladhīna ṭaghaw fī l-bilādi (All of) whom oppressed within the lands. See 89:1

item.title: Al-Fajr:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِينَ طَغَوْا فِي الْبِلَادِ alladhīna ṭaghaw fī l-bilādi Who (all) transgressed in the cities Generalise the previous examples - meaning, anyone who commits inordinacy and commits civil disturbance and creates mischief in the society and in verse 13, gives the consequence and in verse 14 warns man to be careful, to beware that God is vigilant. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Fajr:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَكْثَرُوا فِيهَا الْفَسَادَ fa-aktharū fīhā l-fasāda and caused much corruption in them,

item.title: Al-Fajr:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَكْثَرُوا فِيهَا الْفَسَادَ fa-aktharū fīhā l-fasāda And increased therein the corruption. See 89:1

item.title: Al-Fajr:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَكْثَرُوا فِيهَا الْفَسَادَ fa-aktharū fīhā l-fasāda And multiplied wickedness therein See 89:11

item.title: Al-Fajr:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَصَبَّ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّكَ سَوْطَ عَذَابٍ faṣabba ʿalayhim rabbuka sawṭa ʿadhābin so your Lord poured on them lashes of punishment.

item.title: Al-Fajr:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَصَبَّ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّكَ سَوْطَ عَذَابٍ faṣabba ʿalayhim rabbuka sawṭa ʿadhābin So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment. See 89:1

item.title: Al-Fajr:13 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَصَبَّ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّكَ سَوْطَ عَذَابٍ faṣabba ʿalayhim rabbuka sawṭa ʿadhābin So, thy Lord let fall on them the whip of a chastisement See 89:11

item.title: Al-Fajr:14 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِالْمِرْصَادِ inna rabbaka labil-mir'ṣādi Indeed your Lord is in ambush.

item.title: Al-Fajr:14 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِالْمِرْصَادِ inna rabbaka labil-mir'ṣādi Indeed, your Lord is in observation. See 89:1

item.title: Al-Fajr:14 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِالْمِرْصَادِ inna rabbaka labil-mir'ṣādi Verily, thy Lord is (ever) on watch Though God's punishment for the disbelievers and the wicked might have been delayed, the delay is only a respite. It never means that God has neglected or left the rebellious ones once for all. It is His grace that does not make haste in the punishment and when ultimately it has to come it surely comes.

item.title: Al-Fajr:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا الْإِنْسَانُ إِذَا مَا ابْتَلَاهُ رَبُّهُ فَأَكْرَمَهُ وَنَعَّمَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّي أَكْرَمَنِ fa-ammā l-insānu idhā mā ib'talāhu rabbuhu fa-akramahu wanaʿʿamahu fayaqūlu rabbī akramani As for man, whenever his Lord tests him and grants him honour and blesses him, he says, 'My Lord has honoured me.'

item.title: Al-Fajr:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا الْإِنْسَانُ إِذَا مَا ابْتَلَاهُ رَبُّهُ فَأَكْرَمَهُ وَنَعَّمَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّي أَكْرَمَنِ fa-ammā l-insānu idhā mā ib'talāhu rabbuhu fa-akramahu wanaʿʿamahu fayaqūlu rabbī akramani And as for man, when his Lord tries him and (thus) is generous to him and favors him, he says, "My Lord has honored me."1 As for man, when his Lord tries him by giving him honor and bounties, then he says: "My Lord has honored me (89:15). But when He tries him by straitening his means of life, he says: "My Lord has humiliated me! (89:16). But no! But you treat not the orphans with kindness and generosity (89:17). And urge not one another on the feeding of the Miskin (89:18). And you devour the Turath – devouring with greed (89:19). And you love wealth with love Jamma (89:20). Wealth and Poverty are Both a Test and…

item.title: Al-Fajr:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا الْإِنْسَانُ إِذَا مَا ابْتَلَاهُ رَبُّهُ فَأَكْرَمَهُ وَنَعَّمَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّي أَكْرَمَنِ fa-ammā l-insānu idhā mā ib'talāhu rabbuhu fa-akramahu wanaʿʿamahu fayaqūlu rabbī akramani And as for man, when trieth him his Lord, and honoureth him, and is bounteous unto him, then saith he: ''My Lord hath honoured me! It is commonly seen in the world that man in spite of God's grace and mercy done to him and the bounties showered on man, man, when given prosperity forgets the Beneficent Lord, the Giver of all his wealth and happiness and gets puffed up with his prosperity and thinks that what was given to him was his due and will last for ever.

item.title: Al-Fajr:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا إِذَا مَا ابْتَلَاهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّي أَهَانَنِ wa-ammā idhā mā ib'talāhu faqadara ʿalayhi riz'qahu fayaqūlu rabbī ahānani But when He tests him and tightens for him his provision, he says, 'My Lord has humiliated me.'

item.title: Al-Fajr:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا إِذَا مَا ابْتَلَاهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّي أَهَانَنِ wa-ammā idhā mā ib'talāhu faqadara ʿalayhi riz'qahu fayaqūlu rabbī ahānani But when He tries him and restricts his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me." See 89:15

item.title: Al-Fajr:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا إِذَا مَا ابْتَلَاهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّي أَهَانَنِ wa-ammā idhā mā ib'talāhu faqadara ʿalayhi riz'qahu fayaqūlu rabbī ahānani But when trieth him, and then straiteneth unto him his sustenance, then saith he: ''My Lord hath disgraced me! And when man is given in the measure, restricted to his actual needs or according to the situation circumstanced by himself, but not up to his own lust and expectation, he is depressed in the adversity putting the blame upon God's grace not having been granted to him, and complains to have been degraded and lowered in the eyes of the others.

item.title: Al-Fajr:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا بَلْ لَا تُكْرِمُونَ الْيَتِيمَ kallā bal lā tuk'rimūna l-yatīma No indeed! Rather you do not honour the orphan,

item.title: Al-Fajr:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا بَلْ لَا تُكْرِمُونَ الْيَتِيمَ kallā bal lā tuk'rimūna l-yatīma No!1 But you do not honor the orphan. See 89:15

item.title: Al-Fajr:17 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا بَلْ لَا تُكْرِمُونَ الْيَتِيمَ kallā bal lā tuk'rimūna l-yatīma Nay! rather ye honour not the orphan Even when favoured by fortune and granted prosperity with abundant wealth, man does not think of the destitute orphans, the helpless poor ones struggling hard under the pressure of the needs of their life and the life of their poor family and innocent children. Man wastes his wealth on his lust for luxury and enjoyments but does not supply the needs of the needy. It is a denial of God being responsible for the straightness, the actions of man himself being responsible for it. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Fajr:18 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا تَحَاضُّونَ عَلَى طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ walā taḥāḍḍūna ʿalā ṭaʿāmi l-mis'kīni and do not urge the feeding of the needy,

item.title: Al-Fajr:18 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا تَحَاضُّونَ عَلَى طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ walā taḥāḍḍūna ʿalā ṭaʿāmi l-mis'kīni And you do not encourage one another to feed the poor. See 89:15

item.title: Al-Fajr:18 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا تَحَاضُّونَ عَلَى طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ walā taḥāḍḍūna ʿalā ṭaʿāmi l-mis'kīni Nor urge ye one another to feed the poor! When a man is under the grip of his own hard-heartedness and is void of a charitable disposition, he finds plausible excuses for his own shortcomings and defects and even obstructs the others from being charitable and kind to others.

item.title: Al-Fajr:19 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَتَأْكُلُونَ التُّرَاثَ أَكْلًا لَمًّا watakulūna l-turātha aklan lamman and you eat the inheritance rapaciously,

item.title: Al-Fajr:19 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَتَأْكُلُونَ التُّرَاثَ أَكْلًا لَمًّا watakulūna l-turātha aklan lamman And you consume inheritance, devouring (it) altogether.1 See 89:15

item.title: Al-Fajr:19 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَتَأْكُلُونَ التُّرَاثَ أَكْلًا لَمًّا watakulūna l-turātha aklan lamman And ye devour heritage, devouring (everything) in greed (indiscriminately) People used to deprive women and children of their dues in the property and used to devour their share also. It implies in general the misappropriation of any trusts entrusted by the trustees.

item.title: Al-Fajr:20 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَتُحِبُّونَ الْمَالَ حُبًّا جَمًّا watuḥibbūna l-māla ḥubban jamman and you love wealth with much fondness.

item.title: Al-Fajr:20 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَتُحِبُّونَ الْمَالَ حُبًّا جَمًّا watuḥibbūna l-māla ḥubban jamman And you love wealth with immense love. See 89:15

item.title: Al-Fajr:20 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَتُحِبُّونَ الْمَالَ حُبًّا جَمًّا watuḥibbūna l-māla ḥubban jamman And ye love wealth with exceeding love See 89:19

item.title: Al-Fajr:21 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا إِذَا دُكَّتِ الْأَرْضُ دَكًّا دَكًّا kallā idhā dukkati l-arḍu dakkan dakkan No indeed! When the earth is levelled1 to a plain,

item.title: Al-Fajr:21 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا إِذَا دُكَّتِ الْأَرْضُ دَكًّا دَكًّا kallā idhā dukkati l-arḍu dakkan dakkan No! When the earth has been leveled - pounded and crushed. Nay! When the earth is flatened, Dakkan Dakka (89:21). And your Lord comes with the angels in rows (89:22). And Hell will be brought near that Day. On that Day will man remember, but how will that remembrance avail him (89:23). He will say: Alas! Would that I had sent forth for my life! (89:24). So on that Day none will punish as He will punish (89:25). And none will bind as He will bind (89:26). "O tranquil soul! (89:27). "Come back to your Lord, – well-pleased and well-pleasing! (89:28). "Enter then among My servants, (89:29). "And enter My Paradise! (89:30). On the Day of Judgement Everyone will be recompensed according to what He did of Good…

item.title: Al-Fajr:21 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا إِذَا دُكَّتِ الْأَرْضُ دَكًّا دَكًّا kallā idhā dukkati l-arḍu dakkan dakkan Nay! when the earth shall be pounded to powder See 89:19

item.title: Al-Fajr:22 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَاءَ رَبُّكَ وَالْمَلَكُ صَفًّا صَفًّا wajāa rabbuka wal-malaku ṣaffan ṣaffan and your Lord and the angels arrive in ranks,

item.title: Al-Fajr:22 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَاءَ رَبُّكَ وَالْمَلَكُ صَفًّا صَفًّا wajāa rabbuka wal-malaku ṣaffan ṣaffan And your Lord has come1 and the angels, rank upon rank. See 89:21

item.title: Al-Fajr:22 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَاءَ رَبُّكَ وَالْمَلَكُ صَفًّا صَفًّا wajāa rabbuka wal-malaku ṣaffan ṣaffan And cometh (the Command of) thy Lord (Refer to: 2:210.) , with the angels in ranges arrayed Coming of the Lord, means issue of His command1, and the coming of the angels' arrival of the punishment through the angels concerned with the act of chastisement. This is one of the verses which the anthropomorphists quote in favour of their doctrine but when the irrefutable reason supported by Qur'an proves the absolute unity of God in His essence and attributes, such expressions should be interpreted in such a way to be in conformity with reason. The Absolute One is far from being subject to motion. Therefore, His coming means His Final manifestation of His Authority. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Fajr:23 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجِاىءَ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِجَهَنَّمَ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَذَكَّرُ الْإِنْسَانُ وَأَنَّى لَهُ الذِّكْرَى wajīa yawma-idhin bijahannama yawma-idhin yatadhakkaru l-insānu wa-annā lahu l-dhik'rā the day when hell is brought [near], on that day man will take admonition but what will the admonition avail him?

item.title: Al-Fajr:23 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجِاىءَ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِجَهَنَّمَ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَذَكَّرُ الْإِنْسَانُ وَأَنَّى لَهُ الذِّكْرَى wajīa yawma-idhin bijahannama yawma-idhin yatadhakkaru l-insānu wa-annā lahu l-dhik'rā And brought (within view), that Day, is Hell - that Day, man will remember, but how (i.e., what good) to him will be the remembrance? See 89:21

item.title: Al-Fajr:23 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجِاىءَ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِجَهَنَّمَ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَذَكَّرُ الْإِنْسَانُ وَأَنَّى لَهُ الذِّكْرَى wajīa yawma-idhin bijahannama yawma-idhin yatadhakkaru l-insānu wa-annā lahu l-dhik'rā And the Hell shall be made to appear that Day, (and) that Day shall man get awakened, but of what avail unto him shall be the awakening? When the decree will have been passed and the punishment is to be executed, the respite had ended and the time for repentance would have gone. No amount of repentance would be of any avail.

item.title: Al-Fajr:24 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَقُولُ يَالَيْتَنِي قَدَّمْتُ لِحَيَاتِي yaqūlu yālaytanī qaddamtu liḥayātī He will say, 'Alas, had I sent ahead for my life!'

item.title: Al-Fajr:24 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَقُولُ يَالَيْتَنِي قَدَّمْتُ لِحَيَاتِي yaqūlu yālaytanī qaddamtu liḥayātī He will say, "Oh, I wish I had sent ahead (some good) for my life."1 See 89:21

item.title: Al-Fajr:24 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَقُولُ يَالَيْتَنِي قَدَّمْتُ لِحَيَاتِي yaqūlu yālaytanī qaddamtu liḥayātī He shall say: ''Oh! Would that I had sent before (provisions for) my life! The repentant will wish for having sent good deeds to be of avail to him on that occasion. But the time given for action had gone. This indicates that the life hereafter is not only a continuation but a development which actually deserves to be called life1. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Fajr:25 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لَا يُعَذِّبُ عَذَابَهُ أَحَدٌ fayawma-idhin lā yuʿadhibu ʿadhābahu aḥadun On that day none shall punish as He punishes,

item.title: Al-Fajr:25 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لَا يُعَذِّبُ عَذَابَهُ أَحَدٌ fayawma-idhin lā yuʿadhibu ʿadhābahu aḥadun So on that Day, none will punish (as severely) as His punishment. See 89:21

item.title: Al-Fajr:25 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لَا يُعَذِّبُ عَذَابَهُ أَحَدٌ fayawma-idhin lā yuʿadhibu ʿadhābahu aḥadun For, on that day shall chastise not any one like unto His chastisement The chastisement and the torture that will be affected will be such that none else would have had inflicted such a punishment as any one before.

item.title: Al-Fajr:26 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا يُوثِقُ وَثَاقَهُ أَحَدٌ walā yūthiqu wathāqahu aḥadun and none shall bind as He binds.

item.title: Al-Fajr:26 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا يُوثِقُ وَثَاقَهُ أَحَدٌ walā yūthiqu wathāqahu aḥadun And none will bind (as severely) as His binding (of the evildoers). See 89:21

item.title: Al-Fajr:26 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا يُوثِقُ وَثَاقَهُ أَحَدٌ walā yūthiqu wathāqahu aḥadun And shall bind not any one like unto His binding See 89:25

item.title: Al-Fajr:27 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاأَيَّتُهَا النَّفْسُ الْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ yāayyatuhā l-nafsu l-muṭ'ma-inatu 'O soul at peace!

item.title: Al-Fajr:27 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاأَيَّتُهَا النَّفْسُ الْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ yāayyatuhā l-nafsu l-muṭ'ma-inatu (To the righteous it will be said), "O reassured soul. See 89:21

item.title: Al-Fajr:27 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاأَيَّتُهَا النَّفْسُ الْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ yāayyatuhā l-nafsu l-muṭ'ma-inatu (It will be said unto some) ''O' tranquilled soul at (complete) rest! The human soul passes through states or stages. The state in which the soul seeks the fulfilment of his lower desire crossing the limits prescribed by God's laws is called Ammura (12:53) and the soul which reproaches against the rebellious intentions is called 'La Wama' (75:2). And the soul which has conquered all desires and surrendered itself to the Lord is called 'Mutmainnah' the satisfied one, i.e., at rest in peace and perfect harmony with the divine will, triumphed over every kind of passion, desire, sorrow, pain, disappointment, for the sake of any enjoyment of this life getting totally mindful of pleasing the Lord and none else. This is the highest stage of the spiritual progress the human soul in this world…

item.title: Al-Fajr:28 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اِرْجِعِي إِلَى رَبِّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيَّةً ir'jiʿī ilā rabbiki rāḍiyatan marḍiyyatan Return to your Lord, pleased, pleasing!

item.title: Al-Fajr:28 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
