item.description: اَللَّهُ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَنْعَامَ لِتَرْكَبُوا مِنْهَا وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ al-lahu alladhī jaʿala lakumu l-anʿāma litarkabū min'hā wamin'hā takulūna God is He Who made for you the cattle that ye may ride on some of them, and of them ye may eat. See 40:78

item.title: Al-Ghaafir:80 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا مَنَافِعُ وَلِتَبْلُغُوا عَلَيْهَا حَاجَةً فِي صُدُورِكُمْ وَعَلَيْهَا وَعَلَى الْفُلْكِ تُحْمَلُونَ walakum fīhā manāfiʿu walitablughū ʿalayhā ḥājatan fī ṣudūrikum waʿalayhā waʿalā l-ful'ki tuḥ'malūna and there are [numerous] uses in them for you, and that over them1 you may satisfy any need that is in your breasts, and you are carried on them and on ships.

item.title: Al-Ghaafir:80 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا مَنَافِعُ وَلِتَبْلُغُوا عَلَيْهَا حَاجَةً فِي صُدُورِكُمْ وَعَلَيْهَا وَعَلَى الْفُلْكِ تُحْمَلُونَ walakum fīhā manāfiʿu walitablughū ʿalayhā ḥājatan fī ṣudūrikum waʿalayhā waʿalā l-ful'ki tuḥ'malūna And for you therein are (other) benefits and that you may realize upon them a need which is in your breasts;1 and upon them and upon ships you are carried. See 40:79

item.title: Al-Ghaafir:80 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا مَنَافِعُ وَلِتَبْلُغُوا عَلَيْهَا حَاجَةً فِي صُدُورِكُمْ وَعَلَيْهَا وَعَلَى الْفُلْكِ تُحْمَلُونَ walakum fīhā manāfiʿu walitablughū ʿalayhā ḥājatan fī ṣudūrikum waʿalayhā waʿalā l-ful'ki tuḥ'malūna And for you in them are other benefits, and that ye may realize thereon the need ye cherish in your breasts; and upon them and upon the ships ye are borne. See 40:78

item.title: Al-Ghaafir:81 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيُرِيكُمْ اٰیٰتِهٖ فَأَيَّ اٰیٰتِ اللَّهِ تُنْكِرُونَ wayurīkum āyātihi fa-ayya āyāti l-lahi tunkirūna He shows you His signs. So which of the signs of Allah do you deny?

item.title: Al-Ghaafir:81 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيُرِيكُمْ اٰیٰتِهٖ فَأَيَّ اٰیٰتِ اللَّهِ تُنْكِرُونَ wayurīkum āyātihi fa-ayya āyāti l-lahi tunkirūna And He shows you His signs. So which of the signs of Allah do you deny? See 40:79

item.title: Al-Ghaafir:81 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيُرِيكُمْ اٰیٰتِهٖ فَأَيَّ اٰیٰتِ اللَّهِ تُنْكِرُونَ wayurīkum āyātihi fa-ayya āyāti l-lahi tunkirūna And He showeth you His Signs; which, then, of the Signs of God will ye deny (See verse 55:13 and its repetition in the surah.) ? See 40:78

item.title: Al-Ghaafir:82 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوْۤا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَيَنْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ كَانُوْۤا أَكْثَرَ مِنْهُمْ وَأَشَدَّ قُوَّةً وَءَاثَارًا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَمَا أَغْنَى عَنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوْۤا يَكْسِبُونَ afalam yasīrū fī l-arḍi fayanẓurū kayfa kāna ʿāqibatu alladhīna min qablihim kānū akthara min'hum wa-ashadda quwwatan waāthāran fī l-arḍi famā aghnā ʿanhum mā kānū yaksibūna Have they not travelled over the land so that they may observe how was the fate of those who were before them? They were more numerous than them and were greater [than them] in power and with respect to the effects [they left] in the land. But what they used to earn did not avail them.

item.title: Al-Ghaafir:82 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوْۤا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَيَنْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ كَانُوْۤا أَكْثَرَ مِنْهُمْ وَأَشَدَّ قُوَّةً وَءَاثَارًا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَمَا أَغْنَى عَنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوْۤا يَكْسِبُونَ afalam yasīrū fī l-arḍi fayanẓurū kayfa kāna ʿāqibatu alladhīna min qablihim kānū akthara min'hum wa-ashadda quwwatan waāthāran fī l-arḍi famā aghnā ʿanhum mā kānū yaksibūna Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them? They were more numerous than themselves and greater in strength and in impression on the land, but they were not availed by what they used to earn. Have they not traveled through the earth and seen what was the end of those before them? They were more in number than them and mightier in strength, and in the traces in the land; yet all that they used to earn availed them not (40:82).…

item.title: Al-Ghaafir:82 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوْۤا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَيَنْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ كَانُوْۤا أَكْثَرَ مِنْهُمْ وَأَشَدَّ قُوَّةً وَءَاثَارًا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَمَا أَغْنَى عَنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوْۤا يَكْسِبُونَ afalam yasīrū fī l-arḍi fayanẓurū kayfa kāna ʿāqibatu alladhīna min qablihim kānū akthara min'hum wa-ashadda quwwatan waāthāran fī l-arḍi famā aghnā ʿanhum mā kānū yaksibūna What! have they not travelled in the earth and seen how was the end of those before them? They were more (in number) than those and mightier in strength, and greater are their relics (of their power) in the earth, but availed them not what they were earning. See 40:78

item.title: Al-Ghaafir:83 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا جَاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ فَرِحُوْۤا بِمَا عِنْدَهُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ وَحَاقَ بِهِمْ مَا كَانُوْۤا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ falammā jāathum rusuluhum bil-bayināti fariḥū bimā ʿindahum mina l-ʿil'mi waḥāqa bihim mā kānū bihi yastahziūna When their apostles brought them manifest proofs, they exulted in the knowledge they possessed, and they were besieged by what they used to deride.

item.title: Al-Ghaafir:83 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا جَاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ فَرِحُوْۤا بِمَا عِنْدَهُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ وَحَاقَ بِهِمْ مَا كَانُوْۤا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ falammā jāathum rusuluhum bil-bayināti fariḥū bimā ʿindahum mina l-ʿil'mi waḥāqa bihim mā kānū bihi yastahziūna And when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they (merely) rejoiced in what they had of knowledge, but they were enveloped by what they used to ridicule. See 40:82

item.title: Al-Ghaafir:83 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا جَاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ فَرِحُوْۤا بِمَا عِنْدَهُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ وَحَاقَ بِهِمْ مَا كَانُوْۤا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ falammā jāathum rusuluhum bil-bayināti fariḥū bimā ʿindahum mina l-ʿil'mi waḥāqa bihim mā kānū bihi yastahziūna And when came unto them their apostles with clear proofs (of their truthfulness), exulted they in what they had with them of knowledge, but encompassed (Surrounded them.) them that which they were wont to scoff. This applies to those who exult in their own knowledge of science, mocking at whatever is beyond their experimental sphere. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Ghaafir:84 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْا بَأْسَنَا قَالُوْا اٰمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَحْدَهُ وَكَفَرْنَا بِمَا كُنَّا بِهِ مُشْرِكِينَ falammā ra-aw basanā qālū āmannā bil-lahi waḥdahu wakafarnā bimā kunnā bihi mush'rikīna Then, when they sighted Our punishment, they said, 'We believe in Allah alone, and disavow what we used to take as His partners.'

item.title: Al-Ghaafir:84 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْا بَأْسَنَا قَالُوْا اٰمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَحْدَهُ وَكَفَرْنَا بِمَا كُنَّا بِهِ مُشْرِكِينَ falammā ra-aw basanā qālū āmannā bil-lahi waḥdahu wakafarnā bimā kunnā bihi mush'rikīna And when they saw Our punishment, they said, "We believe in Allah alone and disbelieve in that which we used to associate with Him." See 40:82

item.title: Al-Ghaafir:84 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْا بَأْسَنَا قَالُوْا اٰمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَحْدَهُ وَكَفَرْنَا بِمَا كُنَّا بِهِ مُشْرِكِينَ falammā ra-aw basanā qālū āmannā bil-lahi waḥdahu wakafarnā bimā kunnā bihi mush'rikīna But when they beheld Our punishment said they: "We believe in God alone and we deny what we used to associate with Him." See 40:83

item.title: Al-Ghaafir:85 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمْ يَكُ يَنْفَعُهُمْ إِيمَانُهُمْ لَمَّا رَأَوْا بَأْسَنَا سُنَّتَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي قَدْ خَلَتْ فِي عِبَادِهِ وَخَسِرَ هُنَالِكَ الْكَافِرُونَ falam yaku yanfaʿuhum īmānuhum lammā ra-aw basanā sunnata l-lahi allatī qad khalat fī ʿibādihi wakhasira hunālika l-kāfirūna But their faith was of no benefit to them when they sighted Our punishment —Allah's precedent which has passed among His servants, and it is thence that the faithless will be losers.

item.title: Al-Ghaafir:85 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمْ يَكُ يَنْفَعُهُمْ إِيمَانُهُمْ لَمَّا رَأَوْا بَأْسَنَا سُنَّتَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي قَدْ خَلَتْ فِي عِبَادِهِ وَخَسِرَ هُنَالِكَ الْكَافِرُونَ falam yaku yanfaʿuhum īmānuhum lammā ra-aw basanā sunnata l-lahi allatī qad khalat fī ʿibādihi wakhasira hunālika l-kāfirūna But never did their faith benefit them once they saw Our punishment. (It is) the established way of Allah which has preceded among His servants. And the disbelievers thereupon lost (all). See 40:82

item.title: Al-Ghaafir:85 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمْ يَكُ يَنْفَعُهُمْ إِيمَانُهُمْ لَمَّا رَأَوْا بَأْسَنَا سُنَّتَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي قَدْ خَلَتْ فِي عِبَادِهِ وَخَسِرَ هُنَالِكَ الْكَافِرُونَ falam yaku yanfaʿuhum īmānuhum lammā ra-aw basanā sunnata l-lahi allatī qad khalat fī ʿibādihi wakhasira hunālika l-kāfirūna But shall not benefit them their faith when they had beheld Our punishment; (Getting into the grip of the divine order - creative or legislative. (A.P.).) (such is) the procedure of God which hath indeed been in use concerning His servants; and then (When they get with the grip. (A.P.).) the disbelievers have lost. See 40:83

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: هَلْ أَتَىكَ حَدِیْثُ الْغَاشِيَةِ hal atāka ḥadīthu l-ghāshiyati Did you receive the account of the Enveloper?

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: هَلْ أَتَىكَ حَدِیْثُ الْغَاشِيَةِ hal atāka ḥadīthu l-ghāshiyati Has there reached you the report of the Overwhelming (event)? لَّا يُسْمِنُ وَلَا يُغْنِي مِن جُوعٍ Which will neither nourish nor avail against hunger. This means that the intent in eating it will not be achieved, and nothing harmful will be repelled by it.

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: هَلْ أَتَىكَ حَدِیْثُ الْغَاشِيَةِ hal atāka ḥadīthu l-ghāshiyati Hath not come unto thee the tidings of the Overwhelming Event? (Refer to: 12:107, The Total Resurrection.) 'Ghashiyah', i.e., that which covers or overshadows or overwhelms, i.e., a terrible thing or event which confounds the people and sends them off their senses. The Day of Judgment will be a state of such reality that what we think and see in this life will have been lost in our realisation of the reality which will be laid bare before us1. The Day of Judgment. The enjoyments referred to in this Surah are all figurative presentations of the heavenly entertainment in the heavenly assemblies of the souls. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَاشِعَةٌ wujūhun yawma-idhin khāshiʿatun Some faces on that day will be humbled,

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَاشِعَةٌ wujūhun yawma-idhin khāshiʿatun (Some) faces, that Day, will be humbled. See 88:1

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَاشِعَةٌ wujūhun yawma-idhin khāshiʿatun (Some) faces on that day shall be downcast The feeling of humiliation in a man is manifested only on his face. On the Day of Judgment, the disbelievers and the wicked will be humiliated for their arrogance and pride. Their faces will be awful and terror-stricken and downcast.

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: عَامِلَةٌ نَاصِبَةٌ ʿāmilatun nāṣibatun wrought-up and weary:

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: عَامِلَةٌ نَاصِبَةٌ ʿāmilatun nāṣibatun Working (hard) and exhausted.1 See 88:1

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: عَامِلَةٌ نَاصِبَةٌ ʿāmilatun nāṣibatun Toiling, weary Those who were striving in the life here in hostility against the godly ones. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: تَصْلٰی نَارًا حَامِيَةً taṣlā nāran ḥāmiyatan they will enter a scorching fire,

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: تَصْلٰی نَارًا حَامِيَةً taṣlā nāran ḥāmiyatan They will (enter to) burn in an intensely hot Fire. See 88:1

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: تَصْلٰی نَارًا حَامِيَةً taṣlā nāran ḥāmiyatan Entering into the fire, blazing See 88:3

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: تُسْقَى مِنْ عَيْنٍ ءَانِيَةٍ tus'qā min ʿaynin āniyatin and made to drink from a boiling spring.

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: تُسْقَى مِنْ عَيْنٍ ءَانِيَةٍ tus'qā min ʿaynin āniyatin They will be given drink from a boiling spring. See 88:1

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: تُسْقَى مِنْ عَيْنٍ ءَانِيَةٍ tus'qā min ʿaynin āniyatin Made to drink from a spring (fiercely) boiling (Or a humiliating stuff.) See 88:3

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَيْسَ لَهُمْ طَعَامٌ إِلَّا مِنْ ضَرِیْعٍۙ laysa lahum ṭaʿāmun illā min ḍarīʿin They will have no food except cactus,

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَيْسَ لَهُمْ طَعَامٌ إِلَّا مِنْ ضَرِیْعٍۙ laysa lahum ṭaʿāmun illā min ḍarīʿin For them there will be no food except from a poisonous, thorny plant. See 88:1

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَيْسَ لَهُمْ طَعَامٌ إِلَّا مِنْ ضَرِیْعٍۙ laysa lahum ṭaʿāmun illā min ḍarīʿin For them there shall not be (any) food but of the bitter-thorny fruit 'Zaree' 'Zaree' a kind of dry thorny shrub, so bitter in taste that none of the animals even go near it, it is also loathsome in appearance. This tree will be the food of the fellows in hell.

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا يُسْمِنُ وَلَا يُغْنِي مِنْ جُوعٍ lā yus'minu walā yugh'nī min jūʿin neither nourishing, nor availing against hunger.

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا يُسْمِنُ وَلَا يُغْنِي مِنْ جُوعٍ lā yus'minu walā yugh'nī min jūʿin Which neither nourishes nor avails against hunger. See 88:1

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا يُسْمِنُ وَلَا يُغْنِي مِنْ جُوعٍ lā yus'minu walā yugh'nī min jūʿin Which will neither fatten nor give any relief (Sufficing – satisfying.) from hunger See 88:6

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَاعِمَةٌ wujūhun yawma-idhin nāʿimatun Some faces on that day will be joyous,

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَاعِمَةٌ wujūhun yawma-idhin nāʿimatun (Other) faces, that Day, will show pleasure. Faces that Day will be joyful (88:8). Glad with their endeavor (88:9). In a lofty Paradise (88:10). Where they shall neither hear harmful speech nor falsehood (88:11). Therein will be a running spring (88:12). Therein will be thrones raised high (88:13). And cups set at hand (88:14). And Namariq, set in rows (88:15). And Zarabi, spread out (Mabthuthah) (88:16). The Condition of the People of Paradise on the Day of Judgement After mentioning the situation of the wretched people, Allah changes the discussion to mention those who will be happy. He says: وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ Faces that Day. Meaning: on the Day of Judgement. نَّاعِمَةٌ will be joyful, Meaning: pleasure will be noticeable in them (those faces). This will only occur due to their striving. Sufyan said: لِّسَعْيِهَا…

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَاعِمَةٌ wujūhun yawma-idhin nāʿimatun (Other) faces on that day shall be happy The state of bliss which the righteous will be placed in.

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لِسَعْيِهَا رَاضِيَةٌ lisaʿyihā rāḍiyatun pleased with their endeavour;

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لِسَعْيِهَا رَاضِيَةٌ lisaʿyihā rāḍiyatun With their effort (they are) satisfied. See 88:8

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لِسَعْيِهَا رَاضِيَةٌ lisaʿyihā rāḍiyatun With their efforts past, well pleased See 88:8

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٍ fī jannatin ʿāliyatin in a lofty paradise,

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٍ fī jannatin ʿāliyatin In an elevated garden. See 88:8

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٍ fī jannatin ʿāliyatin In a grand garden See 88:8

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا تَسْمَعُ فِيهَا لَاغِيَةً lā tasmaʿu fīhā lāghiyatan wherein they will not hear any vain talk.

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا تَسْمَعُ فِيهَا لَاغِيَةً lā tasmaʿu fīhā lāghiyatan Wherein they will hear no unsuitable speech.1 See 88:8

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا تَسْمَعُ فِيهَا لَاغِيَةً lā tasmaʿu fīhā lāghiyatan They shall hear not therein any vain talk See 88:8

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيهَا عَيْنٌ جَارِيَةٌ fīhā ʿaynun jāriyatun In it there is a flowing spring

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيهَا عَيْنٌ جَارِيَةٌ fīhā ʿaynun jāriyatun Within it is a flowing spring. See 88:8

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيهَا عَيْنٌ جَارِيَةٌ fīhā ʿaynun jāriyatun Therein a spring flowing See 88:8

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيهَا سُرُرٌ مَرْفُوعَةٌ fīhā sururun marfūʿatun and in it there are raised couches,

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيهَا سُرُرٌ مَرْفُوعَةٌ fīhā sururun marfūʿatun Within it are couches raised high. See 88:8

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:13 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيهَا سُرُرٌ مَرْفُوعَةٌ fīhā sururun marfūʿatun Therein are couches (Exalted - joyful seats raised.) exalted See 88:8

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:14 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَكْوَابٌ مَوْضُوعَةٌ wa-akwābun mawḍūʿatun and goblets set,

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:14 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَكْوَابٌ مَوْضُوعَةٌ wa-akwābun mawḍūʿatun And cups put in place. See 88:8

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:14 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَكْوَابٌ مَوْضُوعَةٌ wa-akwābun mawḍūʿatun And goblets ready placed See 88:8

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَنَمَارِقُ مَصْفُوفَةٌ wanamāriqu maṣfūfatun and cushions laid out in an array,

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَنَمَارِقُ مَصْفُوفَةٌ wanamāriqu maṣfūfatun And cushions lined up. See 88:8

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَنَمَارِقُ مَصْفُوفَةٌ wanamāriqu maṣfūfatun And cushions ranged in order See 88:8

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَزَرَابِيُّ مَبْثُوثَةٌ wazarābiyyu mabthūthatun and carpets spread out.

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَزَرَابِيُّ مَبْثُوثَةٌ wazarābiyyu mabthūthatun And carpets spread around. See 88:8

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَزَرَابِيُّ مَبْثُوثَةٌ wazarābiyyu mabthūthatun And carpets spread forth See 88:8

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَلَا يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَى الْاِبِلِ كَيْفَ خُلِقَتْ afalā yanẓurūna ilā l-ibili kayfa khuliqat Do they not observe1 the camel, [to see] how she has been created?

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَلَا يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَى الْاِبِلِ كَيْفَ خُلِقَتْ afalā yanẓurūna ilā l-ibili kayfa khuliqat Then do they not look at the camels - how they are created? Do they not look at the camels, how they are created (88:17). And at the heaven, how it is raised (88:18). And at the mountains, how they are rooted (88:19). And at the earth, how it is outspread (88:20). So remind them – you are only one who reminds (88:21). You are not a Musaytir over them (88:22). Save the one who turns away and disbelieves (88:23). Then Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment (88:24). Verily, to Us will be their return (88:25). Then verily, for Us will be their reckoning (88:26). The Exhortation to Look at the Creation of the Camel, the Heaven, the Mountains and the Earth Allah commands His servants…

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:17 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَلَا يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَى الْاِبِلِ كَيْفَ خُلِقَتْ afalā yanẓurūna ilā l-ibili kayfa khuliqat What! See they not unto the camels, how they are created? Man's attention is invited to the four things which he sees every day. The Camel, the ship of the desert. The usefulness of the animal, its build and its peculiar traits. The Skies, with their unlimited heights, their wonderful bodies and their mystic functioning with the tremendous control over their regulated activities. The Mountains, their huge sizes, their fixed immovable stand, the usefulness of its material, the stone. The Earth with its extent, being a globe yet serving a wide plane, and its amenability to the growth of the essential produce out of it, and the great store of minerals, metals and the liquids treasured in it. M.A. translates (Ibil) to mean 'clouds' - and in his…

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:18 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِلَى السَّمَاءِ كَيْفَ رُفِعَتْ wa-ilā l-samāi kayfa rufiʿat and the sky, how it has been raised?

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:18 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِلَى السَّمَاءِ كَيْفَ رُفِعَتْ wa-ilā l-samāi kayfa rufiʿat And at the sky - how it is raised? See 88:17

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:18 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِلَى السَّمَاءِ كَيْفَ رُفِعَتْ wa-ilā l-samāi kayfa rufiʿat And Unto the heaven, how it is raised See 88:17

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:19 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِلَى الْجِبَالِ كَيْفَ نُصِبَتْ wa-ilā l-jibāli kayfa nuṣibat and the mountains, how they have been set?

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:19 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِلَى الْجِبَالِ كَيْفَ نُصِبَتْ wa-ilā l-jibāli kayfa nuṣibat And at the mountains - how they are erected? See 88:17

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:19 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِلَى الْجِبَالِ كَيْفَ نُصِبَتْ wa-ilā l-jibāli kayfa nuṣibat And unto the mountains, how they are set up? See 88:17

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:20 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِلَى الْأَرْضِ كَيْفَ سُطِحَتْ wa-ilā l-arḍi kayfa suṭiḥat and the earth, how it has been surfaced?

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:20 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِلَى الْأَرْضِ كَيْفَ سُطِحَتْ wa-ilā l-arḍi kayfa suṭiḥat And at the earth - how it is spread out? See 88:17

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:20 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِلَى الْأَرْضِ كَيْفَ سُطِحَتْ wa-ilā l-arḍi kayfa suṭiḥat And unto the earth, how it is spread out? See 88:17

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:21 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَذَكِّرْ إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ مُذَكِّرٌ fadhakkir innamā anta mudhakkirun So admonish—for you are only an admonisher,

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:21 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَذَكِّرْ إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ مُذَكِّرٌ fadhakkir innamā anta mudhakkirun So remind, (O Muḥammad); you are only a reminder. See 88:17

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:21 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَذَكِّرْ إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ مُذَكِّرٌ fadhakkir innamā anta mudhakkirun So, thou (The Holy Prophet.) (go on) reminding; Thou art only a Reminder (Refer to: 87:9.) The duty of an apostle of God is only to preach the faith and teach the people its practice and show them the right ways of life. It is not for the apostle of God to watch the people against their wickedness or to punish them. 'Musaitir' here is used in sense of compelling one to any action, i.e., Compeller1, as otherwise the Prophet and his successors represent God as His Vicegerent to execute the divine legislative will and it is in absolute conformity with it. (A.P.).

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:22 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَسْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِمُصَيْطِرٍ lasta ʿalayhim bimuṣayṭirin and not a taskmaster over them—

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:22 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَسْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِمُصَيْطِرٍ lasta ʿalayhim bimuṣayṭirin You are not over them a controller. See 88:17

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:22 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَسْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِمُصَيْطِرٍ lasta ʿalayhim bimuṣayṭirin Thou art not, over them, a compeller (Refer to: 2:256, 10:99.) See 88:21

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:23 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِلَّا مَنْ تَوَلَّى وَكَفَرَ illā man tawallā wakafara except him who turns back and disbelieves.

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:23 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِلَّا مَنْ تَوَلَّى وَكَفَرَ illā man tawallā wakafara However, he who turns away and disbelieves. See 88:17

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:23 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِلَّا مَنْ تَوَلَّى وَكَفَرَ illā man tawallā wakafara But whosoever turneth back and disbelieveth Chastising those who turn back and disbelieve in the truth rests only with God. Here and elsewhere God refers to Himself in plural, the totality of His Authority is implied. Thus, all the entities functioning in the machinery of His authority are included1. (A.P.).

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:24 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَيُعَذِّبُهُ اللَّهُ الْعَذَابَ الْأَكْبَرَ fayuʿadhibuhu l-lahu l-ʿadhāba l-akbara Him Allah will punish with the greatest punishment.

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:24 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَيُعَذِّبُهُ اللَّهُ الْعَذَابَ الْأَكْبَرَ fayuʿadhibuhu l-lahu l-ʿadhāba l-akbara Then Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment. See 88:17

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:24 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَيُعَذِّبُهُ اللَّهُ الْعَذَابَ الْأَكْبَرَ fayuʿadhibuhu l-lahu l-ʿadhāba l-akbara Then will chastise him God with the greatest chastisement See 88:23

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:25 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ إِلَيْنَا إِيَابَهُمْ inna ilaynā iyābahum Indeed to Us will be their return.

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:25 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ إِلَيْنَا إِيَابَهُمْ inna ilaynā iyābahum Indeed, to Us is their return. See 88:17

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:25 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ إِلَيْنَا إِيَابَهُمْ inna ilaynā iyābahum Verily unto Us is their return See 88:23

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:26 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا حِسَابَهُمْ thumma inna ʿalaynā ḥisābahum Then, indeed, their reckoning will lie with Us.

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:26 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا حِسَابَهُمْ thumma inna ʿalaynā ḥisābahum Then indeed, upon Us is their account. See 88:17

item.title: Al-Ghaashiya:26 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا حِسَابَهُمْ thumma inna ʿalaynā ḥisābahum Then verily, upon Us is to reckon with them See 88:23

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلْحَاقَّةُ al-ḥāqatu The Besieger!1

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلْحَاقَّةُ al-ḥāqatu The Inevitable Reality. لِنَجْعَلَهَا لَكُمْ تَذْكِرَةً That We might make it an admonition for you The pronoun "it" here refers to the species of the object (ships) due to the general meaning alluding to this. Thus, the meaning is, 'We caused its type of creation (ships) to remain (in the earth) for you, so that you ride upon the currents of the water in the seas. ' This is as Allah says: وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِنَ الْفُلْكِ وَالْأَنْعَامِ مَا تَرْكَبُونَ - لِتَسْتَوُوا عَلَىٰ ظُهُورِهِ ثُمَّ تَذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ رَبِّكُمْ إِذَا اسْتَوَيْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ and has appointed for you ships and cattle on which you ride; In order that you may mount on their backs, and then may remember the favor of your Lord when you mount thereon (43:12-13) And Allah said: وَآيَةٌ لَّهُمْ أَنَّا حَمَلْنَا ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ فِي الْفُلْكِ الْمَشْحُونِ - وَخَلَقْنَا…

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلْحَاقَّةُ al-ḥāqatu The Reality (That which is sure to come) ! The Inevitable: - That which shall surely come to pass without fail - when all falsehood shall vanish, only the absolute truth shall be laid bare - The word 'Alhaqa' is derived from 'Haq' or 'Haqiqah', i.e., the truth. That which is sure to come - the inevitable, i.e., The Resurrection. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا الْحَاقَّةُ mā l-ḥāqatu What is the Besieger?!

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا الْحَاقَّةُ mā l-ḥāqatu What is the Inevitable Reality? See 69:1

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا الْحَاقَّةُ mā l-ḥāqatu What is the Reality? The Resurrection, i.e., passing into new life or the coming into life after death, everyone individually and collectively, according to Qur'an is such a reality and so certain to happen that in many places has been termed as 'Haqq al-Yaqin' - the Certain Truth, as otherwise Qur'an considers the creation as meaningless. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْحَاقَّةُ wamā adrāka mā l-ḥāqatu What will show you what is the Besieger?!

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْحَاقَّةُ wamā adrāka mā l-ḥāqatu And what can make you know what is the Inevitable Reality? See 69:1

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْحَاقَّةُ wamā adrāka mā l-ḥāqatu And what did thou (O' Man) comprehend what the Reality is? See 69:2

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ وَعَادٌ بِالْقَارِعَةِ kadhabat thamūdu waʿādun bil-qāriʿati Thamūd and 'Ād denied the Catastrophe.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ وَعَادٌ بِالْقَارِعَةِ kadhabat thamūdu waʿādun bil-qāriʿati Thamūd and ʿAad denied the Striking Calamity (i.e., the Resurrection). See 69:1

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ وَعَادٌ بِالْقَارِعَةِ kadhabat thamūdu waʿādun bil-qāriʿati Belied Thamood and 'Ad' the striking (Horrible) calamity (Resurrection. Refer to Verses 7:73 - 7:78, 11:61, 51:44.) 'Qariyah' derived from 'Qar' i.e., striking of one thing over the other - here meaning calamity striking terror by the events causing horror and awe in the hearts of the people - The Day of Doom which the people 'Ad' and 'Thamood' disbelieved and called it to be a lie. Qariah is another name for the terrible day of the Final Judgment1. Thamood, the people who defied the apostle 'Saleh' who hamstrung the 'She-Camel' which appeared by God's command - A Mighty Calamity consisting of earthquake and a terrible Thunderstorm overtook them and they were destroyed2.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَأُهْلِكُوا بِالطَّاغِيَةِ fa-ammā thamūdu fa-uh'likū bil-ṭāghiyati As for Thamūd, they were destroyed by the Cry.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَأُهْلِكُوا بِالطَّاغِيَةِ fa-ammā thamūdu fa-uh'likū bil-ṭāghiyati So as for Thamūd, they were destroyed by the overpowering (blast). See 69:1

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَأُهْلِكُوا بِالطَّاغِيَةِ fa-ammā thamūdu fa-uh'likū bil-ṭāghiyati So as to Thamood, they were destroyed by an exceedingly terrible thunder See 69:4

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا عَادٌ فَأُهْلِكُوا بِرِيحٍ صَرْصَرٍ عَاتِيَةٍ wa-ammā ʿādun fa-uh'likū birīḥin ṣarṣarin ʿātiyatin And as for 'Ād, they were destroyed by a fierce icy gale,

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا عَادٌ فَأُهْلِكُوا بِرِيحٍ صَرْصَرٍ عَاتِيَةٍ wa-ammā ʿādun fa-uh'likū birīḥin ṣarṣarin ʿātiyatin And as for ʿAad, they were destroyed by a screaming,1 violent wind. See 69:1

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا عَادٌ فَأُهْلِكُوا بِرِيحٍ صَرْصَرٍ عَاتِيَةٍ wa-ammā ʿādun fa-uh'likū birīḥin ṣarṣarin ʿātiyatin And as to 'Ad, they were destroyed by a roaring violent blast 'Ad' the people who defied the apostle Hud, who were destroyed by a terrible violent blast of the wind1.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: سَخَّرَهَا عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ لَيَالٍ وَثَمَانِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُومًا فَتَرٰی الْقَوْمَ فِيهَا صَرْعَى كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ sakharahā ʿalayhim sabʿa layālin wathamāniyata ayyāmin ḥusūman fatarā l-qawma fīhā ṣarʿā ka-annahum aʿjāzu nakhlin khāwiyatin which He disposed against them for seven grueling1 nights and eight days, so that you could have seen the people lying about therein prostrate as if they were hollow trunks of palm trees.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: سَخَّرَهَا عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ لَيَالٍ وَثَمَانِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُومًا فَتَرٰی الْقَوْمَ فِيهَا صَرْعَى كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ sakharahā ʿalayhim sabʿa layālin wathamāniyata ayyāmin ḥusūman fatarā l-qawma fīhā ṣarʿā ka-annahum aʿjāzu nakhlin khāwiyatin Which He (i.e., Allah) imposed upon them for seven nights and eight days in succession, so you would see the people therein fallen as if they were hollow trunks of palm trees. See 69:1

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: سَخَّرَهَا عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ لَيَالٍ وَثَمَانِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُومًا فَتَرٰی الْقَوْمَ فِيهَا صَرْعَى كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ sakharahā ʿalayhim sabʿa layālin wathamāniyata ayyāmin ḥusūman fatarā l-qawma fīhā ṣarʿā ka-annahum aʿjāzu nakhlin khāwiyatin He made it rage against them for seven nights and eight days uprooting, that thou mightest see the people therein prostrate as if they were the trunks of the hollow palms See 69:6

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَهَلْ تَرٰی لَهُمْ مِنْ بَاقِيَةٍ fahal tarā lahum min bāqiyatin So do you see any trace of them?

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَهَلْ تَرٰی لَهُمْ مِنْ بَاقِيَةٍ fahal tarā lahum min bāqiyatin Then do you see of them any remains? See 69:1

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَهَلْ تَرٰی لَهُمْ مِنْ بَاقِيَةٍ fahal tarā lahum min bāqiyatin Seest thou then, of them any surviving? Not one left alive - Even those who took shelter under the underground cells, were blown out and killed.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَاءَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَنْ قَبْلَهُ وَالْمُؤْتَفِكَاتُ بِالْخَاطِئَةِ wajāa fir'ʿawnu waman qablahu wal-mu'tafikātu bil-khāṭi-ati Then brought Pharaoh and those who were before him, and the towns that were overturned, iniquity.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَاءَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَنْ قَبْلَهُ وَالْمُؤْتَفِكَاتُ بِالْخَاطِئَةِ wajāa fir'ʿawnu waman qablahu wal-mu'tafikātu bil-khāṭi-ati And there came Pharaoh and those before him and the overturned cities1 with sin. See 69:1

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَاءَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَنْ قَبْلَهُ وَالْمُؤْتَفِكَاتُ بِالْخَاطِئَةِ wajāa fir'ʿawnu waman qablahu wal-mu'tafikātu bil-khāṭi-ati And came Pharaoh and those before him and the cities over-thrown, with evil Pharaoh whose inordinate pride and being puffed up with power, has passed into a proverb. He defied the apostle Moses and was destroyed1. The cities overthrown are Sodom and Gomorrah which defied the preachings of the apostle Lot - They were overturned2.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَعَصَوْا رَسُولَ رَبِّهِمْ فَأَخَذَهُمْ أَخْذَةً رَابِيَةً faʿaṣaw rasūla rabbihim fa-akhadhahum akhdhatan rābiyatan Then they disobeyed the apostle of their Lord, so He seized them with a terrible seizing.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَعَصَوْا رَسُولَ رَبِّهِمْ فَأَخَذَهُمْ أَخْذَةً رَابِيَةً faʿaṣaw rasūla rabbihim fa-akhadhahum akhdhatan rābiyatan And they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, so He seized them with a seizure exceeding (in severity). See 69:1

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَعَصَوْا رَسُولَ رَبِّهِمْ فَأَخَذَهُمْ أَخْذَةً رَابِيَةً faʿaṣaw rasūla rabbihim fa-akhadhahum akhdhatan rābiyatan And they disobeyed the Apostle of their Lord, so He seized (Gripped) them with an increasing seizure (Vehement – intense. Refer to Verse 11:42.) See 69:9

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا لَمَّا طَغَى الْمَاءُ حَمَلْنَاكُمْ فِي الْجَارِيَةِ innā lammā ṭaghā l-māu ḥamalnākum fī l-jāriyati Indeed when the Flood rose high, We carried you in a floating ark,

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا لَمَّا طَغَى الْمَاءُ حَمَلْنَاكُمْ فِي الْجَارِيَةِ innā lammā ṭaghā l-māu ḥamalnākum fī l-jāriyati Indeed, when the water overflowed, We carried you (i.e., your ancestors) in the sailing ship.1 See 69:1

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا لَمَّا طَغَى الْمَاءُ حَمَلْنَاكُمْ فِي الْجَارِيَةِ innā lammā ṭaghā l-māu ḥamalnākum fī l-jāriyati Verily, We, when rose the water (of Noah's flood) surpassed the (ordinary) limits, bore you up (O' mankind) in the Ark made to float Reference is to the rescue that Noah along with his sincere followers being saved by through Ark1.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لِنَجْعَلَهَا لَكُمْ تَذْكِرَةً وَتَعِيَهَا أُذُنٌ وَاعِيَةٌ linajʿalahā lakum tadhkiratan wataʿiyahā udhunun wāʿiyatun that We might make it a reminder for you, and that receptive ears might remember it.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لِنَجْعَلَهَا لَكُمْ تَذْكِرَةً وَتَعِيَهَا أُذُنٌ وَاعِيَةٌ linajʿalahā lakum tadhkiratan wataʿiyahā udhunun wāʿiyatun That We might make it for you a reminder and (that) a conscious ear would be conscious of it. See 69:1

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لِنَجْعَلَهَا لَكُمْ تَذْكِرَةً وَتَعِيَهَا أُذُنٌ وَاعِيَةٌ linajʿalahā lakum tadhkiratan wataʿiyahā udhunun wāʿiyatun That We may make it unto you a Reminder, and that retaining ears might retain it According to the Holyat al-aulia, and Kashshaf Ms., etc. This Verse was revealed about Ali Ibn Abu Talib. The above authorities report that the Holy Prophet said: "O' Ali! God hath commanded me, to always keep thee near me and not away from me - and I prayed to God to make thy ear such that whatever thou hearest of the Word of God and receiveth the knowledge from me, thou forgetteth not but preserve it always. I have been commanded by God to convey to you whatever knowledge I receive from Him" It was based on the strength of this divine gift that Ali on the day of his departure from…

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِي الصُّورِ نَفْخَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ fa-idhā nufikha fī l-ṣūri nafkhatun wāḥidatun When the Trumpet is blown with a single blast

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِي الصُّورِ نَفْخَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ fa-idhā nufikha fī l-ṣūri nafkhatun wāḥidatun Then when the Horn is blown with one blast. Then when the Trumpet will be blown with one blowing (69:13). And the earth and the mountains shall be removed from their places, and crushed with a single crushing (69:14). Then on that Day shall the Event occur (69:15). And the heaven will be rent asunder, for that Day it will be frail and torn up (69:16). And the angels will be on its sides, and eight angels will, that Day, bear the Throne of your Lord above them (69:17). That Day shall you be brought to Judgement, not a secret of you will be hidden (69:18). A Mention of the Horrors of the Day of Judgement Allah informs of the horrors that will take place on the Day…

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:13 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِي الصُّورِ نَفْخَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ fa-idhā nufikha fī l-ṣūri nafkhatun wāḥidatun And when is blown by the Trumpet (Refer to Verse 6:73.) , a single blast This refers to the inevitable event, the day of the Final Judgment. The whole creation will first pass through the destruction, to be raised once again to account for each one's faith and conduct. For the first blast1.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:14 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَحُمِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ وَالْجِبَالُ فَدُكَّتَا دَكَّةً وَاحِدَةً waḥumilati l-arḍu wal-jibālu fadukkatā dakkatan wāḥidatan and the earth and the mountains are lifted and levelled with a single leveling,1

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:14 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَحُمِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ وَالْجِبَالُ فَدُكَّتَا دَكَّةً وَاحِدَةً waḥumilati l-arḍu wal-jibālu fadukkatā dakkatan wāḥidatan And the earth and the mountains are lifted and leveled with one blow (i.e., stroke). See 69:13

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:14 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَحُمِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ وَالْجِبَالُ فَدُكَّتَا دَكَّةً وَاحِدَةً waḥumilati l-arḍu wal-jibālu fadukkatā dakkatan wāḥidatan And the earth and the mountains shall be borne away and crushed with a single crushing (Refer to Verses 89:21, 56:1 - 56:6, Chapter – 101.) The whole physical world will pass away and a new one will be brought into being1. The mountains which stand on the earth since its creation, with their hardness, will be rendered into powder and blown into the atmosphere. For what will happen on that day, to the earth and the mountains2.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَيَوْمَئِذٍ وَقَعَتِ الْوَاقِعَةُ fayawma-idhin waqaʿati l-wāqiʿatu then, on that day, will the Imminent [Hour] befall1

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَيَوْمَئِذٍ وَقَعَتِ الْوَاقِعَةُ fayawma-idhin waqaʿati l-wāqiʿatu Then on that Day, the Occurrence (i.e., Resurrection) will occur. See 69:13

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَيَوْمَئِذٍ وَقَعَتِ الْوَاقِعَةُ fayawma-idhin waqaʿati l-wāqiʿatu On that Day shall come to pass the Great Event (of Reckoning) (Refer to Verse 89:21, 59:1 - 59:6, Chap. 101, 56:1.) See 69:14

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَانْشَقَّتِ السَّمَاءُ فَهِيَ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَاهِيَةٌ wa-inshaqqati l-samāu fahiya yawma-idhin wāhiyatun and the sky will be split open —for it will be frail that day—

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَانْشَقَّتِ السَّمَاءُ فَهِيَ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَاهِيَةٌ wa-inshaqqati l-samāu fahiya yawma-idhin wāhiyatun And the heaven will split (open), for that Day it is infirm.1 See 69:13

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَانْشَقَّتِ السَّمَاءُ فَهِيَ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَاهِيَةٌ wa-inshaqqati l-samāu fahiya yawma-idhin wāhiyatun And shall cleave asunder the heaven (Refer to Verse 84:1 - 84:5.) , so that on that Day it shall be (mere) frail (Nebular State.) See 69:14

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْمَلَكُ عَلَى أَرْجَائِهَا وَيَحْمِلُ عَرْشَ رَبِّكَ فَوْقَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ ثَمَانِيَةٌ wal-malaku ʿalā arjāihā wayaḥmilu ʿarsha rabbika fawqahum yawma-idhin thamāniyatun and the angels will be all over it, and the Throne of your Lord will be borne that day by eight [angels].

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْمَلَكُ عَلَى أَرْجَائِهَا وَيَحْمِلُ عَرْشَ رَبِّكَ فَوْقَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ ثَمَانِيَةٌ wal-malaku ʿalā arjāihā wayaḥmilu ʿarsha rabbika fawqahum yawma-idhin thamāniyatun And the angels are at its edges. And there will bear the Throne of your Lord above them, that Day, eight (of them). See 69:13

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:17 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْمَلَكُ عَلَى أَرْجَائِهَا وَيَحْمِلُ عَرْشَ رَبِّكَ فَوْقَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ ثَمَانِيَةٌ wal-malaku ʿalā arjāihā wayaḥmilu ʿarsha rabbika fawqahum yawma-idhin thamāniyatun And the angels shall be on the sides of it; and above them shall bear that Day 'Arsh' (the Throne of Authority) of thy Lord, eight (The divine attributes of God.) (of them) The 'Arsh' i.e., the seat of the Might, Wisdom and Authority of God, will be borne by eight angels. Angels representing the various aspects of the divine attributes of God.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:18 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ لَا تَخْفَى مِنْكُمْ خَافِيَةٌ yawma-idhin tuʿ'raḍūna lā takhfā minkum khāfiyatun That day you will be exposed: none of your secrets will remain hidden.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:18 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ لَا تَخْفَى مِنْكُمْ خَافِيَةٌ yawma-idhin tuʿ'raḍūna lā takhfā minkum khāfiyatun That Day, you will be exhibited (for judgement); not hidden among you is anything concealed.1 See 69:13

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:18 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ لَا تَخْفَى مِنْكُمْ خَافِيَةٌ yawma-idhin tuʿ'raḍūna lā takhfā minkum khāfiyatun On the Day ye shall be exposed, (and) shall remain not hidden any secret of yours See 69:17

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:19 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ فَيَقُولُ هَاؤُمُ اقْرَءُوْۤا كِتَابِيَهْ fa-ammā man ūtiya kitābahu biyamīnihi fayaqūlu hāumu iq'raū kitābiyah As for him who is given his book in his right hand, he will say, 'Here, take and read my book!

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:19 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ فَيَقُولُ هَاؤُمُ اقْرَءُوْۤا كِتَابِيَهْ fa-ammā man ūtiya kitābahu biyamīnihi fayaqūlu hāumu iq'raū kitābiyah So as for he who is given his record in his right hand, he will say, "Here, read my record! Then as for him who will be given his Record in his right hand will say: "Here! read my Record! (69:19). "Surely, I did believe that I shall meet my account! (69:20). So, he shall be in a life, well-pleasing (69:21). In a lofty Paradise (69:22). The fruits in bunches whereof will be low and near at hand (69:23). Eat and drink at ease for that which you have sent on before you in days past (69:24). The Happiness of the Person Who will Receive His Book in His Right Hand and His Good Situation Allah informs of the happiness of those…

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:19 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ فَيَقُولُ هَاؤُمُ اقْرَءُوْۤا كِتَابِيَهْ fa-ammā man ūtiya kitābahu biyamīnihi fayaqūlu hāumu iq'raū kitābiyah Then he, who is given the (Record) Book (of his deeds) in his right hand (Refer to Verses 17:71, 84:7.) , will say: 'Lo! read ye my book! (Refer to Verse 35:11 - 35:14.) ' The righteous are called the Companions of the Right Hand1. Righteous are said to receive the record of their deeds in their Right Hand2.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:20 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اِنِّیْ ظَنَنْتُ أَنِّي مُلَاقٍ حِسَابِيَهْ innī ẓanantu annī mulāqin ḥisābiyah Indeed I knew that I shall encounter my account.'

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:20 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اِنِّیْ ظَنَنْتُ أَنِّي مُلَاقٍ حِسَابِيَهْ innī ẓanantu annī mulāqin ḥisābiyah Indeed, I was certain that I would be meeting my account." See 69:19

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:20 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اِنِّیْ ظَنَنْتُ أَنِّي مُلَاقٍ حِسَابِيَهْ innī ẓanantu annī mulāqin ḥisābiyah Verily, I did feel (Think – realise.) that I shall meet my account (See Verse 2:46.) See 69:19

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:21 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ fahuwa fī ʿīshatin rāḍiyatin So he will have a pleasant life,

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:21 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ fahuwa fī ʿīshatin rāḍiyatin So he will be in a pleasant life. See 69:19

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:21 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ fahuwa fī ʿīshatin rāḍiyatin So shall he be in a life (of bliss), pleased (with it) See 69:19

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:22 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٍ fī jannatin ʿāliyatin in an elevated garden,

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:22 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٍ fī jannatin ʿāliyatin In an elevated garden. See 69:19

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:22 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٍ fī jannatin ʿāliyatin In the Garden Exalted (See Verses 88:10; 56:12; 52:17; 55:46.) See 69:19

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:23 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُطُوفُهَا دَانِيَةٌ quṭūfuhā dāniyatun whose clusters [of fruits] will be within easy reach.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:23 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُطُوفُهَا دَانِيَةٌ quṭūfuhā dāniyatun Its (fruit) to be picked hanging near. See 69:19

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:23 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُطُوفُهَا دَانِيَةٌ quṭūfuhā dāniyatun The fruits of it being low and near at hand There will not be the least difficulty or hindrance in the enjoyment of the bounties in the heaven. Fruits in bunches will be hanging low within the reach of everyone. All the descriptions of the heavenly bliss, given in the Qur'an, are figurative.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:24 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: كُلُوْۤا وَاشْرَبُوا هَنِيئًا بِمَا أَسْلَفْتُمْ فِي الْأَيَّامِ الْخَالِيَةِ kulū wa-ish'rabū hanīan bimā aslaftum fī l-ayāmi l-khāliyati [He will be told]: 'Enjoy your food and drink, for what you had sent in advance in past days.'

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:24 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: كُلُوْۤا وَاشْرَبُوا هَنِيئًا بِمَا أَسْلَفْتُمْ فِي الْأَيَّامِ الْخَالِيَةِ kulū wa-ish'rabū hanīan bimā aslaftum fī l-ayāmi l-khāliyati (They will be told), "Eat and drink in satisfaction for what you put forth1 in the days past." See 69:19

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:24 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: كُلُوْۤا وَاشْرَبُوا هَنِيئًا بِمَا أَسْلَفْتُمْ فِي الْأَيَّامِ الْخَالِيَةِ kulū wa-ish'rabū hanīan bimā aslaftum fī l-ayāmi l-khāliyati (It will be said unto them): "Eat ye and drink ye for health and pleasure, for what goodness ye sent before (Refer to Verse 77:20.) you, in the days past (Refer to Verse 2:110.) !" Everybody will be justly repaid for his deeds in this life1. The days gone by are referred to the life in this world for then the world be wholly new. This earth and the heaven would have been changed2. There would not be the present conception or the realisation of even the time and the space. The address 'Eat and drink' will be particularly to those righteous ones, who in this life, in the way of the Lord, suffered hunger and thirst and fasted to please the Lord.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:25 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِشِمَالِهِ فَيَقُولُ يَالَيْتَنِي لَمْ أُوتَ كِتَابِيَهْ wa-ammā man ūtiya kitābahu bishimālihi fayaqūlu yālaytanī lam ūta kitābiyah But as for him who is given his book in his left hand, he will say, 'I wish I had not been given my book,

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:25 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِشِمَالِهِ فَيَقُولُ يَالَيْتَنِي لَمْ أُوتَ كِتَابِيَهْ wa-ammā man ūtiya kitābahu bishimālihi fayaqūlu yālaytanī lam ūta kitābiyah But as for he who is given his record in his left hand, he will say, "Oh, I wish I had not been given my record. But as for him who will be given his Record in his left hand, will say: I wish that I had not been given my Record!") (69:25). "And that I had never known how my account is! (69:26). "Would that it had been my end! (69:27). "My wealth has not availed me; (69:28). "My power has gone from me! (69:29). (It will be said): "Seize him and fetter him; (69:30). "Then throw him in the blazing Fire (69:31). "Then fasten him on a chain whereof the length is seventy cubits! (69:32). Verily, he used…

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:25 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِشِمَالِهِ فَيَقُولُ يَالَيْتَنِي لَمْ أُوتَ كِتَابِيَهْ wa-ammā man ūtiya kitābahu bishimālihi fayaqūlu yālaytanī lam ūta kitābiyah But he, who is given the (Record) Book (of deeds) in his left (Refer to Verses 84:10 - 84:12.) hand, will say: "O' that the Book had not been given me! (Refer to Verse 35:11 - 35:14.)" In contrast to the righteous ones, the wicked ones, will be given the records of their deeds in their left hand who would remember their past life with agony and repentance which would be of no avail to them causing them a mental torture. They would like to have not been given any records at all1. Right always means the direction towards God and the left, i.e., to the material world. In this sense it is correct to term the direction 'left' as…

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:26 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَمْ أَدْرِ مَا حِسَابِيَهْ walam adri mā ḥisābiyah nor had I ever known what my account is!

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:26 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَمْ أَدْرِ مَا حِسَابِيَهْ walam adri mā ḥisābiyah And had not known what is my account. See 69:25

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:26 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَمْ أَدْرِ مَا حِسَابِيَهْ walam adri mā ḥisābiyah And I had not known what my account was See 69:25

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:27 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَا‎لَيْتَهَا كَانَتِ الْقَاضِيَةَ yālaytahā kānati l-qāḍiyata I wish death had been the end of it all!

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:27 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَا‎لَيْتَهَا كَانَتِ الْقَاضِيَةَ yālaytahā kānati l-qāḍiyata I wish it (i.e., my death) had been the decisive one.1 See 69:25

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:27 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَا‎لَيْتَهَا كَانَتِ الْقَاضِيَةَ yālaytahā kānati l-qāḍiyata O' would that it had made an end (of me)! They would wish death to have been an end of the world and their life in it, but to their disappointment death was only a transition to a new world, in a new state of reality and actual realization. This has always been the tendency of the evil doers when they face the consequence of their own misdeeds, they wished that they had not been in the know of it. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:28 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا أَغْنَى عَنِّي مَالِيَهْ mā aghnā ʿannī māliyah My wealth did not avail me.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:28 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا أَغْنَى عَنِّي مَالِيَهْ mā aghnā ʿannī māliyah My wealth has not availed me. See 69:25

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:28 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا أَغْنَى عَنِّي مَالِيَهْ mā aghnā ʿannī māliyah Availed me naught my wealth! See 69:27

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:29 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: هَلَكَ عَنِّي سُلْطَانِيَهْ halaka ʿannī sul'ṭāniyah My authority has departed from me.'

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:29 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: هَلَكَ عَنِّي سُلْطَانِيَهْ halaka ʿannī sul'ṭāniyah Gone from me is my authority."1 See 69:25

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:29 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: هَلَكَ عَنِّي سُلْطَانِيَهْ halaka ʿannī sul'ṭāniyah And hath gone from me (all) my power! Every soul would have lost hold on itself and the power and authority, as a whole, would be only of God and none else. He would be the only King, the Master, the Lord of the Day1.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:30 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: خُذُوهُ فَغُلُّوهُ khudhūhu faghullūhu [The angels will be told:] 'Seize him, and fetter him!

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:30 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: خُذُوهُ فَغُلُّوهُ khudhūhu faghullūhu (Allah will say), "Seize him and shackle him. See 69:25

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:30 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: خُذُوهُ فَغُلُّوهُ khudhūhu faghullūhu (It will he said unto him)'. "Seize him ye (angels)" and fetter him! See 69:29

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:31 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ الْجَحِيمَ صَلُّوهُ thumma l-jaḥīma ṣallūhu Then put him into hell.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:31 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ الْجَحِيمَ صَلُّوهُ thumma l-jaḥīma ṣallūhu Then into Hellfire drive him. See 69:25

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:31 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ الْجَحِيمَ صَلُّوهُ thumma l-jaḥīma ṣallūhu Then into the blazing fire burn him! See 69:29

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:32 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُهَا سَبْعُونَ ذِرَاعًا فَاسْلُكُوهُ thumma fī sil'silatin dharʿuhā sabʿūna dhirāʿan fa-us'lukūhu Then, in a chain whose length is seventy cubits, bind him.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:32 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُهَا سَبْعُونَ ذِرَاعًا فَاسْلُكُوهُ thumma fī sil'silatin dharʿuhā sabʿūna dhirāʿan fa-us'lukūhu Then into a chain whose length is seventy cubits insert him." See 69:25

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:32 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُهَا سَبْعُونَ ذِرَاعًا فَاسْلُكُوهُ thumma fī sil'silatin dharʿuhā sabʿūna dhirāʿan fa-us'lukūhu Then into a chain, of the length of cubits, tie him into! 'Seventy Cubits' represent the enormity of the size and the weight and grievous nature of it. Qur'an has a special reference to the number seven and its multiples, particularly in reference to the several stages or the aspects of hell as it is said. The justification for that is the five external and two internal senses through which the devilish temptations are affected1. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:33 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّهُ كَانَ لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ innahu kāna lā yu'minu bil-lahi l-ʿaẓīmi Indeed he had no faith in Allah, the All-supreme,

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:33 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّهُ كَانَ لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ innahu kāna lā yu'minu bil-lahi l-ʿaẓīmi Indeed, he did not used to believe in Allah, the Most Great. See 69:25

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:33 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّهُ كَانَ لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ innahu kāna lā yu'minu bil-lahi l-ʿaẓīmi Verily he used not to believe in God, the Great! See 69:32

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:34 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَى طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ walā yaḥuḍḍu ʿalā ṭaʿāmi l-mis'kīni and he did not urge the feeding of the needy,

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:34 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَى طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ walā yaḥuḍḍu ʿalā ṭaʿāmi l-mis'kīni Nor did he encourage the feeding of the poor. See 69:25

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:34 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَى طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ walā yaḥuḍḍu ʿalā ṭaʿāmi l-mis'kīni And he urged not the feeding of the poor The expression includes obstructing or preventing the dispensation of the poor-rate 'Zakat' and 'Khums' and the aims to the poor. Not felt as necessary - Indicates the sympathy of the needy and service to them here, is of no avail in the hereafter. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:35 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَيْسَ لَهُ الْيَوْمَ هَاهُنَا حَمِيمٌ falaysa lahu l-yawma hāhunā ḥamīmun so he has no friend here today,

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:35 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَيْسَ لَهُ الْيَوْمَ هَاهُنَا حَمِيمٌ falaysa lahu l-yawma hāhunā ḥamīmun So there is not for him here this Day any devoted friend. See 69:25

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:35 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَيْسَ لَهُ الْيَوْمَ هَاهُنَا حَمِيمٌ falaysa lahu l-yawma hāhunā ḥamīmun So for him here today there is not a friend See 69:34

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:36 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا طَعَامٌ إِلَّا مِنْ غِسْلِينٍ walā ṭaʿāmun illā min ghis'līnin nor any food except pus,

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:36 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا طَعَامٌ إِلَّا مِنْ غِسْلِينٍ walā ṭaʿāmun illā min ghis'līnin Nor any food except from the discharge of wounds. See 69:25

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:36 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا طَعَامٌ إِلَّا مِنْ غِسْلِينٍ walā ṭaʿāmun illā min ghis'līnin And no food is for him save the refuse of the wash of wounds! See 69:34

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:37 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا يَأْكُلُهُ إِلَّا الْخَاطِءُونَ lā yakuluhu illā l-khāṭiūna which no one shall eat except the iniquitous.'

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:37 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا يَأْكُلُهُ إِلَّا الْخَاطِءُونَ lā yakuluhu illā l-khāṭiūna None will eat it except the sinners. See 69:25

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:37 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا يَأْكُلُهُ إِلَّا الْخَاطِءُونَ lā yakuluhu illā l-khāṭiūna Which shall eat none but the sinners! See 69:34

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:38 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِمَا تُبْصِرُونَ falā uq'simu bimā tub'ṣirūna I swear by what you see

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:38 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِمَا تُبْصِرُونَ falā uq'simu bimā tub'ṣirūna So I swear by what you see. So, I swear by whatsoever you see (69:38). And by whatsoever you see not (69:39). That this is verily the word of an honored Messenger (69:40). It is not the word of a poet, little is that you believe (69:41). Nor is it the word of a soothsayer, little is that you remember (69:42). This is the revelation sent down from the Lord of all that exists (69:43). The Qur'an is the Speech of Allah Allah swears by His creation, in which some of His signs can be seen in His creatures. These also indicate the perfection of His Names and Attributes. He then swears by the hidden things that they cannot see. This is an oath swearing that the Qur'an is His Speech, His…

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:38 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِمَا تُبْصِرُونَ falā uq'simu bimā tub'ṣirūna So, I swear (Refer to Verses 56:75, 90:1.) by what ye see! Falsehood always yields and gets vanished, giving place to Truth. Though one might deny God or call His word a lie or doubt the Truth and term it as poetry or folklore, but the nature, even that which is seen by man, the visible world itself is quite sufficient to prove the truth and establish it. This refers to the Holy Qur'an being the Word of God and not the fabrication of the Holy Prophet.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:39 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا لَا تُبْصِرُونَ wamā lā tub'ṣirūna and what you do not see:

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:39 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا لَا تُبْصِرُونَ wamā lā tub'ṣirūna And what you do not see. See 69:38

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:39 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا لَا تُبْصِرُونَ wamā lā tub'ṣirūna And what ye see (All-Enveloping - nothing left over.) not! See 69:38

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:40 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ innahu laqawlu rasūlin karīmin it is indeed the speech of a noble apostle,

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:40 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ innahu laqawlu rasūlin karīmin (That) indeed, it (i.e., the Qur’ān) is the word of a noble Messenger. See 69:38

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:40 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ innahu laqawlu rasūlin karīmin Verily, it is the word of the most honoured Apostle! The Holy Qur'an is the utterance of the Word of God by the Holy Prophet, who is God's Honoured one.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:41 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شَاعِرٍ قَلِيلًا مَا تُؤْمِنُونَ wamā huwa biqawli shāʿirin qalīlan mā tu'minūna and it is not the speech of a poet. Little is the faith that you have!

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:41 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شَاعِرٍ قَلِيلًا مَا تُؤْمِنُونَ wamā huwa biqawli shāʿirin qalīlan mā tu'minūna And it is not the word of a poet; little do you believe. See 69:38

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:41 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شَاعِرٍ قَلِيلًا مَا تُؤْمِنُونَ wamā huwa biqawli shāʿirin qalīlan mā tu'minūna And it is not the word of a poet; (How) little it is what ye believe? See 69:40

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:42 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا بِقَوْلِ كَاهِنٍ قَلِيلًا مَا تَذَكَّرُونَ walā biqawli kāhinin qalīlan mā tadhakkarūna Nor is it the speech of a soothsayer. Little is the admonition that you take!

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:42 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا بِقَوْلِ كَاهِنٍ قَلِيلًا مَا تَذَكَّرُونَ walā biqawli kāhinin qalīlan mā tadhakkarūna Nor the word of a soothsayer; little do you remember. See 69:38

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:42 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا بِقَوْلِ كَاهِنٍ قَلِيلًا مَا تَذَكَّرُونَ walā biqawli kāhinin qalīlan mā tadhakkarūna Nor the word of a soothsayer; (How) little it is what ye reflect? See 69:40

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:43 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: تَنْزِيلٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ tanzīlun min rabbi l-ʿālamīna Gradually sent down from the Lord of all the worlds.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:43 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: تَنْزِيلٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ tanzīlun min rabbi l-ʿālamīna (It is) a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. See 69:38

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:43 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: تَنْزِيلٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ tanzīlun min rabbi l-ʿālamīna It is a despatch descended from the Lord of the worlds See 69:40

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:44 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَوْ تَقَوَّلَ عَلَيْنَا بَعْضَ الْأَقَاوِيلِ walaw taqawwala ʿalaynā baʿḍa l-aqāwīli Had he faked any sayings in Our name,

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:44 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَوْ تَقَوَّلَ عَلَيْنَا بَعْضَ الْأَقَاوِيلِ walaw taqawwala ʿalaynā baʿḍa l-aqāwīli And if he (i.e., Muḥammad) had made up about Us some (false) sayings. And if he had forged a false saying concerning Us (69:44). We surely would have seized him by his right hand (69:45). And then We certainly would have cut off Al-Watin from him (69:46). And none of you could have prevented it from him (69:47). And verily, this is a Reminder for those who have Taqwa (69:48). And verily, We know that there are some among you that deny (69:49). And indeed it will be an anguish for the disbeliever (69:50). And verily, it (this Qur'an) is an absolute truth with certainty (69:51). So, glorify the Name of your Lord, the Most Great (69:52). If the Prophet SAW Forged Anything against Allah, Then Allah would Punish Him…

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:44 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَوْ تَقَوَّلَ عَلَيْنَا بَعْضَ الْأَقَاوِيلِ walaw taqawwala ʿalaynā baʿḍa l-aqāwīli And if (Our Apostle Muhammad) had fabricated against Us any of the sayings This divine undertaking is to assert that those who have been commissioned by God, cannot but deliver whatever they are charged with, and God never allows them to forge anything of their own on His behalf. It does not mean that the imposters or the false prophets who forge lies and falsely claim to have been commissioned by God, need not be exposed - in this manner, the lack of evidence is itself sufficient to expose them. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:45 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَأَخَذْنَا مِنْهُ بِالْيَمِينِ la-akhadhnā min'hu bil-yamīni We would have surely seized him by the right hand

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:45 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَأَخَذْنَا مِنْهُ بِالْيَمِينِ la-akhadhnā min'hu bil-yamīni We would have seized him by the right hand.1 See 69:44

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:45 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَأَخَذْنَا مِنْهُ بِالْيَمِينِ la-akhadhnā min'hu bil-yamīni Certainly, would We have seized him by the right hand See 69:44

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:46 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ لَقَطَعْنَا مِنْهُ الْوَتِينَ thumma laqaṭaʿnā min'hu l-watīna and then cut off his aorta,

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:46 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ لَقَطَعْنَا مِنْهُ الْوَتِينَ thumma laqaṭaʿnā min'hu l-watīna Then We would have cut from him the aorta.1 See 69:44

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:46 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ لَقَطَعْنَا مِنْهُ الْوَتِينَ thumma laqaṭaʿnā min'hu l-watīna Then certainly would We have cut off his aorta See 69:44

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:47 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَمَا مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حَاجِزِينَ famā minkum min aḥadin ʿanhu ḥājizīna and none of you could have held Us off from him.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:47 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَمَا مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حَاجِزِينَ famā minkum min aḥadin ʿanhu ḥājizīna And there is no one of you who could prevent (Us) from him. See 69:44

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:47 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَمَا مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حَاجِزِينَ famā minkum min aḥadin ʿanhu ḥājizīna And of you not one could have withheld (Us) against him See 69:44

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:48 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّهُ لَتَذْكِرَةٌ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ wa-innahu latadhkiratun lil'muttaqīna Indeed it is a reminder for the Godwary.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:48 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّهُ لَتَذْكِرَةٌ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ wa-innahu latadhkiratun lil'muttaqīna And indeed, it (i.e., the Qur’ān) is a reminder for the righteous. See 69:44

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:48 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّهُ لَتَذْكِرَةٌ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ wa-innahu latadhkiratun lil'muttaqīna And verily, it is a reminder unto the pious (Those who guard themselves against evil) ones. (Refer to Verse 2:142 for the part of the Verse related to the Holy Qur'an as a source of guidance, and to 3:137 for the part of the Verse related to the Holy Qur'an as a reminder.) See 69:44

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:49 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّا لَنَعْلَمُ أَنَّ مِنْكُمْ مُكَذِّبِينَ wa-innā lanaʿlamu anna minkum mukadhibīna Indeed We know that there are some among you who deny [it].

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:49 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّا لَنَعْلَمُ أَنَّ مِنْكُمْ مُكَذِّبِينَ wa-innā lanaʿlamu anna minkum mukadhibīna And indeed, We know that among you are deniers. See 69:44

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:49 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّا لَنَعْلَمُ أَنَّ مِنْكُمْ مُكَذِّبِينَ wa-innā lanaʿlamu anna minkum mukadhibīna And verily know We that some of you are the beliers See 69:44

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:50 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّهُ لَحَسْرَةٌ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ wa-innahu laḥasratun ʿalā l-kāfirīna And indeed it will be a [matter of] regret for the faithless.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:50 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّهُ لَحَسْرَةٌ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ wa-innahu laḥasratun ʿalā l-kāfirīna And indeed, it will be (a cause of) regret upon the disbelievers. See 69:44

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:50 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّهُ لَحَسْرَةٌ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ wa-innahu laḥasratun ʿalā l-kāfirīna And verily it is a great grief unto the disbelievers See 69:44

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:51 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّهُ لَحَقُّ الْيَقِينِ wa-innahu laḥaqqu l-yaqīni It is indeed certain truth.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:51 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّهُ لَحَقُّ الْيَقِينِ wa-innahu laḥaqqu l-yaqīni And indeed, it is the truth of certainty. See 69:44

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:51 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّهُ لَحَقُّ الْيَقِينِ wa-innahu laḥaqqu l-yaqīni And verily, it is the very Truth, fully assured (Refer to Verses 102:5, 102:7.) Certainty could be in variant degrees: (1) The knowledge acquired through external evidence, which is to a degree of certainty, is called the ''Ilm al-Yaqin' i.e., the knowledge of the certainty1; (2) Seeing something with one's eye also, leads to a kind of certainty which also sometimes proves to be a deception or the limitation of our vision. It is called 'Ain al-Yaqin', i.e., the vision of the certainty2; (3) 'Haqq al-Yaqin' the Certainty Proper Doubtless which could never be disproved. It is that degree of certainty referred to here.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:52 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ fasabbiḥ bi-is'mi rabbika l-ʿaẓīmi So celebrate the Name of your Lord, the All-supreme.

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:52 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ fasabbiḥ bi-is'mi rabbika l-ʿaẓīmi So exalt the name of your Lord, the Most Great. See 69:44

item.title: Al-Haaqqa:52 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ fasabbiḥ bi-is'mi rabbika l-ʿaẓīmi So Hallow by the name of thy Lord, The Great! See 69:51

item.title: Al-Hadid:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ sabbaḥa lillahi mā fī l-samāwāti wal-arḍi wahuwa l-ʿazīzu l-ḥakīmu Whatever there is in the heavens glorifies Allah and [whatever there is on] the earth and He is the All-mighty, the All-wise.

item.title: Al-Hadid:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ sabbaḥa lillahi mā fī l-samāwāti wal-arḍi wahuwa l-ʿazīzu l-ḥakīmu Whatever is in the heavens and earth exalts Allah,1 and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ وَالظَّاهِرُ وَالْبَاطِنُ ۖ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ He is Al-Awwal and Al-Akhir, Az-Zahir and Al-Batin. And He is the All-Knower of everything. There are about ten and some odd number of different sayings collected from the scholars of Tafsir regarding the explanation of this Ayah. Al-Bukhari said, "Yahya said, 'Az-Zahir: knowing all things, Al-Batin: knowing all things.'" Our Shaykh Al-Hafiz Al-Mizzi said, "Yahya is Ibn Ziyad Al-Farra', who authored a book entitled Ma'ani Al-Qur'an." There are Hadiths mentioned about this. Among them, Imam Ahmad recorded that Abu Hurayrah said that the Messenger of Allah SAW would recite this supplication while going…

item.title: Al-Hadid:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ sabbaḥa lillahi mā fī l-samāwāti wal-arḍi wahuwa l-ʿazīzu l-ḥakīmu Celebrateth the praise of God, whatever is in the heavens and the earth; and He is the Ever-Prevalent, the All-Wise (Refer to Verse 17:44.) The praise or the glorification of the creatures of the Almighty Creator of the Universe is their serving Him, governed by His laws, the laws of nature which none could ever go against. Surrender is of two kinds, the helplessness under which an individual or a group of individuals cannot but act in a given pattern, and while acting realise the Wisdom and the Grace endowed in the behaviour or the pattern and then glorifying the Authority controlling the affairs. The second kind of surrender is, the voluntary submission adopting a pattern or a mode of thought or…

item.title: Al-Hadid:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ lahu mul'ku l-samāwāti wal-arḍi yuḥ'yī wayumītu wahuwa ʿalā kulli shayin qadīrun To Him belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth: He gives life and brings death, and He has power over all things.

item.title: Al-Hadid:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ lahu mul'ku l-samāwāti wal-arḍi yuḥ'yī wayumītu wahuwa ʿalā kulli shayin qadīrun His is the dominion of the heavens and earth. He gives life and causes death, and He is over all things competent. See 57:1

item.title: Al-Hadid:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ lahu mul'ku l-samāwāti wal-arḍi yuḥ'yī wayumītu wahuwa ʿalā kulli shayin qadīrun His is the kingdom of the heavens and the earth; He causeth life and causeth death; and He, over all hath power Compare this Verse with: "Thy kingdom come, Thy will be done on earth, as it is in heaven." (Math 6/10). The manner in which the Bible of the Church, founded in the name of Jesus which suggests that somebody else rules on earth and the will of someone else other than God, is done on it and man is yet praying for the kingdom of God to come and God's will to be done. The Holy Qur'an refutes such a belief and declares that to God, to none else, belongs the kingdom both of the heavens…

item.title: Al-Hadid:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْءَاخِرُ وَالظَّاهِرُ وَالْبَاطِنُ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِیْمٌ huwa l-awalu wal-ākhiru wal-ẓāhiru wal-bāṭinu wahuwa bikulli shayin ʿalīmun He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and He has knowledge of all things.

item.title: Al-Hadid:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْءَاخِرُ وَالظَّاهِرُ وَالْبَاطِنُ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِیْمٌ huwa l-awalu wal-ākhiru wal-ẓāhiru wal-bāṭinu wahuwa bikulli shayin ʿalīmun He is the First1 and the Last,2 the Ascendant3 and the Intimate,4 and He is, of all things, Knowing. See 57:1

item.title: Al-Hadid:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
