item.description: قَالَتِ الْأَعْرَابُ اٰمَنَّا قُلْ لَمْ تُؤْمِنُوْۤا وَلَكِنْ قُولُوْۤا أَسْلَمْنَا وَلَمَّا يَدْخُلِ الْاِیْمَانُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ وَإِنْ تُطِيعُوْۤا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ لَا يَلِتْكُمْ مِنْ أَعْمَالِكُمْ شَيْئًا إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ qālati l-aʿrābu āmannā qul lam tu'minū walākin qūlū aslamnā walammā yadkhuli l-īmānu fī qulūbikum wa-in tuṭīʿū l-laha warasūlahu lā yalit'kum min aʿmālikum shayan inna l-laha ghafūrun raḥīmun Say the desert Arabs "We believe." Say thou (unto them): "Ye believed not, but say ye, "We submit, for faith hath not yet entered (Refer to verse 29:10.) your hearts; and if ye obey God and His Apostle, He will lessen not aught of your deeds; Verily God is Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful." The desert tribe of Bani-Asad who were Muslims merely for namesake and who had refused to accompany the Holy Prophet on the pilgrimage, driven by the miseries of a famine, flocked into Madina…

item.title: Al-Hujuraat:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَرْتَابُوْۤا وَجَاهَدُوا بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ اُولٰٓئِكَ هُمُ الصَّادِقُونَ innamā l-mu'minūna alladhīna āmanū bil-lahi warasūlihi thumma lam yartābū wajāhadū bi-amwālihim wa-anfusihim fī sabīli l-lahi ulāika humu l-ṣādiqūna The faithful are only those who have attained faith in Allah and His Apostle and then have never doubted, and who wage jihād with their possessions and their persons in the way of Allah. It is they who are the truthful.1

item.title: Al-Hujuraat:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَرْتَابُوْۤا وَجَاهَدُوا بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ اُولٰٓئِكَ هُمُ الصَّادِقُونَ innamā l-mu'minūna alladhīna āmanū bil-lahi warasūlihi thumma lam yartābū wajāhadū bi-amwālihim wa-anfusihim fī sabīli l-lahi ulāika humu l-ṣādiqūna The believers are only the ones who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and then doubt not but strive with their properties and their lives in the cause of Allah. It is those who are the truthful. See 49:14

item.title: Al-Hujuraat:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَرْتَابُوْۤا وَجَاهَدُوا بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ اُولٰٓئِكَ هُمُ الصَّادِقُونَ innamā l-mu'minūna alladhīna āmanū bil-lahi warasūlihi thumma lam yartābū wajāhadū bi-amwālihim wa-anfusihim fī sabīli l-lahi ulāika humu l-ṣādiqūna The believers are only those who believe in God and His Apostle, they doubt (Compare this to the doubting at Hudaibiyya. Refer to note on verse 48:25.) not thereafter, and strive (fight) they with their wealth and their lives in the way of God; they are the truthful (Refer to verses 9:119, 2:177.) ones. For a fuller description of a true 'Mu'min' (a sincere believer) and the genuine Truthful and the Pious ones for whom the verse 13 above assigns superiority or the honour in God's view.1 This verse gives out clearly that those who doubted at Hudaibiyya and those who at 'Jihad' the…

item.title: Al-Hujuraat:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ أَتُعَلِّمُونَ اللَّهَ بِدِينِكُمْ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِیْمٌ qul atuʿallimūna l-laha bidīnikum wal-lahu yaʿlamu mā fī l-samāwāti wamā fī l-arḍi wal-lahu bikulli shayin ʿalīmun Say, 'Will you inform Allah about your faith while Allah knows whatever there is in the heavens and whatever there is in the earth, and Allah has knowledge of all things?'

item.title: Al-Hujuraat:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ أَتُعَلِّمُونَ اللَّهَ بِدِينِكُمْ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِیْمٌ qul atuʿallimūna l-laha bidīnikum wal-lahu yaʿlamu mā fī l-samāwāti wamā fī l-arḍi wal-lahu bikulli shayin ʿalīmun Say, "Would you acquaint Allah with your religion while Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is Knowing of all things?" See 49:14

item.title: Al-Hujuraat:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ أَتُعَلِّمُونَ اللَّهَ بِدِينِكُمْ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِیْمٌ qul atuʿallimūna l-laha bidīnikum wal-lahu yaʿlamu mā fī l-samāwāti wamā fī l-arḍi wal-lahu bikulli shayin ʿalīmun Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!): "What! Teach ye God about your religion, and God knoweth whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth; And God knoweth all things." See 49:15

item.title: Al-Hujuraat:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ أَسْلَمُوْۤا قُلْ لَا تَمُنُّوْۤا عَلَيَّ إِسْلَامَكُمْ بَلِ اللَّهُ يَمُنُّ عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْ هَدَاكُمْ لِلْإِيمَانِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ yamunnūna ʿalayka an aslamū qul lā tamunnū ʿalayya is'lāmakum bali l-lahu yamunnu ʿalaykum an hadākum lil'īmāni in kuntum ṣādiqīna They count it as a favour to you that they have embraced Islam. Say, 'Do not count it as a favour to me your embracing of Islam. Rather it is Allah who has done you a favour in that He has guided you to faith, should you be truthful.1

item.title: Al-Hujuraat:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ أَسْلَمُوْۤا قُلْ لَا تَمُنُّوْۤا عَلَيَّ إِسْلَامَكُمْ بَلِ اللَّهُ يَمُنُّ عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْ هَدَاكُمْ لِلْإِيمَانِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ yamunnūna ʿalayka an aslamū qul lā tamunnū ʿalayya is'lāmakum bali l-lahu yamunnu ʿalaykum an hadākum lil'īmāni in kuntum ṣādiqīna They consider it a favor to you that they have accepted Islām. Say, "Do not consider your Islām a favor to me. Rather, Allah has conferred favor upon you that He has guided you to the faith, if you should be truthful." See 49:14

item.title: Al-Hujuraat:17 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ أَسْلَمُوْۤا قُلْ لَا تَمُنُّوْۤا عَلَيَّ إِسْلَامَكُمْ بَلِ اللَّهُ يَمُنُّ عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْ هَدَاكُمْ لِلْإِيمَانِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ yamunnūna ʿalayka an aslamū qul lā tamunnū ʿalayya is'lāmakum bali l-lahu yamunnu ʿalaykum an hadākum lil'īmāni in kuntum ṣādiqīna Lay they an obligation upon thee that they have submitted (embraced Islam) (Submitted themselves to God.) Say thou: "Lay ye not upon me any obligation by your submission (Islam) (Submitted themselves to God.) rather God layeth an obligation upon you that He guided you unto the faith if ye be truthful ones." Let none think that by embracing Islam, he has in any way obliged God or even the Holy Prophet. On the other hand, it is God's obligation on him for if God by His infinite mercy had not arranged for the guidance of man through the series of his chosen…

item.title: Al-Hujuraat:18 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ غَيْبَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ inna l-laha yaʿlamu ghayba l-samāwāti wal-arḍi wal-lahu baṣīrun bimā taʿmalūna Indeed Allah knows the Unseen of the heavens and the earth, and Allah sees best what you do.'

item.title: Al-Hujuraat:18 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ غَيْبَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ inna l-laha yaʿlamu ghayba l-samāwāti wal-arḍi wal-lahu baṣīrun bimā taʿmalūna Indeed, Allah knows the unseen (aspects) of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is Seeing of what you do. See 49:14

item.title: Al-Hujuraat:18 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ غَيْبَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ inna l-laha yaʿlamu ghayba l-samāwāti wal-arḍi wal-lahu baṣīrun bimā taʿmalūna Verily God knoweth (all) the unseen things of the heavens and the earth; and God seeth (all) whatever ye do. See 49:17

item.title: Al-Humaza:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيْلٌ لِكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ لُمَزَةٍ waylun likulli humazatin lumazatin Woe to every scandal-monger and slanderer,

item.title: Al-Humaza:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيْلٌ لِكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ لُمَزَةٍ waylun likulli humazatin lumazatin Woe to every scorner and mocker. فِي عَمَدٍ مُّمَدَّدَةٍ In pillars stretched forth. Atiyah Al-'Awfi said, "Pillars of Iron." As-Suddi said, "Made of fire." Al-'Awfi reported from Ibn 'Abbas, "He will make them enter pillars stretched forth, meaning there will be columns over them, and they will have chains on their necks, and the gates (of Hell) will be shut upon them." This is the end of the Tafsir of Surat Al-Humazah, and all praise and thanks are due to Allah.

item.title: Al-Humaza:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيْلٌ لِكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ لُمَزَةٍ waylun likulli humazatin lumazatin Woe unto every slanderer, defamer! Akhnas Ibn Quraishe Saqfi used to backbite the Holy Prophet to Walid Ibn Moghaira who listened to Akhnas with special interest and used to spread all sorts of falsehood against the Holy personality in order to obstruct the outsiders coming to Mecca during the annual pilgrimage period, from coming in contact with the Holy Prophet or listening to the preaching of the truth. Akhnas was also very wealthy and very avaricious to pile up wealth and was very much infatuated of his extraordinary economic position and his social influence. Akhnas was busy slandering the Apostle of God and spreading false notes against the truth preached by him. This Surah was revealed with the immediate application of the reference to Akhnas and his comrades, but it applies to…

item.title: Al-Humaza:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي جَمَعَ مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ alladhī jamaʿa mālan waʿaddadahu who amasses wealth and counts it over.

item.title: Al-Humaza:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي جَمَعَ مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ alladhī jamaʿa mālan waʿaddadahu Who collects wealth and (continuously) counts it.1 See 104:1

item.title: Al-Humaza:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي جَمَعَ مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ alladhī jamaʿa mālan waʿaddadahu Who amasseth wealth and hoardeth it See 104:1

item.title: Al-Humaza:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ yaḥsabu anna mālahu akhladahu He supposes his wealth will make him immortal!

item.title: Al-Humaza:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ yaḥsabu anna mālahu akhladahu He thinks that his wealth will make him immortal. See 104:1

item.title: Al-Humaza:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ yaḥsabu anna mālahu akhladahu Deemeth he that his wealth will make him live forever (Eternal.) The question here is a warning to the one who avariciously piles up wealth that whatever' amount of it, one might possess, it shall go, and shall not remain with him for ever, for he has to pass away from here empty-handed as a destitute. Hence, if anyone thinks that his wealth will abide with him for ever, he is fooled by his imagination for it is a matter of certainty that it is only a passing show, with a great many commitments with it, in its disposal, why should man toil more than what he must reasonably do and why should he be proud of a thing which is of only a temporary value and of no permanent worth or…

item.title: Al-Humaza:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا لَيُنْبَذَنَّ فِي الْحُطَمَةِ kallā layunbadhanna fī l-ḥuṭamati No indeed! He will surely be cast into the Crusher.

item.title: Al-Humaza:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا لَيُنْبَذَنَّ فِي الْحُطَمَةِ kallā layunbadhanna fī l-ḥuṭamati No! He will surely be thrown into the Crusher.1 See 104:1

item.title: Al-Humaza:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا لَيُنْبَذَنَّ فِي الْحُطَمَةِ kallā layunbadhanna fī l-ḥuṭamati Nay! verily, he shall be flung into the 'Hutama (Consuming or a crushing disaster.) '! The root of 'Hutama' is 'Hatima', i.e., getting rendered or broken into pieces, i.e., it will be crushed, destroyed and thrown into Hell before the eyes of those who spent their lives in amassing it and prided over it and got intoxicated of it, thinking it to be of a permanent value to them - deprived the others of their share, did not spend of it for the benefit of the others who suffered miserably for want of something of it. Besides they had been so much maddened by the acquisition of their wealth they had forgotten God who had allowed them to have it, and thought themselves totally independent of Him and acted as their devilish…

item.title: Al-Humaza:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْحُطَمَةُ wamā adrāka mā l-ḥuṭamatu And what will show you what is the Crusher?

item.title: Al-Humaza:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْحُطَمَةُ wamā adrāka mā l-ḥuṭamatu And what can make you know what is the Crusher? See 104:1

item.title: Al-Humaza:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْحُطَمَةُ wamā adrāka mā l-ḥuṭamatu What maketh thee know what the 'Hutama' is? The question put in this verse about 'Hutama' means to signify that man in this life, not having seen anything like it, cannot correctly visualise or understand what 'Hutama' would actually be.

item.title: Al-Humaza:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: نَارُ اللَّهِ الْمُوقَدَةُ nāru l-lahi l-mūqadatu [It is] the fire of Allah, set ablaze,

item.title: Al-Humaza:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: نَارُ اللَّهِ الْمُوقَدَةُ nāru l-lahi l-mūqadatu It is the fire of Allah, (eternally) fueled. See 104:1

item.title: Al-Humaza:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: نَارُ اللَّهِ الْمُوقَدَةُ nāru l-lahi l-mūqadatu It is the fire God hath kindled The fire which will not be restricted to effect only the outer body of the individual but penetrating to the innermost parts of the individual's existence as well as cover the whole of him, enveloping him in huge columns from all sides. It will be a fire kindled by God Whose existence was disbelieved and Whose authority was rejected and disobeyed.

item.title: Al-Humaza:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّتِي تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى الْأَفْئِدَةِ allatī taṭṭaliʿu ʿalā l-afidati which will overspread the hearts.

item.title: Al-Humaza:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّتِي تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى الْأَفْئِدَةِ allatī taṭṭaliʿu ʿalā l-afidati Which mounts directed at the hearts.1 See 104:1

item.title: Al-Humaza:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّتِي تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى الْأَفْئِدَةِ allatī taṭṭaliʿu ʿalā l-afidati Which shall mount above the hearts (Indicates that it is not a fire coming through physical channels otherwise it would not mount to the hearts – (A.P.).) See 104:6

item.title: Al-Humaza:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّهَا عَلَيْهِمْ مُؤْصَدَةٌ innahā ʿalayhim mu'ṣadatun Indeed it will close in upon them

item.title: Al-Humaza:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّهَا عَلَيْهِمْ مُؤْصَدَةٌ innahā ʿalayhim mu'ṣadatun Indeed, it (i.e., Hellfire) will be closed down upon them. See 104:1

item.title: Al-Humaza:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّهَا عَلَيْهِمْ مُؤْصَدَةٌ innahā ʿalayhim mu'ṣadatun It shall be upon them, closed over It will cover the individual, all around him, i.e., the punishment will be to every part of the individual, outer or the innermost, which will be drowned in the fire, and the columns of the fire will be rising even high above him.

item.title: Al-Humaza:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي عَمَدٍ مُمَدَّدَةٍ fī ʿamadin mumaddadatin in outstretched columns.

item.title: Al-Humaza:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي عَمَدٍ مُمَدَّدَةٍ fī ʿamadin mumaddadatin In extended columns.1 See 104:1

item.title: Al-Humaza:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي عَمَدٍ مُمَدَّدَةٍ fī ʿamadin mumaddadatin In columns outstretched See 104:8

item.title: Al-Ikhlaas:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ qul huwa l-lahu aḥadun Say, 'He is Allah, the One.

item.title: Al-Ikhlaas:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ qul huwa l-lahu aḥadun Say, "He is Allah, (who is) One.1 وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ And there is none comparable to Him. "This means He does not have a spouse." This is as Allah says: بَدِيعُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۖ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لَهُ وَلَدٌ وَلَمْ تَكُن لَّهُ صَاحِبَةٌ ۖ وَخَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ He is the Originator of the heavens and the earth. How can He have children when He has no wife He created all things. (6:101) Meaning: He owns everything and He created everything. So how can He have a peer among His creatures who can be equal to Him, or a relative who can resemble Him? Glorified, Exalted and far removed is Allah from such a thing. Allah says: وَقَالُوا اتَّخَذَ الرَّحْمَٰنُ وَلَدًا - لَّقَدْ جِئْتُمْ شَيْئًا إِدًّا - تَكَادُ السَّمَاوَاتُ يَتَفَطَّرْنَ مِنْهُ وَتَنشَقُّ…

item.title: Al-Ikhlaas:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ qul huwa l-lahu aḥadun Say: ''He, God, is ONE (alone) The Jews asked the Holy Prophet to describe the identity or to relate the genealogy of God and the Messenger Angel brought this Surah. There is a vast difference between the two Arabic words ''Ahad' and 'Wahid' both commonly thought to mean Oneness. To indicate the Unity of God, it is said in this verse that God is 'Ahad' i.e., One, One in the sense of the Absolute Oneness of His Essential Existence, not in the numerical sense of the numeral which has its second and third but the One which has no second of it. The expression one, is in the sense of being the ONLY in conceiving Whose existence all the faculties of the human intellect are helpless. He is such a one that…

item.title: Al-Ikhlaas:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ al-lahu l-ṣamadu Allah is the All-embracing.

item.title: Al-Ikhlaas:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ al-lahu l-ṣamadu Allah, the Eternal Refuge.1 See 112:1

item.title: Al-Ikhlaas:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ al-lahu l-ṣamadu God, the Needless (Perfect - the compact - independent- on Whom all depend. See the note.) 'Samad', i.e., independent of any one - All perfect - The One to Whom recourse is made by everything Eternal for its needs, both for existence and for perfection. The One who needs no subsistence of any kind – Self existing to understand Whose existence every mind is drowned in marvel and wonder. Nothing is hidden from His all-enveloping Knowledge - Is not accommodable in anything not even in intellect, Infinite in all aspects of the existence and attributes. In fact, the names or the attributes mentioned to describe His existence or its nature, are unconveyable in their fullness hence cannot be translated to give the correct or the fullest sense or the meaning of the terms. All the meanings…

item.title: Al-Ikhlaas:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ lam yalid walam yūlad He neither begat, nor was begotten,

item.title: Al-Ikhlaas:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ lam yalid walam yūlad He neither begets nor is born. See 112:1

item.title: Al-Ikhlaas:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ lam yalid walam yūlad He begetteth not, nor is He Begotten Nothing has come out of Him, i.e., He has not begotten any issue. There is no son or daughter born of Him. To assign a son or a daughter to Him, is the greatest blasphemy. Nor is He born of any other being. There is no match or equal to Him in any aspect, in any meaning or in any sense of any of the divine qualities. To assign any wife or mate to Him is a gross blasphemy against His All-Divine Being. Since man is a limited being and he with his inherent limitations cannot correctly conceive of things unknown to him but through some examples in the terms used for the things physical, certain terms have to be helplessly used, otherwise the essence…

item.title: Al-Ikhlaas:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ walam yakun lahu kufuwan aḥadun nor has He any equal.'

item.title: Al-Ikhlaas:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ walam yakun lahu kufuwan aḥadun Nor is there to Him any equivalent." See 112:1

item.title: Al-Ikhlaas:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ walam yakun lahu kufuwan aḥadun And there is none like unto Him See 112:3

item.title: Al-Infitaar:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذَا السَّمَاءُ انْفَطَرَتْ idhā l-samāu infaṭarat When the sky is rent apart,

item.title: Al-Infitaar:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذَا السَّمَاءُ انْفَطَرَتْ idhā l-samāu infaṭarat When the sky breaks apart. كَلَّا بَلْ تُكَذِّبُونَ بِالدِّينِ Nay! But you deny (the Day of) Ad-Din. Meaning: 'you are only compelled to oppose the Most Generous and meet Him with disobedience, by your rejection in your hearts of the Hereafter, the recompense and the reckoning.' Concerning Allah's statement: وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكُمْ لَحَافِظِينَ - كِرَامًا كَاتِبِينَ - يَعْلَمُونَ مَا تَفْعَلُونَ But verily, over you to watch you (are) Kiraman Katibin, they know all that you do. (82:10-12) Meaning: 'indeed there are noble guardian angels over you, so do not meet them with evil deeds, because they write down all that you do.'

item.title: Al-Infitaar:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذَا السَّمَاءُ انْفَطَرَتْ idhā l-samāu infaṭarat When the heavens cleave asunder (Refer to: 84:1.) Here is another Surah about the happening of the Day of Judgment. It can be easily imagined how important and essential is for man, the belief in the Day of Judgment and how much he must fear the Day of Requital and how much he must be concerned about his getting ready for the day before the respite given to him in this life comes to an end or before death, which comes and often times overtakes unawares. The first four verses relate the events of the dawn of the Day of Judgment1. The collective meaning of all these events will be that the Day of the Final Judgment will begin with the total destruction of the present physical world which we See and its disappearance,…

item.title: Al-Infitaar:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا الْكَوَاكِبُ انْتَثَرَتْ wa-idhā l-kawākibu intatharat when the stars are scattered,

item.title: Al-Infitaar:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا الْكَوَاكِبُ انْتَثَرَتْ wa-idhā l-kawākibu intatharat And when the stars fall, scattering. See 82:1

item.title: Al-Infitaar:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا الْكَوَاكِبُ انْتَثَرَتْ wa-idhā l-kawākibu intatharat And When the stars (Refer to: 81:1 - 81:14.) disperse (Scatter.) Note that in 81:2 for the stars the name 'Nojoom' is used, and verb used there is 'Inkadu' i.e., getting covered with darkness, i.e., losing their lustre and here for stars the name 'Kawakib' is used, and the verb used is 'Intasarat', i.e., getting scattered. The state of the change meant there, was as to what will have happened to the native property or the function of the stars and here is meant the disturbance which their usual position will suffer, i.e., in the symmetry, i.e., the arrangement in the great constellations.

item.title: Al-Infitaar:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا الْبِحَارُ فُجِّرَتْ wa-idhā l-biḥāru fujjirat when the seas are merged,

item.title: Al-Infitaar:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا الْبِحَارُ فُجِّرَتْ wa-idhā l-biḥāru fujjirat And when the seas are erupted. See 82:1

item.title: Al-Infitaar:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا الْبِحَارُ فُجِّرَتْ wa-idhā l-biḥāru fujjirat And When the seas (Refer to: 81:6.) be comingled When all kinds of the barriers withholding the rivers and the seas1, natural as well as artificial, preventing the great waters from overflowing, will go. The rivers and seas will burst forth and boil. The fresh and the saltish waters will be mixed, and the flood will cover the whole globe.

item.title: Al-Infitaar:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا الْقُبُورُ بُعْثِرَتْ wa-idhā l-qubūru buʿ'thirat when the graves are overturned,

item.title: Al-Infitaar:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا الْقُبُورُ بُعْثِرَتْ wa-idhā l-qubūru buʿ'thirat And when the (contents of) graves are scattered (i.e., exposed). See 82:1

item.title: Al-Infitaar:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا الْقُبُورُ بُعْثِرَتْ wa-idhā l-qubūru buʿ'thirat And when the graves be overturned (to be vacated) See 82:3

item.title: Al-Infitaar:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ مَا قَدَّمَتْ وَأَخَّرَتْ ʿalimat nafsun mā qaddamat wa-akharat then a soul shall know what it has sent ahead and left behind.

item.title: Al-Infitaar:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ مَا قَدَّمَتْ وَأَخَّرَتْ ʿalimat nafsun mā qaddamat wa-akharat A soul will (then) know what it has put forth and kept back. See 82:1

item.title: Al-Infitaar:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ مَا قَدَّمَتْ وَأَخَّرَتْ ʿalimat nafsun mā qaddamat wa-akharat Then shall every soul know (Refer to: 81:14.) what it hath sent forth and left behind (Refer to: 81:1 - 81:14, 99:6.) Note, in 81:14 is said that man will know what he has put forward, i.e., what provision of good and evil deeds he has done and what a recompense for his own deeds are in store for him and here there are two verbs used, i.e., what he has sent before and what he left over behind him, i.e., what good or evil he himself committed during his life time and what arrangements or what consequences his life created for good and evil to be done after him on his behalf. It might mean also what spiritual prospects he earned and what physical things he prided over he…

item.title: Al-Infitaar:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاأَيُّهَا الْإِنْسَانُ مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ الْكَرِيمِ yāayyuhā l-insānu mā gharraka birabbika l-karīmi O man! What has deceived you about your generous1 Lord,

item.title: Al-Infitaar:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاأَيُّهَا الْإِنْسَانُ مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ الْكَرِيمِ yāayyuhā l-insānu mā gharraka birabbika l-karīmi O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous. See 82:1

item.title: Al-Infitaar:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاأَيُّهَا الْإِنْسَانُ مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ الْكَرِيمِ yāayyuhā l-insānu mā gharraka birabbika l-karīmi O' thou man! What hath beguiled thee from thy Lord, the Most Gracious One Note that God has referred to Himself with His attribute 'Kareem', i.e., the Most Charitable, the Most Noble, the Most Gracious. It is this divine attribute of God that Satan uses to instigate man to sin, encouraging him saying that God is 'Kareem'. He will surely pardon hence why not enjoy life even with the evils in it. Man is warned not to be beguiled by such rebellious belief or confidence in God's grace and mercy. Some say that it is an indirect guidance to man, i.e., man is taught that when he fails in his duties, i.e., if he involved in sins and if he is questioned by God ''What made thee rebel…

item.title: Al-Infitaar:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ alladhī khalaqaka fasawwāka faʿadalaka who created you and proportioned you, and gave you an upright nature,

item.title: Al-Infitaar:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ alladhī khalaqaka fasawwāka faʿadalaka Who created you, proportioned you, and balanced you? See 82:1

item.title: Al-Infitaar:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ alladhī khalaqaka fasawwāka faʿadalaka (He) Who created thee, and fashioned (Gave shape.) thee and (gave thee a body) justly proportioned (Symmetrical.) Reference to God's creative authority over man and His grace in giving man the well-formed perfect body with harmoniously active organism which He did as a grace, of His own accord and not in return for any obligation from anyone. It will be quite sufficient if man only reflects on the great gifts he has received from the Great Author of his very existence with the wonderful native endowments, physical, mental and spiritual1.

item.title: Al-Infitaar:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي أَيِّ صُورَةٍ مَا شَاءَ رَكَّبَكَ fī ayyi ṣūratin mā shāa rakkabaka and composed you in any form that He wished?

item.title: Al-Infitaar:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي أَيِّ صُورَةٍ مَا شَاءَ رَكَّبَكَ fī ayyi ṣūratin mā shāa rakkabaka In whatever form He willed has He assembled you. See 82:1

item.title: Al-Infitaar:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي أَيِّ صُورَةٍ مَا شَاءَ رَكَّبَكَ fī ayyi ṣūratin mā shāa rakkabaka In whatsoever form He willeth He casteth (Refer to: 6:2, 87:2.) thee 'Surat', i.e., shape personality with the gifts of the physical strength and the mental faculties.

item.title: Al-Infitaar:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا بَلْ تُكَذِّبُونَ بِالدِّينِ kallā bal tukadhibūna bil-dīni No indeed! Rather you deny the Retribution.

item.title: Al-Infitaar:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا بَلْ تُكَذِّبُونَ بِالدِّينِ kallā bal tukadhibūna bil-dīni No! But you deny the Recompense. See 82:1

item.title: Al-Infitaar:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا بَلْ تُكَذِّبُونَ بِالدِّينِ kallā bal tukadhibūna bil-dīni Nay! but ye belie the Reckoning See 82:8

item.title: Al-Infitaar:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكُمْ لَحَافِظِينَ wa-inna ʿalaykum laḥāfiẓīna Indeed, there are over you watchers,

item.title: Al-Infitaar:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكُمْ لَحَافِظِينَ wa-inna ʿalaykum laḥāfiẓīna And indeed, (appointed) over you are keepers.1 See 82:1

item.title: Al-Infitaar:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكُمْ لَحَافِظِينَ wa-inna ʿalaykum laḥāfiẓīna While verily over you are posted the Watchers (Refer to: 50:18.) See 82:8

item.title: Al-Infitaar:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: كِرَامًا كَاتِبِينَ kirāman kātibīna noble writers

item.title: Al-Infitaar:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: كِرَامًا كَاتِبِينَ kirāman kātibīna Noble and recording. See 82:1

item.title: Al-Infitaar:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: كِرَامًا كَاتِبِينَ kirāman kātibīna Recorders Honourable (Refer to: 50:18.) See 82:8

item.title: Al-Infitaar:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَعْلَمُونَ مَا تَفْعَلُونَ yaʿlamūna mā tafʿalūna who know whatever you do.

item.title: Al-Infitaar:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَعْلَمُونَ مَا تَفْعَلُونَ yaʿlamūna mā tafʿalūna They know whatever you do. See 82:1

item.title: Al-Infitaar:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَعْلَمُونَ مَا تَفْعَلُونَ yaʿlamūna mā tafʿalūna Know they whatever ye do (Refer to: 50:18.) See 82:8

item.title: Al-Infitaar:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الْأَبْرَارَ لَفِیْ نَعِيمٍ inna l-abrāra lafī naʿīmin Indeed the pious shall be amid bliss,

item.title: Al-Infitaar:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الْأَبْرَارَ لَفِیْ نَعِيمٍ inna l-abrāra lafī naʿīmin Indeed, the righteous will be in pleasure. Verily, the Abrar (the righteous believers) will be in Delight (82:13). And verily, the wicked will be in the blazing Fire (Hell) (82:14). Therein they will enter, and taste its burning flame on the Day of Recompense (82:15). And they will not be absent therefrom (82:16). And what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is (82:17). Again, what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is (82:18). (It will be) the Day when no person shall have power for another, and the Decision, that Day, will be with Allah (82:19). The Reward of the Righteous and the Sinners Allah informs of what the righteous will receive of delight. They are those who obeyed Allah and did not meet Him with…

item.title: Al-Infitaar:13 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الْأَبْرَارَ لَفِیْ نَعِيمٍ inna l-abrāra lafī naʿīmin Verily, the righteous shall be amidst bounteous bliss See 82:8

item.title: Al-Infitaar:14 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّ الْفُجَّارَ لَفِیْ جَحِيمٍ wa-inna l-fujāra lafī jaḥīmin and indeed the vicious shall be in hell

item.title: Al-Infitaar:14 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّ الْفُجَّارَ لَفِیْ جَحِيمٍ wa-inna l-fujāra lafī jaḥīmin And indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire. See 82:13

item.title: Al-Infitaar:14 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّ الْفُجَّارَ لَفِیْ جَحِيمٍ wa-inna l-fujāra lafī jaḥīmin And verily the wicked shall be in the flaming fire See 82:8

item.title: Al-Infitaar:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَصْلَوْنَهَا يَوْمَ الدِّينِ yaṣlawnahā yawma l-dīni entering it on the Day of Retribution,1

item.title: Al-Infitaar:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَصْلَوْنَهَا يَوْمَ الدِّينِ yaṣlawnahā yawma l-dīni They will (enter to) burn therein on the Day of Recompense. See 82:13

item.title: Al-Infitaar:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَصْلَوْنَهَا يَوْمَ الدِّينِ yaṣlawnahā yawma l-dīni They shall be committed to it on the Day of Judgment See 82:8

item.title: Al-Infitaar:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا هُمْ عَنْهَا بِغَائِبِينَ wamā hum ʿanhā bighāibīna and they shall not be absent from it.

item.title: Al-Infitaar:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا هُمْ عَنْهَا بِغَائِبِينَ wamā hum ʿanhā bighāibīna And never therefrom will they be absent. See 82:13

item.title: Al-Infitaar:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا هُمْ عَنْهَا بِغَائِبِينَ wamā hum ʿanhā bighāibīna Nor they shall themselves be absent from it See 82:8

item.title: Al-Infitaar:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا يَوْمُ الدِّينِ wamā adrāka mā yawmu l-dīni And what will show you what is the Day of Retribution?

item.title: Al-Infitaar:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا يَوْمُ الدِّينِ wamā adrāka mā yawmu l-dīni And what can make you know what is the Day of Recompense? See 82:13

item.title: Al-Infitaar:17 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا يَوْمُ الدِّينِ wamā adrāka mā yawmu l-dīni And what will make thee know what the Day of Judgment shall be? See 82:8

item.title: Al-Infitaar:18 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ مَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا يَوْمُ الدِّينِ thumma mā adrāka mā yawmu l-dīni Again, what will show you what is the Day of Retribution?

item.title: Al-Infitaar:18 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ مَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا يَوْمُ الدِّينِ thumma mā adrāka mā yawmu l-dīni Then, what can make you know what is the Day of Recompense? See 82:13

item.title: Al-Infitaar:18 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ مَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا يَوْمُ الدِّينِ thumma mā adrāka mā yawmu l-dīni Then what maketh thee know what the Day of Judgment is? See 82:8

item.title: Al-Infitaar:19 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ لَا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِنَفْسٍ شَيْئًا وَالْأَمْرُ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلَّهِ yawma lā tamliku nafsun linafsin shayan wal-amru yawma-idhin lillahi It is a day when no soul will be of any avail to another soul and all command that day will belong to Allah.

item.title: Al-Infitaar:19 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ لَا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِنَفْسٍ شَيْئًا وَالْأَمْرُ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلَّهِ yawma lā tamliku nafsun linafsin shayan wal-amru yawma-idhin lillahi It is the Day when a soul will not possess for another soul (power to do) a thing; and the command, that Day, is (entirely) with Allah. See 82:13

item.title: Al-Infitaar:19 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ لَا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِنَفْسٍ شَيْئًا وَالْأَمْرُ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلَّهِ yawma lā tamliku nafsun linafsin shayan wal-amru yawma-idhin lillahi (It is) The day on which soul shall own not anything (helpful) for another soul; and the Command Supreme that day shall be God's (alone) No soul has the least power to anything for or against the other. The law of strict equity, i.e., of cause and effect for the individual or the personal responsibility, will be fully enforced as the decreed order of the day1. The whole mastery of the day will rest in God's will Who at His own independent choice, would grant anyone of His own chosen beloved ones to intercede on behalf of anyone they please and this will be in recompense to their perfect surrender to the Lord's will during their life on earth and their suffering…

item.title: Al-Insaan:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: هَلْ أَتٰی عَلَى الْإِنْسَانِ حِينٌ مِنَ الدَّهْرِ لَمْ يَكُنْ شَيْئًا مَذْكُورًا hal atā ʿalā l-insāni ḥīnun mina l-dahri lam yakun shayan madhkūran Has there been for man a period of time when he was not anything worthy of mention?

item.title: Al-Insaan:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: هَلْ أَتٰی عَلَى الْإِنْسَانِ حِينٌ مِنَ الدَّهْرِ لَمْ يَكُنْ شَيْئًا مَذْكُورًا hal atā ʿalā l-insāni ḥīnun mina l-dahri lam yakun shayan madhkūran Has there (not) come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing (even) mentioned? إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ السَّبِيلَ Verily, We guided to him the way, Meaning: 'We explained it to him, made it clear to him and showed it to him.' This is as Allah says: وَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ فَاسْتَحَبُّوا الْعَمَىٰ عَلَى الْهُدَىٰ And as for Thamud, We guided them but they preferred blindness to guidance. (41:17) Allah also said: وَهَدَيْنَاهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ And We guided him to the two ways. (90:10) Meaning: 'We explained to him the path of good and the path of evil.' This is the statement of 'Ikrimah, 'Atiyah, Ibn Zayd and Mujahid from what is well-known from him and the majority.…

item.title: Al-Insaan:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: هَلْ أَتٰی عَلَى الْإِنْسَانِ حِينٌ مِنَ الدَّهْرِ لَمْ يَكُنْ شَيْئًا مَذْكُورًا hal atā ʿalā l-insāni ḥīnun mina l-dahri lam yakun shayan madhkūran Surely did come over Man to pass an occasion of time when he was nothing, mentioned of? The literal meaning of this Verse is that surely there was a time for man when he was not mentioned by anyone, i.e., when he was only a drop of a life-germ. According to the holy Ahl Al-Bayt, the one referred to here, is Ali Ibn Abu Talib and the question is an assertion to say that there was no time when Ali was not in existence in the knowledge of God, or his name was not mentioned in the heavens. The Holy Prophet says that when he visited heavens during the Ascension (Mi'raj) he found on the gate of the…

item.title: Al-Insaan:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا خَلَقْنَا الْاِنْسَانَ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ أَمْشَاجٍ نَبْتَلِيهِ فَجَعَلْنَاهُ سَمِيعًا بَصِيرًا innā khalaqnā l-insāna min nuṭ'fatin amshājin nabtalīhi fajaʿalnāhu samīʿan baṣīran Indeed We created man from the drop of a mixed fluid1 so that We may test him. So We made him endowed with hearing and sight.

item.title: Al-Insaan:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا خَلَقْنَا الْاِنْسَانَ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ أَمْشَاجٍ نَبْتَلِيهِ فَجَعَلْنَاهُ سَمِيعًا بَصِيرًا innā khalaqnā l-insāna min nuṭ'fatin amshājin nabtalīhi fajaʿalnāhu samīʿan baṣīran Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixture1 that We may try him; and We made him hearing and seeing. See 76:1

item.title: Al-Insaan:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا خَلَقْنَا الْاِنْسَانَ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ أَمْشَاجٍ نَبْتَلِيهِ فَجَعَلْنَاهُ سَمِيعًا بَصِيرًا innā khalaqnā l-insāna min nuṭ'fatin amshājin nabtalīhi fajaʿalnāhu samīʿan baṣīran Verily We created man from a (small insignificant) life drop (Refer to Verses 80:19, 86:6.) of inter-mingled life germ (of both sexes); in order that We put him to trial, so We endowed him with hearing, seeing (Made hearer & seen.) ! It is known that a human child starts its response first to sounds and then to light or vision. Ibtila - Lit. trial and wherever in Qur'an it has been used in connection with God it means to give chance to the development of the latent aptitude. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Insaan:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ السَّبِيلَ إِمَّا شَاكِرًا وَإِمَّا كَفُورًا innā hadaynāhu l-sabīla immā shākiran wa-immā kafūran Indeed We have guided him to the way, be he grateful or ungrateful.

item.title: Al-Insaan:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ السَّبِيلَ إِمَّا شَاكِرًا وَإِمَّا كَفُورًا innā hadaynāhu l-sabīla immā shākiran wa-immā kafūran Indeed, We guided him to the way, be he grateful or be he ungrateful. See 76:1

item.title: Al-Insaan:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ السَّبِيلَ إِمَّا شَاكِرًا وَإِمَّا كَفُورًا innā hadaynāhu l-sabīla immā shākiran wa-immā kafūran Verily, have We shown him (Man.) the (Right) way, be he grateful or ungrateful (Refer to Verse 90:10.) ! The Divine guidance is there for all. The choice of availing it thankfully or not availing it thanklessly, is left to each individual human being. This asserts man's responsibility for his destiny. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Insaan:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا أَعْتَدْنَا لِلْكَافِرِينَ سَلَاسِلَا وَأَغْلَالًا وَسَعِيرًا innā aʿtadnā lil'kāfirīna salāsilā wa-aghlālan wasaʿīran Indeed We have prepared for the faithless chains, iron collars, and a blaze.

item.title: Al-Insaan:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا أَعْتَدْنَا لِلْكَافِرِينَ سَلَاسِلَا وَأَغْلَالًا وَسَعِيرًا innā aʿtadnā lil'kāfirīna salāsilā wa-aghlālan wasaʿīran Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains and shackles and a blaze. Verily, We have prepared for the disbelievers iron chains, iron collars, and Sa'ir (76:4). Verily, the Abrar (righteous believers) shall drink of a cup mixed with Kafur (76:5). A spring wherefrom the servants of Allah will drink, causing it to gush forth abundantly (76:6). They fulfill (their) vows, and they fear a Day whose evil will be wide-spreading (76:7). And they give food, inspite of their love for it, to the poor, the orphan and the captive (76:8). (Saying): "We feed you seeking Allah's Face only. We wish for no reward, nor thanks from you (76:9). "Verily, We fear from our Lord a Day that is 'Abus and Qamtarir (76:10). So, Allah saved them from…

item.title: Al-Insaan:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا أَعْتَدْنَا لِلْكَافِرِينَ سَلَاسِلَا وَأَغْلَالًا وَسَعِيرًا innā aʿtadnā lil'kāfirīna salāsilā wa-aghlālan wasaʿīran Verily have We prepared for the disbelievers chains, and shackles and a flaming fire! See 76:3

item.title: Al-Insaan:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الْأَبْرَارَ يَشْرَبُونَ مِنْ كَأْسٍ كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا كَافُورًا inna l-abrāra yashrabūna min kasin kāna mizājuhā kāfūran Indeed the pious will drink from a cup seasoned with Kāfūr,1

item.title: Al-Insaan:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الْأَبْرَارَ يَشْرَبُونَ مِنْ كَأْسٍ كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا كَافُورًا inna l-abrāra yashrabūna min kasin kāna mizājuhā kāfūran Indeed, the righteous will drink from a cup (of wine) whose mixture is of Kāfūr.1 See 76:4

item.title: Al-Insaan:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الْأَبْرَارَ يَشْرَبُونَ مِنْ كَأْسٍ كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا كَافُورًا inna l-abrāra yashrabūna min kasin kāna mizājuhā kāfūran Verily, the righteous ones shall drink of a cup tempered at the fountain 'Kafoor' (Camphor)! 'Kaafoor', i.e., Camphor - either it is the name of a spring in the heaven, or it means a special taste. Some commentators interpret the word 'Kafoor' taking the root word 'Kafr' to cover meaning one who drinks of that water, his thirst for the fulfilment of all sorts of carnal passions is quenched for ever as all poisonous matter is antidoted by Camphor.

item.title: Al-Insaan:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: عَيْنًا يَشْرَبُ بِهَا عِبَادُ اللَّهِ يُفَجِّرُونَهَا تَفْجِيرًا ʿaynan yashrabu bihā ʿibādu l-lahi yufajjirūnahā tafjīran a spring where the servants of Allah drink, which they make to gush forth as they please.

item.title: Al-Insaan:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: عَيْنًا يَشْرَبُ بِهَا عِبَادُ اللَّهِ يُفَجِّرُونَهَا تَفْجِيرًا ʿaynan yashrabu bihā ʿibādu l-lahi yufajjirūnahā tafjīran A spring of which the (righteous) servants of Allah will drink; they will make it gush forth in force (and abundance). See 76:4

item.title: Al-Insaan:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: عَيْنًا يَشْرَبُ بِهَا عِبَادُ اللَّهِ يُفَجِّرُونَهَا تَفْجِيرًا ʿaynan yashrabu bihā ʿibādu l-lahi yufajjirūnahā tafjīran The fountain whereof shall wherever drink the servants (Sincere devotee – the pious.) of God, they shall cause it to flow a desirable (Whenever they desire to have it.) flow The scholars of both the Shia and Sunni schools are unanimous in their statement that these Verses and even the whole of the chapter was revealed in praise of the holy Ahl Al-Bayt. The occasion for the revelation of this Sura is said to be that once Hasan and Husayn the two grandsons of the Holy Prophet were ill, and the Holy Prophet went to his daughter's house to enquire about the health of the children - and suggested to Ali to make a vow of fast for three days at the recovery of the children.…

item.title: Al-Insaan:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يُوفُونَ بِالنَّذْرِ وَيَخَافُونَ يَوْمًا كَانَ شَرُّهُ مُسْتَطِيرًا yūfūna bil-nadhri wayakhāfūna yawman kāna sharruhu mus'taṭīran They fulfill their vows and fear a day whose ill will be widespread.

item.title: Al-Insaan:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يُوفُونَ بِالنَّذْرِ وَيَخَافُونَ يَوْمًا كَانَ شَرُّهُ مُسْتَطِيرًا yūfūna bil-nadhri wayakhāfūna yawman kāna sharruhu mus'taṭīran They (are those who) fulfill (their) vows and fear a Day whose evil will be widespread. See 76:4

item.title: Al-Insaan:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يُوفُونَ بِالنَّذْرِ وَيَخَافُونَ يَوْمًا كَانَ شَرُّهُ مُسْتَطِيرًا yūfūna bil-nadhri wayakhāfūna yawman kāna sharruhu mus'taṭīran They who (The Ahl Al-Bayt.) fulfil their vows, and fear the day the woe of which stretcheth far and wide See 76:6

item.title: Al-Insaan:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيُطْعِمُونَ الطَّعَامَ عَلَى حُبِّهِ مِسْكِينًا وَيَتِيمًا وَأَسِيرًا wayuṭ'ʿimūna l-ṭaʿāma ʿalā ḥubbihi mis'kīnan wayatīman wa-asīran They give food, for the love of Him, to the needy, the orphan and the prisoner,

item.title: Al-Insaan:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيُطْعِمُونَ الطَّعَامَ عَلَى حُبِّهِ مِسْكِينًا وَيَتِيمًا وَأَسِيرًا wayuṭ'ʿimūna l-ṭaʿāma ʿalā ḥubbihi mis'kīnan wayatīman wa-asīran And they give food in spite of love for it1 to the needy, the orphan, and the captive. See 76:4

item.title: Al-Insaan:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيُطْعِمُونَ الطَّعَامَ عَلَى حُبِّهِ مِسْكِينًا وَيَتِيمًا وَأَسِيرًا wayuṭ'ʿimūna l-ṭaʿāma ʿalā ḥubbihi mis'kīnan wayatīman wa-asīran And (while needing it for themselves) they give away food, out of love for Him, to the poor and the orphan and the captive The inseparable pronoun 'Ha' in 'Hubbihi', i.e., Out of love - may refer to God when the phrase would be adverbial modifying Verse 'Yot'imoona' meaning out of love for him and it may refer to 'Ta'aam', i.e., food - then the phrase would be adjectival qualifying food meaning in spite of its being wanted for their own selves. This gets into conformity with Verse 3:92. However, both the interpretations are valid and convey the same significance. This Verse encourages the well treatment of a captive in the manner that a poor - an orphan is treated. Hence the killing, ill-treatment of captives…

item.title: Al-Insaan:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّمَا نُطْعِمُكُمْ لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ لَا نُرِيدُ مِنْكُمْ جَزَاءً وَلَا شُكُورًا innamā nuṭ'ʿimukum liwajhi l-lahi lā nurīdu minkum jazāan walā shukūran [saying,] 'We feed you only for the sake of Allah. We do not want any reward from you nor any thanks.

item.title: Al-Insaan:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّمَا نُطْعِمُكُمْ لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ لَا نُرِيدُ مِنْكُمْ جَزَاءً وَلَا شُكُورًا innamā nuṭ'ʿimukum liwajhi l-lahi lā nurīdu minkum jazāan walā shukūran (Saying), "We feed you only for the face (i.e., approval) of Allah. We wish not from you reward or gratitude. See 76:4

item.title: Al-Insaan:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّمَا نُطْعِمُكُمْ لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ لَا نُرِيدُ مِنْكُمْ جَزَاءً وَلَا شُكُورًا innamā nuṭ'ʿimukum liwajhi l-lahi lā nurīdu minkum jazāan walā shukūran (Saying): "We feed you only for God's sake, we intend (Expect.) not of you any recompense, nor (even) thanks (thereof)!" This is what the godly ones mean and say when they feed anyone for, they do it just to please the Lord and never in the least with the least expectation of any return or to earn any praise or obligation from any one save God. It is a guidance for mankind as a whole as to what extent those who sincerely love God, should sacrifice their personal interest and how selfless any service in the way of the Lord should be. Charity should always be motivated by piety and righteousness and should be unpretentious.

item.title: Al-Insaan:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا نَخَافُ مِنْ رَبِّنَا يَوْمًا عَبُوسًا قَمْطَرِيرًا innā nakhāfu min rabbinā yawman ʿabūsan qamṭarīran Indeed we fear from our Lord a day, frowning and fateful.'

item.title: Al-Insaan:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا نَخَافُ مِنْ رَبِّنَا يَوْمًا عَبُوسًا قَمْطَرِيرًا innā nakhāfu min rabbinā yawman ʿabūsan qamṭarīran Indeed, We fear from our Lord a Day austere and distressful." See 76:4

item.title: Al-Insaan:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا نَخَافُ مِنْ رَبِّنَا يَوْمًا عَبُوسًا قَمْطَرِيرًا innā nakhāfu min rabbinā yawman ʿabūsan qamṭarīran Verily, we dread from our Lord, a stern day of distress See 76:9

item.title: Al-Insaan:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَوَقَاهُمُ اللَّهُ شَرَّ ذٰلِكَ الْيَوْمِ وَلَقَّاهُمْ نَضْرَةً وَسُرُورًا fawaqāhumu l-lahu sharra dhālika l-yawmi walaqqāhum naḍratan wasurūran So Allah saved them from the ills of that day, and granted them freshness and joy.

item.title: Al-Insaan:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَوَقَاهُمُ اللَّهُ شَرَّ ذٰلِكَ الْيَوْمِ وَلَقَّاهُمْ نَضْرَةً وَسُرُورًا fawaqāhumu l-lahu sharra dhālika l-yawmi walaqqāhum naḍratan wasurūran So Allah will protect them from the evil of that Day and give them radiance and happiness. See 76:4

item.title: Al-Insaan:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَوَقَاهُمُ اللَّهُ شَرَّ ذٰلِكَ الْيَوْمِ وَلَقَّاهُمْ نَضْرَةً وَسُرُورًا fawaqāhumu l-lahu sharra dhālika l-yawmi walaqqāhum naḍratan wasurūran So will God guard them from the evil of that day and cause them to meet freshness and pleasure (Refer to Verses 75:22; 75:23. Note: All the references to the heavenly pleasures wherever mentioned i.e. in this sura and elsewhere in the Qur'an all are figurative. (AP).) The godly ones for whom this grace of the Lord is meant are the holy Ahl Al-Bayt and the others would naturally earn it according to the degree of their success in following their footsteps. Verse 11 refers to their being safe from dreadful events of the judgment1. Verse 11 refers to the reward they will receive from the Lord for their patience and endurance in the face of persecution, as well as for their willing surrender…

item.title: Al-Insaan:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَزَاهُمْ بِمَا صَبَرُوْۤا جَنَّةً وَحَرِيرًا wajazāhum bimā ṣabarū jannatan waḥarīran And He rewarded them for their patience with a garden and [garments of] silk,

item.title: Al-Insaan:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَزَاهُمْ بِمَا صَبَرُوْۤا جَنَّةً وَحَرِيرًا wajazāhum bimā ṣabarū jannatan waḥarīran And will reward them for what they patiently endured (with) a garden (in Paradise) and silk (garments). See 76:4

item.title: Al-Insaan:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَزَاهُمْ بِمَا صَبَرُوْۤا جَنَّةً وَحَرِيرًا wajazāhum bimā ṣabarū jannatan waḥarīran And shall recompense them, for what they endured with patience, with garden (to abide) and silk (to wear) All the references to the heavenly pleasures mentioned in this Sura and elsewhere are figurative. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Insaan:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مُتَّكِئِينَ فِيهَا عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ لَا يَرَوْنَ فِيهَا شَمْسًا وَلَا زَمْهَرِيرًا muttakiīna fīhā ʿalā l-arāiki lā yarawna fīhā shamsan walā zamharīran reclining therein on couches. They will find in it neither any [scorching] sun, nor any [biting] cold.

item.title: Al-Insaan:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مُتَّكِئِينَ فِيهَا عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ لَا يَرَوْنَ فِيهَا شَمْسًا وَلَا زَمْهَرِيرًا muttakiīna fīhā ʿalā l-arāiki lā yarawna fīhā shamsan walā zamharīran (They will be) reclining therein on adorned couches. They will not see therein any (burning) sun or (freezing) cold. The Raised Couches and the Lack of Heat and Cold Allah tells us about the people of Paradise and the eternal delights they will experience, as well as the comprehensive favors that they will be given. Allah says: مُّتَّكِئِينَ فِيهَا عَلَى الاٌّرَائِكِ Reclining therein on raised couches. This has already been discussed in Surat As-Saffat and the difference of opinion about the meaning of reclining. Is it lying down, reclining on the elbows, sitting down cross-legged, or being firmly seated We have also mentioned that the Al-Ara'ik are couches beneath curtained canopies. Concerning Allah's statement: لاَ يَرَوْنَ فِيهَا شَمْساً وَلاَ زَمْهَرِيراً…

item.title: Al-Insaan:13 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مُتَّكِئِينَ فِيهَا عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ لَا يَرَوْنَ فِيهَا شَمْسًا وَلَا زَمْهَرِيرًا muttakiīna fīhā ʿalā l-arāiki lā yarawna fīhā shamsan walā zamharīran Reclining therein on exalted couches (Refer to Verses 18:31, 56:15.) , they shall find not therein (the excessive heat of) the sun, nor any (intense) cold See 76:12

item.title: Al-Insaan:14 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَدَانِيَةً عَلَيْهِمْ ظِلَالُهَا وَذُلِّلَتْ قُطُوفُهَا تَذْلِيلًا wadāniyatan ʿalayhim ẓilāluhā wadhullilat quṭūfuhā tadhlīlan Its shades will be close over them and its clusters [of fruits] will be hanging low.

item.title: Al-Insaan:14 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَدَانِيَةً عَلَيْهِمْ ظِلَالُهَا وَذُلِّلَتْ قُطُوفُهَا تَذْلِيلًا wadāniyatan ʿalayhim ẓilāluhā wadhullilat quṭūfuhā tadhlīlan And near above them are its shades, and its (fruit) to be picked will be lowered in compliance. See 76:13

item.title: Al-Insaan:14 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَدَانِيَةً عَلَيْهِمْ ظِلَالُهَا وَذُلِّلَتْ قُطُوفُهَا تَذْلِيلًا wadāniyatan ʿalayhim ẓilāluhā wadhullilat quṭūfuhā tadhlīlan And close low over them (shall be) its shades, and the clustered fruits (Refer to Verses 56:20; 56:21.) thereof (shall be) bowing down (in easy reach) When there will be neither the sun nor the moon the question of the need for any shade does not at all arise, but the illustration is just to give an understanding of the state there in heaven in terms of our life in this world, which is only figurative1.

item.title: Al-Insaan:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيُطَافُ عَلَيْهِمْ بِءَانِيَةٍ مِنْ فِضَّةٍ وَأَكْوَابٍ كَانَتْ قَوَارِيرَا wayuṭāfu ʿalayhim biāniyatin min fiḍḍatin wa-akwābin kānat qawārīrā They will be served around with vessels of silver and goblets of crystal

item.title: Al-Insaan:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيُطَافُ عَلَيْهِمْ بِءَانِيَةٍ مِنْ فِضَّةٍ وَأَكْوَابٍ كَانَتْ قَوَارِيرَا wayuṭāfu ʿalayhim biāniyatin min fiḍḍatin wa-akwābin kānat qawārīrā And there will be circulated among them vessels of silver and cups having been (created) clear (as glass). See 76:13

item.title: Al-Insaan:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيُطَافُ عَلَيْهِمْ بِءَانِيَةٍ مِنْ فِضَّةٍ وَأَكْوَابٍ كَانَتْ قَوَارِيرَا wayuṭāfu ʿalayhim biāniyatin min fiḍḍatin wa-akwābin kānat qawārīrā And shall pass round among them vessels of silver and goblets (Refer to Verses 43:71; 56:18.) of crystal (glass) About the enjoyment, they will have, refer to Verse 43:71. The ideal accommodation in the mention of the metal and the stuff of which the vessels will be, is a figurative indication of the rarity and the preciousness and the splendour of the things.

item.title: Al-Insaan:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَوَارِيرَا مِنْ فِضَّةٍ قَدَّرُوهَا تَقْدِيرًا qawārīrā min fiḍḍatin qaddarūhā taqdīran —crystal of silver—1 [from] which they dispense in a precise measure.

item.title: Al-Insaan:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَوَارِيرَا مِنْ فِضَّةٍ قَدَّرُوهَا تَقْدِيرًا qawārīrā min fiḍḍatin qaddarūhā taqdīran Clear glasses (made) from silver of which they have determined the measure. See 76:13

item.title: Al-Insaan:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَوَارِيرَا مِنْ فِضَّةٍ قَدَّرُوهَا تَقْدِيرًا qawārīrā min fiḍḍatin qaddarūhā taqdīran Bright as glass, made of silver; measure they to a well-measure (As desired.) See note on Verse 15 above. About the kind of drink they will have, refer to Verses 5 and 6 above. Zanjabil or Ginger is an ingredient which gives warmth to the body and zest to the taste. It may be a new kind of drink of a taste and flavour unknown to us in this life. 'Zanjabil' also is a figurative expression.

item.title: Al-Insaan:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيُسْقَوْنَ فِيهَا كَأْسًا كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا زَنْجَبِيلًا wayus'qawna fīhā kasan kāna mizājuhā zanjabīlan They will be served therein with a cup of a drink seasoned with Zanjabīl,1

item.title: Al-Insaan:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيُسْقَوْنَ فِيهَا كَأْسًا كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا زَنْجَبِيلًا wayus'qawna fīhā kasan kāna mizājuhā zanjabīlan And they will be given to drink a cup (of wine) whose mixture is of ginger. See 76:13

item.title: Al-Insaan:17 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيُسْقَوْنَ فِيهَا كَأْسًا كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا زَنْجَبِيلًا wayus'qawna fīhā kasan kāna mizājuhā zanjabīlan And they shall be supplied with the drink therein of a cup tempered with 'Zanjabil' (ginger) (Flavour or strength.) See 76:16

item.title: Al-Insaan:18 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: عَيْنًا فِيهَا تُسَمَّى سَلْسَبِيلًا ʿaynan fīhā tusammā salsabīlan a spring in it, named Salsabīl.

item.title: Al-Insaan:18 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: عَيْنًا فِيهَا تُسَمَّى سَلْسَبِيلًا ʿaynan fīhā tusammā salsabīlan (From) a fountain within it (i.e., Paradise) named Salsabeel. See 76:13

item.title: Al-Insaan:18 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: عَيْنًا فِيهَا تُسَمَّى سَلْسَبِيلًا ʿaynan fīhā tusammā salsabīlan (It is the water of) a spring therein named 'Salsabeel' (The Soft Flowing) It is the name of a spring in heaven specially promised to the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt who are praised in this Sura.

item.title: Al-Insaan:19 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدَانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ إِذَا رَأَيْتَهُمْ حَسِبْتَهُمْ لُؤْلُؤًا مَنْثُورًا wayaṭūfu ʿalayhim wil'dānun mukhalladūna idhā ra-aytahum ḥasib'tahum lu'lu-an manthūran They will be waited upon by immortal youths, whom, when you see them, you will suppose them to be scattered pearls.

item.title: Al-Insaan:19 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدَانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ إِذَا رَأَيْتَهُمْ حَسِبْتَهُمْ لُؤْلُؤًا مَنْثُورًا wayaṭūfu ʿalayhim wil'dānun mukhalladūna idhā ra-aytahum ḥasib'tahum lu'lu-an manthūran There will circulate among them young boys made eternal. When you see them, you would think them (as beautiful as) scattered pearls. See 76:13

item.title: Al-Insaan:19 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدَانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ إِذَا رَأَيْتَهُمْ حَسِبْتَهُمْ لُؤْلُؤًا مَنْثُورًا wayaṭūfu ʿalayhim wil'dānun mukhalladūna idhā ra-aytahum ḥasib'tahum lu'lu-an manthūran And around them in their service shall be boys (graced) with eternal youth (Refer to Verses 56:17; 52:24.) ; when thou seest them thou wilt deem them as pearls scattered about See 76:18

item.title: Al-Insaan:20 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَ ثَمَّ رَأَيْتَ نَعِيمًا وَمُلْكًا كَبِيرًا wa-idhā ra-ayta thamma ra-ayta naʿīman wamul'kan kabīran As you look, you will see there bliss and a great kingdom.

item.title: Al-Insaan:20 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَ ثَمَّ رَأَيْتَ نَعِيمًا وَمُلْكًا كَبِيرًا wa-idhā ra-ayta thamma ra-ayta naʿīman wamul'kan kabīran And when you look there (in Paradise), you will see pleasure and great dominion. See 76:13

item.title: Al-Insaan:20 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَ ثَمَّ رَأَيْتَ نَعِيمًا وَمُلْكًا كَبِيرًا wa-idhā ra-ayta thamma ra-ayta naʿīman wamul'kan kabīran And when thou seest there, thou shalt see bounties (abundant) and a kingdom magnificent The Holy Ahl Al-Bayt have been given a kingdom which in the words of the Almighty is called 'Great.' Thus the kingdom or the authority given to them in the heavens cannot be fully assessed or imagined by the mortals in this physical life.

item.title: Al-Insaan:21 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: عَالِيَهُمْ ثِيَابُ سُنْدُسٍ خُضْرٌ وَإِسْتَبْرَقٌ وَحُلُّوْۤا أَسَاوِرَ مِنْ فِضَّةٍ وَسَقَاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ شَرَابًا طَهُورًا ʿāliyahum thiyābu sundusin khuḍ'run wa-is'tabraqun waḥullū asāwira min fiḍḍatin wasaqāhum rabbuhum sharāban ṭahūran Upon them will be cloaks of green silk and brocade and they will be adorned with bracelets of silver. Their Lord will give them to drink a pure drink.

item.title: Al-Insaan:21 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: عَالِيَهُمْ ثِيَابُ سُنْدُسٍ خُضْرٌ وَإِسْتَبْرَقٌ وَحُلُّوْۤا أَسَاوِرَ مِنْ فِضَّةٍ وَسَقَاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ شَرَابًا طَهُورًا ʿāliyahum thiyābu sundusin khuḍ'run wa-is'tabraqun waḥullū asāwira min fiḍḍatin wasaqāhum rabbuhum sharāban ṭahūran Upon them (i.e., the inhabitants) will be green garments of fine silk and brocade. And they will be adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord will give them a purifying drink. See 76:13

item.title: Al-Insaan:21 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: عَالِيَهُمْ ثِيَابُ سُنْدُسٍ خُضْرٌ وَإِسْتَبْرَقٌ وَحُلُّوْۤا أَسَاوِرَ مِنْ فِضَّةٍ وَسَقَاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ شَرَابًا طَهُورًا ʿāliyahum thiyābu sundusin khuḍ'run wa-is'tabraqun waḥullū asāwira min fiḍḍatin wasaqāhum rabbuhum sharāban ṭahūran Upon them shall be robes of fine green silk and rich brocade, and they shall be adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord give them to drink a drink, pure (and wholesome) (Refer to Verse 18:31.) Regarding adornments in store for the holy ones, refer to Verse 18:31. The idea is of the rarity and the preciousness of the articles. A figure in terms of the things in this world.

item.title: Al-Insaan:22 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ هَذَا كَانَ لَكُمْ جَزَاءً وَكَانَ سَعْيُكُمْ مَشْكُورًا inna hādhā kāna lakum jazāan wakāna saʿyukum mashkūran [They will be told]: 'This is indeed your reward, and your endeavour has been well-appreciated.'

item.title: Al-Insaan:22 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ هَذَا كَانَ لَكُمْ جَزَاءً وَكَانَ سَعْيُكُمْ مَشْكُورًا inna hādhā kāna lakum jazāan wakāna saʿyukum mashkūran (And it will be said), "Indeed, this is for you a reward, and your effort has been appreciated." See 76:13

item.title: Al-Insaan:22 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ هَذَا كَانَ لَكُمْ جَزَاءً وَكَانَ سَعْيُكُمْ مَشْكُورًا inna hādhā kāna lakum jazāan wakāna saʿyukum mashkūran (Saying unto them) "Verily this is unto you a recompense, and your endeavour is accepted (with appreciation)" The address is in clear words to the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt, a reward for their endeavour in the way of the Lord, i.e., for their piety and their selfless life.

item.title: Al-Insaan:23 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ الْقُرْآنَ تَنْزِيلًا innā naḥnu nazzalnā ʿalayka l-qur'āna tanzīlan Indeed We have sent down to you the Qur'ān in a gradual descent.

item.title: Al-Insaan:23 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ الْقُرْآنَ تَنْزِيلًا innā naḥnu nazzalnā ʿalayka l-qur'āna tanzīlan Indeed, it is We who have sent down to you, (O Muḥammad), the Qur’ān progressively. Verily, it is We Who have sent down the Qur'an to you by stages (76:23). Therefore be patient with constancy to the command of your Lord, and obey neither a sinner nor a disbeliever among them (76:24). And remember the Name of your Lord every morning and afternoon (76:25). And during the night, prostrate yourself to Him, and glorify Him a long night through (76:26). Verily, these love the present life of this world, and put behind them a heavy Day (76:27). It is We Who created them, and We have made them of strong build. And when We will, We can replace them with others like them with a complete replacement (76:28).…

item.title: Al-Insaan:23 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ الْقُرْآنَ تَنْزِيلًا innā naḥnu nazzalnā ʿalayka l-qur'āna tanzīlan Verily, We ourselves have sent down unto thee (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) the Qur'an, in a proper descension The Holy Qur'an was revealed in parts, i.e., in Verses and chapters one after another to facilitate the gradual development of the faith and the study of its articles of belief and practice by the people. This Verse hints that the presentation of the facts of the heavenly and the spiritual spheres to a human being will always be in revealed terms graspable by mankind. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Insaan:24 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وَلَا تُطِعْ مِنْهُمْ ءَاثِمًا أَوْ كَفُورًا fa-iṣ'bir liḥuk'mi rabbika walā tuṭiʿ min'hum āthiman aw kafūran So submit patiently to the judgement of your Lord, and do not obey any sinner or ingrate among them,

item.title: Al-Insaan:24 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وَلَا تُطِعْ مِنْهُمْ ءَاثِمًا أَوْ كَفُورًا fa-iṣ'bir liḥuk'mi rabbika walā tuṭiʿ min'hum āthiman aw kafūran So be patient for the decision of your Lord and do not obey from among them a sinner or ungrateful (disbeliever). See 76:23

item.title: Al-Insaan:24 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وَلَا تُطِعْ مِنْهُمْ ءَاثِمًا أَوْ كَفُورًا fa-iṣ'bir liḥuk'mi rabbika walā tuṭiʿ min'hum āthiman aw kafūran Await then with patience the command of thy Lord, and obey not from among them a sinner or an ungrateful one See 76:23

item.title: Al-Insaan:25 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاذْكُرِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا wa-udh'kuri is'ma rabbika buk'ratan wa-aṣīlan and celebrate the Name of your Lord morning and evening,

item.title: Al-Insaan:25 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاذْكُرِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا wa-udh'kuri is'ma rabbika buk'ratan wa-aṣīlan And mention the name of your Lord (in prayer) morning and evening. See 76:23

item.title: Al-Insaan:25 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاذْكُرِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا wa-udh'kuri is'ma rabbika buk'ratan wa-aṣīlan And remember (Glorify or hallow.) thou the name of thy Lord at morn and at even See 76:23

item.title: Al-Insaan:26 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَاسْجُدْ لَهُ وَسَبِّحْهُ لَيْلًا طَوِيلًا wamina al-layli fa-us'jud lahu wasabbiḥ'hu laylan ṭawīlan and worship Him for a watch of the night and glorify Him the night long.

item.title: Al-Insaan:26 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَاسْجُدْ لَهُ وَسَبِّحْهُ لَيْلًا طَوِيلًا wamina al-layli fa-us'jud lahu wasabbiḥ'hu laylan ṭawīlan And during the night prostrate to Him and exalt (i.e., praise) Him a long (part of the) night. See 76:23

item.title: Al-Insaan:26 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَاسْجُدْ لَهُ وَسَبِّحْهُ لَيْلًا طَوِيلًا wamina al-layli fa-us'jud lahu wasabbiḥ'hu laylan ṭawīlan And during a part of the night prostrate thou in obeisance unto Him and celebrate His praise long night through Prayer in the dead of the night has its own facility for concentration and meditation and is also of special spiritual effect on the mind. To be in communion with the Lord when the world around is enjoying rest and when the quiet of the night helps the mind to concentrate, the prayer in such hours is of special value and worth, and gets easily effective.

item.title: Al-Insaan:27 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ يُحِبُّونَ الْعَاجِلَةَ وَيَذَرُونَ وَرَاءَهُمْ يَوْمًا ثَقِيلًا inna hāulāi yuḥibbūna l-ʿājilata wayadharūna warāahum yawman thaqīlan Indeed they love this transitory life, and disregard a weighty day ahead of them.

item.title: Al-Insaan:27 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ يُحِبُّونَ الْعَاجِلَةَ وَيَذَرُونَ وَرَاءَهُمْ يَوْمًا ثَقِيلًا inna hāulāi yuḥibbūna l-ʿājilata wayadharūna warāahum yawman thaqīlan Indeed, these (disbelievers) love the immediate and leave behind them1 a grave Day. See 76:23

item.title: Al-Insaan:27 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ يُحِبُّونَ الْعَاجِلَةَ وَيَذَرُونَ وَرَاءَهُمْ يَوْمًا ثَقِيلًا inna hāulāi yuḥibbūna l-ʿājilata wayadharūna warāahum yawman thaqīlan Verily, these (people) love the fleeting present (The immediate gain of this world. Refer to Verses 21:37; 75:20; 75:21.) , and (neglect) putting away behind them the Day (which shall be) hard People, particularly the disbelievers, are always inclined to avail of the immediate enjoyment in this life which are only passing shows and neglect the hereafter though it is of a permanent duration1.

item.title: Al-Insaan:28 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: نَحْنُ خَلَقْنَاهُمْ وَشَدَدْنَا أَسْرَهُمْ وَإِذَا شِئْنَا بَدَّلْنَا أَمْثَالَهُمْ تَبْدِيلًا naḥnu khalaqnāhum washadadnā asrahum wa-idhā shi'nā baddalnā amthālahum tabdīlan We created them and made their joints firm, and whenever We like We will replace them with others like them.

item.title: Al-Insaan:28 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: نَحْنُ خَلَقْنَاهُمْ وَشَدَدْنَا أَسْرَهُمْ وَإِذَا شِئْنَا بَدَّلْنَا أَمْثَالَهُمْ تَبْدِيلًا naḥnu khalaqnāhum washadadnā asrahum wa-idhā shi'nā baddalnā amthālahum tabdīlan We have created them and strengthened their forms, and when We will, We can change their likenesses with (complete) alteration. See 76:23

item.title: Al-Insaan:28 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: نَحْنُ خَلَقْنَاهُمْ وَشَدَدْنَا أَسْرَهُمْ وَإِذَا شِئْنَا بَدَّلْنَا أَمْثَالَهُمْ تَبْدِيلًا naḥnu khalaqnāhum washadadnā asrahum wa-idhā shi'nā baddalnā amthālahum tabdīlan We Ourselves created them and made them strong in their parts, and when We will, with the like of them, will We replace them (Refer to Verses 47:38; 56:61; 56:62.) This may mean also the change of form in conformity with Verses 56:61; 56:62 or it may mean to replace you with some other generation in conformity with 47:38. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Insaan:29 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ هَذِهِ تَذْكِرَةٌ فَمَنْ شَاءَ اتَّخَذَ إِلَى رَبِّهِ سَبِيلًا inna hādhihi tadhkiratun faman shāa ittakhadha ilā rabbihi sabīlan This is indeed a reminder. So let anyone who wishes take the way toward his Lord.

item.title: Al-Insaan:29 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ هَذِهِ تَذْكِرَةٌ فَمَنْ شَاءَ اتَّخَذَ إِلَى رَبِّهِ سَبِيلًا inna hādhihi tadhkiratun faman shāa ittakhadha ilā rabbihi sabīlan Indeed, this is a reminder, so he who wills may take to his Lord a way. See 76:23

item.title: Al-Insaan:29 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ هَذِهِ تَذْكِرَةٌ فَمَنْ شَاءَ اتَّخَذَ إِلَى رَبِّهِ سَبِيلًا inna hādhihi tadhkiratun faman shāa ittakhadha ilā rabbihi sabīlan Verily this is a Reminder, so whosoever pleaseth, taketh unto his Lord the (Right) way See 76:28

item.title: Al-Insaan:30 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا تَشَاءُونَ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا wamā tashāūna illā an yashāa l-lahu inna l-laha kāna ʿalīman ḥakīman But you do not wish unless it is wished by Allah. Indeed Allah is all-knowing, all-wise.

item.title: Al-Insaan:30 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا تَشَاءُونَ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا wamā tashāūna illā an yashāa l-lahu inna l-laha kāna ʿalīman ḥakīman And you do not will except that Allah wills. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise. See 76:23

item.title: Al-Insaan:30 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا تَشَاءُونَ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا wamā tashāūna illā an yashāa l-lahu inna l-laha kāna ʿalīman ḥakīman And ye desire not save what God desireth; Verily God is All-Knowing, the All-Wise This is the exclusive quality of the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt which God wants to please them with His acknowledgement of it in open words. The whole of this chapter is an open acknowledgment of the Lord, of the unique excellence of the Holy Ahl Al-Bayt whom He Himself had purified to the limits of purification. This confirms what is said in Verse 74:55 and Verse 74:56. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Insaan:31 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يُدْخِلُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ وَالظَّالِمِينَ أَعَدَّ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا yud'khilu man yashāu fī raḥmatihi wal-ẓālimīna aʿadda lahum ʿadhāban alīman He admits whomever He wishes into His mercy, and as for the wrongdoers, He has prepared for them a painful punishment.

item.title: Al-Insaan:31 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يُدْخِلُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ وَالظَّالِمِينَ أَعَدَّ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا yud'khilu man yashāu fī raḥmatihi wal-ẓālimīna aʿadda lahum ʿadhāban alīman He admits whom He wills into His mercy; but the wrongdoers - He has prepared for them a painful punishment. See 76:23

item.title: Al-Insaan:31 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يُدْخِلُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ وَالظَّالِمِينَ أَعَدَّ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا yud'khilu man yashāu fī raḥmatihi wal-ẓālimīna aʿadda lahum ʿadhāban alīman He admitteth whosoever He willeth into His mercy; and (as for) the unjust ones, He hath prepared for them a painful chastisement See 76:30

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذَا السَّمَاءُ انْشَقَّتْ idhā l-samāu inshaqqat When the sky is split open

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذَا السَّمَاءُ انْشَقَّتْ idhā l-samāu inshaqqat When the sky has split (open). بَلَىٰ إِنَّ رَبَّهُ كَانَ بِهِ بَصِيرًا Yes! Verily, his Lord has been ever beholding him! Meaning: certainly Allah will repeat his creation just as he began his creation, and He will reward him based upon his deeds, whether they were good or bad. He was ever watchful of him, meaning All-Knowing and All-Aware.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذَا السَّمَاءُ انْشَقَّتْ idhā l-samāu inshaqqat When the heaven shall rend asunder (Refer to: 82:1.) Refers to what will happen to the sky at the dawn of the Day of Judgment, i.e., when the sky will be rent asunder - to manifest the state of reality.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّهَا وَحُقَّتْ wa-adhinat lirabbihā waḥuqqat and gives ear to its Lord as it should.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّهَا وَحُقَّتْ wa-adhinat lirabbihā waḥuqqat And has listened (i.e., responded)1 to its Lord and was obligated (to do so). See 84:1

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّهَا وَحُقَّتْ wa-adhinat lirabbihā waḥuqqat And it shall hearken unto its Lord, and (as) it ought to do! The heavens with their greatness, and limitless extent, only await the command of the Lord which shall be carried out.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا الْأَرْضُ مُدَّتْ wa-idhā l-arḍu muddat When the earth is spread out

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا الْأَرْضُ مُدَّتْ wa-idhā l-arḍu muddat And when the earth has been extended.1 See 84:1

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا الْأَرْضُ مُدَّتْ wa-idhā l-arḍu muddat And when the earth shall be stretched out (flattened) (Refer to: 71:26 or disintegrated.) The earth will be changed from its global form to a flat levelled plain.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَلْقَتْ مَا فِيهَا وَتَخَلَّتْ wa-alqat mā fīhā watakhallat and throws out what is in it, emptying itself,

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَلْقَتْ مَا فِيهَا وَتَخَلَّتْ wa-alqat mā fīhā watakhallat And has cast out that within it1 and relinquished (it). See 84:1

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَلْقَتْ مَا فِيهَا وَتَخَلَّتْ wa-alqat mā fīhā watakhallat And shall cast forth whatever is in it and becometh empty (Refer to: 99:1 - 99:2.) All the things - minerals, metals and the bodies of the innumerable generations buried in it, i.e., all its contents, will be thrown out, i.e., the earth will vanish with all its contents destroyed, and reduced to nothing. In this verse and 99:2 points out the time for the disintegration, i.e., when the earth's productive capacity gets exhausted, and this principle is applicable to all growing and evolutionary movement in every part and particle of the Universe. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّهَا وَحُقَّتْ wa-adhinat lirabbihā waḥuqqat and gives ear to its Lord as it should.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّهَا وَحُقَّتْ wa-adhinat lirabbihā waḥuqqat And has listened (i.e., responded) to its Lord and was obligated (to do so). See 84:1
