item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّهَا وَحُقَّتْ wa-adhinat lirabbihā waḥuqqat And it shall hearken unto its Lord, and as it aught to do! See 84:4

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاأَيُّهَا الْإِنْسَانُ إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَى رَبِّكَ كَدْحًا فَمُلَاقِيهِ yāayyuhā l-insānu innaka kādiḥun ilā rabbika kadḥan famulāqīhi O man! You are labouring toward your Lord laboriously, and you will encounter Him.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاأَيُّهَا الْإِنْسَانُ إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَى رَبِّكَ كَدْحًا فَمُلَاقِيهِ yāayyuhā l-insānu innaka kādiḥun ilā rabbika kadḥan famulāqīhi O mankind, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with (great) exertion1 and will meet it.2 See 84:1

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاأَيُّهَا الْإِنْسَانُ إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَى رَبِّكَ كَدْحًا فَمُلَاقِيهِ yāayyuhā l-insānu innaka kādiḥun ilā rabbika kadḥan famulāqīhi O' man! Verily thou art in strive unto thy Lord, (with) a striving, and thus thou art meeting Him! The path of righteousness, i.e., the path of those who earnestly wish to get nearer to the Lord, is full of toil and misery. It is the godly ones that scorn and forego the pleasures of this life and choose the life of want and difficulties. Those who toil in the sincere hope of meeting the Lord, are assured of their success so that they may not fall victims to dejection and give up their quest for Him.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ fa-ammā man ūtiya kitābahu biyamīnihi Then as for him who is given his record in his right hand,

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ fa-ammā man ūtiya kitābahu biyamīnihi Then as for he who is given his record in his right hand. See 84:1

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ fa-ammā man ūtiya kitābahu biyamīnihi And he who is given his Book in his right hand. (Refer to: 17:71, 69:19.) Those who suffered, and yet led pure lives of faith and righteousness and suffered miseries in the way of the Lord 1and yet toiled continuously to earn His pleasure for which they avoided the pleasures of this life and chose for themselves and remained contented with the miseries and sufferings. They avoided evil in spite of its strong attractions and earned goodness at all costs.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَسَوْفَ يُحَاسَبُ حِسَابًا يَسِيرًا fasawfa yuḥāsabu ḥisāban yasīran he shall soon receive an easy reckoning,

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَسَوْفَ يُحَاسَبُ حِسَابًا يَسِيرًا fasawfa yuḥāsabu ḥisāban yasīran He will be judged with an easy account. See 84:1

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَسَوْفَ يُحَاسَبُ حِسَابًا يَسِيرًا fasawfa yuḥāsabu ḥisāban yasīran Soon shall he be reckoned (with) an easy reckoning The reckoning will be affected without the least difficulty. The Holy Prophet said that he who has these three qualities shall meet a very easy accounting at the judgment. He said: - To provide the one who hath deprived thee of the legitimate due. Meet the one who shuns you. Pardon him who has been unkind to you.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَنْقَلِبُ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ مَسْرُورًا wayanqalibu ilā ahlihi masrūran and he will return to his folks joyfully.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَنْقَلِبُ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ مَسْرُورًا wayanqalibu ilā ahlihi masrūran And return to his people in happiness. See 84:1

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَنْقَلِبُ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ مَسْرُورًا wayanqalibu ilā ahlihi masrūran And he shall return unto his people delighted To his people, i.e., to his kith and kin and the others spiritually on the same level with him without the restriction of the age, i.e., preceding or succeeding him in time.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ وَرَاءَ ظَهْرِهِ wa-ammā man ūtiya kitābahu warāa ẓahrihi But as for him who is given his record from behind his back,

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ وَرَاءَ ظَهْرِهِ wa-ammā man ūtiya kitābahu warāa ẓahrihi But as for he who is given his record behind his back. See 84:1

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ وَرَاءَ ظَهْرِهِ wa-ammā man ūtiya kitābahu warāa ẓahrihi And he who is given his Book (from) behind (Left Side, Refer to: 69:25.) his back The disbelievers and the wicked will have their hands tied at their back and hence they will be given their records from behind them. He would wish that he had not been given any record at all1.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَسَوْفَ يَدْعُوْۤا ثُبُورًا fasawfa yadʿū thubūran he will pray for annihilation,1

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَسَوْفَ يَدْعُوْۤا ثُبُورًا fasawfa yadʿū thubūran He will cry out for destruction. See 84:1

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَسَوْفَ يَدْعُوْۤا ثُبُورًا fasawfa yadʿū thubūran He shall invoke destruction The wicked would wish for death and annihilation once for all but they will be in a state which will be neither life nor death1.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَصْلَى سَعِيرًا wayaṣlā saʿīran and he will enter the Blaze.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَصْلَى سَعِيرًا wayaṣlā saʿīran And (enter to) burn in a Blaze. See 84:1

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَصْلَى سَعِيرًا wayaṣlā saʿīran And shall be committed to the flaming fire See 84:11

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّهُ كَانَ فِي أَهْلِهِ مَسْرُورًا innahu kāna fī ahlihi masrūran Indeed he used to be joyful among his folk,

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّهُ كَانَ فِي أَهْلِهِ مَسْرُورًا innahu kāna fī ahlihi masrūran Indeed, he had (once) been among his people in happiness. See 84:1

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:13 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّهُ كَانَ فِي أَهْلِهِ مَسْرُورًا innahu kāna fī ahlihi masrūran Verily he was joyous (In his life in the world before death.) among his people While in this life the wicked one was happy rejoicing and enjoying the pleasures of the world among his people, i.e., relatives and friends, without any regard to the pleasure or the displeasure of the Lord.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:14 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّهُ ظَنَّ أَنْ لَنْ يَحُورَ innahu ẓanna an lan yaḥūra and indeed he thought he would never return.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:14 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّهُ ظَنَّ أَنْ لَنْ يَحُورَ innahu ẓanna an lan yaḥūra Indeed, he had thought he would never return (to Allah). See 84:1

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:14 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّهُ ظَنَّ أَنْ لَنْ يَحُورَ innahu ẓanna an lan yaḥūra Verily he thought that never will he return (unto God) Man is led into the evil ways of life mostly of his self-complacence and self-conceit and getting himself intoxicated of the enjoyment of his carnal desires in his lower life, forgetting his personal responsibility and his accountability on his return to the Lord in the ultimate. He must remember the inevitability of his return to Him.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلَى إِنَّ رَبَّهُ كَانَ بِهِ بَصِيرًا balā inna rabbahu kāna bihi baṣīran Yes indeed, his Lord sees him best.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلَى إِنَّ رَبَّهُ كَانَ بِهِ بَصِيرًا balā inna rabbahu kāna bihi baṣīran But yes! Indeed, his Lord was ever, of him, Seeing. See 84:1

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلَى إِنَّ رَبَّهُ كَانَ بِهِ بَصِيرًا balā inna rabbahu kāna bihi baṣīran Yea! Verily his Lord was always vigilant of him Man forgets that the Lord is ever watchful of him for his motives as well as his deeds.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِالشَّفَقِ falā uq'simu bil-shafaqi So I swear by the evening glow,

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِالشَّفَقِ falā uq'simu bil-shafaqi So I swear by the twilight glow. But no! I swear by Ash-Shafaq (84:16). And the night and what it Wasaqa (84:17). And the moon when it Ittasaq (84:18). You shall certainly travel from stage to stage (84:19). What is the matter with them, that they believe not (84:20). And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they fall not prostrate (84:21). Nay, those who disbelieve deny (84:22). And Allah knows best what they gather (84:23). So, announce to them a painful torment (84:24). Save those who believe and do righteous good deeds, for them is a reward that will never come to an end (84:25). Swearing by the Various Stages of Man's Journey It has been reported from Ali, Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ubadah bin As-Samit, Abu Hurayrah, Shaddad bin Aws, Ibn Umar, Muhammad bin…

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِالشَّفَقِ falā uq'simu bil-shafaqi And I swear by the Glow of the sunset" (84:61) The beautiful and wonderful show of the radiance of the sun in the evening which is the work of nature. The note on this verse by a commentator1 is another example of a wishful distortion of the Qur'an narrowing its original significance to the rise and the fall of the Arabs in power. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاللَّيْلِ وَمَا وَسَقَ wa-al-layli wamā wasaqa by the night and what it is fraught with,

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاللَّيْلِ وَمَا وَسَقَ wa-al-layli wamā wasaqa And (by) the night and what it envelops. See 84:16

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:17 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاللَّيْلِ وَمَا وَسَقَ wa-al-layli wamā wasaqa And (by) the night and what it enshroudeth Man's attention is drawn to the mystic functioning of the great and the wonderful phenomena of nature in the daily life in this world, the functioning of the wonderful organization of the universe being before man's eyes all the while he takes these great events of the life, to be so common and so easy that he does not think of ever pondering over the secret of the genetic factors in the functions of nature which every moment passes from one stage or state into another or regulated and controlled that the daily repetition is maintained with perfect success without the least failure.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:18 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْقَمَرِ إِذَا اتَّسَقَ wal-qamari idhā ittasaqa by the moon when it blooms full:

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:18 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْقَمَرِ إِذَا اتَّسَقَ wal-qamari idhā ittasaqa And (by) the moon when it becomes full. See 84:16

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:18 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْقَمَرِ إِذَا اتَّسَقَ wal-qamari idhā ittasaqa And (by) the moon when at her full See 84:17

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:19 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَتَرْكَبُنَّ طَبَقًا عَنْ طَبَقٍ latarkabunna ṭabaqan ʿan ṭabaqin you will surely fare from stage to stage.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:19 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَتَرْكَبُنَّ طَبَقًا عَنْ طَبَقٍ latarkabunna ṭabaqan ʿan ṭabaqin (That) you will surely embark upon (i.e., experience) state after state.1 See 84:16

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:19 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَتَرْكَبُنَّ طَبَقًا عَنْ طَبَقٍ latarkabunna ṭabaqan ʿan ṭabaqin That ye shall certainly march (Ride.) from state to state See 84:17

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:20 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَمَا لَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ famā lahum lā yu'minūna So what is the matter with them that they will not believe?

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:20 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَمَا لَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ famā lahum lā yu'minūna So what is (the matter) with them (that) they do not believe. See 84:16

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:20 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَمَا لَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ famā lahum lā yu'minūna But what then hath happened unto them that they believe not? With so much of the guidance from heaven through the wonderful manifestation of the Might, and the Wisdom and the Existence of God and so much of the exertion to bring home to man the Truth, through a long line of God's inspired men, His apostles, if man still fails to believe in the reality, it is naturally a matter of wonder and surprise.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:21 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا قُرِئَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقُرْاٰنُ لَا يَسْجُدُونَ wa-idhā quri-a ʿalayhimu l-qur'ānu lā yasjudūna And when the Qur'ān is recited to them they will not prostrate?

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:21 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا قُرِئَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقُرْاٰنُ لَا يَسْجُدُونَ wa-idhā quri-a ʿalayhimu l-qur'ānu lā yasjudūna And when the Qur’ān is recited to them, they do not prostrate (to Allah)? See 84:16

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:21 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا قُرِئَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقُرْاٰنُ لَا يَسْجُدُونَ wa-idhā quri-a ʿalayhimu l-qur'ānu lā yasjudūna And when is recited unto them the Qur'an, they prostrate not in obeisance (Refer to: 7:206, 13:15, 22:77, 32:15.) ? The Prostration means respect, reverence and the humble submission to God1 - Prostration on the part of the reciters of this verse is only 'Sunnat', traditional, and not 'Wajib', i.e., compulsory.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:22 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا يُكَذِّبُونَ bali alladhīna kafarū yukadhibūna Rather the faithless deny,

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:22 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا يُكَذِّبُونَ bali alladhīna kafarū yukadhibūna But those who have disbelieved deny. See 84:16

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:22 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا يُكَذِّبُونَ bali alladhīna kafarū yukadhibūna Nay! those who disbelieve belie (the Truth) It is said that when above verse 21 was revealed, the Holy Prophet went into prostration and the believers present there followed his example. The disbelievers got over the backs of the believers lying in prostration and standing on the heads began clapping their hands. It was then these verses were revealed.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:23 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يُوعُونَ wal-lahu aʿlamu bimā yūʿūna and Allah knows best what they keep to themselves.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:23 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يُوعُونَ wal-lahu aʿlamu bimā yūʿūna And Allah is most knowing of what they keep within themselves. See 84:16

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:23 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يُوعُونَ wal-lahu aʿlamu bimā yūʿūna And Verily God knoweth best what they hide (in their hearts) See 84:22

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:24 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَبَشِّرْهُمْ بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ fabashir'hum biʿadhābin alīmin So warn them of a painful punishment,

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:24 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَبَشِّرْهُمْ بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ fabashir'hum biʿadhābin alīmin So give them tidings of a painful punishment. See 84:16

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:24 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَبَشِّرْهُمْ بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ fabashir'hum biʿadhābin alīmin So announce thou unto them the tidings of a painful chastisement! See 84:22

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:25 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِلَّا الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا وَعَمِلُوْۤا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ illā alladhīna āmanū waʿamilū l-ṣāliḥāti lahum ajrun ghayru mamnūnin except such as are faithful and do righteous deeds: there will be an everlasting reward for them.

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:25 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِلَّا الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا وَعَمِلُوْۤا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ illā alladhīna āmanū waʿamilū l-ṣāliḥāti lahum ajrun ghayru mamnūnin Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds. For them is a reward uninterrupted. See 84:16

item.title: Al-Inshiqaaq:25 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِلَّا الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا وَعَمِلُوْۤا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ illā alladhīna āmanū waʿamilū l-ṣāliḥāti lahum ajrun ghayru mamnūnin Save those who believe and do good deeds, for them shall be a recompense unending (Refer to: 41:8.) See 84:22

item.title: Al-Israa:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي أَسْرٰی بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلًا مِنَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ الْأَقْصَا الَّذِي بَارَكْنَا حَوْلَهُ لِنُرِيَهُ مِنْ ءَايَاتِنَا إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ sub'ḥāna alladhī asrā biʿabdihi laylan mina l-masjidi l-ḥarāmi ilā l-masjidi l-aqṣā alladhī bāraknā ḥawlahu linuriyahu min āyātinā innahu huwa l-samīʿu l-baṣīru Immaculate is He who carried His servant on a journey by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque whose environs We have blessed, that We might show him some of Our signs. Indeed He is the All-hearing, the All-seeing.

item.title: Al-Israa:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي أَسْرٰی بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلًا مِنَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ الْأَقْصَا الَّذِي بَارَكْنَا حَوْلَهُ لِنُرِيَهُ مِنْ ءَايَاتِنَا إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ sub'ḥāna alladhī asrā biʿabdihi laylan mina l-masjidi l-ḥarāmi ilā l-masjidi l-aqṣā alladhī bāraknā ḥawlahu linuriyahu min āyātinā innahu huwa l-samīʿu l-baṣīru Exalted1 is He who took His Servant (i.e., Prophet Muḥammad SAW) by night from al-Masjid al-Ḥarām to al-Masjid al-Aqṣā,2 whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him of Our signs. Indeed, He is the Hearing,3 the Seeing.4

item.title: Al-Israa:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي أَسْرٰی بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلًا مِنَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ الْأَقْصَا الَّذِي بَارَكْنَا حَوْلَهُ لِنُرِيَهُ مِنْ ءَايَاتِنَا إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ sub'ḥāna alladhī asrā biʿabdihi laylan mina l-masjidi l-ḥarāmi ilā l-masjidi l-aqṣā alladhī bāraknā ḥawlahu linuriyahu min āyātinā innahu huwa l-samīʿu l-baṣīru Glory be to Him Who carried (Caused the journey.) His servant (Apostle Muhammad) by night from the Holy Mosque (of the Ka'ba) to the Farthest Mosque, which We have blessed its environment (Precincts – Neighbourhood.) that We may show unto him, of Our signs; Verily He, is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. Read verses 53:8 & 53:9. This verse relates about the Holy Prophet's Mi'raj, i.e., Ascension to meet God at His Very Seat (the Arsh) the Centre of His authority. 'Masjid al-Haram,' i.e., the Mosque built around the Ka'ba and 'Masjid al-Aqsa,' i.e., the Farthest Mosque - The…

item.title: Al-Israa:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَءَاتَيْنَا مُوسٰی الْكِتَابَ وَجَعَلْنَاهُ هُدًى لِبَنِي إِسْرَاءِيلَ أَلَّا تَتَّخِذُوا مِنْ دُونِي وَكِيلًا waātaynā mūsā l-kitāba wajaʿalnāhu hudan libanī is'rāīla allā tattakhidhū min dūnī wakīlan We gave Moses the Book, and made it a guide for the Children of Israel —[saying,] 'Do not take any trustee besides Me'—

item.title: Al-Israa:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَءَاتَيْنَا مُوسٰی الْكِتَابَ وَجَعَلْنَاهُ هُدًى لِبَنِي إِسْرَاءِيلَ أَلَّا تَتَّخِذُوا مِنْ دُونِي وَكِيلًا waātaynā mūsā l-kitāba wajaʿalnāhu hudan libanī is'rāīla allā tattakhidhū min dūnī wakīlan And We gave Musa the Scripture and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel that you not take other than Me as Disposer of affairs.1 And We gave Musa the Scripture and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel (saying): "Take none other than Me as (your) Wakil (17:2). "O offspring of those whom We carried (in the ship) with Nuh! Verily, he was a grateful servant (17:3). Musa and How He was Given the Tawrah When Allah mentions how He took His servant Muhammad SAW, on the Journey by Night, He follows it by mentioning Musa, His servant and Messenger who also spoke with Him. Allah often mentions Muhammad and Musa…

item.title: Al-Israa:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَءَاتَيْنَا مُوسٰی الْكِتَابَ وَجَعَلْنَاهُ هُدًى لِبَنِي إِسْرَاءِيلَ أَلَّا تَتَّخِذُوا مِنْ دُونِي وَكِيلًا waātaynā mūsā l-kitāba wajaʿalnāhu hudan libanī is'rāīla allā tattakhidhū min dūnī wakīlan And gave We unto Moses the Book (Torah) and made it a guidance for the children of Israel, (saying) that "Take ye not other than Me (any one as) a guardian." After stating the Ascension, Qur'an makes a comparison with Moses, the way he received the Book from God on the mountain and the receiving of the highest knowledge including all that was given to all the previous Prophets at the highest level and both events are miracles if one is possible the other is also possible, i.e., the power which brings the Book to the mountain can take a person up into heaven. The object of both the events of the Revelation and the Ascension…

item.title: Al-Israa:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ذُرِّيَّةَ مَنْ حَمَلْنَا مَعَ نُوحٍ إِنَّهُ كَانَ عَبْدًا شَكُورًا dhurriyyata man ḥamalnā maʿa nūḥin innahu kāna ʿabdan shakūran descendants of those whom We carried [in the ark] with Noah. Indeed he was a grateful servant.

item.title: Al-Israa:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ذُرِّيَّةَ مَنْ حَمَلْنَا مَعَ نُوحٍ إِنَّهُ كَانَ عَبْدًا شَكُورًا dhurriyyata man ḥamalnā maʿa nūḥin innahu kāna ʿabdan shakūran O descendants of those We carried (in the ship) with Nuh. Indeed, he was a grateful servant. See 17:2

item.title: Al-Israa:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ذُرِّيَّةَ مَنْ حَمَلْنَا مَعَ نُوحٍ إِنَّهُ كَانَ عَبْدًا شَكُورًا dhurriyyata man ḥamalnā maʿa nūḥin innahu kāna ʿabdan shakūran (O' ye!) The offspring of those (The faithful issues of Noah and the righteous members of his family.) whom We bore with Noah (in the Ark); Verily, he (Noah) was a grateful servant. See 17:2

item.title: Al-Israa:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَضَيْنَا إِلَى بَنِي إِسْرَاءِيلَ فِي الْكِتَابِ لَتُفْسِدُنَّ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَرَّتَيْنِ وَلَتَعْلُنَّ عُلُوًّا كَبِيرًا waqaḍaynā ilā banī is'rāīla fī l-kitābi latuf'sidunna fī l-arḍi marratayni walataʿlunna ʿuluwwan kabīran We revealed to the Children of Israel in the Book: 'Twice you will cause corruption on the earth, and you will perpetrate great tyranny.'

item.title: Al-Israa:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَضَيْنَا إِلَى بَنِي إِسْرَاءِيلَ فِي الْكِتَابِ لَتُفْسِدُنَّ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَرَّتَيْنِ وَلَتَعْلُنَّ عُلُوًّا كَبِيرًا waqaḍaynā ilā banī is'rāīla fī l-kitābi latuf'sidunna fī l-arḍi marratayni walataʿlunna ʿuluwwan kabīran And We conveyed1 to the Children of Israel in the Scripture that, "You will surely cause corruption on the earth twice, and you will surely reach (a degree of) great haughtiness." And We decreed for the Children of Israel in the Scripture: Indeed you would do mischief in the land twice and you will become tyrants and extremely arrogant! (17:4). So, when the promise came for the first of the two, We sent against you servants of Ours given to terrible warfare. They entered the very innermost parts of your homes. And it was a promise (completely) fulfilled (17:5). Then We gave you a return of victory over them. And We helped you with…

item.title: Al-Israa:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَضَيْنَا إِلَى بَنِي إِسْرَاءِيلَ فِي الْكِتَابِ لَتُفْسِدُنَّ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَرَّتَيْنِ وَلَتَعْلُنَّ عُلُوًّا كَبِيرًا waqaḍaynā ilā banī is'rāīla fī l-kitābi latuf'sidunna fī l-arḍi marratayni walataʿlunna ʿuluwwan kabīran And (Refer to verse 5:78.) We had (expressly) declared unto the children of Israel (a warning) in the Book (Torah saying): "Certainly ye will make mischief in the land twice, (Refer to verse 5:78.) and certainly will ye be elated with great arrogance." Twice, i.e., Once slaying the Apostle Usha and disobeying the Apostle Ermia. Again, slaying the Apostle Yahya (John) and plotting to kill Jesus. 1Those of the Israelites who disbelieved their apostles were cursed by David and Jesus and owing to the transgression of the Israelites, Jerusalem was destroyed once by the Babylonians and again by the Romans. For warnings from Jesus see Math. 23/38 and Luke 21/24 and the Psalms are…

item.title: Al-Israa:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِذَا جَاءَ وَعْدُ أُولَاهُمَا بَعَثْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ عِبَادًا لَنَا أُولِي بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ فَجَاسُوْۤا خِلَالَ الدِّيَارِ وَكَانَ وَعْدًا مَفْعُولًا fa-idhā jāa waʿdu ūlāhumā baʿathnā ʿalaykum ʿibādan lanā ulī basin shadīdin fajāsū khilāla l-diyāri wakāna waʿdan mafʿūlan So when the first occasion of the two [prophecies] came, We aroused against you Our servants possessing great might, and they ransacked [your] habitations, and the promise was bound to be fulfilled.

item.title: Al-Israa:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِذَا جَاءَ وَعْدُ أُولَاهُمَا بَعَثْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ عِبَادًا لَنَا أُولِي بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ فَجَاسُوْۤا خِلَالَ الدِّيَارِ وَكَانَ وَعْدًا مَفْعُولًا fa-idhā jāa waʿdu ūlāhumā baʿathnā ʿalaykum ʿibādan lanā ulī basin shadīdin fajāsū khilāla l-diyāri wakāna waʿdan mafʿūlan So when the (time of) promise came for the first of them,1 We sent against you servants of Ours - those of great military might, and they probed (even) into the homes,2 and it was a promise fulfilled. See 17:4

item.title: Al-Israa:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِذَا جَاءَ وَعْدُ أُولَاهُمَا بَعَثْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ عِبَادًا لَنَا أُولِي بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ فَجَاسُوْۤا خِلَالَ الدِّيَارِ وَكَانَ وَعْدًا مَفْعُولًا fa-idhā jāa waʿdu ūlāhumā baʿathnā ʿalaykum ʿibādan lanā ulī basin shadīdin fajāsū khilāla l-diyāri wakāna waʿdan mafʿūlan So when came the first of the two (promises), raised We upon you Our servants, with terrible prowess, so they invaded (They treaded every nook and corner.) the innermost parts of your abodes; and it was a warning (completely) fulfilled. Jalut tortured the Israelites and plundered their habitations and there he was defeated by Talut and was killed by David. Some commentators say that the reference is to the punishment which was inflicted through violent winds and dreadful thunderous sounds.

item.title: Al-Israa:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَا لَكُمُ الْكَرَّةَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَمْدَدْنَاكُمْ بِأَمْوَالٍ وَبَنِينَ وَجَعَلْنَاكُمْ أَكْثَرَ نَفِيرًا thumma radadnā lakumu l-karata ʿalayhim wa-amdadnākum bi-amwālin wabanīna wajaʿalnākum akthara nafīran Then We gave you back the turn [to prevail] over them, and We aided you with children and wealth, and made you greater in number,

item.title: Al-Israa:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَا لَكُمُ الْكَرَّةَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَمْدَدْنَاكُمْ بِأَمْوَالٍ وَبَنِينَ وَجَعَلْنَاكُمْ أَكْثَرَ نَفِيرًا thumma radadnā lakumu l-karata ʿalayhim wa-amdadnākum bi-amwālin wabanīna wajaʿalnākum akthara nafīran Then We gave back to you a return victory over them. And We reinforced you with wealth and sons and made you more numerous in manpower. See 17:4

item.title: Al-Israa:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَا لَكُمُ الْكَرَّةَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَمْدَدْنَاكُمْ بِأَمْوَالٍ وَبَنِينَ وَجَعَلْنَاكُمْ أَكْثَرَ نَفِيرًا thumma radadnā lakumu l-karata ʿalayhim wa-amdadnākum bi-amwālin wabanīna wajaʿalnākum akthara nafīran Then returned We unto you the turn (to prevail) against them and aided you with wealth and offspring and made you a numerous host. The return of fortune referred to is the return of the Israelites to Jerusalem and their building the temple under Zurubbabel and their once again being prosperous. This is the second promise, i.e., The Roman onslaught and the destruction of Jerusalem when the Jews could not establish any dominion of their own anywhere until the recent Israelite republic - to which verse 17:8 refers to, with a warning that should they repeat the mischief, God will repeat the punishment after which there will be no more respite - excepting conviction to Hell. This is…

item.title: Al-Israa:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنْ أَحْسَنْتُمْ أَحْسَنْتُمْ لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ وَإِنْ أَسَأْتُمْ فَلَهَا فَإِذَا جَاءَ وَعْدُ الْاٰخِرَةُ لِيَسُوءُوْۤا وُجُوهَكُمْ وَلِيَدْخُلُوا الْمَسْجِدَ كَمَا دَخَلُوهُ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَلِيُتَبِّرُوا مَا عَلَوْا تَتْبِيرًا in aḥsantum aḥsantum li-anfusikum wa-in asatum falahā fa-idhā jāa waʿdu l-ākhirati liyasūū wujūhakum waliyadkhulū l-masjida kamā dakhalūhu awwala marratin waliyutabbirū mā ʿalaw tatbīran [saying,] 'If you do good, you will do good to your [own] souls, and if you do evil, it will be [evil] for them.' So when the occasion for the other [prophecy] comes, they will make your faces1 wretched, and enter the Temple just as they entered it the first time, and utterly destroy whatever they come upon.

item.title: Al-Israa:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنْ أَحْسَنْتُمْ أَحْسَنْتُمْ لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ وَإِنْ أَسَأْتُمْ فَلَهَا فَإِذَا جَاءَ وَعْدُ الْاٰخِرَةُ لِيَسُوءُوْۤا وُجُوهَكُمْ وَلِيَدْخُلُوا الْمَسْجِدَ كَمَا دَخَلُوهُ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَلِيُتَبِّرُوا مَا عَلَوْا تَتْبِيرًا in aḥsantum aḥsantum li-anfusikum wa-in asatum falahā fa-idhā jāa waʿdu l-ākhirati liyasūū wujūhakum waliyadkhulū l-masjida kamā dakhalūhu awwala marratin waliyutabbirū mā ʿalaw tatbīran (And said), "If you do good, you do good for yourselves; and if you do evil, (you do it) to them (i.e., yourselves)." Then when the final (i.e., second) promise came, (We sent your enemies) to sadden your faces and to enter the masjid (i.e., the temple in Jerusalem), as they entered it the first time, and to destroy what they had taken over with (total) destruction. See 17:4

item.title: Al-Israa:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنْ أَحْسَنْتُمْ أَحْسَنْتُمْ لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ وَإِنْ أَسَأْتُمْ فَلَهَا فَإِذَا جَاءَ وَعْدُ الْاٰخِرَةُ لِيَسُوءُوْۤا وُجُوهَكُمْ وَلِيَدْخُلُوا الْمَسْجِدَ كَمَا دَخَلُوهُ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَلِيُتَبِّرُوا مَا عَلَوْا تَتْبِيرًا in aḥsantum aḥsantum li-anfusikum wa-in asatum falahā fa-idhā jāa waʿdu l-ākhirati liyasūū wujūhakum waliyadkhulū l-masjida kamā dakhalūhu awwala marratin waliyutabbirū mā ʿalaw tatbīran If ye do good, ye do it for your own selves; and if ye do evil it is (in like manner) for your ownselves; So when came the second promise (warning to be fulfilled) (We roused your enemies to) sadden (with grief & sorrow.) your faces, and that they may enter the Mosque (The Mosque at Jerusalem.) as they entered it the first time, and to destroy whatever they conquered (with) total destruction. The opening words of the verse clearly declare the personal responsibility of each and every individual regarding his or her deeds.…

item.title: Al-Israa:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: عَسٰۤی رَبُّكُمْ أَنْ يَرْحَمَكُمْ وَإِنْ عُدْتُمْ عُدْنَا وَجَعَلْنَا جَهَنَّمَ لِلْكَافِرِينَ حَصِيرًا ʿasā rabbukum an yarḥamakum wa-in ʿudttum ʿud'nā wajaʿalnā jahannama lil'kāfirīna ḥaṣīran Maybe your Lord will have mercy on you, but if you revert, We [too] will revert, and We have made hell a prison for the faithless.

item.title: Al-Israa:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: عَسٰۤی رَبُّكُمْ أَنْ يَرْحَمَكُمْ وَإِنْ عُدْتُمْ عُدْنَا وَجَعَلْنَا جَهَنَّمَ لِلْكَافِرِينَ حَصِيرًا ʿasā rabbukum an yarḥamakum wa-in ʿudttum ʿud'nā wajaʿalnā jahannama lil'kāfirīna ḥaṣīran (Then Allah said), "It is expected, (if you repent), that your Lord will have mercy upon you. But if you return (to sin), We will return (to punishment). And We have made Hell, for the disbelievers, a prison-bed." See 17:4

item.title: Al-Israa:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: عَسٰۤی رَبُّكُمْ أَنْ يَرْحَمَكُمْ وَإِنْ عُدْتُمْ عُدْنَا وَجَعَلْنَا جَهَنَّمَ لِلْكَافِرِينَ حَصِيرًا ʿasā rabbukum an yarḥamakum wa-in ʿudttum ʿud'nā wajaʿalnā jahannama lil'kāfirīna ḥaṣīran It may be that your Lord will have mercy on you, but if ye (again) return (to disobedience) We (too) will return (to chastisement), and We have made Hell for the infidels a prison. See 17:7

item.title: Al-Israa:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ يَهْدِي لِلَّتِي هِيَ أَقْوَمُ وَيُبَشِّرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ الَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ الصَّالِحَاتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ أَجْرًا كَبِيرًا inna hādhā l-qur'āna yahdī lillatī hiya aqwamu wayubashiru l-mu'minīna alladhīna yaʿmalūna l-ṣāliḥāti anna lahum ajran kabīran Indeed this Qur'ān guides to what is most upright, and gives the good news to the faithful who do righteous deeds that there is a great reward for them.

item.title: Al-Israa:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ يَهْدِي لِلَّتِي هِيَ أَقْوَمُ وَيُبَشِّرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ الَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ الصَّالِحَاتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ أَجْرًا كَبِيرًا inna hādhā l-qur'āna yahdī lillatī hiya aqwamu wayubashiru l-mu'minīna alladhīna yaʿmalūna l-ṣāliḥāti anna lahum ajran kabīran Indeed, this Qur’ān guides to that which is most suitable and gives good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a great reward. Verily, this Qur'an guides to that which is most just and right and gives good news to those who believe, those who do righteous deeds, that they will have a great reward (Paradise) (17:9). And that those who do not believe in the Hereafter, for them We have prepared a painful torment (Hell) (17:10). Praising the Qur'an Allah praises His noble Book, the Qur'an, which He revealed to His Messenger Muhammad SAW. It directs people to the best and clearest…

item.title: Al-Israa:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ يَهْدِي لِلَّتِي هِيَ أَقْوَمُ وَيُبَشِّرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ الَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ الصَّالِحَاتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ أَجْرًا كَبِيرًا inna hādhā l-qur'āna yahdī lillatī hiya aqwamu wayubashiru l-mu'minīna alladhīna yaʿmalūna l-ṣāliḥāti anna lahum ajran kabīran Verily, this Qur'an guideth unto that which is the most upright and announceth glad tidings unto the believers who do good that they shall have a great reward, After referring to the ascension to the farthest state of worship or the highest stage of the finite realm beyond which is nothing but absolute infinity, it asserts that Qur'an being originated there in that height is the most comprehensive, perfect Book of guidance in comparison to what was revealed to the other previous prophets whose ascension was not to that height and horizon. The guidance which they received was the stages lower than 'Aw Adna', i.e., rather the nearest.1…

item.title: Al-Israa:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْاٰخِرَةِ أَعْتَدْنَا لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا wa-anna alladhīna lā yu'minūna bil-ākhirati aʿtadnā lahum ʿadhāban alīman As for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, We have prepared a painful punishment for them.

item.title: Al-Israa:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْاٰخِرَةِ أَعْتَدْنَا لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا wa-anna alladhīna lā yu'minūna bil-ākhirati aʿtadnā lahum ʿadhāban alīman And that those who do not believe in the Hereafter - We have prepared for them a painful punishment. See 17:9

item.title: Al-Israa:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْاٰخِرَةِ أَعْتَدْنَا لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا wa-anna alladhīna lā yu'minūna bil-ākhirati aʿtadnā lahum ʿadhāban alīman And those who believe not in the hereafter, We have prepared for them a painful torment. See 17:9

item.title: Al-Israa:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَدْعُ الْإِنْسَانُ بِالشَّرِّ دُعَاءَهُ بِالْخَيْرِ وَكَانَ الْإِنْسَانُ عَجُولًا wayadʿu l-insānu bil-shari duʿāahu bil-khayri wakāna l-insānu ʿajūlan Man prays for ill as [avidly as] he prays for good, and man is overhasty.

item.title: Al-Israa:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَدْعُ الْإِنْسَانُ بِالشَّرِّ دُعَاءَهُ بِالْخَيْرِ وَكَانَ الْإِنْسَانُ عَجُولًا wayadʿu l-insānu bil-shari duʿāahu bil-khayri wakāna l-insānu ʿajūlan And man supplicates for evil (when angry) as he supplicates for good, and man is ever hasty.1 And man invokes (Allah) for evil as he invokes (Allah) for good and man is ever hasty (17:11). Man's Haste and Prayers against Himself Allah tells us about man's haste and how he sometimes prays against himself or his children or his wealth, praying for something bad to happen for them, or for them to die or be destroyed, invoking curses, etc. If Allah were to answer his prayer, he would be destroyed because of it, as Allah says: وَلَوْ يُعَجِّلُ اللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ الشَّرَّ And were Allah to hasten for mankind the evil... (10:11) This is how it was interpreted by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah. We…

item.title: Al-Israa:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَدْعُ الْإِنْسَانُ بِالشَّرِّ دُعَاءَهُ بِالْخَيْرِ وَكَانَ الْإِنْسَانُ عَجُولًا wayadʿu l-insānu bil-shari duʿāahu bil-khayri wakāna l-insānu ʿajūlan And prayeth man for evil as he prayeth (As sincerely as he ought to pray in the manner for good.) for good; and man in ever hasty. This verse applies to the following occasions: When one is worried or angry against himself or his people in disgust, the individual starts cursing himself and his people in the same earnestness as he prays for good. If God only grants such prayers the individual will meet only perdition, which. But God by His mercy does not do it. Praying for immediate gains, neglecting the ultimate consequences. Praying for things not allowed in the same way that he prays for things allowed. This depicts the common aspects of these three tendencies in man. (A.P.).

item.title: Al-Israa:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ ءَايَتَيْنِ فَمَحَوْنَا ءَايَةَ اللَّيْلِ وَجَعَلْنَا ءَايَةَ النَّهَارِ مُبْصِرَةً لِتَبْتَغُوا فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَلِتَعْلَمُوا عَدَدَ السِّنِينَ وَالْحِسَابَ وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ فَصَّلْنَاهُ تَفْصِيلًا wajaʿalnā al-layla wal-nahāra āyatayni famaḥawnā āyata al-layli wajaʿalnā āyata l-nahāri mub'ṣiratan litabtaghū faḍlan min rabbikum walitaʿlamū ʿadada l-sinīna wal-ḥisāba wakulla shayin faṣṣalnāhu tafṣīlan We made the night and the day two signs. Then We effaced the sign of the night, and made the sign of the day lightsome that you may seek grace from your Lord and that you may know the number of years and the calculation [of time], and We have elaborated everything in detail.1

item.title: Al-Israa:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ ءَايَتَيْنِ فَمَحَوْنَا ءَايَةَ اللَّيْلِ وَجَعَلْنَا ءَايَةَ النَّهَارِ مُبْصِرَةً لِتَبْتَغُوا فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَلِتَعْلَمُوا عَدَدَ السِّنِينَ وَالْحِسَابَ وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ فَصَّلْنَاهُ تَفْصِيلًا wajaʿalnā al-layla wal-nahāra āyatayni famaḥawnā āyata al-layli wajaʿalnā āyata l-nahāri mub'ṣiratan litabtaghū faḍlan min rabbikum walitaʿlamū ʿadada l-sinīna wal-ḥisāba wakulla shayin faṣṣalnāhu tafṣīlan And We have made the night and day two signs, and We erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible1 that you may seek bounty from your Lord and may know the number of years and the account (of time). And everything We have set out in detail. And We have appointed the night and the day as two Ayat (signs). Then, We have obliterated the sign of the night (with darkness) while We have made the sign of the day illuminating, that you may seek bounty from…

item.title: Al-Israa:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ ءَايَتَيْنِ فَمَحَوْنَا ءَايَةَ اللَّيْلِ وَجَعَلْنَا ءَايَةَ النَّهَارِ مُبْصِرَةً لِتَبْتَغُوا فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَلِتَعْلَمُوا عَدَدَ السِّنِينَ وَالْحِسَابَ وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ فَصَّلْنَاهُ تَفْصِيلًا wajaʿalnā al-layla wal-nahāra āyatayni famaḥawnā āyata al-layli wajaʿalnā āyata l-nahāri mub'ṣiratan litabtaghū faḍlan min rabbikum walitaʿlamū ʿadada l-sinīna wal-ḥisāba wakulla shayin faṣṣalnāhu tafṣīlan And We have made the night and the day two (of Our) signs, then cause We the sign of the night to pass away and have made We the sign of the day sight-giving that ye may seek grace from your Lord, and that ye may know the number and the count of the years; and every thing have We explained in detail. The mental tendency of haste in man is in resemblance with the sign of the night which passes away and the ultimate as the sign of the day. The sign of…

item.title: Al-Israa:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَكُلَّ إِنْسَانٍ أَلْزَمْنَاهُ طَائِرَهُ فِي عُنُقِهِ وَنُخْرِجُ لَهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ كِتَابًا يَلْقَاهُ مَنْشُورًا wakulla insānin alzamnāhu ṭāirahu fī ʿunuqihi wanukh'riju lahu yawma l-qiyāmati kitāban yalqāhu manshūran We have attached every person's omen to his neck, and We shall bring it out for him on the Day of Resurrection as a wide open book that he will encounter.

item.title: Al-Israa:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَكُلَّ إِنْسَانٍ أَلْزَمْنَاهُ طَائِرَهُ فِي عُنُقِهِ وَنُخْرِجُ لَهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ كِتَابًا يَلْقَاهُ مَنْشُورًا wakulla insānin alzamnāhu ṭāirahu fī ʿunuqihi wanukh'riju lahu yawma l-qiyāmati kitāban yalqāhu manshūran And (for) every person We have imposed his fate upon his neck,1 and We will produce for him on the Day of Resurrection a record which he will encounter spread open. And We have fastened every man's Ta'irah (deeds) to his neck, and on the Day of Resurrection, We shall bring out for him a Book which he will find wide open (17:13). (It will be said to him): Read your Book. You yourself are sufficient as a reckoner against you this Day (17:14). Every Person will have the Book of his Deeds with Him After mentioning time, and the deeds of the son of Adam that take place therein, Allah says: وَكُلَّ إِنسَانٍ…

item.title: Al-Israa:13 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَكُلَّ إِنْسَانٍ أَلْزَمْنَاهُ طَائِرَهُ فِي عُنُقِهِ وَنُخْرِجُ لَهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ كِتَابًا يَلْقَاهُ مَنْشُورًا wakulla insānin alzamnāhu ṭāirahu fī ʿunuqihi wanukh'riju lahu yawma l-qiyāmati kitāban yalqāhu manshūran And every man's destiny (Arabic 'Taa'ir' i.e., deeds wrought by the individual.) We have caused to cling to his neck; and We will bring forth unto him on the Day of Resurrection a book which he will find wide open. See 17:12

item.title: Al-Israa:14 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اِقْرَأْ كِتَابَكَ كَفَى بِنَفْسِكَ الْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكَ حَسِيبًا iq'ra kitābaka kafā binafsika l-yawma ʿalayka ḥasīban 'Read your book! Today your soul suffices as your own reckoner.'1

item.title: Al-Israa:14 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اِقْرَأْ كِتَابَكَ كَفَى بِنَفْسِكَ الْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكَ حَسِيبًا iq'ra kitābaka kafā binafsika l-yawma ʿalayka ḥasīban (It will be said), "Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as accountant." See 17:13

item.title: Al-Israa:14 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اِقْرَأْ كِتَابَكَ كَفَى بِنَفْسِكَ الْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكَ حَسِيبًا iq'ra kitābaka kafā binafsika l-yawma ʿalayka ḥasīban (It will be said unto him) "Read thou thy book; Sufficeth thine own self today, as a reckoner against thee." Every individual will have the record of his own deeds clung to his neck and they will be weighed in the balance of equity which never mistakes in the least1.

item.title: Al-Israa:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَنِ اهْتَدَى فَإِنَّمَا يَهْتَدِي لِنَفْسِهِ وَمَنْ ضَلَّ فَإِنَّمَا يَضِلُّ عَلَيْهَا وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرٰی وَمَا كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتّٰی نَبْعَثَ رَسُولًا mani ih'tadā fa-innamā yahtadī linafsihi waman ḍalla fa-innamā yaḍillu ʿalayhā walā taziru wāziratun wiz'ra ukh'rā wamā kunnā muʿadhibīna ḥattā nabʿatha rasūlan Whoever is guided is guided only for [the good of] his own soul, and whoever goes astray, goes astray only to its detriment. No bearer shall bear another's burden. We do not punish [any community] until We have sent [it] an apostle.

item.title: Al-Israa:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَنِ اهْتَدَى فَإِنَّمَا يَهْتَدِي لِنَفْسِهِ وَمَنْ ضَلَّ فَإِنَّمَا يَضِلُّ عَلَيْهَا وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرٰی وَمَا كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتّٰی نَبْعَثَ رَسُولًا mani ih'tadā fa-innamā yahtadī linafsihi waman ḍalla fa-innamā yaḍillu ʿalayhā walā taziru wāziratun wiz'ra ukh'rā wamā kunnā muʿadhibīna ḥattā nabʿatha rasūlan Whoever is guided is only guided for (the benefit of) his soul. And whoever errs only errs against it. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And never would We punish until We sent a messenger. Whoever goes right, then he goes right only for the benefit of himself. And whoever goes astray, then he goes astray at his own loss. No one laden with burdens can bear another's burden. And We never punish until We have sent a Messenger (to give warning) (17:15). No One will have to Bear the Sins of Another…

item.title: Al-Israa:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَنِ اهْتَدَى فَإِنَّمَا يَهْتَدِي لِنَفْسِهِ وَمَنْ ضَلَّ فَإِنَّمَا يَضِلُّ عَلَيْهَا وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرٰی وَمَا كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتّٰی نَبْعَثَ رَسُولًا mani ih'tadā fa-innamā yahtadī linafsihi waman ḍalla fa-innamā yaḍillu ʿalayhā walā taziru wāziratun wiz'ra ukh'rā wamā kunnā muʿadhibīna ḥattā nabʿatha rasūlan Whosoever getteth guided aright, verily he getteth guided aright for his ownself; and he who goeth astray, verily he goeth astray against his ownself; nor shall the bearer of a burden bear the burden of another; And We chastise not (any people) until We raise an apostle (among them) See 17:14

item.title: Al-Israa:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا أَرَدْنَا أَنْ نُهْلِكَ قَرْيَةً أَمَرْنَا مُتْرَفِيهَا فَفَسَقُوْۤا فِيهَا فَحَقَّ عَلَيْهَا الْقَوْلُ فَدَمَّرْنَاهَا تَدْمِيرًا wa-idhā aradnā an nuh'lika qaryatan amarnā mut'rafīhā fafasaqū fīhā faḥaqqa ʿalayhā l-qawlu fadammarnāhā tadmīran And when We desire to destroy a town We command its affluent ones [to obey Allah]. But they commit transgression in it, and so the word becomes due against it, and We destroy it utterly.

item.title: Al-Israa:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا أَرَدْنَا أَنْ نُهْلِكَ قَرْيَةً أَمَرْنَا مُتْرَفِيهَا فَفَسَقُوْۤا فِيهَا فَحَقَّ عَلَيْهَا الْقَوْلُ فَدَمَّرْنَاهَا تَدْمِيرًا wa-idhā aradnā an nuh'lika qaryatan amarnā mut'rafīhā fafasaqū fīhā faḥaqqa ʿalayhā l-qawlu fadammarnāhā tadmīran And when We intend to destroy a city, We command its affluent1 but they defiantly disobey therein; so the word (i.e., deserved decree) comes into effect upon it, and We destroy it with (complete) destruction. And when We decide to destroy a town (population), Amarna those who live luxuriously. Then, they transgress therein, and thus the word (of torment) is justified against it (them). Then We destroy it with complete destruction (17:16). Meanings of Amarna The commentators differed over the meaning of this word. It was said that the phrase translated here as "Amarna those who live luxuriously. Then, they transgress therein" means, "We send Our decree upon them" as Allah says…

item.title: Al-Israa:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا أَرَدْنَا أَنْ نُهْلِكَ قَرْيَةً أَمَرْنَا مُتْرَفِيهَا فَفَسَقُوْۤا فِيهَا فَحَقَّ عَلَيْهَا الْقَوْلُ فَدَمَّرْنَاهَا تَدْمِيرًا wa-idhā aradnā an nuh'lika qaryatan amarnā mut'rafīhā fafasaqū fīhā faḥaqqa ʿalayhā l-qawlu fadammarnāhā tadmīran And when intend We to destroy a town, (first) send We Our commandment to its people who lead easy lives (to obey Us), and yet (when) they transgress (Disobey the Commands. Refer to verse 18:50.) in it, then proveth true against it, the (Then the decree of punishment is passed.) word so We destroy it to a complete destruction. See 17:14

item.title: Al-Israa:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِنَ الْقُرُونِ مِنْ بَعْدِ نُوحٍ وَكَفَى بِرَبِّكَ بِذُنُوبِ عِبَادِهِ خَبِيرًا بَصِيرًا wakam ahlaknā mina l-qurūni min baʿdi nūḥin wakafā birabbika bidhunūbi ʿibādihi khabīran baṣīran How many generations We have destroyed since Noah! Your Lord suffices as one well aware and percipient of His servants' sins.

item.title: Al-Israa:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِنَ الْقُرُونِ مِنْ بَعْدِ نُوحٍ وَكَفَى بِرَبِّكَ بِذُنُوبِ عِبَادِهِ خَبِيرًا بَصِيرًا wakam ahlaknā mina l-qurūni min baʿdi nūḥin wakafā birabbika bidhunūbi ʿibādihi khabīran baṣīran And how many have We destroyed from the generations after Nuh. And sufficient is your Lord, concerning the sins of His servants, as Aware and Seeing. And how many generations have We destroyed after Nuh! And sufficient is your Lord as All-Knower and Seer of the sins of His servants (17:17). A Threat to Quraysh Warning the disbelievers of the Quraysh for rejecting His Messenger Muhammad SAW, Allah says that He destroyed other nations who rejected the Messengers after Nuh. This indicates that during the centuries between Adam and Nuh, humans were following Islam, as Ibn 'Abbas said: "Between Adam and Nuh there were ten generations, during all of which humans were following Islam."…

item.title: Al-Israa:17 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِنَ الْقُرُونِ مِنْ بَعْدِ نُوحٍ وَكَفَى بِرَبِّكَ بِذُنُوبِ عِبَادِهِ خَبِيرًا بَصِيرًا wakam ahlaknā mina l-qurūni min baʿdi nūḥin wakafā birabbika bidhunūbi ʿibādihi khabīran baṣīran And how many have We destroyed of the peoples after Noah! and thy Lord is (Himself) sufficient (Sufficient Knower and Seer of the Sins, the hidden and manifest alike.) with regard to the sins of his servants, (for He is) the All-Aware, (Sufficient Knower and Seer of the Sins, the hidden and manifest alike.) the All-Seeing (Sufficient Knower and Seer of the Sins, the hidden and manifest alike.) . See 17:14

item.title: Al-Israa:18 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَنْ كَانَ يُرِيدُ الْعَاجِلَةَ عَجَّلْنَا لَهُ فِيهَا مَا نَشَاءُ لِمَنْ نُرِيدُ ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَا لَهُ جَهَنَّمَ يَصْلَاهَا مَذْمُومًا مَدْحُورًا man kāna yurīdu l-ʿājilata ʿajjalnā lahu fīhā mā nashāu liman nurīdu thumma jaʿalnā lahu jahannama yaṣlāhā madhmūman madḥūran Whoever desires this transitory life, We expedite for him therein whatever We wish, for whomever We desire. Then We appoint hell for him, to enter it, blameful and spurned.

item.title: Al-Israa:18 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَنْ كَانَ يُرِيدُ الْعَاجِلَةَ عَجَّلْنَا لَهُ فِيهَا مَا نَشَاءُ لِمَنْ نُرِيدُ ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَا لَهُ جَهَنَّمَ يَصْلَاهَا مَذْمُومًا مَدْحُورًا man kāna yurīdu l-ʿājilata ʿajjalnā lahu fīhā mā nashāu liman nurīdu thumma jaʿalnā lahu jahannama yaṣlāhā madhmūman madḥūran Whoever should desire the immediate1 - We hasten for him from it what We will to whom We intend. Then We have made for him Hell, which he will (enter to) burn, censured and banished. Whoever desires the quick-passing (transitory enjoyment of this world), We readily grant him what We will for whom We like. Then, afterwards, We have appointed for him Hell; he will burn therein disgraced and rejected (17:18). And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it, with the necessary effort due for it while he is a believer, then such are the ones whose striving shall be appreciated, (rewarded by…

item.title: Al-Israa:18 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَنْ كَانَ يُرِيدُ الْعَاجِلَةَ عَجَّلْنَا لَهُ فِيهَا مَا نَشَاءُ لِمَنْ نُرِيدُ ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَا لَهُ جَهَنَّمَ يَصْلَاهَا مَذْمُومًا مَدْحُورًا man kāna yurīdu l-ʿājilata ʿajjalnā lahu fīhā mā nashāu liman nurīdu thumma jaʿalnā lahu jahannama yaṣlāhā madhmūman madḥūran Whosoever intendeth this (fast hastening) immediate (life) We hasten unto him in it what We please for whomsoever We intend, then assign We unto him the hell; he shall enter it despised, driven away. See 17:14

item.title: Al-Israa:19 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَنْ أَرَادَ الْاٰخِرَةَ وَسَعَى لَهَا سَعْيَهَا وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَأُولَئِكَ كَانَ سَعْيُهُمْ مَشْكُورًا waman arāda l-ākhirata wasaʿā lahā saʿyahā wahuwa mu'minun fa-ulāika kāna saʿyuhum mashkūran Whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it with an endeavour worthy of it, should he be faithful —the endeavour of such will be well-appreciated.

item.title: Al-Israa:19 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَنْ أَرَادَ الْاٰخِرَةَ وَسَعَى لَهَا سَعْيَهَا وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَأُولَئِكَ كَانَ سَعْيُهُمْ مَشْكُورًا waman arāda l-ākhirata wasaʿā lahā saʿyahā wahuwa mu'minun fa-ulāika kāna saʿyuhum mashkūran But whoever desires the Hereafter and exerts the effort due to it while he is a believer - it is those whose effort is ever appreciated (by Allah). See 17:18

item.title: Al-Israa:19 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَنْ أَرَادَ الْاٰخِرَةَ وَسَعَى لَهَا سَعْيَهَا وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَأُولَئِكَ كَانَ سَعْيُهُمْ مَشْكُورًا waman arāda l-ākhirata wasaʿā lahā saʿyahā wahuwa mu'minun fa-ulāika kāna saʿyuhum mashkūran And whosoever intendeth the hereafter and striveth for it a (sincere) striving and he is a believer, these, their striving shall be (recompensed fully) appreciated. See 17:14

item.title: Al-Israa:20 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: كُلًّا نُمِدُّ هَؤُلَاءِ وَهَؤُلَاءِ مِنْ عَطَاءِ رَبِّكَ وَمَا كَانَ عَطَاءُ رَبِّكَ مَحْظُورًا kullan numiddu hāulāi wahāulāi min ʿaṭāi rabbika wamā kāna ʿaṭāu rabbika maḥẓūran To these and to those—to all We extend the bounty of your Lord, and the bounty of your Lord is not confined.

item.title: Al-Israa:20 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: كُلًّا نُمِدُّ هَؤُلَاءِ وَهَؤُلَاءِ مِنْ عَطَاءِ رَبِّكَ وَمَا كَانَ عَطَاءُ رَبِّكَ مَحْظُورًا kullan numiddu hāulāi wahāulāi min ʿaṭāi rabbika wamā kāna ʿaṭāu rabbika maḥẓūran To each (category) We extend - to these and to those - from the gift of your Lord. And never has the gift of your Lord been restricted. On each these as well as those We bestow from the bounties of your Lord. And the bounties of your Lord can never be forbidden (17:20). See how We prefer one above another (in this world), and verily, the Hereafter will be greater in degrees and greater in preferment.) Allah say (17:21). كُلًّا On each meaning, on each of the two groups, those who desire this world and those who desire the Hereafter, We bestow what they want: مِنْ عَطَاءِ رَبِّكَ from the bounties of your Lord. means,…

item.title: Al-Israa:20 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: كُلًّا نُمِدُّ هَؤُلَاءِ وَهَؤُلَاءِ مِنْ عَطَاءِ رَبِّكَ وَمَا كَانَ عَطَاءُ رَبِّكَ مَحْظُورًا kullan numiddu hāulāi wahāulāi min ʿaṭāi rabbika wamā kāna ʿaṭāu rabbika maḥẓūran All We do aid, these and (also) those out of the bounty of thy Lord; and the bounty of thy Lord is not confined. See 17:14

item.title: Al-Israa:21 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اُنْظُرْ كَيْفَ فَضَّلْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ وَلَلْءَاخِرَةُ أَكْبَرُ دَرَجَاتٍ وَأَكْبَرُ تَفْضِيلًا unẓur kayfa faḍḍalnā baʿḍahum ʿalā baʿḍin walalākhiratu akbaru darajātin wa-akbaru tafḍīlan Observe how We have given some of them an advantage over some others; yet the Hereafter is surely greater in respect of ranks and greater in respect of relative merit.1

item.title: Al-Israa:21 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اُنْظُرْ كَيْفَ فَضَّلْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ وَلَلْءَاخِرَةُ أَكْبَرُ دَرَجَاتٍ وَأَكْبَرُ تَفْضِيلًا unẓur kayfa faḍḍalnā baʿḍahum ʿalā baʿḍin walalākhiratu akbaru darajātin wa-akbaru tafḍīlan Look how We have favored (in provision) some of them over others. But the Hereafter is greater in degrees (of difference) and greater in distinction. See 17:20

item.title: Al-Israa:21 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اُنْظُرْ كَيْفَ فَضَّلْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ وَلَلْءَاخِرَةُ أَكْبَرُ دَرَجَاتٍ وَأَكْبَرُ تَفْضِيلًا unẓur kayfa faḍḍalnā baʿḍahum ʿalā baʿḍin walalākhiratu akbaru darajātin wa-akbaru tafḍīlan Behold (thou) how We caused some of them excel the others; and surely the hereafter is much greater in respect of degrees and greater still in respect of excellence. See 17:14

item.title: Al-Israa:22 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا تَجْعَلْ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَهًا ءَاخَرَ فَتَقْعُدَ مَذْمُومًا مَخْذُولًا lā tajʿal maʿa l-lahi ilāhan ākhara fataqʿuda madhmūman makhdhūlan Do not set up another god besides Allah, or you will sit blameworthy, forsaken.

item.title: Al-Israa:22 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا تَجْعَلْ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَهًا ءَاخَرَ فَتَقْعُدَ مَذْمُومًا مَخْذُولًا lā tajʿal maʿa l-lahi ilāhan ākhara fataqʿuda madhmūman makhdhūlan Do not make (as equal) with Allah another deity and (thereby) become censured and forsaken. Set not up with Allah any other ilah (god), or you will sit down reproved, forsaken (in the Hellfire) (17:22). Do Not Associate Anything in Worship with Allah Addressing those who are responsible among this Ummah, Allah says, "Do not admit any partner into your worship of your Lord." فَتَقْعُدَ مَذْمُومًا or you will sit down reproved, Meaning: because of associating others with Him. مَّخْذُولًا forsaken. means, because the Lord, may He be exalted, will not help you; He will leave you to the one whom you worshipped, and he has no power either to benefit or to harm, because the Only One Who has the power…

item.title: Al-Israa:22 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا تَجْعَلْ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَهًا ءَاخَرَ فَتَقْعُدَ مَذْمُومًا مَخْذُولًا lā tajʿal maʿa l-lahi ilāhan ākhara fataqʿuda madhmūman makhdhūlan Associate not with God any other gods, lest thou sittest despised, neglected. See 17:14

item.title: Al-Israa:23 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَضَى رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوْۤا إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِنْدَكَ الْكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَا أَوْ كِلَاهُمَا فَلَا تَقُلْ لَهُمَا أُفٍّ وَلَا تَنْهَرْهُمَا وَقُلْ لَهُمَا قَوْلًا كَرِيمًا waqaḍā rabbuka allā taʿbudū illā iyyāhu wabil-wālidayni iḥ'sānan immā yablughanna ʿindaka l-kibara aḥaduhumā aw kilāhumā falā taqul lahumā uffin walā tanharhumā waqul lahumā qawlan karīman Your Lord has decreed that you shall not worship anyone except Him, and [He has enjoined] kindness to parents. Should they reach old age at your side —one of them or both— do not say to them, 'Fie!'1 And do not chide them, but speak to them noble words.

item.title: Al-Israa:23 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَضَى رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوْۤا إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِنْدَكَ الْكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَا أَوْ كِلَاهُمَا فَلَا تَقُلْ لَهُمَا أُفٍّ وَلَا تَنْهَرْهُمَا وَقُلْ لَهُمَا قَوْلًا كَرِيمًا waqaḍā rabbuka allā taʿbudū illā iyyāhu wabil-wālidayni iḥ'sānan immā yablughanna ʿindaka l-kibara aḥaduhumā aw kilāhumā falā taqul lahumā uffin walā tanharhumā waqul lahumā qawlan karīman And your Lord has decreed that you worship not except Him, and to parents, good treatment. Whether one or both of them reach old age (while) with you, say not to them (so much as), "uff,"1 and do not repel them but speak to them a noble word. And your Lord has Qada (decreed) that you worship none but Him. And that you be dutiful to your parents. If one of them or both of them attain old age in your life, say not to them a word of disrespect,…

item.title: Al-Israa:23 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَضَى رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوْۤا إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِنْدَكَ الْكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَا أَوْ كِلَاهُمَا فَلَا تَقُلْ لَهُمَا أُفٍّ وَلَا تَنْهَرْهُمَا وَقُلْ لَهُمَا قَوْلًا كَرِيمًا waqaḍā rabbuka allā taʿbudū illā iyyāhu wabil-wālidayni iḥ'sānan immā yablughanna ʿindaka l-kibara aḥaduhumā aw kilāhumā falā taqul lahumā uffin walā tanharhumā waqul lahumā qawlan karīman And commanded thy Lord hath that thou shalt worship not (any one) but Him, and goodness to parents; if either or both of them reach old age with thee, utter not unto them (even so much as) "Fie" nor chide them, and speak unto them a generous word. Note the rank Islam has given to obedience to parents, which is next only to God. The extent to which one has to regard his parents and obey them is peculiar only to Islam. None should even raise his voice higher than…

item.title: Al-Israa:24 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاخْفِضْ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ الذُّلِّ مِنَ الرَّحْمَةِ وَقُلْ رَبِّ ارْحَمْهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِي صَغِيرًا wa-ikh'fiḍ lahumā janāḥa l-dhuli mina l-raḥmati waqul rabbi ir'ḥamhumā kamā rabbayānī ṣaghīran Lower the wing of humility to them, out of mercy, and say, 'My Lord! Have mercy on them, just as they reared me when I was [a] small [child]!'

item.title: Al-Israa:24 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاخْفِضْ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ الذُّلِّ مِنَ الرَّحْمَةِ وَقُلْ رَبِّ ارْحَمْهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِي صَغِيرًا wa-ikh'fiḍ lahumā janāḥa l-dhuli mina l-raḥmati waqul rabbi ir'ḥamhumā kamā rabbayānī ṣaghīran And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy and say, "My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up (when I was) small." See 17:23

item.title: Al-Israa:24 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاخْفِضْ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ الذُّلِّ مِنَ الرَّحْمَةِ وَقُلْ رَبِّ ارْحَمْهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِي صَغِيرًا wa-ikh'fiḍ lahumā janāḥa l-dhuli mina l-raḥmati waqul rabbi ir'ḥamhumā kamā rabbayānī ṣaghīran And lower unto them the wing of humility out of compassion, and say (Praying to God.) thou: "O' My Lord! Have mercy on them as they cherished me when I was little." See 17:23

item.title: Al-Israa:25 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: رَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا فِي نُفُوسِكُمْ إِنْ تَكُونُوْۤا صَالِحِينَ فَإِنَّهُ كَانَ لِلْأَوَّابِينَ غَفُورًا rabbukum aʿlamu bimā fī nufūsikum in takūnū ṣāliḥīna fa-innahu kāna lil'awwābīna ghafūran Your Lord knows best what is in your hearts. Should you be righteous, He is indeed most forgiving toward penitents.

item.title: Al-Israa:25 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: رَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا فِي نُفُوسِكُمْ إِنْ تَكُونُوْۤا صَالِحِينَ فَإِنَّهُ كَانَ لِلْأَوَّابِينَ غَفُورًا rabbukum aʿlamu bimā fī nufūsikum in takūnū ṣāliḥīna fa-innahu kāna lil'awwābīna ghafūran Your Lord is most knowing of what is within yourselves. If you should be righteous (in intention) - then indeed He is ever, to the often returning (to Him), Forgiving.1 Your Lord knows best what is in your souls. If you are righteous, then, verily, He is Ever Most Forgiving to those who turn to Him in repentance (17:25). Omissions Comitted against Parents are Pardoned with Good Relations and Repentance Sa'id bin Jubayr said: "This refers to a man who said something that he did not think would be offensive to his parents." According to another report: "He did not mean anything bad by that." So Allah said: رَّبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا فِي نُفُوسِكُمْ ۚ إِن تَكُونُوا…

item.title: Al-Israa:25 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: رَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا فِي نُفُوسِكُمْ إِنْ تَكُونُوْۤا صَالِحِينَ فَإِنَّهُ كَانَ لِلْأَوَّابِينَ غَفُورًا rabbukum aʿlamu bimā fī nufūsikum in takūnū ṣāliḥīna fa-innahu kāna lil'awwābīna ghafūran Your Lord knoweth best what is in yourselves (Your hearts.) ; if ye be righteous, then verily He is for the repentants Oft-Forgiving. See 17:23

item.title: Al-Israa:26 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَءَاتِ ذَا الْقُرْبٰی حَقَّهُ وَالْمِسْكِينَ وَابْنَ السَّبِيلِ وَلَا تُبَذِّرْ تَبْذِيرًا waāti dhā l-qur'bā ḥaqqahu wal-mis'kīna wa-ib'na l-sabīli walā tubadhir tabdhīran Give the relatives their [due] right, and the needy and the traveller [as well], but do not squander wastefully.

item.title: Al-Israa:26 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَءَاتِ ذَا الْقُرْبٰی حَقَّهُ وَالْمِسْكِينَ وَابْنَ السَّبِيلِ وَلَا تُبَذِّرْ تَبْذِيرًا waāti dhā l-qur'bā ḥaqqahu wal-mis'kīna wa-ib'na l-sabīli walā tubadhir tabdhīran And give the relative his right, and (also) the poor and the traveler, and do not spend wastefully.1 And give to the kinsman his due, and to the Miskin (poor), and to the wayfarer. But spend not wastefully (your wealth) in the manner of a spendthrift (17:26). Verily, the spendthrifts are brothers of the Shayatin (devils), and the Shaytan is ever ungrateful to his Lord (17:27). And if you turn away from them and you are awaiting a mercy from your Lord for which you hope, then, speak unto them a soft, kind word (17:28). The Command to Maintain the Ties of Kinship and the Prohibition of Extravagance When Allah mentions honoring one's parents, He follows this with the command…

item.title: Al-Israa:26 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَءَاتِ ذَا الْقُرْبٰی حَقَّهُ وَالْمِسْكِينَ وَابْنَ السَّبِيلِ وَلَا تُبَذِّرْ تَبْذِيرًا waāti dhā l-qur'bā ḥaqqahu wal-mis'kīna wa-ib'na l-sabīli walā tubadhir tabdhīran And give to the near of kin his due and to the needy and the wayfarer, and squander not (thy earnings) wastefully. See verses 8:41, 16:90, 17:26, 30:38, 59:7. Ibn Jarir reports that the Fourth Holy Imam Ali Ibn Husayn al-Zain al-Abidin asked a Syrian, "Hast thou read in the Chapter Bani-Israel in the Holy Qur'an. Give the near of kin his due?" He said, 'Yes'. Then the Holy Imam said: "We are the near of kin meant by the verse." Bazaz Abu Ya'la, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh relate on the authority of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that immediately as this verse was revealed the Holy Prophet called his daughter Fatimah and gifted the garden of Fadak. (D.M., M.F.A.).…

item.title: Al-Israa:27 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الْمُبَذِّرِينَ كَانُوْۤا إِخْوَانَ الشَّيَاطِينِ وَكَانَ الشَّيْطَانُ لِرَبِّهِ كَفُورًا inna l-mubadhirīna kānū ikh'wāna l-shayāṭīni wakāna l-shayṭānu lirabbihi kafūran Indeed the wasteful are brothers of satans, and Satan is ungrateful to his Lord.

item.title: Al-Israa:27 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الْمُبَذِّرِينَ كَانُوْۤا إِخْوَانَ الشَّيَاطِينِ وَكَانَ الشَّيْطَانُ لِرَبِّهِ كَفُورًا inna l-mubadhirīna kānū ikh'wāna l-shayāṭīni wakāna l-shayṭānu lirabbihi kafūran Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils, and ever has Satan been to his Lord ungrateful. See 17:26

item.title: Al-Israa:27 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الْمُبَذِّرِينَ كَانُوْۤا إِخْوَانَ الشَّيَاطِينِ وَكَانَ الشَّيْطَانُ لِرَبِّهِ كَفُورًا inna l-mubadhirīna kānū ikh'wāna l-shayāṭīni wakāna l-shayṭānu lirabbihi kafūran Verily the squanderers are the brethren of the satans; and Satan to his Lord is ever an ingrate. See 17:26

item.title: Al-Israa:28 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِمَّا تُعْرِضَنَّ عَنْهُمُ ابْتِغَاءَ رَحْمَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكَ تَرْجُوهَا فَقُلْ لَهُمْ قَوْلًا مَيْسُورًا wa-immā tuʿ'riḍanna ʿanhumu ib'tighāa raḥmatin min rabbika tarjūhā faqul lahum qawlan maysūran And if you have to overlook them [for now], seeking the mercy of your Lord which you expect [in the future], speak to them gentle words.

item.title: Al-Israa:28 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِمَّا تُعْرِضَنَّ عَنْهُمُ ابْتِغَاءَ رَحْمَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكَ تَرْجُوهَا فَقُلْ لَهُمْ قَوْلًا مَيْسُورًا wa-immā tuʿ'riḍanna ʿanhumu ib'tighāa raḥmatin min rabbika tarjūhā faqul lahum qawlan maysūran And if you (must) turn away from them (i.e., the needy) awaiting mercy from your Lord which you expect,1 then speak to them a gentle word. See 17:26

item.title: Al-Israa:28 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِمَّا تُعْرِضَنَّ عَنْهُمُ ابْتِغَاءَ رَحْمَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكَ تَرْجُوهَا فَقُلْ لَهُمْ قَوْلًا مَيْسُورًا wa-immā tuʿ'riḍanna ʿanhumu ib'tighāa raḥmatin min rabbika tarjūhā faqul lahum qawlan maysūran If thou (helplessly) turn away from them (The kindred, the needy, the wayfarers.) seeking mercy from thy Lord which thou hopest for, then speak unto them (The kindred, the needy, the wayfarers.) (at- least) a kindly (Gentle - a word of ease.) word. See 17:26

item.title: Al-Israa:29 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إِلَى عُنُقِكَ وَلَا تَبْسُطْهَا كُلَّ الْبَسْطِ فَتَقْعُدَ مَلُومًا مَحْسُورًا walā tajʿal yadaka maghlūlatan ilā ʿunuqika walā tabsuṭ'hā kulla l-basṭi fataqʿuda malūman maḥsūran Do not keep your hand chained to your neck, nor open it altogether,1 or you will sit blameworthy, regretful.

item.title: Al-Israa:29 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إِلَى عُنُقِكَ وَلَا تَبْسُطْهَا كُلَّ الْبَسْطِ فَتَقْعُدَ مَلُومًا مَحْسُورًا walā tajʿal yadaka maghlūlatan ilā ʿunuqika walā tabsuṭ'hā kulla l-basṭi fataqʿuda malūman maḥsūran And do not make your hand (as) chained to your neck1 or extend it completely2 and (thereby) become blamed and insolvent. And let not your hand be tied (like a miser) to your neck, nor overextend it (like a spendthrift), so that you become blameworthy and in severe poverty (17:29). Truly, your Lord expands the provision for whom He wills and straitens (for whom He wills). Verily, He is Ever All-Knower, All-Seer of His servants (17:30). Moderation in Spending Allah enjoins moderation in living. He condemns miserliness and forbids extravagance. وَلَا تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إِلَىٰ عُنُقِكَ And let not your hand be tied (like a miser) to your neck, this means, do not be…

item.title: Al-Israa:29 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إِلَى عُنُقِكَ وَلَا تَبْسُطْهَا كُلَّ الْبَسْطِ فَتَقْعُدَ مَلُومًا مَحْسُورًا walā tajʿal yadaka maghlūlatan ilā ʿunuqika walā tabsuṭ'hā kulla l-basṭi fataqʿuda malūman maḥsūran And cause thou not to shackle thy hand unto thy neck, nor stretch it forth to the maximum (limits of) stretching forth, lest thou shouldst (thereafter) sit down blamed, destituted. Neither be niggardly nor be wasting but be moderate in even charity, neither abstain from giving any thing at all to any one, nor give away everything and put thyself in need and misery.

item.title: Al-Israa:30 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ إِنَّهُ كَانَ بِعِبَادِهِ خَبِيرًا بَصِيرًا inna rabbaka yabsuṭu l-riz'qa liman yashāu wayaqdiru innahu kāna biʿibādihi khabīran baṣīran Indeed your Lord expands the provision for whomever He wishes, and tightens it. Indeed He is well aware and percipient of His servants.

item.title: Al-Israa:30 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ إِنَّهُ كَانَ بِعِبَادِهِ خَبِيرًا بَصِيرًا inna rabbaka yabsuṭu l-riz'qa liman yashāu wayaqdiru innahu kāna biʿibādihi khabīran baṣīran Indeed, your Lord extends provision for whom He wills and restricts (it). Indeed He is ever, concerning His servants, Aware and Seeing. See 17:29

item.title: Al-Israa:30 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ إِنَّهُ كَانَ بِعِبَادِهِ خَبِيرًا بَصِيرًا inna rabbaka yabsuṭu l-riz'qa liman yashāu wayaqdiru innahu kāna biʿibādihi khabīran baṣīran Verily thy Lord extendeth (Maketh plenty.) the sustenance for whomsoever He willeth and measureth (Restricteth.) it He (to a just measure); Verily He is, of His servants ever Fully- Aware, All-Seeing. See 17:29

item.title: Al-Israa:31 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا تَقْتُلُوْۤا أَوْلَادَكُمْ خَشْيَةَ إِمْلَاقٍ نَحْنُ نَرْزُقُهُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ إِنَّ قَتْلَهُمْ كَانَ خِطْءًا كَبِيرًا walā taqtulū awlādakum khashyata im'lāqin naḥnu narzuquhum wa-iyyākum inna qatlahum kāna khiṭ'an kabīran Do not kill your children for the fear of penury: We will provide for them and for you. Killing them is indeed a great iniquity.

item.title: Al-Israa:31 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا تَقْتُلُوْۤا أَوْلَادَكُمْ خَشْيَةَ إِمْلَاقٍ نَحْنُ نَرْزُقُهُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ إِنَّ قَتْلَهُمْ كَانَ خِطْءًا كَبِيرًا walā taqtulū awlādakum khashyata im'lāqin naḥnu narzuquhum wa-iyyākum inna qatlahum kāna khiṭ'an kabīran And do not kill your children for fear of poverty. We provide for them and for you. Indeed, their killing is ever a great sin. And kill not your children for fear of poverty. We shall provide for them as well as for you. Surely, the killing of them is a great sin (17:31). Prohibition of Killing Children This Ayah indicates that Allah is more compassionate towards His servants than a father to his child, because He forbids killing children just as He enjoins parents to take care of their children in matters of inheritance. The people of Jahiliyyah would not allow their daughters to inherit from them, and some would even kill their…

item.title: Al-Israa:31 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا تَقْتُلُوْۤا أَوْلَادَكُمْ خَشْيَةَ إِمْلَاقٍ نَحْنُ نَرْزُقُهُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ إِنَّ قَتْلَهُمْ كَانَ خِطْءًا كَبِيرًا walā taqtulū awlādakum khashyata im'lāqin naḥnu narzuquhum wa-iyyākum inna qatlahum kāna khiṭ'an kabīran And kill ye not your children for fear of want; (Compare this to the modern un-natural Family Planning.) We sustain them and yourselves (too); Verily killing them is a great sin. The people used to kill their children. Particularly a female issue was considered to be a disgraceful encumbrance to the parents. People feared their inability to provide themselves with the necessary subsistence. This admonition was required not only in the days of the ignorance of the Arabs but even today its need is more than it had ever been, for the tendency to decrease the birth-rate by all unnatural devices of birth-control is ever on the increase under the modern civilization with highly…

item.title: Al-Israa:32 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا تَقْرَبُوْۤا الزِّنَى إِنَّهُ كَانَ فَاحِشَةً وَسَاءَ سَبِيلًا walā taqrabū l-zinā innahu kāna fāḥishatan wasāa sabīlan Do not approach fornication. It is indeed an indecency and an evil way.

item.title: Al-Israa:32 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا تَقْرَبُوْۤا الزِّنَى إِنَّهُ كَانَ فَاحِشَةً وَسَاءَ سَبِيلًا walā taqrabū l-zinā innahu kāna fāḥishatan wasāa sabīlan And do not approach unlawful sexual intercourse.1 Indeed, it is ever an immorality and is evil as a way. And come not near to unlawful sex. Verily, it is Fahishah (immoral sin) and an evil way (17:32). The Command to Avoid Zina (Unlawful Sex) and Everything that Leads to it Allah says, forbidding His servants to commit Zina or to approach it or to do anything that may lead to it: وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا الزِّنَا ۖ إِنَّهُ كَانَ فَاحِشَةً And come not near to unlawful sex. Verily, it is a Fahishah (immoral sin) meaning a major sin: وَسَاءَ سَبِيلًا and an evil way. Meaning: a terrible way to behave. Imam Ahmad recorded Abu Umamah saying that a young man came to the Prophet SAW and…

item.title: Al-Israa:32 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا تَقْرَبُوْۤا الزِّنَى إِنَّهُ كَانَ فَاحِشَةً وَسَاءَ سَبِيلًا walā taqrabū l-zinā innahu kāna fāḥishatan wasāa sabīlan And approach ye not adultery, (Refer to verse 6:151. Refer to note on verse 17:23.) Verily, it is a shameful act, and an evil way (opening to many other evils) This is an evil which is ever on the increase under the modern civilization. Islam not only forbids adultery but forbids even going near it, i.e., to avoid all opportunities for it, like co-education, clubs, associations of mixed gathering of the sexes, conducting of dances and such demoralising activities as dancing and singing in the name of Social and Benefit Performances etc.

item.title: Al-Israa:33 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا تَقْتُلُوْۤا النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَمَنْ قُتِلَ مَظْلُومًا فَقَدْ جَعَلْنَا لِوَلِيِّهِ سُلْطَانًا فَلَا يُسْرِفْ فِي الْقَتْلِ إِنَّهُ كَانَ مَنْصُورًا walā taqtulū l-nafsa allatī ḥarrama l-lahu illā bil-ḥaqi waman qutila maẓlūman faqad jaʿalnā liwaliyyihi sul'ṭānan falā yus'rif fī l-qatli innahu kāna manṣūran Do not kill a soul [whose life] Allah has made inviolable, except with due cause, and whoever is killed wrongfully, We have certainly given his heir an authority. But let him not commit any excess in killing,1 for he enjoys the support [of law].

item.title: Al-Israa:33 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا تَقْتُلُوْۤا النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَمَنْ قُتِلَ مَظْلُومًا فَقَدْ جَعَلْنَا لِوَلِيِّهِ سُلْطَانًا فَلَا يُسْرِفْ فِي الْقَتْلِ إِنَّهُ كَانَ مَنْصُورًا walā taqtulū l-nafsa allatī ḥarrama l-lahu illā bil-ḥaqi waman qutila maẓlūman faqad jaʿalnā liwaliyyihi sul'ṭānan falā yus'rif fī l-qatli innahu kāna manṣūran And do not kill the soul (i.e., person) which Allah has forbidden, except by right.1 And whoever is killed unjustly - We have given his heir authority,2 but let him not exceed limits in (the matter of) taking life. Indeed, he has been supported (by the law). And do not kill anyone whose killing Allah has forbidden, except for a just cause. And whoever is killed wrongfully (not by mistake), We have given his heir the authority. But let him not exceed limits in the matter of taking life. Verily, he is helped (17:33). Prohibition of…

item.title: Al-Israa:33 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا تَقْتُلُوْۤا النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَمَنْ قُتِلَ مَظْلُومًا فَقَدْ جَعَلْنَا لِوَلِيِّهِ سُلْطَانًا فَلَا يُسْرِفْ فِي الْقَتْلِ إِنَّهُ كَانَ مَنْصُورًا walā taqtulū l-nafsa allatī ḥarrama l-lahu illā bil-ḥaqi waman qutila maẓlūman faqad jaʿalnā liwaliyyihi sul'ṭānan falā yus'rif fī l-qatli innahu kāna manṣūran And kill ye not any one whom God hath forbidden but for a just cause; and whoever is slain unjustly, then indeed have We given his heir the authority, but he shall not be extravagant (Exceed the limits of justice.) in slaying; Verily he is aided (by God). The administrators of the Islamic law should help the heir of the murdered one in bringing the murderer to account for the crime. None, not even the heir should take the law in his own hands nor the punishment should exceed the limits of the crime. When Abdur…

item.title: Al-Israa:34 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا تَقْرَبُوْۤا مَالَ الْيَتِيمِ إِلَّا بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ حَتّٰی يَبْلُغَ أَشُدَّهُ وَأَوْفُوْۤا بِالْعَهْدِ إِنَّ الْعَهْدَ كَانَ مَسْءُولًا walā taqrabū māla l-yatīmi illā bi-allatī hiya aḥsanu ḥattā yablugha ashuddahu wa-awfū bil-ʿahdi inna l-ʿahda kāna masūlan Do not approach the orphan's property except in the best manner until he comes of age.
