item.title: Al-Mutaffifin:30 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا مَرُّوْۤا بِهِمْ يَتَغَامَزُونَ wa-idhā marrū bihim yataghāmazūna And when they passed by them, they would exchange derisive glances. See 83:29

item.title: Al-Mutaffifin:30 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا مَرُّوْۤا بِهِمْ يَتَغَامَزُونَ wa-idhā marrū bihim yataghāmazūna And when they pass by them, wink (While in the world.) they at one another See 83:29

item.title: Al-Mutaffifin:31 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا انْقَلَبُوا إِلَى أَهْلِهِمُ انْقَلَبُوا فَكِهِينَ wa-idhā inqalabū ilā ahlihimu inqalabū fakihīna and when they returned to their folks they would return rejoicing,

item.title: Al-Mutaffifin:31 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا انْقَلَبُوا إِلَى أَهْلِهِمُ انْقَلَبُوا فَكِهِينَ wa-idhā inqalabū ilā ahlihimu inqalabū fakihīna And when they returned to their people, they would return jesting. See 83:29

item.title: Al-Mutaffifin:31 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا انْقَلَبُوا إِلَى أَهْلِهِمُ انْقَلَبُوا فَكِهِينَ wa-idhā inqalabū ilā ahlihimu inqalabū fakihīna And when return they unto their people, return they jesting See 83:29

item.title: Al-Mutaffifin:32 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا رَأَوْهُمْ قَالُوْا إِنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ لَضَالُّونَ wa-idhā ra-awhum qālū inna hāulāi laḍāllūna and when they saw them they would say, 'Indeed those are the astray!'

item.title: Al-Mutaffifin:32 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا رَأَوْهُمْ قَالُوْا إِنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ لَضَالُّونَ wa-idhā ra-awhum qālū inna hāulāi laḍāllūna And when they saw them, they would say, "Indeed, those are truly lost." See 83:29

item.title: Al-Mutaffifin:32 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذَا رَأَوْهُمْ قَالُوْا إِنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ لَضَالُّونَ wa-idhā ra-awhum qālū inna hāulāi laḍāllūna And when they see them, say (While in the world.) they: ''Verily these are the straying ones" See 83:29

item.title: Al-Mutaffifin:33 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أُرْسِلُوْۤا عَلَيْهِمْ حَافِظِينَ wamā ur'silū ʿalayhim ḥāfiẓīna Though they were not sent to watch over them.

item.title: Al-Mutaffifin:33 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أُرْسِلُوْۤا عَلَيْهِمْ حَافِظِينَ wamā ur'silū ʿalayhim ḥāfiẓīna But they had not been sent as guardians over them. See 83:29

item.title: Al-Mutaffifin:33 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أُرْسِلُوْۤا عَلَيْهِمْ حَافِظِينَ wamā ur'silū ʿalayhim ḥāfiẓīna While they are sent not over them to be the watchers The reference is to those who mocked at Ali and also those who mocked at the other believers - that they had no business to behave as they did for, they were not posted by God to watch the movements of those righteous ones.

item.title: Al-Mutaffifin:34 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَالْيَوْمَ الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ يَضْحَكُونَ fal-yawma alladhīna āmanū mina l-kufāri yaḍḥakūna So today the faithful will laugh at the faithless,

item.title: Al-Mutaffifin:34 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَالْيَوْمَ الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ يَضْحَكُونَ fal-yawma alladhīna āmanū mina l-kufāri yaḍḥakūna So Today1 those who believed are laughing at the disbelievers. See 83:29

item.title: Al-Mutaffifin:34 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَالْيَوْمَ الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ يَضْحَكُونَ fal-yawma alladhīna āmanū mina l-kufāri yaḍḥakūna So, today, those who believe shall be at the disbelievers laugh Those who mocked at the righteous ones among the believers - will be made to be mocked at on the Day of Judgment by the believers.

item.title: Al-Mutaffifin:35 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ يَنْظُرُونَ ʿalā l-arāiki yanẓurūna observing from couches:

item.title: Al-Mutaffifin:35 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ يَنْظُرُونَ ʿalā l-arāiki yanẓurūna On adorned couches, observing. See 83:29

item.title: Al-Mutaffifin:35 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ يَنْظُرُونَ ʿalā l-arāiki yanẓurūna On couches (exalted they shall be) seeing (the delightful sights) The righteous ones or believers will be seen on exalted position enjoying the bliss in heaven seated on the exalted thrones of dignity and excellence.

item.title: Al-Mutaffifin:36 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: هَلْ ثُوِّبَ الْكُفَّارُ مَا كَانُوْۤا يَفْعَلُونَ hal thuwwiba l-kufāru mā kānū yafʿalūna Have the faithless been requited for what they used to do?

item.title: Al-Mutaffifin:36 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: هَلْ ثُوِّبَ الْكُفَّارُ مَا كَانُوْۤا يَفْعَلُونَ hal thuwwiba l-kufāru mā kānū yafʿalūna Have the disbelievers (not) been rewarded (this Day) for what they used to do? See 83:29

item.title: Al-Mutaffifin:36 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: هَلْ ثُوِّبَ الْكُفَّارُ مَا كَانُوْۤا يَفْعَلُونَ hal thuwwiba l-kufāru mā kānū yafʿalūna Shall not the disbelievers be (also) recompensed for what they used to do? The evil return for the conduct of the disbelievers is sure and certain. The arrogant braggarts will certainly he brought low - a recompense for their own disbelief and wickedness. This is an expression in terms of the feelings of an opponent for the adversity of the other just for the sake of warning the disbelievers, that on the Day of Judgment their position will be such that if the believers would be in a retaliative state they would be justified to laugh at them, but in fact it is far above the believers to enjoy the sufferings of the others. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاأَيُّهَا الْمُزَّمِّلُ yāayyuhā l-muzamilu O you wrapped up in your mantle!

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاأَيُّهَا الْمُزَّمِّلُ yāayyuhā l-muzamilu O you who wraps himself (in clothing).1 رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَاتَّخِذْهُ وَكِيلًا Lord of the east and the west; La ilaha illa Huwa. So take Him a trustee. Meaning: He is the Owner and Controller of affairs in the eastern regions and the western regions. He is the One except whom there is no deity worthy of worship. Just as you single Him out for worship, you should also single Him out for reliance. Therefore, take Him as a guardian and trustee. This is as Allah says in another Ayah: فَاعْبُدْهُ وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَيْهِ So worship Him and rely upon him. (11:123) It is also similar to His statement: إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ You (Alone) we worship, and you (Alone) we ask for help. (1:5) The Ayat with this meaning are numerous. They…

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاأَيُّهَا الْمُزَّمِّلُ yāayyuhā l-muzamilu O' thou the Wrapped (The Holy Prophet Muhanmad.) up in thy mantle! 'The Wrapped up' is the address to the Holy Prophet. In the early days, i.e., in the beginning of his ministry, the Holy Prophet used to pray covering his whole body with a big piece of cloth and when this Verse was revealed he was preparing to start his prayers and was wrapped up. It is said whenever the Holy Prophet got into the state of receiving any revelation, he used to feel a shivering in his body and felt the necessity of getting himself covered with some cloth. God liked His most loved Apostle in the state of being covered that He addressed him as the 'Muzzammil', i.e., the Wrapped up one. 'Muzzammil' is also interpreted as the one burdened or charged with…

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُمِ اللَّيْلَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا qumi al-layla illā qalīlan Stand vigil through the night, except a little,

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُمِ اللَّيْلَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا qumi al-layla illā qalīlan Arise (to pray) the night, except for a little. See 73:1

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُمِ اللَّيْلَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا qumi al-layla illā qalīlan Rise thou in the night to pray (Reference to 'Tahajjud' prayer.) but a little! (and not for the whole night) (Refer to Verse 17:79.) In the beginning, the believers had to offer the midnight 'Tahajjud' prayers. The people did not know the exact hour when they had to pray and hence, they used to keep awake the whole night in prayers. The merciful Lord had to reveal His will that they had to stand in prayers only for a small part of the night and not for the whole of it. This prayer, i.e., 'Tahajjud' is optional with the highest recommendation to offer it to achieve spiritual progress.

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: نِصْفَهُ أَوِ انْقُصْ مِنْهُ قَلِيلًا niṣ'fahu awi unquṣ min'hu qalīlan a half, or reduce a little from that

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: نِصْفَهُ أَوِ انْقُصْ مِنْهُ قَلِيلًا niṣ'fahu awi unquṣ min'hu qalīlan Half of it - or subtract from it a little. See 73:1

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: نِصْفَهُ أَوِ انْقُصْ مِنْهُ قَلِيلًا niṣ'fahu awi unquṣ min'hu qalīlan Half of it or curtail of it a little! See 73:2

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ وَرَتِّلِ الْقُرْآنَ تَرْتِيلًا aw zid ʿalayhi warattili l-qur'āna tartīlan or add to it, and recite the Qur'ān in a measured tone.

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ وَرَتِّلِ الْقُرْآنَ تَرْتِيلًا aw zid ʿalayhi warattili l-qur'āna tartīlan Or add to it, and recite the Qur’ān with measured recitation. See 73:1

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ وَرَتِّلِ الْقُرْآنَ تَرْتِيلًا aw zid ʿalayhi warattili l-qur'āna tartīlan Or add to it, and intone the Qur'an in a regulated tone! The choice to increase the duration of prayer is left to the individuals. The recital of the Holy Qur'an is not to be in a hurry or hasty, just for the purpose of covering the passage. It has to be recited slowly in studious way and the beauty of the Word of God has to be manifested in an attractive tone observing duly the punctuation. This indicates that the Holy Prophet already knew the Qur'an and he was only ordered to recite it in a well-measured way. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا سَنُلْقِي عَلَيْكَ قَوْلًا ثَقِيلًا innā sanul'qī ʿalayka qawlan thaqīlan Indeed soon We shall cast on you a weighty word.

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا سَنُلْقِي عَلَيْكَ قَوْلًا ثَقِيلًا innā sanul'qī ʿalayka qawlan thaqīlan Indeed, We will cast upon you a heavy word.1 See 73:1

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا سَنُلْقِي عَلَيْكَ قَوْلًا ثَقِيلًا innā sanul'qī ʿalayka qawlan thaqīlan Verily soon will We send down upon thee (some) weighty words (Refer to Verses 94:2; 94:3.) The 'Weighty word' is the Holy Qur'an - The Holy Prophet has addressed the Holy Qur'an and his Ahl Al-Bayt as 'Thaqalayn' the two weighty things. (Tafsir al-Kabir, D.M., etc.) Thus the Ahl Al-Bayt and the Holy Qur'an are of equal weight or importance to mankind, the Holy Qur'an being the Word of God and the Ahl Al-Bayt the godly means to understand it duly i. e., The responsibility of guiding mankind which is termed here as weighty words but in 94:2 and 94:3 as a burden for which he required an assistant in the manner that Moses required Aaron to assist him - as hinted in Verse 15. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ اللَّيْلِ هِيَ أَشَدُّ وَطْئًا وَأَقْوَمُ قِيلًا inna nāshi-ata al-layli hiya ashaddu waṭan wa-aqwamu qīlan Indeed the watch of the night is firmer in tread and more upright in respect to speech,

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ اللَّيْلِ هِيَ أَشَدُّ وَطْئًا وَأَقْوَمُ قِيلًا inna nāshi-ata al-layli hiya ashaddu waṭan wa-aqwamu qīlan Indeed, the hours of the night are more effective for concurrence (of heart and tongue)1 and more suitable for words.2 See 73:1

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ اللَّيْلِ هِيَ أَشَدُّ وَطْئًا وَأَقْوَمُ قِيلًا inna nāshi-ata al-layli hiya ashaddu waṭan wa-aqwamu qīlan Verily the rising at night when impression is intense and straightest in words Note how Islam wants man to avail of the best time in the nature of the day and night for concentration, meditation, supplication and for disciplining the soul to get into communion with the All-Divine. Night is the time when the world seeking the material profit in the earth gets practically all still, silent and when there is the cessation of voices of the day time, which distract and even destroy contemplation, concentration and meditation it is the best and most suitable time for a human soul to get mindful of its Creator Lord. Only those who get up at midnight and engage themselves in prayers would know the realisation of…

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ لَكَ فِي النَّهَارِ سَبْحًا طَوِيلًا inna laka fī l-nahāri sabḥan ṭawīlan for indeed during the day you have drawn-out engagements.

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ لَكَ فِي النَّهَارِ سَبْحًا طَوِيلًا inna laka fī l-nahāri sabḥan ṭawīlan Indeed, for you by day is prolonged occupation. See 73:1

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ لَكَ فِي النَّهَارِ سَبْحًا طَوِيلًا inna laka fī l-nahāri sabḥan ṭawīlan Verily thou hast in the day long occupation (For serving the Lord and for the legitimate purpose of self - For propagating the truth - for doing as much good as possible before death - none knows, when) See 73:6

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاذْكُرِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلًا wa-udh'kuri is'ma rabbika watabattal ilayhi tabtīlan So celebrate the Name of your Lord and dedicate yourself to Him with total dedication.1

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاذْكُرِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلًا wa-udh'kuri is'ma rabbika watabattal ilayhi tabtīlan And remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with (complete) devotion. See 73:1

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاذْكُرِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلًا wa-udh'kuri is'ma rabbika watabattal ilayhi tabtīlan And remember thou, the name of thy Lord, and devote thyself unto Him with an exclusive devotion 'Tabattul' to cut away one's self and get communion exclusive, with the Lord - The Holy Lady Fatimah, the daughter of the Holy Prophet is called 'Batool' for she used to turn to God in prayers, disconnecting herself from everything in the world, or for her life as a whole being dedicated exclusively to God.

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَاتَّخِذْهُ وَكِيلًا rabbu l-mashriqi wal-maghribi lā ilāha illā huwa fa-ittakhidh'hu wakīlan Lord of the east and the west, there is no god except Him, so take Him for your trustee,

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَاتَّخِذْهُ وَكِيلًا rabbu l-mashriqi wal-maghribi lā ilāha illā huwa fa-ittakhidh'hu wakīlan (He is) the Lord of the East and the West; there is no deity except Him, so take Him as Disposer of (your) affairs.1 See 73:1

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَاتَّخِذْهُ وَكِيلًا rabbu l-mashriqi wal-maghribi lā ilāha illā huwa fa-ittakhidh'hu wakīlan The Lord of the East and the West, there is no god but He, take Him then as the Protector! This is also to be a counter to the false and the imaginary belief of the heathens about the existence of regional gods and the local and the other deities. It is to say that God is the Lord of the whole uniVerse, and no part of the world is out of His control and authority. Hence the believers need not fear anyone besides God.

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاصْبِرْ عَلَى مَا يَقُولُونَ وَاهْجُرْهُمْ هَجْرًا جَمِيلًا wa-iṣ'bir ʿalā mā yaqūlūna wa-uh'jur'hum hajran jamīlan and be patient over what they say, and keep away from them in a graceful manner.

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاصْبِرْ عَلَى مَا يَقُولُونَ وَاهْجُرْهُمْ هَجْرًا جَمِيلًا wa-iṣ'bir ʿalā mā yaqūlūna wa-uh'jur'hum hajran jamīlan And be patient over what they say and avoid them with gracious avoidance. And be patient with what they say, and keep away from them in a good way (73:10). And leave Me alone to deal with the deniers, those who are in possession of good things of life. And give them respite for a little (73:11). Verily, with Us are Ankal, and Jahim (73:12). And a food that chokes, and a painful torment (73:13). On the Day when the earth and the mountains will (Tarjufu) shake, and the mountains will be a heap of sand poured out (73:14). Verily, We have sent to you a Messenger to be a witness over you, as We did send a Messenger to Fir'awn (73:15). But Fir'awn disobeyed the…

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاصْبِرْ عَلَى مَا يَقُولُونَ وَاهْجُرْهُمْ هَجْرًا جَمِيلًا wa-iṣ'bir ʿalā mā yaqūlūna wa-uh'jur'hum hajran jamīlan And be thou patient against whatever they say and avoid them with a decorous avoidance The disbelievers and the ungrateful ones among the men who forget the bounties of God bestowed on them and speak nonsense and ridicule the faith and the faithful. These must be ignored and left to themselves in a noble and a respectable way making them realise that the real believer in God does not care for them at all for all his hopes rest only in God and in none else.

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَذَرْنِي وَالْمُكَذِّبِينَ أُولِي النَّعْمَةِ وَمَهِّلْهُمْ قَلِيلًا wadharnī wal-mukadhibīna ulī l-naʿmati wamahhil'hum qalīlan Leave Me [to deal] with the deniers, the opulent, and give them a little respite.

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَذَرْنِي وَالْمُكَذِّبِينَ أُولِي النَّعْمَةِ وَمَهِّلْهُمْ قَلِيلًا wadharnī wal-mukadhibīna ulī l-naʿmati wamahhil'hum qalīlan And leave Me with (the matter of) the deniers, those of ease (in life), and allow them respite a little. See 73:10

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَذَرْنِي وَالْمُكَذِّبِينَ أُولِي النَّعْمَةِ وَمَهِّلْهُمْ قَلِيلًا wadharnī wal-mukadhibīna ulī l-naʿmati wamahhil'hum qalīlan And leave Me (to deal), and the beliers, the possessors of the bounties, and respite them a little Those who enjoy the abundance of the bounties of God must be more and more grateful to Him and if they are not, it is God's concern to deal with them duly.

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ لَدَيْنَا أَنْكَالًا وَجَحِيمًا inna ladaynā ankālan wajaḥīman Indeed with Us are heavy fetters and a fierce fire,

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ لَدَيْنَا أَنْكَالًا وَجَحِيمًا inna ladaynā ankālan wajaḥīman Indeed, with Us (for them) are shackles and burning fire. See 73:10

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ لَدَيْنَا أَنْكَالًا وَجَحِيمًا inna ladaynā ankālan wajaḥīman Verily with Us are strong fetters and the flaming fire When a tooth pain made one restless, the First Holy Imam Ali Ibn Abu Talib said 'When a small lot of bone could make man feel so much and make him restless, what would the chastisement on the Day of Judgment do to man and how would he bear it.'

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَطَعَامًا ذَا غُصَّةٍ وَعَذَابًا أَلِيمًا waṭaʿāman dhā ghuṣṣatin waʿadhāban alīman and a food that chokes [those who gulp it], and a painful punishment [prepared for]

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَطَعَامًا ذَا غُصَّةٍ وَعَذَابًا أَلِيمًا waṭaʿāman dhā ghuṣṣatin waʿadhāban alīman And food that chokes and a painful punishment. See 73:10

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:13 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَطَعَامًا ذَا غُصَّةٍ وَعَذَابًا أَلِيمًا waṭaʿāman dhā ghuṣṣatin waʿadhāban alīman The food that choketh, and a painful chastisement See 73:12

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:14 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الْأَرْضُ وَالْجِبَالُ وَكَانَتِ الْجِبَالُ كَثِيبًا مَهِيلًا yawma tarjufu l-arḍu wal-jibālu wakānati l-jibālu kathīban mahīlan the day when the earth and the mountains will quake, and the mountains will be like dunes of shifting sand.

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:14 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الْأَرْضُ وَالْجِبَالُ وَكَانَتِ الْجِبَالُ كَثِيبًا مَهِيلًا yawma tarjufu l-arḍu wal-jibālu wakānati l-jibālu kathīban mahīlan On the Day the earth and the mountains will convulse and the mountains will become a heap of sand pouring down. See 73:10

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:14 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الْأَرْضُ وَالْجِبَالُ وَكَانَتِ الْجِبَالُ كَثِيبًا مَهِيلًا yawma tarjufu l-arḍu wal-jibālu wakānati l-jibālu kathīban mahīlan On the day when the earth and mountains shall be shaken and mountains shall become heaps of sand, rendered loose The dawn of the Day of Judgment would cause such a violent commotion that it would change the whole face of the physical world affecting violently the laws of nature working in them. The hard rocks of the mountains would suffer the loss of cohesion within their matter and the mountains will be turned into heaps of loose sand.

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْكُمْ رَسُولًا شَاهِدًا عَلَيْكُمْ كَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ رَسُولًا innā arsalnā ilaykum rasūlan shāhidan ʿalaykum kamā arsalnā ilā fir'ʿawna rasūlan Indeed We have sent to you an apostle, to be a witness to you, just as We sent an apostle to Pharaoh.

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْكُمْ رَسُولًا شَاهِدًا عَلَيْكُمْ كَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ رَسُولًا innā arsalnā ilaykum rasūlan shāhidan ʿalaykum kamā arsalnā ilā fir'ʿawna rasūlan Indeed, We have sent to you a Messenger as a witness upon you just as We sent to Pharaoh a messenger. See 73:10

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْكُمْ رَسُولًا شَاهِدًا عَلَيْكُمْ كَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ رَسُولًا innā arsalnā ilaykum rasūlan shāhidan ʿalaykum kamā arsalnā ilā fir'ʿawna rasūlan Verily, we have sent unto you an Apostle, a witness against you, as sent We an Apostle unto Pharaoh (Refer to Verses 10:75 - 10:92.) See 73:14

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَعَصَى فِرْعَوْنُ الرَّسُولَ فَأَخَذْنَاهُ أَخْذًا وَبِيلًا faʿaṣā fir'ʿawnu l-rasūla fa-akhadhnāhu akhdhan wabīlan But Pharaoh disobeyed the apostle; so We seized him with a terrible seizing.

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَعَصَى فِرْعَوْنُ الرَّسُولَ فَأَخَذْنَاهُ أَخْذًا وَبِيلًا faʿaṣā fir'ʿawnu l-rasūla fa-akhadhnāhu akhdhan wabīlan But Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger, so We seized him with a ruinous seizure. See 73:10

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَعَصَى فِرْعَوْنُ الرَّسُولَ فَأَخَذْنَاهُ أَخْذًا وَبِيلًا faʿaṣā fir'ʿawnu l-rasūla fa-akhadhnāhu akhdhan wabīlan But Pharaoh disobeyed the Apostle, whereupon We seized him with a severe (a violent seizure.) seizure Pharaoh disobeyed God's laws and defied God's authority - what happened to him? God's laws must stand and shall be fulfilled and all else shall be swept away and vanish - The wisdom, authority, power and the might of the forces of Pharaoh had been of no avail to him by one surprise from the Divine will, all vanished away for ever.

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَكَيْفَ تَتَّقُونَ إِنْ كَفَرْتُمْ يَوْمًا يَجْعَلُ الْوِلْدَانَ شِيبًا fakayfa tattaqūna in kafartum yawman yajʿalu l-wil'dāna shīban So, if you disbelieve, how will you avoid the day which will make children white-headed,

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَكَيْفَ تَتَّقُونَ إِنْ كَفَرْتُمْ يَوْمًا يَجْعَلُ الْوِلْدَانَ شِيبًا fakayfa tattaqūna in kafartum yawman yajʿalu l-wil'dāna shīban Then how can you fear, if you disbelieve, a Day that will make the children white-haired?1 See 73:10

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:17 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَكَيْفَ تَتَّقُونَ إِنْ كَفَرْتُمْ يَوْمًا يَجْعَلُ الْوِلْدَانَ شِيبًا fakayfa tattaqūna in kafartum yawman yajʿalu l-wil'dāna shīban How, then, will ye guard yourselves, if ye disbelieve, against the day which shall turn children greyheaded? If man defies the authority of the Lord in this life which is only a period of probation, what will he do on the day of the Final Requital which will be a day of the terrible manifestation of the reality. The transformation of the present into the hereafter will be so terrible and violent that even young children would be shocked so much that they will look like hoary-headed old men and the skies will be cleft asunder 82:1. The state of affairs will undergo a violent change manifesting the true value of everything in the uniVerse.

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:18 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلسَّمَاءُ مُنْفَطِرٌ بِهِ كَانَ وَعْدُهُ مَفْعُولًا al-samāu munfaṭirun bihi kāna waʿduhu mafʿūlan and wherein the sky will be rent apart? His promise is bound to be fulfilled.

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:18 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلسَّمَاءُ مُنْفَطِرٌ بِهِ كَانَ وَعْدُهُ مَفْعُولًا al-samāu munfaṭirun bihi kāna waʿduhu mafʿūlan The heaven will break apart therefrom;1 ever is His promise fulfilled. See 73:10

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:18 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلسَّمَاءُ مُنْفَطِرٌ بِهِ كَانَ وَعْدُهُ مَفْعُولًا al-samāu munfaṭirun bihi kāna waʿduhu mafʿūlan The heaven shall be rent asunder by it; His promise is always made to be fulfilled God's promise of justice being meted out to every individual being and everyone being duly recompensed for one's own good and evil, shall be fulfilled.

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:19 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ هَذِهِ تَذْكِرَةٌ فَمَنْ شَاءَ اتَّخَذَ إِلَى رَبِّهِ سَبِيلًا inna hādhihi tadhkiratun faman shāa ittakhadha ilā rabbihi sabīlan This is indeed a reminder. So let anyone who wishes take the way toward his Lord.

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:19 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ هَذِهِ تَذْكِرَةٌ فَمَنْ شَاءَ اتَّخَذَ إِلَى رَبِّهِ سَبِيلًا inna hādhihi tadhkiratun faman shāa ittakhadha ilā rabbihi sabīlan Indeed, this is a reminder, so whoever wills may take to his Lord a way. Verily, this is an admonition, therefore whosoever wills, let him take a path to His Lord (73:19). Verily, your Lord knows that you do stand a little less than two-thirds of the night, or half the night, or a third of the night, and also a party of those with you. And Allah measures the night and the day. He knows that you are unable to pray the whole night, so He has turned to you. So, recite you of the Qur'an as much as may be easy for you. He knows that there will be some among you sick, others traveling through the land, seeking of…

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:19 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ هَذِهِ تَذْكِرَةٌ فَمَنْ شَاءَ اتَّخَذَ إِلَى رَبِّهِ سَبِيلًا inna hādhihi tadhkiratun faman shāa ittakhadha ilā rabbihi sabīlan Verily this is a reminder, let him, whoso will, adopt unto his Lord, the (Right) way! The Holy Qur'an is a reminder to those who sincerely wish to know the right course to earn the grace and the mercy of the Lord. Repentance with the due amendment in the practical life is highway to obtain the forgiveness and the mercy of the Lord and getting nearer to Him. From Verse 1-19 the Verses themselves speak of themselves to belong to the early period of the Holy Prophet's ministry. From the 10th to 19th the Verses show that they belong to the period when the opposition had started - The Verse 20 with its length is obvious that it belongs to the period…

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:20 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ تَقُومُ أَدْنَى مِنْ ثُلُثَيِ اللَّيْلِ وَنِصْفَهُ وَثُلُثَهُ وَطَائِفَةٌ مِنَ الَّذِينَ مَعَكَ وَاللَّهُ يُقَدِّرُ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ عَلِمَ أَنْ لَنْ تُحْصُوهُ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ فَاقْرَءُوا مَا تَيَسَّرَ مِنَ الْقُرْءَانِ عَلِمَ أَنْ سَيَكُونُ مِنْكُمْ مَرْضَى وَءَاخَرُونَ يَضْرِبُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ يَبْتَغُونَ مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ وَءَاخَرُونَ يُقَاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَاقْرَءُوا مَا تَيَسَّرَ مِنْهُ وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ وَاٰتُوْۤا الزَّكَاةَ وَأَقْرِضُوا اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا وَمَا تُقَدِّمُوا لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ تَجِدُوهُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ هُوَ خَيْرًا وَأَعْظَمَ أَجْرًا وَاسْتَغْفِرُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ inna rabbaka yaʿlamu annaka taqūmu adnā min thuluthayi al-layli waniṣ'fahu wathuluthahu waṭāifatun mina alladhīna maʿaka wal-lahu yuqaddiru al-layla wal-nahāra ʿalima an lan tuḥ'ṣūhu fatāba ʿalaykum fa-iq'raū mā tayassara mina l-qur'āni ʿalima an sayakūnu minkum marḍā waākharūna yaḍribūna fī l-arḍi yabtaghūna min faḍli l-lahi waākharūna yuqātilūna fī sabīli l-lahi fa-iq'raū mā tayassara min'hu wa-aqīmū l-ṣalata waātū l-zakata wa-aqriḍū l-laha qarḍan ḥasanan wamā tuqaddimū…

item.title: Al-Muzzammil:20 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran

item.description: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ تَقُومُ أَدْنَى مِنْ ثُلُثَيِ اللَّيْلِ وَنِصْفَهُ وَثُلُثَهُ وَطَائِفَةٌ مِنَ الَّذِينَ مَعَكَ وَاللَّهُ يُقَدِّرُ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ عَلِمَ أَنْ لَنْ تُحْصُوهُ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ فَاقْرَءُوا مَا تَيَسَّرَ مِنَ الْقُرْءَانِ عَلِمَ أَنْ سَيَكُونُ مِنْكُمْ مَرْضَى وَءَاخَرُونَ يَضْرِبُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ يَبْتَغُونَ مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ وَءَاخَرُونَ يُقَاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَاقْرَءُوا مَا تَيَسَّرَ مِنْهُ وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ وَاٰتُوْۤا الزَّكَاةَ وَأَقْرِضُوا اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا وَمَا تُقَدِّمُوا لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ تَجِدُوهُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ هُوَ خَيْرًا وَأَعْظَمَ أَجْرًا وَاسْتَغْفِرُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ inna rabbaka yaʿlamu annaka taqūmu adnā min thuluthayi al-layli waniṣ'fahu wathuluthahu waṭāifatun mina alladhīna maʿaka wal-lahu yuqaddiru al-layla wal-nahāra ʿalima an lan tuḥ'ṣūhu fatāba ʿalaykum fa-iq'raū mā tayassara mina l-qur'āni ʿalima an sayakūnu minkum marḍā waākharūna yaḍribūna fī l-arḍi yabtaghūna min faḍli l-lahi waākharūna yuqātilūna fī sabīli l-lahi fa-iq'raū mā tayassara min'hu wa-aqīmū l-ṣalata waātū l-zakata wa-aqriḍū l-laha qarḍan ḥasanan wamā tuqaddimū…

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلْقَارِعَةُ al-qāriʿatu The Catastrophe!

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلْقَارِعَةُ al-qāriʿatu The Striking Calamity. نَارٌ حَامِيَةٌ A fire Hamiyah! Meaning: extreme heat. It is a heat that is accompanied by a strong flame and fire. It is narrated from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet SAW said: نَارُ بَنِي آدَمَ الَّتِي تُوقِدُونَ، جُزْءٌ مِنْ سَبْعِينَ جُزْءًا مِنْ نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ The fire of the Children of Adam that you all kindle is one part of the seventy parts of the fire of Hell. They (the Companions) said, "O Messenger of Allah! Isn't it sufficient?" He replied: إِنَّهَا فُضِّلَتْ عَلَيْهَا بِتِسْعَةٍ وَسِتِّينَ جُزْءًا It is more than it by sixty-nine times. This has been recorded by Al-Bukhari and Muslim. In some of the wordings he stated: إِنَّهَا فُضِّلَتْ عَلَيْهَا بِتِسْعَةٍ وَسِتِّينَ جُزْءًا، كُلُّهُنَّ مِثْلُ حَرِّهَا It is more than it by sixty-nine times, each of them is like the heat of it.…

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلْقَارِعَةُ al-qāriʿatu The Striking Calamity! 'Qariah', i.e., a tremendously clamorous striking noise which will accompany the inauguration of the great calamity, the earth will suffer at the dawn of the Day of Judgment when the whole of the present order of the world will undergo a thorough change giving place to a totally new atmosphere of a new state of the existence of a new world of a new order of realities with total wiping out of all false appearances and false values.

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا الْقَارِعَةُ mā l-qāriʿatu What is the Catastrophe?

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا الْقَارِعَةُ mā l-qāriʿatu What is the Striking Calamity? See 101:1

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا الْقَارِعَةُ mā l-qāriʿatu What is the Striking Calamity? Since anything similar to the terrible experience of the clamorous noise mentioned here, has never been experienced by anyone in the world, it is an impossibility even to correctly imagine what the noise would be like.

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْقَارِعَةُ wamā adrāka mā l-qāriʿatu What will show you what is the Catastrophe?

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْقَارِعَةُ wamā adrāka mā l-qāriʿatu And what can make you know what is the Striking Calamity? See 101:1

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْقَارِعَةُ wamā adrāka mā l-qāriʿatu What maketh thee know what the Striking Calamity is? See 101:2

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ يَكُونُ النَّاسُ كَالْفَرَاشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ yawma yakūnu l-nāsu kal-farāshi l-mabthūthi The day mankind will be like scattered moths,

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ يَكُونُ النَّاسُ كَالْفَرَاشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ yawma yakūnu l-nāsu kal-farāshi l-mabthūthi It is the Day when people will be like moths, dispersed.1 See 101:1

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ يَكُونُ النَّاسُ كَالْفَرَاشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ yawma yakūnu l-nāsu kal-farāshi l-mabthūthi The day when people shall be like moths scattered Out of the terror, the clamorous voice will create in the minds of the people they will be running bewildered on all sides in tumultuous multitude - out of the fear and the tumult each falling over the other, like the tiny insignificant being, the moths scattered by a violent stormy wind. This is to give an imaginable view of the confusion and distress and helplessness man will be thrown into, all of a sudden.

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَتَكُونُ الْجِبَالُ كَالْعِهْنِ الْمَنْفُوشِ watakūnu l-jibālu kal-ʿih'ni l-manfūshi and the mountains will be like carded wool.

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَتَكُونُ الْجِبَالُ كَالْعِهْنِ الْمَنْفُوشِ watakūnu l-jibālu kal-ʿih'ni l-manfūshi And the mountains will be like wool, fluffed up.1 See 101:1

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَتَكُونُ الْجِبَالُ كَالْعِهْنِ الْمَنْفُوشِ watakūnu l-jibālu kal-ʿih'ni l-manfūshi And the mountains shall become like wool carded (Loosened. Refer to: 70:9.) When even the solid and immovably and unshakably fixed huge mountains will be scattered in the atmosphere, like the insignificant flakes of the carder's wool1.

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا مَنْ ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ fa-ammā man thaqulat mawāzīnuhu As for him whose deeds weigh heavy in the scales,

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا مَنْ ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ fa-ammā man thaqulat mawāzīnuhu Then as for one whose scales are heavy (with good deeds). See 101:1

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا مَنْ ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ fa-ammā man thaqulat mawāzīnuhu Then as for him whose scales (Refer to: 57:25, 55:8, 42:17, 77:20 - 77:21.) (with good deeds) are heavy On that day nothing but the deeds, good and bad will be counted. The appraisement, valuation measuring or the weighing, will be strictly to the real value of each deed and deed means any deed of the physical body given to man and as well as the activity of the mind, i.e., the various faculties he has been endowed with. Every action physical and mental will be weighed viz., the motives, passions, thoughts, imagination, feelings, aspirations, love, hatred, the degree of faith in God anil the extent of the disbelief in Him, and the attitudes etc. And whosoever's measure of his good deeds will exceed the measure of his evils, will receive the…

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ fahuwa fī ʿīshatin rāḍiyatin he will have a pleasing life.

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ fahuwa fī ʿīshatin rāḍiyatin He will be in a pleasant life. See 101:1

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ fahuwa fī ʿīshatin rāḍiyatin He shall be in a life, well pleased with See 101:6

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَازِينُهُ wa-ammā man khaffat mawāzīnuhu But as for him whose deeds weigh light in the scales,

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَازِينُهُ wa-ammā man khaffat mawāzīnuhu But as for one whose scales are light. See 101:1

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَازِينُهُ wa-ammā man khaffat mawāzīnuhu And as for him whose scales (with good, deeds) are light And whosoever's evils will exceed his good deeds will be thrown into the abyss -and 'Haviah' is interpreted to be the abyss or the depth the bottom being immeasurably low in an unfathomable depth.

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ fa-ummuhu hāwiyatun his home will be the Abyss.

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ fa-ummuhu hāwiyatun His refuge1 will be an abyss.2 See 101:1

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ fa-ummuhu hāwiyatun His home shall be 'Haviah' (a burning abyss (It may also mean tending towards the abyss.) ) See 101:8

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا هِيَهْ wamā adrāka mā hiyah And what will show you what it is?

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا هِيَهْ wamā adrāka mā hiyah And what can make you know what that is? See 101:1

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا هِيَهْ wamā adrāka mā hiyah What maketh thee know what 'Haviah' is? As man in this life cannot rightly imagine the like of what the 'Qariah' mentioned in the verse 1 above, will be, he cannot correctly visualise the likeness of the abyss called 'Haviah' which will be the abode of the wicked.

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: نَارٌ حَامِيَةٌ nārun ḥāmiyatun It is a scorching fire!

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: نَارٌ حَامِيَةٌ nārun ḥāmiyatun It is a Fire, intensely hot. See 101:1

item.title: Al-Qaari'a:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: نَارٌ حَامِيَةٌ nārun ḥāmiyatun It is a Raging Fire The simplest note of description of the abyss 'Haviah' is that it is a blazing fire and the rest of it to be experienced and known when it is given to the wicked on the Day of Judgment.

item.title: Al-Qadr:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ innā anzalnāhu fī laylati l-qadri Indeed We sent it1 down on the Night of Ordainment.

item.title: Al-Qadr:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ innā anzalnāhu fī laylati l-qadri Indeed, We sent it (i.e., the Qur’ān) down during the Night of Decree. سَلَامٌ هِيَ There is peace. "This means all of it is good and there is no evil in it until the coming of Fajr (dawn)." Specifying the Night of Decree and its Signs This is supported by what Imam Ahmad recorded from 'Ubadah bin As-Samit that the Messenger of Allah SAW said: لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ فِي الْعَشْرِ الْبَوَاقِي، مَنْ قَامَهُنَّ ابْتِغَاءَ حِسْبَتِهِنَّ فَإِنَّ اللهَ يَغْفِرُ لَهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ وَمَا تَأَخَّرَ، وَهِيَ لَيْلَةُ وِتْرٍ: تِسْعٍ أَوْ سَبْعٍ أَوْ خَامِسَةٍ أَوْ ثَالِثَةٍ أَوْ آخِرِ لَيْلَةٍ The Night of Al-Qadr occurs during the last ten (nights). Whoever stands for them (in prayer) seeking their reward, then indeed Allah will forgive his previous sins and his latter sins. It is…

item.title: Al-Qadr:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ innā anzalnāhu fī laylati l-qadri Verily, We sent it (The Qur'an) down in the Night of 'Qadr' (Grandeur. Refer to: 2:185, 44:3.) ! The word 'Qadr' may mean - Power, Grandeur, Majesty. 'Lailat al-Qadr', i.e., the Night of Grandeur of the Lord - is kept a secret. The verse 2 below clearly means that none knows, what the night is, i.e., which night in the year it is and the special value of it, to its fullest extent. The various statements of the commentators are: Some say it is concealed in the whole month of Shahan. Some say it is the 14th of Shaban. Some say it is one of the nights of Ramadhan. But the majority of the commentators agree on its being one of the odd nights in the latter half of the…

item.title: Al-Qadr:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ wamā adrāka mā laylatu l-qadri What will show you what is the Night of Ordainment?

item.title: Al-Qadr:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ wamā adrāka mā laylatu l-qadri And what can make you know what is the Night of Decree? See 97:1

item.title: Al-Qadr:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ wamā adrāka mā laylatu l-qadri What can make thee know what the Night of 'Qadr' is? The question put in this verse, is a clear indication of the mystic nature and value of the Night of Grandeur which none else but the Lord knows. The succeeding verses only defined the night with its value and do not say which night in the year it is.

item.title: Al-Qadr:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ laylatu l-qadri khayrun min alfi shahrin The Night of Ordainment is better than a thousand months.

item.title: Al-Qadr:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ laylatu l-qadri khayrun min alfi shahrin The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months. See 97:1

item.title: Al-Qadr:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ laylatu l-qadri khayrun min alfi shahrin The Night of 'Qadr' is better than a thousand month! The announcement here in this verse about the night, refers to the greatness of the Night. The Second Holy Imam Hasan Ibn-Ali says that he heard from his grandfather, the Holy Prophet, that once he dreamt of monkeys getting upon his pulpit, and the Messenger Angel Gabriel informed him of the significance of the dream saying that ''Those whom thou dost see get upon thy pulpit are the Bani-Umayyah who would rule the Muslim Empire after thee for a thousand months" And revealed this verse. Quoting 32:4 - 32:5 and 70:4, a commentator says that the term "A Thousand, must be taken in an indefinite sense, i.e., a timeless time - and interprets it to mean that one…

item.title: Al-Qadr:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: تَنَزَّلُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ وَالرُّوحُ فِيهَا بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ مِنْ كُلِّ أَمْرٍ tanazzalu l-malāikatu wal-rūḥu fīhā bi-idh'ni rabbihim min kulli amrin In it the angels and the Spirit descend, by the leave of their Lord, with every command.

item.title: Al-Qadr:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: تَنَزَّلُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ وَالرُّوحُ فِيهَا بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ مِنْ كُلِّ أَمْرٍ tanazzalu l-malāikatu wal-rūḥu fīhā bi-idh'ni rabbihim min kulli amrin The angels and the Spirit (i.e., Jibril) descend therein by permission of their Lord for every matter.1 See 97:1

item.title: Al-Qadr:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: تَنَزَّلُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ وَالرُّوحُ فِيهَا بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ مِنْ كُلِّ أَمْرٍ tanazzalu l-malāikatu wal-rūḥu fīhā bi-idh'ni rabbihim min kulli amrin The Angels and the Spirit descend therein by the permission of their Lord, with (decrees) of all affairs (Refer to: 16:2, 78:38.) It is said that angels and holy spirits descend on earth with the special blessings from God and peace for those who seek them through prayers, supplications to the Lord1.

item.title: Al-Qadr:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: سَلَامٌ هِيَ حَتّٰی مَطْلَعِ الْفَجْرِ salāmun hiya ḥattā maṭlaʿi l-fajri It is peaceful until the rising of the dawn.

item.title: Al-Qadr:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: سَلَامٌ هِيَ حَتّٰی مَطْلَعِ الْفَجْرِ salāmun hiya ḥattā maṭlaʿi l-fajri Peace it is1 until the emergence of dawn. See 97:1

item.title: Al-Qadr:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: سَلَامٌ هِيَ حَتّٰی مَطْلَعِ الْفَجْرِ salāmun hiya ḥattā maṭlaʿi l-fajri Peace is (the whole Nighty)! till the breaking of the dawn! Taking the mystic word 'Night of Grandeur' as one of the sacred nights, in any of the months mentioned above, this verse would mean that the shower of the special boon and the great blessings of God, promised to the sincere devotees that night, continues until the dawn of the succeeding day.

item.title: Al-Qalam:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ن وَالْقَلَمِ وَمَا يَسْطُرُونَ noon wal-qalami wamā yasṭurūna Nūn. By the Pen and what they write:

item.title: Al-Qalam:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ن وَالْقَلَمِ وَمَا يَسْطُرُونَ noon wal-qalami wamā yasṭurūna Nūn.1 By the pen and what they inscribe. إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ ضَلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ Verily, your Lord is the best Knower of him who has gone astray from His path, and He is the best Knower of those who are guided. Meaning: 'He knows which of the two groups are truly guided among you, and He knows the party that is astray from the truth.'

item.title: Al-Qalam:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ن وَالْقَلَمِ وَمَا يَسْطُرُونَ noon wal-qalami wamā yasṭurūna 'Nun' and (N) by the Pen and by what they write The letter with which this Sura begins is supposed to mean the Inkpot from which the pen gets the matter (the ink) with which is the writing is affected to spread knowledge and learning into this world. The pen represents the written form of the Will of the Lord about the creation and the events to be affected in the countless generations from the beginning of the world to its end. The inkpot and the pen mentioned here have a mystic expression of the source of the knowledge through the ret elation front God. When a thing gets common or abundant in quantity, however much it may be invaluable in its worth, man does not note its original value. Take for…

item.title: Al-Qalam:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا أَنْتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِمَجْنُونٍ mā anta biniʿ'mati rabbika bimajnūnin you are not, by your Lord's blessing, crazy,

item.title: Al-Qalam:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا أَنْتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِمَجْنُونٍ mā anta biniʿ'mati rabbika bimajnūnin You are not, (O Muḥammad), by the favor of your Lord, a madman. See 68:1

item.title: Al-Qalam:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا أَنْتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِمَجْنُونٍ mā anta biniʿ'mati rabbika bimajnūnin Thou (O' Our Prophet!) by the grace of thy Lord, art not mad The reference is to what the heathens of Mecca in the beginning of his ministry called the Holy Prophet as 'Majnun' (i.e., mad). The people said: what the Holy Prophet preached was the raving of a mad man - whereas it was the Word of God which was recorded in writing by the angels. Being always under God's special guidance as Ali says that 'Ever since his (the Holy Prophet) birth was tinder the care of the greatest of angels, guiding him to all aspects of life. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Qalam:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّ لَكَ لَأَجْرًا غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍ wa-inna laka la-ajran ghayra mamnūnin and yours indeed will be an everlasting reward,

item.title: Al-Qalam:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّ لَكَ لَأَجْرًا غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍ wa-inna laka la-ajran ghayra mamnūnin And indeed, for you is a reward uninterrupted. See 68:1

item.title: Al-Qalam:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّ لَكَ لَأَجْرًا غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍ wa-inna laka la-ajran ghayra mamnūnin And verily there is for thee a recompense unending (unobliging) The return or the recompense for the Holy Prophet being a continuous and an unending flow of the Grace and the Mercy of the Lord. The reward which unlike any earthly bounty, would never cease or never fail him.

item.title: Al-Qalam:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَى خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ wa-innaka laʿalā khuluqin ʿaẓīmin and indeed you possess a great character.

item.title: Al-Qalam:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَى خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ wa-innaka laʿalā khuluqin ʿaẓīmin And indeed, you are of a great moral character. See 68:1

item.title: Al-Qalam:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَى خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ wa-innaka laʿalā khuluqin ʿaẓīmin And most certainly thou standest on sublime morality (Character. See Verses 2:143, 33:45, 33:21.) The character which the Holy Prophet was endowed with was so matchless that none could reach its limits. The Holy Prophet's is a historic personality. Every detail of his character, even the minutest aspect of it, has been noted and recorded both by his friends and his foes. It was the sword of the ideal heavenly character and godly conduct that subdued the man like Omar to join the ranks of the Muslims. To cite even a very few instances of his marvellous behaviour would need separate volume. It is said that one can visualise his personality in the mirror of the tenets of the Holy Qur'an. But I would say that one can visualise Qur'an in the…

item.title: Al-Qalam:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَسَتُبْصِرُ وَيُبْصِرُونَ fasatub'ṣiru wayub'ṣirūna You will see and they will see,

item.title: Al-Qalam:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَسَتُبْصِرُ وَيُبْصِرُونَ fasatub'ṣiru wayub'ṣirūna So you will see and they will see. See 68:1

item.title: Al-Qalam:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَسَتُبْصِرُ وَيُبْصِرُونَ fasatub'ṣiru wayub'ṣirūna So thou wilt see and they (too) wilt see When the Qoreish (the Meccans) found the Holy Prophet always speaking high of Ali, assigning to him a unique position next only to himself, they taunted saying that the Holy Prophet has gone mad in his love for Ali - 'Muhammad Ibn Sama' reports of Ka'b Ibn Alzah and Abdullah Ibn Masood that once when they were in the presence of the Holy Prophet a man asked him about the personal excellence of Ali to which the Holy Prophet replied: - Ali Ibn Abi Taleb is Foremost in Islam among you and none else before him, mas blessed with this degree in faith. The degree of faith of Ali, is greater than that of all of you. His patience is always triumphant against you all. His anger…

item.title: Al-Qalam:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: بِأَيِّيكُمُ الْمَفْتُونُ bi-ayyikumu l-maftūnu which one of you is crazy.

item.title: Al-Qalam:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: بِأَيِّيكُمُ الْمَفْتُونُ bi-ayyikumu l-maftūnu Which of you is the afflicted (by a devil). See 68:1

item.title: Al-Qalam:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: بِأَيِّيكُمُ الْمَفْتُونُ bi-ayyikumu l-maftūnu Which of you is demented (Fascinated – crazy.) The appeal is to reasoning in view of the factual position of the enemies of the Holy Prophet who were ultimately befooled by their disbelief what was the ultimate position of Walid-Ibn Mughaira, Abu Jehl and Abu Lahab.

item.title: Al-Qalam:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ ضَلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ inna rabbaka huwa aʿlamu biman ḍalla ʿan sabīlihi wahuwa aʿlamu bil-muh'tadīna Indeed your Lord knows best those who stray from His way, and He knows best those who are guided.

item.title: Al-Qalam:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ ضَلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ inna rabbaka huwa aʿlamu biman ḍalla ʿan sabīlihi wahuwa aʿlamu bil-muh'tadīna Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has gone astray from His way, and He is most knowing of the (rightly) guided. See 68:1

item.title: Al-Qalam:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ ضَلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ inna rabbaka huwa aʿlamu biman ḍalla ʿan sabīlihi wahuwa aʿlamu bil-muh'tadīna Verily thy Lord! He knoweth best of him who is astray from His way, and He knoweth best of those guided aright This Verse warns man against the false standards and the wrong and the mistaken standpoints of judgment about men and matters. The correct viewpoint is always that of God Whose knowledge of every being in the Universe is complete and all-comprehending. To Him alone are known the hidden motives and the open conduct of men. It is He and He alone Who knows the past in which are embedded the roots of the present and also the future of everyone, which is always generated from the present. Hence the value which man assesses to anyone is…

item.title: Al-Qalam:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَا تُطِعِ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ falā tuṭiʿi l-mukadhibīna So do not obey the deniers,

item.title: Al-Qalam:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَا تُطِعِ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ falā tuṭiʿi l-mukadhibīna Then do not obey the deniers. So, do not obey the deniers (68:8). They wish that you should compromise with them, so they (too) would compromise with you (68:9). And do not obey every Hallaf Mahin (68:10). A Hammaz, going about with Namim (68:11). Hinderer of the good, transgressor, sinful (68:12). 'Utul, and moreover Zanim (68:13). (He was so) because he had wealth and children (68:14). When Our Ayat are recited to him, he says: Tales of the men of old! (68:15). We shall brand him on the snout (nose) (68:16). Prohibition of giving in to the Pressure of the Disbelievers and Their Suggestions, and that They like to meet in the Middle of the Path Allah says, 'just as We have favored you and given you the upright legislation and great (standard of)…

item.title: Al-Qalam:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَا تُطِعِ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ falā tuṭiʿi l-mukadhibīna So yield (The Prophet addressed for the people.) thou not to the beliers! Though the address is to the Holy Prophet - which means a consolation to him against the offending remarks of the hypocrites, but it means a command to the Ummat (the Muslims) not to be deluded by the false estimation about anyone if they have to earn the approval and the pleasure of God.

item.title: Al-Qalam:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَدُّوْۤا لَوْ تُدْهِنُ فَيُدْهِنُونَ waddū law tud'hinu fayud'hinūna who are eager that you should be pliable, so that they may be pliable [towards you].

item.title: Al-Qalam:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَدُّوْۤا لَوْ تُدْهِنُ فَيُدْهِنُونَ waddū law tud'hinu fayud'hinūna They wish that you would soften (in your position), so they would soften (toward you). See 68:8

item.title: Al-Qalam:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَدُّوْۤا لَوْ تُدْهِنُ فَيُدْهِنُونَ waddū law tud'hinu fayud'hinūna Wish they that thou shouldst be pliant so they (too) would be pliant (Compromising.) The hateful qualities mentioned in this Verse refer to the personal qualities of the enemies of the Holy Prophet, particularly the hypocrites who doubted about the bonafide of the statement of the Holy Prophet about the unique excellence of the holy personality of Ali. As the guided ones shall never be compromising with their opponents (the unguided ones). (A.P.) There, such people depicted in the Verses above, cannot be guided. Therefore they should not be followed. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Qalam:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا تُطِعْ كُلَّ حَلَّافٍ مَهِينٍ walā tuṭiʿ kulla ḥallāfin mahīnin And do not obey any vile swearer,

item.title: Al-Qalam:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا تُطِعْ كُلَّ حَلَّافٍ مَهِينٍ walā tuṭiʿ kulla ḥallāfin mahīnin And do not obey every worthless habitual swearer. See 68:8

item.title: Al-Qalam:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا تُطِعْ كُلَّ حَلَّافٍ مَهِينٍ walā tuṭiʿ kulla ḥallāfin mahīnin And yield thou not unto any despicable swearer (Refer to Verse 2:224.) See 68:9

item.title: Al-Qalam:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: هَمَّازٍ مَشَّاءٍ بِنَمِيمٍ hammāzin mashāin binamīmin scandal-monger, talebearer,

item.title: Al-Qalam:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: هَمَّازٍ مَشَّاءٍ بِنَمِيمٍ hammāzin mashāin binamīmin (And) scorner, going about with malicious gossip. See 68:8

item.title: Al-Qalam:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: هَمَّازٍ مَشَّاءٍ بِنَمِيمٍ hammāzin mashāin binamīmin Defamer, going about with slander See 68:9

item.title: Al-Qalam:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَنَّاعٍ لِلْخَيْرِ مُعْتَدٍ أَثِيمٍ mannāʿin lil'khayri muʿ'tadin athīmin hinderer of all good, sinful transgressor,

item.title: Al-Qalam:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَنَّاعٍ لِلْخَيْرِ مُعْتَدٍ أَثِيمٍ mannāʿin lil'khayri muʿ'tadin athīmin A preventer of good, transgressing and sinful. See 68:8

item.title: Al-Qalam:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَنَّاعٍ لِلْخَيْرِ مُعْتَدٍ أَثِيمٍ mannāʿin lil'khayri muʿ'tadin athīmin Vehement hinderer of good, uncontrolled transgressor, sunk deep in sin See 68:9

item.title: Al-Qalam:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: عُتُلٍّ بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ زَنِيمٍ ʿutullin baʿda dhālika zanīmin callous and, on top of that, baseborn,

item.title: Al-Qalam:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: عُتُلٍّ بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ زَنِيمٍ ʿutullin baʿda dhālika zanīmin Cruel, moreover, and an illegitimate pretender.1 See 68:8

item.title: Al-Qalam:13 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: عُتُلٍّ بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ زَنِيمٍ ʿutullin baʿda dhālika zanīmin Cruelly violent, besides all that, baseborn (Ar. 'Zaneem', He whose father is not known, and whose mother is unchaste. He is a base born.) 'Zaneen' a product of adultery. Walid who was a Qoreishite chief, did not know that he owned the quality. When this Verse was revealed, Walid said to himself. "I am the Qoreishite Chief and Mughaira is known to be my father, I am also sure that Muhammad never utters a falsehood" He got wild, drew his sword and with a drawn sword went to his mother and asked her to tell him the truth about his parentage. She had to helplessly disclose saying "Look! Thy father Mughaira was unfit for any woman. Since I had no issues from him, his brother's sons coveted to inherit the enormous wealth…

item.title: Al-Qalam:14 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنْ كَانَ ذَا مَالٍ وَبَنِينَ an kāna dhā mālin wabanīna —[only] because he has wealth and children.

item.title: Al-Qalam:14 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنْ كَانَ ذَا مَالٍ وَبَنِينَ an kāna dhā mālin wabanīna Because he is a possessor of wealth and children. See 68:8

item.title: Al-Qalam:14 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنْ كَانَ ذَا مَالٍ وَبَنِينَ an kāna dhā mālin wabanīna Just because possesses he wealth and sons Abundance of wealth and male issues was a matter of pride. It is not uncommon among the people even today. People who are puffed up with wealth and the largeness of the number of their family members, are in the view of the Lord branded as rebellious. A believer is not to heed to such worldly possessions and positions.

item.title: Al-Qalam:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذَا تُتْلَى عَلَيْهِ آيَاتُنَا قَالَ أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ idhā tut'lā ʿalayhi āyātunā qāla asāṭīru l-awalīna When Our signs are recited to him, he says, 'Myths of the ancients!'

item.title: Al-Qalam:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذَا تُتْلَى عَلَيْهِ آيَاتُنَا قَالَ أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ idhā tut'lā ʿalayhi āyātunā qāla asāṭīru l-awalīna When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Legends of the former peoples." See 68:8

item.title: Al-Qalam:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذَا تُتْلَى عَلَيْهِ آيَاتُنَا قَالَ أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ idhā tut'lā ʿalayhi āyātunā qāla asāṭīru l-awalīna When unto him are recited Our signs, sayeth he: (they are the) "Stories of yore" (legends of the ancients) (Refer to Verses 6:25, 83:13.) Nose being the most prominent or the raised part of the face, is always used to indicate the proud part of it and it is a popular proverb to rub the nose of one on the ground or to cut or disfigure it, is to degrade or humiliate the individual. Walid Ibn Mughaira was branded with a wound in the Battle of Badr, the mark of which remained to his shame and disgrace until his death. (Bd., Rz., MS) (Kartoom) literally means the proboscis, the most sensitive part of elephant's body by which he could very easily be controlled, the rebellious one…

item.title: Al-Qalam:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: سَنَسِمُهُ عَلَى الْخُرْطُومِ sanasimuhu ʿalā l-khur'ṭūmi Soon We shall brand him on the snout.

item.title: Al-Qalam:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: سَنَسِمُهُ عَلَى الْخُرْطُومِ sanasimuhu ʿalā l-khur'ṭūmi We will brand him upon the snout.1 See 68:8

item.title: Al-Qalam:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: سَنَسِمُهُ عَلَى الْخُرْطُومِ sanasimuhu ʿalā l-khur'ṭūmi We will brand him (Walid Ibn Moghaira.) on the snout! The story of the sons of the charitable man related in these Verses serves a double purpose. It gives the state of the conduct of the enemies of the Holy Prophet and the hypocrites, and it also illustrates how the unlimited mercy of the Lord allows wickedness to flourish for some time, allowing the respite for the individuals to turn to the right course. This also refers to the long patience which the infinite mercy of the Lord allowing the individual to behave as they please and then effecting the punishment in gradual stages, allowing chance after chance for the sinner at every stage to repent and rectify, his conduct. The story illustrates how greed and selfishness and the love of wealth, take a…

item.title: Al-Qalam:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا بَلَوْنَاهُمْ كَمَا بَلَوْنَا أَصْحَابَ الْجَنَّةِ إِذْ أَقْسَمُوْۤا لَيَصْرِمُنَّهَا مُصْبِحِينَ innā balawnāhum kamā balawnā aṣḥāba l-janati idh aqsamū layaṣrimunnahā muṣ'biḥīna Indeed we have tested them1 just as We tested the People of the Garden when they vowed they would gather its fruit at dawn,

item.title: Al-Qalam:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا بَلَوْنَاهُمْ كَمَا بَلَوْنَا أَصْحَابَ الْجَنَّةِ إِذْ أَقْسَمُوْۤا لَيَصْرِمُنَّهَا مُصْبِحِينَ innā balawnāhum kamā balawnā aṣḥāba l-janati idh aqsamū layaṣrimunnahā muṣ'biḥīna Indeed, We have tried them as We tried the companions of the garden, when they swore to cut its fruit in the (early) morning. Verily, We have tried them as We tried the People of the Garden, when they swore to pluck the fruits in the morning (68:17). Without (saying: "If Allah wills." (18)Then there passed over it a Ta'if from your Lord while they were asleep (19)So by the morning, it became like As-Sarim (20)Then they called out (one to another as soon) as the morning broke (21)Saying: "Go to your tilth in the morning, if you would pluck (the fruits). (22)So they departed, and they were whispering (23)"No poor person shall enter upon you into it today. (24)And…

item.title: Al-Qalam:17 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا بَلَوْنَاهُمْ كَمَا بَلَوْنَا أَصْحَابَ الْجَنَّةِ إِذْ أَقْسَمُوْۤا لَيَصْرِمُنَّهَا مُصْبِحِينَ innā balawnāhum kamā balawnā aṣḥāba l-janati idh aqsamū layaṣrimunnahā muṣ'biḥīna Verily We will try them as We did try the owners of the garden, when they vowed that they would certainly pluck the fruits at morn See 68:16

item.title: Al-Qalam:18 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا يَسْتَثْنُونَ walā yastathnūna and they did not make any exception.1

item.title: Al-Qalam:18 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا يَسْتَثْنُونَ walā yastathnūna Without making exception.1 See 68:17

item.title: Al-Qalam:18 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا يَسْتَثْنُونَ walā yastathnūna And made no (room for) exception (for the will of God) (saying 'If God willeth it') (In complete conformity with Verses 18:23; 18:24.) See 68:16

item.title: Al-Qalam:19 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَطَافَ عَلَيْهَا طَائِفٌ مِنْ رَبِّكَ وَهُمْ نَائِمُونَ faṭāfa ʿalayhā ṭāifun min rabbika wahum nāimūna Then a visitation from your Lord visited it1 while they were asleep.

item.title: Al-Qalam:19 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَطَافَ عَلَيْهَا طَائِفٌ مِنْ رَبِّكَ وَهُمْ نَائِمُونَ faṭāfa ʿalayhā ṭāifun min rabbika wahum nāimūna So there came upon it (i.e., the garden) an affliction from your Lord while they were asleep. See 68:17

item.title: Al-Qalam:19 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَطَافَ عَلَيْهَا طَائِفٌ مِنْ رَبِّكَ وَهُمْ نَائِمُونَ faṭāfa ʿalayhā ṭāifun min rabbika wahum nāimūna So encircled it a visitation from thy Lord, (rendering the garden desolate) while they were asleep See 68:16

item.title: Al-Qalam:20 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَصْبَحَتْ كَالصَّرِيمِ fa-aṣbaḥat kal-ṣarīmi So by the dawn it was like a harvested field.1

item.title: Al-Qalam:20 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَصْبَحَتْ كَالصَّرِيمِ fa-aṣbaḥat kal-ṣarīmi And it became as though reaped. See 68:17

item.title: Al-Qalam:20 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَصْبَحَتْ كَالصَّرِيمِ fa-aṣbaḥat kal-ṣarīmi And it became like black barren soil (Or reaped land.) See 68:16

item.title: Al-Qalam:21 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَتَنَادَوْا مُصْبِحِينَ fatanādaw muṣ'biḥīna At dawn they called out to one another,

item.title: Al-Qalam:21 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَتَنَادَوْا مُصْبِحِينَ fatanādaw muṣ'biḥīna And they called one another at morning. See 68:17

item.title: Al-Qalam:21 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَتَنَادَوْا مُصْبِحِينَ fatanādaw muṣ'biḥīna And they cried out one unto each other at morn See 68:16

item.title: Al-Qalam:22 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنِ اغْدُوْۤا عَلَى حَرْثِكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَارِمِينَ ani igh'dū ʿalā ḥarthikum in kuntum ṣārimīna 'Get off early to your field if you have to gather [the fruits].'

item.title: Al-Qalam:22 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنِ اغْدُوْۤا عَلَى حَرْثِكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَارِمِينَ ani igh'dū ʿalā ḥarthikum in kuntum ṣārimīna (Saying), "Go early to your crop if you would cut the fruit." See 68:17

item.title: Al-Qalam:22 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنِ اغْدُوْۤا عَلَى حَرْثِكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَارِمِينَ ani igh'dū ʿalā ḥarthikum in kuntum ṣārimīna Be ye early at your tilth if ye would pluck (the fruits) (Refer to Verse 3:117.) See 68:16

item.title: Al-Qalam:23 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَانْطَلَقُوا وَهُمْ يَتَخَافَتُونَ fa-inṭalaqū wahum yatakhāfatūna So off they went, murmuring to one another:

item.title: Al-Qalam:23 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَانْطَلَقُوا وَهُمْ يَتَخَافَتُونَ fa-inṭalaqū wahum yatakhāfatūna So they set out, while lowering their voices. See 68:17

item.title: Al-Qalam:23 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَانْطَلَقُوا وَهُمْ يَتَخَافَتُونَ fa-inṭalaqū wahum yatakhāfatūna And went they whispering unto each other See 68:16

item.title: Al-Qalam:24 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنْ لَا يَدْخُلَنَّهَا الْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِسْكِينٌ an lā yadkhulannahā l-yawma ʿalaykum mis'kīnun 'Today no needy man shall come to you in it.'

item.title: Al-Qalam:24 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنْ لَا يَدْخُلَنَّهَا الْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِسْكِينٌ an lā yadkhulannahā l-yawma ʿalaykum mis'kīnun (Saying), "There will surely not enter it today upon you (any) poor person." See 68:17

item.title: Al-Qalam:24 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنْ لَا يَدْخُلَنَّهَا الْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِسْكِينٌ an lā yadkhulannahā l-yawma ʿalaykum mis'kīnun Saying: "No poor man shall enter it today upon you" See 68:16

item.title: Al-Qalam:25 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَغَدَوْا عَلَى حَرْدٍ قَادِرِينَ waghadaw ʿalā ḥardin qādirīna They set out early morning, [considering themselves] able to grudge.

item.title: Al-Qalam:25 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَغَدَوْا عَلَى حَرْدٍ قَادِرِينَ waghadaw ʿalā ḥardin qādirīna And they went early in determination, (assuming themselves) able.1 See 68:17

item.title: Al-Qalam:25 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَغَدَوْا عَلَى حَرْدٍ قَادِرِينَ waghadaw ʿalā ḥardin qādirīna And at morn went they, strong in their resolve (to prevent the poor) See 68:16

item.title: Al-Qalam:26 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهَا قَالُوْا إِنَّا لَضَالُّونَ falammā ra-awhā qālū innā laḍāllūna But when they saw it, they said, 'We have indeed lost our way!'

item.title: Al-Qalam:26 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهَا قَالُوْا إِنَّا لَضَالُّونَ falammā ra-awhā qālū innā laḍāllūna But when they saw it, they said, "Indeed, we are lost. See 68:17

item.title: Al-Qalam:26 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهَا قَالُوْا إِنَّا لَضَالُّونَ falammā ra-awhā qālū innā laḍāllūna But when they beheld it, said they: "Verily we have strayed!" See 68:16

item.title: Al-Qalam:27 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ bal naḥnu maḥrūmūna 'No, we are deprived!'

item.title: Al-Qalam:27 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ bal naḥnu maḥrūmūna Rather, we have been deprived." See 68:17

item.title: Al-Qalam:27 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ bal naḥnu maḥrūmūna Nay! we are (the) deprived ones (of the fruits of our labour).'' Ibn Abbas says that the sons thereafter repented, and God of His infinite mercy accepted their repentance and granted them a better garden of a greater, i.e., of a more profuse yield. This indicates also that sincere repentance on the part of sinners, earns the pardon from the Lord and the Lord rewards the sincerely repentant ones with greater blessings and bestows more bounties.

item.title: Al-Qalam:28 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ أَوْسَطُهُمْ أَلَمْ أَقُلْ لَكُمْ لَوْلَا تُسَبِّحُونَ qāla awsaṭuhum alam aqul lakum lawlā tusabbiḥūna The most moderate among them said, 'Did I not tell you, "Why do you not glorify [Allah]?" '

item.title: Al-Qalam:28 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ أَوْسَطُهُمْ أَلَمْ أَقُلْ لَكُمْ لَوْلَا تُسَبِّحُونَ qāla awsaṭuhum alam aqul lakum lawlā tusabbiḥūna The most moderate of them said, "Did I not say to you, 'Why do you not exalt (Allah)?'"1 See 68:17

item.title: Al-Qalam:28 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ أَوْسَطُهُمْ أَلَمْ أَقُلْ لَكُمْ لَوْلَا تُسَبِّحُونَ qāla awsaṭuhum alam aqul lakum lawlā tusabbiḥūna Said the most balanced one of them: "Said I not unto you, 'Why should ye not glorify (God)'?" See 68:27

item.title: Al-Qalam:29 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا سُبْحَانَ رَبِّنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ qālū sub'ḥāna rabbinā innā kunnā ẓālimīna They said, 'Immaculate is our Lord! We have indeed been wrongdoers!'

item.title: Al-Qalam:29 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا سُبْحَانَ رَبِّنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ qālū sub'ḥāna rabbinā innā kunnā ẓālimīna They said, "Exalted is our Lord! Indeed, we were wrongdoers." See 68:17

item.title: Al-Qalam:29 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا سُبْحَانَ رَبِّنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ qālū sub'ḥāna rabbinā innā kunnā ẓālimīna Said they: "Hallowed be Our Lord! Verily we have been unjust!" See 68:27

item.title: Al-Qalam:30 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ يَتَلَاوَمُونَ fa-aqbala baʿḍuhum ʿalā baʿḍin yatalāwamūna Then they turned to one another, blaming each other.

item.title: Al-Qalam:30 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ يَتَلَاوَمُونَ fa-aqbala baʿḍuhum ʿalā baʿḍin yatalāwamūna Then they approached one another, blaming each other. See 68:17

item.title: Al-Qalam:30 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ يَتَلَاوَمُونَ fa-aqbala baʿḍuhum ʿalā baʿḍin yatalāwamūna Then some of them proceeded against the others, reproaching each other See 68:27

item.title: Al-Qalam:31 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا يَاوَيْلَنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا طَاغِينَ qālū yāwaylanā innā kunnā ṭāghīna They said, 'Woe to us! Indeed we have been rebellious.

item.title: Al-Qalam:31 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا يَاوَيْلَنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا طَاغِينَ qālū yāwaylanā innā kunnā ṭāghīna They said, "O woe to us; indeed we were transgressors. See 68:17

item.title: Al-Qalam:31 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا يَاوَيْلَنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا طَاغِينَ qālū yāwaylanā innā kunnā ṭāghīna Said they: "O' woe unto us! Verily we have been arrogant! (Inordinate – Transgressing. Refer to Verses. 34:18, 34:19.) " See 68:27

item.title: Al-Qalam:32 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: عَسٰۤی رَبُّنَا أَنْ يُبْدِلَنَا خَيْرًا مِنْهَا إِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا رَاغِبُونَ ʿasā rabbunā an yub'dilanā khayran min'hā innā ilā rabbinā rāghibūna Maybe our Lord will give us a better one in its place. Indeed we turn earnestly to our Lord.'

item.title: Al-Qalam:32 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: عَسٰۤی رَبُّنَا أَنْ يُبْدِلَنَا خَيْرًا مِنْهَا إِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا رَاغِبُونَ ʿasā rabbunā an yub'dilanā khayran min'hā innā ilā rabbinā rāghibūna Perhaps our Lord will substitute for us (one) better than it. Indeed, we are toward our Lord desirous."1 See 68:17

item.title: Al-Qalam:32 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: عَسٰۤی رَبُّنَا أَنْ يُبْدِلَنَا خَيْرًا مِنْهَا إِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا رَاغِبُونَ ʿasā rabbunā an yub'dilanā khayran min'hā innā ilā rabbinā rāghibūna Happly, our Lord will give us in exchange a better one than it; Verily unto our Lord do we turn (in repentance) See 68:27

item.title: Al-Qalam:33 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: كَذٰلِكَ الْعَذَابُ وَلَعَذَابُ الْاٰخِرَةُ أَكْبَرُ لَوْ كَانُوْۤا يَعْلَمُونَ kadhālika l-ʿadhābu walaʿadhābu l-ākhirati akbaru law kānū yaʿlamūna Such was the punishment; and the punishment of the Hereafter is surely greater, had they known.

item.title: Al-Qalam:33 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: كَذٰلِكَ الْعَذَابُ وَلَعَذَابُ الْاٰخِرَةُ أَكْبَرُ لَوْ كَانُوْۤا يَعْلَمُونَ kadhālika l-ʿadhābu walaʿadhābu l-ākhirati akbaru law kānū yaʿlamūna Such is the punishment (of this world). And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew. See 68:17

item.title: Al-Qalam:33 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: كَذٰلِكَ الْعَذَابُ وَلَعَذَابُ الْاٰخِرَةُ أَكْبَرُ لَوْ كَانُوْۤا يَعْلَمُونَ kadhālika l-ʿadhābu walaʿadhābu l-ākhirati akbaru law kānū yaʿlamūna Such hath been Our chastisement, and certainly the chastisement of the hereafter is greater still; Did they but know (it)! (Refer to Verse 39:26.) The punishment in this life might be gradual with the respite for repentance and amendment but in the hereafter, the time for the repentance would have passed and thus the punishment, meted out would naturally be in full.

item.title: Al-Qalam:34 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ inna lil'muttaqīna ʿinda rabbihim jannāti l-naʿīmi Indeed for the Godwary there will be gardens of bliss near their Lord.

item.title: Al-Qalam:34 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ inna lil'muttaqīna ʿinda rabbihim jannāti l-naʿīmi Indeed, for the righteous with their Lord are the Gardens of Pleasure. Verily, for those who have Taqwa are Gardens of Delight with their Lord (68:34). Shall We then treat the Muslims like the criminals (68:35). What is the matter with you? How judge you (68:36). Or have you a Book wherein you learn (68:37). That you shall therein have all that you choose (68:38). Or have you oaths from Us, lasting until the Day of Judgement, that yours will be what you judge (68:39). Ask them, which of them will stand as surety for that (68:40). Or have they "partners"? Then let them bring their "partners" if they are truthful (68:41). The Reward of those Who have Taqwa and that They will Not be Treated like the…

item.title: Al-Qalam:34 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ inna lil'muttaqīna ʿinda rabbihim jannāti l-naʿīmi Verily, for the pious ones (Those who guard themselves against evil.) with their Lord are the Gardens of bliss Those who guard themselves against evil. (A.P.)

item.title: Al-Qalam:35 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
