item.description: لَوْ نَشَاءُ لَجَعَلْنَاهُ حُطَامًا فَظَلْتُمْ تَفَكَّهُونَ law nashāu lajaʿalnāhu ḥuṭāman faẓaltum tafakkahūna Had We willed, We could crumble it to dry bits, and ye would be left only to lament See 56:64

item.title: Al-Waaqia:66 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا لَمُغْرَمُونَ innā lamugh'ramūna 'Indeed we have suffered loss!

item.title: Al-Waaqia:66 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا لَمُغْرَمُونَ innā lamugh'ramūna (Saying), "Indeed, we are (now) in debt. See 56:63

item.title: Al-Waaqia:66 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا لَمُغْرَمُونَ innā lamugh'ramūna (Saying): 'Verily we have been burdened with loss! (We have wasted the money, effort and time and we are deprived of the result.) ' See 56:64

item.title: Al-Waaqia:67 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ bal naḥnu maḥrūmūna Rather we are deprived!'

item.title: Al-Waaqia:67 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ bal naḥnu maḥrūmūna Rather, we have been deprived." See 56:63

item.title: Al-Waaqia:67 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ bal naḥnu maḥrūmūna 'Nay! We are deprived (Suffered the loss.) (of the benefits!)' Can anyone else, except God, cause the life-giving water to rain from heaven. It is not a proof positive of the existence of the One who does it?

item.title: Al-Waaqia:68 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَرَءَيْتُمُ الْمَاءَ الَّذِي تَشْرَبُونَ afara-aytumu l-māa alladhī tashrabūna Have you considered the water that you drink?

item.title: Al-Waaqia:68 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَرَءَيْتُمُ الْمَاءَ الَّذِي تَشْرَبُونَ afara-aytumu l-māa alladhī tashrabūna And have you seen the water that you drink? See 56:63

item.title: Al-Waaqia:68 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَرَءَيْتُمُ الْمَاءَ الَّذِي تَشْرَبُونَ afara-aytumu l-māa alladhī tashrabūna Have ye seen the water which ye drink? See 56:67

item.title: Al-Waaqia:69 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ءَأَنْتُمْ أَنْزَلْتُمُوهُ مِنَ الْمُزْنِ أَمْ نَحْنُ الْمُنْزِلُونَ a-antum anzaltumūhu mina l-muz'ni am naḥnu l-munzilūna Is it you who bring it down from the rain cloud, or is it We who bring [it] down?

item.title: Al-Waaqia:69 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ءَأَنْتُمْ أَنْزَلْتُمُوهُ مِنَ الْمُزْنِ أَمْ نَحْنُ الْمُنْزِلُونَ a-antum anzaltumūhu mina l-muz'ni am naḥnu l-munzilūna Is it you who brought it down from the clouds, or is it We who bring it down? See 56:63

item.title: Al-Waaqia:69 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ءَأَنْتُمْ أَنْزَلْتُمُوهُ مِنَ الْمُزْنِ أَمْ نَحْنُ الْمُنْزِلُونَ a-antum anzaltumūhu mina l-muz'ni am naḥnu l-munzilūna What! Is it ye that send it down from the heaven or are We the Senders ? This refers to the change of the clouds into fresh drinking water without any mixture (A.P.).

item.title: Al-Waaqia:70 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَوْ نَشَاءُ جَعَلْنَاهُ أُجَاجًا فَلَوْلَا تَشْكُرُونَ law nashāu jaʿalnāhu ujājan falawlā tashkurūna If We wish We can make it bitter. Then why do you not give thanks?

item.title: Al-Waaqia:70 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَوْ نَشَاءُ جَعَلْنَاهُ أُجَاجًا فَلَوْلَا تَشْكُرُونَ law nashāu jaʿalnāhu ujājan falawlā tashkurūna If We willed, We could make it bitter, so why are you not grateful? See 56:63

item.title: Al-Waaqia:70 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَوْ نَشَاءُ جَعَلْنَاهُ أُجَاجًا فَلَوْلَا تَشْكُرُونَ law nashāu jaʿalnāhu ujājan falawlā tashkurūna Had We willed, We would have made it saltish (Unfit to drink. Without which there can't be life on earth.) , why then ye thank not? What could we have done, if the water we get from heaven upon which depends the life on earth, had been turned saltish. Is it not God's grace for which we should remain grateful to Him?

item.title: Al-Waaqia:71 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَرَءَيْتُمُ النَّارَ الَّتِي تُورُونَ afara-aytumu l-nāra allatī tūrūna Have you considered the fire that you kindle?

item.title: Al-Waaqia:71 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَرَءَيْتُمُ النَّارَ الَّتِي تُورُونَ afara-aytumu l-nāra allatī tūrūna And have you seen the fire that you ignite? See 56:63

item.title: Al-Waaqia:71 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَرَءَيْتُمُ النَّارَ الَّتِي تُورُونَ afara-aytumu l-nāra allatī tūrūna Have ye seen the fire which ye kindle (by friction)?' Is not the burning quality endowed in fire, a great bounty of God? Could" we have caused it without His will? Or could we have lived without the heat it provides us with? Does it not, prove the existence of the One who does it and should we not remain grateful and obedient to Him? Example of bringing out a deadening and destructive element (fire) from a living and growing being (tree) (A.P.).

item.title: Al-Waaqia:72 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ءَأَنْتُمْ أَنْشَأْتُمْ شَجَرَتَهَا أَمْ نَحْنُ الْمُنْشِئُونَ a-antum anshatum shajaratahā am naḥnu l-munshiūna Was it you who caused its tree to grow, or were We the grower?

item.title: Al-Waaqia:72 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ءَأَنْتُمْ أَنْشَأْتُمْ شَجَرَتَهَا أَمْ نَحْنُ الْمُنْشِئُونَ a-antum anshatum shajaratahā am naḥnu l-munshiūna Is it you who produced its tree, or are We the producer? See 56:63

item.title: Al-Waaqia:72 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ءَأَنْتُمْ أَنْشَأْتُمْ شَجَرَتَهَا أَمْ نَحْنُ الْمُنْشِئُونَ a-antum anshatum shajaratahā am naḥnu l-munshiūna What! Is it ye who produce its tree? Or are We the producers (Produce – grew. Refer to Verse 36:80.) (of) it? Though fire as an essential provision for the human life on earth has many uses, the burning of it, serves also as the signal to the travellers in the desert at night, who make out the human habitation from a distance and they could direct their move on the right track, guided by it. Only those who have an experience of the travel through an extensive desert, particularly at night, know the aptness of this illustration. "Reminder" may refer to the tree or to the fire. Refers two aspects - as a Reminder as well as a provision intellectual as well as physical advantages (A.P.).

item.title: Al-Waaqia:73 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: نَحْنُ جَعَلْنَاهَا تَذْكِرَةً وَمَتَاعًا لِلْمُقْوِينَ naḥnu jaʿalnāhā tadhkiratan wamatāʿan lil'muq'wīna It was We who made it a reminder and a boon for the desert-dwellers.

item.title: Al-Waaqia:73 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: نَحْنُ جَعَلْنَاهَا تَذْكِرَةً وَمَتَاعًا لِلْمُقْوِينَ naḥnu jaʿalnāhā tadhkiratan wamatāʿan lil'muq'wīna We have made it a reminder1 and provision for the travelers.2 See 56:63

item.title: Al-Waaqia:73 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: نَحْنُ جَعَلْنَاهَا تَذْكِرَةً وَمَتَاعًا لِلْمُقْوِينَ naḥnu jaʿalnāhā tadhkiratan wamatāʿan lil'muq'wīna It is We Who have made it a reminder (It may refer to the tree or to the fire.) and a provision (of comfort) for the needy ones (Or the wayfarers.) See 56:72

item.title: Al-Waaqia:74 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ fasabbiḥ bi-is'mi rabbika l-ʿaẓīmi So celebrate the Name of your Lord, the All-supreme.

item.title: Al-Waaqia:74 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ fasabbiḥ bi-is'mi rabbika l-ʿaẓīmi So exalt the name of your Lord, the Most Great. See 56:63

item.title: Al-Waaqia:74 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ fasabbiḥ bi-is'mi rabbika l-ʿaẓīmi So hallow thou the name of thy Lord, the Great See 56:72

item.title: Al-Waaqia:75 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِمَوَاقِعِ النُّجُومِ falā uq'simu bimawāqiʿi l-nujūmi So I swear1 by the places where2 the stars set!3

item.title: Al-Waaqia:75 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِمَوَاقِعِ النُّجُومِ falā uq'simu bimawāqiʿi l-nujūmi Then I swear by the setting of the stars.1 Fala! I swear by the Mawaqi' of the stars (56:75). And verily that is indeed a great oath, if you but know (56:76). That (this) is indeed an honorable recitation (56:77). In a Book Maknun (56:78). Which none touches but the pure ones (56:79). A revelation from the Lord of all that exists (56:80). Is it such a talk that you are Mudhinun (56:81). And you make your provision your denial (56:82). Allah Swears to the Greatness of the Qur'an The usage of La (in Fala) is not an extra character without meaning, as some of the scholars of Tafsir say. Rather it is used at the beginning of an oath when the oath is a negation. This is like when Aisha (RA)said,…

item.title: Al-Waaqia:75 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِمَوَاقِعِ النُّجُومِ falā uq'simu bimawāqiʿi l-nujūmi But nay! I swear by the setting of the stars (Or the position of the Qur'an.) 'Maqam an-Nujum' i.e., the time or the occasion of the setting of the stars - the time between midnight and the approach of the dawn. It is true when the pious ones or the staunch devotees of God are busy in their supplications or adoration to the Lord. Some commentators say that it refers to the revelation of the Qur'an. However, it is the time when the Mercy of the Lord unfolds itself specially for those who are busy seeking it, by their supplications. It is the best time for concentration, meditation, and thus for communion with the All-Divine. This is the time availed of, by the sincere devotees of God to elevate their souls from…

item.title: Al-Waaqia:76 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّهُ لَقَسَمٌ لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عَظِيمٌ wa-innahu laqasamun law taʿlamūna ʿaẓīmun And indeed it is a great oath, should you know.

item.title: Al-Waaqia:76 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّهُ لَقَسَمٌ لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عَظِيمٌ wa-innahu laqasamun law taʿlamūna ʿaẓīmun And indeed, it is an oath - if you could know - (most) great. See 56:75

item.title: Al-Waaqia:76 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّهُ لَقَسَمٌ لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عَظِيمٌ wa-innahu laqasamun law taʿlamūna ʿaẓīmun And verily it is a great oath if ye only knew it See 56:75

item.title: Al-Waaqia:77 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّهُ لَقُرْءَانٌ كَرِيمٌ innahu laqur'ānun karīmun This is indeed a noble Qur'ān,

item.title: Al-Waaqia:77 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّهُ لَقُرْءَانٌ كَرِيمٌ innahu laqur'ānun karīmun Indeed, it is a noble Qur’ān. See 56:75

item.title: Al-Waaqia:77 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّهُ لَقُرْءَانٌ كَرِيمٌ innahu laqur'ānun karīmun Verily it is Qur'an honourable (Refer to Verses 43:4; 50:4.) To get the full meaning, this verse has to be read along with the other following two, i.e., 78 and 79 below. These three verses deserve a serious and intelligent study. Note the Holy Qur'an is called 'Kareem' which may mean Honourable as well as Charitable, Beneficent, Liberal, Kind. All the various meanings of the word 'Kareem' are equally applicable to the Holy Qur'an. Taking the meaning Gracious, Beneficent, it has the quality in perfect consonance with the fact that it is the Word of the Gracious and the Beneficent Lord of the Universe. Beneficence or Grace, is always given to anyone and everyone who seeks it. Similarly, the Holy Qur'an is there, ever ready to benefit or profit whosoever approaches it duly as…

item.title: Al-Waaqia:78 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي كِتَابٍ مَكْنُونٍ fī kitābin maknūnin in a guarded Book,1

item.title: Al-Waaqia:78 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي كِتَابٍ مَكْنُونٍ fī kitābin maknūnin In a Register well-protected;1. See 56:75

item.title: Al-Waaqia:78 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي كِتَابٍ مَكْنُونٍ fī kitābin maknūnin In a Book hidden (Refer to Verses 85:21 - 85:22; 80:13 - 80:16.) It is clearly said, that it (the Holy Qur'an) is treasured in a Concealed or a Hidden Book, which means that the Holy Qur'an is an object contained in a Book which is Concealed or Hidden, i.e., duly protected - in which case the thing in our bands is only a Recital form of the Holy Qur'an and not the actual Book itself, for it is clearly said here that, it is in the 'Kitab al-Maknoon' 'Hidden Book.' Supporting this is verse 43:3, which says, that this is the only Arabic version of the Holy Qur'an, and 43:4 says that the actual Holy Qur'an is in the 'Umm al-Kitab' the 'Mother Book.' The Holy Qur'an was revealed through the Messenger Angel…

item.title: Al-Waaqia:79 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ lā yamassuhu illā l-muṭaharūna —no one touches it except the pure ones—

item.title: Al-Waaqia:79 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ lā yamassuhu illā l-muṭaharūna None touch it except the purified (i.e., the angels). See 56:75

item.title: Al-Waaqia:79 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ lā yamassuhu illā l-muṭaharūna Toucheth it not save the purified ones (Refer to Verse 33:33.) The ordinary rendering of translation of this verse, is that it shall be held in all honour and purity. It shall not even be touched but by the clean at least in body with the prescribed ablution without which none shall even touch its written form. The wording means also that none but the purified one would understand it duly. Here the mental or the intellectual touch is meant. Even the Ahmadi commentator (M.A.) acknowledges this to be one of the meanings of this verse saying: "This also shows that the understanding of the Qur'an is granted only to those who are pure in heart." One should know as to who could be the purified ones who could have the external…

item.title: Al-Waaqia:80 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: تَنْزِيلٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ tanzīlun min rabbi l-ʿālamīna gradually sent down from the Lord of all the worlds.

item.title: Al-Waaqia:80 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: تَنْزِيلٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ tanzīlun min rabbi l-ʿālamīna (It is) a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. See 56:75

item.title: Al-Waaqia:80 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: تَنْزِيلٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ tanzīlun min rabbi l-ʿālamīna Sent down by the Lord of the worlds See 56:79

item.title: Al-Waaqia:81 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَفَبِهٰذَا الْحَدِيثِ أَنْتُمْ مُدْهِنُونَ afabihādhā l-ḥadīthi antum mud'hinūna What! Do you take lightly this discourse?

item.title: Al-Waaqia:81 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَفَبِهٰذَا الْحَدِيثِ أَنْتُمْ مُدْهِنُونَ afabihādhā l-ḥadīthi antum mud'hinūna Then is it to this statement that you are indifferent. See 56:75

item.title: Al-Waaqia:81 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَفَبِهٰذَا الْحَدِيثِ أَنْتُمْ مُدْهِنُونَ afabihādhā l-ḥadīthi antum mud'hinūna What! Hold ye then in scorn (Hypocritically.) this statement? Reference to the disbelievers, ridiculing the Holy Qur'an, calling it a compilation of old stories and not being a revelation from God.

item.title: Al-Waaqia:82 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ watajʿalūna riz'qakum annakum tukadhibūna And make your denial of it your vocation?1

item.title: Al-Waaqia:82 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ watajʿalūna riz'qakum annakum tukadhibūna And make (the thanks for) your provision that you deny (the Provider)? See 56:75

item.title: Al-Waaqia:82 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ watajʿalūna riz'qakum annakum tukadhibūna And make ye your sustenance (Habit similar to the habit of eating (A.P.).) that ye should belie it Once while the Holy Prophet was travelling there happened the dearth of water and the people needed water immediately to quench their killing thirst. The Holy Prophet said if I pray to God and get the water from heaven, you will ascribe it to the effect of some star. They said that they would not. The Holy Prophet prayed and instantaneously it rained very heavily. A man while taking water for him, said that the rain was due to some star's movement. The Holy Prophet heard it and said that I am afraid of three forbidden things in my people: (1) Cruelty to my Ahl Al-Bayt, (2) Disbelief in the Holy Qur'an, (3) Belief…

item.title: Al-Waaqia:83 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَوْلَا إِذَا بَلَغَتِ الْحُلْقُومَ falawlā idhā balaghati l-ḥul'qūma So when it1 reaches the throat [of the dying person]

item.title: Al-Waaqia:83 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَوْلَا إِذَا بَلَغَتِ الْحُلْقُومَ falawlā idhā balaghati l-ḥul'qūma Then why, when it (i.e., the soul at death) reaches the throat. Then why do you not (intervene) when it reaches Al-Hulqum (56:83). And you at the moment are looking (56:84). But We are nearer to him than you, but you see not (56:85). Then why do you not – if you are not Madini (56:86). Return the soul, if you are truthful (56:87). When the Soul Reaches the Throat at the Time of Death, it Cannot be Brought back; this Proves Reckoning shall Occur Allah the Exalted said: فَلَوْلَا إِذَا بَلَغَتِ Then why do you not (intervene) when it reaches Which is in reference to the soul: الْحُلْقُومَ Al-Hulqum I.e., the throat, at the time of death. Allah the Exalted said in other Ayat: كَلَّا إِذَا بَلَغَتِ التَّرَاقِيَ - وَقِيلَ مَنْ…

item.title: Al-Waaqia:83 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَوْلَا إِذَا بَلَغَتِ الْحُلْقُومَ falawlā idhā balaghati l-ḥul'qūma Why then do ye not (help) when (the soul of the dying man) cometh up to the throat (Refer to Verse 56:82.) ? See 56:82

item.title: Al-Waaqia:84 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنْتُمْ حِينَئِذٍ تَنْظُرُونَ wa-antum ḥīna-idhin tanẓurūna and at that moment you are looking on

item.title: Al-Waaqia:84 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنْتُمْ حِينَئِذٍ تَنْظُرُونَ wa-antum ḥīna-idhin tanẓurūna And you are at that time looking on. See 56:83

item.title: Al-Waaqia:84 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنْتُمْ حِينَئِذٍ تَنْظُرُونَ wa-antum ḥīna-idhin tanẓurūna And ye then (remain) only gazing (Helplessly.) (at him) See 56:82

item.title: Al-Waaqia:85 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْكُمْ وَلَكِنْ لَا تُبْصِرُونَ wanaḥnu aqrabu ilayhi minkum walākin lā tub'ṣirūna —and We are nearer to him1 than you are, though you do not perceive—

item.title: Al-Waaqia:85 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْكُمْ وَلَكِنْ لَا تُبْصِرُونَ wanaḥnu aqrabu ilayhi minkum walākin lā tub'ṣirūna And We (i.e., Our angels) are nearer to him than you, but you do not see. See 56:83

item.title: Al-Waaqia:85 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْكُمْ وَلَكِنْ لَا تُبْصِرُونَ wanaḥnu aqrabu ilayhi minkum walākin lā tub'ṣirūna And We are nearer to him than ye, but ye see (Us) not (Refer to Verses 34:50; 50:16.) See 56:82

item.title: Al-Waaqia:86 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَوْلَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ غَيْرَ مَدِينِينَ falawlā in kuntum ghayra madīnīna then why do you not, if you are not subject1

item.title: Al-Waaqia:86 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَوْلَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ غَيْرَ مَدِينِينَ falawlā in kuntum ghayra madīnīna Then why do you not, if you are not to be recompensed. See 56:83

item.title: Al-Waaqia:86 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَوْلَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ غَيْرَ مَدِينِينَ falawlā in kuntum ghayra madīnīna Why not then, if ye are not in bondage (If you are not held under any authority (A.P.).) (unto Us) See 56:82

item.title: Al-Waaqia:87 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: تَرْجِعُونَهَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ tarjiʿūnahā in kuntum ṣādiqīna [to the Divine dispensation], restore it, should you be truthful?

item.title: Al-Waaqia:87 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: تَرْجِعُونَهَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ tarjiʿūnahā in kuntum ṣādiqīna Bring it back,1 if you should be truthful? See 56:83

item.title: Al-Waaqia:87 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: تَرْجِعُونَهَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ tarjiʿūnahā in kuntum ṣādiqīna Ye send it (the soul) back, if ye be truthful The gist of this challenge is that if you think that life and death is not controlled by any Supreme Conscious Agency - then you, the Conscious independent being should be able to bring it under your hold (A.P.).

item.title: Al-Waaqia:88 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا إِنْ كَانَ مِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ fa-ammā in kāna mina l-muqarabīna Then, if he be of those brought near,1

item.title: Al-Waaqia:88 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا إِنْ كَانَ مِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ fa-ammā in kāna mina l-muqarabīna And if he (i.e., the deceased) was of those brought near (to Allah). Then, if he be of the Muqarrabin (56:88). Then Rawh, Rayhan and a Garden of Delights (56:89). And if he be of those on the right (56:90). Then Salam (peace) to you from those on the right (56:91). But if he be of the denying, the erring (56:92). Then for him is an entertainment with Hamim (56:93). And entry in Hellfire (56:94). Verily, this! This is an absolute truth with certainty (56:95). So, glorify with praises the Name of your Lord, the Most Great (56:96). The Condition of People at the Time of Their Death These are the three types of conditions that people face upon their death. Either they are among the near believers or those…

item.title: Al-Waaqia:88 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا إِنْ كَانَ مِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ fa-ammā in kāna mina l-muqarabīna Then if he be of those drawn nigh (unto God) This is a re-assertion of the statement and the classification in the beginning of the chapter (A.P.).

item.title: Al-Waaqia:89 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَرَوْحٌ وَرَيْحَانٌ وَجَنَّتُ نَعِيمٍ farawḥun warayḥānun wajannatu naʿīmin then ease, abundance, and a garden of bliss.

item.title: Al-Waaqia:89 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَرَوْحٌ وَرَيْحَانٌ وَجَنَّتُ نَعِيمٍ farawḥun warayḥānun wajannatu naʿīmin Then (for him is) rest and bounty and a garden of pleasure. See 56:88

item.title: Al-Waaqia:89 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَرَوْحٌ وَرَيْحَانٌ وَجَنَّتُ نَعِيمٍ farawḥun warayḥānun wajannatu naʿīmin (For him is) rest and happiness and a garden (Paradise.) delightful See 56:88

item.title: Al-Waaqia:90 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا إِنْ كَانَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ الْيَمِينِ wa-ammā in kāna min aṣḥābi l-yamīni And if he be of the People of the Right Hand,

item.title: Al-Waaqia:90 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا إِنْ كَانَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ الْيَمِينِ wa-ammā in kāna min aṣḥābi l-yamīni And if he was of the companions of the right. See 56:88

item.title: Al-Waaqia:90 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا إِنْ كَانَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ الْيَمِينِ wa-ammā in kāna min aṣḥābi l-yamīni And if he be of the people of the Right Hand See 56:88

item.title: Al-Waaqia:91 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَسَلَامٌ لَكَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ الْيَمِينِ fasalāmun laka min aṣḥābi l-yamīni then 'Peace be on you,' [a greeting] from the People of the Right Hand!

item.title: Al-Waaqia:91 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَسَلَامٌ لَكَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ الْيَمِينِ fasalāmun laka min aṣḥābi l-yamīni Then (the angels will say), "Peace for you; (you are) from the companions of the right." See 56:88

item.title: Al-Waaqia:91 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَسَلَامٌ لَكَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ الْيَمِينِ fasalāmun laka min aṣḥābi l-yamīni Then Peace unto you from the people of the Right Hand See 56:88

item.title: Al-Waaqia:92 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا إِنْ كَانَ مِنَ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ الضَّالِّينَ wa-ammā in kāna mina l-mukadhibīna l-ḍālīna But if he be of the impugners, the astray ones,

item.title: Al-Waaqia:92 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا إِنْ كَانَ مِنَ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ الضَّالِّينَ wa-ammā in kāna mina l-mukadhibīna l-ḍālīna But if he was of the deniers (who were) astray. See 56:88

item.title: Al-Waaqia:92 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا إِنْ كَانَ مِنَ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ الضَّالِّينَ wa-ammā in kāna mina l-mukadhibīna l-ḍālīna And if he be of those who have belied, gone astray See 56:88

item.title: Al-Waaqia:93 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَنُزُلٌ مِنْ حَمِيمٍ fanuzulun min ḥamīmin then a treat of boiling water

item.title: Al-Waaqia:93 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَنُزُلٌ مِنْ حَمِيمٍ fanuzulun min ḥamīmin Then (for him is) accommodation of scalding water. See 56:88

item.title: Al-Waaqia:93 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَنُزُلٌ مِنْ حَمِيمٍ fanuzulun min ḥamīmin He shall have an entertainment of a boiling water See 56:88

item.title: Al-Waaqia:94 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَتَصْلِيَةُ جَحِيمٍ wataṣliyatu jaḥīmin and entry into hell.1

item.title: Al-Waaqia:94 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَتَصْلِيَةُ جَحِيمٍ wataṣliyatu jaḥīmin And burning in Hellfire. See 56:88

item.title: Al-Waaqia:94 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَتَصْلِيَةُ جَحِيمٍ wataṣliyatu jaḥīmin And the boiling of the hell-fire See 56:88

item.title: Al-Waaqia:95 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ هَذَا لَهُوَ حَقُّ الْيَقِينِ inna hādhā lahuwa ḥaqqu l-yaqīni Indeed this is certain truth.

item.title: Al-Waaqia:95 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ هَذَا لَهُوَ حَقُّ الْيَقِينِ inna hādhā lahuwa ḥaqqu l-yaqīni Indeed, this is the true certainty. See 56:88

item.title: Al-Waaqia:95 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ هَذَا لَهُوَ حَقُّ الْيَقِينِ inna hādhā lahuwa ḥaqqu l-yaqīni Verily, this is truth in certainty This is not a mere fanciful or a wishful thinking but the Truth in its certainty (A.P.).

item.title: Al-Waaqia:96 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ fasabbiḥ bi-is'mi rabbika l-ʿaẓīmi So celebrate the Name of your Lord, the All-supreme!

item.title: Al-Waaqia:96 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ fasabbiḥ bi-is'mi rabbika l-ʿaẓīmi So exalt the name of your Lord, the Most Great. See 56:88

item.title: Al-Waaqia:96 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ fasabbiḥ bi-is'mi rabbika l-ʿaẓīmi Hallow therefore the Name of thy Lord, the Great See 56:95

item.title: An-Naas:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ qul aʿūdhu birabbi l-nāsi Say, 'I seek the protection of the Lord of humans,

item.title: An-Naas:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ qul aʿūdhu birabbi l-nāsi Say, "I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind. مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ Of Jinn and An-Nas is an explanation of who is it that whispers into the breasts of mankind from the devils of mankind and Jinns. This is similar to Allah's saying: وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلْنَا لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ عَدُوًّا شَيَاطِينَ الْإِنسِ وَالْجِنِّ يُوحِي بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَىٰ بَعْضٍ زُخْرُفَ الْقَوْلِ غُرُورًا And so We have appointed for every Prophet enemies – Shayatin among mankind and Jinn, inspiring one another with adorned speech as a delusion. (6:112) Imam Ahmad recorded that Ibn 'Abbas said, A man came to the Prophet SAW and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! Sometimes I say things to myself that I would rather fall from the sky than say (aloud openly).' The Prophet SAW said: اللهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللهُ أَكْبَرٌ الْحَمْدُ للهِ الَّذِي…

item.title: An-Naas:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ qul aʿūdhu birabbi l-nāsi Say: ''I seek refuge in the Lord of the people! This Surah is identical with the previous one, Surah 113. The matter is supplementary to that of the previous Surah. Man is asked to seek refuge in God with His name as "Rabb", i.e., the Lord of Men - i.e., the Cherisher and Sustainer. Invoking this great attribute, man can expect an especially paternal treatment.

item.title: An-Naas:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَلِكِ النَّاسِ maliki l-nāsi Sovereign of humans,

item.title: An-Naas:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَلِكِ النَّاسِ maliki l-nāsi The Sovereign of mankind. See 114:1

item.title: An-Naas:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَلِكِ النَّاسِ maliki l-nāsi The King of the people! To seek refuge in God, invoking His authority over the affairs of men, as their King, i.e., He is the One Who can independently act over His creation.

item.title: An-Naas:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِلَهِ النَّاسِ ilāhi l-nāsi God of humans,

item.title: An-Naas:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِلَهِ النَّاسِ ilāhi l-nāsi The God of mankind. See 114:1

item.title: An-Naas:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِلَهِ النَّاسِ ilāhi l-nāsi The God of the people! To seek the protection invoking the divinity of the Lord as the God of mankind - for it is God's authority which must necessarily be obeyed, i.e., it is His command or His will which is always done.

item.title: An-Naas:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مِنْ شَرِّ الْوَسْوَاسِ الْخَنَّاسِ min sharri l-waswāsi l-khanāsi from the evil of the sneaky tempter

item.title: An-Naas:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مِنْ شَرِّ الْوَسْوَاسِ الْخَنَّاسِ min sharri l-waswāsi l-khanāsi From the evil of the retreating whisperer1. See 114:1

item.title: An-Naas:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مِنْ شَرِّ الْوَسْوَاسِ الْخَنَّاسِ min sharri l-waswāsi l-khanāsi From the evil of the Satan (slinking whisperer,) 'Khannas', i.e., the one who gets back or withdraws. This is a reference to Satan who withdraws himself, the moment he hears the name of the Lord mentioned.

item.title: An-Naas:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ النَّاسِ alladhī yuwaswisu fī ṣudūri l-nāsi who puts temptations into the breasts of humans,

item.title: An-Naas:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ النَّاسِ alladhī yuwaswisu fī ṣudūri l-nāsi Who whispers (evil) into the breasts of mankind. See 114:1

item.title: An-Naas:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ النَّاسِ alladhī yuwaswisu fī ṣudūri l-nāsi Who whispereth into the breasts (hearts) of the people Satan Who whispers evil into the minds of men and leaves them to suffer the consequences of obeying his instigations to evil.

item.title: An-Naas:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ mina l-jinati wal-nāsi from among the jinn and humans.'

item.title: An-Naas:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ mina l-jinati wal-nāsi From among the jinn and mankind."1 See 114:1

item.title: An-Naas:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ mina l-jinati wal-nāsi From among the Jinn and the Men Be the evil doers, the Jinns or human beings. It is a well-known fact that among the forces hidden from the human eye, which are active in the world, there are good and also bad ones among them. Jinns, like Satan are spiritual beings1. The End

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالنَّازِعَاتِ غَرْقًا wal-nāziʿāti gharqan By those [angels] who wrest [the soul] violently,

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالنَّازِعَاتِ غَرْقًا wal-nāziʿāti gharqan By those (angels) who extract with violence.1 فَإِذَا هُم بِالسَّاهِرَةِ When behold, they are at As-Sahirah. Allah says: يَوْمَ تُبَدَّلُ الْأَرْضُ غَيْرَ الْأَرْضِ وَالسَّمَاوَاتُ ۖ وَبَرَزُوا لِلَّهِ الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ On the Day when the earth will be changed to another earth and so will be the heavens, and they will appear before Allah, the One, the Irresistible. (14:48) and He says: وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْجِبَالِ فَقُلْ يَنسِفُهَا رَبِّي نَسْفًا - فَيَذَرُهَا قَاعًا صَفْصَفًا - لَّا تَرَىٰ فِيهَا عِوَجًا وَلَا أَمْتًا And they ask you concerning the mountains, say: "My Lord will blast them and scatter them as particles of dust. Then He shall leave them as a level smooth plain. You will see therein nothing crooked or curved." (20:105-107) and Allah says: وَيَوْمَ نُسَيِّرُ الْجِبَالَ وَتَرَى الْأَرْضَ بَارِزَةً And the Day We shall cause the mountains to…

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالنَّازِعَاتِ غَرْقًا wal-nāziʿāti gharqan ''By those (Angels.) who drag forth violently (Refer to: 51:1 - 51:4, 77:1 - 77:5, 37:1 - 37:3.) The Arabic alphabet is used to indicate the swearing, i.e., by the angels who tear out the souls of the disbelievers from their bodies. The beginning of this Surah is like that of Surah 77. The swearing by the angels and the other forces and the elements in nature, might not give the true sense of the gravity of the act to those ignorant of the greatness of the things or the phenomenon but those who know how great and mysterious are the things and the functioning of the natural phenomena would realise the seriousness or the importance of the occasion for God to do it - and how great and vital the thing must be to mankind…

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالنَّاشِطَاتِ نَشْطًا wal-nāshiṭāti nashṭan by those who draw [it] out gently,

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالنَّاشِطَاتِ نَشْطًا wal-nāshiṭāti nashṭan And (by) those who remove with ease.1 See 79:1

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالنَّاشِطَاتِ نَشْطًا wal-nāshiṭāti nashṭan ''And those (Angels.) who untie (the knot) briskly By the angels who gently cause the soul of the righteous ones to get released of their confinement of their bodies. In contrast to the disbelievers and the wicked ones, the souls of the believers and the righteous ones, only await their release from the material bodies and its commitments. Hence the souls themselves pass out of their bodies willingly and the angel makes the task easy and pleasant.

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالسَّابِحَاتِ سَبْحًا wal-sābiḥāti sabḥan by those who swim smoothly,

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالسَّابِحَاتِ سَبْحًا wal-sābiḥāti sabḥan And (by) those who glide (as if) swimming.1 See 79:1

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالسَّابِحَاتِ سَبْحًا wal-sābiḥāti sabḥan ''And those who glide on (Swiftly) By the angels who are busy moving about briskly in executing their duties in the management or the administration of the universe.

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَالسَّابِقَاتِ سَبْقًا fal-sābiqāti sabqan by those who take the lead, racing,

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَالسَّابِقَاتِ سَبْقًا fal-sābiqāti sabqan And those who race each other in a race.1 See 79:1

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَالسَّابِقَاتِ سَبْقًا fal-sābiqāti sabqan ''Then those who go ahead with a foremost speed By the angels which race with each other in executing the will of the Lord to His satisfaction and pleasure.

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَالْمُدَبِّرَاتِ أَمْرًا fal-mudabirāti amran by those who direct the affairs [of creatures]:

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَالْمُدَبِّرَاتِ أَمْرًا fal-mudabirāti amran And those who arrange (each) matter.1 See 79:1

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَالْمُدَبِّرَاتِ أَمْرًا fal-mudabirāti amran ''Then those who (submissively) manage the affairs By the angels who manage the affairs of the universe in a systematic way.

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الرَّاجِفَةُ yawma tarjufu l-rājifatu the day when the Quaker quakes

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الرَّاجِفَةُ yawma tarjufu l-rājifatu On the Day the blast (of the Horn) will convulse (creation). See 79:1

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الرَّاجِفَةُ yawma tarjufu l-rājifatu ''On the day on which shall quake (Commotion convulsion.) the quaking The reference is to the violent commotion, the greatly agitated state of convulsion that will be affected at the dawn of the Day of Judgment which everything in the universe shall experience.

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: تَتْبَعُهَا الرَّادِفَةُ tatbaʿuhā l-rādifatu and is followed by the Successor,1

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: تَتْبَعُهَا الرَّادِفَةُ tatbaʿuhā l-rādifatu There will follow it the subsequent (one). See 79:1

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: تَتْبَعُهَا الرَّادِفَةُ tatbaʿuhā l-rādifatu ''Shall follow it the quake (by the second trumpet) which shall follow The change that the whole of this present world will undergo. A new state of life will be established in the place of the present one.

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلُوبٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَاجِفَةٌ qulūbun yawma-idhin wājifatun hearts will be trembling on that day,

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلُوبٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَاجِفَةٌ qulūbun yawma-idhin wājifatun Hearts,1 that Day, will tremble. See 79:1

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلُوبٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَاجِفَةٌ qulūbun yawma-idhin wājifatun ''Hearts (Every heart.) that day shall palpitate See 79:7

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَبْصَارُهَا خَاشِعَةٌ abṣāruhā khāshiʿatun bearing a humbled look.

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَبْصَارُهَا خَاشِعَةٌ abṣāruhā khāshiʿatun Their eyes1 humbled. See 79:1

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَبْصَارُهَا خَاشِعَةٌ abṣāruhā khāshiʿatun ''Their eyes shall be cast down See 79:7

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَقُولُونَ أَءِنَّا لَمَرْدُودُونَ فِي الْحَافِرَةِ yaqūlūna a-innā lamardūdūna fī l-ḥāfirati They will say, 'Are we being returned to our earlier state?

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَقُولُونَ أَءِنَّا لَمَرْدُودُونَ فِي الْحَافِرَةِ yaqūlūna a-innā lamardūdūna fī l-ḥāfirati They are (presently) saying, "Will we indeed be returned to (our) former state (of life)? See 79:1

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَقُولُونَ أَءِنَّا لَمَرْدُودُونَ فِي الْحَافِرَةِ yaqūlūna a-innā lamardūdūna fī l-ḥāfirati ''They shall say (then): ''What (Parenthetical sentence referring to what people would say.) ! Shall we indeed be restored to as (we were) at first? This refers to the deniers denying such a sure event which shall take place. A parenthetical sentence referring to what people sat now in this life - doubting about resurrection. (A. P.)

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَءِذَا كُنَّا عِظَامًا نَخِرَةً a-idhā kunnā ʿiẓāman nakhiratan What, when we have been decayed bones?!'

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَءِذَا كُنَّا عِظَامًا نَخِرَةً a-idhā kunnā ʿiẓāman nakhiratan Even if we should be decayed bones?"1 See 79:1

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَءِذَا كُنَّا عِظَامًا نَخِرَةً a-idhā kunnā ʿiẓāman nakhiratan ''What! When we are (even) bones rotten (Refer to: 36:78, 23:35, 23:82, 34:7, 13:5, 32:10, 19:66, 17:49.) ? See 79:10

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا تِلْكَ إِذًا كَرَّةٌ خَاسِرَةٌ qālū til'ka idhan karratun khāsiratun They will say, 'This, then, is a ruinous return!'

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا تِلْكَ إِذًا كَرَّةٌ خَاسِرَةٌ qālū til'ka idhan karratun khāsiratun They say, "That, then, would be a losing return."1 See 79:1

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا تِلْكَ إِذًا كَرَّةٌ خَاسِرَةٌ qālū til'ka idhan karratun khāsiratun ''They said: ''That then will be a return in vain (Losing - With lose.) See 79:10

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِنَّمَا هِيَ زَجْرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ fa-innamā hiya zajratun wāḥidatun Yet it will be only a single shout,

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِنَّمَا هِيَ زَجْرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ fa-innamā hiya zajratun wāḥidatun Indeed, it will be but one shout. See 79:1

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:13 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِنَّمَا هِيَ زَجْرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ fa-innamā hiya zajratun wāḥidatun ''Verily (Refer to: 36:29, 49, 53, 37:19.) , it shall be but a single (violent) blast (Or a cry - or a shaking.) See 79:10

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:14 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِذَا هُمْ بِالسَّاهِرَةِ fa-idhā hum bil-sāhirati and behold, they will be awake.

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:14 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِذَا هُمْ بِالسَّاهِرَةِ fa-idhā hum bil-sāhirati And suddenly they will be (alert) upon the earth's surface. See 79:1

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:14 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِذَا هُمْ بِالسَّاهِرَةِ fa-idhā hum bil-sāhirati ''When lo! they shall (all) be in the awakened state (Refer to: 50:22, 78:40, 75:22.) Said the Holy Prophet: - ''Annas Niyammon Fai'za Maatoo intabaho", i.e., People are asleep, they will awake when they die. To which reference is made in 50:22. (A.P.)

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: هَلْ أَتَىكَ حَدِیْثُ مُوسٰی hal atāka ḥadīthu mūsā Did you receive the story of Moses,

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: هَلْ أَتَىكَ حَدِیْثُ مُوسٰی hal atāka ḥadīthu mūsā Has there reached you the story of Musa?. Has there come to you the story of Musa (79:15). When his Lord called him in the holy valley of Tuwa (79:16). Go to Fir'awn; verily, he has transgressed all bounds (79:17). And say to him: Would you purify yourself? (79:18). "And that I guide you to your Lord, so you should fear Him? (79:19). Then he showed him the great sign (79:20). But he denied and disobeyed (79:21). Then he turned back, striving (79:22). So he gathered and called out (79:23). Saying: "I am your lord, most high (79:24). So Allah seized him with punishing example for the Hereafter and the first (life) (79:25). In this is a lesson for whoever fears (79:26). Mentioning the Story of Musa and that it is a…

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: هَلْ أَتَىكَ حَدِیْثُ مُوسٰی hal atāka ḥadīthu mūsā ''Hath not come unto thee the story (Story of Moses is recollected. Refer to: 20:9 - 20:73.) of Moses? See 79:14

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ نَادَاهُ رَبُّهُ بِالْوَادِ الْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى idh nādāhu rabbuhu bil-wādi l-muqadasi ṭuwan when his Lord called out to him in the holy valley of Ṭuwā?

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ نَادَاهُ رَبُّهُ بِالْوَادِ الْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى idh nādāhu rabbuhu bil-wādi l-muqadasi ṭuwan When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Ṭuwā. See 79:15

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ نَادَاهُ رَبُّهُ بِالْوَادِ الْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى idh nādāhu rabbuhu bil-wādi l-muqadasi ṭuwan ''When called him his Lord in the Holy Valley (called) 'Tuva' (Refer to: 20:12, In a sudden change.) See 79:14

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اِذْهَبْ إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغَى idh'hab ilā fir'ʿawna innahu ṭaghā [And said,] 'Go to Pharaoh, for indeed he has rebelled,

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اِذْهَبْ إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغَى idh'hab ilā fir'ʿawna innahu ṭaghā "Go to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed. See 79:15

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:17 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اِذْهَبْ إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغَى idh'hab ilā fir'ʿawna innahu ṭaghā ''(Saying)-. ''Go thou (O' Moses!) unto Pharaoh (Refer to: 20:24.) ! verily, he hath transgressed the bounds! See 79:14

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:18 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَقُلْ هَلْ لَكَ إِلَى أَنْ تَزَكَّى faqul hal laka ilā an tazakkā and say, "Would you purify yourself?

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:18 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَقُلْ هَلْ لَكَ إِلَى أَنْ تَزَكَّى faqul hal laka ilā an tazakkā And say to him, 'Would you (be willing to) purify yourself. See 79:15

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:18 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَقُلْ هَلْ لَكَ إِلَى أَنْ تَزَكَّى faqul hal laka ilā an tazakkā ''And say (unto him)'. ''Hast thou (Pharaoh.) (a desire) to cleanse thyself (of thy disbelief)? See 79:14

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:19 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَهْدِيَكَ إِلَى رَبِّكَ فَتَخْشٰی wa-ahdiyaka ilā rabbika fatakhshā I will guide you to your Lord, that you may fear [Him]?" '

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:19 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَهْدِيَكَ إِلَى رَبِّكَ فَتَخْشٰی wa-ahdiyaka ilā rabbika fatakhshā And let me guide you to your Lord so you would fear (Him)?'" See 79:15

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:19 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَهْدِيَكَ إِلَى رَبِّكَ فَتَخْشٰی wa-ahdiyaka ilā rabbika fatakhshā ''And I will guide thee unto thy Lord so that thou mayest fear him See 79:14

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:20 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَرَاهُ الْاٰیَةَ الْكُبْرٰی fa-arāhu l-āyata l-kub'rā Then he showed him the greatest sign.

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:20 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَرَاهُ الْاٰیَةَ الْكُبْرٰی fa-arāhu l-āyata l-kub'rā And he showed him the greatest sign.1 See 79:15

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:20 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَرَاهُ الْاٰیَةَ الْكُبْرٰی fa-arāhu l-āyata l-kub'rā ''And he showed him the greatest sign (miracle) (Refer to: 20:20, 22:23, 17:101, 7:133, 20:70, 20:73.) See 79:14

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:21 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَكَذَّبَ وَعَصَى fakadhaba waʿaṣā But he denied, and disobeyed.

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:21 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَكَذَّبَ وَعَصَى fakadhaba waʿaṣā But he (i.e., Pharaoh) denied and disobeyed. See 79:15

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:21 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَكَذَّبَ وَعَصَى fakadhaba waʿaṣā ''But belied he and disobeyed See 79:14

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:22 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ يَسْعَى thumma adbara yasʿā Then he turned back, walking swiftly,

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:22 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ يَسْعَى thumma adbara yasʿā Then he turned his back, striving (i.e., plotting).1 See 79:15

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:22 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ يَسْعَى thumma adbara yasʿā ''Then turned he his back hastily See 79:14

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:23 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَحَشَرَ فَنَادَى faḥashara fanādā and mustered [the people] and proclaimed,

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:23 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَحَشَرَ فَنَادَى faḥashara fanādā And he gathered (his people) and called out. See 79:15

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:23 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَحَشَرَ فَنَادَى faḥashara fanādā ''And gathered (the people) and proclaimed See 79:14

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:24 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَقَالَ أَنَا رَبُّكُمُ الْاَعْلٰی faqāla anā rabbukumu l-aʿlā saying, 'I am your exalted lord!'

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:24 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَقَالَ أَنَا رَبُّكُمُ الْاَعْلٰی faqāla anā rabbukumu l-aʿlā And said, "I am your most exalted lord." See 79:15

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:24 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَقَالَ أَنَا رَبُّكُمُ الْاَعْلٰی faqāla anā rabbukumu l-aʿlā ''And said ''I am your Lord, the most High! See 79:14

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:25 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَخَذَهُ اللَّهُ نَكَالَ الْاٰخِرَةُ وَالْأُولَى fa-akhadhahu l-lahu nakāla l-ākhirati wal-ūlā So Allah seized him with the punishment of this life and the Hereafter.

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:25 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَخَذَهُ اللَّهُ نَكَالَ الْاٰخِرَةُ وَالْأُولَى fa-akhadhahu l-lahu nakāla l-ākhirati wal-ūlā So Allah seized him in exemplary punishment for the last and the first (transgression).1. See 79:15

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:25 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَخَذَهُ اللَّهُ نَكَالَ الْاٰخِرَةُ وَالْأُولَى fa-akhadhahu l-lahu nakāla l-ākhirati wal-ūlā ''So seized him God (Refer to: 20:78, 20:79, 7:135 – 137.) , with the chastisement in the hereafter, and the life before (it) See 79:14

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:26 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ فِي ذٰلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً لِمَنْ يَخْشٰی inna fī dhālika laʿib'ratan liman yakhshā There is indeed a moral in that for someone who fears!

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:26 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ فِي ذٰلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً لِمَنْ يَخْشٰی inna fī dhālika laʿib'ratan liman yakhshā Indeed in that is a lesson (i.e., warning) for whoever would fear (Allah). See 79:15

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:26 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ فِي ذٰلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً لِمَنْ يَخْشٰی inna fī dhālika laʿib'ratan liman yakhshā ''Verily in this there is a lesson unto him who feareth (God). (Refer to: 24:44.) See 79:14

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:27 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ءَأَنْتُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقًا أَمِ السَّمَاءُ بَنَاهَا a-antum ashaddu khalqan ami l-samāu banāhā Is it you whose creation is more prodigious or the sky which He has built?

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:27 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ءَأَنْتُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقًا أَمِ السَّمَاءُ بَنَاهَا a-antum ashaddu khalqan ami l-samāu banāhā Are you a more difficult creation or is the heaven? He (i.e., Allah) constructed it. See 79:15

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:27 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ءَأَنْتُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقًا أَمِ السَّمَاءُ بَنَاهَا a-antum ashaddu khalqan ami l-samāu banāhā ''Are ye the harder to be created, or the heaven which built He (Refer to: 2:29, 41:9 - 41:12.) ? Man is reminded of his insignificant physical position in the universe. When the heavens with all their heavenly bodies will succumb to the will of the Lord and vanish at His will - of what consideration could be man who is nothing more than an insignificant germ in the set-up of the universe.

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:28 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: رَفَعَ سَمْكَهَا فَسَوَّاهَا rafaʿa samkahā fasawwāhā He raised its vault, and fashioned it,

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:28 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: رَفَعَ سَمْكَهَا فَسَوَّاهَا rafaʿa samkahā fasawwāhā He raised its ceiling and proportioned it. See 79:15

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:28 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: رَفَعَ سَمْكَهَا فَسَوَّاهَا rafaʿa samkahā fasawwāhā ''Raised He its heights and established (Put in an established position.) it The mystery of the existence of the heavens and the wonderful heavenly bodies in them, with the perfection in their form and the perfect harmony, with which each one works with the other, was brought into existence by God, and is worked at His will.

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:29 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَغْطَشَ لَيْلَهَا وَأَخْرَجَ ضُحَاهَا wa-aghṭasha laylahā wa-akhraja ḍuḥāhā and darkened its night, and brought forth its day;

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:29 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَغْطَشَ لَيْلَهَا وَأَخْرَجَ ضُحَاهَا wa-aghṭasha laylahā wa-akhraja ḍuḥāhā And He darkened its night and extracted its brightness.1 See 79:15

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:29 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَغْطَشَ لَيْلَهَا وَأَخْرَجَ ضُحَاهَا wa-aghṭasha laylahā wa-akhraja ḍuḥāhā ''And He darkened its night, and brought forth its noon light See 79:28

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:30 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ دَحَاهَا wal-arḍa baʿda dhālika daḥāhā and after that He spread out the earth,

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:30 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ دَحَاهَا wal-arḍa baʿda dhālika daḥāhā And after that He spread the earth. See 79:15

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:30 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ دَحَاهَا wal-arḍa baʿda dhālika daḥāhā ''And the earth, afterwards he stretched forth 'Dab.' here means further expansion1 of its surface long after the creation of the earth and the heavenly bodies. It may refer to the last layer of the earth which produces food for men and the animals. (A.P.)

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:31 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَخْرَجَ مِنْهَا مَاءَهَا وَمَرْعَاهَا akhraja min'hā māahā wamarʿāhā and brought forth from it its water and pastures,

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:31 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَخْرَجَ مِنْهَا مَاءَهَا وَمَرْعَاهَا akhraja min'hā māahā wamarʿāhā He extracted from it its water and its pasture. See 79:15

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:31 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَخْرَجَ مِنْهَا مَاءَهَا وَمَرْعَاهَا akhraja min'hā māahā wamarʿāhā ''He brought forth from it, its waters and its pasteurage The ready supply of water through the underground springs and wells and the wonderful arrangement of rain from heaven and the evaporation of the water from seas; all these are the unquestionable proofs of the Wisdom and Might of the Creator.

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:32 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْجِبَالَ أَرْسَاهَا wal-jibāla arsāhā and set firm the mountains,

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:32 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْجِبَالَ أَرْسَاهَا wal-jibāla arsāhā And the mountains He set firmly. See 79:15

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:32 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْجِبَالَ أَرْسَاهَا wal-jibāla arsāhā ''And the mountains, He set them firm See 79:31

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:33 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَتَاعًا لَكُمْ وَلِأَنْعَامِكُمْ matāʿan lakum wali-anʿāmikum as a [place of] sustenance for you and your livestock.

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:33 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَتَاعًا لَكُمْ وَلِأَنْعَامِكُمْ matāʿan lakum wali-anʿāmikum As enjoyment (i.e., provision) for you and your grazing livestock. See 79:15

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:33 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَتَاعًا لَكُمْ وَلِأَنْعَامِكُمْ matāʿan lakum wali-anʿāmikum ''A provision (Refer to: 80:32.) for you and your cattle See 79:31

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:34 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِذَا جَاءَتِ الطَّامَّةُ الْكُبْرٰی fa-idhā jāati l-ṭāmatu l-kub'rā When the Greatest Catastrophe befalls,

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:34 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِذَا جَاءَتِ الطَّامَّةُ الْكُبْرٰی fa-idhā jāati l-ṭāmatu l-kub'rā But when there comes the greatest Overwhelming Calamity1. But when there comes the Greatest Catastroph (79:34). The Day when man shall remember what he strove for (79:35). And Hell shall be made apparent for whoever sees (79:36). Then for him who transgresse (79:37). And preferred the life of this world (79:38). Verily, his abode will be the Hell (79:39). But as for him who feared standing before his Lord, and forbade himself from desire (79:40). Verily, Paradise will be his abode (79:41). They ask you about the Hour when will be its appointed tim (79:42). What do you have to mention of it (79:43). To your Lord it is limited (79:44). You are only a warner for those who fear it (79:45). The Day they see it (it will be) as if…

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:34 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِذَا جَاءَتِ الطَّامَّةُ الْكُبْرٰی fa-idhā jāati l-ṭāmatu l-kub'rā ''When cometh the Great Calamity. (The day of final Judgment.) See 79:31

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:35 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ يَتَذَكَّرُ الْإِنْسَانُ مَا سَعَى yawma yatadhakkaru l-insānu mā saʿā the day when man will remember his endeavours,

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:35 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ يَتَذَكَّرُ الْإِنْسَانُ مَا سَعَى yawma yatadhakkaru l-insānu mā saʿā The Day when man will remember that for which he strove. See 79:34

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:35 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ يَتَذَكَّرُ الْإِنْسَانُ مَا سَعَى yawma yatadhakkaru l-insānu mā saʿā The day when man shall recollect (This confirms the awakening slate mentioned in Verse 79:14.) (all) that he strove for Every act and motive of evert one, will be laid bare to each individual to account for. This confirms the awakening state referred to in in Verse 79:14 (A.P.).

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:36 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَبُرِّزَتِ الْجَحِيمُ لِمَنْ يَرٰی waburrizati l-jaḥīmu liman yarā and hell is brought into view for one who sees,

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:36 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَبُرِّزَتِ الْجَحِيمُ لِمَنْ يَرٰی waburrizati l-jaḥīmu liman yarā And Hellfire will be exposed for (all) those who see. See 79:34

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:36 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَبُرِّزَتِ الْجَحِيمُ لِمَنْ يَرٰی waburrizati l-jaḥīmu liman yarā And the hell shall be displayed unto him who seeth See 79:35

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:37 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا مَنْ طَغَى fa-ammā man ṭaghā as for him who was rebellious

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:37 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا مَنْ طَغَى fa-ammā man ṭaghā So as for he who transgressed. See 79:34

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:37 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا مَنْ طَغَى fa-ammā man ṭaghā Then, as for him who hath transgressed the bounds Those who wilfully persisted in transgressing the prescribed limits, will have the abiding chastisement and those who were the victims of the common weakness in the human being and who yielded to the human frailty, will have to face the balancing of their evil with their goodness1.

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:38 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَءَاثَرَ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا waāthara l-ḥayata l-dun'yā and preferred the life of this world,

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:38 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَءَاثَرَ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا waāthara l-ḥayata l-dun'yā And preferred the life of the world. See 79:34

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:38 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَءَاثَرَ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا waāthara l-ḥayata l-dun'yā And preferreth the life of this world See 79:37

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:39 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِنَّ الْجَحِيمَ هِيَ الْمَأْوَى fa-inna l-jaḥīma hiya l-mawā his refuge will indeed be hell.

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:39 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِنَّ الْجَحِيمَ هِيَ الْمَأْوَى fa-inna l-jaḥīma hiya l-mawā Then indeed, Hellfire will be (his) refuge. See 79:34

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:39 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِنَّ الْجَحِيمَ هِيَ الْمَأْوَى fa-inna l-jaḥīma hiya l-mawā Then, verily, Hell, that shall be his abode See 79:37

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:40 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ وَنَهَى النَّفْسَ عَنِ الْهَوَى wa-ammā man khāfa maqāma rabbihi wanahā l-nafsa ʿani l-hawā But as for him who is awed to stand before his Lord and forbids the soul from [following] desire,

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:40 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ وَنَهَى النَّفْسَ عَنِ الْهَوَى wa-ammā man khāfa maqāma rabbihi wanahā l-nafsa ʿani l-hawā But as for he who feared the position of his Lord1 and prevented the soul from (unlawful) inclination. See 79:34

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:40 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ وَنَهَى النَّفْسَ عَنِ الْهَوَى wa-ammā man khāfa maqāma rabbihi wanahā l-nafsa ʿani l-hawā And as for him who feareth the standing (The justice.) of his Lord, and forbiddeth (his) self from (following) his inclinations (Submitting to God's will.) Note the key to heaven and the blissful life therein, has been shown and that is the control of the self and refraining from low desires, abstaining from the forbidden.

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:41 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِنَّ الْجَنَّةَ هِيَ الْمَأْوَى fa-inna l-janata hiya l-mawā his refuge will indeed be paradise.

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:41 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِنَّ الْجَنَّةَ هِيَ الْمَأْوَى fa-inna l-janata hiya l-mawā Then indeed, Paradise will be (his) refuge. See 79:34

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:41 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِنَّ الْجَنَّةَ هِيَ الْمَأْوَى fa-inna l-janata hiya l-mawā Then, verily, the Garden (of Paradise), that shall be his abode See 79:40

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:42 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَسْءَلُونَكَ عَنِ السَّاعَةِ أَيَّانَ مُرْسَاهَا yasalūnaka ʿani l-sāʿati ayyāna mur'sāhā They ask you concerning the Hour, "When will it set in,

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:42 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَسْءَلُونَكَ عَنِ السَّاعَةِ أَيَّانَ مُرْسَاهَا yasalūnaka ʿani l-sāʿati ayyāna mur'sāhā They ask you, (O Muḥammad), about the Hour: when is its arrival?1 See 79:34

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:42 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَسْءَلُونَكَ عَنِ السَّاعَةِ أَيَّانَ مُرْسَاهَا yasalūnaka ʿani l-sāʿati ayyāna mur'sāhā They ask thee of 'the Hour' whereto (is) anchorage (Refer to: 53:42, 7:187.) ? See 79:40

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:43 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيمَ أَنْتَ مِنْ ذِكْرَاهَا fīma anta min dhik'rāhā considering your frequent mention of it?"

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:43 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيمَ أَنْتَ مِنْ ذِكْرَاهَا fīma anta min dhik'rāhā In what (position) are you that you should mention it?1 See 79:34

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:43 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيمَ أَنْتَ مِنْ ذِكْرَاهَا fīma anta min dhik'rāhā Wherein art thou of its notion (You are far away from grasping its ultimate significance. Refer to: 11:107, 11:108.) ? The time limit in terms of the state of existence after life or on the Day of Judgment, is quite different from that of our calculation in the present life. God alone knows the extent or its duration. The whole matter lies in the will of the Lord1. You are far away from grasping its ultimate significance. (A.P.)

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:44 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِلَى رَبِّكَ مُنْتَهَاهَا ilā rabbika muntahāhā Its outcome is with your Lord.

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:44 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِلَى رَبِّكَ مُنْتَهَاهَا ilā rabbika muntahāhā To your Lord is its finality.1 See 79:34

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:44 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِلَى رَبِّكَ مُنْتَهَاهَا ilā rabbika muntahāhā Unto thy Lord (alone) is its termination! The duty of an apostle of God ends with warning those who want to avail of the message and the admonition. No apostle of God is responsible for the conduct and character of the people. It indicates that the whole system of universe is in motion and in the state of ever becoming. It is He to Whom the motion terminates. There is nothing in the whole system of the Universe to be termed eternal. Hence 'Hudoose Zamani al-Aalam', i.e., The universe being as a whole and past being created from naught. (A.P.)

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:45 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ مُنْذِرُ مَنْ يَخْشَاهَا innamā anta mundhiru man yakhshāhā You are only a warner for those who fear it.

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:45 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ مُنْذِرُ مَنْ يَخْشَاهَا innamā anta mundhiru man yakhshāhā You are only a warner for those who fear it. See 79:34

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:45 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ مُنْذِرُ مَنْ يَخْشَاهَا innamā anta mundhiru man yakhshāhā Thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) art only a Warner unto him who feareth it None knows the extent of the passage of time1.

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:46 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: كَأَنَّهُمْ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَهَا لَمْ يَلْبَثُوْۤا إِلَّا عَشِيَّةً أَوْ ضُحَاهَا ka-annahum yawma yarawnahā lam yalbathū illā ʿashiyyatan aw ḍuḥāhā The day they see it, it shall be as if they had not stayed [in the world] except for an evening or forenoon.

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:46 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: كَأَنَّهُمْ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَهَا لَمْ يَلْبَثُوْۤا إِلَّا عَشِيَّةً أَوْ ضُحَاهَا ka-annahum yawma yarawnahā lam yalbathū illā ʿashiyyatan aw ḍuḥāhā It will be, on the Day they see it,1 as though they had not remained (in the world) except for an afternoon or a morning thereof. See 79:34

item.title: An-Naazi'aat:46 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: كَأَنَّهُمْ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَهَا لَمْ يَلْبَثُوْۤا إِلَّا عَشِيَّةً أَوْ ضُحَاهَا ka-annahum yawma yarawnahā lam yalbathū illā ʿashiyyatan aw ḍuḥāhā It shall seem unto them, on the day when they see it, as though they tarried not in (their graves) but a (single) evening, or the following morning (Refer to: 10:45.) Refers to the last state of the awakening when the conscious self gets out of the bounds, time and space, the whole system of the four-dimensional state will appear to him and even less than a part of an ordinary day - to which Eqbal says: Referring to the stars addressing man - saying ''Thy century unto Us is only a moment and thine Ocean unto Us is only a drop. We are seeing and passing". Qur'an says the day shall come - man will be in a position to say…

item.title: An-Naba:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: عَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ ʿamma yatasāalūna What is it about which they question each other?!

item.title: An-Naba:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: عَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ ʿamma yatasāalūna About what are they asking one another? وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفَافًا And gardens that are Alfaf. Ibn 'Abbas and other said, "Alfaf means gathered." This is similar to Allah's statement: وَفِي الْأَرْضِ قِطَعٌ مُّتَجَاوِرَاتٌ وَجَنَّاتٌ مِّنْ أَعْنَابٍ وَزَرْعٌ وَنَخِيلٌ صِنْوَانٌ وَغَيْرُ صِنْوَانٍ يُسْقَىٰ بِمَاءٍ وَاحِدٍ وَنُفَضِّلُ بَعْضَهَا عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ فِي الْأُكُلِ ۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ And in the earth are neighboring tracts, and gardens of vines, and green crops, and date palms, growing into two or three from a single stem root, or otherwise, watered with the same water; yet some of them We make more excellent than others to eat. Verily, in these things there are Ayat for the people who understand. (13:4)

item.title: An-Naba:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: عَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ ʿamma yatasāalūna ''Of what ask they one another? 'Naba' al-Adheem' announcement of great importance - Some say it is the apostleship of the Holy Prophet about which the people differed in their views, for some said he was an apostle of God, while the others said he was a sorcerer and some others said he was a mad man. Some say, it is the announcement about the Day of Judgment. Some commentators say it is the Holy Qur'an1. Hafiz Abu Nayeem a Sunni Scholar in his book Hulyat al-Aulia says that the Holy Prophet said that by 'Naba' al-Adheem' is meant Ali Ibn Abu Talib and his succession to Apostolic office as the First Imam or the divinely chosen 'Guide' which fact was announced in Ghadir Khumm about which the people differed. The Fifth Holy Imam Muhammad Ibn…

item.title: An-Naba:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: عَنِ النَّبَإِ الْعَظِيمِ ʿani l-naba-i l-ʿaẓīmi [Is it] about the great tiding,

item.title: An-Naba:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: عَنِ النَّبَإِ الْعَظِيمِ ʿani l-naba-i l-ʿaẓīmi About the great news1. See 78:1

item.title: An-Naba:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: عَنِ النَّبَإِ الْعَظِيمِ ʿani l-naba-i l-ʿaẓīmi ''Of the Great News (Refer to Verses 6:67, 38:67.) See 78:1

item.title: An-Naba:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي هُمْ فِیْهِ مُخْتَلِفُونَ alladhī hum fīhi mukh'talifūna the one about which they differ?

item.title: An-Naba:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي هُمْ فِیْهِ مُخْتَلِفُونَ alladhī hum fīhi mukh'talifūna That over which they are in disagreement. See 78:1

item.title: An-Naba:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي هُمْ فِیْهِ مُخْتَلِفُونَ alladhī hum fīhi mukh'talifūna ''That which they therein differ This verse clarifies the meaning further. It is an undeniable historic fact that it was the announcement of the succession of Ali to the Holy Prophet made at Ghadir Khumm with which the people differed the most and also doubted if what the Holy Prophet did, was in fact at God's command or at his own instance out of his love for Ali1. Relating the instance of Harith Ibn Nu'man al-Qahri questioning the Holy Prophet about the announcement he made at Ghadir about Ali and how he, at his own choice received the wrath of God2. What is said in this verse about the great announcement is true for even to this day the announcement made by the Holy Prophet about Ali succeeding him, is still the…

item.title: An-Naba:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ kallā sayaʿlamūna No indeed! They will soon know!

item.title: An-Naba:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ kallā sayaʿlamūna No! They are going to know. See 78:1

item.title: An-Naba:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ kallā sayaʿlamūna ''Verily! they shall soon come to know See 78:3

item.title: An-Naba:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ thumma kallā sayaʿlamūna Again, no indeed! They will soon know!

item.title: An-Naba:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ thumma kallā sayaʿlamūna Then, no! They are going to know. See 78:1

item.title: An-Naba:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ thumma kallā sayaʿlamūna ''Verily, Verily, they shall soon come to know See 78:3

item.title: An-Naba:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ مِهَادًا alam najʿali l-arḍa mihādan Did We not make the earth a resting place?

item.title: An-Naba:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ مِهَادًا alam najʿali l-arḍa mihādan Have We not made the earth a resting place? See 78:1

item.title: An-Naba:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ مِهَادًا alam najʿali l-arḍa mihādan ''What! Made We not the earth a wide expanse (A preparatory ground - Refers to the surface of the earth on which things develop. (A.P.).) ? Refers to the surface of the earth on which things develop. (A.P.)

item.title: An-Naba:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًا wal-jibāla awtādan and the mountains stakes?

item.title: An-Naba:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًا wal-jibāla awtādan And the mountains as stakes?1 See 78:1

item.title: An-Naba:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًا wal-jibāla awtādan ''And the mountains as bolts (Refer to Verses 13:3, 41:10.) ? The existence of lofty mountains effects in changing the course of earthquake1. (A.P.)

item.title: An-Naba:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَخَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا wakhalaqnākum azwājan and create you in pairs?1

item.title: An-Naba:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَخَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا wakhalaqnākum azwājan And We created you in pairs. See 78:1

item.title: An-Naba:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَخَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا wakhalaqnākum azwājan ''And We created you in pairs See 78:7

item.title: An-Naba:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًا wajaʿalnā nawmakum subātan and make your sleep for rest?

item.title: An-Naba:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًا wajaʿalnā nawmakum subātan And made your sleep (a means for) rest. See 78:1

item.title: An-Naba:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًا wajaʿalnā nawmakum subātan ''And cause your sleep a rest See 78:7

item.title: An-Naba:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا wajaʿalnā al-layla libāsan and make the night a covering?

item.title: An-Naba:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا wajaʿalnā al-layla libāsan And made the night as clothing.1 See 78:1

item.title: An-Naba:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا wajaʿalnā al-layla libāsan ''And caused the night a covering See 78:7

item.title: An-Naba:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا النَّهَارَ مَعَاشًا wajaʿalnā l-nahāra maʿāshan and make the day for livelihood?

item.title: An-Naba:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا النَّهَارَ مَعَاشًا wajaʿalnā l-nahāra maʿāshan And made the day for livelihood. See 78:1

item.title: An-Naba:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا النَّهَارَ مَعَاشًا wajaʿalnā l-nahāra maʿāshan ''And caused the day for (your) seeking livelihood See 78:7

item.title: An-Naba:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًا شِدَادًا wabanaynā fawqakum sabʿan shidādan and build above you the seven mighty heavens?

item.title: An-Naba:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًا شِدَادًا wabanaynā fawqakum sabʿan shidādan And constructed above you seven strong (heavens). See 78:1

item.title: An-Naba:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًا شِدَادًا wabanaynā fawqakum sabʿan shidādan ''And We have erected above you the seven (Refer to: 23:17, 65:12, 71:15, 67:3.) strong ones Meaning1 strongly fixed in a fixed systematic constitution, without any defect or without any weakness to give way to any failure. May refer the seven planets above the earth in comparison to their distance to the sun and it may also refer to the seven non-physical spheres beyond the material and the starred realms. (A.P.)

item.title: An-Naba:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا سِرَاجًا وَهَّاجًا wajaʿalnā sirājan wahhājan and make [the sun for] a radiant lamp?

item.title: An-Naba:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا سِرَاجًا وَهَّاجًا wajaʿalnā sirājan wahhājan And made (therein) a burning lamp. See 78:1

item.title: An-Naba:13 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا سِرَاجًا وَهَّاجًا wajaʿalnā sirājan wahhājan ''And We made therein a lamp (The Sun.) burning Reference is to the sun in the centre of the solar system1. This is a metaphorical reference to the Holy Prophet.

item.title: An-Naba:14 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنْزَلْنَا مِنَ الْمُعْصِرَاتِ مَاءً ثَجَّاجًا wa-anzalnā mina l-muʿ'ṣirāti māan thajjājan and send down water pouring from the rain-clouds,

item.title: An-Naba:14 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنْزَلْنَا مِنَ الْمُعْصِرَاتِ مَاءً ثَجَّاجًا wa-anzalnā mina l-muʿ'ṣirāti māan thajjājan And sent down from the rain clouds pouring water. See 78:1

item.title: An-Naba:14 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنْزَلْنَا مِنَ الْمُعْصِرَاتِ مَاءً ثَجَّاجًا wa-anzalnā mina l-muʿ'ṣirāti māan thajjājan ''And send We down from the clouds water in torrents 'Mo'sirat' the State when the cloud is transformed from a vapour into a liquid shower by the pressure of the temperature - Squeezing. (A.P.)

item.title: An-Naba:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لِنُخْرِجَ بِهِ حَبًّا وَنَبَاتًا linukh'rija bihi ḥabban wanabātan that with it We may bring forth grains and plants,

item.title: An-Naba:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لِنُخْرِجَ بِهِ حَبًّا وَنَبَاتًا linukh'rija bihi ḥabban wanabātan That We may bring forth thereby grain and vegetation. See 78:1

item.title: An-Naba:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لِنُخْرِجَ بِهِ حَبًّا وَنَبَاتًا linukh'rija bihi ḥabban wanabātan ''That We may bring forth by it, corn and herbs See 78:14

item.title: An-Naba:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفَافًا wajannātin alfāfan and luxuriant gardens?

item.title: An-Naba:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفَافًا wajannātin alfāfan And gardens of entwined growth. See 78:1

item.title: An-Naba:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفَافًا wajannātin alfāfan ''And gardens of thick foliage See 78:14

item.title: An-Naba:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ كَانَ مِيقَاتًا inna yawma l-faṣli kāna mīqātan Indeed the Day of Judgement is the tryst,

item.title: An-Naba:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ كَانَ مِيقَاتًا inna yawma l-faṣli kāna mīqātan Indeed, the Day of Judgement is an appointed time. Verily, the Day of Decision is a fixed time (78:17). The Day when the Trumpet will be blown, and you shall come forth in crowds (78:18). And the heaven shall be opened, and it will become as gates (78:19).
