item.description: إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ مُحْسِنُونَ inna l-laha maʿa alladhīna ittaqaw wa-alladhīna hum muḥ'sinūna Indeed Allah is with those who are Godwary and those who are virtuous.

item.title: An-Nahl:128 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ مُحْسِنُونَ inna l-laha maʿa alladhīna ittaqaw wa-alladhīna hum muḥ'sinūna Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good. See 16:126

item.title: An-Nahl:128 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ مُحْسِنُونَ inna l-laha maʿa alladhīna ittaqaw wa-alladhīna hum muḥ'sinūna Verily God is with those who guard (themselves against evil), and those who do good (to others). See 16:126

item.title: An-Najm:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالنَّجْمِ إِذَا هَوَى wal-najmi idhā hawā By the star when it sets:1

item.title: An-Najm:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالنَّجْمِ إِذَا هَوَى wal-najmi idhā hawā By the star when it descends. إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا وَحْيٌ يُوحَىٰ It is only a revelation revealed. Which is means, he only conveys to the people what he was commanded to convey, in its entirety without additions or deletions. Imam Ahmad recorded that Abu Umamah said that he heard the Messenger of Allah SAW say: لَيَدْخُلَنَّ الْجَنَّةَ بِشَفَاعَةِ رَجُلٍ لَيْسَ بِنَبِيٍّ مِثْلُ الْحَيَّيْنِ - أَوْ مِثْلُ أَحَدِ الْحَيَّيْنِ - رَبِيعَةَ وَمُضَرَ Verily, numbers similar to the two tribes, or one of them, Rabi'ah and Mudar, will enter Paradise on account of the intercession of one man, who is not a Prophet. A man asked, "O Allah's Messenger! Is not Rabi'ah a subtribe of Mudar." The Prophet SAW said: إِنَّمَا أَقُولُ مَا أَقُولُ I said what I said. Imam Ahmad recorded that 'Abdullah bin 'Amr…

item.title: An-Najm:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالنَّجْمِ إِذَا هَوَى wal-najmi idhā hawā By the star when it goeth down Verses 1 to 8 assert the infallibility of the Holy Prophet in his movements between the Creator and the creation, similar to the movement of the star in its orbit. It negates any mistake or deviation in action or uttering anything other than what is revealed. It refers to his attaining the realisation and the stage of the realisation he had reached. The first stage of realisation he reached, is the stage of 'Istawa' in the highest horizon which is the highest stage of the angelical force, at which appear the two arcs, the arc of godhead and the arc of creation to meet. Then moving further beyond the dualistic view, assuming the state of pending between the finite and the infinite as the joining point between…

item.title: An-Najm:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا ضَلَّ صَاحِبُكُمْ وَمَا غَوَى mā ḍalla ṣāḥibukum wamā ghawā your companion1 has neither gone astray, nor gone amiss.

item.title: An-Najm:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا ضَلَّ صَاحِبُكُمْ وَمَا غَوَى mā ḍalla ṣāḥibukum wamā ghawā Your companion (i.e., Muḥammad) has not strayed, nor has he erred. See 53:1

item.title: An-Najm:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا ضَلَّ صَاحِبُكُمْ وَمَا غَوَى mā ḍalla ṣāḥibukum wamā ghawā Erreth not your Companion (Our Apostle Muhammad) nor is he led astray (Refer to Verses 4:113; 93:7.) 'Sahib' meaning companion, i.e., The Holy Prophet - he is addressed as such for his living among the people along with them in the same place. The negation about his going astray or deviating from the right path or uttering anything of his own inclination and the assertion of his being directly under the revelation, is not restricted to any particular age or period or any particular aspect of his life but starts from his very pregenetal state to which fact bears testimony and evidence the statement of Abu Talib, the uncle of the Holy Prophet and the father of 'Ali in one of his eulogical verses addressed to the Holy Prophet while…

item.title: An-Najm:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا يَنْطِقُ عَنِ الْهَوَى wamā yanṭiqu ʿani l-hawā Nor does he speak out of [his own] desire:

item.title: An-Najm:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا يَنْطِقُ عَنِ الْهَوَى wamā yanṭiqu ʿani l-hawā Nor does he speak from (his own) inclination. See 53:1

item.title: An-Najm:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا يَنْطِقُ عَنِ الْهَوَى wamā yanṭiqu ʿani l-hawā And nor he speaketh of (his own) inclination (The Holy Prophet.) This unique quality of the godly truthfulness. Everything of the utterance of the Holy Prophet has been referred to while Moses was told by God about the advent of his Apostle (Muhammad)1, and a similar prophecy did Jesus make to his followers, before his departure from the informing of the advent of the Comforter, the Spirit of Truth and the Holy Ghost. "I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee, and will put my words in his mouth: and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him." Deut. 18/18. "Howbeit when he, the Spirit of Truth, is come, he null guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself,…

item.title: An-Najm:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا وَحْيٌ يُوحَى in huwa illā waḥyun yūḥā it is just a revelation that is revealed [to him],

item.title: An-Najm:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا وَحْيٌ يُوحَى in huwa illā waḥyun yūḥā It is not but a revelation revealed. See 53:1

item.title: An-Najm:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا وَحْيٌ يُوحَى in huwa illā waḥyun yūḥā It (the wording) (His speech.) is naught but a revelation revealed (unto him) (Refer to Verse 10:15.) See 53:3

item.title: An-Najm:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: عَلَّمَهُ شَدِيدُ الْقُوَى ʿallamahu shadīdu l-quwā taught him by One of great powers,

item.title: An-Najm:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: عَلَّمَهُ شَدِيدُ الْقُوَى ʿallamahu shadīdu l-quwā Taught to him by one intense in strength (i.e., Jibril). He has been taught by one mighty in power (53:5). Dhu Mirrah then he Istawa (53:6). While he was in the highest part of the horizon (53:7). Then he approached and came closer (53:8). And was at a distance of two bows' length or less (53:9). So (Allah) revealed to His servant whatever He revealed (53:10). The heart lied not in what he saw (53:11). Will you then dispute with him about what he saw (53:12). And indeed he saw him at a second descent (53:13). Near Sidrat Al-Muntaha (53:14). Near it is the Paradise of Abode (53:15). When that covered the lote tree which did cover it (53:16). The sight turned not aside, nor it transgressed beyond the limit (53:17). Indeed he saw…

item.title: An-Najm:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: عَلَّمَهُ شَدِيدُ الْقُوَى ʿallamahu shadīdu l-quwā Taught him the (No one else.) one Intense in power (Refer to Verse 81:20.) 'Allamaho', i.e., 'Taught him', i.e., he revealed to him who is endowed with mighty' power by God, i.e., the Angel Gabriel - meaning the Holy Qur'an is no poetry composed - no stories compiled by the Holy Prophet but the Word of God which has been conveyed to him by the Angel being the nearest of God, 'Mighty in Power' compared to the others of his kind1. Shadid al-Quwa, "the supreme in power", is Allah. To translate and interpret it as the angel Jibrail is to belie the verses 30 to 38 of Baqarah2 and verse 75 of Sad, because Jibrail was one of the angels who prostrated themselves before Adam when Adam taught them "the names" they did not…

item.title: An-Najm:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ذُو مِرَّةٍ فَاسْتَوَى dhū mirratin fa-is'tawā possessed of sound judgement.1 He2 settled,3

item.title: An-Najm:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ذُو مِرَّةٍ فَاسْتَوَى dhū mirratin fa-is'tawā One of soundness.1 And he rose to (his) true form.2 See 53:5

item.title: An-Najm:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ذُو مِرَّةٍ فَاسْتَوَى dhū mirratin fa-is'tawā The one endued with wisdom; (and) hence he (The Holy Prophet.) took an overviewing position This verse refers to the 'Mi'raj,' i.e., Ascension of the Holy Prophet into the heavens and him meeting the Angel Gabriel in his full form of his wonderful strength. For all the details of the Ascension, Mi'raj, see the commentary of Bani Israil 17:1. The Holy Prophet held in view the entire universe from the highest position, where he found Jibrail. Then the Holy Prophet drew near to Allah "till a distance of two bows or still nearer" The nearness described by "still nearer" cannot be imagined by human mind. It is the nearest nearness possible between the finite and the infinite. Arabic idiom qaba qawsayn indicate extreme nearness. "The drawn bows, with their chords touching," make a circle…

item.title: An-Najm:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهُوَ بِالْأُفُقِ الْاَعْلٰی wahuwa bil-ufuqi l-aʿlā while he was on the highest horizon.

item.title: An-Najm:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهُوَ بِالْأُفُقِ الْاَعْلٰی wahuwa bil-ufuqi l-aʿlā While he was in the higher (part of the) horizon.1 See 53:5

item.title: An-Najm:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهُوَ بِالْأُفُقِ الْاَعْلٰی wahuwa bil-ufuqi l-aʿlā While he was in the highest horizon Gabriel was found in the highest part of the heavens and power. At this place the Holy Prophet heard a Voice - he asked the Angel Gabriel who was with him as what the Voice was - the Angel replied that it is Lord's prayer or blessing which was - 'Subboohun Quddoos Ana Rabbul-Malaikato War Rooh-Sabaqat-Ramati Ghazabi' - Hallowed and Holy - 'I am the Lord of the 'Malaika' and the Spirit. My Merry dominates My Wrath.' (A.P.)

item.title: An-Najm:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ دَنَا فَتَدَلَّى thumma danā fatadallā Then he drew nearer and nearer

item.title: An-Najm:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ دَنَا فَتَدَلَّى thumma danā fatadallā Then he approached and descended. See 53:5

item.title: An-Najm:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ دَنَا فَتَدَلَّى thumma danā fatadallā Then he drew nigh, and became pending (Refer to Verse 17:1.) The Holy Prophet drew nearer and nearer to Him - a reference to the 'Mi'raj' (Ascension) of the Holy Prophet and his reaching the nearest point of approach possible for any mortal. The Holy Prophet was drawn nearer and still nearer to the All-Divine Lord. In between the creation and the Creator, i.e., the finite and the infinite (A.P.).

item.title: An-Najm:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَكَانَ قَابَ قَوْسَيْنِ أَوْ أَدْنَى fakāna qāba qawsayni aw adnā until he was within two bows' length or even nearer,

item.title: An-Najm:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَكَانَ قَابَ قَوْسَيْنِ أَوْ أَدْنَى fakāna qāba qawsayni aw adnā And was at a distance of two bow lengths or nearer. See 53:5

item.title: An-Najm:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَكَانَ قَابَ قَوْسَيْنِ أَوْ أَدْنَى fakāna qāba qawsayni aw adnā Thus was (he) the measure between two bows (facing each other) or nigher still (In between the creation and the Creator i.e. between the finite and the infinite (A.P.). Refer to Verse 17:1.) A reference to the highest state of communion with God granted to the Holy Prophet. Note the beautiful illustration given to the maximum communion with God which the Holy Prophet was granted. The measure or the distance of two bows, to mean that when the two bows meet, they meet at their ends but still they are away from each other on all points of their body. It could never mean' that the Holy Prophet was totally absorbed into divinity and yet bodily as is mortal, he was separate from God. It must be remembered that the…

item.title: An-Najm:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَوْحَى إِلَى عَبْدِهِ مَا أَوْحَى fa-awḥā ilā ʿabdihi mā awḥā whereat He revealed to His servant whatever He revealed.

item.title: An-Najm:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَوْحَى إِلَى عَبْدِهِ مَا أَوْحَى fa-awḥā ilā ʿabdihi mā awḥā And he revealed to His Servant1 what he revealed (i.e., conveyed). See 53:5

item.title: An-Najm:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَوْحَى إِلَى عَبْدِهِ مَا أَوْحَى fa-awḥā ilā ʿabdihi mā awḥā Then revealed He unto His Servant what He did reveal The tone of the statement clearly says that which transpired between God and the Select Servant and the Chosen One of His Apostles, i.e., the Holy Prophet, during the State of the maximum communion with the Lord, none could ever know it.

item.title: An-Najm:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا كَذَبَ الْفُؤَادُ مَا رَأَى mā kadhaba l-fuādu mā raā The heart did not deny what it saw.

item.title: An-Najm:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا كَذَبَ الْفُؤَادُ مَا رَأَى mā kadhaba l-fuādu mā raā The heart1 did not lie (about) what it saw. See 53:5

item.title: An-Najm:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا كَذَبَ الْفُؤَادُ مَا رَأَى mā kadhaba l-fuādu mā raā Belied not (his) heart what he saw (In his state of Ascension (A.P.).) What the Holy Prophet said about his seeing the angel Gabriel in his full stature of Strength and power, was not a lie. This does not at all indicate his seeing God with his physical eyes, for the physical eyes can see only physical matter or material things and God is not matter but the Creator of matter. God being only the Absolute Truth that is active in everything, everywhere, an infinite existence, no finite being can ever view the infinite One. What the Holy Prophet saw in the heaven, he saw only the manifestation of His glory and power. No doubt the things of greater glory of God, in His Kingdom in the heavens would naturally…

item.title: An-Najm:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَتُمَارُونَهُ عَلَى مَا يَرٰی afatumārūnahu ʿalā mā yarā Will you then dispute with him about what he saw?!

item.title: An-Najm:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَتُمَارُونَهُ عَلَى مَا يَرٰی afatumārūnahu ʿalā mā yarā So will you dispute with him over what he saw? See 53:5

item.title: An-Najm:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَتُمَارُونَهُ عَلَى مَا يَرٰی afatumārūnahu ʿalā mā yarā What! Dispute ye then with him as to what he saw? It is an interrogatory address to those who disbelieved in what the Holy Prophet related about his experiences in the heavens, during his Ascension - Journey.

item.title: An-Najm:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ رَاٰهُ نَزْلَةً أُخْرٰی walaqad raāhu nazlatan ukh'rā Certainly he saw it1 yet another time,

item.title: An-Najm:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ رَاٰهُ نَزْلَةً أُخْرٰی walaqad raāhu nazlatan ukh'rā And he certainly saw him in another descent.1 See 53:5

item.title: An-Najm:13 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ رَاٰهُ نَزْلَةً أُخْرٰی walaqad raāhu nazlatan ukh'rā And indeed he (The Holy Prophet.) did see him (Archangel Gabriel.) at another descent (The last but one height in Heaven) The Holy Prophet saw Gabriel for a second time.

item.title: An-Najm:14 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: عِنْدَ سِدْرَةِ الْمُنْتَهَى ʿinda sid'rati l-muntahā by the Lote Tree of the Ultimate Boundary,

item.title: An-Najm:14 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: عِنْدَ سِدْرَةِ الْمُنْتَهَى ʿinda sid'rati l-muntahā At the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary. See 53:5

item.title: An-Najm:14 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: عِنْدَ سِدْرَةِ الْمُنْتَهَى ʿinda sid'rati l-muntahā At the 'Sidra' (Overshadowing.) (the Lotetree) 'Muntaha' (the all-Comprehensive Terminus) (Refer to Verses 34:16; 56:28.) The second time the Holy Prophet saw Gabriel, was at the 'Sidratul-Muntaha' the point where ends or stops all knowledge of every one - and no one's knowledge crosses the limit. It is said that when the Holy Prophet reached the point of 'Sidrat ul-Muntaha', Gabriel said "I shall not step an inch further from this." The Holy Prophet passed that point also and what is mentioned in verse 8, 9 & 10 above is what happened after crossing this point when Gabriel had stopped away. There is the mention of the Lote-tree in verses 34:16 and 56:28 as symbolic of the heavenly bliss. But the mention of it here, is a symbol marking the extreme bounds or the…

item.title: An-Najm:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: عِنْدَهَا جَنَّةُ الْمَأْوَى ʿindahā jannatu l-mawā near which is the Garden of the Abode,

item.title: An-Najm:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: عِنْدَهَا جَنَّةُ الْمَأْوَى ʿindahā jannatu l-mawā Near it is the Garden of Refuge (i.e., Paradise). See 53:5

item.title: An-Najm:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: عِنْدَهَا جَنَّةُ الْمَأْوَى ʿindahā jannatu l-mawā Nigh unto it is the Garden-Abode (Paradise, Heavenly adobe of Bliss.) The garden or Paradise or the blissful region near the Sidra is the abode of the pious ones - and some say, it is the place of the highest resort for all angels also.

item.title: An-Najm:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ يَغْشٰی السِّدْرَةَ مَا يَغْشٰی idh yaghshā l-sid'rata mā yaghshā when there covered the Lote Tree what covered it.

item.title: An-Najm:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ يَغْشٰی السِّدْرَةَ مَا يَغْشٰی idh yaghshā l-sid'rata mā yaghshā When there covered the Lote Tree that which covered (it).1 See 53:5

item.title: An-Najm:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ يَغْشٰی السِّدْرَةَ مَا يَغْشٰی idh yaghshā l-sid'rata mā yaghshā When covereth (over) the 'Sidra' (Tree) that which covereth it After reaching the point of Sidra, the realities of the Kingdom of God beyond the point unveiled, i.e., the Holy Prophet was made to visualise the kingdom beyond Sidra which none else besides God has the knowledge of it.

item.title: An-Najm:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا زَاغَ الْبَصَرُ وَمَا طَغَى mā zāgha l-baṣaru wamā ṭaghā The gaze did not swerve, nor did it overstep the bounds.

item.title: An-Najm:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا زَاغَ الْبَصَرُ وَمَا طَغَى mā zāgha l-baṣaru wamā ṭaghā The sight (of the Prophet SAW) did not swerve, nor did it transgress (its limit). See 53:5

item.title: An-Najm:17 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا زَاغَ الْبَصَرُ وَمَا طَغَى mā zāgha l-baṣaru wamā ṭaghā Neither his eye did dazzle nor did it rebel (There was no visual delusion nor any nor any intellectual or emotional disturbance.) In spite of the things around made manifest, being full of marvel and wonder, the Holy Prophet's gaze was only towards the manifest Glory of the Lord and never even cast his glance on anything around him, nor did his eye or his sight or attention was so much engrossed in view the glory of the Lord that it did not care to turn towards anything of his environment though everything was full of marvels and wonder. This is only the skeleton of the great event each expression here has its mystic meaning see note by (A.P.) below. There was no visual delusion nor any physical disturbance. (A.P.)

item.title: An-Najm:18 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَقَدْ رَأَى مِنْ اٰیٰتِ رَبِّهِ الْكُبْرٰی laqad raā min āyāti rabbihi l-kub'rā Certainly he saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord.

item.title: An-Najm:18 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَقَدْ رَأَى مِنْ اٰیٰتِ رَبِّهِ الْكُبْرٰی laqad raā min āyāti rabbihi l-kub'rā He certainly saw of the greatest signs of his Lord. See 53:5

item.title: An-Najm:18 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَقَدْ رَأَى مِنْ اٰیٰتِ رَبِّهِ الْكُبْرٰی laqad raā min āyāti rabbihi l-kub'rā Indeed he did see of the greatest signs of his Lord Let not any misleading idea pollute our faith that it is in the highest heaven that God lives or His existence is found only there, for it is not in the sense of any physical space but it is to denote the excellence or the degree of the special manifestation of His Higher glory, otherwise His 'Arsh' or the Throne of lbs authority and glory extends over the heavens and the earth1. Of all the Apostles of God, it was only Moses whom only the prefigurement of the divine effulgence on earth took place. See 20:10 - 20:14, 20:28 - 20:30 and Exodus here below: "Now Moses kept the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of…

item.title: An-Najm:19 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَرَءَيْتُمُ اللَّاتَ وَالْعُزَّى afara-aytumu l-lāta wal-ʿuzā Have you considered Lāt and 'Uzzā?

item.title: An-Najm:19 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَرَءَيْتُمُ اللَّاتَ وَالْعُزَّى afara-aytumu l-lāta wal-ʿuzā So have you considered al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā? Have you then considered Al-Lat, and Al-'Uzza (53:19). And Manat, the other third (53:20). Is it for you the males and for Him the females (53:21). That indeed is a division most unfair (53:22). They are but names which you have named - you and your fathers - for which Allah has sent down no authority. They follow but a guess and that which they themselves desire, whereas there has surely come to them the guidance from their Lord (53:23). Or shall man have what he wishes (53:24). But to Allah belongs the last (Hereafter) and the first (the world) (53:25). And there are many angels in the heavens, whose intercession will avail nothing, except after Allah has given leave for whom He wills and is pleased…

item.title: An-Najm:19 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَرَءَيْتُمُ اللَّاتَ وَالْعُزَّى afara-aytumu l-lāta wal-ʿuzā See ye then (the idols) Lat and the Uzza ? When the Holy Prophet was reciting this Sura, a voice was heard reciting "There are the lofty idols, verily their intercession is sought", to disturb the recital of the Sura and to put the audience into confusion but the whole context goes against this insertion1 (A.P.).

item.title: An-Najm:20 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَنَوةَ الثَّالِثَةَ الْأُخْرٰی wamanata l-thālithata l-ukh'rā and Manāt, the third one?

item.title: An-Najm:20 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَنَوةَ الثَّالِثَةَ الْأُخْرٰی wamanata l-thālithata l-ukh'rā And Manāt, the third - the other one?1 See 53:19

item.title: An-Najm:20 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَنَوةَ الثَّالِثَةَ الْأُخْرٰی wamanata l-thālithata l-ukh'rā And Manat, the third (idol) besides? (This and the following Verses are in immediate refutation of the confusing satanic insertion (A.P.).) See 53:19

item.title: An-Najm:21 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَكُمُ الذَّكَرُ وَلَهُ الْأُنْثَى alakumu l-dhakaru walahu l-unthā Are you to have males and He females?

item.title: An-Najm:21 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَكُمُ الذَّكَرُ وَلَهُ الْأُنْثَى alakumu l-dhakaru walahu l-unthā Is the male for you and for Him the female? See 53:19

item.title: An-Najm:21 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَكُمُ الذَّكَرُ وَلَهُ الْأُنْثَى alakumu l-dhakaru walahu l-unthā What! for you the males and for Him (God) the females? (Refer to Verses 16:57; 16:58; 43:16; 52:39.) See 53:19

item.title: An-Najm:22 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: تِلْكَ إِذًا قِسْمَةٌ ضِيزَى til'ka idhan qis'matun ḍīzā That, then, will be an unfair division!

item.title: An-Najm:22 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: تِلْكَ إِذًا قِسْمَةٌ ضِيزَى til'ka idhan qis'matun ḍīzā That, then, is an unjust division.1 See 53:19

item.title: An-Najm:22 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: تِلْكَ إِذًا قِسْمَةٌ ضِيزَى til'ka idhan qis'matun ḍīzā This indeed is a division unjust See 53:19

item.title: An-Najm:23 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا أَسْمَاءٌ سَمَّيْتُمُوهَا أَنْتُمْ وَءَابَاؤُكُمْ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ إِنْ يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَمَا تَهْوٰۤی الْأَنْفُسُ وَلَقَدْ جَاءَهُمْ مِنْ رَبِّهِمُ الْهُدَى in hiya illā asmāon sammaytumūhā antum waābāukum mā anzala l-lahu bihā min sul'ṭānin in yattabiʿūna illā l-ẓana wamā tahwā l-anfusu walaqad jāahum min rabbihimu l-hudā These are but names which you have coined —you and your fathers— for which Allah has not sent down any authority. They follow nothing but conjectures and the desires of the [lower] soul, while there has already come to them the guidance from their Lord.

item.title: An-Najm:23 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا أَسْمَاءٌ سَمَّيْتُمُوهَا أَنْتُمْ وَءَابَاؤُكُمْ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ إِنْ يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَمَا تَهْوٰۤی الْأَنْفُسُ وَلَقَدْ جَاءَهُمْ مِنْ رَبِّهِمُ الْهُدَى in hiya illā asmāon sammaytumūhā antum waābāukum mā anzala l-lahu bihā min sul'ṭānin in yattabiʿūna illā l-ẓana wamā tahwā l-anfusu walaqad jāahum min rabbihimu l-hudā They are not but (mere) names you have named them - you and your forefathers - for which Allah has sent down no authority. They follow not except assumption and what (their) souls desire, and there has already come to them from their Lord guidance. See 53:19

item.title: An-Najm:23 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا أَسْمَاءٌ سَمَّيْتُمُوهَا أَنْتُمْ وَءَابَاؤُكُمْ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ إِنْ يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَمَا تَهْوٰۤی الْأَنْفُسُ وَلَقَدْ جَاءَهُمْ مِنْ رَبِّهِمُ الْهُدَى in hiya illā asmāon sammaytumūhā antum waābāukum mā anzala l-lahu bihā min sul'ṭānin in yattabiʿūna illā l-ẓana wamā tahwā l-anfusu walaqad jāahum min rabbihimu l-hudā They are nothing but (mere) names, which have named ye and your fathers (The false gods or the deities which the idolators worship they are mere names of unreal imaginary beings- - hence they are mere names - and nothing more.) , sent not God for them any authority; They follow nothing but a conjecture what their selves are inclined to; and indeed, hath come unto them from their Lord the right guidance (Refer to Verses 7:71; 12:40.) What the idolaters worship as gods, are merely names without any reality…

item.title: An-Najm:24 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَمْ لِلْاِنْسَانِ مَا تَمَنَّى am lil'insāni mā tamannā Shall man have whatever he yearns for?

item.title: An-Najm:24 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَمْ لِلْاِنْسَانِ مَا تَمَنَّى am lil'insāni mā tamannā Or is there for man whatever he wishes? See 53:19

item.title: An-Najm:24 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَمْ لِلْاِنْسَانِ مَا تَمَنَّى am lil'insāni mā tamannā What! Shall man have whatever he wisheth? It is not for man to have anything he covets for, i.e., no man has the power or the authority to provide himself with whatever he wants.

item.title: An-Najm:25 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلِلَّهِ الْءَاخِرَةُ وَالْأُولَى falillahi l-ākhiratu wal-ūlā Yet to Allah belong this world and the Hereafter.

item.title: An-Najm:25 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلِلَّهِ الْءَاخِرَةُ وَالْأُولَى falillahi l-ākhiratu wal-ūlā Rather, to Allah belongs the Hereafter and the first (life). See 53:19

item.title: An-Najm:25 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلِلَّهِ الْءَاخِرَةُ وَالْأُولَى falillahi l-ākhiratu wal-ūlā Nay! God's is the (life) hereafter and the former (life) (God's is the ultimate as is the Start, the Lord of all.) The Kingdom, i.e., the Authority, from the beginning to the end is exclusively God's and of no one else.

item.title: An-Najm:26 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَكَمْ مِنْ مَلَكٍ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ لَا تُغْنِي شَفَاعَتُهُمْ شَيْئًا إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ أَنْ يَأْذَنَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيَرْضَى wakam min malakin fī l-samāwāti lā tugh'nī shafāʿatuhum shayan illā min baʿdi an yadhana l-lahu liman yashāu wayarḍā How many an angel there is in the heavens whose intercession is of no avail in any way except after Allah grants permission to whomever He wishes and approves of!

item.title: An-Najm:26 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَكَمْ مِنْ مَلَكٍ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ لَا تُغْنِي شَفَاعَتُهُمْ شَيْئًا إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ أَنْ يَأْذَنَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيَرْضَى wakam min malakin fī l-samāwāti lā tugh'nī shafāʿatuhum shayan illā min baʿdi an yadhana l-lahu liman yashāu wayarḍā And how many angels there are in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all except (only) after Allah has permitted (it) to whom He wills and approves. See 53:19

item.title: An-Najm:26 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَكَمْ مِنْ مَلَكٍ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ لَا تُغْنِي شَفَاعَتُهُمْ شَيْئًا إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ أَنْ يَأْذَنَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيَرْضَى wakam min malakin fī l-samāwāti lā tugh'nī shafāʿatuhum shayan illā min baʿdi an yadhana l-lahu liman yashāu wayarḍā And how many an angel in heavens are whose intercession is of no avail at all save after that permitteth God whomsoever willeth He and chooseth (This clears the position of the angels regarding intercession.) The disbelievers hoped for the intercession of the angels, for them. It shall be of no avail to them for there could be no intercession without God's permission1.

item.title: An-Najm:27 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْاٰخِرَةِ لَيُسَمُّونَ الْمَلَائِكَةَ تَسْمِيَةَ الْأُنْثَى inna alladhīna lā yu'minūna bil-ākhirati layusammūna l-malāikata tasmiyata l-unthā Indeed those who do not believe in the Hereafter give female names to the angels.

item.title: An-Najm:27 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْاٰخِرَةِ لَيُسَمُّونَ الْمَلَائِكَةَ تَسْمِيَةَ الْأُنْثَى inna alladhīna lā yu'minūna bil-ākhirati layusammūna l-malāikata tasmiyata l-unthā Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter name the angels female names. Verily, those who believe not in the Hereafter, name the angels with female names (53:27). But they have no knowledge thereof. They follow but conjecture, and verily, conjecture is no substitute for the truth (53:28). Therefore withdraw from him who turns away from Our Reminder and desires nothing but the life of this world (53:29). That is what they could reach of knowledge. Verily, your Lord is He, Who knows best him who goes astray from His path, and He knows best him who receives guidance (53:30). Refuting the Claim of the Idolators that the Angels are Allah's Daughters Allah the Exalted admonishes the idolators for calling the…

item.title: An-Najm:27 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْاٰخِرَةِ لَيُسَمُّونَ الْمَلَائِكَةَ تَسْمِيَةَ الْأُنْثَى inna alladhīna lā yu'minūna bil-ākhirati layusammūna l-malāikata tasmiyata l-unthā Verily, those who believe not in the hereafter (The life beyond the physical one.) name the angels (The heathens believed the angels to be the daughters of God.) with female names See 53:26

item.title: An-Najm:28 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا لَهُمْ بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِنْ يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَإِنَّ الظَّنَّ لَا يُغْنِي مِنَ الْحَقِّ شَيْئًا wamā lahum bihi min ʿil'min in yattabiʿūna illā l-ẓana wa-inna l-ẓana lā yugh'nī mina l-ḥaqi shayan They do not have any knowledge of that. They follow nothing but conjectures, and indeed conjecture is no substitute for the truth.

item.title: An-Najm:28 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا لَهُمْ بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِنْ يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَإِنَّ الظَّنَّ لَا يُغْنِي مِنَ الْحَقِّ شَيْئًا wamā lahum bihi min ʿil'min in yattabiʿūna illā l-ẓana wa-inna l-ẓana lā yugh'nī mina l-ḥaqi shayan And they have thereof no knowledge. They follow not except assumption, and indeed, assumption avails not against the truth at all. See 53:27

item.title: An-Najm:28 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا لَهُمْ بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِنْ يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَإِنَّ الظَّنَّ لَا يُغْنِي مِنَ الْحَقِّ شَيْئًا wamā lahum bihi min ʿil'min in yattabiʿūna illā l-ẓana wa-inna l-ẓana lā yugh'nī mina l-ḥaqi shayan But they have not of it anything of knowledge; they follow nothing but a conjecture; verily a conjecture availeth naught the truth at all (This applies to all materialistic schools.) See 53:26

item.title: An-Najm:29 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْ مَنْ تَوَلَّى عَنْ ذِكْرِنَا وَلَمْ يُرِدْ إِلَّا الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا fa-aʿriḍ ʿan man tawallā ʿan dhik'rinā walam yurid illā l-ḥayata l-dun'yā So avoid those who turn away from Our remembrance and desire nothing but the life of the world.

item.title: An-Najm:29 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْ مَنْ تَوَلَّى عَنْ ذِكْرِنَا وَلَمْ يُرِدْ إِلَّا الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا fa-aʿriḍ ʿan man tawallā ʿan dhik'rinā walam yurid illā l-ḥayata l-dun'yā So turn away from whoever turns his back on Our message and desires not except the worldly life. See 53:27

item.title: An-Najm:29 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْ مَنْ تَوَلَّى عَنْ ذِكْرِنَا وَلَمْ يُرِدْ إِلَّا الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا fa-aʿriḍ ʿan man tawallā ʿan dhik'rinā walam yurid illā l-ḥayata l-dun'yā Therefore, turn thou (The Prophet addressed for the people.) aside from him who turneth his back against Our reminder, and desireth not anything but the life of this world (This indicates that the materialists see everything in the term of material life.) See 53:26

item.title: An-Najm:30 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ذٰلِكَ مَبْلَغُهُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ ضَلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ اهْتَدَى dhālika mablaghuhum mina l-ʿil'mi inna rabbaka huwa aʿlamu biman ḍalla ʿan sabīlihi wahuwa aʿlamu bimani ih'tadā That is the ultimate reach of their knowledge. Indeed your Lord knows best those who stray from His way, and He knows best those who are [rightly] guided.

item.title: An-Najm:30 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ذٰلِكَ مَبْلَغُهُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ ضَلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ اهْتَدَى dhālika mablaghuhum mina l-ʿil'mi inna rabbaka huwa aʿlamu biman ḍalla ʿan sabīlihi wahuwa aʿlamu bimani ih'tadā That is their sum of knowledge. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who strays from His way, and He is most knowing of who is guided. See 53:27

item.title: An-Najm:30 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ذٰلِكَ مَبْلَغُهُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ ضَلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ اهْتَدَى dhālika mablaghuhum mina l-ʿil'mi inna rabbaka huwa aʿlamu biman ḍalla ʿan sabīlihi wahuwa aʿlamu bimani ih'tadā That is the (last) reach of their knowledge; Verily, thy Lord knoweth best of him who is astray from His path and He knoweth best of him who is guided aright See 53:26

item.title: An-Najm:31 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ لِيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسَاءُوْۤا بِمَا عَمِلُوْۤا وَيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوْۤا بِالْحُسْنَى walillahi mā fī l-samāwāti wamā fī l-arḍi liyajziya alladhīna asāū bimā ʿamilū wayajziya alladhīna aḥsanū bil-ḥus'nā To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, that He may requite those who do evil for what they have done, and reward those who do good with the best [of rewards].

item.title: An-Najm:31 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ لِيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسَاءُوْۤا بِمَا عَمِلُوْۤا وَيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوْۤا بِالْحُسْنَى walillahi mā fī l-samāwāti wamā fī l-arḍi liyajziya alladhīna asāū bimā ʿamilū wayajziya alladhīna aḥsanū bil-ḥus'nā And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth - that He may recompense those who do evil with (the penalty of) what they have done and recompense those who do good with the best (reward). And to Allah belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is on the earth, that He may requite those who do evil with that which they have done, and reward those who do good, with what is best (53:31). Those who avoid great sins and Al-Fawahish (immoral sins) except Al-Lamam – verily, your Lord is of vast forgiveness. He knows you well when…

item.title: An-Najm:31 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ لِيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسَاءُوْۤا بِمَا عَمِلُوْۤا وَيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوْۤا بِالْحُسْنَى walillahi mā fī l-samāwāti wamā fī l-arḍi liyajziya alladhīna asāū bimā ʿamilū wayajziya alladhīna aḥsanū bil-ḥus'nā And God's is whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, that He may recompense those who do evil for what they did, and that He may recompense those who do good, with what is best See 53:26

item.title: An-Najm:32 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِينَ يَجْتَنِبُونَ كَبَائِرَ الْإِثْمِ وَالْفَوَاحِشَ إِلَّا اللَّمَمَ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ وَاسِعُ الْمَغْفِرَةِ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِكُمْ إِذْ أَنْشَأَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ وَإِذْ أَنْتُمْ أَجِنَّةٌ فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ فَلَا تُزَكُّوْۤا أَنْفُسَكُمْ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ اتَّقَى alladhīna yajtanibūna kabāira l-ith'mi wal-fawāḥisha illā l-lamama inna rabbaka wāsiʿu l-maghfirati huwa aʿlamu bikum idh ansha-akum mina l-arḍi wa-idh antum ajinnatun fī buṭūni ummahātikum falā tuzakkū anfusakum huwa aʿlamu bimani ittaqā Those who avoid major sins and indecencies, excepting [minor and occasional] lapses. Indeed your Lord is expansive in [His] forgiveness. He knows you best since [the time] He produced you from the earth, and since you were fetuses in the bellies of your mothers. So do not flaunt your piety: He knows best those who are Godwary.

item.title: An-Najm:32 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِينَ يَجْتَنِبُونَ كَبَائِرَ الْإِثْمِ وَالْفَوَاحِشَ إِلَّا اللَّمَمَ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ وَاسِعُ الْمَغْفِرَةِ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِكُمْ إِذْ أَنْشَأَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ وَإِذْ أَنْتُمْ أَجِنَّةٌ فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ فَلَا تُزَكُّوْۤا أَنْفُسَكُمْ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ اتَّقَى alladhīna yajtanibūna kabāira l-ith'mi wal-fawāḥisha illā l-lamama inna rabbaka wāsiʿu l-maghfirati huwa aʿlamu bikum idh ansha-akum mina l-arḍi wa-idh antum ajinnatun fī buṭūni ummahātikum falā tuzakkū anfusakum huwa aʿlamu bimani ittaqā Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, only (committing) slight ones. Indeed, your Lord is vast in forgiveness. He was most knowing of you when He produced you from the earth and when you were fetuses in the wombs of your mothers. So do not claim yourselves to be pure; He is most knowing of who fears Him. See 53:31

item.title: An-Najm:32 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِينَ يَجْتَنِبُونَ كَبَائِرَ الْإِثْمِ وَالْفَوَاحِشَ إِلَّا اللَّمَمَ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ وَاسِعُ الْمَغْفِرَةِ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِكُمْ إِذْ أَنْشَأَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ وَإِذْ أَنْتُمْ أَجِنَّةٌ فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ فَلَا تُزَكُّوْۤا أَنْفُسَكُمْ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ اتَّقَى alladhīna yajtanibūna kabāira l-ith'mi wal-fawāḥisha illā l-lamama inna rabbaka wāsiʿu l-maghfirati huwa aʿlamu bikum idh ansha-akum mina l-arḍi wa-idh antum ajinnatun fī buṭūni ummahātikum falā tuzakkū anfusakum huwa aʿlamu bimani ittaqā Those who do avoid the great ones of the sin and shameful (Indecencies.) deeds save accidentally (Provided followed immediately.) verily, thy Lord is (the Lord of) vast forgiveness: He knoweth best about you when He raised you from the earth (Dust.) and when ye are embryos in the wombs of your mothers; so assert ye not the purity of your selves; He knoweth best of him who guardeth (himself against evil) Among 'Kaba'ir', i.e., the great sins, is…

item.title: An-Najm:33 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَرَءَيْتَ الَّذِي تَوَلَّى afara-ayta alladhī tawallā Did you see him who turned away,

item.title: An-Najm:33 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَرَءَيْتَ الَّذِي تَوَلَّى afara-ayta alladhī tawallā Have you seen the one who turned away. Did you observe him who turned away (from Islam) (53:33). And gave a little, then stopped (53:34). Is with him the knowledge of the Unseen so that he sees (53:35). Or is he not informed with what is in the Suhuf of Musa (53:36). And of Ibrahim who fulfilled all that (53:37). That no burdened person (with sins) shall bear the burden (sins) of another (53:38). And that man can have nothing but what he does (53:39). And that his deeds will be seen (53:40). Then he will be recompensed with a full and the best recompense (53:41). Chastising Those Who Disobey Allah and Stop Giving Charity Allah the Exalted chastises those who turn away from His obedience: فَلَا صَدَّقَ وَلَا صَلَّىٰ - وَلَٰكِنْ كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ…

item.title: An-Najm:33 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَرَءَيْتَ الَّذِي تَوَلَّى afara-ayta alladhī tawallā Hast thou then seen him who hath turned his back "He who turns back" refers to those who forsake the faith like those who left the Holy Prophet in the midst of danger and ran away from the battles of Uhud and Hunayn. According to Minhaj us-Sadiqin Uthman bargained with Abdullah Ibn Ubay for a camel load of merchandise if Abdullah would take upon himself the sins of Uthman. After giving the merchandise Uthman put a stop to alms giving relying upon Abdullah's undertaking. Then these verses were revealed. If we accept Islam, we must accept it whole-heartedly and not look back to pagan superstitions. No man can bargain about spiritual matters, for he cannot see what his end will be in the hereafter. It is the unchangeable law of Allah in every age…

item.title: An-Najm:34 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَعْطَى قَلِيلًا وَأَكْدَى wa-aʿṭā qalīlan wa-akdā gave a little and held off?

item.title: An-Najm:34 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَعْطَى قَلِيلًا وَأَكْدَى wa-aʿṭā qalīlan wa-akdā And gave a little and (then) refrained? See 53:33

item.title: An-Najm:34 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَعْطَى قَلِيلًا وَأَكْدَى wa-aʿṭā qalīlan wa-akdā And giveth he a little and withholdeth (his hand) See 53:33

item.title: An-Najm:35 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَعِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ الْغَيْبِ فَهُوَ يَرٰی aʿindahu ʿil'mu l-ghaybi fahuwa yarā Does he have the knowledge of the Unseen so that he sees?

item.title: An-Najm:35 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَعِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ الْغَيْبِ فَهُوَ يَرٰی aʿindahu ʿil'mu l-ghaybi fahuwa yarā Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so he sees?1 See 53:33

item.title: An-Najm:35 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَعِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ الْغَيْبِ فَهُوَ يَرٰی aʿindahu ʿil'mu l-ghaybi fahuwa yarā What! Is with him the know-ledge of the unseen that he seeth The question is to say that the one who believed in Abdullah's undertaking the responsibility of his sins and stopped his charity did not have the knowledge of the hidden, i.e., whether what Abdullah claimed to hold himself responsible for the other man's sins, had any truth in it or not.

item.title: An-Najm:36 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَمْ لَمْ يُنَبَّأْ بِمَا فِي صُحُفِ مُوسٰی am lam yunabba bimā fī ṣuḥufi mūsā Has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Moses,

item.title: An-Najm:36 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَمْ لَمْ يُنَبَّأْ بِمَا فِي صُحُفِ مُوسٰی am lam yunabba bimā fī ṣuḥufi mūsā Or has he not been informed of what was in the scriptures of Musa. See 53:33

item.title: An-Najm:36 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَمْ لَمْ يُنَبَّأْ بِمَا فِي صُحُفِ مُوسٰی am lam yunabba bimā fī ṣuḥufi mūsā Or hath he not been told of what is in the scriptures of Moses? See 53:35

item.title: An-Najm:37 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاِبْرَاهِیْمَ الَّذِي وَفَّى wa-ib'rāhīma alladhī waffā and of Abraham, who fulfilled [his summons]:

item.title: An-Najm:37 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاِبْرَاهِیْمَ الَّذِي وَفَّى wa-ib'rāhīma alladhī waffā And (of) Ibrahim, who fulfilled (his obligations). See 53:33

item.title: An-Najm:37 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاِبْرَاهِیْمَ الَّذِي وَفَّى wa-ib'rāhīma alladhī waffā And of Abraham who fully discharged (his mission)? See 53:35

item.title: An-Najm:38 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَّا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرٰی allā taziru wāziratun wiz'ra ukh'rā that no bearer shall bear another's burden,

item.title: An-Najm:38 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَّا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرٰی allā taziru wāziratun wiz'ra ukh'rā That no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. See 53:33

item.title: An-Najm:38 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَّا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرٰی allā taziru wāziratun wiz'ra ukh'rā That no bearer of a burden shall bear the burden of another (No one shall bear the burden of another. Refer to Verses 2:48; 2:123; 2:254; 17:15; 35:18.) The verse 38 answers the question asked in Verse 35. For further details, see the commentary of 2:48; 2:123; 2:254; 6:165; 17:15; 35:18.

item.title: An-Najm:39 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنْ لَيْسَ لِلْاِنْسَانِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَى wa-an laysa lil'insāni illā mā saʿā and that nothing belongs to man except what he strives for,

item.title: An-Najm:39 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنْ لَيْسَ لِلْاِنْسَانِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَى wa-an laysa lil'insāni illā mā saʿā And that there is not for man except that (good) for which he strives. See 53:33

item.title: An-Najm:39 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنْ لَيْسَ لِلْاِنْسَانِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَى wa-an laysa lil'insāni illā mā saʿā And that there is not for man (aught) save what he striveth for (Refer to Verse 52:21.) Note the individual responsibility every man and woman is charged with to work goodness and shun evil as much as one could do it and thus make this world itself a blissful place to live in.

item.title: An-Najm:40 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّ سَعْيَهُ سَوْفَ يُرٰی wa-anna saʿyahu sawfa yurā and that he will soon be shown his endeavour,

item.title: An-Najm:40 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّ سَعْيَهُ سَوْفَ يُرٰی wa-anna saʿyahu sawfa yurā And that his effort is going to be seen. See 53:33

item.title: An-Najm:40 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّ سَعْيَهُ سَوْفَ يُرٰی wa-anna saʿyahu sawfa yurā And that his striving shall soon be seen (Refer to Verse 52:21.) See 53:39

item.title: An-Najm:41 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ يُجْزَاهُ الْجَزَاءَ الْأَوْفَى thumma yuj'zāhu l-jazāa l-awfā then he will be rewarded for it with the fullest reward;

item.title: An-Najm:41 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ يُجْزَاهُ الْجَزَاءَ الْأَوْفَى thumma yuj'zāhu l-jazāa l-awfā Then he will be recompensed for it with the fullest recompense. See 53:33

item.title: An-Najm:41 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ يُجْزَاهُ الْجَزَاءَ الْأَوْفَى thumma yuj'zāhu l-jazāa l-awfā Then shall he be recompensed to the fullest measure See 53:39

item.title: An-Najm:42 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّ إِلَى رَبِّكَ الْمُنْتَهَى wa-anna ilā rabbika l-muntahā and that the terminus is toward your Lord,

item.title: An-Najm:42 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّ إِلَى رَبِّكَ الْمُنْتَهَى wa-anna ilā rabbika l-muntahā And that to your Lord is the finality. And that to your Lord is the End (53:42). And that it is He Who makes laugh, and makes weep (53:43). And that it is He Who causes death and gives life (53:44). And that He creates the pairs, male and female (53:45). From Nutfah when it is emitted (53:46). And that upon Him is another bringing forth (Resurrection) (53:47). And that it is He Who Aghna and Aqna (53:48). And that He is the Lord of Ash-Shi'ra (53:49). And that it is He Who destroyed the former 'Ad (53:50). And Thamud. He spared none of them (53:51). And the people of Nuh aforetime. Verily, they were more unjust and more rebellious and transgressing (53:52). And He destroyed the overthrown cities (53:53). So, there…

item.title: An-Najm:42 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّ إِلَى رَبِّكَ الْمُنْتَهَى wa-anna ilā rabbika l-muntahā And that unto thy Lord is the end (of all) (Refer to Verses 79:42 - 79:44.) See 53:39

item.title: An-Najm:43 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَضْحَكَ وَأَبْكَى wa-annahu huwa aḍḥaka wa-abkā and that it is He who makes [men] laugh, and makes [them] weep,

item.title: An-Najm:43 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَضْحَكَ وَأَبْكَى wa-annahu huwa aḍḥaka wa-abkā And that it is He who makes (one) laugh and weep. See 53:42

item.title: An-Najm:43 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَضْحَكَ وَأَبْكَى wa-annahu huwa aḍḥaka wa-abkā And verily He it is Who causeth (one) to laugh and causeth (him) to weep See 53:39

item.title: An-Najm:44 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَمَاتَ وَأَحْيَا wa-annahu huwa amāta wa-aḥyā and that it is He who brings death and gives life,

item.title: An-Najm:44 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَمَاتَ وَأَحْيَا wa-annahu huwa amāta wa-aḥyā And that it is He who causes death and gives life. See 53:42

item.title: An-Najm:44 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَمَاتَ وَأَحْيَا wa-annahu huwa amāta wa-aḥyā And that He it is Who causeth death and causeth life See 53:39

item.title: An-Najm:45 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّهُ خَلَقَ الزَّوْجَيْنِ الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنْثَى wa-annahu khalaqa l-zawjayni l-dhakara wal-unthā and that it is He who created the mates,1 the male and the female,

item.title: An-Najm:45 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّهُ خَلَقَ الزَّوْجَيْنِ الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنْثَى wa-annahu khalaqa l-zawjayni l-dhakara wal-unthā And that He creates the two mates - the male and female. See 53:42

item.title: An-Najm:45 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّهُ خَلَقَ الزَّوْجَيْنِ الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنْثَى wa-annahu khalaqa l-zawjayni l-dhakara wal-unthā And He it is Who createth pairs, the male and the female See 53:39

item.title: An-Najm:46 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ إِذَا تُمْنَى min nuṭ'fatin idhā tum'nā from a drop of [seminal] fluid when emitted;

item.title: An-Najm:46 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ إِذَا تُمْنَى min nuṭ'fatin idhā tum'nā From a sperm-drop when it is emitted. See 53:42

item.title: An-Najm:46 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ إِذَا تُمْنَى min nuṭ'fatin idhā tum'nā From the sperm when it is discharged See 53:39

item.title: An-Najm:47 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّ عَلَيْهِ النَّشْأَةَ الْأُخْرٰی wa-anna ʿalayhi l-nashata l-ukh'rā and that with Him lies the second genesis,

item.title: An-Najm:47 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّ عَلَيْهِ النَّشْأَةَ الْأُخْرٰی wa-anna ʿalayhi l-nashata l-ukh'rā And that (incumbent) upon Him is the other (i.e., next) creation. See 53:42

item.title: An-Najm:47 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّ عَلَيْهِ النَّشْأَةَ الْأُخْرٰی wa-anna ʿalayhi l-nashata l-ukh'rā And that on Him (alone) is the raising for a second time See 53:39

item.title: An-Najm:48 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَغْنَى وَأَقْنَى wa-annahu huwa aghnā wa-aqnā and that it is He who enriches and grants possessions,

item.title: An-Najm:48 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَغْنَى وَأَقْنَى wa-annahu huwa aghnā wa-aqnā And that it is He who enriches and suffices. See 53:42

item.title: An-Najm:48 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَغْنَى وَأَقْنَى wa-annahu huwa aghnā wa-aqnā And that He it is Who enricheth and bestoweth contention See 53:39

item.title: An-Najm:49 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ رَبُّ الشِّعْرَى wa-annahu huwa rabbu l-shiʿ'rā and that it is He who is the Lord of Sirius;

item.title: An-Najm:49 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ رَبُّ الشِّعْرَى wa-annahu huwa rabbu l-shiʿ'rā And that it is He who is the Lord of Sirius.1 See 53:42

item.title: An-Najm:49 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ رَبُّ الشِّعْرَى wa-annahu huwa rabbu l-shiʿ'rā And that He it is Who is the Lord of Sirius (A deity of the heathens - zosh-shara was represented in Petra by a quadrangular block of unhewn black stone 4' high and 2' wide - associated with the idol 'Manat' - Sirius was also worshipped by the Egyptians, the Greeks and the Romans.) The constellation beyond the Zodiac line which was the object of some star worshippers. (A.P.)

item.title: An-Najm:50 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّهُ أَهْلَكَ عَادًا الْأُولَى wa-annahu ahlaka ʿādan l-ūlā and that it is He who destroyed the former 'Ād,

item.title: An-Najm:50 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّهُ أَهْلَكَ عَادًا الْأُولَى wa-annahu ahlaka ʿādan l-ūlā And that He destroyed the first (people of) ʿAad. See 53:42

item.title: An-Najm:50 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّهُ أَهْلَكَ عَادًا الْأُولَى wa-annahu ahlaka ʿādan l-ūlā And that He did destroy (the powerful) 'Ad of the ancient (times) (Refer to Verses 7:65; 89:6.) See 53:49

item.title: An-Najm:51 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَثَمُودَ فَمَا أَبْقَى wathamūdā famā abqā and Thamud, sparing none [of them];

item.title: An-Najm:51 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَثَمُودَ فَمَا أَبْقَى wathamūdā famā abqā And Thamūd - and He did not spare (them). See 53:42

item.title: An-Najm:51 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَثَمُودَ فَمَا أَبْقَى wathamūdā famā abqā And Thamood, and He spared not (one to survive) See 53:49

item.title: An-Najm:52 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ مِنْ قَبْلُ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوْۤا هُمْ أَظْلَمَ وَأَطْغَى waqawma nūḥin min qablu innahum kānū hum aẓlama wa-aṭghā and the people of Noah before that; indeed they were more unjust and rebellious;

item.title: An-Najm:52 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ مِنْ قَبْلُ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوْۤا هُمْ أَظْلَمَ وَأَطْغَى waqawma nūḥin min qablu innahum kānū hum aẓlama wa-aṭghā And the people of Nuh before. Indeed, it was they who were (even) more unjust and oppressing. See 53:42

item.title: An-Najm:52 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ مِنْ قَبْلُ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوْۤا هُمْ أَظْلَمَ وَأَطْغَى waqawma nūḥin min qablu innahum kānū hum aẓlama wa-aṭghā And the people of Noah before; Verily they, they were the most unjust and the most transgressing See 53:49

item.title: An-Najm:53 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْمُؤْتَفِكَةَ أَهْوَى wal-mu'tafikata ahwā and He overthrew the town that was overturned,1

item.title: An-Najm:53 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْمُؤْتَفِكَةَ أَهْوَى wal-mu'tafikata ahwā And the overturned towns1 He hurled down. See 53:42

item.title: An-Najm:53 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْمُؤْتَفِكَةَ أَهْوَى wal-mu'tafikata ahwā And the cities overthrown (it is) He (Who) did overthrow See 53:49

item.title: An-Najm:54 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَغَشَّاهَا مَا غَشَّى faghashāhā mā ghashā covering it with what covered it.

item.title: An-Najm:54 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَغَشَّاهَا مَا غَشَّى faghashāhā mā ghashā And covered them by that which He covered.1 See 53:42

item.title: An-Najm:54 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَغَشَّاهَا مَا غَشَّى faghashāhā mā ghashā So covered them what did cover See 53:49

item.title: An-Najm:55 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكَ تَتَمَارٰی fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbika tatamārā Then which of the bounties of your Lord will you dispute?

item.title: An-Najm:55 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكَ تَتَمَارٰی fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbika tatamārā Then which of the favors of your Lord do you doubt? See 53:42

item.title: An-Najm:55 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكَ تَتَمَارٰی fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbika tatamārā Which then of the bounties of thy Lord wilt thou dispute about? The minutest functions in the universe are subject to Allah's sovereignty, so the whole universe is before Him in a single view at every moment (A.P.).

item.title: An-Najm:56 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: هَذَا نَذِيرٌ مِنَ النُّذُرِ الْأُولَى hādhā nadhīrun mina l-nudhuri l-ūlā This is a warner, [in the tradition] of the warners of old.

item.title: An-Najm:56 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: هَذَا نَذِيرٌ مِنَ النُّذُرِ الْأُولَى hādhā nadhīrun mina l-nudhuri l-ūlā This (Prophet SAW) is a warner from (i.e., like) the former warners. This is a warner from the warners of old (53:56). The Azifah draws near (53:57). None besides Allah can avert it (53:58). Do you then wonder at this recitation (53:59). And you laugh at it and weep not (53:60). While you are Sāmidūn (53:61). So fall you down in prostration to Allah and worship Him (53:62). A Warning and Exhortation, the Order to Prostrate and to be Humble Allah said: هَٰذَا نَذِيرٌ This is a warner in reference to Muhammad SAW: مِنَ النُّذُرِ الْأُولَىٰ from the warners of old. means, just like the warners of old, he was sent as a Messenger as they were sent as Messengers. Allah the Exalted said: قُلْ مَا كُنْتُ بِدْعًا مِنَ الرُّسُلِ…

item.title: An-Najm:56 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: هَذَا نَذِيرٌ مِنَ النُّذُرِ الْأُولَى hādhā nadhīrun mina l-nudhuri l-ūlā This (Our Apostle Muhammad) is a Warner of the warners of old (In the line of.) See 53:55

item.title: An-Najm:57 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَزِفَتِ الْءَازِفَةُ azifati l-āzifatu The Imminent [Hour] is near at hand.

item.title: An-Najm:57 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَزِفَتِ الْءَازِفَةُ azifati l-āzifatu The Approaching Day has approached. See 53:56

item.title: An-Najm:57 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَزِفَتِ الْءَازِفَةُ azifati l-āzifatu Draweth nigh the (Hour of Reckoning which is) ever drawing nigh According to Ibn al-'Arabi in his commentary, it may refer to the advent of the Last Mahdi, Muhammad Ibn al-Hasan al-Mahdi - the last Imam, and the partial resurrection and it can also refer to the Total Resurrection (A.P.).

item.title: An-Najm:58 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَيْسَ لَهَا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ كَاشِفَةٌ laysa lahā min dūni l-lahi kāshifatun There is none that may unveil it besides Allah.

item.title: An-Najm:58 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَيْسَ لَهَا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ كَاشِفَةٌ laysa lahā min dūni l-lahi kāshifatun Of it, (from those) besides Allah, there is no remover. See 53:56

item.title: An-Najm:58 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَيْسَ لَهَا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ كَاشِفَةٌ laysa lahā min dūni l-lahi kāshifatun None there is for it other than God to lay it bare (To remove it, to avert it) See 53:57

item.title: An-Najm:59 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَمِنْ هَذَا الْحَدِيثِ تَعْجَبُونَ afamin hādhā l-ḥadīthi taʿjabūna Do you then wonder at this discourse,

item.title: An-Najm:59 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَمِنْ هَذَا الْحَدِيثِ تَعْجَبُونَ afamin hādhā l-ḥadīthi taʿjabūna Then at this statement do you wonder? See 53:56

item.title: An-Najm:59 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَمِنْ هَذَا الْحَدِيثِ تَعْجَبُونَ afamin hādhā l-ḥadīthi taʿjabūna What! Wonder ye then at this statement? See 53:57

item.title: An-Najm:60 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَتَضْحَكُونَ وَلَا تَبْكُونَ wataḍḥakūna walā tabkūna and laugh and not weep,

item.title: An-Najm:60 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَتَضْحَكُونَ وَلَا تَبْكُونَ wataḍḥakūna walā tabkūna And you laugh and do not weep. See 53:56

item.title: An-Najm:60 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَتَضْحَكُونَ وَلَا تَبْكُونَ wataḍḥakūna walā tabkūna And laugh ye and not weep? See 53:57

item.title: An-Najm:61 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنْتُمْ سَامِدُونَ wa-antum sāmidūna while you remain heedless?!

item.title: An-Najm:61 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنْتُمْ سَامِدُونَ wa-antum sāmidūna While you are proudly sporting?1 See 53:56

item.title: An-Najm:61 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنْتُمْ سَامِدُونَ wa-antum sāmidūna And yet sport ye (negligently) See 53:57

item.title: An-Najm:62 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَاسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ وَاعْبُدُوا fa-us'judū lillahi wa-uʿ'budū So prostrate yourselves to Allah and worship Him!

item.title: An-Najm:62 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَاسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ وَاعْبُدُوا fa-us'judū lillahi wa-uʿ'budū So prostrate to Allah and worship (Him). See 53:56

item.title: An-Najm:62 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَاسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ وَاعْبُدُوا fa-us'judū lillahi wa-uʿ'budū Prostration is compulsory at the recitation of this verse for there is the command of the Lord to do it and it must immediately be obeyed then and there and the later part of the Verse is to obey them, i. e., to serve Him, which means to mould the life as a whole as desired by the Lord and actuate it accordingly and not as forced by one's passions.

item.title: An-Naml:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: طس تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الْقُرْءَانِ وَكِتَابٍ مُبِينٍ tta-seen til'ka āyātu l-qur'āni wakitābin mubīnin Ṭā, Sīn. These are the signs of the Qur'ān and a manifest Book,

item.title: An-Naml:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: طس تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الْقُرْءَانِ وَكِتَابٍ مُبِينٍ tta-seen til'ka āyātu l-qur'āni wakitābin mubīnin Ṭā, Seen.1 These are the verses of the Qur’ān (i.e., recitation) and a clear Book. وَإِنَّكَ لَتُلَقَّى الْقُرْآنَ مِنْ لَدُنْ حَكِيمٍ عَلِيمٍ And verily, you are being taught the Qur'an from One, All-Wise, All-Knowing. وَإِنَّكَ And verily, you O Muhammad. Qatadah said: لَتُلَقَّى are being taught "Are receiving." الْقُرْآنَ مِنْ لَدُنْ حَكِيمٍ عَلِيمٍ the Qur'an from One, All-Wise, All-Knowing. from One Who is Wise in His commands and prohibitions, and Who knows all things, major and minor. Whatever He says is absolute Truth, and His rulings are entirely fair and just, as Allah says: وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ صِدْقًا وَعَدْلًا ۚ And the Word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and in justice (6:115)

item.title: An-Naml:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: طس تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الْقُرْءَانِ وَكِتَابٍ مُبِينٍ tta-seen til'ka āyātu l-qur'āni wakitābin mubīnin Ta (Refer to note on verse 2:1.) Seen (Refer to note on verse 2:1.) These are the verses of the Qur'an, and the Book maketh the truth manifesting, See 27:2

item.title: An-Naml:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: هُدًى وَبُشْرٰی لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ hudan wabush'rā lil'mu'minīna a guidance and good news for the faithful

item.title: An-Naml:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: هُدًى وَبُشْرٰی لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ hudan wabush'rā lil'mu'minīna As guidance and good tidings for the believers. See 27:1

item.title: An-Naml:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: هُدًى وَبُشْرٰی لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ hudan wabush'rā lil'mu'minīna A guidance and glad tidings unto the believers, The Holy Qur'an does not mention names of persons but refers to their qualities so that the verse could be applied to any situation or individual, appropriate for the purpose. Here only the believers are mentioned and when any quality is indefinitely mentioned, it would naturally mean its perfection, wherever it might be found. The verse in the first place would mean those who possess the qualities in their perfection. It is the universally acknowledged truth that these qualities and also the others mentioned elsewhere in the Qur'an, are found in their perfection only in the Holy Ahl al-Bayt who were purified by God Himself.1 Hence the guidance and the glad tidings will first be meant to these holy ones and in the case of the…

item.title: An-Naml:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ وَيُؤْتُونَ الزَّكَاةَ وَهُمْ بِالْاٰخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ alladhīna yuqīmūna l-ṣalata wayu'tūna l-zakata wahum bil-ākhirati hum yūqinūna —those who maintain the prayer and pay the zakāt, and who are certain of the Hereafter.

item.title: An-Naml:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ وَيُؤْتُونَ الزَّكَاةَ وَهُمْ بِالْاٰخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ alladhīna yuqīmūna l-ṣalata wayu'tūna l-zakata wahum bil-ākhirati hum yūqinūna Who establish prayer and give zakāh, and of the Hereafter they are certain (in faith). See 27:1

item.title: An-Naml:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ وَيُؤْتُونَ الزَّكَاةَ وَهُمْ بِالْاٰخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ alladhīna yuqīmūna l-ṣalata wayu'tūna l-zakata wahum bil-ākhirati hum yūqinūna Who establish prayer and give the poor-rate, and of the hereafter, they are sure. See 27:2

item.title: An-Naml:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْاٰخِرَةِ زَيَّنَّا لَهُمْ أَعْمَالَهُمْ فَهُمْ يَعْمَهُونَ inna alladhīna lā yu'minūna bil-ākhirati zayyannā lahum aʿmālahum fahum yaʿmahūna As for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, We have made their deeds seem decorous to them, and so they are bewildered.

item.title: An-Naml:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْاٰخِرَةِ زَيَّنَّا لَهُمْ أَعْمَالَهُمْ فَهُمْ يَعْمَهُونَ inna alladhīna lā yu'minūna bil-ākhirati zayyannā lahum aʿmālahum fahum yaʿmahūna Indeed, for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, We have made pleasing to them their deeds, so they wander blindly. See 27:1

item.title: An-Naml:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْاٰخِرَةِ زَيَّنَّا لَهُمْ أَعْمَالَهُمْ فَهُمْ يَعْمَهُونَ inna alladhīna lā yu'minūna bil-ākhirati zayyannā lahum aʿmālahum fahum yaʿmahūna Verily, those who believe not in the hereafter, We have made their deeds fair-seeming unto them, so they wander bewildered. God Himself making the deeds of the disbelievers, fair-seeming to them, means that the disbelievers being endowed with the means to enjoy His bounties in this world, but the people intoxicated with the abundance of the bounties of God, instead of being grateful, meek and submitting to God take undue advantage of their position with the means given to them and get attracted by the evil ways of using the bounties conferred on them. This is what usually happens in the case of the wealthy ones particularly those who have been given by God to rule the States. Instead of…

item.title: An-Naml:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اُولٰٓئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَهُمْ سُوءُ الْعَذَابِ وَهُمْ فِي الْاٰخِرَةُ هُمُ الْأَخْسَرُونَ ulāika alladhīna lahum sūu l-ʿadhābi wahum fī l-ākhirati humu l-akhsarūna They are the ones for whom there is a terrible punishment, and they are the ones who will be the biggest losers in the Hereafter.

item.title: An-Naml:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اُولٰٓئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَهُمْ سُوءُ الْعَذَابِ وَهُمْ فِي الْاٰخِرَةُ هُمُ الْأَخْسَرُونَ ulāika alladhīna lahum sūu l-ʿadhābi wahum fī l-ākhirati humu l-akhsarūna Those are the ones for whom there will be the worst of punishment, and in the Hereafter they are the greatest losers. See 27:1

item.title: An-Naml:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اُولٰٓئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَهُمْ سُوءُ الْعَذَابِ وَهُمْ فِي الْاٰخِرَةُ هُمُ الْأَخْسَرُونَ ulāika alladhīna lahum sūu l-ʿadhābi wahum fī l-ākhirati humu l-akhsarūna These are those for whom shall be a grievous chastisement, and (these are) they in the hereafter, who shall be the greatest losers, See 27:4

item.title: An-Naml:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّكَ لَتُلَقَّى الْقُرْآنَ مِنْ لَدُنْ حَكِيمٍ عَلِيمٍ wa-innaka latulaqqā l-qur'āna min ladun ḥakīmin ʿalīmin Indeed you receive the Qur'ān from One who is all-wise, all-knowing.

item.title: An-Naml:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّكَ لَتُلَقَّى الْقُرْآنَ مِنْ لَدُنْ حَكِيمٍ عَلِيمٍ wa-innaka latulaqqā l-qur'āna min ladun ḥakīmin ʿalīmin And indeed, (O Muḥammad), you receive the Qur’ān from one Wise and Knowing. See 27:1

item.title: An-Naml:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنَّكَ لَتُلَقَّى الْقُرْآنَ مِنْ لَدُنْ حَكِيمٍ عَلِيمٍ wa-innaka latulaqqā l-qur'āna min ladun ḥakīmin ʿalīmin Verily thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) receivest the Qur'an from unto the All-Wise, All-Knowing. See 27:4

item.title: An-Naml:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ قَالَ مُوسٰی لِأَهْلِهِ اِنِّیْ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًا سَءَاتِيكُمْ مِنْهَا بِخَبَرٍ أَوْ ءَاتِيكُمْ بِشِهَابٍ قَبَسٍ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ idh qāla mūsā li-ahlihi innī ānastu nāran saātīkum min'hā bikhabarin aw ātīkum bishihābin qabasin laʿallakum taṣṭalūna When Moses said to his family, 'Indeed I descry a fire! I will bring you some news from it, or bring you a firebrand so that you may warm yourselves.'

item.title: An-Naml:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ قَالَ مُوسٰی لِأَهْلِهِ اِنِّیْ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًا سَءَاتِيكُمْ مِنْهَا بِخَبَرٍ أَوْ ءَاتِيكُمْ بِشِهَابٍ قَبَسٍ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ idh qāla mūsā li-ahlihi innī ānastu nāran saātīkum min'hā bikhabarin aw ātīkum bishihābin qabasin laʿallakum taṣṭalūna (Mention) when Musa said to his family, "Indeed, I have perceived a fire. I will bring you from there information or will bring you a burning torch that you may warm yourselves." (Remember) when Musa said to his household: Verily, I have seen a fire; I will bring you from there some information, or I will bring you a burning ember, that you may warm yourselves (27:7). But when he came to it, he was called: "Blessed is whosoever is in the fire, and whosoever is round about it! And glorified be Allah, the Lord of all that exists (27:8). "O Musa! Verily, it is I, Allah, the…

item.title: An-Naml:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ قَالَ مُوسٰی لِأَهْلِهِ اِنِّیْ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًا سَءَاتِيكُمْ مِنْهَا بِخَبَرٍ أَوْ ءَاتِيكُمْ بِشِهَابٍ قَبَسٍ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ idh qāla mūsā li-ahlihi innī ānastu nāran saātīkum min'hā bikhabarin aw ātīkum bishihābin qabasin laʿallakum taṣṭalūna When said Moses unto his family, "Verily I (Refer to verses 28:29 & 20:10.) perceive fire; soon will I bring unto you of it some tiding or bring I unto you a brand lighted, that ye may warm yourselves." See 27:4

item.title: An-Naml:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا جَاءَهَا نُودِيَ أَنْ بُورِكَ مَنْ فِي النَّارِ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا وَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ falammā jāahā nūdiya an būrika man fī l-nāri waman ḥawlahā wasub'ḥāna l-lahi rabbi l-ʿālamīna So when he came to it, he was called: 'Blessed is He who is in the fire and who is [as well] around it, and immaculate is Allah, the Lord of all the worlds!'

item.title: An-Naml:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا جَاءَهَا نُودِيَ أَنْ بُورِكَ مَنْ فِي النَّارِ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا وَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ falammā jāahā nūdiya an būrika man fī l-nāri waman ḥawlahā wasub'ḥāna l-lahi rabbi l-ʿālamīna But when he came to it, he was called, "Blessed is whoever is at the fire and whoever is around it. And exalted is Allah, Lord of the worlds. See 27:7

item.title: An-Naml:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا جَاءَهَا نُودِيَ أَنْ بُورِكَ مَنْ فِي النَّارِ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا وَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ falammā jāahā nūdiya an būrika man fī l-nāri waman ḥawlahā wasub'ḥāna l-lahi rabbi l-ʿālamīna So when he came unto it, he was called unto saying, "Blessed is whosoever is in the fire and whosoever is about it; and hallowed is God, the Lord of the worlds!" The fire appeared to Moses, being actually the divine manifestation, obviously was blessed itself and whoever surrounded it, (i.e., the angels and Moses) - and to discard the possible conception identification or the of God with the Light or considering it as His incarnation. The last clause has been used to say that God is above being identified or incarnated even in light. (A.P.).

item.title: An-Naml:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَامُوسٰی إِنَّهُ أَنَا اللَّهُ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ yāmūsā innahu anā l-lahu l-ʿazīzu l-ḥakīmu 'O Moses! Indeed I am Allah, the All-mighty, the All-wise.'

item.title: An-Naml:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَامُوسٰی إِنَّهُ أَنَا اللَّهُ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ yāmūsā innahu anā l-lahu l-ʿazīzu l-ḥakīmu O Musa, indeed it is I - Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise." See 27:7

item.title: An-Naml:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَامُوسٰی إِنَّهُ أَنَا اللَّهُ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ yāmūsā innahu anā l-lahu l-ʿazīzu l-ḥakīmu O' Moses! Verily it is, I am God the All-Mighty, the All-Wise, The Voice came from the direction of the fire and not from the fire itself or the direction of the right side of the Valley - or from the Tree.1 There is no room for any conception of form or incarnation or God being a physical substance. (A.P.).

item.title: An-Naml:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَلْقِ عَصَاكَ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهَا تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَانٌّ وَلَّى مُدْبِرًا وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ يَامُوسٰی لَا تَخَفْ اِنِّیْ لَا يَخَافُ لَدَيَّ الْمُرْسَلُونَ wa-alqi ʿaṣāka falammā raāhā tahtazzu ka-annahā jānnun wallā mud'biran walam yuʿaqqib yāmūsā lā takhaf innī lā yakhāfu ladayya l-mur'salūna 'Throw down your staff!' And when he saw it wriggling, as if it were a snake, he turned his back [to flee], without looking back. 'O Moses! 'Do not be afraid. Indeed the apostles are not afraid before Me,

item.title: An-Naml:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَلْقِ عَصَاكَ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهَا تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَانٌّ وَلَّى مُدْبِرًا وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ يَامُوسٰی لَا تَخَفْ اِنِّیْ لَا يَخَافُ لَدَيَّ الْمُرْسَلُونَ wa-alqi ʿaṣāka falammā raāhā tahtazzu ka-annahā jānnun wallā mud'biran walam yuʿaqqib yāmūsā lā takhaf innī lā yakhāfu ladayya l-mur'salūna And (he was told), "Throw down your staff." But when he saw it writhing as if it were a snake, he turned in flight and did not return.1 (Allah said), "O Musa, fear not. Indeed, in My presence the messengers do not fear. See 27:7

item.title: An-Naml:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَلْقِ عَصَاكَ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهَا تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّهَا جَانٌّ وَلَّى مُدْبِرًا وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ يَامُوسٰی لَا تَخَفْ اِنِّیْ لَا يَخَافُ لَدَيَّ الْمُرْسَلُونَ wa-alqi ʿaṣāka falammā raāhā tahtazzu ka-annahā jānnun wallā mud'biran walam yuʿaqqib yāmūsā lā takhaf innī lā yakhāfu ladayya l-mur'salūna And cast thou down thy staff! "So when he saw it moving as if (it was) a serpent, he turned back retreating and returned not: (then it was said unto him): "O' Moses' (Fear befits not the apostles of God. Refer to verse 20:21.) Fear not! for shall not fear (My) apostles in My presence." See verses 27:10 & 20:21. Note, God says that no apostle shall have any fright in His presence. How could the Prince of Apostles, the Holy Prophet Muhammad, have any fright when he was first commissioned by God through the Messenger Angel Gabriel. The blasphemy against the…

item.title: An-Naml:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِلَّا مَنْ ظَلَمَ ثُمَّ بَدَّلَ حُسْنًا بَعْدَ سُوءٍ فَإِنِّي غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ illā man ẓalama thumma baddala ḥus'nan baʿda sūin fa-innī ghafūrun raḥīmun barring someone who does wrong and then makes up with goodness for [his] fault, for indeed I am all-forgiving, all-merciful.'

item.title: An-Naml:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِلَّا مَنْ ظَلَمَ ثُمَّ بَدَّلَ حُسْنًا بَعْدَ سُوءٍ فَإِنِّي غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ illā man ẓalama thumma baddala ḥus'nan baʿda sūin fa-innī ghafūrun raḥīmun Otherwise, he who wrongs, then substitutes good after evil - indeed, I am Forgiving and Merciful. See 27:7

item.title: An-Naml:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِلَّا مَنْ ظَلَمَ ثُمَّ بَدَّلَ حُسْنًا بَعْدَ سُوءٍ فَإِنِّي غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ illā man ẓalama thumma baddala ḥus'nan baʿda sūin fa-innī ghafūrun raḥīmun Save he who hath been unjust, then in its place he doeth good after the evil, for verily I am the Oft-Forgiving, the All- Merciful. See 27:10

item.title: An-Naml:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِي جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَاءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوءٍ فِي تِسْعِ ءَايَاتٍ إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ وَقَوْمِهِ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوْۤا قَوْمًا فَاسِقِينَ wa-adkhil yadaka fī jaybika takhruj bayḍāa min ghayri sūin fī tis'ʿi āyātin ilā fir'ʿawna waqawmihi innahum kānū qawman fāsiqīna 'Insert your hand into your bosom. It will emerge white, without any fault, —among nine signs for Pharaoh and his people. Indeed they are a transgressing lot.'

item.title: An-Naml:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِي جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَاءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوءٍ فِي تِسْعِ ءَايَاتٍ إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ وَقَوْمِهِ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوْۤا قَوْمًا فَاسِقِينَ wa-adkhil yadaka fī jaybika takhruj bayḍāa min ghayri sūin fī tis'ʿi āyātin ilā fir'ʿawna waqawmihi innahum kānū qawman fāsiqīna And put your hand into the opening of your garment (at the breast); it will come out white without disease. (These are) among the nine signs (you will take) to Pharaoh and his people. Indeed, they have been a people defiantly disobedient." See 27:7

item.title: An-Naml:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِي جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَاءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوءٍ فِي تِسْعِ ءَايَاتٍ إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ وَقَوْمِهِ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوْۤا قَوْمًا فَاسِقِينَ wa-adkhil yadaka fī jaybika takhruj bayḍāa min ghayri sūin fī tis'ʿi āyātin ilā fir'ʿawna waqawmihi innahum kānū qawman fāsiqīna Now put thy hand into thy bosom, it shall come forth white, shining, without evil: (this is) along with the nine signs (thou wilt take) unto Pharaoh and his people; Verily, they are a transgressing people See 27:10

item.title: An-Naml:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا جَاءَتْهُمْ آيَاتُنَا مُبْصِرَةً قَالُوْا هَذَا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ falammā jāathum āyātunā mub'ṣiratan qālū hādhā siḥ'run mubīnun But when Our signs came to them, as eye-openers, they said, 'This is plain magic.'

item.title: An-Naml:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا جَاءَتْهُمْ آيَاتُنَا مُبْصِرَةً قَالُوْا هَذَا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ falammā jāathum āyātunā mub'ṣiratan qālū hādhā siḥ'run mubīnun But when there came to them Our visible signs, they said, "This is obvious magic." See 27:7
