Ali Ibn Abi Talib, the first Holy Imam says that even if the whole of the Qur'an is made extinct by the forces of evil and if there…

item.title: Ar-Ra'd:40 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنْ مَا نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعْضَ الَّذِي نَعِدُهُمْ أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ الْبَلَاغُ وَعَلَيْنَا الْحِسَابُ wa-in mā nuriyannaka baʿḍa alladhī naʿiduhum aw natawaffayannaka fa-innamā ʿalayka l-balāghu waʿalaynā l-ḥisābu Whether We show you a part of what We promise them,1 or take you away [before that], your duty is only to communicate, and it is for Us to do the reckoning.

item.title: Ar-Ra'd:40 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنْ مَا نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعْضَ الَّذِي نَعِدُهُمْ أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ الْبَلَاغُ وَعَلَيْنَا الْحِسَابُ wa-in mā nuriyannaka baʿḍa alladhī naʿiduhum aw natawaffayannaka fa-innamā ʿalayka l-balāghu waʿalaynā l-ḥisābu And whether We show you part of what We promise them or take you in death, upon you is only the (duty of) notification, and upon Us is the account. Whether We show you part of what We have promised them or cause you to die, your duty is only to convey (the Message) and on Us is the reckoning (13:40). See they not that We gradually reduce the land from its outlying borders. And Allah judges, there is none to put back His judgement, and He is swift at reckoning (13:41). Punishment is by Allah, and the Messenger's Job is Only to Convey the Message Allah said to His Messenger SAW: وَإِن مَّا…

item.title: Ar-Ra'd:40 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنْ مَا نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعْضَ الَّذِي نَعِدُهُمْ أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ الْبَلَاغُ وَعَلَيْنَا الْحِسَابُ wa-in mā nuriyannaka baʿḍa alladhī naʿiduhum aw natawaffayannaka fa-innamā ʿalayka l-balāghu waʿalaynā l-ḥisābu And We will either show thee a part of what We promised (Threatened with.) them or take unto ourselves thy soul (makes no difference), for verily on thee is (incumbent) only the delivery of the message and on Us the calling them to account. See 13:39

item.title: Ar-Ra'd:41 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا نَأْتِي الْأَرْضَ نَنْقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا وَاللَّهُ يَحْكُمُ لَا مُعَقِّبَ لِحُكْمِهِ وَهُوَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ awalam yaraw annā natī l-arḍa nanquṣuhā min aṭrāfihā wal-lahu yaḥkumu lā muʿaqqiba liḥuk'mihi wahuwa sarīʿu l-ḥisābi Have they not seen how We visit the land diminishing it at its edges? Allah judges, and there is none who may repeal His judgement, and He is swift at reckoning.

item.title: Ar-Ra'd:41 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا نَأْتِي الْأَرْضَ نَنْقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا وَاللَّهُ يَحْكُمُ لَا مُعَقِّبَ لِحُكْمِهِ وَهُوَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ awalam yaraw annā natī l-arḍa nanquṣuhā min aṭrāfihā wal-lahu yaḥkumu lā muʿaqqiba liḥuk'mihi wahuwa sarīʿu l-ḥisābi Have they not seen that We set upon the land, reducing it from its borders?1 And Allah decides; there is no adjuster of His decision. And He is swift in account. See 13:40

item.title: Ar-Ra'd:41 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا نَأْتِي الْأَرْضَ نَنْقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا وَاللَّهُ يَحْكُمُ لَا مُعَقِّبَ لِحُكْمِهِ وَهُوَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ awalam yaraw annā natī l-arḍa nanquṣuhā min aṭrāfihā wal-lahu yaḥkumu lā muʿaqqiba liḥuk'mihi wahuwa sarīʿu l-ḥisābi See they not that We come (Visit - through wrath-like floods - earth quakes, epidemics - which affect the land and the people - which take place in turns.) into their land and reduce its borders? Verily, God pronounceth a doom; there is no reverser for His command and He is swift in reckoning. See 13:39

item.title: Ar-Ra'd:42 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَدْ مَكَرَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ فَلِلَّهِ الْمَكْرُ جَمِيعًا يَعْلَمُ مَا تَكْسِبُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ وَسَيَعْلَمُ الْكُفَّارُ لِمَنْ عُقْبٰی الدَّارِ waqad makara alladhīna min qablihim falillahi l-makru jamīʿan yaʿlamu mā taksibu kullu nafsin wasayaʿlamu l-kufāru liman ʿuq'bā l-dāri Those who were before them [also] schemed;1 yet all devising belongs to Allah. He knows what every soul earns. Soon the faithless will know in whose favour the outcome of that abode will be.

item.title: Ar-Ra'd:42 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَدْ مَكَرَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ فَلِلَّهِ الْمَكْرُ جَمِيعًا يَعْلَمُ مَا تَكْسِبُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ وَسَيَعْلَمُ الْكُفَّارُ لِمَنْ عُقْبٰی الدَّارِ waqad makara alladhīna min qablihim falillahi l-makru jamīʿan yaʿlamu mā taksibu kullu nafsin wasayaʿlamu l-kufāru liman ʿuq'bā l-dāri And those before them had plotted, but to Allah belongs the plan entirely. He knows what every soul earns, and the disbelievers will know for whom is the final home. And verily, those before them did devise plots, but all planning is Allah's. He knows what every person earns, and the disbelievers will know who gets the good end (final destination) (13:42). The Disbelievers Plot, but the Believers Gain the Good End Allah says: وَقَدْ مَكَرَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ And verily, those before them did devise plots, against their Messengers, they wanted to expel them from their land, but Allah devised plots against the…

item.title: Ar-Ra'd:42 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَدْ مَكَرَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ فَلِلَّهِ الْمَكْرُ جَمِيعًا يَعْلَمُ مَا تَكْسِبُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ وَسَيَعْلَمُ الْكُفَّارُ لِمَنْ عُقْبٰی الدَّارِ waqad makara alladhīna min qablihim falillahi l-makru jamīʿan yaʿlamu mā taksibu kullu nafsin wasayaʿlamu l-kufāru liman ʿuq'bā l-dāri And indeed devised plots those before them but God's is all planning; Knoweth He whatever every soul earneth, and soon will know the disbelievers for whom is the sequel of the eternal abode. See 13:39

item.title: Ar-Ra'd:43 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا لَسْتَ مُرْسَلًا قُلْ كَفَى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ وَمَنْ عِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ الْكِتَابِ wayaqūlu alladhīna kafarū lasta mur'salan qul kafā bil-lahi shahīdan baynī wabaynakum waman ʿindahu ʿil'mu l-kitābi The faithless say, 'You have not been sent [by Allah].' Say, 'Allah suffices as a witness between me and you, and he who possesses the knowledge of the Book.'

item.title: Ar-Ra'd:43 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا لَسْتَ مُرْسَلًا قُلْ كَفَى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ وَمَنْ عِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ الْكِتَابِ wayaqūlu alladhīna kafarū lasta mur'salan qul kafā bil-lahi shahīdan baynī wabaynakum waman ʿindahu ʿil'mu l-kitābi And those who have disbelieved say, "You are not a messenger." Say, (O Muḥammad), "Sufficient is Allah as Witness between me and you, and (the witness of) whoever has knowledge of the Scripture."1 And those who disbelieved, say: You are not a Messenger." Say: "Sufficient as a witness between me and you is Allah and those too who have knowledge of the Scripture (13:43). Allah and those who have Knowledge of the Scripture are Sufficient As Witness to the Message of the Prophet SAW Allah says, the disbelievers reject you and say: لَسْتَ مُرْسَلًا You are not a Messenger. from Allah: قُلْ كَفَىٰ بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ Say: "Sufficient as…

item.title: Ar-Ra'd:43 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا لَسْتَ مُرْسَلًا قُلْ كَفَى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ وَمَنْ عِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ الْكِتَابِ wayaqūlu alladhīna kafarū lasta mur'salan qul kafā bil-lahi shahīdan baynī wabaynakum waman ʿindahu ʿil'mu l-kitābi And say those who disbelieve: "Thou art not an apostle (of God)," Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!): "Sufficient is God a witness between me and you and he with whom is the knowledge of the (Refer to verse 2:1. Qur'an or the Open Book of the Universe or Lauhe Mahfooz see note to verses 13:39 & 13:43.) Book." By 'the one who has the knowledge of the Book' (13:43) means the one who is divinely endowed with the fullest of the inner as well as the outer meaning of the Word of God. People asked the Holy Prophet as to who the individual is. The Holy Prophet replied, 'My…

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلرَّحْمَنُ al-raḥmānu The All-beneficent

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلرَّحْمَنُ al-raḥmānu The Most Merciful. فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny? Meaning: "O mankind and Jinn, which of the favors that Allah has given to you do you deny?" Mujahid and others said this, and it is apparent when one reads what comes after it. Meaning the favors that are obvious to you while you are surrounded by them, you cannot deny or reject them. So we say, just as the believers among the Jinns said, "O Allah! None of Your favors do we deny. All praise is due to You." Ibn 'Abbas used to say, "Nay, our Lord!" meaning, "None of Your favors do we deny."

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلرَّحْمَنُ al-raḥmānu (God) The Beneficent It is only the Beneficent God who taught the Holy Qur'an - The Teacher is mentioned to be God, and the Thing taught, i.e., the Book, is said to be the Holy Qur'an, but the question arises, as to who was the student, for there could be none of the mankind, for in the verse, the creation of man, comes after the teaching takes place. It is self-evident that the Beneficent God, first conditioned the soul with the Qur'anic knowledge and then the soul was accommodated into a human frame. Of the attributes presenting God's actions the most comprehensive is Rahman1 - and according to Qur'an the Holy Prophet is the sole manifestation and this attribute of God2, meaning that his mission represents the Universal grace of the Absolute (A.P.).

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: عَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ ʿallama l-qur'āna has taught the Qur'ān.

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: عَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ ʿallama l-qur'āna Taught the Qur’ān. See 55:1

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: عَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ ʿallama l-qur'āna Taught He the Qur'an The Qur'an is the manifestation of the Universal grace, and God Himself is the Teacher (A.P.).

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: خَلَقَ الْاِنْسَانَ khalaqa l-insāna He created man,

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: خَلَقَ الْاِنْسَانَ khalaqa l-insāna Created man. See 55:1

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: خَلَقَ الْاِنْسَانَ khalaqa l-insāna He created man (Refer to Verses 2:30 - 2:38; 15:26 - 15:29; 32:9.) The man referred to here, could never be meant to be a sinner - man of an ordinary order. When a quality is indefinitely mentioned, it means the perfect degree of it. It must be remembered that sinning is a later occurrence in the mankind subsequent to the creation of the First man, and when the Fist man was created the individual must naturally have been with the purity or the divinity of the Creator, reflecting in him. The purity or the divinity was in the sense of the knowledge, the man was charged with. The reflection of the knowledge or the divinity in the human soul was originating directly from the Beneficent God. Beneficent in this regard because. He wills it by…

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: عَلَّمَهُ الْبَيَانَ ʿallamahu l-bayāna [and] taught him articulate speech.

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: عَلَّمَهُ الْبَيَانَ ʿallamahu l-bayāna (And) taught him eloquence. See 55:1

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: عَلَّمَهُ الْبَيَانَ ʿallamahu l-bayāna He taught him expression (The power of speech and expression. Refer to Verses 2:31; 3:138.) 'Biyan', i.e., the means of expressing one's mind - 'Biyan' has also been used for the Holy Qur'an1. Taking the word for the art of verbal expression of the ideas, the Holy Qur'an which is the only record of what spoke out the Holy Prophet, is such a wonderful verbal expression which, in spite of its open challenge2, the world would never till now produce an equal even to the smallest chapter of it. It is further said that even if mankind as a whole and jinns joining with them, try to produce an equal to the Holy Qur'an they shall never be able to do it at all3. As regards the daily discourses, the utterance of the Holy Prophet was…

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ بِحُسْبَانٍ al-shamsu wal-qamaru biḥus'bānin The sun and the moon are [disposed] calculatedly,

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ بِحُسْبَانٍ al-shamsu wal-qamaru biḥus'bānin The sun and the moon (move) by precise calculation. See 55:1

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ بِحُسْبَانٍ al-shamsu wal-qamaru biḥus'bānin The sun and the moon follow the (prescribed) timings (Refer to Verses 13:2; 21:33; 36:38.) The astronomical constitution of the universe is bound by such strict, universal and fixed mathematical laws and calculations and are continuously going on with its work, in such an unchanging manner, that men could depend upon the knowledge of the heavenly bodies without any fear of any change or alteration in the original laws. This verse refers to two of the major heavenly bodies, the sun and the moon, following the computed courses in the prescribed order. This announcement of the natural phenomenon active in the heavens, was made at a time when the world was indulged only in mere conjectures about the astronomical world1.

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالنَّجْمُ وَالشَّجَرُ يَسْجُدَانِ wal-najmu wal-shajaru yasjudāni and the herb and the tree prostrate [to Allah].

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالنَّجْمُ وَالشَّجَرُ يَسْجُدَانِ wal-najmu wal-shajaru yasjudāni And the stars and trees prostrate.1 See 55:1

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالنَّجْمُ وَالشَّجَرُ يَسْجُدَانِ wal-najmu wal-shajaru yasjudāni And the herbs and the trees do obeisance (unto Him) (Refer to Verses 13:4; 16:48; 16:49; 22:18.) Prostration here means submitting to the law of the Lord, i.e., serving them - never going against their respective native endowments. It is in this sense that all nature adores God, its Creator Lord1. Everything in the heavens and in the earth adores God.

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالسَّمَاءَ رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ الْمِيزَانَ wal-samāa rafaʿahā wawaḍaʿa l-mīzāna He raised the sky and set up the balance,

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالسَّمَاءَ رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ الْمِيزَانَ wal-samāa rafaʿahā wawaḍaʿa l-mīzāna And the heaven He raised and imposed the balance. See 55:1

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالسَّمَاءَ رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ الْمِيزَانَ wal-samāa rafaʿahā wawaḍaʿa l-mīzāna And the heaven, He did raise it high, and placed the scale (within reach) (Refer to Verses 42:17; 52:25.) The perfect man as the microcosm is the infallible scale with which the truth of the Universe and the right and wrong, of human action should be measured and viewing the Holy Prophet as such Abu Talib says: 'The Scale of Truth which defaults not even Io an atom - and weigher of the justice his weighing falleth not short' (A.P.).

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَّا تَطْغَوْا فِي الْمِيزَانِ allā taṭghaw fī l-mīzāni declaring, 'Do not infringe the balance!

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَّا تَطْغَوْا فِي الْمِيزَانِ allā taṭghaw fī l-mīzāni That you not transgress within the balance. See 55:1

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَّا تَطْغَوْا فِي الْمِيزَانِ allā taṭghaw fī l-mīzāni So that ye may not transgress in scales See 55:7

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَقِيمُوْۤا الْوَزْنَ بِالْقِسْطِ وَلَا تُخْسِرُوْۤا الْمِيزَانَ wa-aqīmū l-wazna bil-qis'ṭi walā tukh'sirū l-mīzāna Maintain the weights with justice, and do not shorten the balance!'

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَقِيمُوْۤا الْوَزْنَ بِالْقِسْطِ وَلَا تُخْسِرُوْۤا الْمِيزَانَ wa-aqīmū l-wazna bil-qis'ṭi walā tukh'sirū l-mīzāna And establish weight in justice and do not make deficient the balance. See 55:1

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَقِيمُوْۤا الْوَزْنَ بِالْقِسْطِ وَلَا تُخْسِرُوْۤا الْمِيزَانَ wa-aqīmū l-wazna bil-qis'ṭi walā tukh'sirū l-mīzāna And maintain ye the measure with justice and do not cut short in the scale (Refer to Verses 49:1; 57:28.) See 55:7

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْأَرْضَ وَضَعَهَا لِلْأَنَامِ wal-arḍa waḍaʿahā lil'anāmi And the earth, He laid it out for mankind.

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْأَرْضَ وَضَعَهَا لِلْأَنَامِ wal-arḍa waḍaʿahā lil'anāmi And the earth He laid (out) for the creatures. See 55:1

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْأَرْضَ وَضَعَهَا لِلْأَنَامِ wal-arḍa waḍaʿahā lil'anāmi And the earth, He hath made (Made it available (A.P.).) it for (His) (living) creatures Made it available. The right of opportunity shall be maintained and that none shall be deprived of the opportunity (A.P.).

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيهَا فَاكِهَةٌ وَالنَّخْلُ ذَاتُ الْأَكْمَامِ fīhā fākihatun wal-nakhlu dhātu l-akmāmi In it are fruits and date-palms with sheaths,

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيهَا فَاكِهَةٌ وَالنَّخْلُ ذَاتُ الْأَكْمَامِ fīhā fākihatun wal-nakhlu dhātu l-akmāmi Therein is fruit and palm trees having sheaths (of dates). See 55:1

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيهَا فَاكِهَةٌ وَالنَّخْلُ ذَاتُ الْأَكْمَامِ fīhā fākihatun wal-nakhlu dhātu l-akmāmi Therein is fruit and palms having, sheathed clusters See 55:10

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْحَبُّ ذُو الْعَصْفِ وَالرَّيْحَانُ wal-ḥabu dhū l-ʿaṣfi wal-rayḥānu grain with husk, and fragrant herbs.

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْحَبُّ ذُو الْعَصْفِ وَالرَّيْحَانُ wal-ḥabu dhū l-ʿaṣfi wal-rayḥānu And grain having husks and scented plants. See 55:1

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْحَبُّ ذُو الْعَصْفِ وَالرَّيْحَانُ wal-ḥabu dhū l-ʿaṣfi wal-rayḥānu And corn with (its) leaves and stalks and with sweet-smelling herbs See 55:10

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibāni So which of your Lord's bounties will you both1 deny?

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibāni So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?1 See 55:1

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:13 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibāni Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye two (men and jinns (Ref to the note on jinn.) ) (Or man and woman) belie? The question is to both the human beings and the jinns, (i.e., beings other than mankind) who are enjoying alike the bounties of the Lord.

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:14 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: خَلَقَ الْاِنْسَانَ مِنْ صَلْصَالٍ كَالْفَخَّارِ khalaqa l-insāna min ṣalṣālin kal-fakhāri He created man out of dry clay,1 like the potter's,

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:14 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: خَلَقَ الْاِنْسَانَ مِنْ صَلْصَالٍ كَالْفَخَّارِ khalaqa l-insāna min ṣalṣālin kal-fakhāri He created man from clay like (that of) pottery. He created man from sounding clay like the clay of pottery (55:14). And the Jinn He created from a smokeless flame of fire (55:15). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny (55:16). The Lord of the two easts and the Lord of the two wests (55:17). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny (55:18). He has Maraja the two seas meeting together (55:19). Between them is a barrier which none of them can transgress (55:20). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny (55:21). Out of them both come out pearls and Al-Marjan (55:22). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny (55:23).…

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:14 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: خَلَقَ الْاِنْسَانَ مِنْ صَلْصَالٍ كَالْفَخَّارِ khalaqa l-insāna min ṣalṣālin kal-fakhāri He created man from dry clay like that of the earthen vessels See 55:13

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَخَلَقَ الْجَانَّ مِنْ مَارِجٍ مِنْ نَارٍ wakhalaqa l-jāna min mārijin min nārin and created the jinn out of a flame of a fire.

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَخَلَقَ الْجَانَّ مِنْ مَارِجٍ مِنْ نَارٍ wakhalaqa l-jāna min mārijin min nārin And He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire. See 55:14

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَخَلَقَ الْجَانَّ مِنْ مَارِجٍ مِنْ نَارٍ wakhalaqa l-jāna min mārijin min nārin And created He the jinn of a flame of fire (It is made clear that the Jinn are a separate specie with a nature quite different from human beings. Refer to Verses 7:12; 15:27.) See 55:13

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibāni So which of your Lord's bounties will you both deny?

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibāni So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny? See 55:14

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibāni Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye two belie? See 55:13

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ وَرَبُّ الْمَغْرِبَيْنِ rabbu l-mashriqayni warabbu l-maghribayni Lord of the two easts, and Lord of the two wests!1

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ وَرَبُّ الْمَغْرِبَيْنِ rabbu l-mashriqayni warabbu l-maghribayni (He is) Lord of the two sunrises and Lord of the two sunsets.1 See 55:14

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:17 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ وَرَبُّ الْمَغْرِبَيْنِ rabbu l-mashriqayni warabbu l-maghribayni (He alone is the) Lord of the two easts and the Lord of the two wests (Refer to Verses 7:137; 37:5; 70:40.) See 55:13

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:18 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibāni So which of your Lord's bounties will you both deny?

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:18 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibāni So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny? See 55:14

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:18 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibāni Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye two (Twain - may be Man and Woman or - Men and Jinn.) belie? See 55:13

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:19 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ يَلْتَقِيَانِ maraja l-baḥrayni yaltaqiyāni He merged the two seas,1 meeting each other.

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:19 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ يَلْتَقِيَانِ maraja l-baḥrayni yaltaqiyāni He released the two seas,1 meeting (one another). See 55:14

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:19 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ يَلْتَقِيَانِ maraja l-baḥrayni yaltaqiyāni He hath let loose the two seas that they flow together meeting each other (Refer to Verses 18:60; 25:52; 35:12.) See 55:13

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:20 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخٌ لَا يَبْغِيَانِ baynahumā barzakhun lā yabghiyāni There is a barrier between them which they do not overstep.

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:20 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخٌ لَا يَبْغِيَانِ baynahumā barzakhun lā yabghiyāni Between them is a barrier so neither of them transgresses. See 55:14

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:20 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخٌ لَا يَبْغِيَانِ baynahumā barzakhun lā yabghiyāni (Yet) between them (He hath caused) a barrier, (that) they encroach not (one upon another) The Holy Prophet said: "The meeting of the Two Seas indicates the matrimonial union between 'Ali and Fatimah and the 'Barzakh'. i.e., the Barrier between the Two Seas is the Holy Prophet and the coming out of the Pearl and Coral - Hasan and Husayn." This is the report of Ibn Mardwaih, Ibn Abbas, Anas Ibn Malik1 (M.S.). This is true of many geographical flowing of the seas with the barrier between them but it also figuratively has been applied by the Imams of the Ahl Al-Bayt to the two Streams of 'Nubuwwah', Prophethood, and 'Wilayah' which flew together and yet with distinctive barriers preventing the two divine functions from encroaching on each other creating any confusion.…

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:21 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibāni So which of your Lord's bounties will you both deny?

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:21 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibāni So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny? See 55:14

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:21 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibāni Which then of the bounties your Lord will ye two belie? See 55:20

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:22 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالْمَرْجَانُ yakhruju min'humā l-lu'lu-u wal-marjānu From them emerge the pearl and the coral.

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:22 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالْمَرْجَانُ yakhruju min'humā l-lu'lu-u wal-marjānu From both of them emerge pearl and coral. See 55:14

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:22 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالْمَرْجَانُ yakhruju min'humā l-lu'lu-u wal-marjānu Come forth out of the two, pearls and corals See 55:20

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:23 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibāni So which of your Lord's bounties will you both deny?

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:23 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibāni So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny? See 55:14

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:23 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibāni Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye two belie? See 55:20

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:24 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَهُ الْجَوَارِ الْمُنْشَءَاتُ فِي الْبَحْرِ كَالْأَعْلَامِ walahu l-jawāri l-munshaātu fī l-baḥri kal-aʿlāmi His are the sailing ships1 on the sea [appearing] like landmarks.

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:24 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَهُ الْجَوَارِ الْمُنْشَءَاتُ فِي الْبَحْرِ كَالْأَعْلَامِ walahu l-jawāri l-munshaātu fī l-baḥri kal-aʿlāmi And to Him belong the ships (with sails) elevated in the sea like mountains. See 55:14

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:24 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَهُ الْجَوَارِ الْمُنْشَءَاتُ فِي الْبَحْرِ كَالْأَعْلَامِ walahu l-jawāri l-munshaātu fī l-baḥri kal-aʿlāmi And His are the ships (This may refer the physical ships or in a figurative sense to the offsprings of the Holy Prophet. Refer to the tradition: 'The likeness of my Ahl Al-Bayt is that of the Ark of Noah'. Etc., Etc.) towering up at the sea like mountains See 55:20

item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibāni So which of your Lord's bounties will you both deny?

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:26 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍ kullu man ʿalayhā fānin Everyone on it1 is ephemeral,

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:26 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍ kullu man ʿalayhā fānin Everyone upon it (i.e., the earth) will perish. Whatsoever is on it (the earth) will perish (55:26). And the Face of your Lord Dhul-Jalal wal-Ikram will remain forever (55:27). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny (55:28). Whosoever is in the heavens and on the earth begs of Him. Every day He is (engaged) in some affair (55:29). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny (55:30). Allah is the Ever Living, Free of All Need Allah states that all the residents of earth will perish and die. The residents of the heavens will die, except whomever Allah wills. Only Allah's Honorable Face will remain, because our Lord, the Exalted, the Blessed, is the Ever Living Who never dies. Qatadah said, "First, Allah…

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:26 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍ kullu man ʿalayhā fānin Every one on it shall perish See 55:20

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:27 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَبْقَى وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ wayabqā wajhu rabbika dhū l-jalāli wal-ik'rāmi yet lasting is the Face of your Lord, majestic and munificent.1

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:27 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَبْقَى وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ wayabqā wajhu rabbika dhū l-jalāli wal-ik'rāmi And there will remain the Face1 of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor. See 55:26

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:27 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَبْقَى وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ wayabqā wajhu rabbika dhū l-jalāli wal-ik'rāmi But will remain for ever the Face (The countenance.) of thy Lord, the Glorious and Gracious (Refer to Verse 2:112.) The face stands for the cognisable part of a personality. Here, it means the existence of God which is cognisant through His attributes1. Meaning the most glorious and gracious face of the Lord which in last verse of the same sura the same attributes are used for the Lord Himself. Reading all these verses together it shows that everything is perishable except God's face - countenance which is eternal and whatever is with Him2 (A.P.).

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:29 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَسْءَلُهُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ هُوَ فِي شَأْنٍ yasaluhu man fī l-samāwāti wal-arḍi kulla yawmin huwa fī shanin Everyone in the heavens and the earth asks Him. Every day He is engaged in some work.

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:29 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَسْءَلُهُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ هُوَ فِي شَأْنٍ yasaluhu man fī l-samāwāti wal-arḍi kulla yawmin huwa fī shanin Whoever is within the heavens and earth asks Him; every day He is in (i.e., bringing about) a matter.1 See 55:26

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:29 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَسْءَلُهُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ هُوَ فِي شَأْنٍ yasaluhu man fī l-samāwāti wal-arḍi kulla yawmin huwa fī shanin Beseech Him all those in the heavens and the earth; Every day He is in a (new) splendorous manifestation (State glorious.) The day here, applies not only to the ordinary duration of 24 hours but includes all the divine days1, i.e., any period in which some development takes place and this indicates the ever-evolutionary expansion of the universe. Although the movement is rotational, hence no room for the recurrence of events (A.P.).

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:30 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:31 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: سَنَفْرُغُ لَكُمْ أَيُّهَ الثَّقَلَانِ sanafrughu lakum ayyuha l-thaqalāni We shall soon make Ourselves unoccupied for you, O you notable two!1

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:31 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: سَنَفْرُغُ لَكُمْ أَيُّهَ الثَّقَلَانِ sanafrughu lakum ayyuha l-thaqalāni We will attend to you, O prominent beings.1 We shall attend to you, O Thaqalan (55:31). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny (55:32). O assembly of Jinn and men! If you are able to pass beyond the zones of the heavens and the earth, then pass beyond (them)! But you will never be able to pass them, except with authority (from Allah) (55:33). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny (55:34). There will be sent against you both, Shuwāz of fire and Nuhas, and you will not be able to defend yourselves (55:35). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny) ur Lord will you both deny (55:36). A Warning for Humans and Jinn Ibn Jurayj said…

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:31 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: سَنَفْرُغُ لَكُمْ أَيُّهَ الثَّقَلَانِ sanafrughu lakum ayyuha l-thaqalāni Soon will We attend to you, O' ye two groups (of men and jinns) See 55:29

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:33 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَامَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ أَنْ تَنْفُذُوْۤا مِنْ أَقْطَارِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ فَانْفُذُوا لَا تَنْفُذُونَ إِلَّا بِسُلْطَانٍ yāmaʿshara l-jini wal-insi ini is'taṭaʿtum an tanfudhū min aqṭāri l-samāwāti wal-arḍi fa-unfudhū lā tanfudhūna illā bisul'ṭānin O company of jinn and humans! If you can pass through the confines of the heavens and the earth, then do pass through. But you will not pass through except by an authority [from Allah].

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:33 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَامَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ أَنْ تَنْفُذُوْۤا مِنْ أَقْطَارِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ فَانْفُذُوا لَا تَنْفُذُونَ إِلَّا بِسُلْطَانٍ yāmaʿshara l-jini wal-insi ini is'taṭaʿtum an tanfudhū min aqṭāri l-samāwāti wal-arḍi fa-unfudhū lā tanfudhūna illā bisul'ṭānin O company of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass. You will not pass except by authority (from Allah). See 55:31

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:33 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَامَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ أَنْ تَنْفُذُوْۤا مِنْ أَقْطَارِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ فَانْفُذُوا لَا تَنْفُذُونَ إِلَّا بِسُلْطَانٍ yāmaʿshara l-jini wal-insi ini is'taṭaʿtum an tanfudhū min aqṭāri l-samāwāti wal-arḍi fa-unfudhū lā tanfudhūna illā bisul'ṭānin O ye peoples of jinn and humans, if ye can penetrate (Pass through.) the bounds (The length and breadth.) of the heavens and the earth, then do penetrate ye through; (But) ye cannot penetrate but with (Our) authority! (Refer to Verses 6:129 - 6:134; 72:1; 55:33; 28:37.) This Verse clearly recognises the possibility of man going beyond the zones separating the heavens and the earth if he acquires knowledge by observation and contemplation, mentioned in the commentary of verse 55:5, a theory considered impossible till the journey of man began in space. If any attempt is made without knowing the laws made by Allah to govern the creation…

item.description: يُرْسَلُ عَلَيْكُمَا شُوَاظٌ مِنْ نَارٍ وَنُحَاسٌ فَلَا تَنْتَصِرَانِ yur'salu ʿalaykumā shuwāẓun min nārin wanuḥāsun falā tantaṣirāni There will be unleashed upon you a flash of fire and a smoke; then you will not be able to help one another.

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:35 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يُرْسَلُ عَلَيْكُمَا شُوَاظٌ مِنْ نَارٍ وَنُحَاسٌ فَلَا تَنْتَصِرَانِ yur'salu ʿalaykumā shuwāẓun min nārin wanuḥāsun falā tantaṣirāni There will be sent upon you a flame of fire and smoke,1 and you will not defend yourselves. See 55:31

item.description: يُرْسَلُ عَلَيْكُمَا شُوَاظٌ مِنْ نَارٍ وَنُحَاسٌ فَلَا تَنْتَصِرَانِ yur'salu ʿalaykumā shuwāẓun min nārin wanuḥāsun falā tantaṣirāni On ye two shall be sent the flames of fire and molten brass, then ye shall not be able to protect yourselves In case you attempt at penetration without the authority - the consequences are failure, disaster and destruction (A.P.).

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:37 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِذَا انْشَقَّتِ السَّمَاءُ فَكَانَتْ وَرْدَةً كَالدِّهَانِ fa-idhā inshaqqati l-samāu fakānat wardatan kal-dihāni When the sky is split open, and turns crimson like tanned leather.

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:37 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِذَا انْشَقَّتِ السَّمَاءُ فَكَانَتْ وَرْدَةً كَالدِّهَانِ fa-idhā inshaqqati l-samāu fakānat wardatan kal-dihāni And when the heaven is split open and becomes rose-colored like oil1. Then when the heaven is rent asunder, and it becomes Wardah like Dihan (55:37). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny (55:38). So, on that Day he will not be questioned about his sin, (neither) human nor Jinn (55:39). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny (55:40). The criminals will be known by their marks, and they will be seized by their foreheads and feet (55:41). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny (55:42). This is the Hell which the criminals denied (55:43). They will go between it and Ḥamīm Ān (55:44). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will…

item.description: فَإِذَا انْشَقَّتِ السَّمَاءُ فَكَانَتْ وَرْدَةً كَالدِّهَانِ fa-idhā inshaqqati l-samāu fakānat wardatan kal-dihāni And when is rent asunder the heaven, then it becometh red like the tanned hide See 55:35

item.description: فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لَا يُسْءَلُ عَنْ ذَنْبِهِ إِنْسٌ وَلَا جَانٌّ fayawma-idhin lā yus'alu ʿan dhanbihi insun walā jānnun On that day neither humans will be questioned about their sins nor jinn.1

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:39 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لَا يُسْءَلُ عَنْ ذَنْبِهِ إِنْسٌ وَلَا جَانٌّ fayawma-idhin lā yus'alu ʿan dhanbihi insun walā jānnun Then on that Day none will be asked about his sin among men or jinn.1 See 55:37

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:39 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لَا يُسْءَلُ عَنْ ذَنْبِهِ إِنْسٌ وَلَا جَانٌّ fayawma-idhin lā yus'alu ʿan dhanbihi insun walā jānnun And on that Day shall not be asked (None need say or testify for the very bodies of the men and the jinn will say out every thing.) man nor jinn of his sin (Refer to Verses 24:24; 36:65.) The deeds good and bad, of every individual will be so much self-proved, that there would not be any necessity of asking anyone, whether he accepts the report about his conduct and character or not, nor would the convicts be asked for any explanation as to why he did it. Every case will be self-proved and the ultimate state of every individual self-evident. The very organs of the body of every individual would bear witness1. It indicates that this does not refer to the Final…

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:41 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يُعْرَفُ الْمُجْرِمُونَ بِسِيمَاهُمْ فَيُؤْخَذُ بِالنَّوَاصِي وَالْأَقْدَامِ yuʿ'rafu l-muj'rimūna bisīmāhum fayu'khadhu bil-nawāṣī wal-aqdāmi The guilty will be recognized by their mark; so they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet.

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:41 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يُعْرَفُ الْمُجْرِمُونَ بِسِيمَاهُمْ فَيُؤْخَذُ بِالنَّوَاصِي وَالْأَقْدَامِ yuʿ'rafu l-muj'rimūna bisīmāhum fayu'khadhu bil-nawāṣī wal-aqdāmi The criminals will be known by their marks, and they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet. See 55:37

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:41 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يُعْرَفُ الْمُجْرِمُونَ بِسِيمَاهُمْ فَيُؤْخَذُ بِالنَّوَاصِي وَالْأَقْدَامِ yuʿ'rafu l-muj'rimūna bisīmāhum fayu'khadhu bil-nawāṣī wal-aqdāmi The guilty ones shall be re-cognised by their marks, and they shall be seized by their forelocks and their feet See 55:39

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:43 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: هَذِهِ جَهَنَّمُ الَّتِي يُكَذِّبُ بِهَا الْمُجْرِمُونَ hādhihi jahannamu allatī yukadhibu bihā l-muj'rimūna 'This is the hell which the guilty would deny!'

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:43 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: هَذِهِ جَهَنَّمُ الَّتِي يُكَذِّبُ بِهَا الْمُجْرِمُونَ hādhihi jahannamu allatī yukadhibu bihā l-muj'rimūna This is Hell, which the criminals deny. See 55:37

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:43 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:44 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَطُوفُونَ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَ حَمِيمٍ ءَانٍ yaṭūfūna baynahā wabayna ḥamīmin ānin They shall circuit between it and boiling hot water.

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:44 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَطُوفُونَ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَ حَمِيمٍ ءَانٍ yaṭūfūna baynahā wabayna ḥamīmin ānin They will circulate between it and scalding water, heated (to the utmost degree). See 55:37

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:44 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَطُوفُونَ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَ حَمِيمٍ ءَانٍ yaṭūfūna baynahā wabayna ḥamīmin ānin Around in it shall they run in hot, boiling water See 55:39

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:46 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلِمَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ جَنَّتَانِ waliman khāfa maqāma rabbihi jannatāni For him who stands in awe of his Lord will be two gardens.

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:46 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلِمَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ جَنَّتَانِ waliman khāfa maqāma rabbihi jannatāni But for he who has feared the position of his Lord1 are two gardens. But for him who fears the standing before his Lord, there will be two Gardens (55:46). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny (55:47). With Afnān (55:48). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny (55:49). In them (both) will be two springs flowing (free) (55:50). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both den (55:51). In them (both) will be every kind of fruit in pairs (55:52). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny (55:53). The Delight of Those Who have Taqwa in Paradise Allah the Exalted said: وَلِمَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ But for him who fears the…

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:46 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلِمَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ جَنَّتَانِ waliman khāfa maqāma rabbihi jannatāni And for him who feareth the time of standing before his Lord are two gardens (Corresponding to true faith and good deeds.) The Two Gardens, might mean variety of the blissful life the pious ones would have. Corresponding to the true faith and good deeds (A.P.).

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:47 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibāni So which of your Lord's bounties will you both deny?

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:48 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ذَوَاتَا أَفْنَانٍ dhawātā afnānin Both abounding in branches.1

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:48 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ذَوَاتَا أَفْنَانٍ dhawātā afnānin Having (spreading) branches. See 55:46

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:48 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ذَوَاتَا أَفْنَانٍ dhawātā afnānin With over-branching trees (in each of the two gardens) (The description of the heavenly bliss given here or anywhere in the Qur'an is figurative.) See 55:46

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:49 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibāni So which of your Lord's bounties will you both deny?

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:50 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيهِمَا عَيْنَانِ تَجْرِيَانِ fīhimā ʿaynāni tajriyāni In both of them will be two flowing springs.

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:50 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيهِمَا عَيْنَانِ تَجْرِيَانِ fīhimā ʿaynāni tajriyāni In both of them are two springs, flowing. See 55:46

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:50 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيهِمَا عَيْنَانِ تَجْرِيَانِ fīhimā ʿaynāni tajriyāni In both of them are two fountains flowing The Two Springs are called 'Tasneem' and 'Salsaheel' They could be of clean, clear and refreshing waters and of the delicious and pleasing drinks. The dual springs, here also, as in the case of the gardens might mean variety.

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:51 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran

item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibāni So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny? See 55:46

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:51 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibāni Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye two belie? See 55:50

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:52 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيهِمَا مِنْ كُلِّ فَاكِهَةٍ زَوْجَانِ fīhimā min kulli fākihatin zawjāni In both of them will be two kinds of every fruit.

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:52 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيهِمَا مِنْ كُلِّ فَاكِهَةٍ زَوْجَانِ fīhimā min kulli fākihatin zawjāni In both of them are of every fruit, two kinds. See 55:46

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:52 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيهِمَا مِنْ كُلِّ فَاكِهَةٍ زَوْجَانِ fīhimā min kulli fākihatin zawjāni In each of them, of every fruit, are two kinds (All sorts in praise, corresponding to the various aspects of true faith and good deeds (A.P.). Refer to Verse 13:3.) Ibn Abbas says there shall be no fruit of this world the like of which would not be in the heavens, besides there would be such other delicious fruits which would neither have had been seen nor tasted before. All sorts of fruits in pairs, corresponding to various aspects of true faith and good deeds. (A.P.)

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:54 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلَى فُرُشٍ بَطَائِنُهَا مِنْ إِسْتَبْرَقٍ وَجَنَى الْجَنَّتَيْنِ دَانٍ muttakiīna ʿalā furushin baṭāinuhā min is'tabraqin wajanā l-janatayni dānin [They will be] reclining on beds lined with green silk. And the fruit of the two gardens will be near at hand.

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:54 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلَى فُرُشٍ بَطَائِنُهَا مِنْ إِسْتَبْرَقٍ وَجَنَى الْجَنَّتَيْنِ دَانٍ muttakiīna ʿalā furushin baṭāinuhā min is'tabraqin wajanā l-janatayni dānin (They are) reclining on beds whose linings are of silk brocade, and the fruit of the two gardens is hanging low. Reclining upon the couches lined with Istabraq, and the fruits of the two Gardens will be near at hand (55:54). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny (55:55). Wherein both will be Qaşirāt Aṭ-Ṭarf, whom never deflowered a human before nor Jinn (55:56). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny (55:57). They are like Yaqut and Marjan (55:58). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny (55:59). Is there any reward for good other than good (55:60). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you…

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:54 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلَى فُرُشٍ بَطَائِنُهَا مِنْ إِسْتَبْرَقٍ وَجَنَى الْجَنَّتَيْنِ دَانٍ muttakiīna ʿalā furushin baṭāinuhā min is'tabraqin wajanā l-janatayni dānin Reclining on beds, the inner coverings of which are of silk brocade; the fruit of (both) the gardens shall be nigh (within easy reach) See 55:52

item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibāni So which of your Lord's bounties will you both deny?

item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibāni So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny? See 55:54

item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibāni Which then of the bounties of your Lord will ye two belie? See 55:52

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:56 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيهِنَّ قَاصِرَاتُ الطَّرْفِ لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ إِنْسٌ قَبْلَهُمْ وَلَا جَانٌّ fīhinna qāṣirātu l-ṭarfi lam yaṭmith'hunna insun qablahum walā jānnun In them are maidens of restrained glances, whom no human has touched before, nor jinn.

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:56 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيهِنَّ قَاصِرَاتُ الطَّرْفِ لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ إِنْسٌ قَبْلَهُمْ وَلَا جَانٌّ fīhinna qāṣirātu l-ṭarfi lam yaṭmith'hunna insun qablahum walā jānnun In them are women limiting (their) glances,1 untouched2 before them by man or jinnī. See 55:54

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:56 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فِيهِنَّ قَاصِرَاتُ الطَّرْفِ لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ إِنْسٌ قَبْلَهُمْ وَلَا جَانٌّ fīhinna qāṣirātu l-ṭarfi lam yaṭmith'hunna insun qablahum walā jānnun Therein shall be damsels with retiring glances, whom hath touched not ever before, any human being nor a jinn (Refer to Verses 37:48; 37:49; 44:54; 52:20; 56:22.) See 55:52

item.description: فَبِأَيِّ اٰلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ fabi-ayyi ālāi rabbikumā tukadhibāni So which of your Lord's bounties will you both deny?

item.description: كَأَنَّهُنَّ الْيَاقُوتُ وَالْمَرْجَانُ ka-annahunna l-yāqūtu wal-marjānu As though they were rubies and corals.

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:60 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: هَلْ جَزَاءُ الْإِحْسَانِ إِلَّا الْإِحْسَانُ hal jazāu l-iḥ'sāni illā l-iḥ'sānu Is the requital of goodness anything but goodness?

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:60 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: هَلْ جَزَاءُ الْإِحْسَانِ إِلَّا الْإِحْسَانُ hal jazāu l-iḥ'sāni illā l-iḥ'sānu Is the reward for good (anything) but good? See 55:54

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:60 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: هَلْ جَزَاءُ الْإِحْسَانِ إِلَّا الْإِحْسَانُ hal jazāu l-iḥ'sāni illā l-iḥ'sānu Is the recompense for good aught but good? (Refer to Verses 99:7; 99:8.) Note the simplest, shortest and the best expression given to the phenomenon of equity: The return for service to God, increase in the status. The thanksgiving, further increases the grant of the bounties. The piety brings enjoyment. The repentance earns forgiveness. The Holy Prophet said that he who declared God's unity saying: 'La ilaha illa Allah', shall have Paradise. The Holy Prophet said: "If you do any goodness in return for any goodness already done then the one who did it first shall he entitled to a greater reward for the good was one not in return, and if you want your goodness to earn a greater reward, then do more than the goodness what has been…

item.description: وَمِنْ دُونِهِمَا جَنَّتَانِ wamin dūnihimā jannatāni Beside these two, there will be two [other] gardens.

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:62 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمِنْ دُونِهِمَا جَنَّتَانِ wamin dūnihimā jannatāni And below them both (in excellence) are two (other) gardens. And below these two, there are two other Gardens (55:62). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny (55:63). Mudhāmmatān (55:64). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny (55:65). In them (both) will be two springs Naddakhatan (55:66). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny (55:67). In them (both) will be fruits, and date palms and pomegranates (55:68). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny (55:69). Therein (Gardens) will be Khayrat Hisan (55:70). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny (55:71). Hūr (beautiful, fair females) guarded in pavilions (55:72). Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both…

item.title: Ar-Rahmaan:62 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمِنْ دُونِهِمَا جَنَّتَانِ wamin dūnihimā jannatāni And besides these (two) are two other gardens Heavens (Paradise), will not be of any one single fixed nature or kind. There will be gardens or the places of eternal bliss of various kinds and degrees, even the sight of which would be giving pleasure and amusement - These places would be the environment of the blissful abode granted to the pious. Abu Basir asked the Sixth Holy Imam, Ja'far Ibn Muhammad As-Sadiq: "Master! would the believer-pious wife of a believer-pious man be the wife of the man also in the heaven?" The Holy Imam replied, "O' Abu-Muhammad! God is All-Just, if the husband be of a greater faith and piety than his wife, he will have the choice of having his wife as his mate and if the wife be greater than her…

Since God asks to which of His bounties or grace man can deny, it is desirable that the reciter of this Sura, whenever he recites the questioning clause, says 'La bi shayin min alayka Rabbi na kazzib', i.e., nothing of any of Thy bounties "O' Our Lord! do we deny?"1

item.title: Ar-Room:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: غُلِبَتِ الرُّومُ ghulibati l-rūmu The Byzantines have been defeated.1 See 30:1

item.title: Ar-Room:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: غُلِبَتِ الرُّومُ ghulibati l-rūmu The Romans have been defeated, (By the Persians.) In 614-616 A.D. the Romans under Heraclius were defeated by the Persians and the Roman Empire lost many of its territories. The pagans of Mecca rejoiced at the defeat of the Romans who were Christians, i.e., the people of the Book. The Muslims were grieved at the defeat of the Romans because Persians, the victors, were only fire-worshippers.1 The pagans of Mecca began taunting the Muslims saying that the fate of the Muslims would also be the same for they deemed it as an omen of their triumph upon the Muslims.

item.title: Ar-Room:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي أَدْنَى الْأَرْضِ وَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ fī adnā l-arḍi wahum min baʿdi ghalabihim sayaghlibūna in a nearby territory, but following their defeat they will be victors

item.title: Ar-Room:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي أَدْنَى الْأَرْضِ وَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ fī adnā l-arḍi wahum min baʿdi ghalabihim sayaghlibūna In the nearest land.1 But they, after their defeat, will overcome. See 30:1

item.title: Ar-Room:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي أَدْنَى الْأَرْضِ وَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ fī adnā l-arḍi wahum min baʿdi ghalabihim sayaghlibūna In a nearer land, (Near East.) but they after being defeated will soon be victorious, To console the grieved Muslims this verse was revealed prophesying the triumph of the Romans upon the Persians within a short period which is interpreted as seven to nine years, meaning that the enemies of Islam, i.e., the pagans of Mecca who rejoiced at the defeat of the Romans, would very soon be disillusioned both about the fate of the fire-worshippers of Persia and their own fate against the Muslims. The prophecy of the Holy Qur'an was fulfilled, i.e., in 624 A.D., Heraclius defeated Persia and at Badr (2 A.H.) the heathens of Mecca were beaten by the Muslims and this served also as a proof of the Holy…

item.title: Ar-Room:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي بِضْعِ سِنِينَ لِلَّهِ الْأَمْرُ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَمِنْ بَعْدُ وَيَوْمَئِذٍ يَفْرَحُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ fī biḍ'ʿi sinīna lillahi l-amru min qablu wamin baʿdu wayawma-idhin yafraḥu l-mu'minūna in a few years. All command belongs to Allah, before and after, and on that day the faithful will rejoice

item.title: Ar-Room:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي بِضْعِ سِنِينَ لِلَّهِ الْأَمْرُ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَمِنْ بَعْدُ وَيَوْمَئِذٍ يَفْرَحُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ fī biḍ'ʿi sinīna lillahi l-amru min qablu wamin baʿdu wayawma-idhin yafraḥu l-mu'minūna Within three to nine years. To Allah belongs the command (i.e., decree) before and after. And that day the believers will rejoice. See 30:1

item.title: Ar-Room:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فِي بِضْعِ سِنِينَ لِلَّهِ الْأَمْرُ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَمِنْ بَعْدُ وَيَوْمَئِذٍ يَفْرَحُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ fī biḍ'ʿi sinīna lillahi l-amru min qablu wamin baʿdu wayawma-idhin yafraḥu l-mu'minūna Within a (Ar. 'Bidh'i' i.e. a short period from 3 to 9 years 614 A.D. - to 622 A.D.) few years; God's is the authority before and after; and on that day the believers shall rejoice, See 30:3

item.title: Ar-Room:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: بِنَصْرِ اللَّهِ يَنْصُرُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ binaṣri l-lahi yanṣuru man yashāu wahuwa l-ʿazīzu l-raḥīmu at Allah's help. He helps whomever He wishes, and He is the All-mighty, the All-merciful.

item.title: Ar-Room:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: بِنَصْرِ اللَّهِ يَنْصُرُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ binaṣri l-lahi yanṣuru man yashāu wahuwa l-ʿazīzu l-raḥīmu In the victory of Allah.1 He gives victory to whom He wills, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful. See 30:1

item.title: Ar-Room:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: بِنَصْرِ اللَّهِ يَنْصُرُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ binaṣri l-lahi yanṣuru man yashāu wahuwa l-ʿazīzu l-raḥīmu With the aid of God; Aideth He whomsoever He willeth; And He is the All-Mighty, the All-Merciful, See 30:3

item.title: Ar-Room:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَعْدَ اللَّهِ لَا يُخْلِفُ اللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ waʿda l-lahi lā yukh'lifu l-lahu waʿdahu walākinna akthara l-nāsi lā yaʿlamūna [This is] a promise of Allah: Allah does not break His promise, but most people do not know.

item.title: Ar-Room:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَعْدَ اللَّهِ لَا يُخْلِفُ اللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ waʿda l-lahi lā yukh'lifu l-lahu waʿdahu walākinna akthara l-nāsi lā yaʿlamūna (It is) the promise of Allah. Allah does not fail in His promise, but most of the people do not know. See 30:1

item.title: Ar-Room:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَعْدَ اللَّهِ لَا يُخْلِفُ اللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ waʿda l-lahi lā yukh'lifu l-lahu waʿdahu walākinna akthara l-nāsi lā yaʿlamūna (This is) the promise of God! Faileth not God His promise, but most people know not (this). See 30:3

item.title: Ar-Room:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَعْلَمُونَ ظَاهِرًا مِنَ الْحَيَوةِ الدُّنْيَا وَهُمْ عَنِ الْاٰخِرَةُ هُمْ غَافِلُونَ yaʿlamūna ẓāhiran mina l-ḥayati l-dun'yā wahum ʿani l-ākhirati hum ghāfilūna They know just an outward aspect of the life of the world, but they are oblivious of the Hereafter.

item.title: Ar-Room:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَعْلَمُونَ ظَاهِرًا مِنَ الْحَيَوةِ الدُّنْيَا وَهُمْ عَنِ الْاٰخِرَةُ هُمْ غَافِلُونَ yaʿlamūna ẓāhiran mina l-ḥayati l-dun'yā wahum ʿani l-ākhirati hum ghāfilūna They know what is apparent of the worldly life, but they, of the Hereafter, are unaware. See 30:1

item.title: Ar-Room:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَعْلَمُونَ ظَاهِرًا مِنَ الْحَيَوةِ الدُّنْيَا وَهُمْ عَنِ الْاٰخِرَةُ هُمْ غَافِلُونَ yaʿlamūna ẓāhiran mina l-ḥayati l-dun'yā wahum ʿani l-ākhirati hum ghāfilūna They know (only) the appearance of the life of this world, while of the hereafter they are heedless. (Inattentive.) The use of the word 'Ghafilun', i.e., heedless, indicates that man is not totally ignorant or unaware of the life hereafter, but as he is fascinated and attracted by the apparent aspect of this life, he has become inattentive. Otherwise, the human cognitive self, itself bears more affinity to the life hereafter than to the sensual and material world - as hinted in the next verses. (A.P.).

item.title: Ar-Room:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوَلَمْ يَتَفَكَّرُوا فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ مَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَأَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى وَإِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنَ النَّاسِ بِلِقَاءِ رَبِّهِمْ لَكَافِرُونَ awalam yatafakkarū fī anfusihim mā khalaqa l-lahu l-samāwāti wal-arḍa wamā baynahumā illā bil-ḥaqi wa-ajalin musamman wa-inna kathīran mina l-nāsi biliqāi rabbihim lakāfirūna Have they not reflected in their own souls? Allah did not create the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them except with reason and for a specified term. Indeed many of the people disbelieve in the encounter with their Lord.

item.title: Ar-Room:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوَلَمْ يَتَفَكَّرُوا فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ مَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَأَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى وَإِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنَ النَّاسِ بِلِقَاءِ رَبِّهِمْ لَكَافِرُونَ awalam yatafakkarū fī anfusihim mā khalaqa l-lahu l-samāwāti wal-arḍa wamā baynahumā illā bil-ḥaqi wa-ajalin musamman wa-inna kathīran mina l-nāsi biliqāi rabbihim lakāfirūna Do they not contemplate within themselves?1 Allah has not created the heavens and the earth and what is between them except in truth and for a specified term. And indeed, many of the people, in the meeting with their Lord, are disbelievers. وَيَوْمَئِذٍ يَفْرَحُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ - بِنَصْرِ اللَّهِ ۚ And on that day, the believers will rejoice – with the help of Allah. They will rejoice because the Romans, the companions of Caesar, the king of Ash-Sham, defeated the Persians, the companions of Chosroes, who were Zoroastrians. According to many of the scholars, such as Ibn…

item.title: Ar-Room:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوَلَمْ يَتَفَكَّرُوا فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ مَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَأَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى وَإِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنَ النَّاسِ بِلِقَاءِ رَبِّهِمْ لَكَافِرُونَ awalam yatafakkarū fī anfusihim mā khalaqa l-lahu l-samāwāti wal-arḍa wamā baynahumā illā bil-ḥaqi wa-ajalin musamman wa-inna kathīran mina l-nāsi biliqāi rabbihim lakāfirūna What! Reflect they not with in themselves; (that) created not God the heavens and the earth and what is between them two but with truth, and for an appointed term? And verily most of the people in the meeting of their Lord, disbelieve. The grant of the worldly power in this life is controlled by the high purpose of the Creator Lord of the Universe. Hence let none be infatuated with the foolish belief of whatever given to him is for all times and will not be snatched away from him to fulfil God's Plan and…

item.title: Ar-Room:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوَلَمْ يَسِيرُوْۤا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَيَنْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ كَانُوْۤا أَشَدَّ مِنْهُمْ قُوَّةً وَأَثَارُوا الْأَرْضَ وَعَمَرُوهَا أَكْثَرَ مِمَّا عَمَرُوهَا وَجَاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ فَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيَظْلِمَهُمْ وَلَكِنْ كَانُوْۤا أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ awalam yasīrū fī l-arḍi fayanẓurū kayfa kāna ʿāqibatu alladhīna min qablihim kānū ashadda min'hum quwwatan wa-athārū l-arḍa waʿamarūhā akthara mimmā ʿamarūhā wajāathum rusuluhum bil-bayināti famā kāna l-lahu liyaẓlimahum walākin kānū anfusahum yaẓlimūna Have they not traveled in the land so that they may observe how was the fate of those who were before them? They were more powerful than them, and they plowed the earth and developed it more than they have developed it. Their apostles brought them manifest proofs. So it was not Allah who wronged them, but it was they who used to wrong themselves.

item.title: Ar-Room:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوَلَمْ يَسِيرُوْۤا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَيَنْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ كَانُوْۤا أَشَدَّ مِنْهُمْ قُوَّةً وَأَثَارُوا الْأَرْضَ وَعَمَرُوهَا أَكْثَرَ مِمَّا عَمَرُوهَا وَجَاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ فَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيَظْلِمَهُمْ وَلَكِنْ كَانُوْۤا أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ awalam yasīrū fī l-arḍi fayanẓurū kayfa kāna ʿāqibatu alladhīna min qablihim kānū ashadda min'hum quwwatan wa-athārū l-arḍa waʿamarūhā akthara mimmā ʿamarūhā wajāathum rusuluhum bil-bayināti famā kāna l-lahu liyaẓlimahum walākin kānū anfusahum yaẓlimūna Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in power, and they plowed (or excavated) the earth and built it up more than they (i.e., the Makkans) have built it up, and their messengers came to them with clear evidences. And Allah would not ever have wronged them, but they were wronging themselves. الرَّحِيمُ the Most Merciful. means, towards His believing servants.…

item.title: Ar-Room:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَوَلَمْ يَسِيرُوْۤا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَيَنْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ كَانُوْۤا أَشَدَّ مِنْهُمْ قُوَّةً وَأَثَارُوا الْأَرْضَ وَعَمَرُوهَا أَكْثَرَ مِمَّا عَمَرُوهَا وَجَاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ فَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيَظْلِمَهُمْ وَلَكِنْ كَانُوْۤا أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ awalam yasīrū fī l-arḍi fayanẓurū kayfa kāna ʿāqibatu alladhīna min qablihim kānū ashadda min'hum quwwatan wa-athārū l-arḍa waʿamarūhā akthara mimmā ʿamarūhā wajāathum rusuluhum bil-bayināti famā kāna l-lahu liyaẓlimahum walākin kānū anfusahum yaẓlimūna Have they travelled not in the earth and seen how was the end of those before them? They were stronger than them in strength; and they dug up the earth and built on it more than what did these build; and there came unto them their apostles with clear proofs (miracles); (for) it is not God Who should do them (any) injustice, but they did injustice unto their own selves. Let everyone have in view the…

item.title: Ar-Room:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ كَانَ عَاقِبَةَ الَّذِينَ أَسَاءُوْۤا السُّوأَى أَنْ كَذَّبُوْۤا بِءَايَاتِ اللَّهِ وَكَانُوْۤا بِهَا يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ thumma kāna ʿāqibata alladhīna asāū l-sūā an kadhabū biāyāti l-lahi wakānū bihā yastahziūna Then the fate of those who committed misdeeds was that they denied the signs of Allah and they used to deride them.

item.title: Ar-Room:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ كَانَ عَاقِبَةَ الَّذِينَ أَسَاءُوْۤا السُّوأَى أَنْ كَذَّبُوْۤا بِءَايَاتِ اللَّهِ وَكَانُوْۤا بِهَا يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ thumma kāna ʿāqibata alladhīna asāū l-sūā an kadhabū biāyāti l-lahi wakānū bihā yastahziūna Then the end of those who did evil was the worst (consequence) because they denied the signs of Allah and used to ridicule them. Al-Hassan Al-Basri said, “It has reached the state that in this world one of them could put a Dirham on his finger and tell how much it weighs, but he does not know how to pray properly.” أَوَلَمْ يَتَفَكَّرُوا فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ ۗ مَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَأَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى ۗ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنَ النَّاسِ بِلِقَاءِ رَبِّهِمْ لَكَافِرُونَ - أَوَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَيَنظُرُوا كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ ۚ كَانُوا أَشَدَّ مِنْهُمْ قُوَّةً وَأَثَارُوا الْأَرْضَ وَعَمَرُوهَا أَكْثَرَ مِمَّا عَمَرُوهَا وَجَاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُم بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ ۖ فَمَا كَانَ…

item.title: Ar-Room:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ كَانَ عَاقِبَةَ الَّذِينَ أَسَاءُوْۤا السُّوأَى أَنْ كَذَّبُوْۤا بِءَايَاتِ اللَّهِ وَكَانُوْۤا بِهَا يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ thumma kāna ʿāqibata alladhīna asāū l-sūā an kadhabū biāyāti l-lahi wakānū bihā yastahziūna Then evil was the end of those who wrought evil, for belied they the signs of God, and at them they used to mock. This is a strong warning to the sinners that it may result in the total disbelief in God and the denial of the truth. The same passage was quoted by Zaynab, Husayn's sister, in the court of Yazid son of Muawiyah when she was brought as a captive, in answer to Yazid's reciting the verses of Abdullah ibn al-Ziba'ra meaning: Played Hashemites with the kingdom as otherwise neither came any news nor did descend any revelation from heaven. (A.P.).

item.title: Ar-Room:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَللَّهُ يَبْدَؤُا الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ al-lahu yabda-u l-khalqa thumma yuʿīduhu thumma ilayhi tur'jaʿūna Allah originates the creation, then He will bring it back, then you will be brought back to Him.

item.title: Ar-Room:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَللَّهُ يَبْدَؤُا الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ al-lahu yabda-u l-khalqa thumma yuʿīduhu thumma ilayhi tur'jaʿūna Allah begins creation; then He will repeat it; then to Him you will be returned. Allah originates the creation, then He will repeat it, then to Him you will be returned (30:11). And on the Day when the Hour will be established, the criminals will be plunged into destruction with despair (30:12). No intercessors will they have from those whom they made equal with Allah, and they will reject and deny their partners (30:13). And on the Day when the Hour will be established – that Day shall they be separated (30:14). Then as for those who believed and did righteous good deeds, such shall be honored and made to enjoy a luxurious life in a Garden of Delight (30:15). And as for those…

item.title: Ar-Room:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَللَّهُ يَبْدَؤُا الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ al-lahu yabda-u l-khalqa thumma yuʿīduhu thumma ilayhi tur'jaʿūna God (it is Who) originateth the creation, then causeth it to return again, then unto Him shall ye all be returned. As already pointed out, this verse and the verses of the similar tone, confirm the fact that everything returns to the point from where its existence commenced - and it has been passed into a proverb. 'Everything returns to its origin' - and this has been attested by the NT1. This shows that the process of creation though evolutionary, yet it is circular. See introduction. (A.P.).

item.title: Ar-Room:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ يُبْلِسُ الْمُجْرِمُونَ wayawma taqūmu l-sāʿatu yub'lisu l-muj'rimūna And when the Hour sets in, the guilty will despair.

item.title: Ar-Room:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ يُبْلِسُ الْمُجْرِمُونَ wayawma taqūmu l-sāʿatu yub'lisu l-muj'rimūna And the Day the Hour appears the criminals will be in despair. See 30:11

item.title: Ar-Room:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ يُبْلِسُ الْمُجْرِمُونَ wayawma taqūmu l-sāʿatu yub'lisu l-muj'rimūna And on the day when shall come the Hour (of judgment), in despair shall be the guilty (ones) See 30:11

item.title: Ar-Room:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُمْ مِنْ شُرَكَائِهِمْ شُفَعَؤُا وَكَانُوْۤا بِشُرَكَائِهِمْ كَافِرِينَ walam yakun lahum min shurakāihim shufaʿāu wakānū bishurakāihim kāfirīna None of those whom they ascribed as partners [to Allah] will intercede for them, and they will disavow their partners.1

item.title: Ar-Room:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُمْ مِنْ شُرَكَائِهِمْ شُفَعَؤُا وَكَانُوْۤا بِشُرَكَائِهِمْ كَافِرِينَ walam yakun lahum min shurakāihim shufaʿāu wakānū bishurakāihim kāfirīna And there will not be for them among their (alleged) partners any intercessors, and they will (then) be disbelievers in their partners. See 30:11

item.title: Ar-Room:13 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُمْ مِنْ شُرَكَائِهِمْ شُفَعَؤُا وَكَانُوْۤا بِشُرَكَائِهِمْ كَافِرِينَ walam yakun lahum min shurakāihim shufaʿāu wakānū bishurakāihim kāfirīna And there shall not be for them any intercessors from among their (The false deities they associated with God, and worshipped.) partner gods, and they shall be the deniers of their partners. (The false deities they associated with God, and worshipped.) The false deities they associated with God - whom they worshipped as gods, instead of God. (A.P.).

item.title: Ar-Room:14 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَفَرَّقُونَ wayawma taqūmu l-sāʿatu yawma-idhin yatafarraqūna The day the Hour sets in, they will be divided on that day:

item.title: Ar-Room:14 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَفَرَّقُونَ wayawma taqūmu l-sāʿatu yawma-idhin yatafarraqūna And the Day the Hour appears - that Day they will become separated. See 30:11

item.title: Ar-Room:14 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَفَرَّقُونَ wayawma taqūmu l-sāʿatu yawma-idhin yatafarraqūna And the day when arriveth the Hour (of Judgment), on that day shall (they) be separated (Sorted.) from one another. Here and elsewhere the Resurrection Day is presented as the day when people will be separated and in other verses 11:103, 64:9, the day is said to be a day of gathering together. It is clear from the verses that there is no contradiction between the two statements as the reference is to two different aspects of the Resurrection. (A.P.).

item.title: Ar-Room:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا وَعَمِلُوْۤا الصَّالِحَاتِ فَهُمْ فِي رَوْضَةٍ يُحْبَرُونَ fa-ammā alladhīna āmanū waʿamilū l-ṣāliḥāti fahum fī rawḍatin yuḥ'barūna As for those who have faith and do righteous deeds, they shall be in a garden, rejoicing.

item.title: Ar-Room:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا وَعَمِلُوْۤا الصَّالِحَاتِ فَهُمْ فِي رَوْضَةٍ يُحْبَرُونَ fa-ammā alladhīna āmanū waʿamilū l-ṣāliḥāti fahum fī rawḍatin yuḥ'barūna And as for those who had believed and done righteous deeds, they will be in a garden (of Paradise), delighted. See 30:11

item.title: Ar-Room:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا وَعَمِلُوْۤا الصَّالِحَاتِ فَهُمْ فِي رَوْضَةٍ يُحْبَرُونَ fa-ammā alladhīna āmanū waʿamilū l-ṣāliḥāti fahum fī rawḍatin yuḥ'barūna And as to those who believed and did good deeds, they shall be in the garden, made happy. See 30:14

item.title: Ar-Room:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا وَكَذَّبُوا بِاٰیٰتِنَاۤ وَلِقَاءِ الْاٰخِرَةُ فَأُولَئِكَ فِي الْعَذَابِ مُحْضَرُونَ wa-ammā alladhīna kafarū wakadhabū biāyātinā waliqāi l-ākhirati fa-ulāika fī l-ʿadhābi muḥ'ḍarūna But as for those who were faithless and denied Our signs and the encounter of the Hereafter, they will be brought to the punishment.

item.title: Ar-Room:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا وَكَذَّبُوا بِاٰیٰتِنَاۤ وَلِقَاءِ الْاٰخِرَةُ فَأُولَئِكَ فِي الْعَذَابِ مُحْضَرُونَ wa-ammā alladhīna kafarū wakadhabū biāyātinā waliqāi l-ākhirati fa-ulāika fī l-ʿadhābi muḥ'ḍarūna But as for those who disbelieved and denied Our verses and the meeting of the Hereafter, those will be brought into the punishment (to remain). See 30:11

item.title: Ar-Room:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْۤا وَكَذَّبُوا بِاٰیٰتِنَاۤ وَلِقَاءِ الْاٰخِرَةُ فَأُولَئِكَ فِي الْعَذَابِ مُحْضَرُونَ wa-ammā alladhīna kafarū wakadhabū biāyātinā waliqāi l-ākhirati fa-ulāika fī l-ʿadhābi muḥ'ḍarūna And as to those who disbelieved and belied Our signs and the meeting of the hereafter, these shall be brought over to the chastisement. See 30:14

item.title: Ar-Room:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ حِينَ تُمْسُونَ وَحِينَ تُصْبِحُونَ fasub'ḥāna l-lahi ḥīna tum'sūna waḥīna tuṣ'biḥūna So glorify Allah when you enter evening and when you rise at dawn.

item.title: Ar-Room:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ حِينَ تُمْسُونَ وَحِينَ تُصْبِحُونَ fasub'ḥāna l-lahi ḥīna tum'sūna waḥīna tuṣ'biḥūna So exalted is Allah when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning. So glorify Allah, when you enter the evening, and when you enter the morning (30:17). And His is all the praise in the heavens and the earth; and in 'Ashiyya and when Tuẓhirūn (30:18). He brings out the living from the dead, and brings out the dead from the living. And He revives the earth after its death. And thus shall you be brought out (30:19). The Command to Pray Five Times Daily Here Allah glorifies Himself and commands His servants to glorify and praise Him at these times which come one after the other and are indicative of His might and power in the heavens. This is when the night comes with…

item.title: Ar-Room:17 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ حِينَ تُمْسُونَ وَحِينَ تُصْبِحُونَ fasub'ḥāna l-lahi ḥīna tum'sūna waḥīna tuṣ'biḥūna So glory (Glorify God with prayers to Him.) be to God when ye enter the evening and when ye enter the morning. The praise to God referred to here, stands for the prescribed five times daily prayers: Tumsun: Evening, i.e., the evening and night prayers, i.e., Maghrib and Isha. Tusbihun: Morning, i.e., for the morning prayers - Fajr. Ashiyyan: Afternoon, i.e., for the afternoon prayer - Asr. Tuzhirun: Mid-day, for the Noon prayer - Zuhr. Asserting all these changes are the manifestations of His glory. (A.P.).

item.title: Ar-Room:18 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَعَشِيًّا وَحِينَ تُظْهِرُونَ walahu l-ḥamdu fī l-samāwāti wal-arḍi waʿashiyyan waḥīna tuẓ'hirūna To Him belongs all praise in the heavens and the earth, at nightfall and when you enter noontime.

item.title: Ar-Room:18 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَعَشِيًّا وَحِينَ تُظْهِرُونَ walahu l-ḥamdu fī l-samāwāti wal-arḍi waʿashiyyan waḥīna tuẓ'hirūna And to Him is (due all) praise throughout the heavens and the earth. And (exalted is He) at night and when you are at noon. See 30:17

item.title: Ar-Room:18 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَعَشِيًّا وَحِينَ تُظْهِرُونَ walahu l-ḥamdu fī l-samāwāti wal-arḍi waʿashiyyan waḥīna tuẓ'hirūna And His (alone) is all praise in the heavens and the earth, at the sun's decline and when ye enter the noon. See 30:17

item.title: Ar-Room:19 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يُخْرِجُ الْحَيَّ مِنَ الْمَيِّتِ وَيُخْرِجُ الْمَيِّتَ مِنَ الْحَيِّ وَيُحْيِي الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا وَكَذٰلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ yukh'riju l-ḥaya mina l-mayiti wayukh'riju l-mayita mina l-ḥayi wayuḥ'yī l-arḍa baʿda mawtihā wakadhālika tukh'rajūna He brings forth the living from the dead, and brings forth the dead from the living, and revives the earth after its death. Likewise you [too] shall be raised [from the dead].

item.title: Ar-Room:19 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
