item.description: قُلْ إِنَّمَا أَعِظُكُمْ بِوَاحِدَةٍ أَنْ تَقُومُوْۤا لِلَّهِ مَثْنَى وَفُرَادَى ثُمَّ تَتَفَكَّرُوا مَا بِصَاحِبِكُمْ مِنْ جِنَّةٍ إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ لَكُمْ بَيْنَ يَدَيْ عَذَابٍ شَدِيدٍ qul innamā aʿiẓukum biwāḥidatin an taqūmū lillahi mathnā wafurādā thumma tatafakkarū mā biṣāḥibikum min jinnatin in huwa illā nadhīrun lakum bayna yaday ʿadhābin shadīdin Say, 'I give you just a single advice: that you rise up for Allah's sake, in twos, or individually, and then reflect: there is no madness in your companion: he is just a warner to you before [the befalling of] a severe punishment.'

item.title: Saba:46 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ إِنَّمَا أَعِظُكُمْ بِوَاحِدَةٍ أَنْ تَقُومُوْۤا لِلَّهِ مَثْنَى وَفُرَادَى ثُمَّ تَتَفَكَّرُوا مَا بِصَاحِبِكُمْ مِنْ جِنَّةٍ إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ لَكُمْ بَيْنَ يَدَيْ عَذَابٍ شَدِيدٍ qul innamā aʿiẓukum biwāḥidatin an taqūmū lillahi mathnā wafurādā thumma tatafakkarū mā biṣāḥibikum min jinnatin in huwa illā nadhīrun lakum bayna yaday ʿadhābin shadīdin Say, "I only advise you of one (thing) - that you stand for Allah, (seeking truth) in pairs and individually, and then give thought." There is not in your companion any madness. He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment. Say: I exhort you to one (thing) only, that you stand up for Allah's sake in pairs and singly, and reflect, there is no madness in your companion. He is only a warner to you in face of a severe torment (34:46). Refutation of Their Accusation that the Prophet…

item.title: Saba:46 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ إِنَّمَا أَعِظُكُمْ بِوَاحِدَةٍ أَنْ تَقُومُوْۤا لِلَّهِ مَثْنَى وَفُرَادَى ثُمَّ تَتَفَكَّرُوا مَا بِصَاحِبِكُمْ مِنْ جِنَّةٍ إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ لَكُمْ بَيْنَ يَدَيْ عَذَابٍ شَدِيدٍ qul innamā aʿiẓukum biwāḥidatin an taqūmū lillahi mathnā wafurādā thumma tatafakkarū mā biṣāḥibikum min jinnatin in huwa illā nadhīrun lakum bayna yaday ʿadhābin shadīdin Say (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "I exhort you only to one thing, that rise up ye for God's sake in twos and singly, then (Think without prejudice, without preconceived notions.) ponder ye: your companion (Our Apostle Muhammad) is not possessed, he is none but a warner (sent) unto you, before a severe chastisement." It is an exhortation which only an intelligent one would grasp. The Holy Prophet is commanded by God to invite the people to independent thinking about God and his apostleship. The suggestion is to use individual reflection over the…

item.title: Saba:47 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ مَا سَأَلْتُكُمْ مِنْ أَجْرٍ فَهُوَ لَكُمْ إِنْ أَجْرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى اللَّهِ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ qul mā sa-altukum min ajrin fahuwa lakum in ajriya illā ʿalā l-lahi wahuwa ʿalā kulli shayin shahīdun Say, 'Whatever reward I may have asked you is for your own good. My [true] reward lies only with Allah, and He is witness to all things.'

item.title: Saba:47 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ مَا سَأَلْتُكُمْ مِنْ أَجْرٍ فَهُوَ لَكُمْ إِنْ أَجْرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى اللَّهِ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ qul mā sa-altukum min ajrin fahuwa lakum in ajriya illā ʿalā l-lahi wahuwa ʿalā kulli shayin shahīdun Say, "Whatever payment I might have asked of you - it is yours. My payment is only from Allah, and He is, over all things, Witness." Say: "Whatever wage I might have asked of you is yours. My wage is from Allah only, and He is a Witness over all things (34:47). Say: "Verily, my Lord sends down the truth, the All-Knower of the Unseen (34:48). Say: "The truth has come, and the falsehood can neither create anything nor resurrect (34:49). Say: "If (even) I go astray, I shall stray only to my own loss. But if I remain guided, it is because of the Revelation…

item.title: Saba:47 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ مَا سَأَلْتُكُمْ مِنْ أَجْرٍ فَهُوَ لَكُمْ إِنْ أَجْرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى اللَّهِ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ qul mā sa-altukum min ajrin fahuwa lakum in ajriya illā ʿalā l-lahi wahuwa ʿalā kulli shayin shahīdun Say thou: "Whatever recompense (Refer to note on verses 42:23, 6:91 & 10:72.) I have asked of you, it is only for yourselves; my recompense is (to be expected) from God (alone), and He is witness over all things." See 6:91, 10:72, 42:23. The Holy Prophet had nothing to gain in this world by his mission save to guide mankind on the right path. In verse 42:23 God commanded the Holy Prophet "to tell the people that he demands nothing from them as his wages or the return for all that he has done for them as the Apostle of God, save the love of his…

item.title: Saba:48 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ إِنَّ رَبِّي يَقْذِفُ بِالْحَقِّ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ qul inna rabbī yaqdhifu bil-ḥaqi ʿallāmu l-ghuyūbi Say, 'Indeed my Lord hurls1 the truth. [He is] the knower of all that is Unseen.'

item.title: Saba:48 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ إِنَّ رَبِّي يَقْذِفُ بِالْحَقِّ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ qul inna rabbī yaqdhifu bil-ḥaqi ʿallāmu l-ghuyūbi Say, "Indeed, my Lord projects the truth, Knower of the unseen." See 34:47

item.title: Saba:48 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ إِنَّ رَبِّي يَقْذِفُ بِالْحَقِّ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ qul inna rabbī yaqdhifu bil-ḥaqi ʿallāmu l-ghuyūbi Say thou: "Verily my Lord doth hurleth (out) the (light of) Truth, The Greatest Knower of the unseen." What God reveals is, Islam, the right way for the salvation of mankind.

item.title: Saba:49 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ جَاءَ الْحَقُّ وَمَا يُبْدِئُ الْبَاطِلُ وَمَا يُعِيدُ qul jāa l-ḥaqu wamā yub'di-u l-bāṭilu wamā yuʿīdu Say, 'The truth has come, and falsehood neither originates [anything] not does it restore [anything].'

item.title: Saba:49 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ جَاءَ الْحَقُّ وَمَا يُبْدِئُ الْبَاطِلُ وَمَا يُعِيدُ qul jāa l-ḥaqu wamā yub'di-u l-bāṭilu wamā yuʿīdu Say, "The truth has come, and falsehood can neither begin (anything) nor repeat (it)."1 See 34:47

item.title: Saba:49 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ جَاءَ الْحَقُّ وَمَا يُبْدِئُ الْبَاطِلُ وَمَا يُعِيدُ qul jāa l-ḥaqu wamā yub'di-u l-bāṭilu wamā yuʿīdu Say thou: "The truth hath come, (Refer to note on verse 17:81.) and falsehood (Delusions.) neither bringeth forth anything nor doth it reproduce." The Eighth Holy Imam Ali ibn Musa ar-Ridha says that when the Holy Prophet entered Mecca after his victory and visited the Holy Ka'ba, there were 360 idols in it. To every idol he pointed out with his staff repeating this verse, and the idols, one after another, fell headlong to the ground.

item.title: Saba:50 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ إِنْ ضَلَلْتُ فَإِنَّمَا أَضِلُّ عَلَى نَفْسِي وَإِنِ اهْتَدَيْتُ فَبِمَا يُوحِي إِلَيَّ رَبِّي إِنَّهُ سَمِيعٌ قَرِيبٌ qul in ḍalaltu fa-innamā aḍillu ʿalā nafsī wa-ini ih'tadaytu fabimā yūḥī ilayya rabbī innahu samīʿun qarībun Say, 'If I go astray, my going astray is only to my own harm, and if I am rightly guided that is because of what my Lord has revealed to me. Indeed He is all-hearing, nearmost.'

item.title: Saba:50 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ إِنْ ضَلَلْتُ فَإِنَّمَا أَضِلُّ عَلَى نَفْسِي وَإِنِ اهْتَدَيْتُ فَبِمَا يُوحِي إِلَيَّ رَبِّي إِنَّهُ سَمِيعٌ قَرِيبٌ qul in ḍalaltu fa-innamā aḍillu ʿalā nafsī wa-ini ih'tadaytu fabimā yūḥī ilayya rabbī innahu samīʿun qarībun Say, "If I should err, I would only err against myself. But if I am guided, it is by what my Lord reveals to me. Indeed, He is Hearing and near." See 34:47

item.title: Saba:50 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ إِنْ ضَلَلْتُ فَإِنَّمَا أَضِلُّ عَلَى نَفْسِي وَإِنِ اهْتَدَيْتُ فَبِمَا يُوحِي إِلَيَّ رَبِّي إِنَّهُ سَمِيعٌ قَرِيبٌ qul in ḍalaltu fa-innamā aḍillu ʿalā nafsī wa-ini ih'tadaytu fabimā yūḥī ilayya rabbī innahu samīʿun qarībun Say thou: "If I stray, I stray only against my own self, and if I am guided aright, it is of (Due to.) what hath revealed unto me my Lord; Verily He is All-Hearing, the (Most) Nigh." 'Heaven and the Nearest', i.e., God knows the truth, for he hears everything uttered low or aloud for He is the Nearest, Nearer to man than his own self. Hence, He knows everything. This is in reply to verse 34:43. This does not mean that the Holy Prophet ever erred because Qur'an expressively says in the following verse, 'Your Companion never erred and never did he, nor did he ever utter…

item.title: Saba:51 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَوْ تَرٰی إِذْ فَزِعُوْۤا فَلَا فَوْتَ وَأُخِذُوا مِنْ مَكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ walaw tarā idh faziʿū falā fawta wa-ukhidhū min makānin qarībin Were you to see when they are stricken with terror, [and left] without an escape, and are seized from a close quarter.

item.title: Saba:51 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَوْ تَرٰی إِذْ فَزِعُوْۤا فَلَا فَوْتَ وَأُخِذُوا مِنْ مَكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ walaw tarā idh faziʿū falā fawta wa-ukhidhū min makānin qarībin And if you could see1 when they are terrified but there is no escape, and they will be seized from a place nearby. And if you could but see, when they will be terrified with no escape, and they will be seized from a near place (34:51). And they will say: "We do believe (now);" but how could they receive (Tanawush) from a place so far off (34:52). Indeed they did disbelieve before (in this world), and they (used to) conjecture about the Unseen, from a far place (34:53). And a barrier will be set between them and that which they desire, as was done in the past with the people of their kind. Verily, they have been in grave…

item.title: Saba:51 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَوْ تَرٰی إِذْ فَزِعُوْۤا فَلَا فَوْتَ وَأُخِذُوا مِنْ مَكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ walaw tarā idh faziʿū falā fawta wa-ukhidhū min makānin qarībin And couldst thou see when they shall get terrified, then there shall be no escape and they shall be seized from a (Refers to Badr.) near place, 'From or near place,' (34:51). I.e., at the time of death, or the occasion of the Battle of Badr. Reference is to the state when the guilty are sentenced and their punishment gets nearest to them in that state of facing their punishment, they will be far away from the state of the life in which, faith would have been of no avail to them. And when they were in the state when they could have believed, they disbelieved and they considered the unseen world as something far beyond imagination. (A.P.).

item.title: Saba:52 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالُوْۤا اٰمَنَّا بِهِ وَأَنَّى لَهُمُ التَّنَاوُشُ مِنْ مَكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ waqālū āmannā bihi wa-annā lahumu l-tanāwushu min makānin baʿīdin They will say, 'We believe in it [now].' But how can they reach it from a far-off place,

item.title: Saba:52 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالُوْۤا اٰمَنَّا بِهِ وَأَنَّى لَهُمُ التَّنَاوُشُ مِنْ مَكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ waqālū āmannā bihi wa-annā lahumu l-tanāwushu min makānin baʿīdin And they will (then) say, "We believe in it!" But how for them will be the taking1 (of faith) from a place far away?2 See 34:51

item.title: Saba:52 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالُوْۤا اٰمَنَّا بِهِ وَأَنَّى لَهُمُ التَّنَاوُشُ مِنْ مَكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ waqālū āmannā bihi wa-annā lahumu l-tanāwushu min makānin baʿīdin And they shall say: "We (now) believe in it." And whence shall the approach (to faith) be for them from (such) a distant place? 'Distant place', for they would have been removed by death far away from this world. The place or the opportunity to believe in the truth is this world, this life and in the hereafter or on the Day of Judgment any repentant believing, would be of no avail at all to anyone.

item.title: Saba:53 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَدْ كَفَرُوْۤا بِهِ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَيَقْذِفُونَ بِالْغَيْبِ مِنْ مَكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ waqad kafarū bihi min qablu wayaqdhifūna bil-ghaybi min makānin baʿīdin when they have already disbelieved it earlier? They shoot at the invisible from a far-off place!

item.title: Saba:53 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَدْ كَفَرُوْۤا بِهِ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَيَقْذِفُونَ بِالْغَيْبِ مِنْ مَكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ waqad kafarū bihi min qablu wayaqdhifūna bil-ghaybi min makānin baʿīdin And they had already disbelieved in it before and would assault1 the unseen from a place far away.2 See 34:51

item.title: Saba:53 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَدْ كَفَرُوْۤا بِهِ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَيَقْذِفُونَ بِالْغَيْبِ مِنْ مَكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ waqad kafarū bihi min qablu wayaqdhifūna bil-ghaybi min makānin baʿīdin And indeed they did disbelieve in it before, and aim their conjectures about the unseen from a distant place. The people disbelieved in the Holy Prophet and rejecting his message imagined to be safe in the hereafter as they were here. What they conjectured was about something unseen and such unseen things or places are termed as distant ones. It is said that what they say, are things very distant for them which they could never know.

item.title: Saba:54 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَحِيلَ بَيْنَهُمْ وَبَيْنَ مَا يَشْتَهُونَ كَمَا فُعِلَ بِأَشْيَاعِهِمْ مِنْ قَبْلُ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوْۤا فِي شَكٍّ مُرِيبٍ waḥīla baynahum wabayna mā yashtahūna kamā fuʿila bi-ashyāʿihim min qablu innahum kānū fī shakkin murībin A barrier will be set up between them and what they long for, just as was done formerly with their counterparts. Indeed they used to be in grave doubt.

item.title: Saba:54 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَحِيلَ بَيْنَهُمْ وَبَيْنَ مَا يَشْتَهُونَ كَمَا فُعِلَ بِأَشْيَاعِهِمْ مِنْ قَبْلُ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوْۤا فِي شَكٍّ مُرِيبٍ waḥīla baynahum wabayna mā yashtahūna kamā fuʿila bi-ashyāʿihim min qablu innahum kānū fī shakkin murībin And prevention will be placed between them and what they desire,1 as was done with their kind before. Indeed, they were in disquieting doubt (i.e., denial). See 34:51

item.title: Saba:54 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَحِيلَ بَيْنَهُمْ وَبَيْنَ مَا يَشْتَهُونَ كَمَا فُعِلَ بِأَشْيَاعِهِمْ مِنْ قَبْلُ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوْۤا فِي شَكٍّ مُرِيبٍ waḥīla baynahum wabayna mā yashtahūna kamā fuʿila bi-ashyāʿihim min qablu innahum kānū fī shakkin murībin And a gulf shall be set between them and that which they desire, as was done unto the likes of them of yore, verily they have been in a disquieting doubt. The disbelievers will meet disappointment for they would never achieve their desires or realise their conjectures.

item.title: Taa-Haa:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: طه tta-ha Ṭā Hā!1

item.title: Taa-Haa:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: طه tta-ha Ṭā, Hā.1 اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ۖ لَهُ الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَىٰ Allah! There is no God but Him! To Him belongs the Best Names. This means, 'He Who revealed this Qur'an to you (O Muhammad), He is Allah, there is no God except Him. He is the Owner of the Best Names and the most lofty attributes.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: طه tta-ha Ta Ha. (T. H.) 'Ta Ha' - The Sixth Holy Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq says - 'Ta Ha' is one of the names of the Holy Prophet. 'Tayyab' wa 'Tahir', meaning Clean or Pure. This interpretation is in agreement with verse 33:33. It is not a reproaching expression but a consoling one that the Holy Prophet or the faithful should not feel sad for the slow progress of faith among the people. (A.P.).

item.title: Taa-Haa:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ الْقُرْآنَ لِتَشْقَى mā anzalnā ʿalayka l-qur'āna litashqā We did not send down to you the Qur'ān that you should be miserable,

item.title: Taa-Haa:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ الْقُرْآنَ لِتَشْقَى mā anzalnā ʿalayka l-qur'āna litashqā We have not sent down to you the Qur’ān that you be distressed. See 20:1

item.title: Taa-Haa:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ الْقُرْآنَ لِتَشْقَى mā anzalnā ʿalayka l-qur'āna litashqā O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) Sent We not down the Qur'an unto thee that thou distressest (Sadden.) thyself! The Sixth and the Seventh Holy Imams say that the Holy Prophet used to stand in prayer the whole night upon the toes of his feet and consequently his legs used to get swollen. The Holy Prophet prayed like this for ten years until this verse was revealed in which is contained God's directive to give up the physical strain which the Holy Prophet inflicted upon his own self. It was asked that when he was the Divinely purified, sinless and an infallible one, where was the necessity of his being so much prayerful. The Holy Prophet replied: 'Should I not be the grateful servant of the Lord?' In fact, all the righteousness…

item.title: Taa-Haa:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِلَّا تَذْكِرَةً لِمَنْ يَخْشٰی illā tadhkiratan liman yakhshā but only as an admonition to him who fears [his Lord].

item.title: Taa-Haa:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِلَّا تَذْكِرَةً لِمَنْ يَخْشٰی illā tadhkiratan liman yakhshā But only as a reminder for those who fear (Allah). See 20:1

item.title: Taa-Haa:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِلَّا تَذْكِرَةً لِمَنْ يَخْشٰی illā tadhkiratan liman yakhshā Save it is a Reminder unto him who feareth (The pious ones.) (God) 'An admonition for him whose heart is alive, not dead', i.e., whose heart fears the displeasure of the Lord and longs to please Him. The Holy Qur'an is guidance only for the pious and God-fearing.1 Again in verse 3:137 it is clearly said that the Holy Qur'an is only a statement for ordinary men but an admonition to the pious and God-fearing. Thus, sincere faith and piety is the pre-requisite to be benefited by the Qur'an,2 in other words, a disbeliever or an impious one, instead of being guided aright by Qur'an, might get the reverse effect.

item.title: Taa-Haa:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: تَنْزِيلًا مِمَّنْ خَلَقَ الْأَرْضَ وَالسَّمَاوَاتِ الْعُلَى tanzīlan mimman khalaqa l-arḍa wal-samāwāti l-ʿulā A sending down [of the Revelation] from Him who created the earth and the lofty heavens

item.title: Taa-Haa:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: تَنْزِيلًا مِمَّنْ خَلَقَ الْأَرْضَ وَالسَّمَاوَاتِ الْعُلَى tanzīlan mimman khalaqa l-arḍa wal-samāwāti l-ʿulā A revelation from He who created the earth and highest heavens. See 20:1

item.title: Taa-Haa:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: تَنْزِيلًا مِمَّنْ خَلَقَ الْأَرْضَ وَالسَّمَاوَاتِ الْعُلَى tanzīlan mimman khalaqa l-arḍa wal-samāwāti l-ʿulā It is a Missive (Communication from Sovereign.) (sent down) from Him who created the earth and the heavens on high. See 20:3

item.title: Taa-Haa:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلرَّحْمَنُ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ اسْتَوَى al-raḥmānu ʿalā l-ʿarshi is'tawā —the All-beneficent, settled on the Throne.

item.title: Taa-Haa:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلرَّحْمَنُ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ اسْتَوَى al-raḥmānu ʿalā l-ʿarshi is'tawā The Most Merciful (who is) above the Throne established.1 See 20:1

item.title: Taa-Haa:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلرَّحْمَنُ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ اسْتَوَى al-raḥmānu ʿalā l-ʿarshi is'tawā The Beneficent (God) on the 'Arsh' (The throne of administration.) is firm 'Arsh' could be translated into English as the Seat or the Centre of the Authority of the Almighty, All-Knowing and the All-Divine Eternal Being. 'Istawa' - the complete or the perfect universal hold or authority. The whole universe is encircled or enveloped by the 'Arsh'. The hold, the authority or the control of the Omnipotence, Omnipresence and the All-comprehending Knowledge is equally connected and concerned with every composite article of everything in the Universe. The Divine attention is so equitable and so universal that it is the same with everything everywhere and never more in any case nor less in any other. Thus, God's authority penetrates and encompasses everything on the earth, in the heavens and whatever there is in…

item.title: Taa-Haa:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَمَا تَحْتَ الثَّرٰی lahu mā fī l-samāwāti wamā fī l-arḍi wamā baynahumā wamā taḥta l-tharā To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and whatever is between them, and whatever is under the ground.

item.title: Taa-Haa:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَمَا تَحْتَ الثَّرٰی lahu mā fī l-samāwāti wamā fī l-arḍi wamā baynahumā wamā taḥta l-tharā To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is on the earth and what is between them and what is under the soil. See 20:1

item.title: Taa-Haa:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَمَا تَحْتَ الثَّرٰی lahu mā fī l-samāwāti wamā fī l-arḍi wamā baynahumā wamā taḥta l-tharā His is what is in the heavens and what is in the earth and what is between them two and what is beneath the lowest of the low below the earth. 'Tahta th-Thara' - Beneath or under, i.e., whatever is in the lower-most chamber below the surface of the earth - or taking in the sense of the relativity of the direction - it will mean, God's alone is every thing, be that in the highest or in the lowest direction or the place of the Universe. This to negate or to refute the false notions of the polytheists who assign the various regions of the earth and the heavens to different imaginary deities to rule…

item.title: Taa-Haa:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنْ تَجْهَرْ بِالْقَوْلِ فَإِنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ السِّرَّ وَأَخْفَى wa-in tajhar bil-qawli fa-innahu yaʿlamu l-sira wa-akhfā Whether you speak loudly [or in secret tones] He indeed knows the secret and what is still more hidden.

item.title: Taa-Haa:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنْ تَجْهَرْ بِالْقَوْلِ فَإِنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ السِّرَّ وَأَخْفَى wa-in tajhar bil-qawli fa-innahu yaʿlamu l-sira wa-akhfā And if you speak aloud - then indeed, He knows the secret and what is (even) more hidden. See 20:1

item.title: Taa-Haa:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنْ تَجْهَرْ بِالْقَوْلِ فَإِنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ السِّرَّ وَأَخْفَى wa-in tajhar bil-qawli fa-innahu yaʿlamu l-sira wa-akhfā And if thou utter aloud (or in whisper) Verily (alike) knoweth He (all that is) secret (Mysteries of the Unseen.) and (whatsoever is) yet more hidden. There is nothing hidden from His All-Comprehending and All-Penetrating Knowledge. Every thing in the Universe is wholly manifest to Him, nothing is hidden from Him, be that a loud voice or a low utterance or a whisper of even the heart or the sincerity or the insincerity of the intentions - the love and the hatred, faith and disbelief, all are equally manifest to Him. Hence it is said that with God the actions of man are judged according to the intention behind them.

item.title: Taa-Haa:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ لَهُ الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَى al-lahu lā ilāha illā huwa lahu l-asmāu l-ḥus'nā Allah—there is no god except Him— to Him belong the Best Names.

item.title: Taa-Haa:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ لَهُ الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَى al-lahu lā ilāha illā huwa lahu l-asmāu l-ḥus'nā Allah - there is no deity except Him. To Him belong the best names. See 20:1

item.title: Taa-Haa:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ لَهُ الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَى al-lahu lā ilāha illā huwa lahu l-asmāu l-ḥus'nā God, there is no god but He; His are (all) the Best names. It is a natural phenomenon that unless the plate is clean, free from every kind of impression no desired figure can ever have a distinctive impression on it. Unless the mind or heart is thoroughly clean, free from belief of any degree or nature in false deities or falsehood, the correct faith in God and truth can never take its place therein. Hence washing the mind of every kind of false conceptions is the first requisite, the foremost essential step towards faith in God and this act is called 'Tabarra' and embracing the truth thereafter is 'Tawallah'. These two conditions are of the fundamentals of the practice of the Islam-Original identified…

item.title: Taa-Haa:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهَلْ أَتَىكَ حَدِیْثُ مُوسٰی wahal atāka ḥadīthu mūsā Did the story of Moses come to you,

item.title: Taa-Haa:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهَلْ أَتَىكَ حَدِیْثُ مُوسٰی wahal atāka ḥadīthu mūsā And has the story of Musa reached you?. And has there come to you the story of Musa (20:9). When he saw a fire, he said to his family: Wait! Verily, I have seen a fire; perhaps I can bring you some burning brand therefrom, or find some guidance at the fire (20:10). A Discussion of the Message of Musa From this point, Allah begins to mention the story of Musa, how revelation began to come to Him, and Allah's speaking directly to him. This occurred after Musa had completed the time agreed upon between he and his father-in-law that he would herd sheep. He was traveling with his family, and it has been said that he was headed for the land of Egypt, after having been away from it for more…

item.title: Taa-Haa:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَهَلْ أَتَىكَ حَدِیْثُ مُوسٰی wahal atāka ḥadīthu mūsā And hath come unto thee the story of Moses? See 20:8

item.title: Taa-Haa:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ رَءَا نَارًا فَقَالَ لِأَهْلِهِ امْكُثُوْۤا اِنِّیْ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًا لَعَلِّي ءَاتِيكُمْ مِنْهَا بِقَبَسٍ أَوْ أَجِدُ عَلَى النَّارِ هُدًى idh raā nāran faqāla li-ahlihi um'kuthū innī ānastu nāran laʿallī ātīkum min'hā biqabasin aw ajidu ʿalā l-nāri hudan when he sighted a fire, and said to his family, 'Wait! Indeed I descry a fire! Maybe I will bring you a brand from it, or find some guidance at the fire.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ رَءَا نَارًا فَقَالَ لِأَهْلِهِ امْكُثُوْۤا اِنِّیْ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًا لَعَلِّي ءَاتِيكُمْ مِنْهَا بِقَبَسٍ أَوْ أَجِدُ عَلَى النَّارِ هُدًى idh raā nāran faqāla li-ahlihi um'kuthū innī ānastu nāran laʿallī ātīkum min'hā biqabasin aw ajidu ʿalā l-nāri hudan When he saw a fire and said to his family, "Stay here; indeed, I have perceived a fire; perhaps I can bring you a torch or find at the fire some guidance." See 20:9

item.title: Taa-Haa:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ رَءَا نَارًا فَقَالَ لِأَهْلِهِ امْكُثُوْۤا اِنِّیْ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًا لَعَلِّي ءَاتِيكُمْ مِنْهَا بِقَبَسٍ أَوْ أَجِدُ عَلَى النَّارِ هُدًى idh raā nāran faqāla li-ahlihi um'kuthū innī ānastu nāran laʿallī ātīkum min'hā biqabasin aw ajidu ʿalā l-nāri hudan When he saw fire, then said he unto his family, "Tarry ye here, for verily I perceive a fire: happly I may bring unto you a brand from it, or I find at the fire some guidance." The experiences of Moses have been referred to in many places in the Holy Qur'an and the various references are to the appropriateness of each occasion.1 These verses refer to the occasion when Moses after ten years of marriage with Lady Safura the daughter of Shu'aib, started to his mother's place and during the journey in a wilderness, his wife delivered a son and there was no…

item.title: Taa-Haa:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا أَتَاهَا نُودِيَ يَامُوسٰی falammā atāhā nūdiya yāmūsā So when he came to it, he was called, 'O Moses!

item.title: Taa-Haa:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا أَتَاهَا نُودِيَ يَامُوسٰی falammā atāhā nūdiya yāmūsā And when he came to it, he was called, "O Musa. And when he came to it (the fire), he was called by name: "O Musa! (20:11). "Verily, I am your Lord! So take off your shoes; you are in the sacred valley, Tuwa (20:12). "And I have chosen you. So listen to that which will be revealed (to you) (20:13). "Verily, I am Allah! There is no God but Me, so worship Me, and perform Salah for My remembrance (20:14). "Verily, the Hour is coming – and I am almost hiding it – that every person may be rewarded for that which he strives (20:15). "Therefore, let not the one who believes not therein, but follows his own lusts, divert you therefrom, lest you perish (20:16). The First Revelation to Musa…

item.title: Taa-Haa:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا أَتَاهَا نُودِيَ يَامُوسٰی falammā atāhā nūdiya yāmūsā So when he came unto it (the fire) a voice (Sounded.) called: "O' Moses!" God encouraged Moses with a voice of consolation calling Moses by his name. Moses awoke shouting 'Here I am, My Lord.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اِنِّیْ أَنَا رَبُّكَ فَاخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ إِنَّكَ بِالْوَادِ الْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى innī anā rabbuka fa-ikh'laʿ naʿlayka innaka bil-wādi l-muqadasi ṭuwan Indeed I am your Lord! So take off your sandals. You are indeed in the sacred valley of Ṭuwā.

item.title: Taa-Haa:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اِنِّیْ أَنَا رَبُّكَ فَاخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ إِنَّكَ بِالْوَادِ الْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى innī anā rabbuka fa-ikh'laʿ naʿlayka innaka bil-wādi l-muqadasi ṭuwan Indeed, I am your Lord, so remove your sandals. Indeed, you are in the blessed valley of Ṭuwā. See 20:11

item.title: Taa-Haa:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اِنِّیْ أَنَا رَبُّكَ فَاخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ إِنَّكَ بِالْوَادِ الْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى innī anā rabbuka fa-ikh'laʿ naʿlayka innaka bil-wādi l-muqadasi ṭuwan Verily I; I (alone) am thy Lord! So take off thy shoes! Verily thou art (OT Exodus 3/2-5.) in the sacred valley of 'Tuwa' The voice again said 'Verily I am thy Lord.' Moses asked "Where art Thou my Lord? I do not see Thee!" 'The voice came 'O' Moses! I am above thee - below thee, in front of thee and behind thee!" And Moses was asked to take off his shoes for he was in a sacred valley. The command to take off the shoes is interpreted as to taking away from his mind the love of family and children, i.e., getting selfless and devoted exclusively to the Lord. This is 'Tabarra.' Though the Sunni commentators are unanimous in the…

item.title: Taa-Haa:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَا اخْتَرْتُكَ فَاسْتَمِعْ لِمَا يُوحَى wa-anā ikh'tartuka fa-is'tamiʿ limā yūḥā I have chosen you; so listen to what is revealed.

item.title: Taa-Haa:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَا اخْتَرْتُكَ فَاسْتَمِعْ لِمَا يُوحَى wa-anā ikh'tartuka fa-is'tamiʿ limā yūḥā And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed (to you). See 20:11

item.title: Taa-Haa:13 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَا اخْتَرْتُكَ فَاسْتَمِعْ لِمَا يُوحَى wa-anā ikh'tartuka fa-is'tamiʿ limā yūḥā And I have chosen thee (for apostleship) then hearken thou unto what is revealed (unto thee)? Moses was informed of his being chosen by God for the ministry.

item.title: Taa-Haa:14 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّنِي أَنَا اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاعْبُدْنِي وَأَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ لِذِكْرِي innanī anā l-lahu lā ilāha illā anā fa-uʿ'bud'nī wa-aqimi l-ṣalata lidhik'rī Indeed I am Allah —there is no god except Me. So worship Me, and maintain the prayer for My remembrance.

item.title: Taa-Haa:14 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّنِي أَنَا اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاعْبُدْنِي وَأَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ لِذِكْرِي innanī anā l-lahu lā ilāha illā anā fa-uʿ'bud'nī wa-aqimi l-ṣalata lidhik'rī Indeed, I am Allah. There is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance. See 20:11

item.title: Taa-Haa:14 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّنِي أَنَا اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاعْبُدْنِي وَأَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ لِذِكْرِي innanī anā l-lahu lā ilāha illā anā fa-uʿ'bud'nī wa-aqimi l-ṣalata lidhik'rī Verily I, I (alone) am God: There is no god but I: worship thou (only) Me, and establish prayer for My remembrance! Moses informed of the strict and the pure monotheistic concept he had to bear and to preach, and was enjoined prayer and remembrance of the Lord.

item.title: Taa-Haa:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ السَّاعَةَ ءَاتِيَةٌ أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا لِتُجْزَى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا تَسْعَى inna l-sāʿata ātiyatun akādu ukh'fīhā lituj'zā kullu nafsin bimā tasʿā Indeed the Hour is bound to come: I will have it hidden, so that every soul may be rewarded for what it strives for.

item.title: Taa-Haa:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ السَّاعَةَ ءَاتِيَةٌ أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا لِتُجْزَى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا تَسْعَى inna l-sāʿata ātiyatun akādu ukh'fīhā lituj'zā kullu nafsin bimā tasʿā Indeed, the Hour is coming - I almost conceal it1 - so that every soul may be recompensed according to that for which it strives. See 20:11

item.title: Taa-Haa:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ السَّاعَةَ ءَاتِيَةٌ أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا لِتُجْزَى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا تَسْعَى inna l-sāʿata ātiyatun akādu ukh'fīhā lituj'zā kullu nafsin bimā tasʿā Verily the Hour (of Doom) is sure to come but I am about to keep it hidden, so that every soul may be recompensed as he striveth: The coming of the Hour of the Final Judgment being a matter of certainty is made known, saying that the Hour is certain to come but the day or the time of its taking effect, is kept a secret, and by informing that every soul shall get the just return for his own conduct, meaning to impress that every soul shall be responsible for his individual faith and action and none shall bear the burden of the other nor any one be deprived of his due.1

item.title: Taa-Haa:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَا يَصُدَّنَّكَ عَنْهَا مَنْ لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِهَا وَاتَّبَعَ هَوَاهُ فَتَرْدَى falā yaṣuddannaka ʿanhā man lā yu'minu bihā wa-ittabaʿa hawāhu fatardā So do not let yourself be distracted from it by those who do not believe in it and who follow their desires, lest you should perish.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَا يَصُدَّنَّكَ عَنْهَا مَنْ لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِهَا وَاتَّبَعَ هَوَاهُ فَتَرْدَى falā yaṣuddannaka ʿanhā man lā yu'minu bihā wa-ittabaʿa hawāhu fatardā So do not let one avert you from it1 who does not believe in it and follows his desire, for you (then) would perish. See 20:11

item.title: Taa-Haa:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَا يَصُدَّنَّكَ عَنْهَا مَنْ لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِهَا وَاتَّبَعَ هَوَاهُ فَتَرْدَى falā yaṣuddannaka ʿanhā man lā yu'minu bihā wa-ittabaʿa hawāhu fatardā Therefore let him who believeth not in it and followeth his own vain desires turn thee away from the truth, lest thou perish. (A caution to Moses.) The injunction here in this verse though addressed to Moses is meant for the people, for the apostles of God are not such weak-minded beings to be led astray from any forces of falsehood.

item.title: Taa-Haa:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا تِلْكَ بِيَمِينِكَ يَامُوسٰی wamā til'ka biyamīnika yāmūsā 'Moses, what is that in your right hand?'

item.title: Taa-Haa:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا تِلْكَ بِيَمِينِكَ يَامُوسٰی wamā til'ka biyamīnika yāmūsā And what is that in your right hand, O Musa?" "And what is that in your right hand, O Musa? (20:17). He said: "This is my stick, whereon I lean, and wherewith I beat down branches for my sheep, and wherein I find other uses (20:18). (Allah) said: "Cast it down, O Musa! (20:19). He cast it down, and behold! It was a snake, moving quickly (20:20). Allah said: "Grasp it and fear not; We shall return it to its former state (20:21). The Stick of Musa Turned into a Snake This was a proof from Allah for Musa and a great miracle. This was something that broke through the boundaries of what is considered normal, thus, it was a brilliant evidence that none but Allah could do. It was also a…

item.title: Taa-Haa:17 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا تِلْكَ بِيَمِينِكَ يَامُوسٰی wamā til'ka biyamīnika yāmūsā And what is this in thy hand O' Moses! The Rod is the Miraculous Rod which was made to act as a great sign to prove the bonafide of Moses being the Apostle of God. It is reported1 that the Rod was of different mystic usage to Moses and acted differently in different situations of his needs.

item.title: Taa-Haa:18 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ هِيَ عَصَايَ أَتَوَكَّؤُا عَلَيْهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَى غَنَمِي وَلِيَ فِيهَا مَءَارِبُ أُخْرٰی qāla hiya ʿaṣāya atawakka-u ʿalayhā wa-ahushu bihā ʿalā ghanamī waliya fīhā maāribu ukh'rā He said, 'It is my staff. I lean upon it, and with it I beat down leaves for my sheep; and I have other uses for it.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:18 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ هِيَ عَصَايَ أَتَوَكَّؤُا عَلَيْهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَى غَنَمِي وَلِيَ فِيهَا مَءَارِبُ أُخْرٰی qāla hiya ʿaṣāya atawakka-u ʿalayhā wa-ahushu bihā ʿalā ghanamī waliya fīhā maāribu ukh'rā He said, "It is my staff; I lean upon it, and I bring down leaves for my sheep and I have therein other uses." See 20:17

item.title: Taa-Haa:18 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ هِيَ عَصَايَ أَتَوَكَّؤُا عَلَيْهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَى غَنَمِي وَلِيَ فِيهَا مَءَارِبُ أُخْرٰی qāla hiya ʿaṣāya atawakka-u ʿalayhā wa-ahushu bihā ʿalā ghanamī waliya fīhā maāribu ukh'rā Said he: "This is my staff; I recline on it, and I beat down leaves with it for my sheep, and for me therein are other uses (also)." See 20:17

item.title: Taa-Haa:19 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ أَلْقِهَا يَامُوسٰی qāla alqihā yāmūsā He said, 'Moses, throw it down.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:19 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ أَلْقِهَا يَامُوسٰی qāla alqihā yāmūsā (Allah) said, "Throw it down, O Musa." See 20:17

item.title: Taa-Haa:19 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ أَلْقِهَا يَامُوسٰی qāla alqihā yāmūsā He (God.) said: "Cast it down, O' Moses!" See 20:17

item.title: Taa-Haa:20 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَلْقَاهَا فَإِذَا هِيَ حَيَّةٌ تَسْعَى fa-alqāhā fa-idhā hiya ḥayyatun tasʿā So he threw it down, and behold, it was a snake, moving swiftly.

item.title: Taa-Haa:20 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَلْقَاهَا فَإِذَا هِيَ حَيَّةٌ تَسْعَى fa-alqāhā fa-idhā hiya ḥayyatun tasʿā So he threw it down, and thereupon it was a snake, moving swiftly. See 20:17

item.title: Taa-Haa:20 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَلْقَاهَا فَإِذَا هِيَ حَيَّةٌ تَسْعَى fa-alqāhā fa-idhā hiya ḥayyatun tasʿā Then he cast it down, and lo! it was a serpent running. See 20:17

item.title: Taa-Haa:21 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ خُذْهَا وَلَا تَخَفْ سَنُعِيدُهَا سِيرَتَهَا الْأُولَى qāla khudh'hā walā takhaf sanuʿīduhā sīratahā l-ūlā He said, 'Take hold of it, and do not fear. We will restore it to its former state.

item.title: Taa-Haa:21 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ خُذْهَا وَلَا تَخَفْ سَنُعِيدُهَا سِيرَتَهَا الْأُولَى qāla khudh'hā walā takhaf sanuʿīduhā sīratahā l-ūlā (Allah) said, "Seize it and fear not; We will return it to its former condition. See 20:17

item.title: Taa-Haa:21 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ خُذْهَا وَلَا تَخَفْ سَنُعِيدُهَا سِيرَتَهَا الْأُولَى qāla khudh'hā walā takhaf sanuʿīduhā sīratahā l-ūlā He said: "Lay hold on it, and fear thou not; for We will restore it to its former state (of a staff)" When Moses saw for the first time his Rod becoming a dreadful huge serpent, he was frightened. Moses was commanded not to fear but to hold it with the assurance of its returning to its original state of a rod. And Moses answered and said, But, behold, they will not believe me, nor hearken unto my voice: for they will say, The Lord hath not spoken unto thee. And the Lord said unto him, What is that in thine hand? And he said, A rod. And he said, Cast it on the ground, And he cast it on the ground, and it became a…

item.title: Taa-Haa:22 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاضْمُمْ يَدَكَ إِلَى جَنَاحِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَاءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوءٍ اٰیَةً أُخْرٰی wa-uḍ'mum yadaka ilā janāḥika takhruj bayḍāa min ghayri sūin āyatan ukh'rā Now clasp your hand to your armpit: it will emerge white, without any fault. [This is yet] another sign,

item.title: Taa-Haa:22 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاضْمُمْ يَدَكَ إِلَى جَنَاحِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَاءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوءٍ اٰیَةً أُخْرٰی wa-uḍ'mum yadaka ilā janāḥika takhruj bayḍāa min ghayri sūin āyatan ukh'rā And draw in your hand to your side; it will come out white without disease - another sign. "And press your (right) hand to your (left) side: it will come forth white (and shining), without any disease as another sign, (20:22). "That We may show you (some) of Our greater signs (20:23). "Go to Fir'awn! Verily, he has transgressed (20:24). He said: "O my Lord! Open for me my chest (20:25). "And ease my task for me; (20:26). "And loosen the knot from my tongue, (20:27). "That they understand my speech (20:28). "And appoint for me a helper from my family, (20:29). "Harun, my brother (20:30). "Increase my strength with him, (20:31). "And let him share my task,…

item.title: Taa-Haa:22 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاضْمُمْ يَدَكَ إِلَى جَنَاحِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَاءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوءٍ اٰیَةً أُخْرٰی wa-uḍ'mum yadaka ilā janāḥika takhruj bayḍāa min ghayri sūin āyatan ukh'rā And place thy hand under thy armpit, (Bosom.) it shall come forth white, without any harm (As a miracle without any hurt to Moses.) , (and this is) another sign (miracle), See 20:21

item.title: Taa-Haa:23 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لِنُرِيَكَ مِنْ ءَايَاتِنَا الْكُبْرٰی linuriyaka min āyātinā l-kub'rā that We may show you some of Our great signs.

item.title: Taa-Haa:23 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran

item.title: Taa-Haa:23 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran

item.title: Taa-Haa:24 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اِذْهَبْ إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغَى idh'hab ilā fir'ʿawna innahu ṭaghā Go to Pharaoh. He has indeed rebelled.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:24 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اِذْهَبْ إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغَى idh'hab ilā fir'ʿawna innahu ṭaghā Go to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed (i.e., tyrannized)." See 20:22

item.title: Taa-Haa:24 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اِذْهَبْ إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغَى idh'hab ilā fir'ʿawna innahu ṭaghā Go (Armed with the two miracles.) thou unto Pharaoh! Verily he hath transgressed the bounds! See 20:21

item.title: Taa-Haa:25 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي qāla rabbi ish'raḥ lī ṣadrī He said, 'My Lord! Open my breast for me.

item.title: Taa-Haa:25 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي qāla rabbi ish'raḥ lī ṣadrī (Musa) said, "My Lord, expand (i.e., relax) for me my breast (with assurance). See 20:22

item.title: Taa-Haa:25 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي qāla rabbi ish'raḥ lī ṣadrī Said (Moses.) he "O' My Lord! Expand for me my breast," Moses was armed with the two Ever-triumphant Weapons of the two wonderful signs, and yet he wanted another one like him to assist him in the task against Pharaoh. It would be seen by the life history of Moses and the Holy Prophet that both these Apostles of God have many things in common. The task before the Holy Prophet was several times greater and more difficult. Moses had to face one Pharaoh, but the Holy Prophet had a multitude of Pharaohs, for every Qurayshite chieftain was in no way less than the Pharaoh of Moses. The Holy Prophet had asked God to give him an assistant to assist him in the great task of facing the leaders of…

item.title: Taa-Haa:26 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمْرِي wayassir lī amrī Make my affair easy for me.

item.description: يَفْقَهُوْۤا قَوْلِي yafqahū qawlī (That) they may understand my speech, See 20:25

item.description: هَارُونَ أَخِي hārūna akhī Aaron, my brother.

item.description: وَنَذْكُرَكَ كَثِيرًا wanadhkuraka kathīran And remember Thee much See 20:25

item.description: إِنَّكَ كُنْتَ بِنَا بَصِيرًا innaka kunta binā baṣīran Indeed You see us best.'

item.description: إِنَّكَ كُنْتَ بِنَا بَصِيرًا innaka kunta binā baṣīran Indeed, You are of us ever Seeing." See 20:22

item.description: إِنَّكَ كُنْتَ بِنَا بَصِيرًا innaka kunta binā baṣīran Verily Thou art ever seeing of us. See 20:25

item.title: Taa-Haa:36 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ قَدْ أُوتِيتَ سُؤْلَكَ يَامُوسٰی qāla qad ūtīta su'laka yāmūsā He said, 'Moses, your request has been granted!

item.title: Taa-Haa:36 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ قَدْ أُوتِيتَ سُؤْلَكَ يَامُوسٰی qāla qad ūtīta su'laka yāmūsā (Allah) said, "You have been granted your request, O Musa. (Allah) said: "You are granted your request, O Musa! (20:36). "And indeed We conferred a favor on you another time (before) (20:37). "When We inspired your mother with that which We inspired (20:38). "Saying: 'Put him (the child) into the Tabut and put it into the river; then the river shall cast it up on the bank, and there, an enemy of Mine and an enemy of his shall take him.' And I endued you with love from Me, in order that you may be brought up under My Eye (20:39). Glad Tidings of the Acceptance of Musa's Supplication and the Reminder of the Previous Blessings This is a response from Allah to His Messenger, Musa, for what he requested…

item.title: Taa-Haa:36 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ قَدْ أُوتِيتَ سُؤْلَكَ يَامُوسٰی qāla qad ūtīta su'laka yāmūsā Said (God.) He: "Granted is thy prayer, O' Moses!" Refer to note on verse 20:94 - A justification for the Holy Prophet saying 'O' Ali thou art to me as Aaron was to Moses (in all respects) save that there is no prophet to come after me' (A.P.).

item.title: Taa-Haa:37 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ مَنَنَّا عَلَيْكَ مَرَّةً أُخْرٰی walaqad manannā ʿalayka marratan ukh'rā Certainly, We have done you a favour another time,

item.title: Taa-Haa:37 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ مَنَنَّا عَلَيْكَ مَرَّةً أُخْرٰی walaqad manannā ʿalayka marratan ukh'rā And We had already conferred favor upon you another time. See 20:36

item.title: Taa-Haa:37 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ مَنَنَّا عَلَيْكَ مَرَّةً أُخْرٰی walaqad manannā ʿalayka marratan ukh'rā And indeed We conferred Our favour on thee at another time, See 20:36

item.title: Taa-Haa:38 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى أُمِّكَ مَا يُوحَى idh awḥaynā ilā ummika mā yūḥā when We revealed to your mother whatever was revealed:

item.title: Taa-Haa:38 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى أُمِّكَ مَا يُوحَى idh awḥaynā ilā ummika mā yūḥā When We inspired to your mother what We inspired. See 20:36

item.title: Taa-Haa:38 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى أُمِّكَ مَا يُوحَى idh awḥaynā ilā ummika mā yūḥā When We revealed unto thy mother what was revealed (unto her), This is a reference to how Moses when he as a just-born, was Divinely saved from being killed by Pharaoh. Pharaoh dreamt that a fire from the habitation of the Israelites was coming around his palace and destroying it. The learned ones of his chiefs interpreted the dream saying, that a boy born of the Israelites would cause his destruction. Pharaoh ordered every male child born to the Israelites to be killed. When Moses was born during that time the mother of Moses did not know how to save the child. 'Wahi', i.e., revelation here means inspiration, as in the case of the Bee.1'Wahi' means also the instinct.

item.title: Taa-Haa:39 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنِ اقْذِفِيهِ فِي التَّابُوتِ فَاقْذِفِيهِ فِي الْيَمِّ فَلْيُلْقِهِ الْيَمُّ بِالسَّاحِلِ يَأْخُذْهُ عَدُوٌّ لِي وَعَدُوٌّ لَهُ وَأَلْقَيْتُ عَلَيْكَ مَحَبَّةً مِنِّي وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلَى عَيْنِي ani iq'dhifīhi fī l-tābūti fa-iq'dhifīhi fī l-yami falyul'qihi l-yamu bil-sāḥili yakhudh'hu ʿaduwwun lī waʿaduwwun lahu wa-alqaytu ʿalayka maḥabbatan minnī walituṣ'naʿa ʿalā ʿaynī "Put him in the casket, and cast it into the river. Then the river will cast it on the bank, and he shall be picked up by an enemy of Mine and an enemy of his." And I cast upon you a love from Me,1 and that you might be reared under My eyes.

item.title: Taa-Haa:39 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنِ اقْذِفِيهِ فِي التَّابُوتِ فَاقْذِفِيهِ فِي الْيَمِّ فَلْيُلْقِهِ الْيَمُّ بِالسَّاحِلِ يَأْخُذْهُ عَدُوٌّ لِي وَعَدُوٌّ لَهُ وَأَلْقَيْتُ عَلَيْكَ مَحَبَّةً مِنِّي وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلَى عَيْنِي ani iq'dhifīhi fī l-tābūti fa-iq'dhifīhi fī l-yami falyul'qihi l-yamu bil-sāḥili yakhudh'hu ʿaduwwun lī waʿaduwwun lahu wa-alqaytu ʿalayka maḥabbatan minnī walituṣ'naʿa ʿalā ʿaynī (Saying), 'Cast him into the chest and cast it into the river, and the river will throw it onto the bank; there will take him an enemy to Me and an enemy to him.' And I bestowed upon you love from Me1 that you would be brought up under My eye (i.e., observation and care). See 20:36

item.title: Taa-Haa:39 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَنِ اقْذِفِيهِ فِي التَّابُوتِ فَاقْذِفِيهِ فِي الْيَمِّ فَلْيُلْقِهِ الْيَمُّ بِالسَّاحِلِ يَأْخُذْهُ عَدُوٌّ لِي وَعَدُوٌّ لَهُ وَأَلْقَيْتُ عَلَيْكَ مَحَبَّةً مِنِّي وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلَى عَيْنِي ani iq'dhifīhi fī l-tābūti fa-iq'dhifīhi fī l-yami falyul'qihi l-yamu bil-sāḥili yakhudh'hu ʿaduwwun lī waʿaduwwun lahu wa-alqaytu ʿalayka maḥabbatan minnī walituṣ'naʿa ʿalā ʿaynī That: "Cast him into a chest, then cast it into the sea, then the sea (River.) shall throw him ashore"; there taketh him (up) one (who is an) enemy unto Me and an enemy unto him; and I cast down upon thee love from Me (that everyone may love thee); so that thou mightest be brought up under My eyes (Attention – Blessings.) (as I will): God inspired Moses' mother to put the baby into a box and float it away into the Nile. A channel from the Nile passed into the Palace Garden of Pharaoh.…

item.title: Taa-Haa:40 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ تَمْشِي أُخْتُكَ فَتَقُولُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَى مَنْ يَكْفُلُهُ فَرَجَعْنَاكَ إِلَى أُمِّكَ كَيْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ وَقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًا فَنَجَّيْنَاكَ مِنَ الْغَمِّ وَفَتَنَّاكَ فُتُونًا فَلَبِثْتَ سِنِينَ فِي أَهْلِ مَدْيَنَ ثُمَّ جِئْتَ عَلَى قَدَرٍ يَامُوسٰی idh tamshī ukh'tuka fataqūlu hal adullukum ʿalā man yakfuluhu farajaʿnāka ilā ummika kay taqarra ʿaynuhā walā taḥzana waqatalta nafsan fanajjaynāka mina l-ghami wafatannāka futūnan falabith'ta sinīna fī ahli madyana thumma ji'ta ʿalā qadarin yāmūsā When your sister walked up [to Pharaoh's palace] saying, "Shall I show you someone who will take care of him?" Then We restored you to your mother, that she might be comforted and not grieve. Then you slew a soul, whereupon We delivered you from anguish, and We tried you with various ordeals. Then you stayed for several years among the people of Midian. Then you turned up as ordained, O Moses!

item.title: Taa-Haa:40 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ تَمْشِي أُخْتُكَ فَتَقُولُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَى مَنْ يَكْفُلُهُ فَرَجَعْنَاكَ إِلَى أُمِّكَ كَيْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ وَقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًا فَنَجَّيْنَاكَ مِنَ الْغَمِّ وَفَتَنَّاكَ فُتُونًا فَلَبِثْتَ سِنِينَ فِي أَهْلِ مَدْيَنَ ثُمَّ جِئْتَ عَلَى قَدَرٍ يَامُوسٰی idh tamshī ukh'tuka fataqūlu hal adullukum ʿalā man yakfuluhu farajaʿnāka ilā ummika kay taqarra ʿaynuhā walā taḥzana waqatalta nafsan fanajjaynāka mina l-ghami wafatannāka futūnan falabith'ta sinīna fī ahli madyana thumma ji'ta ʿalā qadarin yāmūsā (And We favored you) when your sister went and said, 'Shall I direct you to someone who will be responsible for him?' So We restored you to your mother that she might be content and not grieve. And you killed someone,1 but We saved you from retaliation and tried you with a (severe) trial. And you remained (some) years among the people of Madyan. Then you came (here) at the decreed time,…

item.title: Taa-Haa:40 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ تَمْشِي أُخْتُكَ فَتَقُولُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَى مَنْ يَكْفُلُهُ فَرَجَعْنَاكَ إِلَى أُمِّكَ كَيْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ وَقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًا فَنَجَّيْنَاكَ مِنَ الْغَمِّ وَفَتَنَّاكَ فُتُونًا فَلَبِثْتَ سِنِينَ فِي أَهْلِ مَدْيَنَ ثُمَّ جِئْتَ عَلَى قَدَرٍ يَامُوسٰی idh tamshī ukh'tuka fataqūlu hal adullukum ʿalā man yakfuluhu farajaʿnāka ilā ummika kay taqarra ʿaynuhā walā taḥzana waqatalta nafsan fanajjaynāka mina l-ghami wafatannāka futūnan falabith'ta sinīna fī ahli madyana thumma ji'ta ʿalā qadarin yāmūsā When thy sister went (unto Pharaoh's wife) and said: "Shall I show you one who will take care of him?" So We brought thee back unto thy mother, that her eyes be cooled and she might grieve not; And thou didst kill a man (and wert perturbed) and We delivered thee from the grief and We tried thee with a heavy trial and then thou didst tarry years among the people of…

item.title: Taa-Haa:41 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاصْطَنَعْتُكَ لِنَفْسِي wa-iṣ'ṭanaʿtuka linafsī And I chose you for Myself.

item.title: Taa-Haa:41 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاصْطَنَعْتُكَ لِنَفْسِي wa-iṣ'ṭanaʿtuka linafsī And I produced you for Myself.1 See 20:40

item.title: Taa-Haa:41 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاصْطَنَعْتُكَ لِنَفْسِي wa-iṣ'ṭanaʿtuka linafsī And I have chosen (Conditioned – Moulded – Cultured - for the apostleship.) thee for Myself; See 20:40

item.title: Taa-Haa:42 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اِذْهَبْ أَنْتَ وَأَخُوكَ بِءَايَاتِي وَلَا تَنِيَا فِي ذِكْرِي idh'hab anta wa-akhūka biāyātī walā taniyā fī dhik'rī Go ahead, you and your brother, with My signs and do not flag in My remembrance.

item.title: Taa-Haa:42 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اِذْهَبْ أَنْتَ وَأَخُوكَ بِءَايَاتِي وَلَا تَنِيَا فِي ذِكْرِي idh'hab anta wa-akhūka biāyātī walā taniyā fī dhik'rī Go, you and your brother, with My signs and do not slacken in My remembrance. See 20:40

item.title: Taa-Haa:42 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اِذْهَبْ أَنْتَ وَأَخُوكَ بِءَايَاتِي وَلَا تَنِيَا فِي ذِكْرِي idh'hab anta wa-akhūka biāyātī walā taniyā fī dhik'rī Go thou and thy Brother (Aaron.) with My signs (miracles) and (Remiss.) slacken not either of you in remembering Me. See 20:40

item.title: Taa-Haa:43 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اِذْهَبَا إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغَى idh'habā ilā fir'ʿawna innahu ṭaghā Let the two of you go to Pharaoh. Indeed he has rebelled.

item.title: Taa-Haa:43 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اِذْهَبَا إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغَى idh'habā ilā fir'ʿawna innahu ṭaghā Go, both of you, to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed. See 20:40

item.title: Taa-Haa:43 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اِذْهَبَا إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغَى idh'habā ilā fir'ʿawna innahu ṭaghā Go ye both unto Pharaoh, Verily he hath transgressed (Rebelled - Become inordinate.) (the bounds) See 20:40

item.title: Taa-Haa:44 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَقُولَا لَهُ قَوْلًا لَيِّنًا لَعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوْ يَخْشٰی faqūlā lahu qawlan layyinan laʿallahu yatadhakkaru aw yakhshā Speak to him in a soft manner; maybe he will take admonition or fear.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:44 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَقُولَا لَهُ قَوْلًا لَيِّنًا لَعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوْ يَخْشٰی faqūlā lahu qawlan layyinan laʿallahu yatadhakkaru aw yakhshā And speak to him with gentle speech that perhaps he may be reminded or fear (Allah)." See 20:40

item.title: Taa-Haa:44 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَقُولَا لَهُ قَوْلًا لَيِّنًا لَعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوْ يَخْشٰی faqūlā lahu qawlan layyinan laʿallahu yatadhakkaru aw yakhshā Then speak ye both unto him a gentle word, happly he may get admonished (Pay heed.) or fear (Our punishment), See 20:40

item.title: Taa-Haa:45 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَا رَبَّنَا إِنَّنَا نَخَافُ أَنْ يَفْرُطَ عَلَيْنَا أَوْ أَنْ يَطْغَى qālā rabbanā innanā nakhāfu an yafruṭa ʿalaynā aw an yaṭghā The two of them said, 'Our Lord! We are indeed afraid that he will forestall us or will overstep the bounds.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:45 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَا رَبَّنَا إِنَّنَا نَخَافُ أَنْ يَفْرُطَ عَلَيْنَا أَوْ أَنْ يَطْغَى qālā rabbanā innanā nakhāfu an yafruṭa ʿalaynā aw an yaṭghā They said, "Our Lord, indeed we are afraid that he will hasten (punishment) against us or that he will transgress." Both of them said: Our Lord! Verily, we fear lest he should hasten to punish us or lest he should transgress (20:45). He (Allah) said: "Fear not, verily, I am with you both, hearing and seeing (20:46). "So go you both to him, and say: 'Verily, we are both Messengers of your Lord, so let the Children of Israel go with us, and torment them not; indeed, we have come with a sign from your Lord! And peace will be upon him who follows the guidance! (20:47). 'Truly, it has been revealed to us that the torment will be for…

item.title: Taa-Haa:45 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَا رَبَّنَا إِنَّنَا نَخَافُ أَنْ يَفْرُطَ عَلَيْنَا أَوْ أَنْ يَطْغَى qālā rabbanā innanā nakhāfu an yafruṭa ʿalaynā aw an yaṭghā Said both (Moses and Aaron.) "O' Our Lord! Verily fear we that he breaketh forth against us, or lest he getteth uncontrolled." See 20:40

item.title: Taa-Haa:46 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ لَا تَخَافَا إِنَّنِي مَعَكُمَا أَسْمَعُ وَأَرٰی qāla lā takhāfā innanī maʿakumā asmaʿu wa-arā He said, 'Do not be afraid, for I will be with the two of you, hearing and seeing [whatever happens].

item.title: Taa-Haa:46 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ لَا تَخَافَا إِنَّنِي مَعَكُمَا أَسْمَعُ وَأَرٰی qāla lā takhāfā innanī maʿakumā asmaʿu wa-arā (Allah) said, "Fear not. Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see. See 20:45

item.title: Taa-Haa:46 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ لَا تَخَافَا إِنَّنِي مَعَكُمَا أَسْمَعُ وَأَرٰی qāla lā takhāfā innanī maʿakumā asmaʿu wa-arā Said (God): "Fear not ye both! Verily I am with ye both; I do hear and see" See 20:40

item.title: Taa-Haa:47 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأْتِيَاهُ فَقُولَا إِنَّا رَسُولَا رَبِّكَ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِي إِسْرَاءِيلَ وَلَا تُعَذِّبْهُمْ قَدْ جِئْنَاكَ بِاٰیَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكَ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى مَنِ اتَّبَعَ الْهُدَى fatiyāhu faqūlā innā rasūlā rabbika fa-arsil maʿanā banī is'rāīla walā tuʿadhib'hum qad ji'nāka biāyatin min rabbika wal-salāmu ʿalā mani ittabaʿa l-hudā So approach him and say, "We are the apostles of your Lord. Let the Children of Israel go with us, and do not torture them! We certainly bring you a sign from your Lord, and may peace be upon him who follows guidance!

item.title: Taa-Haa:47 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأْتِيَاهُ فَقُولَا إِنَّا رَسُولَا رَبِّكَ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِي إِسْرَاءِيلَ وَلَا تُعَذِّبْهُمْ قَدْ جِئْنَاكَ بِاٰیَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكَ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى مَنِ اتَّبَعَ الْهُدَى fatiyāhu faqūlā innā rasūlā rabbika fa-arsil maʿanā banī is'rāīla walā tuʿadhib'hum qad ji'nāka biāyatin min rabbika wal-salāmu ʿalā mani ittabaʿa l-hudā So go to him and say, 'Indeed, we are messengers of your Lord, so send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord. And peace1 will be upon he who follows the guidance. See 20:45

item.title: Taa-Haa:47 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأْتِيَاهُ فَقُولَا إِنَّا رَسُولَا رَبِّكَ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِي إِسْرَاءِيلَ وَلَا تُعَذِّبْهُمْ قَدْ جِئْنَاكَ بِاٰیَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكَ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى مَنِ اتَّبَعَ الْهُدَى fatiyāhu faqūlā innā rasūlā rabbika fa-arsil maʿanā banī is'rāīla walā tuʿadhib'hum qad ji'nāka biāyatin min rabbika wal-salāmu ʿalā mani ittabaʿa l-hudā So go ye both unto him, and say": "Verily we are apostles from thy Lord, so send thou with us the children of Israel, and torment them not! indeed have we brought signs (miracles) from thy Lord; and peace will be unto him who followeth the guidance; See 20:40

item.title: Taa-Haa:48 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا قَدْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيْنَا أَنَّ الْعَذَابَ عَلَى مَنْ كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى innā qad ūḥiya ilaynā anna l-ʿadhāba ʿalā man kadhaba watawallā Indeed it has been revealed to us that the punishment shall befall those who deny and turn their backs [on us]." '

item.title: Taa-Haa:48 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا قَدْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيْنَا أَنَّ الْعَذَابَ عَلَى مَنْ كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى innā qad ūḥiya ilaynā anna l-ʿadhāba ʿalā man kadhaba watawallā Indeed, it has been revealed to us that the punishment will be upon whoever denies and turns away.'" See 20:45

item.title: Taa-Haa:48 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا قَدْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيْنَا أَنَّ الْعَذَابَ عَلَى مَنْ كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى innā qad ūḥiya ilaynā anna l-ʿadhāba ʿalā man kadhaba watawallā Verily, hath it been revealed unto us that indeed the chastisement shall certainly come upon him who belieth and turneth back. See 20:40

item.title: Taa-Haa:49 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ فَمَنْ رَبُّكُمَا يَامُوسٰی qāla faman rabbukumā yāmūsā He said, 'Who is your Lord, Moses?'

item.title: Taa-Haa:49 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ فَمَنْ رَبُّكُمَا يَامُوسٰی qāla faman rabbukumā yāmūsā (Pharaoh) said, "So who is the Lord of you two, O Musa?" Fir'awn said: "Who then, O Musa, is the Lord of you two (20:49). (Musa) said: "Our Lord is He Who gave to each thing its form and nature, then guided it aright (20:50). (Fir'awn) said: "What about the generations of old (20:51). Musa said: "The knowledge thereof is with my Lord, in a Record. My Lord neither errs nor forgets (20:52). The Conversation between Musa and Fir'awn Allah, the Exalted, informs about Fir'awn that he said to Musa, in his rejection of the existence of a Supreme Maker and Creator, Who is the God of everything and his own Lord and Owner: فَمَن رَّبُّكُمَا يَا مُوسَىٰ Who then, O Musa, is the Lord of you two? meaning "Who is the…

item.title: Taa-Haa:49 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ فَمَنْ رَبُّكُمَا يَامُوسٰی qāla faman rabbukumā yāmūsā Said (Pharaoh): "And who is the Lord of ye two, O' Moses!" See 20:40

item.title: Taa-Haa:50 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ رَبُّنَا الَّذِي أَعْطَى كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلْقَهُ ثُمَّ هَدَى qāla rabbunā alladhī aʿṭā kulla shayin khalqahu thumma hadā He said, 'Our Lord is He who gave everything its creation and then guided it.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:50 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ رَبُّنَا الَّذِي أَعْطَى كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلْقَهُ ثُمَّ هَدَى qāla rabbunā alladhī aʿṭā kulla shayin khalqahu thumma hadā He said, "Our Lord is He who gave each thing its form and then guided (it)." See 20:49

item.title: Taa-Haa:50 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ رَبُّنَا الَّذِي أَعْطَى كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلْقَهُ ثُمَّ هَدَى qāla rabbunā alladhī aʿṭā kulla shayin khalqahu thumma hadā Said he (Moses): "Our Lord is He Who gave unto everything its (suitable) form, (Form – mould.) and then (also) guided it (aright)" See 20:40

item.title: Taa-Haa:51 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ فَمَا بَالُ الْقُرُونِ الْأُولَى qāla famā bālu l-qurūni l-ūlā He said, 'What about the former generations?'

item.title: Taa-Haa:51 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ فَمَا بَالُ الْقُرُونِ الْأُولَى qāla famā bālu l-qurūni l-ūlā (Pharaoh) said, "Then what is the case of the former generations?" See 20:49

item.title: Taa-Haa:51 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ فَمَا بَالُ الْقُرُونِ الْأُولَى qāla famā bālu l-qurūni l-ūlā (Pharaoh) said: "What then is the state of the generations past?" See 20:40

item.title: Taa-Haa:52 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ عِلْمُهَا عِنْدَ رَبِّي فِي كِتَابٍ لَا يَضِلُّ رَبِّي وَلَا يَنْسٰی qāla ʿil'muhā ʿinda rabbī fī kitābin lā yaḍillu rabbī walā yansā He said, 'Their knowledge is with my Lord, in a Book. My Lord neither makes any error nor forgets.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:52 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ عِلْمُهَا عِنْدَ رَبِّي فِي كِتَابٍ لَا يَضِلُّ رَبِّي وَلَا يَنْسٰی qāla ʿil'muhā ʿinda rabbī fī kitābin lā yaḍillu rabbī walā yansā (Musa) said, "The knowledge thereof is with my Lord in a record. My Lord neither errs nor forgets." See 20:49

item.title: Taa-Haa:52 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ عِلْمُهَا عِنْدَ رَبِّي فِي كِتَابٍ لَا يَضِلُّ رَبِّي وَلَا يَنْسٰی qāla ʿil'muhā ʿinda rabbī fī kitābin lā yaḍillu rabbī walā yansā He (Moses.) said: "The knowledge thereof is with my Lord in a Book (secured by Him), erreth not my Lord, nor doth He forget." See 20:40

item.title: Taa-Haa:53 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ مَهْدًا وَسَلَكَ لَكُمْ فِيهَا سُبُلًا وَأَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِ أَزْوَاجًا مِنْ نَبَاتٍ شَتَّى alladhī jaʿala lakumu l-arḍa mahdan wasalaka lakum fīhā subulan wa-anzala mina l-samāi māan fa-akhrajnā bihi azwājan min nabātin shattā He who made the earth for you a cradle, and in it threaded for you ways, and sent down water from the sky, and with it We brought forth various kinds of vegetation.

item.title: Taa-Haa:53 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ مَهْدًا وَسَلَكَ لَكُمْ فِيهَا سُبُلًا وَأَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِ أَزْوَاجًا مِنْ نَبَاتٍ شَتَّى alladhī jaʿala lakumu l-arḍa mahdan wasalaka lakum fīhā subulan wa-anzala mina l-samāi māan fa-akhrajnā bihi azwājan min nabātin shattā (It is He) who has made for you the earth as a bed (spread out) and inserted therein for you roadways and sent down from the sky, rain and produced thereby categories of various plants. Who has made earth for you like a bed; and has opened ways for you therein, and has sent down water (rain) from the sky. And We have brought forth with it various kinds of vegetation (20:53). Eat and pasture your cattle; verily, in this are Ayat for men of understanding (20:54). Thereof We created you, and into it We shall return you, and from it We…

item.title: Taa-Haa:53 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اَلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ مَهْدًا وَسَلَكَ لَكُمْ فِيهَا سُبُلًا وَأَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِ أَزْوَاجًا مِنْ نَبَاتٍ شَتَّى alladhī jaʿala lakumu l-arḍa mahdan wasalaka lakum fīhā subulan wa-anzala mina l-samāi māan fa-akhrajnā bihi azwājan min nabātin shattā He Who made the earth for you a bed (Cradle.) and made for you therein paths, and sent down from the heavens water; then thereby have We brought forth pairs of plants, various (Varying from each other.) (in kinds) See 20:40

item.title: Taa-Haa:54 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: كُلُوْۤا وَارْعَوْا أَنْعَامَكُمْ إِنَّ فِي ذٰلِكَ لَءَايَاتٍ لِأُولِي النُّهَى kulū wa-ir'ʿaw anʿāmakum inna fī dhālika laāyātin li-ulī l-nuhā 'Eat and pasture your cattle.' There are indeed signs in that for those who have sense.

item.title: Taa-Haa:54 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: كُلُوْۤا وَارْعَوْا أَنْعَامَكُمْ إِنَّ فِي ذٰلِكَ لَءَايَاتٍ لِأُولِي النُّهَى kulū wa-ir'ʿaw anʿāmakum inna fī dhālika laāyātin li-ulī l-nuhā Eat (therefrom) and pasture your livestock. Indeed in that are signs for those of intelligence. See 20:53

item.title: Taa-Haa:54 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: كُلُوْۤا وَارْعَوْا أَنْعَامَكُمْ إِنَّ فِي ذٰلِكَ لَءَايَاتٍ لِأُولِي النُّهَى kulū wa-ir'ʿaw anʿāmakum inna fī dhālika laāyātin li-ulī l-nuhā Eat ye and pasture your cattle; Verily in this there are signs for those endowed with (Endowed with intellect & will power & reasoning.) understanding See 20:40

item.title: Taa-Haa:55 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مِنْهَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ وَفِيهَا نُعِيدُكُمْ وَمِنْهَا نُخْرِجُكُمْ تَارَةً أُخْرٰی min'hā khalaqnākum wafīhā nuʿīdukum wamin'hā nukh'rijukum tāratan ukh'rā From it did We create you, into it shall We return you, and from it shall We bring you forth another time.

item.title: Taa-Haa:55 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مِنْهَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ وَفِيهَا نُعِيدُكُمْ وَمِنْهَا نُخْرِجُكُمْ تَارَةً أُخْرٰی min'hā khalaqnākum wafīhā nuʿīdukum wamin'hā nukh'rijukum tāratan ukh'rā From it (i.e., the earth) We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will extract you another time. See 20:53

item.title: Taa-Haa:55 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مِنْهَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ وَفِيهَا نُعِيدُكُمْ وَمِنْهَا نُخْرِجُكُمْ تَارَةً أُخْرٰی min'hā khalaqnākum wafīhā nuʿīdukum wamin'hā nukh'rijukum tāratan ukh'rā From it (the earth) We created you, and into it will We return you, and out of it will We bring you forth for a second time. From this very earth were created men and their ancestors and after death they are sent back into it and from it again they shall be raised for the Final Judgment.

item.title: Taa-Haa:56 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ أَرَيْنَاهُ ءَايَاتِنَا كُلَّهَا فَكَذَّبَ وَأَبٰی walaqad araynāhu āyātinā kullahā fakadhaba wa-abā Certainly We showed him all Our signs. But he denied [them] and refused [to believe them].

item.title: Taa-Haa:56 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ أَرَيْنَاهُ ءَايَاتِنَا كُلَّهَا فَكَذَّبَ وَأَبٰی walaqad araynāhu āyātinā kullahā fakadhaba wa-abā And We certainly showed him (i.e., Pharaoh) Our signs - all of them - but he denied and refused. See 20:53

item.title: Taa-Haa:56 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ أَرَيْنَاهُ ءَايَاتِنَا كُلَّهَا فَكَذَّبَ وَأَبٰی walaqad araynāhu āyātinā kullahā fakadhaba wa-abā And indeed We did show unto him (Pharaoh.) Our signs, all of them, but he belied and refused (to believe) Moses threw down his staff and it became a huge dreadful serpent. He took it back. Then he showed his hand with his palm shining bright, and also the other miracles, and yet Pharaoh did not believe.

item.title: Taa-Haa:57 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ أَجِئْتَنَا لِتُخْرِجَنَا مِنْ أَرْضِنَا بِسِحْرِكَ يَامُوسٰی qāla aji'tanā litukh'rijanā min arḍinā bisiḥ'rika yāmūsā He said, 'Have you come to us, Moses, to expel us from our land with your magic?

item.title: Taa-Haa:57 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ أَجِئْتَنَا لِتُخْرِجَنَا مِنْ أَرْضِنَا بِسِحْرِكَ يَامُوسٰی qāla aji'tanā litukh'rijanā min arḍinā bisiḥ'rika yāmūsā He said, "Have you come to us to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Musa? He (Fir'awn) said: Have you come to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Musa? (20:57). "Then verily, we can produce magic the like thereof; so appoint a meeting between us and you, which neither we nor you shall fail to keep, in an open place where both shall have a just and equal chance (20:58). (Musa) said: "Your appointed meeting is the day of the festival, and let the people assemble when the sun has risen (forenoon) (20:59). Fir'awn Describes Musa's Proofs As being Magic and Their Agreement to Hold a Contest Allah, the Exalted, informs of what Fir'awn said to Musa when…

item.title: Taa-Haa:57 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ أَجِئْتَنَا لِتُخْرِجَنَا مِنْ أَرْضِنَا بِسِحْرِكَ يَامُوسٰی qāla aji'tanā litukh'rijanā min arḍinā bisiḥ'rika yāmūsā Said he: "Hast thou come unto us that thou turneth us out of our land by thy sorcery, O' Moses!" See 20:56

item.title: Taa-Haa:58 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّكَ بِسِحْرٍ مِثْلِهِ فَاجْعَلْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكَ مَوْعِدًا لَا نُخْلِفُهُ نَحْنُ وَلَا أَنْتَ مَكَانًا سُوًى falanatiyannaka bisiḥ'rin mith'lihi fa-ij'ʿal baynanā wabaynaka mawʿidan lā nukh'lifuhu naḥnu walā anta makānan suwan Yet we [too] will bring you a magic like it! So fix a tryst between us and you, which neither we shall fail nor you, at a middle place.'1

item.title: Taa-Haa:58 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّكَ بِسِحْرٍ مِثْلِهِ فَاجْعَلْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكَ مَوْعِدًا لَا نُخْلِفُهُ نَحْنُ وَلَا أَنْتَ مَكَانًا سُوًى falanatiyannaka bisiḥ'rin mith'lihi fa-ij'ʿal baynanā wabaynaka mawʿidan lā nukh'lifuhu naḥnu walā anta makānan suwan Then we will surely bring you magic like it, so make between us and you an appointment, which we will not fail to keep and neither will you, in a place assigned."1 See 20:57

item.title: Taa-Haa:58 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّكَ بِسِحْرٍ مِثْلِهِ فَاجْعَلْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكَ مَوْعِدًا لَا نُخْلِفُهُ نَحْنُ وَلَا أَنْتَ مَكَانًا سُوًى falanatiyannaka bisiḥ'rin mith'lihi fa-ij'ʿal baynanā wabaynaka mawʿidan lā nukh'lifuhu naḥnu walā anta makānan suwan Then we too will certainly produce before thee a sorcery like unto it, so make between us and thee a tryst, we will not fail it, (neither) we nor thou, in a place alike (Central) for both See 20:56

item.title: Taa-Haa:59 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ الزِّينَةِ وَأَنْ يُحْشَرَ النَّاسُ ضُحًى qāla mawʿidukum yawmu l-zīnati wa-an yuḥ'shara l-nāsu ḍuḥan He said, 'Your tryst shall be the Day of Adornment, and let the people be assembled in early forenoon.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:59 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ الزِّينَةِ وَأَنْ يُحْشَرَ النَّاسُ ضُحًى qāla mawʿidukum yawmu l-zīnati wa-an yuḥ'shara l-nāsu ḍuḥan (Musa) said, "Your appointment is on the day of the festival when the people assemble at mid-morning."1 See 20:57

item.title: Taa-Haa:59 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ الزِّينَةِ وَأَنْ يُحْشَرَ النَّاسُ ضُحًى qāla mawʿidukum yawmu l-zīnati wa-an yuḥ'shara l-nāsu ḍuḥan (Moses) said: "Your tryst be the day of the (Day of adornment.) Festival, and let the people be gathered together in the bright of the noon." See 20:56

item.title: Taa-Haa:60 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَتَوَلَّى فِرْعَوْنُ فَجَمَعَ كَيْدَهُ ثُمَّ أَتٰی fatawallā fir'ʿawnu fajamaʿa kaydahu thumma atā Then Pharaoh withdrew [to consult privately], summoned up his guile, and then arrived [at the scene of the contest].

item.title: Taa-Haa:60 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَتَوَلَّى فِرْعَوْنُ فَجَمَعَ كَيْدَهُ ثُمَّ أَتٰی fatawallā fir'ʿawnu fajamaʿa kaydahu thumma atā So Pharaoh went away, put together his plan, and then came (to Musa). So Fir'awn withdrew, devised his plot and then came back (20:60). Musa said to them: "Woe unto you! Invent not a lie against Allah, lest He should destroy you completely by a torment. And surely, he who invents a lie (against Allah) will fail miserably.") (62 Then they debated one with another what they must do, and they kept their talk secret (61)They said: "Verily, these are two magicians. Their object is to drive you out from your land with magic, and to take you away from your exemplary way. (62)"So devise your plot, and then assemble in line. And whoever overcomes this day will be indeed successful. (63) The Meeting of the Two Parties,…

item.title: Taa-Haa:60 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَتَوَلَّى فِرْعَوْنُ فَجَمَعَ كَيْدَهُ ثُمَّ أَتٰی fatawallā fir'ʿawnu fajamaʿa kaydahu thumma atā So Pharaoh turned back and collected his crafts (Plans.) thereafter he came. See 20:56

item.title: Taa-Haa:61 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ لَهُمْ مُوسٰی وَيْلَكُمْ لَا تَفْتَرُوْۤا عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا فَيُسْحِتَكُمْ بِعَذَابٍ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنِ افْتَرٰی qāla lahum mūsā waylakum lā taftarū ʿalā l-lahi kadhiban fayus'ḥitakum biʿadhābin waqad khāba mani if'tarā Moses said to them, 'Woe to you! Do not fabricate a lie against Allah, lest He should annihilate you with a punishment. Whoever fabricates lies certainly fails.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:61 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ لَهُمْ مُوسٰی وَيْلَكُمْ لَا تَفْتَرُوْۤا عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا فَيُسْحِتَكُمْ بِعَذَابٍ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنِ افْتَرٰی qāla lahum mūsā waylakum lā taftarū ʿalā l-lahi kadhiban fayus'ḥitakum biʿadhābin waqad khāba mani if'tarā Musa said to them (i.e., the magicians summoned by Pharaoh), "Woe to you! Do not invent a lie against Allah or He will exterminate you with a punishment; and he has failed who invents (such falsehood)." See 20:60

item.title: Taa-Haa:61 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ لَهُمْ مُوسٰی وَيْلَكُمْ لَا تَفْتَرُوْۤا عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا فَيُسْحِتَكُمْ بِعَذَابٍ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنِ افْتَرٰی qāla lahum mūsā waylakum lā taftarū ʿalā l-lahi kadhiban fayus'ḥitakum biʿadhābin waqad khāba mani if'tarā Said Moses unto them, "Woe unto you! forge ye not a lie against God: lest He destroyeth you by a sorcery. And faileth he who forgeth a lie." See 20:56

item.title: Taa-Haa:62 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَتَنَازَعُوا أَمْرَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ وَأَسَرُّوا النَّجْوَى fatanāzaʿū amrahum baynahum wa-asarrū l-najwā So they disputed their matter among themselves, and kept their confidential talks secret.

item.title: Taa-Haa:62 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَتَنَازَعُوا أَمْرَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ وَأَسَرُّوا النَّجْوَى fatanāzaʿū amrahum baynahum wa-asarrū l-najwā So they disputed over their affair among themselves and concealed their private conversation. See 20:60

item.title: Taa-Haa:62 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَتَنَازَعُوا أَمْرَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ وَأَسَرُّوا النَّجْوَى fatanāzaʿū amrahum baynahum wa-asarrū l-najwā Then they (the magicians) disputed about their affair among themselves and they spake apart in secret. The magicians began disputing quietly among themselves acknowledging Moses as not a mere magician but some one with some divine powers.

item.title: Taa-Haa:63 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا إِنْ هَذَانِ لَسَاحِرَانِ يُرِيدَانِ أَنْ يُخْرِجَاكُمْ مِنْ أَرْضِكُمْ بِسِحْرِهِمَا وَيَذْهَبَا بِطَرِيقَتِكُمُ الْمُثْلَى qālū in hādhāni lasāḥirāni yurīdāni an yukh'rijākum min arḍikum bisiḥ'rihimā wayadhhabā biṭarīqatikumu l-muth'lā They said, 'These two are indeed magicians who intend to expel you from your land with their magic, and to abolish your excellent tradition!1

item.title: Taa-Haa:63 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا إِنْ هَذَانِ لَسَاحِرَانِ يُرِيدَانِ أَنْ يُخْرِجَاكُمْ مِنْ أَرْضِكُمْ بِسِحْرِهِمَا وَيَذْهَبَا بِطَرِيقَتِكُمُ الْمُثْلَى qālū in hādhāni lasāḥirāni yurīdāni an yukh'rijākum min arḍikum bisiḥ'rihimā wayadhhabā biṭarīqatikumu l-muth'lā They said, "Indeed, these are two magicians who want to drive you out of your land with their magic and do away with your most exemplary way (i.e., religion or tradition). See 20:60

item.title: Taa-Haa:63 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
