item.description: قَالُوْا إِنْ هَذَانِ لَسَاحِرَانِ يُرِيدَانِ أَنْ يُخْرِجَاكُمْ مِنْ أَرْضِكُمْ بِسِحْرِهِمَا وَيَذْهَبَا بِطَرِيقَتِكُمُ الْمُثْلَى qālū in hādhāni lasāḥirāni yurīdāni an yukh'rijākum min arḍikum bisiḥ'rihimā wayadhhabā biṭarīqatikumu l-muth'lā (At last) Said they: "These two are certainly two (expert) sorcerers who intend to drive you out from your land by the sorcery of them both and wipe out your most exemplary tradition! (Creed - religion – faith – belief.)" On Pharaoh asking what the matter was and the magicians out of fear for him said this.

item.title: Taa-Haa:64 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَجْمِعُوا كَيْدَكُمْ ثُمَّ ائْتُوْۤا صَفًّا وَقَدْ أَفْلَحَ الْيَوْمَ مَنِ اسْتَعْلَى fa-ajmiʿū kaydakum thumma i'tū ṣaffan waqad aflaḥa l-yawma mani is'taʿlā So summon up your ingenuity, then come in ranks. Today he who has the upper hand will be saved!'

item.title: Taa-Haa:64 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَجْمِعُوا كَيْدَكُمْ ثُمَّ ائْتُوْۤا صَفًّا وَقَدْ أَفْلَحَ الْيَوْمَ مَنِ اسْتَعْلَى fa-ajmiʿū kaydakum thumma i'tū ṣaffan waqad aflaḥa l-yawma mani is'taʿlā So resolve upon your plan and then come (forward) in line. And he has succeeded today who overcomes." See 20:60

item.title: Taa-Haa:64 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَجْمِعُوا كَيْدَكُمْ ثُمَّ ائْتُوْۤا صَفًّا وَقَدْ أَفْلَحَ الْيَوْمَ مَنِ اسْتَعْلَى fa-ajmiʿū kaydakum thumma i'tū ṣaffan waqad aflaḥa l-yawma mani is'taʿlā So muster your plan: then come in (organized) order: And indeed shall succeed he this day who (Succeeds.) overcometh! Then Pharaoh ordered the magicians to join together with a strongly-determined plan to defeat Moses.

item.title: Taa-Haa:65 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا يَامُوسٰی إِمَّا أَنْ تُلْقِيَ وَإِمَّا أَنْ نَكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَلْقَى qālū yāmūsā immā an tul'qiya wa-immā an nakūna awwala man alqā They said, 'O Moses! Either you will throw down, or we shall be the first to throw.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:65 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا يَامُوسٰی إِمَّا أَنْ تُلْقِيَ وَإِمَّا أَنْ نَكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَلْقَى qālū yāmūsā immā an tul'qiya wa-immā an nakūna awwala man alqā They said, "O Musa, either you throw or we will be the first to throw." They said: "O Musa! Either you throw first or we be the first to throw? (20:65). (Musa) said: "Nay, throw you (first)!" Then behold! their ropes and their sticks, by their magic, appeared to him as though they moved fast (20:66). So Musa conceived fear in himself (20:67). We (Allah) said: "Fear not! Surely, you will have the upper hand (20:68). "And throw that which is in your right hand! It will swallow up that which they have made. That which they have made is only a magician's trick, and the magician will never be successful, to whatever amount (of skill) he may…

item.title: Taa-Haa:65 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا يَامُوسٰی إِمَّا أَنْ تُلْقِيَ وَإِمَّا أَنْ نَكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَلْقَى qālū yāmūsā immā an tul'qiya wa-immā an nakūna awwala man alqā They said: "O' Moses! Either cast thou (first) or shall we be the first who cast down?" God and the godly ones never take the initiative of challenging any one but take the challenge and answer it. Moses could have cast the Rod first but, he allowed the magicians to do whatever they could, and then he played his role as needed by the situation. When the Holy Prophet (at Khandaq) faced one of the greatest Pharaohs of the Qurayshite of Mecca viz. Umar ibn Abd Wudd al-Amiri the unconquerable hero of the heathens, challenging the Holy Prophet, asking if there was any one on the side of God (i.e., God's prescribed faith Islam) to meet him in…

item.title: Taa-Haa:66 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ بَلْ أَلْقُوْۤا فَإِذَا حِبَالُهُمْ وَعِصِيُّهُمْ يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ سِحْرِهِمْ أَنَّهَا تَسْعَى qāla bal alqū fa-idhā ḥibāluhum waʿiṣiyyuhum yukhayyalu ilayhi min siḥ'rihim annahā tasʿā He said, 'Rather you throw down first.' Behold, their ropes and staffs appeared to him by their magic to wriggle swiftly.

item.title: Taa-Haa:66 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ بَلْ أَلْقُوْۤا فَإِذَا حِبَالُهُمْ وَعِصِيُّهُمْ يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ سِحْرِهِمْ أَنَّهَا تَسْعَى qāla bal alqū fa-idhā ḥibāluhum waʿiṣiyyuhum yukhayyalu ilayhi min siḥ'rihim annahā tasʿā He said, "Rather, you throw." And suddenly their ropes and staffs seemed to him from their magic that they were moving (like snakes). See 20:65

item.title: Taa-Haa:66 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ بَلْ أَلْقُوْۤا فَإِذَا حِبَالُهُمْ وَعِصِيُّهُمْ يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ سِحْرِهِمْ أَنَّهَا تَسْعَى qāla bal alqū fa-idhā ḥibāluhum waʿiṣiyyuhum yukhayyalu ilayhi min siḥ'rihim annahā tasʿā (Moses) said: "Nay! cast ye down (first) Then lo! Their cords and their rods, (Imaged.) seemed to him by their sorcery as if they were running." See 20:65

item.title: Taa-Haa:67 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَوْجَسَ فِي نَفْسِهِ خِيفَةً مُوسٰی fa-awjasa fī nafsihi khīfatan mūsā Then Moses felt a fear within his heart.

item.title: Taa-Haa:67 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَوْجَسَ فِي نَفْسِهِ خِيفَةً مُوسٰی fa-awjasa fī nafsihi khīfatan mūsā And he sensed within himself apprehension, did Musa. See 20:65

item.title: Taa-Haa:67 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَوْجَسَ فِي نَفْسِهِ خِيفَةً مُوسٰی fa-awjasa fī nafsihi khīfatan mūsā Then Moses felt in himself a fear. Amir al-Mu'minin Ali Ibn Abi Talib says that the fear felt by Moses was not of serpents or for himself but against the people being misled.1 The next verse 20:68 supports this interpretation2. (A.P.).

item.title: Taa-Haa:68 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْنَا لَا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْاَعْلٰی qul'nā lā takhaf innaka anta l-aʿlā We said, 'Do not be afraid. Indeed you will have the upper hand.

item.title: Taa-Haa:68 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْنَا لَا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْاَعْلٰی qul'nā lā takhaf innaka anta l-aʿlā We (i.e., Allah) said, "Fear not. Indeed, it is you who are superior. See 20:65

item.title: Taa-Haa:68 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْنَا لَا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْاَعْلٰی qul'nā lā takhaf innaka anta l-aʿlā Said We: (God.) "Fear thou not! Verily thou shalt be the uppermost. (Triumphant.)" See 20:67

item.title: Taa-Haa:69 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَلْقِ مَا فِي يَمِينِكَ تَلْقَفْ مَا صَنَعُوْۤا إِنَّمَا صَنَعُوْۤا كَيْدُ سَاحِرٍ وَلَا يُفْلِحُ السَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتٰی wa-alqi mā fī yamīnika talqaf mā ṣanaʿū innamā ṣanaʿū kaydu sāḥirin walā yuf'liḥu l-sāḥiru ḥaythu atā Throw down what is in your right hand, and it will swallow what they have conjured. What they have conjured is only a magician's trick, and the magician does not fare well wherever he may show up.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:69 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَلْقِ مَا فِي يَمِينِكَ تَلْقَفْ مَا صَنَعُوْۤا إِنَّمَا صَنَعُوْۤا كَيْدُ سَاحِرٍ وَلَا يُفْلِحُ السَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتٰی wa-alqi mā fī yamīnika talqaf mā ṣanaʿū innamā ṣanaʿū kaydu sāḥirin walā yuf'liḥu l-sāḥiru ḥaythu atā And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow up what they have crafted. What they have crafted is but the trick of a magician, and the magician will not succeed wherever he is." See 20:65

item.title: Taa-Haa:69 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَلْقِ مَا فِي يَمِينِكَ تَلْقَفْ مَا صَنَعُوْۤا إِنَّمَا صَنَعُوْۤا كَيْدُ سَاحِرٍ وَلَا يُفْلِحُ السَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتٰی wa-alqi mā fī yamīnika talqaf mā ṣanaʿū innamā ṣanaʿū kaydu sāḥirin walā yuf'liḥu l-sāḥiru ḥaythu atā And cast down what is in thy right hand: It shall swallow up what they have wrought; Verily they have wrought by the plan of a sorcerer, and a sorcerer shall not be successful whatso ever manner (of skill) (Whatever point of Skill they may come with.) he may come from. See 20:67

item.title: Taa-Haa:70 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأُلْقِيَ السَّحَرَةُ سُجَّدًا قَالُوْا اٰمَنَّا بِرَبِّ هَارُونَ وَمُوسٰی fa-ul'qiya l-saḥaratu sujjadan qālū āmannā birabbi hārūna wamūsā Thereat the magicians fell down prostrating. They said, 'We have believed in the Lord of Aaron and Moses!'

item.title: Taa-Haa:70 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأُلْقِيَ السَّحَرَةُ سُجَّدًا قَالُوْا اٰمَنَّا بِرَبِّ هَارُونَ وَمُوسٰی fa-ul'qiya l-saḥaratu sujjadan qālū āmannā birabbi hārūna wamūsā So the magicians fell down in prostration.1 They said, "We have believed in the Lord of Harun and Musa." See 20:65

item.title: Taa-Haa:70 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأُلْقِيَ السَّحَرَةُ سُجَّدًا قَالُوْا اٰمَنَّا بِرَبِّ هَارُونَ وَمُوسٰی fa-ul'qiya l-saḥaratu sujjadan qālū āmannā birabbi hārūna wamūsā Then fell down the sorcerers prostrating (in obeisance) they said: "We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses!" This indicates the difference between miracle and sorcery. The result of a miracle is real and lasting whereas that of sorcery is unreal and momentary1. (A.P.).

item.title: Taa-Haa:71 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ ءَامَنْتُمْ لَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمْ إِنَّهُ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ الَّذِي عَلَّمَكُمُ السِّحْرَ فَلَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ مِنْ خِلَافٍ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِي جُذُوعِ النَّخْلِ وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أَيُّنَا أَشَدُّ عَذَابًا وَأَبْقَى qāla āmantum lahu qabla an ādhana lakum innahu lakabīrukumu alladhī ʿallamakumu l-siḥ'ra fala-uqaṭṭiʿanna aydiyakum wa-arjulakum min khilāfin wala-uṣallibannakum fī judhūʿi l-nakhli walataʿlamunna ayyunā ashaddu ʿadhāban wa-abqā He said, 'Do you profess faith in Him before I may permit you? He is indeed your chief who has taught you magic! Surely I will cut off your hands and feet from opposite sides, and I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees. So you will know which of us can inflict a punishment severer and more lasting.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:71 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ ءَامَنْتُمْ لَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمْ إِنَّهُ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ الَّذِي عَلَّمَكُمُ السِّحْرَ فَلَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ مِنْ خِلَافٍ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِي جُذُوعِ النَّخْلِ وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أَيُّنَا أَشَدُّ عَذَابًا وَأَبْقَى qāla āmantum lahu qabla an ādhana lakum innahu lakabīrukumu alladhī ʿallamakumu l-siḥ'ra fala-uqaṭṭiʿanna aydiyakum wa-arjulakum min khilāfin wala-uṣallibannakum fī judhūʿi l-nakhli walataʿlamunna ayyunā ashaddu ʿadhāban wa-abqā (Pharaoh) said, "You believed him (i.e., Musa) before I gave you permission. Indeed, he is your leader who has taught you magic. So I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, and you will surely know which of us is more severe in (giving) punishment and more enduring." (Fir'awn) said: Believe you in him before I give you permission? Verily, he is your chief who has taught you magic. So I will…

item.title: Taa-Haa:71 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ ءَامَنْتُمْ لَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمْ إِنَّهُ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ الَّذِي عَلَّمَكُمُ السِّحْرَ فَلَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ مِنْ خِلَافٍ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِي جُذُوعِ النَّخْلِ وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أَيُّنَا أَشَدُّ عَذَابًا وَأَبْقَى qāla āmantum lahu qabla an ādhana lakum innahu lakabīrukumu alladhī ʿallamakumu l-siḥ'ra fala-uqaṭṭiʿanna aydiyakum wa-arjulakum min khilāfin wala-uṣallibannakum fī judhūʿi l-nakhli walataʿlamunna ayyunā ashaddu ʿadhāban wa-abqā Said (Pharaoh): "Believe ye in him ere I give ye leave (to do it)? Verily he is your Chief (sorcerer) who hath taught you sorcery, so I shall certainly cut off your hands and your feet on the opposite sides, and I will certainly crucify you on the trunks of the palm trees, then will ye certainly know which (Me or the Lord of Moses.) of us is more severe in tormenting and abiding!" See 20:70

item.title: Taa-Haa:72 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا لَنْ نُؤْثِرَكَ عَلَى مَا جَاءَنَا مِنَ الْبَيِّنَاتِ وَالَّذِي فَطَرَنَا فَاقْضِ مَا أَنْتَ قَاضٍ إِنَّمَا تَقْضِي هَذِهِ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا qālū lan nu'thiraka ʿalā mā jāanā mina l-bayināti wa-alladhī faṭaranā fa-iq'ḍi mā anta qāḍin innamā taqḍī hādhihi l-ḥayata l-dun'yā They said, 'We will never prefer you to the manifest proofs which have come to us and [to] Him who originated us. Decide whatever you may. You can only decide about the life of this world.

item.title: Taa-Haa:72 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا لَنْ نُؤْثِرَكَ عَلَى مَا جَاءَنَا مِنَ الْبَيِّنَاتِ وَالَّذِي فَطَرَنَا فَاقْضِ مَا أَنْتَ قَاضٍ إِنَّمَا تَقْضِي هَذِهِ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا qālū lan nu'thiraka ʿalā mā jāanā mina l-bayināti wa-alladhī faṭaranā fa-iq'ḍi mā anta qāḍin innamā taqḍī hādhihi l-ḥayata l-dun'yā They said, "Never will we prefer you over what has come to us of clear proofs and (over) He who created us.1 So decree whatever you are to decree. You can only decree for this worldly life. See 20:71

item.title: Taa-Haa:72 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا لَنْ نُؤْثِرَكَ عَلَى مَا جَاءَنَا مِنَ الْبَيِّنَاتِ وَالَّذِي فَطَرَنَا فَاقْضِ مَا أَنْتَ قَاضٍ إِنَّمَا تَقْضِي هَذِهِ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا qālū lan nu'thiraka ʿalā mā jāanā mina l-bayināti wa-alladhī faṭaranā fa-iq'ḍi mā anta qāḍin innamā taqḍī hādhihi l-ḥayata l-dun'yā They said: "Never will we prefer thee (O' Pharaoh!) to what hath come unto us of the clear signs, and to Him Who made us, so decree thou whatever decree thou decreeth; for thou canst decree only about the life of this world" See 20:70

item.title: Taa-Haa:73 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا اٰمَنَّا بِرَبِّنَا لِيَغْفِرَ لَنَا خَطَايَانَا وَمَا أَكْرَهْتَنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ السِّحْرِ وَاللَّهُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَى innā āmannā birabbinā liyaghfira lanā khaṭāyānā wamā akrahtanā ʿalayhi mina l-siḥ'ri wal-lahu khayrun wa-abqā We have indeed believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our iniquities and the magic you compelled us to perform. Allah is better and more lasting.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:73 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا اٰمَنَّا بِرَبِّنَا لِيَغْفِرَ لَنَا خَطَايَانَا وَمَا أَكْرَهْتَنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ السِّحْرِ وَاللَّهُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَى innā āmannā birabbinā liyaghfira lanā khaṭāyānā wamā akrahtanā ʿalayhi mina l-siḥ'ri wal-lahu khayrun wa-abqā Indeed, we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and what you compelled us (to do) of magic. And Allah is better and more enduring."1 See 20:71

item.title: Taa-Haa:73 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا اٰمَنَّا بِرَبِّنَا لِيَغْفِرَ لَنَا خَطَايَانَا وَمَا أَكْرَهْتَنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ السِّحْرِ وَاللَّهُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَى innā āmannā birabbinā liyaghfira lanā khaṭāyānā wamā akrahtanā ʿalayhi mina l-siḥ'ri wal-lahu khayrun wa-abqā Verily we! we do believe in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and the sorcery thou didst compel us (to do); and God is the Best and the Most (The Eternal.) Abiding! See 20:70

item.title: Taa-Haa:74 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّهُ مَنْ يَأْتِ رَبَّهُ مُجْرِمًا فَإِنَّ لَهُ جَهَنَّمَ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَى innahu man yati rabbahu muj'riman fa-inna lahu jahannama lā yamūtu fīhā walā yaḥyā Whoever comes to his Lord laden with guilt, indeed for him shall be hell where he will neither live nor die.

item.title: Taa-Haa:74 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّهُ مَنْ يَأْتِ رَبَّهُ مُجْرِمًا فَإِنَّ لَهُ جَهَنَّمَ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَى innahu man yati rabbahu muj'riman fa-inna lahu jahannama lā yamūtu fīhā walā yaḥyā Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal - indeed, for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live. Verily, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal, then surely, for him is Hell, wherein he will neither die nor live (20:74). But whoever comes to Him as a believer, and has done righteous good deeds, for such are the high ranks (20:75). 'Adn Gardens, under which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever, and such is the reward of those who purify themselves (20:76). The Magicians Admonish Fir'awn The clear intent of this is to be a completion of what the magicians admonished Fir'awn with. They warned him of the…

item.title: Taa-Haa:74 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّهُ مَنْ يَأْتِ رَبَّهُ مُجْرِمًا فَإِنَّ لَهُ جَهَنَّمَ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَى innahu man yati rabbahu muj'riman fa-inna lahu jahannama lā yamūtu fīhā walā yaḥyā And verily he who cometh unto his Lord as guilty, for him certainly is Hell; he shall die not in it nor shall he live. Those committed to Hell would suffer the life which would be worse than death, and though they would prefer death but it would not be given to them, for death would mean the cessation of the torment to which they would be committed. The life in Hell would be a continued consciousness.

item.title: Taa-Haa:75 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَنْ يَأْتِهِ مُؤْمِنًا قَدْ عَمِلَ الصَّالِحَاتِ فَأُولَئِكَ لَهُمُ الدَّرَجَاتُ الْعُلَى waman yatihi mu'minan qad ʿamila l-ṣāliḥāti fa-ulāika lahumu l-darajātu l-ʿulā But whoever comes to Him with faith and he has done righteous deeds, for such shall be the highest ranks

item.title: Taa-Haa:75 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَنْ يَأْتِهِ مُؤْمِنًا قَدْ عَمِلَ الصَّالِحَاتِ فَأُولَئِكَ لَهُمُ الدَّرَجَاتُ الْعُلَى waman yatihi mu'minan qad ʿamila l-ṣāliḥāti fa-ulāika lahumu l-darajātu l-ʿulā But whoever comes to Him as a believer having done righteous deeds - for those will be the highest degrees (in position). See 20:74

item.title: Taa-Haa:75 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَنْ يَأْتِهِ مُؤْمِنًا قَدْ عَمِلَ الصَّالِحَاتِ فَأُولَئِكَ لَهُمُ الدَّرَجَاتُ الْعُلَى waman yatihi mu'minan qad ʿamila l-ṣāliḥāti fa-ulāika lahumu l-darajātu l-ʿulā And whosoever cometh unto Him as a believer and who hath indeed done good deeds, these, for them are the ranks high, The life in Paradise will be a continued consciousness of enjoyment of the sublime bliss and the grace of the Lord mentioned in these verses.

item.title: Taa-Haa:76 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا وَذٰلِكَ جَزَاءُ مَنْ تَزَكَّى jannātu ʿadnin tajrī min taḥtihā l-anhāru khālidīna fīhā wadhālika jazāu man tazakkā —the Gardens of Eden, with streams running in them, to abide in them [forever], and that is the reward of him who keeps pure.

item.title: Taa-Haa:76 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا وَذٰلِكَ جَزَاءُ مَنْ تَزَكَّى jannātu ʿadnin tajrī min taḥtihā l-anhāru khālidīna fīhā wadhālika jazāu man tazakkā Gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. And that is the reward of one who purifies himself.1 See 20:74

item.title: Taa-Haa:76 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا وَذٰلِكَ جَزَاءُ مَنْ تَزَكَّى jannātu ʿadnin tajrī min taḥtihā l-anhāru khālidīna fīhā wadhālika jazāu man tazakkā The Gardens (Paradise.) of Eternity, beneath which flow rivers, to abide therein; and this is the recompense of him who purifieth (Refer to verses 8:14(in contrast) & 91:9 & 91:10.) himself (from evil). See 20:75

item.title: Taa-Haa:77 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى مُوسٰی أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبَادِي فَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ طَرِيقًا فِي الْبَحْرِ يَبَسًا لَا تَخَافُ دَرَكًا وَلَا تَخْشٰی walaqad awḥaynā ilā mūsā an asri biʿibādī fa-iḍ'rib lahum ṭarīqan fī l-baḥri yabasan lā takhāfu darakan walā takhshā Certainly We revealed to Moses, [saying], 'Take My servants on a journey by night. Then strike out for them a dry path through the sea. Do not be afraid of being overtaken, and have no fear [of getting drowned].

item.title: Taa-Haa:77 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى مُوسٰی أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبَادِي فَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ طَرِيقًا فِي الْبَحْرِ يَبَسًا لَا تَخَافُ دَرَكًا وَلَا تَخْشٰی walaqad awḥaynā ilā mūsā an asri biʿibādī fa-iḍ'rib lahum ṭarīqan fī l-baḥri yabasan lā takhāfu darakan walā takhshā And We had inspired to Musa, "Travel by night with My servants and strike for them a dry path through the sea; you will not fear being overtaken (by Pharaoh) nor be afraid (of drowning)." And indeed We revealed to Musa: Travel by night with My servants and strike a dry path for them in the sea, fearing neither to be overtaken nor being afraid (20:77). Then Fir'awn pursued them with his hosts, but the sea (Al-Yamm) completely overwhelmed them and covered them up (20:78). And Fir'awn led his people astray, and he did not guide them (20:79). The Children of Israel Leave Egypt…

item.title: Taa-Haa:77 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى مُوسٰی أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبَادِي فَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ طَرِيقًا فِي الْبَحْرِ يَبَسًا لَا تَخَافُ دَرَكًا وَلَا تَخْشٰی walaqad awḥaynā ilā mūsā an asri biʿibādī fa-iḍ'rib lahum ṭarīqan fī l-baḥri yabasan lā takhāfu darakan walā takhshā And indeed We revealed unto Moses (saying); "Travel thou by night with My servants, and strike for them a dry path in the sea, not fearing to be overtaken (by Pharaoh), nor be thou afraid (of getting drowned)" Moses was Commanded by God to strike at the water of the sea in front of him. Twelve dry paths were effected through the deep water, for the Twelve Tribes of the Israelites to march away to safety. Moses was assured of not being overtaken by Pharaoh in the safe passage through the sea. The water was split and made to stand still like huge walls…

item.title: Taa-Haa:78 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ بِجُنُودِهِ فَغَشِيَهُمْ مِنَ الْيَمِّ مَا غَشِيَهُمْ fa-atbaʿahum fir'ʿawnu bijunūdihi faghashiyahum mina l-yami mā ghashiyahum Then Pharaoh pursued them with his troops, whereat they were engulfed by what engulfed them of the sea.

item.title: Taa-Haa:78 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ بِجُنُودِهِ فَغَشِيَهُمْ مِنَ الْيَمِّ مَا غَشِيَهُمْ fa-atbaʿahum fir'ʿawnu bijunūdihi faghashiyahum mina l-yami mā ghashiyahum So Pharaoh pursued them with his soldiers, and there covered them from the sea that which covered them.1 See 20:77

item.title: Taa-Haa:78 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ بِجُنُودِهِ فَغَشِيَهُمْ مِنَ الْيَمِّ مَا غَشِيَهُمْ fa-atbaʿahum fir'ʿawnu bijunūdihi faghashiyahum mina l-yami mā ghashiyahum And followed them Pharaoh with his hosts, so covered them (the billows) of the sea, as they were they covered (drowned). See 20:77

item.title: Taa-Haa:79 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَضَلَّ فِرْعَوْنُ قَوْمَهُ وَمَا هَدَى wa-aḍalla fir'ʿawnu qawmahu wamā hadā Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide them.

item.title: Taa-Haa:79 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَضَلَّ فِرْعَوْنُ قَوْمَهُ وَمَا هَدَى wa-aḍalla fir'ʿawnu qawmahu wamā hadā And Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide (them). See 20:77

item.title: Taa-Haa:79 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَضَلَّ فِرْعَوْنُ قَوْمَهُ وَمَا هَدَى wa-aḍalla fir'ʿawnu qawmahu wamā hadā And Pharaoh led astray his people and he did not guide them (aright) See 20:77

item.title: Taa-Haa:80 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَابَنِي إِسْرَاءِيلَ قَدْ أَنْجَيْنَاكُمْ مِنْ عَدُوِّكُمْ وَوَاعَدْنَاكُمْ جَانِبَ الطُّورِ الْأَيْمَنَ وَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَنَّ وَالسَّلْوَى yābanī is'rāīla qad anjaynākum min ʿaduwwikum wawāʿadnākum jāniba l-ṭūri l-aymana wanazzalnā ʿalaykumu l-mana wal-salwā O Children of Israel! We delivered you from your enemy, and We appointed with you a tryst on the right side of the Mount and We sent down to you manna and quails:

item.title: Taa-Haa:80 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَابَنِي إِسْرَاءِيلَ قَدْ أَنْجَيْنَاكُمْ مِنْ عَدُوِّكُمْ وَوَاعَدْنَاكُمْ جَانِبَ الطُّورِ الْأَيْمَنَ وَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَنَّ وَالسَّلْوَى yābanī is'rāīla qad anjaynākum min ʿaduwwikum wawāʿadnākum jāniba l-ṭūri l-aymana wanazzalnā ʿalaykumu l-mana wal-salwā O Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy, and We made an appointment with you1 at the right side of the mount, and We sent down to you manna and quails. O Children of Israel! We delivered you from your enemy, and We made a covenant with you on the right side of the Mount, and We sent down to you manna and quail (20:80). (Saying) eat of the Tayyibat wherewith We have provided you, and commit no transgression or oppression therein, lest My anger should justly descend on you. And he on whom My anger descends, he is indeed perished (20:81). And verily, I am indeed forgiving to him…

item.title: Taa-Haa:80 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَابَنِي إِسْرَاءِيلَ قَدْ أَنْجَيْنَاكُمْ مِنْ عَدُوِّكُمْ وَوَاعَدْنَاكُمْ جَانِبَ الطُّورِ الْأَيْمَنَ وَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَنَّ وَالسَّلْوَى yābanī is'rāīla qad anjaynākum min ʿaduwwikum wawāʿadnākum jāniba l-ṭūri l-aymana wanazzalnā ʿalaykumu l-mana wal-salwā ("O' Children of Israel!) We rescued you from your foe; and We made a covenant with of Israel!) you on the right side of 'Tur' (the Mount Sinai), and We sent down unto you Manna and quails:" See 20:77

item.title: Taa-Haa:81 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: كُلُوْۤا مِنْ طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ وَلَا تَطْغَوْا فِیْهِ فَيَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبِي وَمَنْ يَحْلِلْ عَلَيْهِ غَضَبِي فَقَدْ هَوَى kulū min ṭayyibāti mā razaqnākum walā taṭghaw fīhi fayaḥilla ʿalaykum ghaḍabī waman yaḥlil ʿalayhi ghaḍabī faqad hawā 'Eat of the good things We have provided you, but do not overstep the bounds therein, lest My wrath should descend on you. And he on whom My wrath descends certainly perishes.1

item.title: Taa-Haa:81 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: كُلُوْۤا مِنْ طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ وَلَا تَطْغَوْا فِیْهِ فَيَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبِي وَمَنْ يَحْلِلْ عَلَيْهِ غَضَبِي فَقَدْ هَوَى kulū min ṭayyibāti mā razaqnākum walā taṭghaw fīhi fayaḥilla ʿalaykum ghaḍabī waman yaḥlil ʿalayhi ghaḍabī faqad hawā (Saying), "Eat from the good things with which We have provided you and do not transgress (or oppress others) therein, lest My anger should descend upon you. And he upon whom My anger descends has certainly fallen (i.e., perished)." See 20:80

item.title: Taa-Haa:81 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: كُلُوْۤا مِنْ طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ وَلَا تَطْغَوْا فِیْهِ فَيَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبِي وَمَنْ يَحْلِلْ عَلَيْهِ غَضَبِي فَقَدْ هَوَى kulū min ṭayyibāti mā razaqnākum walā taṭghaw fīhi fayaḥilla ʿalaykum ghaḍabī waman yaḥlil ʿalayhi ghaḍabī faqad hawā Eat ye of the good things We have provided you with and transgress (Exceed not.) not in it, lest descendeth on you My wrath, and on whomsoever My wrath doth descend, indeed he is perished. See 20:77

item.title: Taa-Haa:82 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنِّي لَغَفَّارٌ لِمَنْ تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا ثُمَّ اهْتَدَى wa-innī laghaffārun liman tāba waāmana waʿamila ṣāliḥan thumma ih'tadā Indeed I am all-forgiver toward him who repents, becomes faithful and acts righteously, and then follows guidance.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:82 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنِّي لَغَفَّارٌ لِمَنْ تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا ثُمَّ اهْتَدَى wa-innī laghaffārun liman tāba waāmana waʿamila ṣāliḥan thumma ih'tadā But indeed, I am the Perpetual Forgiver of whoever repents and believes and does righteousness and then continues in guidance. See 20:80

item.title: Taa-Haa:82 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنِّي لَغَفَّارٌ لِمَنْ تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا ثُمَّ اهْتَدَى wa-innī laghaffārun liman tāba waāmana waʿamila ṣāliḥan thumma ih'tadā And verily I am the Most Forgiving unto him who repenteth and believeth and doth good, then he doth continue to follow the right guidance. Note the most reasonable assurance of forgiveness extended to the sinner which is subject to sincere repentance with the amendment of the conduct on the part of the offender of the Divine Law, against the belief in the unconditional redemption of the sinners based upon the belief of the price of the sins having been paid away to God in the blood of any one. Any such belief is a greatest danger to the moral and the social life of the human race on earth, for any one can merely profess such a dogmatic belief and do…

item.title: Taa-Haa:83 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَعْجَلَكَ عَنْ قَوْمِكَ يَامُوسٰی wamā aʿjalaka ʿan qawmika yāmūsā 'What has hurried you from your people, O Moses?'

item.title: Taa-Haa:83 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَعْجَلَكَ عَنْ قَوْمِكَ يَامُوسٰی wamā aʿjalaka ʿan qawmika yāmūsā (Allah said), "And what made you hasten from your people, O Musa?" And what made you hasten from your people, O Musa (20:83). He said: "They are close on my footsteps, and I hastened to You, O my Lord, that You might be pleased (20:84). (Allah) said: "Verily, We have tried your people in your absence, and As-Samiri has led them astray (20:85). Then Musa returned to his people in a state of anger and sorrow (Asif). He said: "O my people! Did not your Lord promise you a fair promise? Did then the promise seem to you long in coming? Or did you desire that wrath should descend from your Lord on you, that you broke your promise to me? (20:86). They said: "We broke not the promise to…

item.title: Taa-Haa:83 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَعْجَلَكَ عَنْ قَوْمِكَ يَامُوسٰی wamā aʿjalaka ʿan qawmika yāmūsā (Said God): "But what made thee hasten (thyself on apart) from thy people, O' Moses!" After they had been recovered from the clutches of Pharaoh, the Israelites wanted Moses to get for them the laws regulating their lives to be prescribed by God. When Moses prayed for the laws, God summoned Moses to Mount Sinai. Moses left his brother Aaron in his place at the head of the people and went on the Mount. On reaching the Mount, Moses left the chosen men at the foot of the Mountain and hastened himself up on the mountain. Similarly, when the Holy Prophet was commanded by God to migrate to Madina, he left Ali in his bed as did Moses leave Aaron. Again, when the Holy Prophet left for Tabuk, he left…

item.title: Taa-Haa:84 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ هُمْ أُولَاءِ عَلَى أَثَرِي وَعَجِلْتُ إِلَيْكَ رَبِّ لِتَرْضَى qāla hum ulāi ʿalā atharī waʿajil'tu ilayka rabbi litarḍā He said, 'They are close upon my heels, and I hurried on to You, my Lord, that You may be pleased.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:84 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ هُمْ أُولَاءِ عَلَى أَثَرِي وَعَجِلْتُ إِلَيْكَ رَبِّ لِتَرْضَى qāla hum ulāi ʿalā atharī waʿajil'tu ilayka rabbi litarḍā He said, "They are close upon my tracks, and I hastened to You, my Lord, that You be pleased." See 20:83

item.title: Taa-Haa:84 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ هُمْ أُولَاءِ عَلَى أَثَرِي وَعَجِلْتُ إِلَيْكَ رَبِّ لِتَرْضَى qāla hum ulāi ʿalā atharī waʿajil'tu ilayka rabbi litarḍā Said (Moses): "They are close on my track and I hastened unto Thee O' my Lord! that thou mightest be well pleased (with me)!" Moses' haste was to please God with his readiness and haste in carrying out His Command to report himself with the men at the place.

item.title: Taa-Haa:85 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ فَإِنَّا قَدْ فَتَنَّا قَوْمَكَ مِنْ بَعْدِكَ وَأَضَلَّهُمُ السَّامِرِيُّ qāla fa-innā qad fatannā qawmaka min baʿdika wa-aḍallahumu l-sāmiriyu He said, 'Indeed We tried your people in your absence, and the Sāmirī1 has led them astray.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:85 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ فَإِنَّا قَدْ فَتَنَّا قَوْمَكَ مِنْ بَعْدِكَ وَأَضَلَّهُمُ السَّامِرِيُّ qāla fa-innā qad fatannā qawmaka min baʿdika wa-aḍallahumu l-sāmiriyu (Allah) said, "But indeed, We have tried your people after you (departed), and the Sāmirī1 has led them astray." See 20:83

item.title: Taa-Haa:85 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ فَإِنَّا قَدْ فَتَنَّا قَوْمَكَ مِنْ بَعْدِكَ وَأَضَلَّهُمُ السَّامِرِيُّ qāla fa-innā qad fatannā qawmaka min baʿdika wa-aḍallahumu l-sāmiriyu Said (God): "Verily We have tried thy people in thine absence, and the Samiri had led them astray." Samiri, a calf-worshipper who only professed belief in God and at heart was a disbeliever, was among those who followed Moses out of Egypt. When Moses had gone on Mount Sinai with the chosen men and there was only Aaron in his place at the head of the people, Samiri managed to get the people agreed to making a calf of the jewels of gold which the Israelites had bought from the Egyptians. By some witchcraft Samiri managed to create some sound from the hollow of the golden calf made by him and in spite of Aaron's efforts to keep the people away from…

item.title: Taa-Haa:86 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَرَجَعَ مُوسٰی إِلَى قَوْمِهِ غَضْبَانَ أَسِفًا قَالَ يَاقَوْمِ أَلَمْ يَعِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ وَعْدًا حَسَنًا أَفَطَالَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْعَهْدُ أَمْ أَرَدْتُمْ أَنْ يَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فَأَخْلَفْتُمْ مَوْعِدِي farajaʿa mūsā ilā qawmihi ghaḍbāna asifan qāla yāqawmi alam yaʿid'kum rabbukum waʿdan ḥasanan afaṭāla ʿalaykumu l-ʿahdu am aradttum an yaḥilla ʿalaykum ghaḍabun min rabbikum fa-akhlaftum mawʿidī Thereupon Moses returned to his people, indignant and grieved. He said, 'O my people! Did not your Lord give you a true promise? Did the period [of my absence]seem too long to you? Or did you desire that your Lord's wrath should descend on you and so you failed your tryst with me?'

item.title: Taa-Haa:86 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَرَجَعَ مُوسٰی إِلَى قَوْمِهِ غَضْبَانَ أَسِفًا قَالَ يَاقَوْمِ أَلَمْ يَعِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ وَعْدًا حَسَنًا أَفَطَالَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْعَهْدُ أَمْ أَرَدْتُمْ أَنْ يَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فَأَخْلَفْتُمْ مَوْعِدِي farajaʿa mūsā ilā qawmihi ghaḍbāna asifan qāla yāqawmi alam yaʿid'kum rabbukum waʿdan ḥasanan afaṭāla ʿalaykumu l-ʿahdu am aradttum an yaḥilla ʿalaykum ghaḍabun min rabbikum fa-akhlaftum mawʿidī So Musa returned to his people, angry and grieved.1 He said, "O my people, did your Lord not make you a good promise?2 Then, was the time (of its fulfillment) too long for you, or did you wish that wrath from your Lord descend upon you, so you broke your promise (of obedience) to me?" See 20:83

item.title: Taa-Haa:86 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَرَجَعَ مُوسٰی إِلَى قَوْمِهِ غَضْبَانَ أَسِفًا قَالَ يَاقَوْمِ أَلَمْ يَعِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ وَعْدًا حَسَنًا أَفَطَالَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْعَهْدُ أَمْ أَرَدْتُمْ أَنْ يَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فَأَخْلَفْتُمْ مَوْعِدِي farajaʿa mūsā ilā qawmihi ghaḍbāna asifan qāla yāqawmi alam yaʿid'kum rabbukum waʿdan ḥasanan afaṭāla ʿalaykumu l-ʿahdu am aradttum an yaḥilla ʿalaykum ghaḍabun min rabbikum fa-akhlaftum mawʿidī So returned Moses unto his people angered, sorrowfully said he! "O' my people! Did not your Lord promise you a goodly promise? Did then the promise seem long to you? or did ye wish, or desired ye that the wrath from your Lord should light (Came upon.) upon you? that ye violated the tryst with me?" See 20:85

item.title: Taa-Haa:87 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا مَا أَخْلَفْنَا مَوْعِدَكَ بِمَلْكِنَا وَلَكِنَّا حُمِّلْنَا أَوْزَارًا مِنْ زِينَةِ الْقَوْمِ فَقَذَفْنَاهَا فَكَذٰلِكَ أَلْقَى السَّامِرِيُّ qālū mā akhlafnā mawʿidaka bimalkinā walākinnā ḥummil'nā awzāran min zīnati l-qawmi faqadhafnāhā fakadhālika alqā l-sāmiriyu They said, 'We did not fail our tryst with you of our own accord, but we were laden with the weight of the people's ornaments, and we cast them [into the fire] and so did the Sāmirī throw.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:87 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا مَا أَخْلَفْنَا مَوْعِدَكَ بِمَلْكِنَا وَلَكِنَّا حُمِّلْنَا أَوْزَارًا مِنْ زِينَةِ الْقَوْمِ فَقَذَفْنَاهَا فَكَذٰلِكَ أَلْقَى السَّامِرِيُّ qālū mā akhlafnā mawʿidaka bimalkinā walākinnā ḥummil'nā awzāran min zīnati l-qawmi faqadhafnāhā fakadhālika alqā l-sāmiriyu They said, "We did not break our promise to you by our will, but we were made to carry burdens from the ornaments of the people (of Pharaoh), so we threw them (into the fire), and thus did the Sāmirī throw." See 20:83

item.title: Taa-Haa:87 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا مَا أَخْلَفْنَا مَوْعِدَكَ بِمَلْكِنَا وَلَكِنَّا حُمِّلْنَا أَوْزَارًا مِنْ زِينَةِ الْقَوْمِ فَقَذَفْنَاهَا فَكَذٰلِكَ أَلْقَى السَّامِرِيُّ qālū mā akhlafnā mawʿidaka bimalkinā walākinnā ḥummil'nā awzāran min zīnati l-qawmi faqadhafnāhā fakadhālika alqā l-sāmiriyu Said they: "We violated not the tryst with thee of our own accord, but we were made to bear the burdens of the ornaments of the people, so we cast them away, and thus didst the Samiri suggest" See 20:85

item.title: Taa-Haa:88 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَخْرَجَ لَهُمْ عِجْلًا جَسَدًا لَهُ خُوَارٌ فَقَالُوْۤا هَذَا إِلَهُكُمْ وَإِلَهُ مُوسٰی فَنَسِيَ fa-akhraja lahum ʿij'lan jasadan lahu khuwārun faqālū hādhā ilāhukum wa-ilāhu mūsā fanasiya Then he produced for them a calf —a [lifeless] body with a low— and they said, This is your god and the god of Moses, so he1 forgot!

item.title: Taa-Haa:88 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَخْرَجَ لَهُمْ عِجْلًا جَسَدًا لَهُ خُوَارٌ فَقَالُوْۤا هَذَا إِلَهُكُمْ وَإِلَهُ مُوسٰی فَنَسِيَ fa-akhraja lahum ʿij'lan jasadan lahu khuwārun faqālū hādhā ilāhukum wa-ilāhu mūsā fanasiya And he extracted for them (the statue of) a calf which had a lowing sound, and they said, "This is your god and the god of Musa, but he forgot." See 20:83

item.title: Taa-Haa:88 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَخْرَجَ لَهُمْ عِجْلًا جَسَدًا لَهُ خُوَارٌ فَقَالُوْۤا هَذَا إِلَهُكُمْ وَإِلَهُ مُوسٰی فَنَسِيَ fa-akhraja lahum ʿij'lan jasadan lahu khuwārun faqālū hādhā ilāhukum wa-ilāhu mūsā fanasiya Then he brought forth (from the fire) for them (the image of) a calf, a (mere) body; which (also) gave out the lowing sound; Then they said: "This is your god and the god of Moses, but he (Moses) hath forgotten," See 20:85

item.title: Taa-Haa:89 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَلَّا يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَوْلًا وَلَا يَمْلِكُ لَهُمْ ضَرًّا وَلَا نَفْعًا afalā yarawna allā yarjiʿu ilayhim qawlan walā yamliku lahum ḍarran walā nafʿan Did they not see that it did not answer them, nor could it bring them any benefit or harm?

item.title: Taa-Haa:89 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَلَّا يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَوْلًا وَلَا يَمْلِكُ لَهُمْ ضَرًّا وَلَا نَفْعًا afalā yarawna allā yarjiʿu ilayhim qawlan walā yamliku lahum ḍarran walā nafʿan Did they not see that it could not return to them any speech (i.e., response) and that it did not possess for them any harm or benefit? See 20:83

item.title: Taa-Haa:89 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَلَّا يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَوْلًا وَلَا يَمْلِكُ لَهُمْ ضَرًّا وَلَا نَفْعًا afalā yarawna allā yarjiʿu ilayhim qawlan walā yamliku lahum ḍarran walā nafʿan What! See they not that it could not return unto them a word (In reply.) (for an answer) and that it could neither hurt nor benefit them? See 20:85

item.title: Taa-Haa:90 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ قَالَ لَهُمْ هَارُونُ مِنْ قَبْلُ يَاقَوْمِ إِنَّمَا فُتِنْتُمْ بِهِ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ الرَّحْمَنُ فَاتَّبِعُونِي وَأَطِيعُوا أَمْرِي walaqad qāla lahum hārūnu min qablu yāqawmi innamā futintum bihi wa-inna rabbakumu l-raḥmānu fa-ittabiʿūnī wa-aṭīʿū amrī Aaron had certainly told them earlier, 'O my people! You are only being tested by it. Indeed your Lord is the All-beneficent. So follow me and obey my command!'

item.title: Taa-Haa:90 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ قَالَ لَهُمْ هَارُونُ مِنْ قَبْلُ يَاقَوْمِ إِنَّمَا فُتِنْتُمْ بِهِ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ الرَّحْمَنُ فَاتَّبِعُونِي وَأَطِيعُوا أَمْرِي walaqad qāla lahum hārūnu min qablu yāqawmi innamā futintum bihi wa-inna rabbakumu l-raḥmānu fa-ittabiʿūnī wa-aṭīʿū amrī And Harun had already told them before (the return of Musa), "O my people, you are only being tested by it, and indeed, your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my order." And Harun indeed had said to them beforehand: "O my people! You are being tried in this, and verily, your Lord is (Allah) the Most Gracious, so follow me and obey my order (20:90). They said: "We will not stop worshipping it, until Musa returns to us (20:91). Harun Prohibits them from Worship of the Calf and the Persistence of the Children of Israel in Doing so Allah, the Exalted, informs of…

item.title: Taa-Haa:90 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ قَالَ لَهُمْ هَارُونُ مِنْ قَبْلُ يَاقَوْمِ إِنَّمَا فُتِنْتُمْ بِهِ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ الرَّحْمَنُ فَاتَّبِعُونِي وَأَطِيعُوا أَمْرِي walaqad qāla lahum hārūnu min qablu yāqawmi innamā futintum bihi wa-inna rabbakumu l-raḥmānu fa-ittabiʿūnī wa-aṭīʿū amrī And indeed Aaron had said unto them before: "O' my people! Verily, ye are tried by it (the image) and verily your Lord is the Beneficent (God), so follow me and obey ye my order." Though Aaron was warning them against the misleading temptation, the Israelites were being tested by God - the Israelites did not pay any heed to Aaron's admonition.

item.title: Taa-Haa:91 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا لَنْ نَبْرَحَ عَلَيْهِ عَاكِفِينَ حَتّٰی يَرْجِعَ إِلَيْنَا مُوسٰی qālū lan nabraḥa ʿalayhi ʿākifīna ḥattā yarjiʿa ilaynā mūsā They had said, 'We will keep on clinging to it until Moses returns to us.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:91 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا لَنْ نَبْرَحَ عَلَيْهِ عَاكِفِينَ حَتّٰی يَرْجِعَ إِلَيْنَا مُوسٰی qālū lan nabraḥa ʿalayhi ʿākifīna ḥattā yarjiʿa ilaynā mūsā They said, "We will never cease being devoted to it (i.e., the calf) until Musa returns to us." See 20:90

item.title: Taa-Haa:91 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا لَنْ نَبْرَحَ عَلَيْهِ عَاكِفِينَ حَتّٰی يَرْجِعَ إِلَيْنَا مُوسٰی qālū lan nabraḥa ʿalayhi ʿākifīna ḥattā yarjiʿa ilaynā mūsā Said they: "Never will we cease worshipping it until returneth unto us Moses." See 20:90

item.title: Taa-Haa:92 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ يَاهَارُونُ مَا مَنَعَكَ إِذْ رَأَيْتَهُمْ ضَلُّوْۤا qāla yāhārūnu mā manaʿaka idh ra-aytahum ḍallū He said, 'O Aaron! What kept you, when you saw them going astray,

item.title: Taa-Haa:92 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ يَاهَارُونُ مَا مَنَعَكَ إِذْ رَأَيْتَهُمْ ضَلُّوْۤا qāla yāhārūnu mā manaʿaka idh ra-aytahum ḍallū (Musa) said, "O Harun, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray. (Musa) said: O Harun! What prevented you when you saw them going astray; (20:92). "That you followed me not (according to my advice to you)? Have you then disobeyed my order? (20:93). He (Harun) said: "O son of my mother! Seize (me) not by my beard, nor by my head! Verily, I feared lest you should say: 'You have caused a division among the Children of Israel, and you have not respected my word!' (20:94). What Happened between Musa and Harun after Musa Returned Allah informs of what happened when Musa returned to his people and saw the great matter that had taken place among them. With this he became filled with anger…

item.title: Taa-Haa:92 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ يَاهَارُونُ مَا مَنَعَكَ إِذْ رَأَيْتَهُمْ ضَلُّوْۤا qāla yāhārūnu mā manaʿaka idh ra-aytahum ḍallū (Moses) said: "O' Aaron! What hindered thee when thou didst see them going astray," See 20:90

item.title: Taa-Haa:93 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَّا تَتَّبِعَنِ أَفَعَصَيْتَ أَمْرِي allā tattabiʿani afaʿaṣayta amrī from following me? Did you disobey my command?'

item.title: Taa-Haa:93 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَّا تَتَّبِعَنِ أَفَعَصَيْتَ أَمْرِي allā tattabiʿani afaʿaṣayta amrī From following me? Then have you disobeyed my order?" See 20:92

item.title: Taa-Haa:93 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَّا تَتَّبِعَنِ أَفَعَصَيْتَ أَمْرِي allā tattabiʿani afaʿaṣayta amrī That thou didst not follow me? Hast thou then disobeyed my order? The attitude of Moses towards Aaron was not because of any doubt against the stand taken by Aaron towards Samiri but he wanted the matter to be exhibited to the public and that Aaron should explain his stand so that no room be left for accusing Aaron of joining hands with Samiri or neglecting his duty. All that Aaron was anxious to see was that no rift in the ranks of the Children of Israel was created before the return of Moses. (A.P.).

item.title: Taa-Haa:94 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ يَاابْنَأُمَّ لَا تَأْخُذْ بِلِحْيَتِي وَلَا بِرَأْسِي اِنِّیْ خَشِيتُ أَنْ تَقُولَ فَرَّقْتَ بَيْنَ بَنِي إِسْرَاءِيلَ وَلَمْ تَرْقُبْ قَوْلِي qāla yabna-umma lā takhudh biliḥ'yatī walā birasī innī khashītu an taqūla farraqta bayna banī is'rāīla walam tarqub qawlī He said, 'O son of my mother! Do not hold my beard or my head! I feared lest you should say, "You have caused a rift among the Children of Israel, and did not heed my word [of advice]." '

item.title: Taa-Haa:94 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ يَاابْنَأُمَّ لَا تَأْخُذْ بِلِحْيَتِي وَلَا بِرَأْسِي اِنِّیْ خَشِيتُ أَنْ تَقُولَ فَرَّقْتَ بَيْنَ بَنِي إِسْرَاءِيلَ وَلَمْ تَرْقُبْ قَوْلِي qāla yabna-umma lā takhudh biliḥ'yatī walā birasī innī khashītu an taqūla farraqta bayna banī is'rāīla walam tarqub qawlī (Harun) said, "O son of my mother, do not seize (me) by my beard or by my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say, 'You caused division among the Children of Israel, and you did not observe (or await) my word.'" See 20:92

item.title: Taa-Haa:94 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ يَاابْنَأُمَّ لَا تَأْخُذْ بِلِحْيَتِي وَلَا بِرَأْسِي اِنِّیْ خَشِيتُ أَنْ تَقُولَ فَرَّقْتَ بَيْنَ بَنِي إِسْرَاءِيلَ وَلَمْ تَرْقُبْ قَوْلِي qāla yabna-umma lā takhudh biliḥ'yatī walā birasī innī khashītu an taqūla farraqta bayna banī is'rāīla walam tarqub qawlī Said (Aaron): "O' son of my mother! Seize me not by my beard (Get not angry.) nor by my head; I was afraid lest sayest thou: "Thou hast caused a division among the children of Israel and didst not respect my word!" See 20:93

item.title: Taa-Haa:95 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ فَمَا خَطْبُكَ يَاسَامِرِيُّ qāla famā khaṭbuka yāsāmiriyyu He said, 'What is your business, O Sāmirī?'

item.title: Taa-Haa:95 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ فَمَا خَطْبُكَ يَاسَامِرِيُّ qāla famā khaṭbuka yāsāmiriyyu (Musa) said, "And what is your case, O Sāmirī?" (Musa) said: And what is the matter with you. O Samiri? (20:95). (Samiri) said: "I saw what they saw not, so I took a (Qabdah) handful (of dust) from the (hoof) print of the messenger and threw it. Thus my inner self suggested to me (20:96). Musa said: "Then go away! And verily, your (punishment) in this life will be that you will say: 'Touch me not;' and verily, you have a promise that will not fail. And look at your god to which you have been devoted. We will certainly burn it, and scatter its particles in the sea (20:97). Your God is only Allah, there is no God but Him. He has full knowledge of all things (20:98). How As-Samiri Made…

item.title: Taa-Haa:95 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ فَمَا خَطْبُكَ يَاسَامِرِيُّ qāla famā khaṭbuka yāsāmiriyyu (Moses) said: "What was thy object O' Samiri?" See 20:93

item.title: Taa-Haa:96 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ بَصُرْتُ بِمَا لَمْ يَبْصُرُوْۤا بِهِ فَقَبَضْتُ قَبْضَةً مِنْ أَثَرِ الرَّسُولِ فَنَبَذْتُهَا وَكَذٰلِكَ سَوَّلَتْ لِي نَفْسِي qāla baṣur'tu bimā lam yabṣurū bihi faqabaḍtu qabḍatan min athari l-rasūli fanabadhtuhā wakadhālika sawwalat lī nafsī He said, 'I saw what they did not see. I took a handful [of dust] from the messenger's trail and threw it. That is how my soul prompted me.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:96 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ بَصُرْتُ بِمَا لَمْ يَبْصُرُوْۤا بِهِ فَقَبَضْتُ قَبْضَةً مِنْ أَثَرِ الرَّسُولِ فَنَبَذْتُهَا وَكَذٰلِكَ سَوَّلَتْ لِي نَفْسِي qāla baṣur'tu bimā lam yabṣurū bihi faqabaḍtu qabḍatan min athari l-rasūli fanabadhtuhā wakadhālika sawwalat lī nafsī He said, "I saw what they did not see, so I took a handful (of dust) from the track of the messenger1 and threw it,2 and thus did my soul entice me." See 20:95

item.title: Taa-Haa:96 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ بَصُرْتُ بِمَا لَمْ يَبْصُرُوْۤا بِهِ فَقَبَضْتُ قَبْضَةً مِنْ أَثَرِ الرَّسُولِ فَنَبَذْتُهَا وَكَذٰلِكَ سَوَّلَتْ لِي نَفْسِي qāla baṣur'tu bimā lam yabṣurū bihi faqabaḍtu qabḍatan min athari l-rasūli fanabadhtuhā wakadhālika sawwalat lī nafsī Said (Samiri): "I saw what they did not see, so I took a handful of (the dust) from the track of the Messenger (Angel), and flung it (into the image of the calf) for so did my self prompt me (to do)" Samiri relates that he only used the earth under the hoof of the Messenger Angel and use of it enchanted him. It has already been said above that the life-history of Moses has an identity with that of the Holy Prophet. The Holy Prophet left this world leaving Ali in his place to be at the head of the people. The Samiris among the Muslims set…

item.title: Taa-Haa:97 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ فَاذْهَبْ فَإِنَّ لَكَ فِي الْحَيَوةِ أَنْ تَقُولَ لَا مِسَاسَ وَإِنَّ لَكَ مَوْعِدًا لَنْ تُخْلَفَهُ وَانْظُرْ إِلَى إِلَهِكَ الَّذِي ظَلْتَ عَلَيْهِ عَاكِفًا لَنُحَرِّقَنَّهُ ثُمَّ لَنَنْسِفَنَّهُ فِي الْيَمِّ نَسْفًا qāla fa-idh'hab fa-inna laka fī l-ḥayati an taqūla lā misāsa wa-inna laka mawʿidan lan tukh'lafahu wa-unẓur ilā ilāhika alladhī ẓalta ʿalayhi ʿākifan lanuḥarriqannahu thumma lanansifannahu fī l-yami nasfan He said, 'Begone! It shall be your [lot] throughout life to say, "Do not touch me!" Indeed there is a tryst for you which you will not fail to keep! Now look at your god to whom you went on clinging. We will burn it down and then scatter it[s ashes] into the sea.

item.title: Taa-Haa:97 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ فَاذْهَبْ فَإِنَّ لَكَ فِي الْحَيَوةِ أَنْ تَقُولَ لَا مِسَاسَ وَإِنَّ لَكَ مَوْعِدًا لَنْ تُخْلَفَهُ وَانْظُرْ إِلَى إِلَهِكَ الَّذِي ظَلْتَ عَلَيْهِ عَاكِفًا لَنُحَرِّقَنَّهُ ثُمَّ لَنَنْسِفَنَّهُ فِي الْيَمِّ نَسْفًا qāla fa-idh'hab fa-inna laka fī l-ḥayati an taqūla lā misāsa wa-inna laka mawʿidan lan tukh'lafahu wa-unẓur ilā ilāhika alladhī ẓalta ʿalayhi ʿākifan lanuḥarriqannahu thumma lanansifannahu fī l-yami nasfan (Musa) said, "Then go. And indeed, it is (decreed) for you in (this) life to say, 'No contact.'1 And indeed, you have an appointment (in the Hereafter) you will not fail to keep. And look at your 'god' to which you remained devoted. We will surely burn it and blow it (i.e., its ashes) into the sea with a blast. See 20:95

item.title: Taa-Haa:97 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ فَاذْهَبْ فَإِنَّ لَكَ فِي الْحَيَوةِ أَنْ تَقُولَ لَا مِسَاسَ وَإِنَّ لَكَ مَوْعِدًا لَنْ تُخْلَفَهُ وَانْظُرْ إِلَى إِلَهِكَ الَّذِي ظَلْتَ عَلَيْهِ عَاكِفًا لَنُحَرِّقَنَّهُ ثُمَّ لَنَنْسِفَنَّهُ فِي الْيَمِّ نَسْفًا qāla fa-idh'hab fa-inna laka fī l-ḥayati an taqūla lā misāsa wa-inna laka mawʿidan lan tukh'lafahu wa-unẓur ilā ilāhika alladhī ẓalta ʿalayhi ʿākifan lanuḥarriqannahu thumma lanansifannahu fī l-yami nasfan (Moses) said: "Begone then, verily for thee it shall be in this life to say: (No contact with any. It is said Samiri was banished into the desert.) 'Touch me not'; and (besides this) thou hast a tryst (of punishment) never will that fail; and (now) look at thy god whose worship thou kept (so long); Certainly will we burn it, then certainly will we scatter (the ashes of) it in the sea (with a wide) scattering!" See 20:96

item.title: Taa-Haa:98 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّمَا إِلَهُكُمُ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَسِعَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عِلْمًا innamā ilāhukumu l-lahu alladhī lā ilāha illā huwa wasiʿa kulla shayin ʿil'man Indeed your God is Allah. There is no god except Him. He embraces all things in [His] knowledge.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:98 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّمَا إِلَهُكُمُ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَسِعَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عِلْمًا innamā ilāhukumu l-lahu alladhī lā ilāha illā huwa wasiʿa kulla shayin ʿil'man Your god is only Allah, except for whom there is no deity. He has encompassed all things in knowledge." See 20:95

item.title: Taa-Haa:98 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّمَا إِلَهُكُمُ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَسِعَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عِلْمًا innamā ilāhukumu l-lahu alladhī lā ilāha illā huwa wasiʿa kulla shayin ʿil'man Verily your God is only 'Allah' (God); There is no god but He; He comprehendeth all things in (His) knowledge! See 20:96

item.title: Taa-Haa:99 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: كَذٰلِكَ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ مَا قَدْ سَبَقَ وَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَاكَ مِنْ لَدُنَّا ذِكْرًا kadhālika naquṣṣu ʿalayka min anbāi mā qad sabaqa waqad ātaynāka min ladunnā dhik'ran Thus do We relate to you some accounts of what is past. Certainly We have given you a Reminder from Ourselves.

item.title: Taa-Haa:99 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: كَذٰلِكَ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ مَا قَدْ سَبَقَ وَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَاكَ مِنْ لَدُنَّا ذِكْرًا kadhālika naquṣṣu ʿalayka min anbāi mā qad sabaqa waqad ātaynāka min ladunnā dhik'ran Thus, (O Muḥammad), We relate to you from the news of what has preceded. And We have certainly given you from Us a message (i.e., the Qur’ān). Thus We relate to you some information of what happened before. And indeed We have given you from Us a Reminder (20:99). Whoever turns away from it, verily, they will bear a heavy burden on the Day of Resurrection (20:100). They will abide in that – and evil indeed will it be that load for them on the Day of Resurrection (20:101). The Entire Qur'an is the Remembrance of Allah and Mentioning the Punishment of Those Who Turn Away from It Allah, the Exalted, is saying to…

item.title: Taa-Haa:99 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: كَذٰلِكَ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ مَا قَدْ سَبَقَ وَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَاكَ مِنْ لَدُنَّا ذِكْرًا kadhālika naquṣṣu ʿalayka min anbāi mā qad sabaqa waqad ātaynāka min ladunnā dhik'ran Thus do We relate unto thee (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) of the (historic) accounts of what hath (Gone before.) passed (of old); and indeed have We given unto thee from Ourselves a Reminder (Qur'an). See 20:96

item.title: Taa-Haa:100 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَنْ أَعْرَضَ عَنْهُ فَإِنَّهُ يَحْمِلُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وِزْرًا man aʿraḍa ʿanhu fa-innahu yaḥmilu yawma l-qiyāmati wiz'ran Whoever disregards it shall bear its onus on the Day of Resurrection,

item.title: Taa-Haa:100 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَنْ أَعْرَضَ عَنْهُ فَإِنَّهُ يَحْمِلُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وِزْرًا man aʿraḍa ʿanhu fa-innahu yaḥmilu yawma l-qiyāmati wiz'ran Whoever turns away from it - then indeed, he will bear on the Day of Resurrection a burden (i.e., great sin). See 20:99

item.title: Taa-Haa:100 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَنْ أَعْرَضَ عَنْهُ فَإِنَّهُ يَحْمِلُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وِزْرًا man aʿraḍa ʿanhu fa-innahu yaḥmilu yawma l-qiyāmati wiz'ran Whosoever turneth aside from it, verily he shall bear on the Day of Resurrection, a burden, See 20:96

item.title: Taa-Haa:101 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: خَالِدِينَ فِیْهِ وَسَاءَ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ حِمْلًا khālidīna fīhi wasāa lahum yawma l-qiyāmati ḥim'lan remaining in it [forever]. Evil is their burden on the Day of Resurrection

item.title: Taa-Haa:101 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: خَالِدِينَ فِیْهِ وَسَاءَ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ حِمْلًا khālidīna fīhi wasāa lahum yawma l-qiyāmati ḥim'lan (Abiding) eternally therein,1 and evil it is for them on the Day of Resurrection as a load. See 20:99

item.title: Taa-Haa:101 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: خَالِدِينَ فِیْهِ وَسَاءَ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ حِمْلًا khālidīna fīhi wasāa lahum yawma l-qiyāmati ḥim'lan Abiding in it; while grievous will (The bearing.) it be for them on the Day of Resurrection to bear, See 20:96

item.title: Taa-Haa:102 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ وَنَحْشُرُ الْمُجْرِمِينَ يَوْمَئِذٍ زُرْقًا yawma yunfakhu fī l-ṣūri wanaḥshuru l-muj'rimīna yawma-idhin zur'qan —the day the Trumpet will be blown— on that day We shall muster the guilty with blind eyes.1

item.title: Taa-Haa:102 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ وَنَحْشُرُ الْمُجْرِمِينَ يَوْمَئِذٍ زُرْقًا yawma yunfakhu fī l-ṣūri wanaḥshuru l-muj'rimīna yawma-idhin zur'qan The Day the Horn will be blown. And We will gather the criminals, that Day, blue-eyed.1 The Day when the Sur will be blown: that Day, We shall gather the criminals blue-eyed (20:102). They will speak in a very low voice to each other (saying): "You stayed not longer than ten (20:103). We know very well what they will say, when the best among them in knowledge and wisdom will say: "You stayed no longer than a day! (20:104). The Blowing of the Sur and the Day of Resurrection It has been confirmed in a Hadith that the Messenger of Allah SAW was asked about the Sur and he replied: قَرْنٌ يُنْفَخُ فِيهِ It is a horn that will be blown into. It has…

item.title: Taa-Haa:102 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ وَنَحْشُرُ الْمُجْرِمِينَ يَوْمَئِذٍ زُرْقًا yawma yunfakhu fī l-ṣūri wanaḥshuru l-muj'rimīna yawma-idhin zur'qan (On) the day when the Trumpet shall be blown and We will gather the guilty ones, and the blue (Blinded with horror. Refer to verse 20:124.) eyed ones. See 20:96

item.title: Taa-Haa:103 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَتَخَافَتُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ إِنْ لَبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا عَشْرًا yatakhāfatūna baynahum in labith'tum illā ʿashran They will whisper to one another: 'You have stayed only for ten [days].'

item.title: Taa-Haa:103 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَتَخَافَتُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ إِنْ لَبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا عَشْرًا yatakhāfatūna baynahum in labith'tum illā ʿashran They will murmur among themselves, "You remained not but ten (days in the world)." See 20:102

item.title: Taa-Haa:103 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَتَخَافَتُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ إِنْ لَبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا عَشْرًا yatakhāfatūna baynahum in labith'tum illā ʿashran They shall consult among themselves in a low voice (saying): "Ye did tarry but ten (days)" Since the chastisement on the Day of Judgment would be far greater and more grievous than that of the one immediately following death, the sinners will imagine their story in the grave or the interval between their death and the judgment or their stay in the world to be very short, like only a few days.

item.title: Taa-Haa:104 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ إِذْ يَقُولُ أَمْثَلُهُمْ طَرِيقَةً إِنْ لَبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا يَوْمًا naḥnu aʿlamu bimā yaqūlūna idh yaqūlu amthaluhum ṭarīqatan in labith'tum illā yawman We know best what they will say, when the best of them in conduct will say, 'You stayed only a day!'

item.title: Taa-Haa:104 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ إِذْ يَقُولُ أَمْثَلُهُمْ طَرِيقَةً إِنْ لَبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا يَوْمًا naḥnu aʿlamu bimā yaqūlūna idh yaqūlu amthaluhum ṭarīqatan in labith'tum illā yawman We are most knowing of what they say when the best of them in manner (i.e., wisdom or speech) will say, "You remained not but one day." See 20:102

item.title: Taa-Haa:104 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ إِذْ يَقُولُ أَمْثَلُهُمْ طَرِيقَةً إِنْ لَبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا يَوْمًا naḥnu aʿlamu bimā yaqūlūna idh yaqūlu amthaluhum ṭarīqatan in labith'tum illā yawman We know best what they will say, when the most ideal ones of them in conduct will say: "Ye tarried not but a day!" The opinion of the more sensitive of them would be that the stay before the judgment was only a day, i.e., shorter still.

item.title: Taa-Haa:105 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَسْءَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْجِبَالِ فَقُلْ يَنْسِفُهَا رَبِّي نَسْفًا wayasalūnaka ʿani l-jibāli faqul yansifuhā rabbī nasfan They question you concerning the mountains. Say, 'My Lord will scatter them [like dust].'

item.title: Taa-Haa:105 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَسْءَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْجِبَالِ فَقُلْ يَنْسِفُهَا رَبِّي نَسْفًا wayasalūnaka ʿani l-jibāli faqul yansifuhā rabbī nasfan And they ask you about the mountains, so say, "My Lord will blow them away with a blast.1 And they ask you concerning the mountains. Say: My Lord will blast them and scatter them as particles of dust (20:105). "Then He shall leave it as a level smooth plain (20:106). "You will see therein no crookedness nor curve (20:107). On that Day mankind will follow strictly (the voice of) Allah's caller, no crookedness (that is without going to the right or left of that voice) will they show him (Allah's caller). And all voices will be humbled for the Most Gracious (Allah), and nothing shall you hear except Hamsa (20:108). The Destruction of the Mountains, and the Earth Becomes a Smooth Plain Allah says: وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ…

item.title: Taa-Haa:105 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَيَسْءَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْجِبَالِ فَقُلْ يَنْسِفُهَا رَبِّي نَسْفًا wayasalūnaka ʿani l-jibāli faqul yansifuhā rabbī nasfan And they ask thee (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) about (what will happen to) the mountains (on the Day of Resurrection), say then, "My Lord will root them up and scatter them away as dust," People had asked the Holy Prophet as to what would happen to the huge mountains on the Day of Judgment. This verse is in reply to the enquiry.

item.title: Taa-Haa:106 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَيَذَرُهَا قَاعًا صَفْصَفًا fayadharuhā qāʿan ṣafṣafan Then He will leave it1 a level plain.

item.title: Taa-Haa:106 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَيَذَرُهَا قَاعًا صَفْصَفًا fayadharuhā qāʿan ṣafṣafan And He will leave it (i.e., the earth) a level plain. See 20:105

item.title: Taa-Haa:106 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَيَذَرُهَا قَاعًا صَفْصَفًا fayadharuhā qāʿan ṣafṣafan Then leave it a plain, smooth level, See 20:105

item.title: Taa-Haa:107 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا تَرٰی فِيهَا عِوَجًا وَلَا أَمْتًا lā tarā fīhā ʿiwajan walā amtan You will not see any crookedness or unevenness in it.

item.title: Taa-Haa:107 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا تَرٰی فِيهَا عِوَجًا وَلَا أَمْتًا lā tarā fīhā ʿiwajan walā amtan You will not see therein a depression or an elevation." See 20:105

item.title: Taa-Haa:107 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَا تَرٰی فِيهَا عِوَجًا وَلَا أَمْتًا lā tarā fīhā ʿiwajan walā amtan Thou shall see not in it any crookedness or unevenness See 20:105

item.title: Taa-Haa:108 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَّبِعُونَ الدَّاعِيَ لَا عِوَجَ لَهُ وَخَشَعَتِ الْأَصْوَاتُ لِلرَّحْمَنِ فَلَا تَسْمَعُ إِلَّا هَمْسًا yawma-idhin yattabiʿūna l-dāʿiya lā ʿiwaja lahu wakhashaʿati l-aṣwātu lilrraḥmāni falā tasmaʿu illā hamsan On that day they will follow a summoner in whom there will be no deviousness. The voices will be muted before the All-beneficent, and you will hear nothing but a murmur.

item.title: Taa-Haa:108 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَّبِعُونَ الدَّاعِيَ لَا عِوَجَ لَهُ وَخَشَعَتِ الْأَصْوَاتُ لِلرَّحْمَنِ فَلَا تَسْمَعُ إِلَّا هَمْسًا yawma-idhin yattabiʿūna l-dāʿiya lā ʿiwaja lahu wakhashaʿati l-aṣwātu lilrraḥmāni falā tasmaʿu illā hamsan That Day, they (i.e., everyone) will follow (the call of) the Caller1 (with) no deviation therefrom, and (all) voices will be stilled before the Most Merciful, so you will not hear except a whisper (of footsteps). See 20:105

item.title: Taa-Haa:108 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَّبِعُونَ الدَّاعِيَ لَا عِوَجَ لَهُ وَخَشَعَتِ الْأَصْوَاتُ لِلرَّحْمَنِ فَلَا تَسْمَعُ إِلَّا هَمْسًا yawma-idhin yattabiʿūna l-dāʿiya lā ʿiwaja lahu wakhashaʿati l-aṣwātu lilrraḥmāni falā tasmaʿu illā hamsan On that day they shall follow the summoner no crookedness (shall be shown) unto him, and low shall be the voices before the Beneficent (God), that thou shalt hear not aught but the light footfall. 'Inviter', i.e., the Angel Israfil who would give the call to the world by blowing his Trumpet, to assemble for the Final Judgment.

item.title: Taa-Haa:109 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَئِذٍ لَا تَنْفَعُ الشَّفَاعَةُ إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ الرَّحْمَنُ وَرَضِيَ لَهُ قَوْلًا yawma-idhin lā tanfaʿu l-shafāʿatu illā man adhina lahu l-raḥmānu waraḍiya lahu qawlan Intercession will not avail that day except from him whom the All-beneficent allows and approves of his word.

item.title: Taa-Haa:109 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَئِذٍ لَا تَنْفَعُ الشَّفَاعَةُ إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ الرَّحْمَنُ وَرَضِيَ لَهُ قَوْلًا yawma-idhin lā tanfaʿu l-shafāʿatu illā man adhina lahu l-raḥmānu waraḍiya lahu qawlan That Day, no intercession will benefit except (that of) one to whom the Most Merciful has given permission and has accepted his word. On that day no intercession shall avail, except the one for whom the Most Gracious has given permission and whose word is acceptable to Him (20:109). He knows what happens to them, and what will happen to them, but they will never encompass anything of His knowledge (20:110). And (all) faces shall be humbled before the Ever Living, the Sustainer. And he who carried wrongdoing, will be indeed a complete failure (20:111). And he who works deeds of righteousness, while he is a believer, then he will have no fear of injustice, nor…

item.title: Taa-Haa:109 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَوْمَئِذٍ لَا تَنْفَعُ الشَّفَاعَةُ إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ الرَّحْمَنُ وَرَضِيَ لَهُ قَوْلًا yawma-idhin lā tanfaʿu l-shafāʿatu illā man adhina lahu l-raḥmānu waraḍiya lahu qawlan On that day shall avail not intercession (of any) save (that of) whom hath permitted God, and whose word He is pleased with. See verses 4:85, 2:255, 4:85, 10:3, 19:86, 21:28, 34:23, 39:44. Indicates that there is intercession but by those permitted, whose words are approved by God. As to who are these - Refer to verse 43:86. (A.P.).

item.title: Taa-Haa:110 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِهِ عِلْمًا yaʿlamu mā bayna aydīhim wamā khalfahum walā yuḥīṭūna bihi ʿil'man He knows that which is before them and that which is behind them, but they cannot comprehend Him in their knowledge.

item.title: Taa-Haa:110 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِهِ عِلْمًا yaʿlamu mā bayna aydīhim wamā khalfahum walā yuḥīṭūna bihi ʿil'man He (i.e., Allah) knows what is (presently) before them and what will be after them,1 but they do not encompass it (i.e., what He knows) in knowledge. See 20:109

item.title: Taa-Haa:110 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِهِ عِلْمًا yaʿlamu mā bayna aydīhim wamā khalfahum walā yuḥīṭūna bihi ʿil'man Knoweth He what is before them and what is behind them, while they comprehend Him not in (their) knowledge. While the knowledge of the finite beings in its widest sense cannot comprehend, it is obvious that no faculties of the senses can ever comprehend Him. (A.P.)

item.title: Taa-Haa:111 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَعَنَتِ الْوُجُوهُ لِلْحَيِّ الْقَيُّومِ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنْ حَمَلَ ظُلْمًا waʿanati l-wujūhu lil'ḥayyi l-qayūmi waqad khāba man ḥamala ẓul'man All faces shall be humbled before the Living One, the All-sustainer, and he will fail who bears [the onus of] wrongdoing.

item.title: Taa-Haa:111 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَعَنَتِ الْوُجُوهُ لِلْحَيِّ الْقَيُّومِ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنْ حَمَلَ ظُلْمًا waʿanati l-wujūhu lil'ḥayyi l-qayūmi waqad khāba man ḥamala ẓul'man And (all) faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining.1 And he will have failed who carries injustice.2 See 20:109

item.title: Taa-Haa:111 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَعَنَتِ الْوُجُوهُ لِلْحَيِّ الْقَيُّومِ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنْ حَمَلَ ظُلْمًا waʿanati l-wujūhu lil'ḥayyi l-qayūmi waqad khāba man ḥamala ẓul'man And (all) faces shall be humbled before the Ever-Living, The Self- Subsistent (by Whom all subsist.) God, and indeed disappointed (Be in loss.) will be he who beareth iniquity. See 20:110

item.title: Taa-Haa:112 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِنَ الصَّالِحَاتِ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَا يَخَافُ ظُلْمًا وَلَا هَضْمًا waman yaʿmal mina l-ṣāliḥāti wahuwa mu'minun falā yakhāfu ẓul'man walā haḍman But whoever does righteous deeds, should he be faithful, shall neither fear any wrong nor detraction.

item.title: Taa-Haa:112 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِنَ الصَّالِحَاتِ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَا يَخَافُ ظُلْمًا وَلَا هَضْمًا waman yaʿmal mina l-ṣāliḥāti wahuwa mu'minun falā yakhāfu ẓul'man walā haḍman But he who does of righteous deeds while he is a believer - he will neither fear injustice nor deprivation. See 20:109

item.title: Taa-Haa:112 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِنَ الصَّالِحَاتِ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَا يَخَافُ ظُلْمًا وَلَا هَضْمًا waman yaʿmal mina l-ṣāliḥāti wahuwa mu'minun falā yakhāfu ẓul'man walā haḍman And whosoever doth good deeds and he be a believer, he shall fear not of (the least) injustice (unto him), nor of (any) curtailment (of his dues). It indicates the gravity of iniquity to which all evils are reduced and as opposed to it the import of equity to which all virtues are reduced. (A.P.).

item.title: Taa-Haa:113 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَكَذٰلِكَ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا وَصَرَّفْنَا فِیْهِ مِنَ الْوَعِيدِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ أَوْ يُحْدِثُ لَهُمْ ذِكْرًا wakadhālika anzalnāhu qur'ānan ʿarabiyyan waṣarrafnā fīhi mina l-waʿīdi laʿallahum yattaqūna aw yuḥ'dithu lahum dhik'ran Thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'ān and We have paraphrased the threats in it so that they may be Godwary or it may evoke remembrance for them.

item.title: Taa-Haa:113 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَكَذٰلِكَ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا وَصَرَّفْنَا فِیْهِ مِنَ الْوَعِيدِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ أَوْ يُحْدِثُ لَهُمْ ذِكْرًا wakadhālika anzalnāhu qur'ānan ʿarabiyyan waṣarrafnā fīhi mina l-waʿīdi laʿallahum yattaqūna aw yuḥ'dithu lahum dhik'ran And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur’ān1 and have diversified therein the warnings that perhaps they will avoid (sin) or it would cause them remembrance. And thus We have sent it down as a Qur'an in Arabic, and have explained therein in detail the warnings, in order that they may have Taqwa, or that it may cause them to have a lesson from it (20:113). Then High above all be Allah, the True King. And be not in haste with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you, and say: My Lord! Increase me in knowledge (20:114). The Qur'an was Revealed so that the People would have…

item.title: Taa-Haa:113 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَكَذٰلِكَ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا وَصَرَّفْنَا فِیْهِ مِنَ الْوَعِيدِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ أَوْ يُحْدِثُ لَهُمْ ذِكْرًا wakadhālika anzalnāhu qur'ānan ʿarabiyyan waṣarrafnā fīhi mina l-waʿīdi laʿallahum yattaqūna aw yuḥ'dithu lahum dhik'ran Thus have We sent down (unto thee O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) an Arabic Qur'an and (Displayed.) explained therein some of the threats, that they may adopt piety or that it may serve (Lit. produce.) unto them a reminder. See 20:112

item.title: Taa-Haa:114 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَتَعَالَى اللَّهُ الْمَلِكُ الْحَقُّ وَلَا تَعْجَلْ بِالْقُرْءَانِ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يُقْضَى إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُ وَقُلْ رَبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْمًا fataʿālā l-lahu l-maliku l-ḥaqu walā taʿjal bil-qur'āni min qabli an yuq'ḍā ilayka waḥyuhu waqul rabbi zid'nī ʿil'man So exalted is Allah, the True Sovereign. Do not hasten with the Qur'ān before its revelation is completed for you, and say, 'My Lord! Increase me in knowledge.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:114 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَتَعَالَى اللَّهُ الْمَلِكُ الْحَقُّ وَلَا تَعْجَلْ بِالْقُرْءَانِ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يُقْضَى إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُ وَقُلْ رَبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْمًا fataʿālā l-lahu l-maliku l-ḥaqu walā taʿjal bil-qur'āni min qabli an yuq'ḍā ilayka waḥyuhu waqul rabbi zid'nī ʿil'man So high (above all) is Allah, the Sovereign,1 the Truth.2 And, (O Muḥammad), do not hasten with (recitation of) the Qur’ān before its revelation is completed to you, and say, "My Lord, increase me in knowledge." See 20:113

item.title: Taa-Haa:114 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَتَعَالَى اللَّهُ الْمَلِكُ الْحَقُّ وَلَا تَعْجَلْ بِالْقُرْءَانِ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يُقْضَى إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُ وَقُلْ رَبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْمًا fataʿālā l-lahu l-maliku l-ḥaqu walā taʿjal bil-qur'āni min qabli an yuq'ḍā ilayka waḥyuhu waqul rabbi zid'nī ʿil'man High above all is God, the King, the (Self-Existent) Truth; And (Refer to verses 75:16 - 75:19, 73:4 & 25:32.) hasten not (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) with the Qur'an ere its completed unto thee its revelation, and say thou: "O' my Lord! increase me in (of the hidden significance - folds of the Book.) knowledge!" This verse makes it quite clear that the matter of the whole of the Holy Qur'an was already there in the heart of the Holy Prophet even before it was revealed to him gradually. Here, God desires the Holy Prophet to follow the order of the revelation and to disclose it…

item.title: Taa-Haa:115 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ عَهِدْنَا إِلَى اٰدَمَ مِنْ قَبْلُ فَنَسِيَ وَلَمْ نَجِدْ لَهُ عَزْمًا walaqad ʿahid'nā ilā ādama min qablu fanasiya walam najid lahu ʿazman Certainly We had enjoined Adam earlier; but he forgot, and We did not find any resoluteness in him.

item.title: Taa-Haa:115 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ عَهِدْنَا إِلَى اٰدَمَ مِنْ قَبْلُ فَنَسِيَ وَلَمْ نَجِدْ لَهُ عَزْمًا walaqad ʿahid'nā ilā ādama min qablu fanasiya walam najid lahu ʿazman And We had already taken a promise from Adam before, but he forgot; and We found not in him determination.1 And indeed We made a covenant with Adam before, but he forgot, and We found on his part no firm willpower (20:115). And (remember) when We said to the angels: "Prostrate yourselves to Adam." They prostrated themselves (all) except Iblis; he refused (20:116). Then We said: "O Adam! Verily, this is an enemy to you and to your wife. So let him not get you both out of Paradise, so that you will be distressed (20:117). "You will never be hungry therein nor naked (20:118). "And you (will) suffer not from thirst therein nor from the sun's heat…

item.title: Taa-Haa:115 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَقَدْ عَهِدْنَا إِلَى اٰدَمَ مِنْ قَبْلُ فَنَسِيَ وَلَمْ نَجِدْ لَهُ عَزْمًا walaqad ʿahid'nā ilā ādama min qablu fanasiya walam najid lahu ʿazman And indeed had We covenanted unto Adam before, but he (Bypassed.) forgot; but We did not find in him any intention (to disobey Us). Adam was advised not to approach the Tree, if he wanted to continue in the blissful life of the lower Paradise, as otherwise he will have to suffer the trouble of being thrown out of Paradise and will have to work hard to gain the bliss of the Heavenly Paradise. But Adam did not show any decision to remain there. Hence, he bypassed the advice. (A.P.)

item.title: Taa-Haa:116 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوْۤا لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ أَبٰی wa-idh qul'nā lil'malāikati us'judū liādama fasajadū illā ib'līsa abā When We said to the angels, 'Prostrate before Adam,' they prostrated, but not Iblis: he refused.

item.title: Taa-Haa:116 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوْۤا لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ أَبٰی wa-idh qul'nā lil'malāikati us'judū liādama fasajadū illā ib'līsa abā And (mention) when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except Iblees;1 he refused. See 20:115

item.title: Taa-Haa:116 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوْۤا لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ أَبٰی wa-idh qul'nā lil'malāikati us'judū liādama fasajadū illā ib'līsa abā When said We unto the angels "Prostrate ye in obeisance unto Adam!" they did prostrate on obeisance save 'Iblis'; (Who did it not.) he refused. See 20:115

item.title: Taa-Haa:117 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَقُلْنَا يَاءَادَمُ إِنَّ هَذَا عَدُوٌّ لَكَ وَلِزَوْجِكَ فَلَا يُخْرِجَنَّكُمَا مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ فَتَشْقَى faqul'nā yāādamu inna hādhā ʿaduwwun laka walizawjika falā yukh'rijannakumā mina l-janati fatashqā We said, 'O Adam! This is indeed an enemy of yours and your mate's. So do not let him expel you from paradise, or you will be miserable.

item.title: Taa-Haa:117 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَقُلْنَا يَاءَادَمُ إِنَّ هَذَا عَدُوٌّ لَكَ وَلِزَوْجِكَ فَلَا يُخْرِجَنَّكُمَا مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ فَتَشْقَى faqul'nā yāādamu inna hādhā ʿaduwwun laka walizawjika falā yukh'rijannakumā mina l-janati fatashqā So We said, "O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife. Then let him not remove you from Paradise so you would suffer. See 20:115

item.title: Taa-Haa:117 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَقُلْنَا يَاءَادَمُ إِنَّ هَذَا عَدُوٌّ لَكَ وَلِزَوْجِكَ فَلَا يُخْرِجَنَّكُمَا مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ فَتَشْقَى faqul'nā yāādamu inna hādhā ʿaduwwun laka walizawjika falā yukh'rijannakumā mina l-janati fatashqā Then said We: "O' Adam! Verily this is an enemy unto thee and thy wife; therefore, let him not drive ye both out of the Garden (The blissful state.) for (then) thou shouldst be put to toil." See 20:115

item.title: Taa-Haa:118 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ لَكَ أَلَّا تَجُوعَ فِيهَا وَلَا تَعْرٰی inna laka allā tajūʿa fīhā walā taʿrā Indeed you will neither be hungry in it nor naked.

item.title: Taa-Haa:118 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّ لَكَ أَلَّا تَجُوعَ فِيهَا وَلَا تَعْرٰی inna laka allā tajūʿa fīhā walā taʿrā Indeed, it is (promised) for you not to be hungry therein or be unclothed. See 20:115

item.title: Taa-Haa:118 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
