item.description: إِنَّ لَكَ أَلَّا تَجُوعَ فِيهَا وَلَا تَعْرٰی inna laka allā tajūʿa fīhā walā taʿrā For thee it is ordained that thou shalt not be hungry in it, nor (shalt thou be) naked, This was all that Adam would have enjoyed in the lower Paradise in the animal life1 and there is no mention in it, of the higher bliss of the Heavenly Paradise promised in verses 8:15 & 9:72, i.e., the blessings of God's being pleased with - which is termed as the greatest enjoyment. But as Satan had no idea of such a Paradise awaiting Adam, he only saw the troubles of the temporal life and the ease and the comfort of the Paradise in which Adam was. Therefore, drifting in the spirit of vengeance, he aimed to see that Adam was out of the Lower Paradise. Otherwise, Satan's…

item.title: Taa-Haa:119 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّكَ لَا تَظْمَؤُا فِيهَا وَلَا تَضْحَى wa-annaka lā taẓma-u fīhā walā taḍḥā Indeed you will neither be thirsty in it, nor suffer from the sun.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:119 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّكَ لَا تَظْمَؤُا فِيهَا وَلَا تَضْحَى wa-annaka lā taẓma-u fīhā walā taḍḥā And indeed, you will not be thirsty therein or be hot from the sun." See 20:115

item.title: Taa-Haa:119 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأَنَّكَ لَا تَظْمَؤُا فِيهَا وَلَا تَضْحَى wa-annaka lā taẓma-u fīhā walā taḍḥā And that thou shalt not be thirsty in it, nor shalt thou feel the heat of the sun. See 20:118

item.title: Taa-Haa:120 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَوَسْوَسَ إِلَيْهِ الشَّيْطَانُ قَالَ يَاءَادَمُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَى شَجَرَةِ الْخُلْدِ وَمُلْكٍ لَا يَبْلَى fawaswasa ilayhi l-shayṭānu qāla yāādamu hal adulluka ʿalā shajarati l-khul'di wamul'kin lā yablā Then Satan tempted him. He said, 'O Adam! Shall I show you the tree of immortality, and an imperishable kingdom?'

item.title: Taa-Haa:120 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَوَسْوَسَ إِلَيْهِ الشَّيْطَانُ قَالَ يَاءَادَمُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَى شَجَرَةِ الْخُلْدِ وَمُلْكٍ لَا يَبْلَى fawaswasa ilayhi l-shayṭānu qāla yāādamu hal adulluka ʿalā shajarati l-khul'di wamul'kin lā yablā Then Satan whispered to him; he said, "O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and possession that will not deteriorate?" See 20:115

item.title: Taa-Haa:120 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَوَسْوَسَ إِلَيْهِ الشَّيْطَانُ قَالَ يَاءَادَمُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَى شَجَرَةِ الْخُلْدِ وَمُلْكٍ لَا يَبْلَى fawaswasa ilayhi l-shayṭānu qāla yāādamu hal adulluka ʿalā shajarati l-khul'di wamul'kin lā yablā But Satan whispered unto him saying: "O' Adam! shall I guide thee unto the tree of eternity and unto a kingdom which decayeth not?" See 20:118

item.title: Taa-Haa:121 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَكَلَا مِنْهَا فَبَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْءَاتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِنْ وَرَقِ الْجَنَّةِ وَعَصَى اٰدَمُ رَبَّهُ فَغَوَى fa-akalā min'hā fabadat lahumā sawātuhumā waṭafiqā yakhṣifāni ʿalayhimā min waraqi l-janati waʿaṣā ādamu rabbahu faghawā So they both ate of it, and their nakedness became evident to them, and they began to stitch over themselves with the leaves of paradise. Adam disobeyed his Lord, and went amiss.

item.title: Taa-Haa:121 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَكَلَا مِنْهَا فَبَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْءَاتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِنْ وَرَقِ الْجَنَّةِ وَعَصَى اٰدَمُ رَبَّهُ فَغَوَى fa-akalā min'hā fabadat lahumā sawātuhumā waṭafiqā yakhṣifāni ʿalayhimā min waraqi l-janati waʿaṣā ādamu rabbahu faghawā And they (i.e., Adam and his wife) ate of it, and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten over themselves from the leaves of Paradise. And Adam disobeyed his Lord and erred. See 20:115

item.title: Taa-Haa:121 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَأَكَلَا مِنْهَا فَبَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْءَاتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِنْ وَرَقِ الْجَنَّةِ وَعَصَى اٰدَمُ رَبَّهُ فَغَوَى fa-akalā min'hā fabadat lahumā sawātuhumā waṭafiqā yakhṣifāni ʿalayhimā min waraqi l-janati waʿaṣā ādamu rabbahu faghawā Then they both ate of it, so their nakedness appeared unto them, and they both began to cover themselves with the leaves of the Garden; And Adam acted not (to the advices of) his Lord (deceived by Satan) and got astray. (From the state of bliss but without any intention to disobey the Lord.) See 20:118

item.title: Taa-Haa:122 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ اجْتَبَاهُ رَبُّهُ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ وَهَدَى thumma ij'tabāhu rabbuhu fatāba ʿalayhi wahadā Then his Lord chose him, and turned to him clemently, and guided him.

item.title: Taa-Haa:122 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ اجْتَبَاهُ رَبُّهُ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ وَهَدَى thumma ij'tabāhu rabbuhu fatāba ʿalayhi wahadā Then his Lord chose him and turned to him in forgiveness and guided (him). See 20:115

item.title: Taa-Haa:122 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ اجْتَبَاهُ رَبُّهُ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ وَهَدَى thumma ij'tabāhu rabbuhu fatāba ʿalayhi wahadā Then his Lord chose (This indicates that what Adam did was not a revolt or disobedience otherwise there remains no justification for his being chosen. (A.P.).) him and turned unto him (accepting his repentance) and guided him. See 20:118

item.title: Taa-Haa:123 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ اهْبِطَا مِنْهَا جَمِيعًا بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ مِنِّي هُدًى فَمَنِ اتَّبَعَ هُدَايَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَى qāla ih'biṭā min'hā jamīʿan baʿḍukum libaʿḍin ʿaduwwun fa-immā yatiyannakum minnī hudan famani ittabaʿa hudāya falā yaḍillu walā yashqā He said, 'Get down both of you1 from it, all together, being enemies of one another! Yet, should any guidance come to you from Me, those who follow My guidance will not go astray, nor will they be miserable.

item.title: Taa-Haa:123 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ اهْبِطَا مِنْهَا جَمِيعًا بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ مِنِّي هُدًى فَمَنِ اتَّبَعَ هُدَايَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَى qāla ih'biṭā min'hā jamīʿan baʿḍukum libaʿḍin ʿaduwwun fa-immā yatiyannakum minnī hudan famani ittabaʿa hudāya falā yaḍillu walā yashqā (Allah) said, "Descend from it (i.e., Paradise) - all, (your descendants) being enemies to one another. And if there should come to you guidance from Me - then whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray (in the world) nor suffer (in the Hereafter). He (Allah) said: Get you down, both of you, together, some of you are an enemy to some others. Then if there comes to you guidance from Me, then whoever follows My guidance he shall neither go astray nor shall be distressed (20:123). But whosoever turns away from My Reminder, verily, for him is a life of hardship, and We…

item.title: Taa-Haa:123 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ اهْبِطَا مِنْهَا جَمِيعًا بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ مِنِّي هُدًى فَمَنِ اتَّبَعَ هُدَايَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَى qāla ih'biṭā min'hā jamīʿan baʿḍukum libaʿḍin ʿaduwwun fa-immā yatiyannakum minnī hudan famani ittabaʿa hudāya falā yaḍillu walā yashqā (And God) said: "Get down hence ye two, all together, one of you (being) the enemy unto another. So will surely come unto you guidance from Me, then whoever followed! My guidance, he shall go not astray nor put to grief" See 20:118

item.title: Taa-Haa:124 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَنْ أَعْرَضَ عَنْ ذِكْرِي فَإِنَّ لَهُ مَعِيشَةً ضَنْكًا وَنَحْشُرُهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ أَعْمَى waman aʿraḍa ʿan dhik'rī fa-inna lahu maʿīshatan ḍankan wanaḥshuruhu yawma l-qiyāmati aʿmā But whoever disregards My remembrance, his shall be a wretched life, and on the Day of Resurrection We shall raise him blind.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:124 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَنْ أَعْرَضَ عَنْ ذِكْرِي فَإِنَّ لَهُ مَعِيشَةً ضَنْكًا وَنَحْشُرُهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ أَعْمَى waman aʿraḍa ʿan dhik'rī fa-inna lahu maʿīshatan ḍankan wanaḥshuruhu yawma l-qiyāmati aʿmā And whoever turns away from My remembrance - indeed, he will have a depressed (i.e., difficult) life, and We will gather (i.e., raise) him on the Day of Resurrection blind." See 20:123

item.title: Taa-Haa:124 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَنْ أَعْرَضَ عَنْ ذِكْرِي فَإِنَّ لَهُ مَعِيشَةً ضَنْكًا وَنَحْشُرُهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ أَعْمَى waman aʿraḍa ʿan dhik'rī fa-inna lahu maʿīshatan ḍankan wanaḥshuruhu yawma l-qiyāmati aʿmā And whoever turneth away from My monition, verily his shall be a life straitened, and We shall raise him up on the Day of Judgment, blind. See 20:118

item.title: Taa-Haa:125 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ رَبِّ لِمَ حَشَرْتَنِي أَعْمَى وَقَدْ كُنْتُ بَصِيرًا qāla rabbi lima ḥashartanī aʿmā waqad kuntu baṣīran He will say, 'My Lord! Why have You raised me blind, though I used to see?'

item.title: Taa-Haa:125 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ رَبِّ لِمَ حَشَرْتَنِي أَعْمَى وَقَدْ كُنْتُ بَصِيرًا qāla rabbi lima ḥashartanī aʿmā waqad kuntu baṣīran He will say, "My Lord, why have you raised me blind while I was (once) seeing?" See 20:123

item.title: Taa-Haa:125 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ رَبِّ لِمَ حَشَرْتَنِي أَعْمَى وَقَدْ كُنْتُ بَصِيرًا qāla rabbi lima ḥashartanī aʿmā waqad kuntu baṣīran He shall say: "O' my Lord! why hast thou raised me blind? Whereas indeed I was seeing (With sight.) (before)?" See 20:118

item.title: Taa-Haa:126 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ كَذٰلِكَ أَتَتْكَ آيَاتُنَا فَنَسِيتَهَا وَكَذٰلِكَ الْيَوْمَ تُنْسٰی qāla kadhālika atatka āyātunā fanasītahā wakadhālika l-yawma tunsā He will say: 'So it is. Our signs came to you, but you forgot them, and thus you will be forgotten today.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:126 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ كَذٰلِكَ أَتَتْكَ آيَاتُنَا فَنَسِيتَهَا وَكَذٰلِكَ الْيَوْمَ تُنْسٰی qāla kadhālika atatka āyātunā fanasītahā wakadhālika l-yawma tunsā (Allah) will say, "Thus did Our signs come to you, and you forgot (i.e., disregarded) them; and thus will you this Day be forgotten." See 20:123

item.title: Taa-Haa:126 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ كَذٰلِكَ أَتَتْكَ آيَاتُنَا فَنَسِيتَهَا وَكَذٰلِكَ الْيَوْمَ تُنْسٰی qāla kadhālika atatka āyātunā fanasītahā wakadhālika l-yawma tunsā (God) will say: "Thus (is the recompense) for did come unto thee Our signs but thou didst ignore them; And even so art thou forsaken this day" The address is to the one who would be raised blind on the Day of Judgment. It is giving the reason for his being raised so.

item.title: Taa-Haa:127 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَكَذٰلِكَ نَجْزِي مَنْ أَسْرَفَ وَلَمْ يُؤْمِنْ بِءَايَاتِ رَبِّهِ وَلَعَذَابُ الْاٰخِرَةُ أَشَدُّ وَأَبْقَى wakadhālika najzī man asrafa walam yu'min biāyāti rabbihi walaʿadhābu l-ākhirati ashaddu wa-abqā Thus do We requite him who is a profligate and does not believe in the signs of his Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is severer and more lasting.

item.title: Taa-Haa:127 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَكَذٰلِكَ نَجْزِي مَنْ أَسْرَفَ وَلَمْ يُؤْمِنْ بِءَايَاتِ رَبِّهِ وَلَعَذَابُ الْاٰخِرَةُ أَشَدُّ وَأَبْقَى wakadhālika najzī man asrafa walam yu'min biāyāti rabbihi walaʿadhābu l-ākhirati ashaddu wa-abqā And thus do We recompense he who transgressed and did not believe in the signs of his Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more enduring.1 And thus do We requite him who transgresses beyond bounds and believes not in the Ayat of his Lord; and the torment of the Hereafter is far more severe and more lasting (20:127). Severe Torment for Him Who Transgresses Beyond Bounds Allah says: 'Thus We do requite those who transgress beyond bounds and believe the Ayat of Allah in this world and in the Hereafter.' لَّهُمْ عَذَابٌ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا ۖ وَلَعَذَابُ الْآخِرَةِ أَشَقُّ ۖ وَمَا لَهُم مِّنَ اللَّهِ مِن وَاقٍ For them is a torment…

item.title: Taa-Haa:127 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَكَذٰلِكَ نَجْزِي مَنْ أَسْرَفَ وَلَمْ يُؤْمِنْ بِءَايَاتِ رَبِّهِ وَلَعَذَابُ الْاٰخِرَةُ أَشَدُّ وَأَبْقَى wakadhālika najzī man asrafa walam yu'min biāyāti rabbihi walaʿadhābu l-ākhirati ashaddu wa-abqā And thus will We recompense him who doth transgress and believeth not in the signs of his Lord; and certainly the torment of the hereafter be more severe and more lasting. See 20:126

item.title: Taa-Haa:128 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهُمْ كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِنَ الْقُرُونِ يَمْشُونَ فِي مَسَاكِنِهِمْ إِنَّ فِي ذٰلِكَ لَءَايَاتٍ لِأُولِي النُّهَى afalam yahdi lahum kam ahlaknā qablahum mina l-qurūni yamshūna fī masākinihim inna fī dhālika laāyātin li-ulī l-nuhā Does it not dawn upon them how many generations We have destroyed before them, amid [the ruins of] whose dwellings they walk? There are indeed signs in this for those who have reason.

item.title: Taa-Haa:128 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهُمْ كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِنَ الْقُرُونِ يَمْشُونَ فِي مَسَاكِنِهِمْ إِنَّ فِي ذٰلِكَ لَءَايَاتٍ لِأُولِي النُّهَى afalam yahdi lahum kam ahlaknā qablahum mina l-qurūni yamshūna fī masākinihim inna fī dhālika laāyātin li-ulī l-nuhā Then, has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them as they walk among their dwellings? Indeed in that are signs for those of intelligence. And had it not been for a Word that went forth before from your Lord, and a term determined, (their punishment) must necessarily have come (in this world) (20:128). So bear patiently what they say, and glorify the praises of your Lord before the rising of the sun, and before its setting, and during some hours of the night, and at the ends of the day, that you may become pleased with the reward which Allah…

item.title: Taa-Haa:128 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَفَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهُمْ كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِنَ الْقُرُونِ يَمْشُونَ فِي مَسَاكِنِهِمْ إِنَّ فِي ذٰلِكَ لَءَايَاتٍ لِأُولِي النُّهَى afalam yahdi lahum kam ahlaknā qablahum mina l-qurūni yamshūna fī masākinihim inna fī dhālika laāyātin li-ulī l-nuhā What! Doth it guide them not aright (to know) how many of the generations We did destroy before them, amidst whose dwellings they (now) walk about? Verily, in this are signs for those (endowed) with (with intellect - will power – reasoning.) understanding. See 20:126

item.title: Taa-Haa:129 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَوْلَا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِنْ رَبِّكَ لَكَانَ لِزَامًا وَأَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى walawlā kalimatun sabaqat min rabbika lakāna lizāman wa-ajalun musamman And were it not for a prior decree of your Lord and a specified time, it was inevitable.

item.title: Taa-Haa:129 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَوْلَا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِنْ رَبِّكَ لَكَانَ لِزَامًا وَأَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى walawlā kalimatun sabaqat min rabbika lakāna lizāman wa-ajalun musamman And if not for a word1 that preceded from your Lord, it (i.e., punishment) would have been an obligation (due immediately),2 and (if not for) a specified term (decreed). See 20:128

item.title: Taa-Haa:129 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَوْلَا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِنْ رَبِّكَ لَكَانَ لِزَامًا وَأَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى walawlā kalimatun sabaqat min rabbika lakāna lizāman wa-ajalun musamman And had not a word (Decree.) (of respite) from thy Lord gone forth their arrest (Catch hold.) had immediately been ensued; And the term (of respite for them) is appointed Reading this verse and verse 25:77 together, it indicates that the respite and the postponement of the punishment is just to give a chance to the people to redress their defects and to repent and resort to prayer to God. (A.P.).

item.title: Taa-Haa:130 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَاصْبِرْ عَلَى مَا يَقُولُونَ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ غُرُوبِهَا وَمِنْ آنَاءِ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْ وَأَطْرَافَ النَّهَارِ لَعَلَّكَ تَرْضَى fa-iṣ'bir ʿalā mā yaqūlūna wasabbiḥ biḥamdi rabbika qabla ṭulūʿi l-shamsi waqabla ghurūbihā wamin ānāi al-layli fasabbiḥ wa-aṭrāfa l-nahāri laʿallaka tarḍā So be patient with what they say, and celebrate the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before the sunset, and glorify Him in watches of the night and at the day's ends, that you may be pleased.

item.title: Taa-Haa:130 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَاصْبِرْ عَلَى مَا يَقُولُونَ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ غُرُوبِهَا وَمِنْ آنَاءِ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْ وَأَطْرَافَ النَّهَارِ لَعَلَّكَ تَرْضَى fa-iṣ'bir ʿalā mā yaqūlūna wasabbiḥ biḥamdi rabbika qabla ṭulūʿi l-shamsi waqabla ghurūbihā wamin ānāi al-layli fasabbiḥ wa-aṭrāfa l-nahāri laʿallaka tarḍā So be patient over what they say and exalt (Allah) with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting; and during periods of the night (exalt Him) and at the ends of the day, that you may be satisfied. See 20:128

item.title: Taa-Haa:130 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَاصْبِرْ عَلَى مَا يَقُولُونَ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ غُرُوبِهَا وَمِنْ آنَاءِ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْ وَأَطْرَافَ النَّهَارِ لَعَلَّكَ تَرْضَى fa-iṣ'bir ʿalā mā yaqūlūna wasabbiḥ biḥamdi rabbika qabla ṭulūʿi l-shamsi waqabla ghurūbihā wamin ānāi al-layli fasabbiḥ wa-aṭrāfa l-nahāri laʿallaka tarḍā So be thou patient with what they say, and glorify (The address is to the Prophet and through the Prophet to his followers.) thy Lord by praising Him ere the rising of the sun and ere the setting of it; And in some hours of the night also do glorify (Him), and during parts of the day, that thou mayest achieve the pleasure (of they Lord). See verse 11:114. This verse gives out in the best comprehensive way the five obligatory and optional prayers. Before the rising of the sun - 'Salat al-Fajr or the Morning Prayer. Before the setting…

item.title: Taa-Haa:131 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلَى مَا مَتَّعْنَا بِهِ أَزْوَاجًا مِنْهُمْ زَهْرَةَ الْحَيَوةِ الدُّنْيَا لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِیْهِ وَرِزْقُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَى walā tamuddanna ʿaynayka ilā mā mattaʿnā bihi azwājan min'hum zahrata l-ḥayati l-dun'yā linaftinahum fīhi wariz'qu rabbika khayrun wa-abqā Do not extend your glance toward what We have provided certain groups of them as a glitter of the life of this world, so that We may test them thereby. And the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting.

item.title: Taa-Haa:131 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلَى مَا مَتَّعْنَا بِهِ أَزْوَاجًا مِنْهُمْ زَهْرَةَ الْحَيَوةِ الدُّنْيَا لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِیْهِ وَرِزْقُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَى walā tamuddanna ʿaynayka ilā mā mattaʿnā bihi azwājan min'hum zahrata l-ḥayati l-dun'yā linaftinahum fīhi wariz'qu rabbika khayrun wa-abqā And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to (some) categories of them, (its being but) the splendor of worldly life by which We test them. And the provision of your Lord is better and more enduring. And strain not your eyes in longing for the things We have given for enjoyment to various groups of them, the splendor of the life of this world, that We may test them thereby. But the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting (20:131). And enjoin Salah on your family, and be patient in offering them. We ask not…

item.title: Taa-Haa:131 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلَى مَا مَتَّعْنَا بِهِ أَزْوَاجًا مِنْهُمْ زَهْرَةَ الْحَيَوةِ الدُّنْيَا لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِیْهِ وَرِزْقُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَى walā tamuddanna ʿaynayka ilā mā mattaʿnā bihi azwājan min'hum zahrata l-ḥayati l-dun'yā linaftinahum fīhi wariz'qu rabbika khayrun wa-abqā And strain not thine (The Prophet addressed for the people.) eyes unto that which We have provided (different) parties of them, (of) the splendour of the life of this world, so that We may try them in it; for the provision of thy Lord is better and more abiding. (More lasting.) The address is meant for the people. When the verse was revealed, the Holy Prophet sat erect and addressing the people around him said: He who seeks grace from other than that of God shall depart from this world disappointed and dejected. He who covets the others' wealth shall always be in grief…

item.title: Taa-Haa:132 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأْمُرْ أَهْلَكَ بِالصَّلَاةِ وَاصْطَبِرْ عَلَيْهَا لَا نَسْءَلُكُ رِزْقًا نَحْنُ نَرْزُقُكَ وَالْعَاقِبَةُ لِلتَّقْوَى wamur ahlaka bil-ṣalati wa-iṣ'ṭabir ʿalayhā lā nasaluka riz'qan naḥnu narzuquka wal-ʿāqibatu lilttaqwā And bid your family to prayer and be steadfast in its maintenance. We do not ask any provision of you. It is We who provide for you, and the outcome will be in favour of Godwariness.

item.title: Taa-Haa:132 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأْمُرْ أَهْلَكَ بِالصَّلَاةِ وَاصْطَبِرْ عَلَيْهَا لَا نَسْءَلُكُ رِزْقًا نَحْنُ نَرْزُقُكَ وَالْعَاقِبَةُ لِلتَّقْوَى wamur ahlaka bil-ṣalati wa-iṣ'ṭabir ʿalayhā lā nasaluka riz'qan naḥnu narzuquka wal-ʿāqibatu lilttaqwā And enjoin prayer upon your family (and people) and be steadfast therein. We ask you not for provision; We provide for you, and the (best) outcome is for (those of) righteousness. See 20:131

item.title: Taa-Haa:132 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَأْمُرْ أَهْلَكَ بِالصَّلَاةِ وَاصْطَبِرْ عَلَيْهَا لَا نَسْءَلُكُ رِزْقًا نَحْنُ نَرْزُقُكَ وَالْعَاقِبَةُ لِلتَّقْوَى wamur ahlaka bil-ṣalati wa-iṣ'ṭabir ʿalayhā lā nasaluka riz'qan naḥnu narzuquka wal-ʿāqibatu lilttaqwā And enjoin prayer on thy followers, and adhere thou steadily unto it, We ask thee not for subsistence; (but) We (Ourselves) give thee subsistence; and the (success of the) hereafter is for the guarding (against evil). The first thing a believer would be questioned on the Day of Judgment should be about the Prescribed Compulsory Prayers, because for the offer of prayers, one needs nothing besides his own self. If one cannot stand and pray, he may do it sitting. If that also be not possible, to do it lying, and if one cannot move his hands, he can do it even by signs. Under any circumstances none is exempted from the Prescribed Prayers excepting the…

item.title: Taa-Haa:133 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالُوْۤا لَوْلَا يَأْتِينَا بِاٰیَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّهِ أَوَلَمْ تَأْتِهِمْ بَيِّنَةُ مَا فِي الصُّحُفِ الْأُولَى waqālū lawlā yatīnā biāyatin min rabbihi awalam tatihim bayyinatu mā fī l-ṣuḥufi l-ūlā They say, 'Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?' Has there not come to them a manifest proof in that which is in the former scriptures?

item.title: Taa-Haa:133 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالُوْۤا لَوْلَا يَأْتِينَا بِاٰیَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّهِ أَوَلَمْ تَأْتِهِمْ بَيِّنَةُ مَا فِي الصُّحُفِ الْأُولَى waqālū lawlā yatīnā biāyatin min rabbihi awalam tatihim bayyinatu mā fī l-ṣuḥufi l-ūlā And they say, "Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?" Has there not come to them evidence of what was in the former scriptures?1 Allah, the Exalted, informs about the disbelievers in their statement: لَوْلَا Why does not This means, 'Why doesn't Muhammad bring us some proof from his Lord?' They meant a sign that was proof of his truthfulness in his claim that he was the Messenger of Allah. Allah, the Exalted, said: أَوَلَمْ تَأْتِهِم بَيِّنَةُ مَا فِي الصُّحُفِ الْأُولَىٰ Has there not come to them the proof of that which is in the former papers (Scriptures)? This means the Qur'an which Allah revealed to him while he was…

item.title: Taa-Haa:133 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالُوْۤا لَوْلَا يَأْتِينَا بِاٰیَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّهِ أَوَلَمْ تَأْتِهِمْ بَيِّنَةُ مَا فِي الصُّحُفِ الْأُولَى waqālū lawlā yatīnā biāyatin min rabbihi awalam tatihim bayyinatu mā fī l-ṣuḥufi l-ūlā And say they: "Why doth he not bring unto us a sign from his Lord," What! Hath not there come unto them the clear evidence which were in the former scriptures? See 20:132

item.title: Taa-Haa:134 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَوْ أَنَّا أَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ بِعَذَابٍ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَقَالُوْۤا رَبَّنَا لَوْلَا أَرْسَلْتَ إِلَيْنَا رَسُولًا فَنَتَّبِعَ ءَايَاتِكَ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ نَذِلَّ وَنَخْزَى walaw annā ahlaknāhum biʿadhābin min qablihi laqālū rabbanā lawlā arsalta ilaynā rasūlan fanattabiʿa āyātika min qabli an nadhilla wanakhzā Had We destroyed them with a punishment before it,1 they would have surely said, 'Our Lord! Why did You not send us an apostle so that we might follow Your signs before we were abased and disgraced?'

item.title: Taa-Haa:134 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَوْ أَنَّا أَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ بِعَذَابٍ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَقَالُوْۤا رَبَّنَا لَوْلَا أَرْسَلْتَ إِلَيْنَا رَسُولًا فَنَتَّبِعَ ءَايَاتِكَ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ نَذِلَّ وَنَخْزَى walaw annā ahlaknāhum biʿadhābin min qablihi laqālū rabbanā lawlā arsalta ilaynā rasūlan fanattabiʿa āyātika min qabli an nadhilla wanakhzā And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before him,1 they would have said, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so we could have followed Your verses (i.e., teachings) before we were humiliated and disgraced?" See 20:133

item.title: Taa-Haa:134 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَوْ أَنَّا أَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ بِعَذَابٍ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَقَالُوْۤا رَبَّنَا لَوْلَا أَرْسَلْتَ إِلَيْنَا رَسُولًا فَنَتَّبِعَ ءَايَاتِكَ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ نَذِلَّ وَنَخْزَى walaw annā ahlaknāhum biʿadhābin min qablihi laqālū rabbanā lawlā arsalta ilaynā rasūlan fanattabiʿa āyātika min qabli an nadhilla wanakhzā And had We destroyed them with a chastisement before him (The Apostle Muhammad) certainly would they have said: "O' Our Lord! Why didst thou not send unto us an apostle, for then would we have followed Thy signs ere that we were (thus) humbled and disgraced." See 20:132

item.title: Taa-Haa:135 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ كُلٌّ مُتَرَبِّصٌ فَتَرَبَّصُوا فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ أَصْحَابُ الصِّرَاطِ السَّوِيِّ وَمَنِ اهْتَدَى qul kullun mutarabbiṣun fatarabbaṣū fasataʿlamūna man aṣḥābu l-ṣirāṭi l-sawiyi wamani ih'tadā Say, 'Each [of us] is waiting. So wait! Soon you will know who are the people of the right path, and who is guided.'

item.title: Taa-Haa:135 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ كُلٌّ مُتَرَبِّصٌ فَتَرَبَّصُوا فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ أَصْحَابُ الصِّرَاطِ السَّوِيِّ وَمَنِ اهْتَدَى qul kullun mutarabbiṣun fatarabbaṣū fasataʿlamūna man aṣḥābu l-ṣirāṭi l-sawiyi wamani ih'tadā Say, "Each (of us) is waiting;1 so wait. For you will know who are the companions of the sound path and who is guided." See 20:133

item.title: Taa-Haa:135 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قُلْ كُلٌّ مُتَرَبِّصٌ فَتَرَبَّصُوا فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ أَصْحَابُ الصِّرَاطِ السَّوِيِّ وَمَنِ اهْتَدَى qul kullun mutarabbiṣun fatarabbaṣū fasataʿlamūna man aṣḥābu l-ṣirāṭi l-sawiyi wamani ih'tadā Say thou (O' Our Apostle Muhammad!) "Every one (of us) is awaiting, so do ye (also) await: then soon ye will come to know who have been the followers of the even way and who hath been the guided aright." After revealing the truth, i.e., the Right Path to salvation and identifying the proper or the Divinely commissioned guides who should be followed after the departure of the Holy Prophet from this world, the people, particularly those who have joined the ranks of the believers, have been given the respite with the choice of following the right course shown to them and the right guides identified by God and the Holy Prophet or otherwise as they chose. The…

item.title: Yaseen:1 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يس ya-seen Yā Sīn!

item.title: Yaseen:1 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يس ya-seen Yā, Seen.1 لَقَدْ حَقَّ الْقَوْلُ عَلَىٰ أَكْثَرِهِمْ Indeed the Word has proved true against most of them, Ibn Jarir said, The punishment has become inevitable for most of them, because Allah has decreed in the Mother of the Book (Al-Lawh Al-Mahfuz) that they will not believe. فَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ so they will not believe. in Allah, or in His Messengers.

item.title: Yaseen:1 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يس ya-seen Ya Seen (Y. S.) Some commentators take 'Ya' as the vocative particle, and the letter 'Sin' standing as an abbreviation for 'Insan', i.e., Man - the term 'Ya-Sin' meaning 'O Man!' Taking even this interpretation to be correct it would naturally mean the 'Man-Perfect' or the 'Leader of Men', i.e., the Model-Man sent to guide the human race as a whole, i.e., the Holy Prophet Muhammad, for the context of the events which demanded the revelation of this verse justifies the inference. The pagans had disbelieved in the mission of the Holy Prophet and had said "that the Holy Prophet was not the one sent by God nor was Qur'an the Word of God, it is his own composition.'' The First Holy Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib says that 'Yasin' is one of the names of the Holy…

item.title: Yaseen:2 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْقُرْاٰنِ الْحَكِيمِ wal-qur'āni l-ḥakīmi By the Wise1 Qur'ān,

item.title: Yaseen:2 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْقُرْاٰنِ الْحَكِيمِ wal-qur'āni l-ḥakīmi By the wise1 Qur’ān. See 36:1

item.title: Yaseen:2 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَالْقُرْاٰنِ الْحَكِيمِ wal-qur'āni l-ḥakīmi By Qur'an (The Word of) the All-Wise, See 36:1

item.title: Yaseen:3 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّكَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِیْنَ innaka lamina l-mur'salīna you are indeed one of the apostles,

item.title: Yaseen:3 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّكَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِیْنَ innaka lamina l-mur'salīna Indeed you, (O Muḥammad), are from among the messengers. See 36:1

item.title: Yaseen:3 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّكَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِیْنَ innaka lamina l-mur'salīna Verily thou (O' Muhammad!) art of the apostles (sent by Us), See 36:1

item.title: Yaseen:4 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: عَلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ ʿalā ṣirāṭin mus'taqīmin on a straight path.

item.title: Yaseen:4 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: عَلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ ʿalā ṣirāṭin mus'taqīmin On a straight path. See 36:1

item.title: Yaseen:4 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: عَلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ ʿalā ṣirāṭin mus'taqīmin On the straight path See 36:1

item.title: Yaseen:5 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: تَنْزِيلَ الْعَزِيزِ الرَّحِيمِ tanzīla l-ʿazīzi l-raḥīmi [It is a scripture] sent down gradually from the All-mighty, the All-merciful

item.title: Yaseen:5 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: تَنْزِيلَ الْعَزِيزِ الرَّحِيمِ tanzīla l-ʿazīzi l-raḥīmi (This is) a revelation of the Exalted in Might, the Merciful. See 36:1

item.title: Yaseen:5 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: تَنْزِيلَ الْعَزِيزِ الرَّحِيمِ tanzīla l-ʿazīzi l-raḥīmi Sent down of the All-Mighty, the All-Merciful, See 36:1

item.title: Yaseen:6 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لِتُنْذِرَ قَوْمًا مَا أُنْذِرَ اٰبَآؤُهُمْ فَهُمْ غَافِلُونَ litundhira qawman mā undhira ābāuhum fahum ghāfilūna that you may warn a people whose fathers were not warned,1 so they are oblivious.

item.title: Yaseen:6 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لِتُنْذِرَ قَوْمًا مَا أُنْذِرَ اٰبَآؤُهُمْ فَهُمْ غَافِلُونَ litundhira qawman mā undhira ābāuhum fahum ghāfilūna That you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are unaware. See 36:1

item.title: Yaseen:6 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لِتُنْذِرَ قَوْمًا مَا أُنْذِرَ اٰبَآؤُهُمْ فَهُمْ غَافِلُونَ litundhira qawman mā undhira ābāuhum fahum ghāfilūna So that thou mayest warn a people whose fathers were (Since Abraham until the Holy Prophet no apostle had visited the place.) not warned, and who therefore are heedless (of the truth) The heathens of Mecca had not received any apostle of God for a long time before, i.e., since Abraham no prophet had visited the place. It does not mean that his mission was exclusively for the particular people. He was sent unto mankind as a whole1 which indicates the universality of his mission. This verse refers only to the people of his immediate audience similar to 'Wa-andhir 'ashirataka al-aqrabin' (26:214) who are supposed to be the descendants of Abraham through Ishmael. (a) Though the lineage between Ishmael and the Holy Prophet's ancestral chain, maintained…

item.title: Yaseen:7 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لَقَدْ حَقَّ الْقَوْلُ عَلَى أَكْثَرِهِمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ laqad ḥaqqa l-qawlu ʿalā aktharihim fahum lā yu'minūna The word has certainly become due against most of them, so they will not have faith.

item.title: Yaseen:7 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لَقَدْ حَقَّ الْقَوْلُ عَلَى أَكْثَرِهِمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ laqad ḥaqqa l-qawlu ʿalā aktharihim fahum lā yu'minūna Already the word (i.e., decree) has come into effect upon most of them, so they do not believe. See 36:1

item.title: Yaseen:7 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لَقَدْ حَقَّ الْقَوْلُ عَلَى أَكْثَرِهِمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ laqad ḥaqqa l-qawlu ʿalā aktharihim fahum lā yu'minūna Indeed the word hath been proved true of most of them, and wherefore they believe not. When the people obstinately refuse to be guided aright and reject all guidance and the respite given only increases their obstinacy and perversity, the decree for their punishment is naturally pronounced.1 (a) Ref. to the divine decision declared in the Qur'an against Satan and the children of Adam who followed him Refer to verses 7:13 - 7:18 and in the other places. This indicates that the majority of the people referred to here, would not believe. (A.P.).

item.title: Yaseen:8 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا فِي أَعْنَاقِهِمْ أَغْلَالًا فَهِيَ إِلَى الْأَذْقَانِ فَهُمْ مُقْمَحُونَ innā jaʿalnā fī aʿnāqihim aghlālan fahiya ilā l-adhqāni fahum muq'maḥūna Indeed We have put iron collars around their necks, which are up to the chins, so their heads are upturned.1

item.title: Yaseen:8 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا فِي أَعْنَاقِهِمْ أَغْلَالًا فَهِيَ إِلَى الْأَذْقَانِ فَهُمْ مُقْمَحُونَ innā jaʿalnā fī aʿnāqihim aghlālan fahiya ilā l-adhqāni fahum muq'maḥūna Indeed, We have put shackles on their necks, and they are to their chins, so they are with heads (kept) aloft. Verily, We have put on their necks iron collars reaching to the chins, so that their heads are raised up (36:8). And We have put a barrier before them, and a barrier behind them, and We have covered them up, so that they cannot see (36:9). It is the same to them whether you warn them or you warn them not, they will not believe (36:10). You can only warn him who follows the Reminder, and fears the Most Gracious unseen. Bear you to such one the glad tidings of forgiveness, and a generous reward (36:11). Verily, We give…

item.title: Yaseen:8 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا فِي أَعْنَاقِهِمْ أَغْلَالًا فَهِيَ إِلَى الْأَذْقَانِ فَهُمْ مُقْمَحُونَ innā jaʿalnā fī aʿnāqihim aghlālan fahiya ilā l-adhqāni fahum muq'maḥūna Verily, We have put chains in their necks, and these reach up to their chins, and their heads are forced up stiffed. Abu Jahl has vowed that if he saw the Holy Prophet praying, he would drop upon him a big stone. Once when the Holy Prophet was engaged in prayer, Abu Jahl fetched a big stone and when he approached the Holy Prophet and raised up the stone to drop it upon his head, his hand got stuck to his neck and the stone remained on his own head. When one of his partymen saw this, he got up saying that he would kill the Holy Prophet, but when he came near and heard the Holy Qur'an recited, he…

item.title: Yaseen:9 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا مِنْ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ سَدًّا وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ سَدًّا فَأَغْشَيْنَاهُمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُبْصِرُونَ wajaʿalnā min bayni aydīhim saddan wamin khalfihim saddan fa-aghshaynāhum fahum lā yub'ṣirūna And We have put a barrier before them and a barrier behind them, then We have blind-folded them, so they do not see.

item.title: Yaseen:9 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا مِنْ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ سَدًّا وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ سَدًّا فَأَغْشَيْنَاهُمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُبْصِرُونَ wajaʿalnā min bayni aydīhim saddan wamin khalfihim saddan fa-aghshaynāhum fahum lā yub'ṣirūna And We have put before them a barrier and behind them a barrier and covered them, so they do not see. See 36:8

item.title: Yaseen:9 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا مِنْ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ سَدًّا وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ سَدًّا فَأَغْشَيْنَاهُمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُبْصِرُونَ wajaʿalnā min bayni aydīhim saddan wamin khalfihim saddan fa-aghshaynāhum fahum lā yub'ṣirūna And We have to set before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and We covered them over, so that they see not. A man from the Banu Makhzum got up with a similar vowful determination to kill the Holy Prophet but when he came near, he was turned blind and could not see the Apostle of God though he was there engaged in prayer. This man also returned to his party with the same report of his finding a lion there intending to attack him. Thus, God had caused some barriers, and they could not see the Holy Prophet. Figurative reference to the pride of the pagans among the Arabs. Similarly, the barriers referred…

item.title: Yaseen:10 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَسَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ wasawāon ʿalayhim a-andhartahum am lam tundhir'hum lā yu'minūna It is the same to them whether you warn them or do not warn them, they will not have faith.

item.title: Yaseen:10 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَسَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ wasawāon ʿalayhim a-andhartahum am lam tundhir'hum lā yu'minūna And it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe. See 36:8

item.title: Yaseen:10 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَسَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ wasawāon ʿalayhim a-andhartahum am lam tundhir'hum lā yu'minūna And alike is it unto them if thou warneth them not, for they will not believe. The history of the early Muslims, bears the best testimony to the truth in this passage. (A.P.).

item.title: Yaseen:11 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّمَا تُنْذِرُ مَنِ اتَّبَعَ الذِّكْرَ وَخَشِيَ الرَّحْمَنَ بِالْغَيْبِ فَبَشِّرْهُ بِمَغْفِرَةٍ وَأَجْرٍ كَرِيمٍ innamā tundhiru mani ittabaʿa l-dhik'ra wakhashiya l-raḥmāna bil-ghaybi fabashir'hu bimaghfiratin wa-ajrin karīmin You can only warn someone who follows the Reminder1 and fears the All-beneficent in secret; so give him the good news of forgiveness and a noble reward.

item.title: Yaseen:11 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّمَا تُنْذِرُ مَنِ اتَّبَعَ الذِّكْرَ وَخَشِيَ الرَّحْمَنَ بِالْغَيْبِ فَبَشِّرْهُ بِمَغْفِرَةٍ وَأَجْرٍ كَرِيمٍ innamā tundhiru mani ittabaʿa l-dhik'ra wakhashiya l-raḥmāna bil-ghaybi fabashir'hu bimaghfiratin wa-ajrin karīmin You can only warn one who follows the message and fears the Most Merciful unseen. So give him good tidings of forgiveness and noble reward. See 36:8

item.title: Yaseen:11 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّمَا تُنْذِرُ مَنِ اتَّبَعَ الذِّكْرَ وَخَشِيَ الرَّحْمَنَ بِالْغَيْبِ فَبَشِّرْهُ بِمَغْفِرَةٍ وَأَجْرٍ كَرِيمٍ innamā tundhiru mani ittabaʿa l-dhik'ra wakhashiya l-raḥmāna bil-ghaybi fabashir'hu bimaghfiratin wa-ajrin karīmin Verily thou canst warn only him who abideth by the Reminder (Qur'an and the Holy Prophet.) and feareth the Beneficent (God) unseen; so bear thou unto him the glad tidings of forgiveness and an honourable recompense. (i.e., whoever follows the Book (Qur'an) and the Holy Prophet (Sunnah). Any one deviating even in the least would be classed with the majority - Refer to verses 36:7 & 36:8.) See verse 35:18. (a) Qur'an and the Holy Prophet and 65:10 & 65:11. Book and the tradition meaning whosoever follows the contents of the Qur'an and the Sunnah of the Holy Prophet. Anyone deviating even slightly from the Qur'an and the Sunnah would be classed under majority in verses…

item.title: Yaseen:12 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِي الْمَوْتٰی وَنَكْتُبُ مَا قَدَّمُوْۤا وَءَاثَارَهُمْ وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَاهُ فِي إِمَامٍ مُبِينٍ innā naḥnu nuḥ'yī l-mawtā wanaktubu mā qaddamū waāthārahum wakulla shayin aḥṣaynāhu fī imāmin mubīnin Indeed it is We who revive the dead and write what they have sent ahead1 and their effects [which they left behind],2 and We have figured everything in a manifest Imam.3

item.title: Yaseen:12 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِي الْمَوْتٰی وَنَكْتُبُ مَا قَدَّمُوْۤا وَءَاثَارَهُمْ وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَاهُ فِي إِمَامٍ مُبِينٍ innā naḥnu nuḥ'yī l-mawtā wanaktubu mā qaddamū waāthārahum wakulla shayin aḥṣaynāhu fī imāmin mubīnin Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life and record what they have put forth and what they left behind, and all things We have enumerated in a clear register. See 36:8

item.title: Yaseen:12 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِي الْمَوْتٰی وَنَكْتُبُ مَا قَدَّمُوْۤا وَءَاثَارَهُمْ وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَاهُ فِي إِمَامٍ مُبِينٍ innā naḥnu nuḥ'yī l-mawtā wanaktubu mā qaddamū waāthārahum wakulla shayin aḥṣaynāhu fī imāmin mubīnin Verily We, (and) We (alone) give life unto the dead, and We write down what they have sent before them and (even) their footprints (which they leave behind them): And everything have We confined (recorded) into a (Said the Holy Prophet - He who died while he recognised not the Imam of his age, certainly died of ignorance (Hadith).) Manifesting Imam (Guide). Every individual, man and woman would be brought to account for his or her deeds, on the Day of Judgment and even the effects of the deeds left behind the people will not be spared from the account. It is a clear indication that every individual is accountable not only…

item.title: Yaseen:13 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ مَثَلًا أَصْحَابَ الْقَرْيَةِ إِذْ جَاءَهَا الْمُرْسَلُونَ wa-iḍ'rib lahum mathalan aṣḥāba l-qaryati idh jāahā l-mur'salūna Cite for them the example of the inhabitants of the town when the apostles came to it.

item.title: Yaseen:13 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ مَثَلًا أَصْحَابَ الْقَرْيَةِ إِذْ جَاءَهَا الْمُرْسَلُونَ wa-iḍ'rib lahum mathalan aṣḥāba l-qaryati idh jāahā l-mur'salūna And present to them an example: the people of the city, when the messengers came to it. And put forward to them a similitude; the Dwellers of the Town, when there came Messengers to them (36:13). When We sent to them two Messengers, they denied them both; so We reinforced them with a third, and they said: "Verily, we have been sent to you as Messengers (36:14). They said: "You are only human beings like ourselves, and the Most Gracious has revealed nothing. You are only telling lies (36:15). The Messengers said: "Our Lord knows that we have been sent as Messengers to you, (36:16). "And our duty is only to convey plainly (36:17). The Story of the Dwellers of the Town and Their…

item.title: Yaseen:13 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ مَثَلًا أَصْحَابَ الْقَرْيَةِ إِذْ جَاءَهَا الْمُرْسَلُونَ wa-iḍ'rib lahum mathalan aṣḥāba l-qaryati idh jāahā l-mur'salūna And set forth unto them the instance of the people of a town when came unto it (Our) Apostles, The reference is said to be to the people of the city of Antioch, one of the most important cities in North Syria. It was a Greek city founded by Seleucus Nicator, one of the successors of Alexander about 300 B.C. in memory of his father, Antiochus. There are stories forwarded as examples. The real application of the passage is to the early conditions. While the Holy Prophet started his mission, from among the people followed only by Ali, the dignitaries of Mecca started ridiculing them. It is said that once Abu Talib accompanied by his elder son Jafar, entered the Holy Mosque of Mecca…

item.title: Yaseen:14 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْهِمُ اثْنَيْنِ فَكَذَّبُوهُمَا فَعَزَّزْنَا بِثَالِثٍ فَقَالُوْۤا إِنَّا إِلَيْكُمْ مُرْسَلُونَ idh arsalnā ilayhimu ith'nayni fakadhabūhumā faʿazzaznā bithālithin faqālū innā ilaykum mur'salūna When We sent to them two [apostles], they impugned both of them. Then We reinforced them with a third, and they said, 'We have indeed been sent to you.'

item.title: Yaseen:14 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْهِمُ اثْنَيْنِ فَكَذَّبُوهُمَا فَعَزَّزْنَا بِثَالِثٍ فَقَالُوْۤا إِنَّا إِلَيْكُمْ مُرْسَلُونَ idh arsalnā ilayhimu ith'nayni fakadhabūhumā faʿazzaznā bithālithin faqālū innā ilaykum mur'salūna When We sent to them two but they denied them, so We strengthened (them) with a third, and they said, "Indeed, we are messengers to you." See 36:13

item.title: Yaseen:14 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِذْ أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْهِمُ اثْنَيْنِ فَكَذَّبُوهُمَا فَعَزَّزْنَا بِثَالِثٍ فَقَالُوْۤا إِنَّا إِلَيْكُمْ مُرْسَلُونَ idh arsalnā ilayhimu ith'nayni fakadhabūhumā faʿazzaznā bithālithin faqālū innā ilaykum mur'salūna When sent We unto them two (of Our apostles) they belied them both, then We strengthened (the two) with a third (one from Us) and said they (unto the people): "Verily we are unto you the apostles (from God)" Jesus had sent two of his disciples to preach his message. It is said that they were John and Jonah. When they approached the outskirts of the city, they met a shepherd who asked as to who they were. They said that they were the messengers from Jesus the Apostle of God, and had been sent to invite the people to the Islam, the true faith. The shepherd asked if they had any signs to prove their bonafide. They…

item.title: Yaseen:15 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا مَا أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُنَا وَمَا أَنْزَلَ الرَّحْمَنُ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِنْ أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا تَكْذِبُونَ qālū mā antum illā basharun mith'lunā wamā anzala l-raḥmānu min shayin in antum illā takdhibūna They said, 'You are nothing but humans like us, and the All-beneficent has not sent down anything, and you are only lying.'

item.title: Yaseen:15 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا مَا أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُنَا وَمَا أَنْزَلَ الرَّحْمَنُ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِنْ أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا تَكْذِبُونَ qālū mā antum illā basharun mith'lunā wamā anzala l-raḥmānu min shayin in antum illā takdhibūna They said, "You are not but human beings like us, and the Most Merciful has not revealed a thing. You are only telling lies." See 36:13

item.title: Yaseen:15 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا مَا أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُنَا وَمَا أَنْزَلَ الرَّحْمَنُ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِنْ أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا تَكْذِبُونَ qālū mā antum illā basharun mith'lunā wamā anzala l-raḥmānu min shayin in antum illā takdhibūna They said: "Ye are not but men like unto us, nor hath sent down the Beneficent (God) any thing, ye only utter a lie." When Simon had gained sufficient influence over the king, he one day asked the king to get the two persons to be questioned about their faith. When the two messengers appeared, they saw Simon but did not give vent to their recognition. Simon asked them as to who they were and the purpose of their visit to the place. They said that they were the messengers of Jesus the Apostle of God, sent to invite the king to give up idolatry and embrace the faith in…

item.title: Yaseen:16 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا رَبُّنَا يَعْلَمُ إِنَّا إِلَيْكُمْ لَمُرْسَلُونَ qālū rabbunā yaʿlamu innā ilaykum lamur'salūna They said, 'Our Lord knows that we have indeed been sent to you,

item.title: Yaseen:16 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا رَبُّنَا يَعْلَمُ إِنَّا إِلَيْكُمْ لَمُرْسَلُونَ qālū rabbunā yaʿlamu innā ilaykum lamur'salūna They said, "Our Lord knows that we are messengers to you. See 36:13

item.title: Yaseen:16 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا رَبُّنَا يَعْلَمُ إِنَّا إِلَيْكُمْ لَمُرْسَلُونَ qālū rabbunā yaʿlamu innā ilaykum lamur'salūna They said: "Our Lord knoweth that we are verily unto you the apostles." The best proof of the genuineness of their claim as the apostles of God and their having been sent by none else but God was that whenever the people disbelieved their position as the heavenly teachers and rejected the message they preached, the apostles always invoked the authority and the mercy of God and faithfully and patiently suffered the worst of persecution and tortures and never yielded to any authority other than God's. Their conviction about God's knowledge was so firm and unshakable that in the events of the difficulties they met and the people disbelieving and rejecting them, they were perfectly satisfied for they knew that God was seeing them executing His Command and…

item.title: Yaseen:17 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا عَلَيْنَا إِلَّا الْبَلَاغُ الْمُبِينُ wamā ʿalaynā illā l-balāghu l-mubīnu and our duty is only to communicate in clear terms.'

item.title: Yaseen:17 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا عَلَيْنَا إِلَّا الْبَلَاغُ الْمُبِينُ wamā ʿalaynā illā l-balāghu l-mubīnu And we are not responsible except for clear notification." See 36:13

item.title: Yaseen:17 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا عَلَيْنَا إِلَّا الْبَلَاغُ الْمُبِينُ wamā ʿalaynā illā l-balāghu l-mubīnu And on us is nothing but a clear deliverance (of the message) 'Tayr' means a bird. Like the Romans, the Arabs also derived Omens from birds - For the Egyptians imagining that their ill-luck was due to Moses. See verse 7:131 and Thamud's thinking their ill-luck being due to the preachings of Salih.1 The people warned the messengers from Jesus that if they did not desist, they would be stoned and inflicted with a painful chastisement.

item.title: Yaseen:18 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا إِنَّا تَطَيَّرْنَا بِكُمْ لَئِنْ لَمْ تَنْتَهُوْۤا لَنَرْجُمَنَّكُمْ وَلَيَمَسَّنَّكُمْ مِنَّا عَذَابٌ اَلِیْمٌ qālū innā taṭayyarnā bikum la-in lam tantahū lanarjumannakum walayamassannakum minnā ʿadhābun alīmun They said, 'Indeed we take you for a bad omen. If you do not relinquish we will stone you, and surely a painful punishment will visit you from us.'

item.title: Yaseen:18 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا إِنَّا تَطَيَّرْنَا بِكُمْ لَئِنْ لَمْ تَنْتَهُوْۤا لَنَرْجُمَنَّكُمْ وَلَيَمَسَّنَّكُمْ مِنَّا عَذَابٌ اَلِیْمٌ qālū innā taṭayyarnā bikum la-in lam tantahū lanarjumannakum walayamassannakum minnā ʿadhābun alīmun They said, "Indeed, we consider you a bad omen. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you, and there will surely touch you, from us, a painful punishment." They (people) said: For us, we see an evil omen from you; if you cease not, we will surely stone you, and a painful torment will touch you from us (36:18). They (Messengers) said: "Your evil omens be with you! Because you are admonished? Nay, but you are a people mischievous.") Then the people of the city said to the (36:19). إِنَّا تَطَيَّرْنَا بِكُمْ (For us, we see an evil omen from you;) meaning, 'we do not see in your faces any sign of good for…

item.title: Yaseen:18 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا إِنَّا تَطَيَّرْنَا بِكُمْ لَئِنْ لَمْ تَنْتَهُوْۤا لَنَرْجُمَنَّكُمْ وَلَيَمَسَّنَّكُمْ مِنَّا عَذَابٌ اَلِیْمٌ qālū innā taṭayyarnā bikum la-in lam tantahū lanarjumannakum walayamassannakum minnā ʿadhābun alīmun Said they: "Verily we augur ill from you, if ye desist not, we will certainly stone you, and there shall afflict you from us a painful torment." See 36:17

item.title: Yaseen:19 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا طَائِرُكُمْ مَعَكُمْ أَئِنْ ذُكِّرْتُمْ بَلْ أَنْتُمْ قَوْمٌ مُسْرِفُونَ qālū ṭāirukum maʿakum a-in dhukkir'tum bal antum qawmun mus'rifūna They said, 'Your bad omens attend you. What! If you are admonished ….1 Rather you are a profligate lot.'

item.title: Yaseen:19 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا طَائِرُكُمْ مَعَكُمْ أَئِنْ ذُكِّرْتُمْ بَلْ أَنْتُمْ قَوْمٌ مُسْرِفُونَ qālū ṭāirukum maʿakum a-in dhukkir'tum bal antum qawmun mus'rifūna They said, "Your omen (i.e., fate) is with yourselves. Is it1 because you were reminded? Rather, you are a transgressing people." See 36:18

item.title: Yaseen:19 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا طَائِرُكُمْ مَعَكُمْ أَئِنْ ذُكِّرْتُمْ بَلْ أَنْتُمْ قَوْمٌ مُسْرِفُونَ qālū ṭāirukum maʿakum a-in dhukkir'tum bal antum qawmun mus'rifūna They said: "your augury of ill is with yourselves; What! when ye are admonished (deem ye ill of it) 1 Nay! ye are people transgressing (exceedingly)" The messengers replied that the calamity which would overtake the people, would be the earning of their rebellious conduct.

item.title: Yaseen:20 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَاءَ مِنْ أَقْصَا الْمَدِينَةِ رَجُلٌ يَسْعَى قَالَ يَاقَوْمِ اتَّبِعُوْۤا الْمُرْسَلِیْنَ wajāa min aqṣā l-madīnati rajulun yasʿā qāla yāqawmi ittabiʿū l-mur'salīna There came a man from the city outskirts, hurrying. He said, 'O my people! Follow the apostles!

item.title: Yaseen:20 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَاءَ مِنْ أَقْصَا الْمَدِينَةِ رَجُلٌ يَسْعَى قَالَ يَاقَوْمِ اتَّبِعُوْۤا الْمُرْسَلِیْنَ wajāa min aqṣā l-madīnati rajulun yasʿā qāla yāqawmi ittabiʿū l-mur'salīna And there came from the farthest end of the city a man, running. He said, "O my people, follow the messengers. And there came a man running from the farthest part of the town. He said, "O my people! Obey the Messengers (36:20). "Obey those who ask no wages of you, and who are rightly guided (36:21). "And why should I not worship Him Who has created me and to Whom you shall be returned (36:22). "Shall I take besides Him gods? If the Most Gracious intends me any harm, their intercession will be of no use for me whatsoever, nor can they save me (36:23). "Then verily, I should be in plain error (36:24). "Verily, I have believed in…

item.title: Yaseen:20 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَاءَ مِنْ أَقْصَا الْمَدِينَةِ رَجُلٌ يَسْعَى قَالَ يَاقَوْمِ اتَّبِعُوْۤا الْمُرْسَلِیْنَ wajāa min aqṣā l-madīnati rajulun yasʿā qāla yāqawmi ittabiʿū l-mur'salīna And came from the (Also for Mu'min Aal-e-Fir'aun – Refer to note on verse 40:28 - as was Abu Talib, father of Ali who hid his faith and protected the Holy Prophet - and Ali was the first to believe when none believed.) farthest part of the city a man running and said: "O' my people! Follow ye (these) the apostles (of God)," When the people of the city disbelieved and rejected the Message from Jesus, a man from the outskirts of the city, i.e., Habib al-Najjar (Habib the Carpenter) who is a popularly known as the 'Mu'min-e-Aal-e-Ya-Sin' (The believers in the children of Ya-Sin, i.e., Muhammad) came running and exhorted his people to believe in the message of the…

item.title: Yaseen:21 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اِتَّبِعُوا مَنْ لَا يَسْءَلُكُمْ أَجْرًا وَهُمْ مُهْتَدُونَ ittabiʿū man lā yasalukum ajran wahum muh'tadūna Follow them who do not ask you any reward and they are rightly guided.

item.title: Yaseen:21 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اِتَّبِعُوا مَنْ لَا يَسْءَلُكُمْ أَجْرًا وَهُمْ مُهْتَدُونَ ittabiʿū man lā yasalukum ajran wahum muh'tadūna Follow those who do not ask of you (any) payment, and they are (rightly) guided. See 36:20

item.title: Yaseen:21 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اِتَّبِعُوا مَنْ لَا يَسْءَلُكُمْ أَجْرًا وَهُمْ مُهْتَدُونَ ittabiʿū man lā yasalukum ajran wahum muh'tadūna Follow ye those who ask you not any recompense, and they are guided aright. For no reward was demanded in return for their Services. The one who deserves to be followed, i.e., the person who does not expect any reward or return from you - secondly, he himself should be well guided and not taking guidance from others for himself.1 (A.P.). When Ubaydah ibn Harith fell at the battle of Badr, the Holy Prophet came to him while he was still alive. Ubaydah smiled and said - 'I wished Abu Talib had been alive to see that I am the first one of his house who lays down his life for the sake of the divine cause'. (A.P.).

item.title: Yaseen:22 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا لِيَ لَا أَعْبُدُ الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ wamā liya lā aʿbudu alladhī faṭaranī wa-ilayhi tur'jaʿūna Why should I not worship Him who has originated me, and to whom you shall be brought back?

item.title: Yaseen:22 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا لِيَ لَا أَعْبُدُ الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ wamā liya lā aʿbudu alladhī faṭaranī wa-ilayhi tur'jaʿūna And why should I not worship He who created me and to whom you will be returned? See 36:20

item.title: Yaseen:22 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا لِيَ لَا أَعْبُدُ الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ wamā liya lā aʿbudu alladhī faṭaranī wa-ilayhi tur'jaʿūna And why should not I worship only Him Who brought me into being? and unto Whom ye shall all be returned: What is said in this verse is what the individual had been personally convinced, with which he wants to appeal to his people to follow his conviction. He argues for himself saying, as to how it could be possible for him not to serve or adore his real Maker, to whom alone is their ultimate return.

item.title: Yaseen:23 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ءَأَتَّخِذُ مِنْ دُونِهِ آلِهَةً إِنْ يُرِدْنِ الرَّحْمَنُ بِضُرٍّ لَا تُغْنِ عَنِّي شَفَاعَتُهُمْ شَيْئًا وَلَا يُنْقِذُونِ a-attakhidhu min dūnihi ālihatan in yurid'ni l-raḥmānu biḍurrin lā tugh'ni ʿannī shafāʿatuhum shayan walā yunqidhūni Shall I take gods besides Him? If the All-beneficent desired to cause me any distress their intercession will not avail me in any way, nor will they rescue me.

item.title: Yaseen:23 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ءَأَتَّخِذُ مِنْ دُونِهِ آلِهَةً إِنْ يُرِدْنِ الرَّحْمَنُ بِضُرٍّ لَا تُغْنِ عَنِّي شَفَاعَتُهُمْ شَيْئًا وَلَا يُنْقِذُونِ a-attakhidhu min dūnihi ālihatan in yurid'ni l-raḥmānu biḍurrin lā tugh'ni ʿannī shafāʿatuhum shayan walā yunqidhūni Should I take other than Him (false) deities (while), if the Most Merciful intends for me some adversity, their intercession will not avail me at all, nor can they save me? See 36:20

item.title: Yaseen:23 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ءَأَتَّخِذُ مِنْ دُونِهِ آلِهَةً إِنْ يُرِدْنِ الرَّحْمَنُ بِضُرٍّ لَا تُغْنِ عَنِّي شَفَاعَتُهُمْ شَيْئًا وَلَا يُنْقِذُونِ a-attakhidhu min dūnihi ālihatan in yurid'ni l-raḥmānu biḍurrin lā tugh'ni ʿannī shafāʿatuhum shayan walā yunqidhūni What! Shall I take besides Him any gods, if (God) The Beneficent willeth to afflict me with harm, their (the false gods & the deities.) intercession shall not avail me aught, neither can they (the false gods & the deities.) deliver (Save – relieve.) me? This is the continuation of the previous verse. Another argument is advanced here, against worship in the false gods. Since God alone is the Omnipotent Whose will to punish anyone shall always be worship in the false gods. Since God alone is the Omnipotent Whose will to punish anyone shall always be done and none of the false deities could ever resist it nor could…

item.title: Yaseen:24 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اِنِّیْ إِذًا لَفِیْ ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ innī idhan lafī ḍalālin mubīnin Indeed then I would be in manifest error.

item.title: Yaseen:24 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اِنِّیْ إِذًا لَفِیْ ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ innī idhan lafī ḍalālin mubīnin Indeed, I would then be in manifest error. See 36:20

item.title: Yaseen:24 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اِنِّیْ إِذًا لَفِیْ ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ innī idhan lafī ḍalālin mubīnin Verily, I in which case shall be in manifest error: If what is said in the previous verse is acted upon by anyone, the individual would indeed manifest error.

item.title: Yaseen:25 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: اِنِّیْ ءَامَنْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ فَاسْمَعُونِ innī āmantu birabbikum fa-is'maʿūni Indeed I have faith in your Lord, so listen to me.'

item.title: Yaseen:25 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: اِنِّیْ ءَامَنْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ فَاسْمَعُونِ innī āmantu birabbikum fa-is'maʿūni Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me." See 36:20

item.title: Yaseen:25 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: اِنِّیْ ءَامَنْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ فَاسْمَعُونِ innī āmantu birabbikum fa-is'maʿūni Verily, I believe in your Lord, so hear me! This refers to the assured personal conviction of the man (the Mu'min-e-Ale-Ya-Sin) about God, which he wants to convey to his people and exhort them to embrace it and get themselves guided aright. While the godly man, preached the truth to the people and exhorted them to embrace it, the people stoned him and killed him and buried him in the marketplace of Antioch (Antakya).

item.title: Yaseen:26 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قِيلَ ادْخُلِ الْجَنَّةَ قَالَ يَالَيْتَ قَوْمِي يَعْلَمُونَ qīla ud'khuli l-janata qāla yālayta qawmī yaʿlamūna He was told, 'Enter paradise!' He said, 'Alas! Had my people only known

item.title: Yaseen:26 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قِيلَ ادْخُلِ الْجَنَّةَ قَالَ يَالَيْتَ قَوْمِي يَعْلَمُونَ qīla ud'khuli l-janata qāla yālayta qawmī yaʿlamūna It was said, "Enter Paradise."1 He said, "I wish my people could know. It was said: "Enter Paradise." He said: "Would that my people knew (36:26). "That my Lord (Allah) has forgiven me, and made me of the honored ones! (36:27). And We sent not against his people after him an army from the heaven, nor was it needful for Us to send (such a thing) (36:28). It was but one 'Şayḥah' and lo! they (all) were still (36:29). Muhammad bin Ishaq reported from some of his companions from Ibn Mas'ud (RA), that they stamped on him until his intestines came out of his back passage. Allah said to him: ادْخُلِ الْجَنَّةَ "Enter Paradise." so he entered it with all its bountiful provision, when Allah had…

item.title: Yaseen:26 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قِيلَ ادْخُلِ الْجَنَّةَ قَالَ يَالَيْتَ قَوْمِي يَعْلَمُونَ qīla ud'khuli l-janata qāla yālayta qawmī yaʿlamūna It Was said (unto him): "Enter thou, the (Paradise.) garden!" Said he: "Oh! would (Remembering others in the bliss.) that my people had known," The soul of the godly man was asked by the angels to enter Paradise on which occasion in the bliss granted to him, the liberated soul remembers his people saying: 'Had the people known what a blissful life is granted to the believers in the truth and the righteous ones, they also would have enjoyed the bounties of God and as he has received'.

item.title: Yaseen:27 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: بِمَا غَفَرَ لِي رَبِّي وَجَعَلَنِي مِنَ الْمُكْرَمِينَ bimā ghafara lī rabbī wajaʿalanī mina l-muk'ramīna for what my Lord forgave me and made me one of the honoured ones!'

item.title: Yaseen:27 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: بِمَا غَفَرَ لِي رَبِّي وَجَعَلَنِي مِنَ الْمُكْرَمِينَ bimā ghafara lī rabbī wajaʿalanī mina l-muk'ramīna Of how my Lord has forgiven me and placed me among the honored." See 36:26

item.title: Yaseen:27 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: بِمَا غَفَرَ لِي رَبِّي وَجَعَلَنِي مِنَ الْمُكْرَمِينَ bimā ghafara lī rabbī wajaʿalanī mina l-muk'ramīna Of that for which my Lord hath forgiven me and hath made me of the honoured ones This verse is the continuation of the previous one meaning had the people known the worth of the faith in the Only True God and righteousness in life on account of which qualities he has been made honourable in the life after death.

item.title: Yaseen:28 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَى قَوْمِهِ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ مِنْ جُنْدٍ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ وَمَا كُنَّا مُنْزِلِينَ wamā anzalnā ʿalā qawmihi min baʿdihi min jundin mina l-samāi wamā kunnā munzilīna After him We did not send down on his people a host from the sky, nor We would have sent down.1

item.title: Yaseen:28 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَى قَوْمِهِ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ مِنْ جُنْدٍ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ وَمَا كُنَّا مُنْزِلِينَ wamā anzalnā ʿalā qawmihi min baʿdihi min jundin mina l-samāi wamā kunnā munzilīna And We did not send down upon his people after him any soldiers from the heaven, nor would We have done so. See 36:26

item.title: Yaseen:28 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَى قَوْمِهِ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ مِنْ جُنْدٍ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ وَمَا كُنَّا مُنْزِلِينَ wamā anzalnā ʿalā qawmihi min baʿdihi min jundin mina l-samāi wamā kunnā munzilīna We sent not down upon his people any hosts from heaven, nor were We (in need) to send (any such hosts). The enforcement of the justice of the Almighty God, needs not the pomp, show and the circumstance which the ordinary powers and the authorities of earthly beings, manifest to create awe in the minds of the fellow beings to establish or to increase the regard for their strength and glory, nor does God need any of the forces of human wickedness or any manifest use of the mighty and the unconquerable spiritual forces to punish them or to even wipe them out of existence. Hence no hosts from heaven were sent to punish…

item.title: Yaseen:29 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنْ كَانَتْ إِلَّا صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً فَإِذَا هُمْ خَامِدُونَ in kānat illā ṣayḥatan wāḥidatan fa-idhā hum khāmidūna It was but a single Cry, and, behold, they were stilled [like burnt ashes]!

item.title: Yaseen:29 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنْ كَانَتْ إِلَّا صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً فَإِذَا هُمْ خَامِدُونَ in kānat illā ṣayḥatan wāḥidatan fa-idhā hum khāmidūna It was not but one shout,1 and immediately they were extinguished. See 36:26

item.title: Yaseen:29 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: إِنْ كَانَتْ إِلَّا صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً فَإِذَا هُمْ خَامِدُونَ in kānat illā ṣayḥatan wāḥidatan fa-idhā hum khāmidūna It was nothing but one terrible cry, and lo! they were (like ashes) extinct. A single blast either through the rumbling of an earthquake or a violent stormy wind with a thunder was sufficient as it was in the case of the people of Thamud.1 A blast was quite sufficient to effect a complete perdition to the people and they were like ashes, quenched and silent. This verse speaks of hosts not being sent in the case of the event of Antioch, with nothing to speak about what was effected at Badr, Ahzab and elsewhere. Ref. to the sudden disastrous calamity which befell the people who killed Theophilus - (Habib al-Najjar). (A.P.)

item.title: Yaseen:30 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاحَسْرَةً عَلَى الْعِبَادِ مَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا كَانُوْۤا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ yāḥasratan ʿalā l-ʿibādi mā yatīhim min rasūlin illā kānū bihi yastahziūna How regrettable of the servants! There did not come to them any apostle but that they used to deride him.

item.title: Yaseen:30 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاحَسْرَةً عَلَى الْعِبَادِ مَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا كَانُوْۤا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ yāḥasratan ʿalā l-ʿibādi mā yatīhim min rasūlin illā kānū bihi yastahziūna How regretful for the servants. There did not come to them any messenger except that they used to ridicule him. Alas for mankind! There never came a Messenger to them but they used to mock at him (36:30). Do they not see how many of the generations We have destroyed before them? Verily, they will not return to them (36:31). And surely, all – everyone of them will be brought before Us (36:32). Woe to the Disbelievers! Ali bin Abi Talhah reported that Ibn 'Abbas commented on the Ayah: يَا حَسْرَةً عَلَى الْعِبَادِ ۚ Alas for mankind! This means, woe to mankind! Qatadah said: يَا حَسْرَةً عَلَى الْعِبَادِ ۚ Alas for mankind! means, "Alas for mankind, who have…

item.title: Yaseen:30 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاحَسْرَةً عَلَى الْعِبَادِ مَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا كَانُوْۤا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ yāḥasratan ʿalā l-ʿibādi mā yatīhim min rasūlin illā kānū bihi yastahziūna Alas! the servants (are misled and yet) there cometh not unto them an apostle but they mock at him. See verses 6:10, 21:40. The ignorant masses of the human race have always been mocking at any one and everyone who professed religion seriously and advocated its cause to the others of his race. Particularly the religious leaders and more particularly the apostles of God had suffered heartless persecution and torturous death.1 The people never reflected upon, how countless generations before them, were destroyed for rejecting the Truth. Such people never realised that levity surely and unfailingly reacts on themselves and invites their own degradation, suffering and destruction even in this life, besides what is in store for them…

item.title: Yaseen:31 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَمْ يَرَوْا كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِنَ الْقُرُونِ أَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ alam yaraw kam ahlaknā qablahum mina l-qurūni annahum ilayhim lā yarjiʿūna Have they not regarded how many generations We have destroyed before them who will not come back to them?

item.title: Yaseen:31 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَمْ يَرَوْا كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِنَ الْقُرُونِ أَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ alam yaraw kam ahlaknā qablahum mina l-qurūni annahum ilayhim lā yarjiʿūna Have they not considered how many generations We destroyed before them - that they to them1 will not return? See 36:30

item.title: Yaseen:31 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: أَلَمْ يَرَوْا كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِنَ الْقُرُونِ أَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ alam yaraw kam ahlaknā qablahum mina l-qurūni annahum ilayhim lā yarjiʿūna What! See they not how many of the generation We did destroy before them? they will return not unto them. Those punished by God in this life for their wickedness, would not be returned to this world and some commentators say that the people were punished even for their not honouring those apostles of God whom they ridiculed and rejected.

item.title: Yaseen:32 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنْ كُلٌّ لَمَّا جَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنَا مُحْضَرُونَ wa-in kullun lammā jamīʿun ladaynā muḥ'ḍarūna And all of them will indeed be presented before Us.

item.title: Yaseen:32 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنْ كُلٌّ لَمَّا جَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنَا مُحْضَرُونَ wa-in kullun lammā jamīʿun ladaynā muḥ'ḍarūna And indeed, all of them will yet be brought present before Us. See 36:30

item.title: Yaseen:32 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَإِنْ كُلٌّ لَمَّا جَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنَا مُحْضَرُونَ wa-in kullun lammā jamīʿun ladaynā muḥ'ḍarūna And assuredly all, gathered together, shall be brought before Us. Certainly, every one of them shall be brought together before God as commanded. (A.P.).

item.title: Yaseen:33 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاٰیَةٌ لَهُمُ الْأَرْضُ الْمَيْتَةُ أَحْيَيْنَاهَا وَأَخْرَجْنَا مِنْهَا حَبًّا فَمِنْهُ يَأْكُلُونَ waāyatun lahumu l-arḍu l-maytatu aḥyaynāhā wa-akhrajnā min'hā ḥabban famin'hu yakulūna A sign for them is the dead earth, which We revive and out of it bring forth grain, so they eat of it.

item.title: Yaseen:33 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاٰیَةٌ لَهُمُ الْأَرْضُ الْمَيْتَةُ أَحْيَيْنَاهَا وَأَخْرَجْنَا مِنْهَا حَبًّا فَمِنْهُ يَأْكُلُونَ waāyatun lahumu l-arḍu l-maytatu aḥyaynāhā wa-akhrajnā min'hā ḥabban famin'hu yakulūna And a sign for them is the dead earth. We have brought it to life and brought forth from it grain, and from it they eat. And a sign for them is the dead land. We give it life, and We bring forth from it grains, so that they eat thereof (36:33). And We have made therein gardens of date palms and grapes, and We have caused springs of water to gush forth therein (36:34). So that they may eat of the fruit thereof – and their hands made it not. Will they not then give thanks (36:35). Glory be to Him Who has created all the pairs of that which the earth produces, as well as of their own…

item.title: Yaseen:33 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاٰیَةٌ لَهُمُ الْأَرْضُ الْمَيْتَةُ أَحْيَيْنَاهَا وَأَخْرَجْنَا مِنْهَا حَبًّا فَمِنْهُ يَأْكُلُونَ waāyatun lahumu l-arḍu l-maytatu aḥyaynāhā wa-akhrajnā min'hā ḥabban famin'hu yakulūna And a sign unto them is the dead earth; We give life to it and bring We forth from it grain of which they eat. Let those who disbelieve their resurrection after death for the Final Judgment, take the note of guidance from the earth which for all intents and purposes, seems to be dead in a season every year and get quickened again and becomes once more productive as it was before. it was before1. Indicates here, a higher stage is made to develop from the lower one as a continuity of the movement. (A.P.).

item.title: Yaseen:34 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا جَنَّاتٍ مِنْ نَخِيلٍ وَأَعْنَابٍ وَفَجَّرْنَا فِيهَا مِنَ الْعُيُونِ wajaʿalnā fīhā jannātin min nakhīlin wa-aʿnābin wafajjarnā fīhā mina l-ʿuyūni And We make in it orchards of date palms and vines, and We cause springs to gush forth in it,

item.title: Yaseen:34 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا جَنَّاتٍ مِنْ نَخِيلٍ وَأَعْنَابٍ وَفَجَّرْنَا فِيهَا مِنَ الْعُيُونِ wajaʿalnā fīhā jannātin min nakhīlin wa-aʿnābin wafajjarnā fīhā mina l-ʿuyūni And We placed therein gardens of palm trees and grapevines and caused to burst forth therefrom some springs. See 36:33

item.title: Yaseen:34 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا جَنَّاتٍ مِنْ نَخِيلٍ وَأَعْنَابٍ وَفَجَّرْنَا فِيهَا مِنَ الْعُيُونِ wajaʿalnā fīhā jannātin min nakhīlin wa-aʿnābin wafajjarnā fīhā mina l-ʿuyūni And make We therein gardens of date-palms and grapevines, and cause We to flow therein springs, Date palms and vines are mentioned as symbols of fruit trees of various kinds. It may be noted that the description of the blissful life in the Hereafter given in the Qur'an is figurative for the heavenly bliss is unimaginable here.

item.title: Yaseen:35 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: لِيَأْكُلُوا مِنْ ثَمَرِهِ وَمَا عَمِلَتْهُ أَيْدِيهِمْ أَفَلَا يَشْكُرُونَ liyakulū min thamarihi wamā ʿamilathu aydīhim afalā yashkurūna so that they may eat of its fruit and what their hands have cultivated.1 Will they not then give thanks?

item.title: Yaseen:35 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: لِيَأْكُلُوا مِنْ ثَمَرِهِ وَمَا عَمِلَتْهُ أَيْدِيهِمْ أَفَلَا يَشْكُرُونَ liyakulū min thamarihi wamā ʿamilathu aydīhim afalā yashkurūna That they may eat of His fruit.1 And their hands have not produced it,2 so will they not be grateful? See 36:33

item.title: Yaseen:35 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: لِيَأْكُلُوا مِنْ ثَمَرِهِ وَمَا عَمِلَتْهُ أَيْدِيهِمْ أَفَلَا يَشْكُرُونَ liyakulū min thamarihi wamā ʿamilathu aydīhim afalā yashkurūna That they may eat of its fruits, and made it not their hands; What! will they not then be grateful? However, much man may prepare the soil and sow the seed or plant a tree but unless the forces of nature help him, which are God's own and are effected only by His independent will, nothing could profit man, in getting any produce from the earth or to do anything else also in the world. Hence whatever grains or fruits man eats, are the products of God's willed functions of the natural forces in the formulation of which energies and their working in perfect harmony with each other, there is no hand of anyone else besides Him. Should not man be grateful to God?…

item.title: Yaseen:36 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ الْأَزْوَاجَ كُلَّهَا مِمَّا تُنْبِتُ الْأَرْضُ وَمِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ وَمِمَّا لَا يَعْلَمُونَ sub'ḥāna alladhī khalaqa l-azwāja kullahā mimmā tunbitu l-arḍu wamin anfusihim wamimmā lā yaʿlamūna Immaculate is He who has created all the kinds1 of what the earth grows, and of themselves, and of what they do not know.

item.title: Yaseen:36 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ الْأَزْوَاجَ كُلَّهَا مِمَّا تُنْبِتُ الْأَرْضُ وَمِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ وَمِمَّا لَا يَعْلَمُونَ sub'ḥāna alladhī khalaqa l-azwāja kullahā mimmā tunbitu l-arḍu wamin anfusihim wamimmā lā yaʿlamūna Exalted is He who created all pairs1 - from what the earth grows and from themselves and from that which they do not know. See 36:33

item.title: Yaseen:36 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ الْأَزْوَاجَ كُلَّهَا مِمَّا تُنْبِتُ الْأَرْضُ وَمِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ وَمِمَّا لَا يَعْلَمُونَ sub'ḥāna alladhī khalaqa l-azwāja kullahā mimmā tunbitu l-arḍu wamin anfusihim wamimmā lā yaʿlamūna Hallowed is He Who created pairs (of) all things, of what groweth the earth, of their selves and of what they know not. The mystery of sex exists in all species of creation. The constitution of the material world and the various kinds of energies functioning in the universe, are working in pairs of opposite kinds. There is the factor of sex active in the human, animal and vegetable life and in the other forms of activity manifest and hidden, known to us like electricity (positive and negative) and also unknown to us. Scientific enquiry until recently could not reach the fact that even the atom consists of a positive charge called the proton…

item.title: Yaseen:37 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاٰیَةٌ لَهُمُ اللَّيْلُ نَسْلَخُ مِنْهُ النَّهَارَ فَإِذَا هُمْ مُظْلِمُونَ waāyatun lahumu al-laylu naslakhu min'hu l-nahāra fa-idhā hum muẓ'limūna And a sign for them is the night, which We strip of daylight, and, behold, they find themselves in the dark!

item.title: Yaseen:37 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاٰیَةٌ لَهُمُ اللَّيْلُ نَسْلَخُ مِنْهُ النَّهَارَ فَإِذَا هُمْ مُظْلِمُونَ waāyatun lahumu al-laylu naslakhu min'hu l-nahāra fa-idhā hum muẓ'limūna And a sign for them is the night. We remove1 from it the (light of) day, so they are (left) in darkness. And a sign for them is the night. We withdraw therefrom the day, and behold, they are in darkness (36:37). And the sun runs on its fixed course for a term (appointed). That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing (36:38). And the moon, We have decreed for it stages, till it returns like the old dried curved date stalk (36:39). It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day. They all float, each in an orbit (36:40). Among the Signs of the Might and Power of Allah are the Night…

item.title: Yaseen:37 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
