item.description: قَالَ رَبِّ السِّجْنُ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِمَّا يَدْعُونَنِي إِلَيْهِ وَإِلَّا تَصْرِفْ عَنِّي كَيْدَهُنَّ أَصْبُ إِلَيْهِنَّ وَأَكُنْ مِنَ الْجٰهِلِیْنَ qāla rabbi l-sij'nu aḥabbu ilayya mimmā yadʿūnanī ilayhi wa-illā taṣrif ʿannī kaydahunna aṣbu ilayhinna wa-akun mina l-jāhilīna Said he (Joseph.) "O' my Lord! The prison is dearer to me than that unto which they invite me; and if thou turneth (The turning away of the guile by God does not mean overpowering Joseph against his will and choice. It means raising his Cognitive self above the level of the sexual desires, in response to what he asked for.) not away from me their guile I may yearn unto them and become of the ignorant ones." See 12:31

item.title: Yusuf:34 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَاسْتَجَابَ لَهُ رَبُّهُ فَصَرَفَ عَنْهُ كَيْدَهُنَّ إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ fa-is'tajāba lahu rabbuhu faṣarafa ʿanhu kaydahunna innahu huwa l-samīʿu l-ʿalīmu So his Lord answered him and turned away their stratagems from him. Indeed He is the All-hearing, the All-knowing.

item.title: Yusuf:34 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَاسْتَجَابَ لَهُ رَبُّهُ فَصَرَفَ عَنْهُ كَيْدَهُنَّ إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ fa-is'tajāba lahu rabbuhu faṣarafa ʿanhu kaydahunna innahu huwa l-samīʿu l-ʿalīmu So his Lord responded to him and averted from him their plan. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing. See 12:30

item.title: Yusuf:34 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَاسْتَجَابَ لَهُ رَبُّهُ فَصَرَفَ عَنْهُ كَيْدَهُنَّ إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ fa-is'tajāba lahu rabbuhu faṣarafa ʿanhu kaydahunna innahu huwa l-samīʿu l-ʿalīmu Thereupon heard him (granted his prayer.) his Lord and turned (See note to verse 12:33.) He away their guile from him; Verily He is the All Hearing, The All-Knowing. See 12:31

item.title: Yusuf:35 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا رَأَوُا ٱلْـَٔايَـٰتِ لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ حَتّٰی حِينٍ thumma badā lahum min baʿdi mā ra-awū l-āyāti layasjununnahu ḥattā ḥīnin Then it appeared to them,1 after they had seen all the signs [of his innocence], that they should confine him for some time.

item.title: Yusuf:35 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا رَأَوُا ٱلْـَٔايَـٰتِ لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ حَتّٰی حِينٍ thumma badā lahum min baʿdi mā ra-awū l-āyāti layasjununnahu ḥattā ḥīnin Then it appeared to them after they had seen the signs1 that he (i.e., al-ʿAzeez) should surely imprison him for a time.2 Then it occurred to them, after they had seen the proofs (of his innocence), to imprison him for a time (12:35). Yusuf is Imprisoned without Justification Allah says, 'Then it occurred to them that it would be in their interest to imprison Yusuf for a time, even after they were convinced of his innocence and saw the proofs of his truth, honesty and chastity.' It appears, and Allah knows best, that they imprisoned him after the news of what happened spread. They wanted to pretend that Yusuf was the one who tried to seduce the 'Aziz's…

item.title: Yusuf:35 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا رَأَوُا ٱلْـَٔايَـٰتِ لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ حَتّٰی حِينٍ thumma badā lahum min baʿdi mā ra-awū l-āyāti layasjununnahu ḥattā ḥīnin Then it occurred to them (even) after they had seen the signs (of his innocence) that they should imprison him for a time. When the women got hopeless of winning over Joseph, they suggested Zulaikha to imprison Joseph for a few days and subject him to the miseries therein so that he might then realize the value of the luxuries in the palace. Zulaikha readily accepted the suggestion, for that would make the public know that it was Joseph who was guilty and not she. Joseph was enchained and taken through the streets of the town with an announcer calling in the front 'Look ye'! This is the punishment for the attempt against the chastity of the wife…

item.title: Yusuf:36 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَدَخَلَ مَعَهُ السِّجْنَ فَتَيَانِ قَالَ أَحَدُهُمَا اِنِّیْ أَرَانِي أَعْصِرُ خَمْرًا وَقَالَ الْءَاخَرُ اِنِّیْ أَرَانِي أَحْمِلُ فَوْقَ رَأْسِي خُبْزًا تَأْكُلُ الطَّيْرُ مِنْهُ نَبِّئْنَا بِتَأْوِيلِهِ إِنَّا نَرَاكَ مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ wadakhala maʿahu l-sij'na fatayāni qāla aḥaduhumā innī arānī aʿṣiru khamran waqāla l-ākharu innī arānī aḥmilu fawqa rasī khub'zan takulu l-ṭayru min'hu nabbi'nā bitawīlihi innā narāka mina l-muḥ'sinīna There entered the prison two youths along with him. One of them said, 'I dreamt that I am pressing grapes.' The other said, 'I dreamt that I am carrying bread on my head from which the birds are eating.' 'Inform us of its interpretation,' [they said], 'for indeed we see you to be a virtuous man.'

item.title: Yusuf:36 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَدَخَلَ مَعَهُ السِّجْنَ فَتَيَانِ قَالَ أَحَدُهُمَا اِنِّیْ أَرَانِي أَعْصِرُ خَمْرًا وَقَالَ الْءَاخَرُ اِنِّیْ أَرَانِي أَحْمِلُ فَوْقَ رَأْسِي خُبْزًا تَأْكُلُ الطَّيْرُ مِنْهُ نَبِّئْنَا بِتَأْوِيلِهِ إِنَّا نَرَاكَ مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ wadakhala maʿahu l-sij'na fatayāni qāla aḥaduhumā innī arānī aʿṣiru khamran waqāla l-ākharu innī arānī aḥmilu fawqa rasī khub'zan takulu l-ṭayru min'hu nabbi'nā bitawīlihi innā narāka mina l-muḥ'sinīna And there entered the prison with him two young men. One of them said, "Indeed, I have seen myself (in a dream) pressing (grapes for) wine." The other said, "Indeed, I have seen myself carrying upon my head (some) bread, from which the birds were eating. Inform us of its interpretation; indeed, we see you to be of those who do good." And there entered with him two young men in the prison. One of them said: Verily, I saw myself (in a dream) pressing wine."…

item.title: Yusuf:36 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَدَخَلَ مَعَهُ السِّجْنَ فَتَيَانِ قَالَ أَحَدُهُمَا اِنِّیْ أَرَانِي أَعْصِرُ خَمْرًا وَقَالَ الْءَاخَرُ اِنِّیْ أَرَانِي أَحْمِلُ فَوْقَ رَأْسِي خُبْزًا تَأْكُلُ الطَّيْرُ مِنْهُ نَبِّئْنَا بِتَأْوِيلِهِ إِنَّا نَرَاكَ مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ wadakhala maʿahu l-sij'na fatayāni qāla aḥaduhumā innī arānī aʿṣiru khamran waqāla l-ākharu innī arānī aḥmilu fawqa rasī khub'zan takulu l-ṭayru min'hu nabbi'nā bitawīlihi innā narāka mina l-muḥ'sinīna And with him entered the prison, two youths; Said one of them (Unto Joseph) "Verily I saw (in dream) myself pressing wine." And said the other: "I saw (in dream) myself carrying bread on my head, and birds eating there of. Inform us of its interpretation: Verily we see thee of the doers of good (to all)." The two young men were: The 'Saqi' (the servant who serves the drinks) called 'Yunan' who used to draw wine from the grapes for the King. The Cook of…

item.title: Yusuf:37 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ لَا يَأْتِيكُمَا طَعَامٌ تُرْزَقَانِهِ إِلَّا نَبَّأْتُكُمَا بِتَأْوِيلِهِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَأْتِيَكُمَا ذَلِكُمَا مِمَّا عَلَّمَنِي رَبِّي اِنِّیْ تَرَكْتُ مِلَّةَ قَوْمٍ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَهُمْ بِالْاٰخِرَةِ هُمْ كَافِرُونَ qāla lā yatīkumā ṭaʿāmun tur'zaqānihi illā nabbatukumā bitawīlihi qabla an yatiyakumā dhālikumā mimmā ʿallamanī rabbī innī taraktu millata qawmin lā yu'minūna bil-lahi wahum bil-ākhirati hum kāfirūna He said, 'Before the meals you are served come to you I will inform you of its interpretation. That is among things my Lord has taught me. Indeed I renounce the creed of the people who have no faith in Allah and who [also] disbelieve in the Hereafter.

item.title: Yusuf:37 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ لَا يَأْتِيكُمَا طَعَامٌ تُرْزَقَانِهِ إِلَّا نَبَّأْتُكُمَا بِتَأْوِيلِهِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَأْتِيَكُمَا ذَلِكُمَا مِمَّا عَلَّمَنِي رَبِّي اِنِّیْ تَرَكْتُ مِلَّةَ قَوْمٍ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَهُمْ بِالْاٰخِرَةِ هُمْ كَافِرُونَ qāla lā yatīkumā ṭaʿāmun tur'zaqānihi illā nabbatukumā bitawīlihi qabla an yatiyakumā dhālikumā mimmā ʿallamanī rabbī innī taraktu millata qawmin lā yu'minūna bil-lahi wahum bil-ākhirati hum kāfirūna He said, "You will not receive food that is provided to you except that I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you. That is from what my Lord has taught me. Indeed, I have left the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah, and they, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers. He said: "No food will come to you as your provision, but I will inform its interpretation before it comes. This is of that which my Lord has taught me. Verily,…

item.title: Yusuf:37 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ لَا يَأْتِيكُمَا طَعَامٌ تُرْزَقَانِهِ إِلَّا نَبَّأْتُكُمَا بِتَأْوِيلِهِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَأْتِيَكُمَا ذَلِكُمَا مِمَّا عَلَّمَنِي رَبِّي اِنِّیْ تَرَكْتُ مِلَّةَ قَوْمٍ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَهُمْ بِالْاٰخِرَةِ هُمْ كَافِرُونَ qāla lā yatīkumā ṭaʿāmun tur'zaqānihi illā nabbatukumā bitawīlihi qabla an yatiyakumā dhālikumā mimmā ʿallamanī rabbī innī taraktu millata qawmin lā yu'minūna bil-lahi wahum bil-ākhirati hum kāfirūna Said he (Joseph): "There shall not come unto you the food which ye are fed with but I inform ye two of its interpretation before it cometh unto ye two; This is of what my Lord hath taught me; Verily I have forsaken the religion of the people who believe not in God, and of the hereafter, they are dis believers." Joseph wanted to be quick in interpreting the dreams for there was death for one of them. He first preached Islam, the correct faith in God, so…

item.title: Yusuf:38 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاتَّبَعْتُ مِلَّةَ ءَابَاءِي اِبْرَاهِیْمَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ مَا كَانَ لَنَا أَنْ نُشْرِكَ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ ذٰلِكَ مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى النَّاسِ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَشْكُرُونَ wa-ittabaʿtu millata ābāī ib'rāhīma wa-is'ḥāqa wayaʿqūba mā kāna lanā an nush'rika bil-lahi min shayin dhālika min faḍli l-lahi ʿalaynā waʿalā l-nāsi walākinna akthara l-nāsi lā yashkurūna I follow the creed of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. It is not for us to ascribe any partner to Allah. That is by virtue of Allah's grace upon us and upon all mankind, but most people do not give thanks.

item.title: Yusuf:38 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاتَّبَعْتُ مِلَّةَ ءَابَاءِي اِبْرَاهِیْمَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ مَا كَانَ لَنَا أَنْ نُشْرِكَ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ ذٰلِكَ مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى النَّاسِ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَشْكُرُونَ wa-ittabaʿtu millata ābāī ib'rāhīma wa-is'ḥāqa wayaʿqūba mā kāna lanā an nush'rika bil-lahi min shayin dhālika min faḍli l-lahi ʿalaynā waʿalā l-nāsi walākinna akthara l-nāsi lā yashkurūna And I have followed the religion of my fathers, Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub. And it was not for us to associate anything with Allah. That is from the favor of Allah upon us and upon the people, but most of the people are not grateful. See 12:37

item.title: Yusuf:38 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَاتَّبَعْتُ مِلَّةَ ءَابَاءِي اِبْرَاهِیْمَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ مَا كَانَ لَنَا أَنْ نُشْرِكَ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ ذٰلِكَ مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى النَّاسِ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَشْكُرُونَ wa-ittabaʿtu millata ābāī ib'rāhīma wa-is'ḥāqa wayaʿqūba mā kāna lanā an nush'rika bil-lahi min shayin dhālika min faḍli l-lahi ʿalaynā waʿalā l-nāsi walākinna akthara l-nāsi lā yashkurūna And I follow the religion of my fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; and it is not (lawful) for us to associate aught with God; This is by God's grace upon us and on mankind, but most people give not thanks. See 12:37

item.title: Yusuf:39 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاصَاحِبَيِ السِّجْنِ ءَأَرْبَابٌ مُتَفَرِّقُونَ خَيْرٌ أَمِ اللَّهُ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ yāṣāḥibayi l-sij'ni a-arbābun mutafarriqūna khayrun ami l-lahu l-wāḥidu l-qahāru O my prison mates! Are different masters better, or Allah, the One, the All-paramount?

item.title: Yusuf:39 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاصَاحِبَيِ السِّجْنِ ءَأَرْبَابٌ مُتَفَرِّقُونَ خَيْرٌ أَمِ اللَّهُ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ yāṣāḥibayi l-sij'ni a-arbābun mutafarriqūna khayrun ami l-lahu l-wāḥidu l-qahāru O (my) two companions of prison, are separate lords better or Allah, the One,1 the Prevailing?2 "O two companions of the prison! Are many different lords (gods) better or Allah, the One, the Irresistible? (12:39). "You do not worship besides Him but only names which you have named (forged) - you and your fathers - for which Allah has sent down no authority. The command is for none but Allah. He has commanded that you worship none but Him; that is the straight religion, but most men know not (12:40). Prophet Yusuf went on calling his two prison companions to worship Allah alone, without partners, and to reject whatever is being worshipped instead of Him like the idols, which were worshipped by…

item.title: Yusuf:39 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاصَاحِبَيِ السِّجْنِ ءَأَرْبَابٌ مُتَفَرِّقُونَ خَيْرٌ أَمِ اللَّهُ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ yāṣāḥibayi l-sij'ni a-arbābun mutafarriqūna khayrun ami l-lahu l-wāḥidu l-qahāru O' my (two) fellows of the prison! Are (many) lords differing from each other better or God the One, the All-Dominant? See 12:37

item.title: Yusuf:40 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلَّا أَسْمَاءً سَمَّيْتُمُوهَا أَنْتُمْ وَءَابَاؤُكُمْ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ إِنِ الْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ أَمَرَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوْۤا إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ ذٰلِكَ الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ mā taʿbudūna min dūnihi illā asmāan sammaytumūhā antum waābāukum mā anzala l-lahu bihā min sul'ṭānin ini l-ḥuk'mu illā lillahi amara allā taʿbudū illā iyyāhu dhālika l-dīnu l-qayimu walākinna akthara l-nāsi lā yaʿlamūna You do not worship besides Him but [mere] names that you and your fathers have coined, for which Allah has not sent down any authority. Sovereignty belongs only to Allah. He has commanded you to worship none except Him. That is the upright religion, but most people do not know.

item.title: Yusuf:40 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلَّا أَسْمَاءً سَمَّيْتُمُوهَا أَنْتُمْ وَءَابَاؤُكُمْ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ إِنِ الْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ أَمَرَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوْۤا إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ ذٰلِكَ الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ mā taʿbudūna min dūnihi illā asmāan sammaytumūhā antum waābāukum mā anzala l-lahu bihā min sul'ṭānin ini l-ḥuk'mu illā lillahi amara allā taʿbudū illā iyyāhu dhālika l-dīnu l-qayimu walākinna akthara l-nāsi lā yaʿlamūna You worship not besides Him except (mere) names you have named them,1 you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no evidence. Legislation is not but for Allah. He has commanded that you worship not except Him. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know. See 12:39

item.title: Yusuf:40 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: مَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلَّا أَسْمَاءً سَمَّيْتُمُوهَا أَنْتُمْ وَءَابَاؤُكُمْ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ إِنِ الْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ أَمَرَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوْۤا إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ ذٰلِكَ الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ mā taʿbudūna min dūnihi illā asmāan sammaytumūhā antum waābāukum mā anzala l-lahu bihā min sul'ṭānin ini l-ḥuk'mu illā lillahi amara allā taʿbudū illā iyyāhu dhālika l-dīnu l-qayimu walākinna akthara l-nāsi lā yaʿlamūna Ye worship not besides Him but (mere) names (Mere imaginary beings without any existence - or without any authority or hold as imagined.) which ye have named, ye and your fathers, God hath not sent down for them any authority; there is no judgment but God's; He hath bidden that ye worship not but unto Him; This is the right religion, but most people know (it) not. See 12:37

item.title: Yusuf:41 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاصَاحِبَيِ السِّجْنِ أَمَّا أَحَدُكُمَا فَيَسْقِي رَبَّهُ خَمْرًا وَأَمَّا الْءَاخَرُ فَيُصْلَبُ فَتَأْكُلُ الطَّيْرُ مِنْ رَأْسِهِ قُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ الَّذِي فِیْهِ تَسْتَفْتِيَانِ yāṣāḥibayi l-sij'ni ammā aḥadukumā fayasqī rabbahu khamran wa-ammā l-ākharu fayuṣ'labu fatakulu l-ṭayru min rasihi quḍiya l-amru alladhī fīhi tastaftiyāni O my prison mates! As for one of you, he will serve wine to his master, and as for the other, he will be crucified, and vultures will eat from his head. The matter about which you inquire has been decided.'

item.title: Yusuf:41 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاصَاحِبَيِ السِّجْنِ أَمَّا أَحَدُكُمَا فَيَسْقِي رَبَّهُ خَمْرًا وَأَمَّا الْءَاخَرُ فَيُصْلَبُ فَتَأْكُلُ الطَّيْرُ مِنْ رَأْسِهِ قُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ الَّذِي فِیْهِ تَسْتَفْتِيَانِ yāṣāḥibayi l-sij'ni ammā aḥadukumā fayasqī rabbahu khamran wa-ammā l-ākharu fayuṣ'labu fatakulu l-ṭayru min rasihi quḍiya l-amru alladhī fīhi tastaftiyāni O two companions of prison, as for one of you, he will give drink to his master of wine; but as for the other, he will be crucified, and the birds will eat from his head. The matter has been decreed about which you both inquire." O two companions of the prison! As for one of you, he will pour out wine for his master to drink; and as for the other, he will be crucified and birds will eat from his head. Thus is the case judged concerning which you both did inquire (12:41). The Interpretation of the Dreams Yusuf said:…

item.title: Yusuf:41 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يَاصَاحِبَيِ السِّجْنِ أَمَّا أَحَدُكُمَا فَيَسْقِي رَبَّهُ خَمْرًا وَأَمَّا الْءَاخَرُ فَيُصْلَبُ فَتَأْكُلُ الطَّيْرُ مِنْ رَأْسِهِ قُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ الَّذِي فِیْهِ تَسْتَفْتِيَانِ yāṣāḥibayi l-sij'ni ammā aḥadukumā fayasqī rabbahu khamran wa-ammā l-ākharu fayuṣ'labu fatakulu l-ṭayru min rasihi quḍiya l-amru alladhī fīhi tastaftiyāni O' my (two) fellows of the prison! As to one of you, he will pour out wine for his lord to drink; As for the other, he shall be crucified, so that the birds shall eat from his head. The matter is decreed about which ye two inquired. Note that the word 'Sahibi', i.e., my fellow or companion, has been used by Joseph in addressing polytheists. The mere the two fellow-prisoners who were polytheists. The mere use of the word 'Sahibi' can never mean that two fellows who were disbelievers in God were in any sense of the term the equals of…

item.title: Yusuf:42 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالَ لِلَّذِي ظَنَّ أَنَّهُ نَاجٍ مِنْهُمَا اذْكُرْنِي عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ فَأَنْسَاهُ الشَّيْطَانُ ذِكْرَ رَبِّهِ فَلَبِثَ فِي السِّجْنِ بِضْعَ سِنِينَ waqāla lilladhī ẓanna annahu nājin min'humā udh'kur'nī ʿinda rabbika fa-ansāhu l-shayṭānu dhik'ra rabbihi falabitha fī l-sij'ni biḍ'ʿa sinīna Then he said to the one whom he knew would be delivered from among the two: 'Mention me to your master.' But Satan caused him to forget mentioning [it] to his master. So he remained in the prison for several years.

item.title: Yusuf:42 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالَ لِلَّذِي ظَنَّ أَنَّهُ نَاجٍ مِنْهُمَا اذْكُرْنِي عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ فَأَنْسَاهُ الشَّيْطَانُ ذِكْرَ رَبِّهِ فَلَبِثَ فِي السِّجْنِ بِضْعَ سِنِينَ waqāla lilladhī ẓanna annahu nājin min'humā udh'kur'nī ʿinda rabbika fa-ansāhu l-shayṭānu dhik'ra rabbihi falabitha fī l-sij'ni biḍ'ʿa sinīna And he said to the one whom he knew would go free, "Mention me before your master." But Satan made him forget the mention (to) his master, and he (i.e., Yusuf) remained in prison several years. And he said to the one whom he knew to be saved: "Mention me to your king." But Shaytan made him forget to mention it to his master. So (Yusuf) stayed in prison a few (more) years (12:42). Yusuf Asks the King's Distiller to Mention Him to the King Yusuf knew that the distiller would be saved. So discretely, so that the other man's suspicion that he would…

item.title: Yusuf:42 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالَ لِلَّذِي ظَنَّ أَنَّهُ نَاجٍ مِنْهُمَا اذْكُرْنِي عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ فَأَنْسَاهُ الشَّيْطَانُ ذِكْرَ رَبِّهِ فَلَبِثَ فِي السِّجْنِ بِضْعَ سِنِينَ waqāla lilladhī ẓanna annahu nājin min'humā udh'kur'nī ʿinda rabbika fa-ansāhu l-shayṭānu dhik'ra rabbihi falabitha fī l-sij'ni biḍ'ʿa sinīna And he (Joseph.) said unto him whom he knew would be delivered of the two: "mention me unto thy lord;" (The King.) But the devil caused him (The fellow prisoner.) to forget mentioning (it) to his lord, (The King.) so he (Joseph.) remained in the prison a few years (more). Before the prisoners were released, Joseph had desired them to remind the King of him and since Joseph forgot God, his true Lord, and sought help from the King and not from God, he was made to stay in the prison a few more years. When Joseph was informed of the consequence of his…

item.title: Yusuf:43 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ اِنِّیْ أَرٰی سَبْعَ بَقَرَاتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ وَسَبْعَ سُنْبُلَاتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَاتٍ يَاأَيُّهَا الْمَلَأُ أَفْتُونِي فِي رُءْيَايَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ لِلرُّءْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ waqāla l-maliku innī arā sabʿa baqarātin simānin yakuluhunna sabʿun ʿijāfun wasabʿa sunbulātin khuḍ'rin wa-ukhara yābisātin yāayyuhā l-mala-u aftūnī fī ru'yāya in kuntum lilrru'yā taʿburūna [One day] the king said, 'I saw [in a dream] seven fat cows being devoured by seven lean ones, and seven green ears and [seven] others [that were] dry. O courtiers, give me your opinion about my dream, if you can interpret dreams.'

item.title: Yusuf:43 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ اِنِّیْ أَرٰی سَبْعَ بَقَرَاتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ وَسَبْعَ سُنْبُلَاتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَاتٍ يَاأَيُّهَا الْمَلَأُ أَفْتُونِي فِي رُءْيَايَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ لِلرُّءْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ waqāla l-maliku innī arā sabʿa baqarātin simānin yakuluhunna sabʿun ʿijāfun wasabʿa sunbulātin khuḍ'rin wa-ukhara yābisātin yāayyuhā l-mala-u aftūnī fī ru'yāya in kuntum lilrru'yā taʿburūna And (subsequently) the king said, "Indeed, I have seen (in a dream) seven fat cows being eaten by seven (that were) lean, and seven green spikes (of grain) and others (that were) dry. O eminent ones, explain to me my vision, if you should interpret visions." And the king (of Egypt) said: Verily, I saw (in a dream) seven fat cows, whom seven lean ones were devouring, and seven green ears of corn, and (seven) others dry. O notables! Explain to me my dream, if it be that you can interpret dreams…

item.title: Yusuf:43 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ اِنِّیْ أَرٰی سَبْعَ بَقَرَاتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ وَسَبْعَ سُنْبُلَاتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَاتٍ يَاأَيُّهَا الْمَلَأُ أَفْتُونِي فِي رُءْيَايَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ لِلرُّءْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ waqāla l-maliku innī arā sabʿa baqarātin simānin yakuluhunna sabʿun ʿijāfun wasabʿa sunbulātin khuḍ'rin wa-ukhara yābisātin yāayyuhā l-mala-u aftūnī fī ru'yāya in kuntum lilrru'yā taʿburūna And said the king "Verily, I did see in (dream) seven fat kine which seven lean ones devoured, and seven green ears and (seven) others dry; O' chiefs (of my court)! Explain (Opine.) ye unto me my dream, if ye can interpret a dream." When the chiefs, the great scholars who were experts in interpreting dreams got helpless against the confused nature of the dreams, the one of the two fellow-prisoners, (i.e., the Saqi), requested permission to go to the prison and get the correct interpretation from the one (i.e., Joseph) who…

item.title: Yusuf:44 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلَامٍ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِتَأْوِيلِ الْأَحْلَامِ بِعَالِمِينَ qālū aḍghāthu aḥlāmin wamā naḥnu bitawīli l-aḥlāmi biʿālimīna They said, '[These are] confused nightmares, and we do not know the interpretation of nightmares.'

item.title: Yusuf:44 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلَامٍ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِتَأْوِيلِ الْأَحْلَامِ بِعَالِمِينَ qālū aḍghāthu aḥlāmin wamā naḥnu bitawīli l-aḥlāmi biʿālimīna They said, "(It is but) a mixture of false dreams, and we are not learned in the interpretation of dreams." See 12:43

item.title: Yusuf:44 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلَامٍ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِتَأْوِيلِ الْأَحْلَامِ بِعَالِمِينَ qālū aḍghāthu aḥlāmin wamā naḥnu bitawīli l-aḥlāmi biʿālimīna Said they: "Confused (Fantastic – Jumbled.) dreams (are these)! and we know not the interpretation of such (confused) dreams." See 12:43

item.title: Yusuf:45 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالَ الَّذِي نَجَا مِنْهُمَا وَادَّكَرَ بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ أَنَا أُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِتَأْوِيلِهِ فَأَرْسِلُونِ waqāla alladhī najā min'humā wa-iddakara baʿda ummatin anā unabbi-ukum bitawīlihi fa-arsilūni Said the one of the two who had been delivered, remembering [Joseph] after a long time: 'I will inform you of its interpretation; so let me go [to meet Joseph in the prison].'

item.title: Yusuf:45 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالَ الَّذِي نَجَا مِنْهُمَا وَادَّكَرَ بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ أَنَا أُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِتَأْوِيلِهِ فَأَرْسِلُونِ waqāla alladhī najā min'humā wa-iddakara baʿda ummatin anā unabbi-ukum bitawīlihi fa-arsilūni But the one who was freed and remembered after a time said, "I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me forth." See 12:43

item.title: Yusuf:45 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالَ الَّذِي نَجَا مِنْهُمَا وَادَّكَرَ بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ أَنَا أُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِتَأْوِيلِهِ فَأَرْسِلُونِ waqāla alladhī najā min'humā wa-iddakara baʿda ummatin anā unabbi-ukum bitawīlihi fa-arsilūni And said he of the two who had been released, and re membered after a long (Arabic: 'Ummat' used here as time. Considerable lapse of time.) time; "I will expound unto you its interpretation, so let me go (to the prison)." See 12:43

item.title: Yusuf:46 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: يُوسُفُ أَيُّهَا الصِّدِّيقُ أَفْتِنَا فِي سَبْعِ بَقَرَاتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ وَسَبْعِ سُنْبُلَاتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَاتٍ لَعَلِّي أَرْجِعُ إِلَى النَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ yūsufu ayyuhā l-ṣidīqu aftinā fī sabʿi baqarātin simānin yakuluhunna sabʿun ʿijāfun wasabʿi sunbulātin khuḍ'rin wa-ukhara yābisātin laʿallī arjiʿu ilā l-nāsi laʿallahum yaʿlamūna 'Joseph,' [he said], 'O truthful one, give us your opinion concerning seven fat cows who are eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green ears and [seven] others dry, that I may return to the people so that they may know [the truth of the matter].'

item.title: Yusuf:46 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: يُوسُفُ أَيُّهَا الصِّدِّيقُ أَفْتِنَا فِي سَبْعِ بَقَرَاتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ وَسَبْعِ سُنْبُلَاتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَاتٍ لَعَلِّي أَرْجِعُ إِلَى النَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ yūsufu ayyuhā l-ṣidīqu aftinā fī sabʿi baqarātin simānin yakuluhunna sabʿun ʿijāfun wasabʿi sunbulātin khuḍ'rin wa-ukhara yābisātin laʿallī arjiʿu ilā l-nāsi laʿallahum yaʿlamūna (He said), "Yusuf, O man of truth, explain to us about seven fat cows eaten by seven (that were) lean, and seven green spikes (of grain) and others (that were) dry - that I may return to the people (i.e., the king and his court); perhaps they will know (about you)." See 12:43

item.title: Yusuf:46 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: يُوسُفُ أَيُّهَا الصِّدِّيقُ أَفْتِنَا فِي سَبْعِ بَقَرَاتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ وَسَبْعِ سُنْبُلَاتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَاتٍ لَعَلِّي أَرْجِعُ إِلَى النَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ yūsufu ayyuhā l-ṣidīqu aftinā fī sabʿi baqarātin simānin yakuluhunna sabʿun ʿijāfun wasabʿi sunbulātin khuḍ'rin wa-ukhara yābisātin laʿallī arjiʿu ilā l-nāsi laʿallahum yaʿlamūna Joseph! O' truthful (The term 'Siddeeq' can never be applicable to one who has ever believed in anything besides God.) one! expound thou unto us seven fat kine which seven lean ones devour, and seven ears green and seven (others) dry, that I may return unto the people so that they may know. The Saqi went into the prison and asked the interpretation of the dream from Joseph. Note that the address 'Siddeeq', the truthful one, is given to the one like Joseph the Apostle of God who never, not even once in his life had…

item.title: Yusuf:47 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ تَزْرَعُونَ سَبْعَ سِنِينَ دَأَبًا فَمَا حَصَدْتُمْ فَذَرُوهُ فِي سُنْبُلِهِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِمَّا تَأْكُلُونَ qāla tazraʿūna sabʿa sinīna da-aban famā ḥaṣadttum fadharūhu fī sunbulihi illā qalīlan mimmā takulūna He said, 'You will sow for seven consecutive years. Then leave in the ear whatever [grain] you harvest, except a little that you eat.

item.title: Yusuf:47 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ تَزْرَعُونَ سَبْعَ سِنِينَ دَأَبًا فَمَا حَصَدْتُمْ فَذَرُوهُ فِي سُنْبُلِهِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِمَّا تَأْكُلُونَ qāla tazraʿūna sabʿa sinīna da-aban famā ḥaṣadttum fadharūhu fī sunbulihi illā qalīlan mimmā takulūna (Yusuf) said, "You will plant for seven years consecutively; and what you harvest leave in its spikes, except a little from which you will eat. See 12:43

item.title: Yusuf:47 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ تَزْرَعُونَ سَبْعَ سِنِينَ دَأَبًا فَمَا حَصَدْتُمْ فَذَرُوهُ فِي سُنْبُلِهِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِمَّا تَأْكُلُونَ qāla tazraʿūna sabʿa sinīna da-aban famā ḥaṣadttum fadharūhu fī sunbulihi illā qalīlan mimmā takulūna Said (Joseph.) he: "Ye shall sow seven years as usual, but that which ye reap leave ye in its ears, except a little of which ye eat." Joseph advises the ruling authority to hoard the surplus of the foodstuff for the unseen emergencies in the interest of the people and how to preserve it so that it may not get rotten and useless. It is a lesson to the authorities to be always on guard against a possible famine which might overtake a country. (A.P.).

item.title: Yusuf:48 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ يَأْتِي مِنْ بَعْدِ ذٰلِكَ سَبْعٌ شِدَادٌ يَأْكُلْنَ مَا قَدَّمْتُمْ لَهُنَّ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِمَّا تُحْصِنُونَ thumma yatī min baʿdi dhālika sabʿun shidādun yakul'na mā qaddamtum lahunna illā qalīlan mimmā tuḥ'ṣinūna Then after that there will come seven hard years which will eat up whatever you have set aside for them —all except a little which you preserve [for seed].

item.title: Yusuf:48 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ يَأْتِي مِنْ بَعْدِ ذٰلِكَ سَبْعٌ شِدَادٌ يَأْكُلْنَ مَا قَدَّمْتُمْ لَهُنَّ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِمَّا تُحْصِنُونَ thumma yatī min baʿdi dhālika sabʿun shidādun yakul'na mā qaddamtum lahunna illā qalīlan mimmā tuḥ'ṣinūna Then will come after that seven difficult (years) which will consume what you advanced (i.e., saved) for them, except a little from which you will store. See 12:43

item.title: Yusuf:48 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ يَأْتِي مِنْ بَعْدِ ذٰلِكَ سَبْعٌ شِدَادٌ يَأْكُلْنَ مَا قَدَّمْتُمْ لَهُنَّ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِمَّا تُحْصِنُونَ thumma yatī min baʿdi dhālika sabʿun shidādun yakul'na mā qaddamtum lahunna illā qalīlan mimmā tuḥ'ṣinūna Then shall come after that seven years of hardship (famine), which shall eat away all that ye have laid by beforehand for them, except a little of which ye have preserved. (For seeds.) See 12:47

item.title: Yusuf:49 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ يَأْتِي مِنْ بَعْدِ ذٰلِكَ عَامٌ فِیْهِ يُغَاثُ النَّاسُ وَفِيهِ يَعْصِرُونَ thumma yatī min baʿdi dhālika ʿāmun fīhi yughāthu l-nāsu wafīhi yaʿṣirūna Then after that there will come a year wherein the people will be granted relief and provided with rains therein.1

item.title: Yusuf:49 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ يَأْتِي مِنْ بَعْدِ ذٰلِكَ عَامٌ فِیْهِ يُغَاثُ النَّاسُ وَفِيهِ يَعْصِرُونَ thumma yatī min baʿdi dhālika ʿāmun fīhi yughāthu l-nāsu wafīhi yaʿṣirūna Then will come after that a year in which the people will be given rain and in which they will press (olives and grapes)." See 12:43

item.title: Yusuf:49 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ثُمَّ يَأْتِي مِنْ بَعْدِ ذٰلِكَ عَامٌ فِیْهِ يُغَاثُ النَّاسُ وَفِيهِ يَعْصِرُونَ thumma yatī min baʿdi dhālika ʿāmun fīhi yughāthu l-nāsu wafīhi yaʿṣirūna Then will come after that a year people will have abundant rain and in having it they will press wine. See 12:47

item.title: Yusuf:50 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ ائْتُونِي بِهِ فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُ الرَّسُولُ قَالَ ارْجِعْ إِلَى رَبِّكَ فَسْءَلْهُ مَا بَالُ النِّسْوَةِ اللَّاتِي قَطَّعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ إِنَّ رَبِّي بِكَيْدِهِنَّ عَلِیْمٌ waqāla l-maliku i'tūnī bihi falammā jāahu l-rasūlu qāla ir'jiʿ ilā rabbika fasalhu mā bālu l-nis'wati allātī qaṭṭaʿna aydiyahunna inna rabbī bikaydihinna ʿalīmun The king said, 'Bring him to me!' When the messenger came to him,1 he said, 'Go back to your master, and ask him about the affair of women who cut their hands. My Lord is indeed well aware of their stratagems.'

item.title: Yusuf:50 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ ائْتُونِي بِهِ فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُ الرَّسُولُ قَالَ ارْجِعْ إِلَى رَبِّكَ فَسْءَلْهُ مَا بَالُ النِّسْوَةِ اللَّاتِي قَطَّعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ إِنَّ رَبِّي بِكَيْدِهِنَّ عَلِیْمٌ waqāla l-maliku i'tūnī bihi falammā jāahu l-rasūlu qāla ir'jiʿ ilā rabbika fasalhu mā bālu l-nis'wati allātī qaṭṭaʿna aydiyahunna inna rabbī bikaydihinna ʿalīmun And the king said, "Bring him to me." But when the messenger came to him, (Yusuf) said, "Return to your master and ask him what is the case of the women who cut their hands. Indeed, my Lord is Knowing of their plan." And the king said: Bring him to me." But when the messenger came to him, (Yusuf) said: "Return to your king and ask him, 'What happened to the women who cut their hands Surely, my Lord (Allah) is Well-Aware of their plot.' (12:50). (The king) said (to the women): "What was your affair…

item.title: Yusuf:50 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ ائْتُونِي بِهِ فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُ الرَّسُولُ قَالَ ارْجِعْ إِلَى رَبِّكَ فَسْءَلْهُ مَا بَالُ النِّسْوَةِ اللَّاتِي قَطَّعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ إِنَّ رَبِّي بِكَيْدِهِنَّ عَلِیْمٌ waqāla l-maliku i'tūnī bihi falammā jāahu l-rasūlu qāla ir'jiʿ ilā rabbika fasalhu mā bālu l-nis'wati allātī qaṭṭaʿna aydiyahunna inna rabbī bikaydihinna ʿalīmun And said the king: "Bring him (Joseph.) unto me!" So when the messenger came unto him, said he (Joseph): "Go thou back unto thy lord and ask him, what is the matter with the women (Joseph when summoned he sent word to the Aziz to first enquire from the women about the guilt. The Aziz called the women and enquired.) who cut their hands; Verily my Lord knoweth their guile." When the Saqi conveyed the interpretation to the King, the King got extremely pleased and wanted to hear the interpretation directly from the prisoner (Joseph) and…

item.title: Yusuf:51 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ مَا خَطْبُكُنَّ إِذْ رَاوَدْتُنَّ يُوسُفَ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ قُلْنَ حَاشَ لِلَّهِ مَا عَلِمْنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنْ سُوءٍ قَالَتِ امْرَأَتُ الْعَزِيزِ الْءَانَ حَصْحَصَ الْحَقُّ أَنَا رَاوَدْتُهُ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ وَإِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ qāla mā khaṭbukunna idh rāwadttunna yūsufa ʿan nafsihi qul'na ḥāsha lillahi mā ʿalim'nā ʿalayhi min sūin qālati im'ra-atu l-ʿazīzi l-āna ḥaṣḥaṣa l-ḥaqu anā rāwadttuhu ʿan nafsihi wa-innahu lamina l-ṣādiqīna The king said, 'What was your business, women, when you solicited Joseph?' They said, 'Heaven be praised! We know of no evil in him.' The prince's wife said, 'Now the truth has come to light! It was I who solicited him, and he is indeed telling the truth.'

item.title: Yusuf:51 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ مَا خَطْبُكُنَّ إِذْ رَاوَدْتُنَّ يُوسُفَ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ قُلْنَ حَاشَ لِلَّهِ مَا عَلِمْنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنْ سُوءٍ قَالَتِ امْرَأَتُ الْعَزِيزِ الْءَانَ حَصْحَصَ الْحَقُّ أَنَا رَاوَدْتُهُ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ وَإِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ qāla mā khaṭbukunna idh rāwadttunna yūsufa ʿan nafsihi qul'na ḥāsha lillahi mā ʿalim'nā ʿalayhi min sūin qālati im'ra-atu l-ʿazīzi l-āna ḥaṣḥaṣa l-ḥaqu anā rāwadttuhu ʿan nafsihi wa-innahu lamina l-ṣādiqīna Said (the king to the women), "What was your condition when you sought to seduce Yusuf?" They said, "Perfect is Allah!1 We know about him no evil." The wife of al-ʿAzeez said, "Now the truth has become evident. It was I who sought to seduce him, and indeed, he is of the truthful. See 12:50

item.title: Yusuf:51 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ مَا خَطْبُكُنَّ إِذْ رَاوَدْتُنَّ يُوسُفَ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ قُلْنَ حَاشَ لِلَّهِ مَا عَلِمْنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنْ سُوءٍ قَالَتِ امْرَأَتُ الْعَزِيزِ الْءَانَ حَصْحَصَ الْحَقُّ أَنَا رَاوَدْتُهُ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ وَإِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ qāla mā khaṭbukunna idh rāwadttunna yūsufa ʿan nafsihi qul'na ḥāsha lillahi mā ʿalim'nā ʿalayhi min sūin qālati im'ra-atu l-ʿazīzi l-āna ḥaṣḥaṣa l-ḥaqu anā rāwadttuhu ʿan nafsihi wa-innahu lamina l-ṣādiqīna Said the king (unto the women) what was the matter with you when ye sought to seduce Joseph from his (pure) self?" Said (replied) the women! "Hasha-lillah (Far from God is every imperfection) we know not any evil against him!" Said the Aziz's (Zulaikha Confessed.) wife: "Now the truth hath become manifest, I (it was who) sought to seduce him from his (pure) self; And verily he is of the truthful ones! See 12:50

item.title: Yusuf:52 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: ذٰلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ أَنِّي لَمْ أَخُنْهُ بِالْغَيْبِ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِي كَيْدَ الْخَائِنِينَ dhālika liyaʿlama annī lam akhun'hu bil-ghaybi wa-anna l-laha lā yahdī kayda l-khāinīna [Joseph said], [I initiated] this [inquiry], that he1 may know that I did not betray him in his absence, and that Allah does not further the schemes of the treacherous.

item.title: Yusuf:52 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: ذٰلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ أَنِّي لَمْ أَخُنْهُ بِالْغَيْبِ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِي كَيْدَ الْخَائِنِينَ dhālika liyaʿlama annī lam akhun'hu bil-ghaybi wa-anna l-laha lā yahdī kayda l-khāinīna That is so he (i.e., al-ʿAzeez) will know that I did not betray him in (his) absence and that Allah does not guide the plan of betrayers. See 12:50

item.title: Yusuf:52 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: ذٰلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ أَنِّي لَمْ أَخُنْهُ بِالْغَيْبِ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِي كَيْدَ الْخَائِنِينَ dhālika liyaʿlama annī lam akhun'hu bil-ghaybi wa-anna l-laha lā yahdī kayda l-khāinīna (Said Joseph) This (Inquiry I caused) that he (the King) might know that I have not been unfaithful unto him in his absence, and that God guideth not the guile of the unfaithful ones. See 12:50

item.title: Yusuf:53 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أُبَرِّئُ نَفْسِي إِنَّ النَّفْسَ لَأَمَّارَةٌ بِالسُّوءِ إِلَّا مَا رَحِمَ رَبِّي إِنَّ رَبِّي غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ wamā ubarri-u nafsī inna l-nafsa la-ammāratun bil-sūi illā mā raḥima rabbī inna rabbī ghafūrun raḥīmun Yet I do not absolve my [own carnal] soul, for the [carnal] soul indeed prompts [men] to evil, except inasmuch as my Lord has mercy. Indeed my Lord is all-forgiving, all-merciful.'

item.title: Yusuf:53 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أُبَرِّئُ نَفْسِي إِنَّ النَّفْسَ لَأَمَّارَةٌ بِالسُّوءِ إِلَّا مَا رَحِمَ رَبِّي إِنَّ رَبِّي غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ wamā ubarri-u nafsī inna l-nafsa la-ammāratun bil-sūi illā mā raḥima rabbī inna rabbī ghafūrun raḥīmun And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil, except those upon which my Lord has mercy. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful."1 See 12:50

item.title: Yusuf:53 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَمَا أُبَرِّئُ نَفْسِي إِنَّ النَّفْسَ لَأَمَّارَةٌ بِالسُّوءِ إِلَّا مَا رَحِمَ رَبِّي إِنَّ رَبِّي غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ wamā ubarri-u nafsī inna l-nafsa la-ammāratun bil-sūi illā mā raḥima rabbī inna rabbī ghafūrun raḥīmun I exculpate not myself, verily (one's) self is wont to bid (him to) evil, except such as my Lord hath had mercy on; Verily my Lord is Oft-Forgiving, All- Merciful. Some say that the wordings of this verse refer to the confession of Zulaikha acknowledging the fault to be her own and declaring Joseph as innocent. 'Ammarah' - the urge in man which commands the individual to do evil. If the individual fights out this urge successfully with his faith in God and his determination to do only good, the strength of the will is increased and the individual, he or she, remains safe against the strong attractions from the…

item.title: Yusuf:54 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ ائْتُونِي بِهِ أَسْتَخْلِصْهُ لِنَفْسِي فَلَمَّا كَلَّمَهُ قَالَ إِنَّكَ الْيَوْمَ لَدَيْنَا مَكِينٌ أَمِينٌ waqāla l-maliku i'tūnī bihi astakhliṣ'hu linafsī falammā kallamahu qāla innaka l-yawma ladaynā makīnun amīnun The king said, 'Bring him to me, I will make him my favourite.' Then, when he had spoken with him, he said, 'Indeed today [onwards] you will be honoured and trustworthy with us.'

item.title: Yusuf:54 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ ائْتُونِي بِهِ أَسْتَخْلِصْهُ لِنَفْسِي فَلَمَّا كَلَّمَهُ قَالَ إِنَّكَ الْيَوْمَ لَدَيْنَا مَكِينٌ أَمِينٌ waqāla l-maliku i'tūnī bihi astakhliṣ'hu linafsī falammā kallamahu qāla innaka l-yawma ladaynā makīnun amīnun And the king said, "Bring him to me; I will appoint him exclusively for myself." And when he spoke to him, he said, "Indeed, you are today established (in position) and trusted." And the king said: "Bring him to me that I may attach him to my person." Then, when he spoke to him, he said: "Verily, this day, you are with us high in rank and fully trusted (12:54). Yusuf said: "Set me over the storehouses of the land; I will indeed guard them with full knowledge (12:55). Yusuf's Rank with the King of Egypt Allah states that when he became aware of Yusuf's innocence and his innocense of what he…

item.title: Yusuf:54 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ ائْتُونِي بِهِ أَسْتَخْلِصْهُ لِنَفْسِي فَلَمَّا كَلَّمَهُ قَالَ إِنَّكَ الْيَوْمَ لَدَيْنَا مَكِينٌ أَمِينٌ waqāla l-maliku i'tūnī bihi astakhliṣ'hu linafsī falammā kallamahu qāla innaka l-yawma ladaynā makīnun amīnun And the king said (Ordered) "Bring him (Joseph.) unto me, I will exclude him for (service to) my (own) self!" So when he had spoken unto him: he (the king) said: "Verily thou art (from) this day in our (own) presence, accommodated (honourably) (as) a Trusted one!" Thus, Joseph became the dearest, the most honoured and the nearest in position to the king - and was placed in charge of the treasuries of the land. Joseph ordered that all people should start and carry on cultivation of foodgrains as much as they could. Only the grain fit to be reaped were taken away from the plants and the rest were left in…

item.title: Yusuf:55 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ اجْعَلْنِي عَلَى خَزَائِنِ الْأَرْضِ اِنِّیْ حَفِيظٌ عَلِیْمٌ qāla ij'ʿalnī ʿalā khazāini l-arḍi innī ḥafīẓun ʿalīmun He said, 'Put me in charge of the country's granaries. I am indeed fastidious [and] well-informed.'

item.title: Yusuf:55 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ اجْعَلْنِي عَلَى خَزَائِنِ الْأَرْضِ اِنِّیْ حَفِيظٌ عَلِیْمٌ qāla ij'ʿalnī ʿalā khazāini l-arḍi innī ḥafīẓun ʿalīmun (Yusuf) said, "Appoint me over the storehouses of the land. Indeed, I will be a knowing guardian." See 12:54

item.title: Yusuf:55 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ اجْعَلْنِي عَلَى خَزَائِنِ الْأَرْضِ اِنِّیْ حَفِيظٌ عَلِیْمٌ qāla ij'ʿalnī ʿalā khazāini l-arḍi innī ḥafīẓun ʿalīmun Said he: (Joseph.) "Set me (in authority) over the treasuries of the land; Verily I am a (faithful) keeper, knowing well (its management)." When to be in charge of a terrestrial treasury requires the knowledge and ability as to how to manage it, what about to be in charge of guiding mankind towards the ultimate aim and the object of creation. (A.P.).

item.title: Yusuf:56 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَكَذٰلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِي الْأَرْضِ يَتَبَوَّأُ مِنْهَا حَيْثُ يَشَاءُ نُصِيبُ بِرَحْمَتِنَا مَنْ نَشَاءُ وَلَا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ wakadhālika makkannā liyūsufa fī l-arḍi yatabawwa-u min'hā ḥaythu yashāu nuṣību biraḥmatinā man nashāu walā nuḍīʿu ajra l-muḥ'sinīna That is how We established Joseph in the land that he may settle in it wherever he wished. We confer Our mercy on whomever We wish, and We do not waste the reward of the virtuous.

item.title: Yusuf:56 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَكَذٰلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِي الْأَرْضِ يَتَبَوَّأُ مِنْهَا حَيْثُ يَشَاءُ نُصِيبُ بِرَحْمَتِنَا مَنْ نَشَاءُ وَلَا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ wakadhālika makkannā liyūsufa fī l-arḍi yatabawwa-u min'hā ḥaythu yashāu nuṣību biraḥmatinā man nashāu walā nuḍīʿu ajra l-muḥ'sinīna And thus We established Yusuf in the land to settle therein wherever he willed. We touch with Our mercy whom We will, and We do not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good. Thus did We give full authority to Yusuf in the land, to take possession therein, when or where he likes. We bestow of Our mercy on whom We will, and We make not to be lost the reward of the good doers (12:56). And verily, the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believed and had Taqwa (12:57). Yusuf's Reign in Egypt Allah said next: وَكَذَٰلِكَ مَكَّنَّا…

item.title: Yusuf:56 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَكَذٰلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِي الْأَرْضِ يَتَبَوَّأُ مِنْهَا حَيْثُ يَشَاءُ نُصِيبُ بِرَحْمَتِنَا مَنْ نَشَاءُ وَلَا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ wakadhālika makkannā liyūsufa fī l-arḍi yatabawwa-u min'hā ḥaythu yashāu nuṣību biraḥmatinā man nashāu walā nuḍīʿu ajra l-muḥ'sinīna Thus We did establish Joseph in the land; to take possession therein as he pleased; We do bestow Our mercy on whomsoever We will, and We waste not the recompense of the doers of good. See 12:54

item.title: Yusuf:57 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَأَجْرُ الْاٰخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لِلَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا وَكَانُوْۤا يَتَّقُونَ wala-ajru l-ākhirati khayrun lilladhīna āmanū wakānū yattaqūna And the reward of the Hereafter is surely better for those who have faith and are Godwary.

item.title: Yusuf:57 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَأَجْرُ الْاٰخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لِلَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا وَكَانُوْۤا يَتَّقُونَ wala-ajru l-ākhirati khayrun lilladhīna āmanū wakānū yattaqūna And the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believed and were fearing Allah. See 12:56

item.title: Yusuf:57 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَأَجْرُ الْاٰخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لِلَّذِينَ اٰمَنُوْا وَكَانُوْۤا يَتَّقُونَ wala-ajru l-ākhirati khayrun lilladhīna āmanū wakānū yattaqūna And certainly the recompense of the hereafter is (much) better for those who believe and guard (themselves) against evil. See 12:54

item.title: Yusuf:58 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَاءَ إِخْوَةُ يُوسُفَ فَدَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ فَعَرَفَهُمْ وَهُمْ لَهُ مُنْكِرُونَ wajāa ikh'watu yūsufa fadakhalū ʿalayhi faʿarafahum wahum lahu munkirūna [After some years] the brothers of Joseph came and entered his presence. He recognized them, but they did not recognize him.

item.title: Yusuf:58 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَاءَ إِخْوَةُ يُوسُفَ فَدَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ فَعَرَفَهُمْ وَهُمْ لَهُ مُنْكِرُونَ wajāa ikh'watu yūsufa fadakhalū ʿalayhi faʿarafahum wahum lahu munkirūna And the brothers of Yusuf came (seeking food), and they entered upon him; and he recognized them, but he was to them unknown.1 And Yusuf's brethren came and they entered unto him, and he recognized them, but they recognized him not (12:58). And when he furnished them with their provisions, he said: Bring me a brother of yours from your father. See you not that I give full measure, and that I am the best of the hosts? (12:59). "But if you bring him not to me, there shall be no measure (of corn) for you with me, nor shall you come near me (12:60). They said: "We shall try to get permission (for him) from his father, and verily, we shall…

item.title: Yusuf:58 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَجَاءَ إِخْوَةُ يُوسُفَ فَدَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ فَعَرَفَهُمْ وَهُمْ لَهُ مُنْكِرُونَ wajāa ikh'watu yūsufa fadakhalū ʿalayhi faʿarafahum wahum lahu munkirūna And came the brothers of Joseph and entered they unto him, (Joseph.) and he knew them but (While.) they knew (Recognise.) him (Joseph.) not. When Canaan also got affected by the famine, people there also became helpless. At last, the sons of Jacob approached Jacob and said, "Father, we hear that the king of Egypt is reported to be a very kind and very charitable man, helping the famine-stricken people and hence we seek thy permission to got to Egypt and try there our luck and get some grain if possible". Jacob permitted but kept Bin-Yamin, the brother of Joseph with him for he felt consoled by the presence of the boy in the absence of Joseph. The party of the ten…

item.title: Yusuf:59 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُمْ بِجَهَازِهِمْ قَالَ ائْتُونِي بِأَخٍ لَكُمْ مِنْ أَبِيكُمْ أَلَا تَرَوْنَ أَنِّي أُوفِي الْكَيْلَ وَأَنَا خَيْرُ الْمُنْزِلِينَ walammā jahhazahum bijahāzihim qāla i'tūnī bi-akhin lakum min abīkum alā tarawna annī ūfī l-kayla wa-anā khayru l-munzilīna When he had furnished them with their provision, he said, 'Bring me a brother that you have through your father. Do you not see that I give the full measure and that I am the best of hosts?

item.title: Yusuf:59 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُمْ بِجَهَازِهِمْ قَالَ ائْتُونِي بِأَخٍ لَكُمْ مِنْ أَبِيكُمْ أَلَا تَرَوْنَ أَنِّي أُوفِي الْكَيْلَ وَأَنَا خَيْرُ الْمُنْزِلِينَ walammā jahhazahum bijahāzihim qāla i'tūnī bi-akhin lakum min abīkum alā tarawna annī ūfī l-kayla wa-anā khayru l-munzilīna And when he had furnished them with their supplies, he said, "Bring me a brother of yours from your father.1 Do you not see that I give full measure and that I am the best of accommodators? See 12:58

item.title: Yusuf:59 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُمْ بِجَهَازِهِمْ قَالَ ائْتُونِي بِأَخٍ لَكُمْ مِنْ أَبِيكُمْ أَلَا تَرَوْنَ أَنِّي أُوفِي الْكَيْلَ وَأَنَا خَيْرُ الْمُنْزِلِينَ walammā jahhazahum bijahāzihim qāla i'tūnī bi-akhin lakum min abīkum alā tarawna annī ūfī l-kayla wa-anā khayru l-munzilīna And when he (Joseph.) hath furnished them with their provision, said he (unto them): "Bring ye unto me a brother of yours from your father; See ye not that I give full measure? and that I am the best of hosts?" Bin-Yamin (Benjamin) was detained by Jacob to remain with him and the ten brothers had brought a camel to carry his share of the grain. Joseph said that the supply would be according to the number of the men that came demanding it and not according to the number of the camels that people come with and thus they were told to bring their brother…

item.title: Yusuf:60 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِنْ لَمْ تَأْتُونِي بِهِ فَلَا كَيْلَ لَكُمْ عِنْدِي وَلَا تَقْرَبُونِ fa-in lam tatūnī bihi falā kayla lakum ʿindī walā taqrabūni But if you do not bring him to me, then there will be no rations for you with me, and don't [ever] come near me.'

item.title: Yusuf:60 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِنْ لَمْ تَأْتُونِي بِهِ فَلَا كَيْلَ لَكُمْ عِنْدِي وَلَا تَقْرَبُونِ fa-in lam tatūnī bihi falā kayla lakum ʿindī walā taqrabūni But if you do not bring him to me, no measure will there be (hereafter) for you from me, nor will you approach me." See 12:58

item.title: Yusuf:60 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَإِنْ لَمْ تَأْتُونِي بِهِ فَلَا كَيْلَ لَكُمْ عِنْدِي وَلَا تَقْرَبُونِ fa-in lam tatūnī bihi falā kayla lakum ʿindī walā taqrabūni But if ye bring him not unto me, then there shall be no measure (of corn) for you with me, nor shall ye (even) come near me. See 12:59

item.title: Yusuf:61 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا سَنُرَاوِدُ عَنْهُ أَبَاهُ وَإِنَّا لَفَاعِلُونَ qālū sanurāwidu ʿanhu abāhu wa-innā lafāʿilūna They said, 'We will solicit him from his father. [That] we will surely do.'

item.title: Yusuf:61 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا سَنُرَاوِدُ عَنْهُ أَبَاهُ وَإِنَّا لَفَاعِلُونَ qālū sanurāwidu ʿanhu abāhu wa-innā lafāʿilūna They said, "We will attempt to dissuade his father from (keeping) him, and indeed, we will do (it)." See 12:58

item.title: Yusuf:61 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا سَنُرَاوِدُ عَنْهُ أَبَاهُ وَإِنَّا لَفَاعِلُونَ qālū sanurāwidu ʿanhu abāhu wa-innā lafāʿilūna They said: "We will seek to get him from his father, and verily We certainly shall do it." See 12:59

item.title: Yusuf:62 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالَ لِفِتْيَانِهِ اجْعَلُوْۤا بِضَاعَتَهُمْ فِي رِحَالِهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْرِفُونَهَا إِذَا انْقَلَبُوا إِلَى أَهْلِهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ waqāla lifit'yānihi ij'ʿalū biḍāʿatahum fī riḥālihim laʿallahum yaʿrifūnahā idhā inqalabū ilā ahlihim laʿallahum yarjiʿūna He said to his servants, 'Put their money in their saddlebags. Maybe they will recognize it when they return to their folks, and maybe they will come back [again].'

item.title: Yusuf:62 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالَ لِفِتْيَانِهِ اجْعَلُوْۤا بِضَاعَتَهُمْ فِي رِحَالِهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْرِفُونَهَا إِذَا انْقَلَبُوا إِلَى أَهْلِهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ waqāla lifit'yānihi ij'ʿalū biḍāʿatahum fī riḥālihim laʿallahum yaʿrifūnahā idhā inqalabū ilā ahlihim laʿallahum yarjiʿūna And (Yusuf) said to his servants, "Put their merchandise1 into their saddlebags so they might recognize it when they have gone back to their people that perhaps they will (again) return." See 12:58

item.title: Yusuf:62 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالَ لِفِتْيَانِهِ اجْعَلُوْۤا بِضَاعَتَهُمْ فِي رِحَالِهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْرِفُونَهَا إِذَا انْقَلَبُوا إِلَى أَهْلِهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ waqāla lifit'yānihi ij'ʿalū biḍāʿatahum fī riḥālihim laʿallahum yaʿrifūnahā idhā inqalabū ilā ahlihim laʿallahum yarjiʿūna And said he (Joseph.) unto his servants: "Put their goods (Money - or the goods they had brought to barter.) into their saddle-bags that they may perceive it when they return unto their family, so that they may come back." Joseph ordered the slaves who measured the grain to the people to place the things which Joseph's brothers had given as the price of the wheat in their own bags, without their knowledge, so that when after reaching their destination they would see the price of the grain had somehow been returned to them along with the supply and they would surely return.

item.title: Yusuf:63 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا رَجَعُوْۤا إِلَى أَبِيهِمْ قَالُوْا يَاأَبَانَا مُنِعَ مِنَّا الْكَيْلُ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا أَخَانَا نَكْتَلْ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحَافِظُونَ falammā rajaʿū ilā abīhim qālū yāabānā muniʿa minnā l-kaylu fa-arsil maʿanā akhānā naktal wa-innā lahu laḥāfiẓūna So when they returned to their father, they said, 'Father, the measure has been withheld from us, so let our brother go with us so that we may obtain the measure, and we will indeed take [good] care of him.'

item.title: Yusuf:63 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا رَجَعُوْۤا إِلَى أَبِيهِمْ قَالُوْا يَاأَبَانَا مُنِعَ مِنَّا الْكَيْلُ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا أَخَانَا نَكْتَلْ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحَافِظُونَ falammā rajaʿū ilā abīhim qālū yāabānā muniʿa minnā l-kaylu fa-arsil maʿanā akhānā naktal wa-innā lahu laḥāfiẓūna So when they returned to their father, they said, "O our father, (further) measure has been denied to us, so send with us our brother (that) we will be given measure. And indeed, we will be his guardians." So, when they returned to their father, they said: "O our father! No more measure of grain shall we get (unless we take our brother). So send our brother with us, and we shall get our measure and truly, we will guard him (12:63). He said: "Can I entrust him to you except as I entrusted his brother (Yusuf) to you aforetime? But Allah is the Best to guard, and…

item.title: Yusuf:63 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا رَجَعُوْۤا إِلَى أَبِيهِمْ قَالُوْا يَاأَبَانَا مُنِعَ مِنَّا الْكَيْلُ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا أَخَانَا نَكْتَلْ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحَافِظُونَ falammā rajaʿū ilā abīhim qālū yāabānā muniʿa minnā l-kaylu fa-arsil maʿanā akhānā naktal wa-innā lahu laḥāfiẓūna So when they returned unto their father, said they: "O' our father! The measure is denied unto us, so send with us our ('Bin-Yamin' (Benjamin).) brother, so that we may get the measure: And verily, certainly we will we guard him (well)." See 12:62

item.title: Yusuf:64 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ هَلْ ءَامَنُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ إِلَّا كَمَا أَمِنْتُكُمْ عَلَى أَخِيهِ مِنْ قَبْلُ فَاللَّهُ خَيْرٌ حَافِظًا وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ qāla hal āmanukum ʿalayhi illā kamā amintukum ʿalā akhīhi min qablu fal-lahu khayrun ḥāfiẓan wahuwa arḥamu l-rāḥimīna He said, 'Should I trust you with him just as I trusted you with his brother before? Yet Allah is the best of protectors, and He is the most merciful of merciful ones.'

item.title: Yusuf:64 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ هَلْ ءَامَنُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ إِلَّا كَمَا أَمِنْتُكُمْ عَلَى أَخِيهِ مِنْ قَبْلُ فَاللَّهُ خَيْرٌ حَافِظًا وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ qāla hal āmanukum ʿalayhi illā kamā amintukum ʿalā akhīhi min qablu fal-lahu khayrun ḥāfiẓan wahuwa arḥamu l-rāḥimīna He said, "Should I entrust you with him except (under coercion) as I entrusted you with his brother before? But Allah is the best guardian, and He is the most merciful of the merciful." See 12:63

item.title: Yusuf:64 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ هَلْ ءَامَنُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ إِلَّا كَمَا أَمِنْتُكُمْ عَلَى أَخِيهِ مِنْ قَبْلُ فَاللَّهُ خَيْرٌ حَافِظًا وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ qāla hal āmanukum ʿalayhi illā kamā amintukum ʿalā akhīhi min qablu fal-lahu khayrun ḥāfiẓan wahuwa arḥamu l-rāḥimīna He said: "Can I trust him unto you except as I entrusted his (Joseph.) brother unto you aforetime? but God is the Best Guard, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful ones." Jacob wanted his sons to realise that their undertaking to guardianship had no value with him whatsoever. He entrusted them in this case the same as he did in the case of Joseph before, and at that time also he did not attach value to their undertaking; he trusted only God. (A.P.).

item.title: Yusuf:65 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَمَّا فَتَحُوْۤا مَتَاعَهُمْ وَجَدُوْۤا بِضَاعَتَهُمْ رُدَّتْ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالُوْا يَاأَبَانَا مَا نَبْغِي هَذِهِ بِضَاعَتُنَا رُدَّتْ إِلَيْنَا وَنَمِيرُ أَهْلَنَا وَنَحْفَظُ أَخَانَا وَنَزْدَادُ كَيْلَ بَعِيرٍ ذٰلِكَ كَيْلٌ يَسِيرٌ walammā fataḥū matāʿahum wajadū biḍāʿatahum ruddat ilayhim qālū yāabānā mā nabghī hādhihi biḍāʿatunā ruddat ilaynā wanamīru ahlanā wanaḥfaẓu akhānā wanazdādu kayla baʿīrin dhālika kaylun yasīrun And when they opened their baggage, they found their money restored to them. They said, 'Father, what [more] do we want?! This is our money, restored to us! We will get provisions for our family and take care of our brother, and add another camel-load of rations. These are meagre rations.'

item.title: Yusuf:65 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَمَّا فَتَحُوْۤا مَتَاعَهُمْ وَجَدُوْۤا بِضَاعَتَهُمْ رُدَّتْ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالُوْا يَاأَبَانَا مَا نَبْغِي هَذِهِ بِضَاعَتُنَا رُدَّتْ إِلَيْنَا وَنَمِيرُ أَهْلَنَا وَنَحْفَظُ أَخَانَا وَنَزْدَادُ كَيْلَ بَعِيرٍ ذٰلِكَ كَيْلٌ يَسِيرٌ walammā fataḥū matāʿahum wajadū biḍāʿatahum ruddat ilayhim qālū yāabānā mā nabghī hādhihi biḍāʿatunā ruddat ilaynā wanamīru ahlanā wanaḥfaẓu akhānā wanazdādu kayla baʿīrin dhālika kaylun yasīrun And when they opened their baggage, they found their merchandise returned to them. They said, "O our father, what (more) could we desire? This is our merchandise returned to us. And we will obtain supplies (i.e., food) for our family and protect our brother and obtain an increase of a camel's load; that is an easy measurement."1 And when they opened their bags, they found their money had been returned to them. They said: "O our father! What (more) can we desire? This, our money has been returned to us;…

item.title: Yusuf:65 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَمَّا فَتَحُوْۤا مَتَاعَهُمْ وَجَدُوْۤا بِضَاعَتَهُمْ رُدَّتْ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالُوْا يَاأَبَانَا مَا نَبْغِي هَذِهِ بِضَاعَتُنَا رُدَّتْ إِلَيْنَا وَنَمِيرُ أَهْلَنَا وَنَحْفَظُ أَخَانَا وَنَزْدَادُ كَيْلَ بَعِيرٍ ذٰلِكَ كَيْلٌ يَسِيرٌ walammā fataḥū matāʿahum wajadū biḍāʿatahum ruddat ilayhim qālū yāabānā mā nabghī hādhihi biḍāʿatunā ruddat ilaynā wanamīru ahlanā wanaḥfaẓu akhānā wanazdādu kayla baʿīrin dhālika kaylun yasīrun And when they opened their belongings, they found their goods (Money - or the goods of barter.) returned unto them. Said they: "O' our father! What (more) can we desire? This our goods hath been returned unto us; and we will bring (more) corn for our family and guard our brother, and we shall have in addition the measure of a camel (load); This (what we have now brought) is (only) an easy (Light measure - small quantity.) measure." See 12:64

item.title: Yusuf:66 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ لَنْ أُرْسِلَهُ مَعَكُمْ حَتّٰی تُؤْتُونِ مَوْثِقًا مِنَ اللَّهِ لَتَأْتُنَّنِي بِهِ إِلَّا أَنْ يُحَاطَ بِكُمْ فَلَمَّا ءَاتَوْهُ مَوْثِقَهُمْ قَالَ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَا نَقُولُ وَكِيلٌ qāla lan ur'silahu maʿakum ḥattā tu'tūni mawthiqan mina l-lahi latatunnanī bihi illā an yuḥāṭa bikum falammā ātawhu mawthiqahum qāla l-lahu ʿalā mā naqūlu wakīlun He said, 'I will not let him go with you until you give me a [solemn] pledge by Allah that you will surely bring him back to me, unless you are made to perish.' When they had given him their [solemn] pledge, he said, 'Allah is witness over what we say.'

item.title: Yusuf:66 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ لَنْ أُرْسِلَهُ مَعَكُمْ حَتّٰی تُؤْتُونِ مَوْثِقًا مِنَ اللَّهِ لَتَأْتُنَّنِي بِهِ إِلَّا أَنْ يُحَاطَ بِكُمْ فَلَمَّا ءَاتَوْهُ مَوْثِقَهُمْ قَالَ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَا نَقُولُ وَكِيلٌ qāla lan ur'silahu maʿakum ḥattā tu'tūni mawthiqan mina l-lahi latatunnanī bihi illā an yuḥāṭa bikum falammā ātawhu mawthiqahum qāla l-lahu ʿalā mā naqūlu wakīlun (Ya'qub) said, "Never will I send him with you until you give me a promise (i.e., oath) by Allah that you will bring him (back) to me, unless you should be surrounded (i.e., overcome by enemies)." And when they had given their promise, he said, "Allah, over what we say, is Entrusted."1 See 12:65

item.title: Yusuf:66 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالَ لَنْ أُرْسِلَهُ مَعَكُمْ حَتّٰی تُؤْتُونِ مَوْثِقًا مِنَ اللَّهِ لَتَأْتُنَّنِي بِهِ إِلَّا أَنْ يُحَاطَ بِكُمْ فَلَمَّا ءَاتَوْهُ مَوْثِقَهُمْ قَالَ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَا نَقُولُ وَكِيلٌ qāla lan ur'silahu maʿakum ḥattā tu'tūni mawthiqan mina l-lahi latatunnanī bihi illā an yuḥāṭa bikum falammā ātawhu mawthiqahum qāla l-lahu ʿalā mā naqūlu wakīlun Said (Jacob) "Never will I send him with you until ye pledge a firm covenant in God's name that ye will most surely bring him back unto me, unless ye are completely (Overpowered.) surrounded; And when pledged they unto him a covenant, said (Jacob.) he: (There is) God over all what we say, a Guardian-Witness." See 12:64

item.title: Yusuf:67 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالَ يَابَنِيَّ لَا تَدْخُلُوْۤا مِنْ بَابٍ وَاحِدٍ وَادْخُلُوا مِنْ أَبْوَابٍ مُتَفَرِّقَةٍ وَمَا أُغْنِي عَنْكُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِنِ الْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَعَلَيْهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ waqāla yābaniyya lā tadkhulū min bābin wāḥidin wa-ud'khulū min abwābin mutafarriqatin wamā ugh'nī ʿankum mina l-lahi min shayin ini l-ḥuk'mu illā lillahi ʿalayhi tawakkaltu waʿalayhi falyatawakkali l-mutawakilūna And he said, 'My sons, do not enter by one gate, but enter by separate gates, though I cannot avail you anything against Allah. Sovereignty belongs only to Allah. In Him I have put my trust; and in Him let all the trusting put their trust.'

item.title: Yusuf:67 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالَ يَابَنِيَّ لَا تَدْخُلُوْۤا مِنْ بَابٍ وَاحِدٍ وَادْخُلُوا مِنْ أَبْوَابٍ مُتَفَرِّقَةٍ وَمَا أُغْنِي عَنْكُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِنِ الْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَعَلَيْهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ waqāla yābaniyya lā tadkhulū min bābin wāḥidin wa-ud'khulū min abwābin mutafarriqatin wamā ugh'nī ʿankum mina l-lahi min shayin ini l-ḥuk'mu illā lillahi ʿalayhi tawakkaltu waʿalayhi falyatawakkali l-mutawakilūna And he said, "O my sons, do not enter from one gate but enter from different gates; and I cannot avail you against (the decree of) Allah at all. The decision is only for Allah; upon Him I have relied, and upon Him let those who would rely (indeed) rely." And he said: O my sons! Do not enter by one gate, but enter by different gates, and I cannot avail you against Allah at all. Verily, the decision rests only with Allah. In Him, I…

item.title: Yusuf:67 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَقَالَ يَابَنِيَّ لَا تَدْخُلُوْۤا مِنْ بَابٍ وَاحِدٍ وَادْخُلُوا مِنْ أَبْوَابٍ مُتَفَرِّقَةٍ وَمَا أُغْنِي عَنْكُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِنِ الْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَعَلَيْهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ waqāla yābaniyya lā tadkhulū min bābin wāḥidin wa-ud'khulū min abwābin mutafarriqatin wamā ugh'nī ʿankum mina l-lahi min shayin ini l-ḥuk'mu illā lillahi ʿalayhi tawakkaltu waʿalayhi falyatawakkali l-mutawakilūna And said (Jacob.) he: "O' my sons! Enter (To avoid being envied by the people, they were advised to enter separately by different doors. This indicates that Islam does not discard the effect of the evil eye, and there are authentic traditions from the Holy Prophet indicating that there are some, the evil of whose sight affect the other objects. The remedy for it is firm trust in God. There are particular prayers for this - there are authentic records of the actual instances in support…

item.title: Yusuf:68 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَمَّا دَخَلُوْۤا مِنْ حَيْثُ أَمَرَهُمْ أَبُوهُمْ مَا كَانَ يُغْنِي عَنْهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِلَّا حَاجَةً فِي نَفْسِ يَعْقُوبَ قَضَاهَا وَإِنَّهُ لَذُو عِلْمٍ لِمَا عَلَّمْنَاهُ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ walammā dakhalū min ḥaythu amarahum abūhum mā kāna yugh'nī ʿanhum mina l-lahi min shayin illā ḥājatan fī nafsi yaʿqūba qaḍāhā wa-innahu ladhū ʿil'min limā ʿallamnāhu walākinna akthara l-nāsi lā yaʿlamūna When they entered whence their father had bidden them, it did not avail them anything against Allah, but only fulfilled a wish in Jacob's heart. Indeed he had the knowledge of what We had taught him, but most people do not know.

item.title: Yusuf:68 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَمَّا دَخَلُوْۤا مِنْ حَيْثُ أَمَرَهُمْ أَبُوهُمْ مَا كَانَ يُغْنِي عَنْهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِلَّا حَاجَةً فِي نَفْسِ يَعْقُوبَ قَضَاهَا وَإِنَّهُ لَذُو عِلْمٍ لِمَا عَلَّمْنَاهُ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ walammā dakhalū min ḥaythu amarahum abūhum mā kāna yugh'nī ʿanhum mina l-lahi min shayin illā ḥājatan fī nafsi yaʿqūba qaḍāhā wa-innahu ladhū ʿil'min limā ʿallamnāhu walākinna akthara l-nāsi lā yaʿlamūna And when they entered from where their father had ordered them, it did not avail them against Allah at all except (it was) a need (i.e., concern) within the soul of Ya'qub, which he satisfied. And indeed, he was a possessor of knowledge because of what We had taught him, but most of the people do not know. See 12:67

item.title: Yusuf:68 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَمَّا دَخَلُوْۤا مِنْ حَيْثُ أَمَرَهُمْ أَبُوهُمْ مَا كَانَ يُغْنِي عَنْهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِلَّا حَاجَةً فِي نَفْسِ يَعْقُوبَ قَضَاهَا وَإِنَّهُ لَذُو عِلْمٍ لِمَا عَلَّمْنَاهُ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ walammā dakhalū min ḥaythu amarahum abūhum mā kāna yugh'nī ʿanhum mina l-lahi min shayin illā ḥājatan fī nafsi yaʿqūba qaḍāhā wa-innahu ladhū ʿil'min limā ʿallamnāhu walākinna akthara l-nāsi lā yaʿlamūna And when they had entered as they were bidden by their father; it did not avail them aught against (the decree of) God; but (it was only) a desire in Jacob's soul which he satisfied; and verily, he was possessed of knowledge for we had taught him, but most people know (this) not. In spite of the caution taken, Bin-Yamin entering the city alone, separated by his other brothers, lost his way and Gabriel at last guided him and got…

item.title: Yusuf:69 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَمَّا دَخَلُوْۤا عَلَى يُوسُفَ ءَاوَى إِلَيْهِ أَخَاهُ قَالَ اِنِّیْ أَنَا أَخُوكَ فَلَا تَبْتَئِسْ بِمَا كَانُوْۤا يَعْمَلُونَ walammā dakhalū ʿalā yūsufa āwā ilayhi akhāhu qāla innī anā akhūka falā tabta-is bimā kānū yaʿmalūna And when they entered into the presence of Joseph, he set his brother close to himself, and said, 'Indeed I am your brother, so do not sorrow for what they used to do.'

item.title: Yusuf:69 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَمَّا دَخَلُوْۤا عَلَى يُوسُفَ ءَاوَى إِلَيْهِ أَخَاهُ قَالَ اِنِّیْ أَنَا أَخُوكَ فَلَا تَبْتَئِسْ بِمَا كَانُوْۤا يَعْمَلُونَ walammā dakhalū ʿalā yūsufa āwā ilayhi akhāhu qāla innī anā akhūka falā tabta-is bimā kānū yaʿmalūna And when they entered upon Yusuf, he took his brother to himself; he said, "Indeed, I am your brother, so do not despair over what they used to do (to me)." And when they went in before Yusuf, he took his brother (Binyamin) to himself and said: Verily, I am your brother, so grieve not for what they used to do (12:69). Yusuf Comforts Binyamin Allah states that when Yusuf's brothers went in before him along with his full brother Binyamin, he invited them to a place of honor as privileged guests. He granted them gifts and generous hospitality and kindness. He met his brother in confidence and…

item.title: Yusuf:69 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: وَلَمَّا دَخَلُوْۤا عَلَى يُوسُفَ ءَاوَى إِلَيْهِ أَخَاهُ قَالَ اِنِّیْ أَنَا أَخُوكَ فَلَا تَبْتَئِسْ بِمَا كَانُوْۤا يَعْمَلُونَ walammā dakhalū ʿalā yūsufa āwā ilayhi akhāhu qāla innī anā akhūka falā tabta-is bimā kānū yaʿmalūna And when they entered in unto Joseph, he lodged his (own) brother (Benjamin) with himself, said (into his ears) "I am thy brother (Joseph), therefore grieve thou not at what they do." The brothers of Joseph entered the court of Joseph and presented themselves and said they had brought with them their brother Bin-Yameen and they also wanted to return the price of the wheat which by some mistake had been left in the grains supplied to them. Joseph ordered for six trays of food for them and desired that on each tray should sit the children of one and the same parents. On the five trays sat…

item.title: Yusuf:70 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُمْ بِجَهَازِهِمْ جَعَلَ السِّقَايَةَ فِي رَحْلِ أَخِيهِ ثُمَّ أَذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنٌ أَيَّتُهَا الْعِيرُ إِنَّكُمْ لَسَارِقُونَ falammā jahhazahum bijahāzihim jaʿala l-siqāyata fī raḥli akhīhi thumma adhana mu-adhinun ayyatuhā l-ʿīru innakum lasāriqūna When he had furnished them with their provision, he put the drinking-cup into his brother's saddlebag. Then a herald shouted: 'O [men of the] caravan! You are indeed thieves!'

item.title: Yusuf:70 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُمْ بِجَهَازِهِمْ جَعَلَ السِّقَايَةَ فِي رَحْلِ أَخِيهِ ثُمَّ أَذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنٌ أَيَّتُهَا الْعِيرُ إِنَّكُمْ لَسَارِقُونَ falammā jahhazahum bijahāzihim jaʿala l-siqāyata fī raḥli akhīhi thumma adhana mu-adhinun ayyatuhā l-ʿīru innakum lasāriqūna So when he had furnished them with their supplies, he put the (gold measuring) bowl into the bag of his brother. Then an announcer called out, "O caravan, indeed you are thieves." So when he furnished them forth with their provisions, he put the bowl in his brother's bag. Then a crier cried: O you (in) the caravan! Surely, you are thieves! (12:70). They, turning towards them, said: "What is it that you have lost? (12:71). They said: "We have lost the bowl of the king and for him who produces it is (the reward of) a camel load; and I will be bound by it (12:72). Yusuf had His…

item.title: Yusuf:70 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: فَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُمْ بِجَهَازِهِمْ جَعَلَ السِّقَايَةَ فِي رَحْلِ أَخِيهِ ثُمَّ أَذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنٌ أَيَّتُهَا الْعِيرُ إِنَّكُمْ لَسَارِقُونَ falammā jahhazahum bijahāzihim jaʿala l-siqāyata fī raḥli akhīhi thumma adhana mu-adhinun ayyatuhā l-ʿīru innakum lasāriqūna And when he (Joseph.) had furnished them with their provisions, (at the instance of Joseph) was placed the drinking cup in his brother's saddle-bag; Then cried out a crier: "O' ye (of) the caravan! Verily ye are thieves!" The valuable cup with which the supply of the grain was measured was intentionally left in the bag of Bin-Yamin and at last when it was found in it, no amount of argument on the part of the brothers, particularly of Yahood, was of any avail. According to Jacobian Law Bin-Yamin was detained to be a slave to the owner of the stolen property.

item.title: Yusuf:71 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا وَأَقْبَلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ مَاذَا تَفْقِدُونَ qālū wa-aqbalū ʿalayhim mādhā tafqidūna They said, as they turned towards them, 'What are you missing?'

item.title: Yusuf:71 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا وَأَقْبَلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ مَاذَا تَفْقِدُونَ qālū wa-aqbalū ʿalayhim mādhā tafqidūna They said while approaching them, "What is it you are missing?" See 12:70

item.title: Yusuf:71 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا وَأَقْبَلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ مَاذَا تَفْقِدُونَ qālū wa-aqbalū ʿalayhim mādhā tafqidūna Said they, while turning unto them: "What is it that ye miss?" See 12:70

item.title: Yusuf:72 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا نَفْقِدُ صُوَاعَ الْمَلِكِ وَلِمَنْ جَاءَ بِهِ حِمْلُ بَعِيرٍ وَأَنَا بِهِ زَعِيمٌ qālū nafqidu ṣuwāʿa l-maliki waliman jāa bihi ḥim'lu baʿīrin wa-anā bihi zaʿīmun They said, 'We miss the king's goblet.' 'Whoever brings it shall have a camel-load [of grain],' [said the steward], 'I will guarantee that.'

item.title: Yusuf:72 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا نَفْقِدُ صُوَاعَ الْمَلِكِ وَلِمَنْ جَاءَ بِهِ حِمْلُ بَعِيرٍ وَأَنَا بِهِ زَعِيمٌ qālū nafqidu ṣuwāʿa l-maliki waliman jāa bihi ḥim'lu baʿīrin wa-anā bihi zaʿīmun They said, "We are missing the measure of the king. And for he who produces it is (the reward of) a camel's load, and I am responsible for it." See 12:70

item.title: Yusuf:72 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا نَفْقِدُ صُوَاعَ الْمَلِكِ وَلِمَنْ جَاءَ بِهِ حِمْلُ بَعِيرٍ وَأَنَا بِهِ زَعِيمٌ qālū nafqidu ṣuwāʿa l-maliki waliman jāa bihi ḥim'lu baʿīrin wa-anā bihi zaʿīmun Said they (The King's servants.) : "We miss the king's drinking cup and whosoever bringeth it, shall have a camel load (of corn); and I am responsible for it." See 12:70

item.title: Yusuf:73 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا تَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمْ مَا جِئْنَا لِنُفْسِدَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَا كُنَّا سَارِقِينَ qālū tal-lahi laqad ʿalim'tum mā ji'nā linuf'sida fī l-arḍi wamā kunnā sāriqīna They said, 'By Allah! You certainly know that we did not come to make trouble in this country, and we are not thieves.'

item.title: Yusuf:73 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا تَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمْ مَا جِئْنَا لِنُفْسِدَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَا كُنَّا سَارِقِينَ qālū tal-lahi laqad ʿalim'tum mā ji'nā linuf'sida fī l-arḍi wamā kunnā sāriqīna They said, "By Allah, you have certainly known that we did not come to cause corruption in the land, and we have not been thieves." They said: By Allah! Indeed you know that we came not to make mischief in the land, and we are no thieves! (12:73). They said: "What then shall be the penalty of him, if you are (proved to be) liars (12:74). They (Yusuf's brothers) said: "His penalty should be that he, in whose bag it is found, should be held for the punishment (of the crime). Thus we punish the wrongdoers! (12:75). So he Yusuf began (the search) in their bags before the bag of his brother. Then he brought it…

item.title: Yusuf:73 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا تَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمْ مَا جِئْنَا لِنُفْسِدَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَا كُنَّا سَارِقِينَ qālū tal-lahi laqad ʿalim'tum mā ji'nā linuf'sida fī l-arḍi wamā kunnā sāriqīna Said they: (Brothers of Joseph.) "By God! Ye know that we came not to make mischief in the land, and nor we are thieves." See 12:70

item.title: Yusuf:74 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا فَمَا جَزَاؤُهُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ كَاذِبِينَ qālū famā jazāuhu in kuntum kādhibīna They said, 'What shall be its requital if you [prove to] be lying?'

item.title: Yusuf:74 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا فَمَا جَزَاؤُهُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ كَاذِبِينَ qālū famā jazāuhu in kuntum kādhibīna They (the accusers) said, "Then what would be its recompense1 if you should be liars?" See 12:73

item.title: Yusuf:74 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا فَمَا جَزَاؤُهُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ كَاذِبِينَ qālū famā jazāuhu in kuntum kādhibīna They (The King's servants.) said: "But what shall be the punishment for this, if ye be liars?" See 12:70

item.title: Yusuf:75 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا جَزَاؤُهُ مَنْ وُجِدَ فِي رَحْلِهِ فَهُوَ جَزَاؤُهُ كَذٰلِكَ نَجْزِي الظَّالِمِينَ qālū jazāuhu man wujida fī raḥlihi fahuwa jazāuhu kadhālika najzī l-ẓālimīna They said, 'The requital for it shall be that he in whose saddlebag it is found shall give himself over as its requital. Thus do we requite the wrongdoers.'

item.title: Yusuf:75 Tafsir Ibn Kathir - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا جَزَاؤُهُ مَنْ وُجِدَ فِي رَحْلِهِ فَهُوَ جَزَاؤُهُ كَذٰلِكَ نَجْزِي الظَّالِمِينَ qālū jazāuhu man wujida fī raḥlihi fahuwa jazāuhu kadhālika najzī l-ẓālimīna (The brothers) said, "Its recompense is that he in whose bag it is found - he (himself) will be its recompense.1 Thus do we recompense the wrongdoers." See 12:73

item.title: Yusuf:75 Tafsir Mir Ahmad Ali - bil-Quran
item.description: قَالُوْا جَزَاؤُهُ مَنْ وُجِدَ فِي رَحْلِهِ فَهُوَ جَزَاؤُهُ كَذٰلِكَ نَجْزِي الظَّالِمِينَ qālū jazāuhu man wujida fī raḥlihi fahuwa jazāuhu kadhālika najzī l-ẓālimīna Said they: (The King's servants.) "The punishment (Refer to note on verse 12:83.) for it shall be that he in whose bag it is found shall himself be (held as bondsman) in penalty for it; Thus do we punish the wrong-doers." According to the Egyptian Law, the penalty for theft was a very severe punishment with whipping - but here the punishment was allowed to be determined by the son of Jacob, who pledged the undertaking according to the Jacobian Law, i.e., the thief to be a slave of the owner of the stolen property for one complete year.

item.title: Yusuf:76 Tafsir Ali Quli Qara'i - bil-Quran
item.description: فَبَدَأَ بِأَوْعِيَتِهِمْ قَبْلَ وِعَاءِ أَخِيهِ ثُمَّ اسْتَخْرَجَهَا مِنْ وِعَاءِ أَخِيهِ كَذٰلِكَ كِدْنَا لِيُوسُفَ مَا كَانَ لِيَأْخُذَ أَخَاهُ فِي دِينِ الْمَلِكِ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ نَرْفَعُ دَرَجَاتٍ مَنْ نَشَاءُ وَفَوْقَ كُلِّ ذِي عِلْمٍ عَلِیْمٌ fabada-a bi-awʿiyatihim qabla wiʿāi akhīhi thumma is'takhrajahā min wiʿāi akhīhi kadhālika kid'nā liyūsufa mā kāna liyakhudha akhāhu fī dīni l-maliki illā an yashāa l-lahu narfaʿu darajātin man nashāu wafawqa kulli dhī ʿil'min ʿalīmun Then he began with their sacks, before [opening] his brother's sack.
